author: aryamurray
body:
This is the root cause of the Windows flakiness that has been surfacing all week, including the archive corruption fixed in #51.

## Problem

MSVC detection wrote a batch wrapper to a **fixed** path — `%TEMP%\harbour_vcvars.bat` — ran it, then deleted it:

```rust
let temp_batch = std::env::temp_dir().join("harbour_vcvars.bat");
std::fs::write(&temp_batch, &batch_content)?;
let output = Command::new("cmd").args(["/c", batch_path]).output();
let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&temp_batch);
```

Two concurrent `harbour` processes race over that one filename: one deletes the file while the other is about to execute it, and cmd.exe reports **"The batch file cannot be found"** — precisely the message seen in CI. Detection then fails, Harbour silently falls back to another toolchain, and the object extension flips from `.obj` to `.o` mid-project.

## Why it matters more than it looks

That single race is behind three separate failures:

1. **Static archive corruption.** A freshly compiled object arriving under a *new* member name (`lib.o` beside `lib.obj`) left the stale member in the archive, where it won symbol resolution — a library reporting pre-change behaviour despite everything having recompiled. #51 fixed the archive half by recreating rather than updating; this fixes what triggered it.
2. **Spurious full rebuilds**, since every object's fingerprint includes the toolchain.
3. **Incremental no-op assertions are untestable on Windows.** If the toolchain can change between two builds of the same tree, "nothing recompiled" is legitimately false. This is currently blocking the e2e hardening work in #69, where strict no-op assertions fail on Windows for what may be this reason rather than a test defect.

It only ever reproduced under concurrent load — which is exactly what `cargo test` produces, running integration tests in parallel with each spawning its own `harbour`. That is why it presented as flakiness rather than a race, and why it never reproduced when the failing test was run alone.

## Solution

The wrapper gets a unique name from `tempfile`, which also owns deletion, so no other process can remove a file it is about to execute.

## Design decisions worth your attention

**The wrapper batch file is kept, not removed.** It exists so cmd.exe handles quoting of the `vcvarsall.bat` path, which is a real problem worth solving that way; only the naming was wrong.

**`tempfile` rather than a pid-suffixed name.** It is already a dependency, it guarantees uniqueness rather than assuming it, and tying deletion to the guard's lifetime makes the use-after-delete shape impossible to reintroduce by editing the surrounding code.

## Known limitations

**I cannot verify the behaviour, only the types.** This function is `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`, so an ordinary macOS build does not compile it and proves nothing — I flagged this rather than claiming a green local build as evidence. I compiled it by temporarily removing the gates (`cargo check --lib` exits 0 with the new code included) and cross-checking to `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` was not possible because `libz-sys` needs a Windows C toolchain. Whether MSVC detection is now reliable under load is for CI to demonstrate, and the honest test is whether the intermittent Windows failures stop recurring over several runs.

**Other fixed-path temp usages are not audited.** I fixed the one implicated in the observed failures; I did not survey the codebase for the same pattern elsewhere.

## Verification

554 unit + 194 + 43 integration green on macOS, fmt and clippy clean. The Windows-gated function type-checks. Since the bug is a race, absence of failure in a single CI run is weak evidence — this wants watching across a few runs.

author: delwing
body:
`autoReconnect` goes back to meaning only "dial when this profile is opened, instead of opening
offline" — what it did before #111, and what the label said. The reconnect-on-drop behaviour is
refiled as #130, to be done as Mudlet actually does it.

### Why revert rather than fix

**The behaviour was not Mudlet's.** A connection attempt that never landed got a
5s→10s→20s→40s→60s ladder announced as `Trying again in %n second(s)...`, credited to a
`handleFailedConnection` and `FAILED_CONNECTION_RETRY_DELAY` in `ctelnet.cpp`. Neither the
message nor those symbols exist — `grep -r "Trying again" src/` over the Mudlet checkout finds
nothing, and Mudlet never retries an attempt that failed to connect. Its entire auto-reconnect
is four lines of `slot_socketDisconnected` (`ctelnet.cpp:918-923`): redial once, immediately,
silently, and only when the session had been *connected* for five seconds.

**And it always waited 5s anyway** — the symptom that prompted this. The failure counter reset
on `client.connect`, which is emitted from `socket.onopen` (`MudClient.ts:709`). In proxy mode
the proxy accepts the WebSocket first and only then attempts the upstream TCP connect
(`proxy/server.ts:237-305`), reporting nothing back when that fails. So every dial at a dead
game "connected", zeroed the counter, and the next wait was `retryDelayMs(1)` forever. Mudlet's
clock, `mConnectionTimer.start()` in `slot_socketConnected` (`ctelnet.cpp:723`), runs on a real
socket to the game — a signal we do not have here at all.

That missing signal is why this is a revert and not a repair: no settled-session rule can be
written until the proxy says when the game answered. #130 carries the port as Mudlet really does
it, including the fact that Mudlet keeps `autologin` and `autoreconnect` as two separate profile
options — we have only the first, under a name that reads like the second.

### Changes

- delete `src/hooks/useAutoReconnect.ts` and its test, and the wiring in `ProfileSession`
- label back to "Auto-connect on profile open" / "Dial automatically when this profile is
  opened, instead of opening offline."
- `MudSession.deliberateDisconnect` stays — e5cff75 uses it to name "User Disconnected" in the
  disconnect notice. Only its comments, which pointed at the hook, are reworded.

Nothing else from #111 is touched: the address validation, IPv6 handling, `viaProxy` error
wording and profile Duplicate all stand.

Closes nothing; opens #130.

`yarn test` 221 files / 2424 tests pass, `yarn typecheck` clean.

author: alyciabhz
body:
AI disclosure, up front: produced by Claude Code (Opus 5) as orchestrator, with codex-cli seats
under the `consensus-rnd:sshx` skill. A scouting seat proposed the target; the orchestrator wrote
the Lean and the Scribe blueprint; separate codex-cli seats review it adversarially. Every count,
freeze fact, prior-art reading and axiom closure below was re-run by the orchestrator, not taken
from a seat's report. Seats and orchestrator are the same model family, so the reviews are not
independent evidence in the cross-family sense.

## Shape and place on the chain (Art. 7')

- **Form**: deposit.
- **This link**: no theory atom; a direct Lean node at
  `D5/S3/Entropy/Forgetting/TrajectoryLawMass`, with its Scribe mirror, `.md` projection, one
  `Freeze` event and its frozen-state record.
- **After landing**: one `Freeze` event, hash recorded below.

## What this adds

The frozen module `Entropy/Forgetting/TrajectoryEntropyTelescoping` defines

```
trajectoryLaw update initial 0       = initial
trajectoryLaw update initial (k + 1) = pushforward update (trajectoryLaw update initial k)
```

with type `ℕ → Y → ℝ`. Two facts about it are named here:

```
trajectoryLaw_sum_eq : ∀ k, (∑ y, trajectoryLaw update initial k y) = ∑ y, initial y
trajectoryLaw_nonneg : (∀ y, 0 ≤ initial y) → ∀ k y, 0 ≤ trajectoryLaw update initial k y
```

Both require `[Fintype Y]` — the finiteness the finite sums need, which comes with the definition.
**Beyond that instance, `trajectoryLaw_sum_eq` carries no hypothesis**: not nonnegativity, not
normalisation, nothing about `update`. It holds for an arbitrary real weighting.

## Why the mass statement is stated this way

Four private declarations in two frozen modules re-derive this pair:
`Entropy/Forgetting/TrajectoryEntropyTelescoping` and `Entropy/Forgetting/DeterministicEntropyStep`,
two each. Each private mass copy assumes `∑ y, initial y = 1` and concludes `∑ y, … k y = 1`.

Reading those proofs, the hypothesis enters **only through the base case** (`| zero => exact
hinitial`). The successor branch is a `calc` chain that establishes `∑ (k+1) = ∑ k` by
`Finset.sum_comm` and a pointwise collapse — using nothing about normalisation — and then closes
with the induction hypothesis. So the normalisation is decoration relative to what the step
actually establishes, and the statement here drops it and names the conserved quantity instead.
**The mass statement is strictly stronger than the private mass copies** (they follow from it by
substituting `∑ y, initial y = 1`), while `trajectoryLaw_nonneg` matches the private nonnegativity
copies rather than strengthening them.

The nonnegativity statement does need its hypothesis, so it is a separate theorem rather than a
conjunct — bundling the two would attach an unnecessary hypothesis to the half that needs none.

## Library-before-proof (Art. 11)

- **Pinned mathlib: hit.** The induction step of the mass proof is
  `Finset.sum_fiberwise`, and the proof **applies** it rather than reproving it:
  `simpa [Finset.sum_filter] using Finset.sum_fiberwise (Finset.univ : Finset Y) update (…)`.
- The fiberwise family lives in `Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean`. Measured
  with `grep -n "^lemma prod_fiberwise" <file>`: **six** declarations in that section, at lines
  240, 248, 256, 264, 274 and 279, plus two more at 1010 and 1017. All carry `@[to_additive]`.
  The one this proof uses is `prod_fiberwise` at line **274**, whose additive form takes
  `(s) (g) (f)` — matching the call `Finset.sum_fiberwise (Finset.univ : Finset Y) update (…)`.
- **Search note, recorded because the failure mode is reusable**: these lemmas are declared under
  their `prod_` names, so no declaration line carries the additive name. A name search restricted
  to declaration keywords therefore misses them, while a plain name search finds the additive name
  at its use sites. Searching the `prod_` family is what surfaces the declarations.
- This repository, searched by declaration name for the two proposed names: 0 hits
  (`git grep -c … origin/dev -- D5`). Searched for the existing private copies: 4 declarations,
  all `private`, in the two modules named above; every hit was opened.
- **Scope of that count**: it counts declarations of these two propositions *about
  `trajectoryLaw`* under those two names. It is not a count of every place the one-step fact
  appears. As a syntactic upper bound on where to look, 23 files under `D5` mention both
  `pushforward` and `Finset.sum_comm`; those were not opened, so nothing is claimed about how many
  of them re-derive the argument.

## Consumers

Both modules that carry the private copies are frozen, and so is
`TrajectoryEntropyTelescoping`, which supplies the definition. Being frozen, none of them can
import this module, and this change removes none of the four private copies. **This module has
zero consumers on landing.** That is the standing shape for this line of work, not an oversight.

## Machine readings

- `make lean`: `LEAN_EXIT=0`; the new module compiles with zero errors and zero warnings of its own.
- Axiom closure, both theorems: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
- `make lean-report`, `deposit-header-check` (`SL-012`), `make emit`: all exit 0.
- `ledger-append`: `LEDGER_EXIT=0`, exactly one new event,
  `Golden/Frozen/accepted/9d0f74502341160317f78d21922b249fbd0a47c9f290b39c3afbbd00a3052f6f.json`,
  together with its frozen-state record
  `Golden/Frozen/state/D5/S3/Entropy/Forgetting/TrajectoryLawMass.lean.json`.
- Delivery shape against base `1711de8872`: 2 commits, 5 files — both readable from the commit
  range. The delivery chain additionally reported `FINAL_CLEAN=0` for the working tree at the time
  the commits were made; that is a chain reading, not something the range establishes.
- `check --protected-base 1711de8872`: `ADMISSION_RC=3` with exactly one protected-surface change,
  `SL-022 Blueprint/D5/S3/Entropy/Forgetting/TrajectoryLawMass.scribe.cs`. No rejected and no
  blocking findings.
- Bucket `D5/S3/Entropy/Forgetting`: 11 → 12 of 24.

## Where these ran

The Lean build, `make lean-report`, `make emit`, `ledger-append` and the admission run were executed
on a separate machine reached over SSH, not in the orchestrator's own checkout. The two commits were
brought back as a `git bundle`, verified byte-for-byte by sha256 (`452b4b4407593c53`), and rewritten
with `git commit-tree` so the author is this repository's identity rather than that machine's
default — the tree objects are reused unchanged, asserted by comparing the new and old tree ids. The
branch was then pushed locally and the pushed sha was read back with `git ls-remote`.

author: tesseractaz
body:
The last of the two owner decisions from the 2026-09-03 audit.

## The cushion could never be met, and that had consequences

`ARB_OUTAGE_CUSHION_PCT` was a flat 15 % of pool, tested by asking whether a deliberately grid-blind forward simulation stayed above floor+cushion. That simulation runs the **whole house** off the battery for the entire remaining forecast horizon — 25 to 49 hours.

On this plant: P90 load **156–185 kWh/day** against a **92.16 kWh** pool. The trough hit zero **1–8 hours after window close on 7 of 7 nights**, so `cushionShortfall` was pinned `true` by arithmetic.

Being a constant, it was also the exemption key for three separate mechanisms — the under-buy pool, the buy de-bias learner, and the engine-fault strike detector. Each reported "nothing to see" for a reason unrelated to whether there was anything to see. `activeStrikes: 0` meant *cannot count*, not *no faults*.

## Why it was unreachable: the model described something the hardware doesn't do

When the grid drops, the SHP2 carries its **backup circuits**. The rest of the house is simply dead. Measured live on 2026-09-05:

| | |
|---|---|
| `panel_load_watts` | **1,445 W** — the SHP2's circuits, what runs islanded |
| `runway_recent_load_watts` | **4,863 W** — the whole house |

A 3.4× difference. Draining the pack at whole-house load modelled an island the panel cannot create.

## The re-scope

```
cushionKwh = outageHours × islandedLoadKw × safetyFactor / dischargeEff
```

tested against the pack at window close. At 1.445 kW, 8 h and 1.5× that is **~18.5 kWh — larger than the old flat 13.8 kWh band**, so this is not a loosening in magnitude. What changes is that it states something reachable ("we can run the backup circuits for eight hours") instead of something impossible ("we can run the whole house for two days").

There's a test asserting the requirement actually **discriminates** — that some recent nights meet it and some miss it. A cushion that everything passes would be as useless as one nothing passes.

Two knobs: `ARB_OUTAGE_CUSHION_HOURS` (default 8) and `ARB_ISLANDED_LOAD_SAFETY` (default 1.5). The safety factor is **monotone the strict way** — raising it makes the requirement harder — and there's a test pinning that direction, because a "safety" factor that made things easier would be the worst possible thing to get backwards. No PV is credited: an outage can begin at dusk.

## Fail-closed

With no islanded-load measurement (an SHP2 not reporting), the legacy flat band **and** the legacy whole-house trough both stand. The pair is never mixed — a bounded drain tested against a flat band would quietly grant a weaker guarantee than either form intends.

The whole-house trough is still computed and reported as `minProjSocPct` / `baselineMinSocPct`. "What if the entire house ran off the pack" remains true and worth disclosing; it just isn't what the cushion is sized against. The rationale text now names whichever test actually ran, instead of printing one number against the other — it previously produced the self-contradiction *"trough (0%) stays at/above the 31% floor+cushion"*.

## Verification

- **Mutation-verified 3/3**, including the bug this change actually hit: `buildNightChargeInputs` destructures field-by-field, so inputs added to *both* interfaces still arrived as `undefined` and silently took the legacy path. Every unit test of the pure function passed; only the end-to-end test caught it. That mutant is now in the harness.
- Suite **2262/2262**. `validate-addon-config: OK — 81 options, en + es`.

author: wiltshirek
body:
## Root cause

The mobile default runtime was a hand-maintained digest. Runtime fixes could merge and publish successfully while the app continued launching an older image. CI verified each artifact independently but never verified that they represented the same runtime source.

## Invariant

A mobile artifact can be produced only when its committed runtime lock is `ready` and all of these agree:

- every runtime build input's deterministic fingerprint
- the source commit recorded by the lock
- the anonymously pullable immutable OCI digest
- the `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label on both Linux platform manifests

## Enforcement

- Runtime-changing PRs must mark the lock `pending`; CI rejects a falsely ready lock.
- A pending lock allows the runtime image to publish but blocks mobile release.
- The publish summary emits the exact command for the separate reviewed ready-lock PR.
- Local preview/development wrappers validate the full lock before EAS submission.
- EAS remote builds fail in `eas-build-pre-install` when the lock is pending.
- Install-link lookup rejects builds older than current mobile source or any dirty mobile tree.
- The current default advances from the September 1 image to the verified September 4 PTT-fix image (`sha256:183bde18...`).

## Verification

- Runtime: lint, typecheck, 105 tests, and build pass; adapter 76 tests pass.
- Mobile: lint, typecheck, 157 tests, Expo config check pass.
- Ready lock validates its runtime fingerprint, source tree, public OCI digest, and amd64/arm64 revision labels.
- Synthetic stale runtime input is rejected.
- Pending lock is accepted for publication but rejected by strict and EAS pre-install checks.
- Workflow YAML, Node scripts, shell syntax, and diff formatting validate.

author: cirinocarvalho
body:
Completes P2-2 from the review and closes the bracket: entry, take-profit, and now a stop.

## Stop loss

Entry triggers an **OCO** pair, so the first to fill cancels the other. Without that both can fill — the position closes twice, the second time opening a new one in the opposite direction. Verified end to end:

```
entry   LIMIT 3.12                                     TRIGGER
child   OCO
        ├─ LIMIT      6.24               SELL_TO_CLOSE  GTC
        └─ STOP_LIMIT stop 1.56 lim 1.40 SELL_TO_CLOSE  GTC

Schwab: advancedOrderType = OTOCO, accepted
```

Two constraints established by probing the API, not assumed:

**Stops are single-leg only.** A spread is priced as a net debit or credit and neither is a stop order type; Schwab rejects the attempt outright with *"Stop price must be populated only for stop orders."* The field disables for spreads and the dialog explains why, rather than accepting a stop and quietly not attaching one. A defined-risk spread's bounded worst case is already its stop.

**Emitted as `STOP_LIMIT`, never `STOP`.** A plain stop becomes a market order the instant it triggers, which on an options book is exactly when the spread is widest — and this codebase does not send market orders. The limit sits 10% through the trigger so a triggered stop can actually fill; priced at the trigger it frequently would not, which is the failure that leaves someone believing they were protected. It can still miss in a fast move, and the dialog says so.

Worth recording for anyone probing this later: standalone `SELL_TO_CLOSE` stops come back *"account is not approved for this level of options trading."* That is a naked-short rejection from previewing a close with no position, not an unsupported order type — inside the OTOCO the entry establishes the position first.

## Pre-expiry valuation

`PayoffCalculator.ValueAt` answers "what if it reaches X **on date D**" — the question the expiration figure cannot. Deliberately parallel to `PayoffAt`; the only difference is that a leg is worth its Black-Scholes value rather than its intrinsic value, so the two converge as the date approaches expiry. A test pins that convergence to the cent, which makes the settlement figure a special case rather than a separate quantity.

The gap is not small. A long SPY 770 call at 6.43, underlying unchanged at 770.19:

| | P&L |
|---|---|
| 7 days before expiry | −$97.15 |
| At expiry, same price | −$624.65 |

Six times worse for an identical price, purely from time value.

**Three volatility scenarios are shown, never one.** That position spans −$309 to +$115 across ±5 vol points — a wider swing than the price move being contemplated. A single figure would be the same false precision the expiration payoff already invites. The risk-free rate comes from the chain's own `interestRate` rather than an assumed number.

Valuation assumes European exercise. Equity and ETF options are American, so the model understates a deep in-the-money put and a call before a dividend, and is otherwise the standard approximation.

## Two bugs worth reading

**The normal CDF carried a spurious 0.5 factor**, pricing a textbook 10.4506 call at 7.66. Put-call parity still passed — it constrains the *difference* between call and put, so an error affecting both equally cancels. Only the known-value test caught it. Two centring regressions added alongside.

**The stop field was never rendered.** The edits adding the input and its helper targeted markup the formatter had since reindented and failed to match, silently, while the pieces that did land left `renderTicket()` calling an undefined `stopPrice()` — so the ticket threw on every render. The builder, handlers and tests were correct throughout; only the control was missing, which is exactly the kind of gap that passing tests and a green API probe will not reveal. Now verified against the served page rather than the source.

## Reviewer notes

- 644 tests pass. New coverage: Black-Scholes (textbook value, put-call parity, CDF centring, convergence to expiration payoff), OCO pairing, stop refusal on spreads.
- `OptionLeg` gains `ImpliedVolatility` and `Expiration`, both defaulted, so existing callers are unaffected; `ValueAt` returns null rather than a number when a leg lacks either.
- No migrations.

author: psaab
body:
The duplicate-pair cell scanned the source with a regex and read **521 of 548** case strings. Refs #8690.

**Nothing in its output said so.** It reported 52 duplicates — a plausible number — and its degeneracy check was `len(counts) == 0`, which could never fire, because a pattern matching 500+ entries masks the fact that a whole *shape* matches zero. **A degeneracy check on the TOTAL cannot see a gap in the SHAPES.**

## What was invisible

gofmt writes a multi-entry clause as `case "a",` / `\t\t"b",` / `\t\t"c":` — so the **first** pair sits on the `case` line and the **last** ends in a colon. A pattern anchored to `\t\t"..."` with an optional comma missed **both ends of every clause**:

| shape | count | seen by the regex |
|---|---|---|
| `\t\t"X",` | 521 | ✅ |
| `\t\t"X":` | 15 | ❌ last pair of each clause |
| `\tcase "X",` | 11 | ❌ first pair of each clause |
| `\tcase "X":` | 1 | ❌ single-entry clause |

**Six of those 27 were real cross-switch duplicates** — the exact silent-non-exclusion the cell exists to catch — and **two of the six are pairs this lane added** in the system-arrivals increment. The guard was blind to duplicates its own author introduced.

## Why a second regex isn't the fix

A `case`-line pattern was landed first; it closes the 11 and leaves the 16. **Two patterns is still a set of spellings somebody enumerated by looking.** This walks the file with `go/parser` and reads the case expressions, which covers every shape by construction and cannot be broken by a future gofmt change — which is what caused this in the first place.

True count **548**, distinct **490**, duplicates **58** rather than 52.

## The control is now made of evidence

The degeneracy check is **replaced by a reach control**, not strengthened: two pairs only reachable through the `case`-line shape must be present, and they are the two real duplicates the regex missed. Plus a total-against-source floor, which is the shape-independent form — with a parser there are no patterns to assert, so the equivalent question is whether the walk read as many pairs as the file holds.

Both totals are reported, so a future reach gap shows as **a total that disagrees with the source** rather than as a plausible duplicate count.

## Validation

Full `go test ./pkg/...` green; canaries and tree-wide `gofmt -l` run regardless of diff scope.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| skip the first expression of each clause (reproduces the regex gap exactly) | **red** — reach control names the pair it lost |
| introduce a cross-switch duplicate | **red**, names it |
| resolve an existing duplicate | **red**, names it |

Each edit verified by occurrence count before its result was read.

author: naipeloz
body:
Revisión de las cuatro skills de `elegir-bien-el-problema/`, más una capacidad nueva en la que vive en el repo.

## Los arreglos

Todos son la misma clase de defecto: **lo que la skill promete no es lo que su plantilla de salida produce**.

| # | Skill | Qué estaba mal |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `elegir-problema` | Exigía pasar seis criterios y la plantilla reportaba cinco — faltaba *¿alguien juzga una salida en un minuto?*. Se preguntaba y después desaparecía del entregable, así que nadie lo auditaba. |
| 2 | `poc-a-spec` | El puente mapeaba cinco piezas del OKR al spec; la plantilla cubría tres. Sin sección para el eval y sin la fecha de corte del KR2. |
| 3 | `poc-a-spec` + ejemplo | El spec declaraba cuatro tickets en paralelo mientras sus contratos declaraban una cadena 2→3→4 — exactamente lo que la skill prohíbe fingir. |
| 4 | `poc-a-spec` + `formato-de-ticket` | Una mandaba marcar las reglas pendientes en el ticket; la otra rechaza criterios de aceptación no verificables. Un pendiente no se verifica. |
| 5 | `okr-de-poc` | El caso *"el KR2 valida el instrumento"* no tenía forma de salida propia, y el umbral quedaba en el KR2 midiendo dos cosas a la vez. |

Para el 3, la corrección de fondo es separar dos conceptos que estaban colapsados en un solo campo: **bloquear el arranque** (nadie puede empezar) y **consumir la salida** (se escribe contra el contrato, se integra después). Con el contrato fijado, consumir no bloquea — que es justamente el punto que el ejemplo quería demostrar, ahora dicho sin exagerar.

Para el 4, la decisión queda escrita en las dos skills: los ⚠️ pendientes van a **restricciones de alcance**, nunca a criterios de aceptación.

## La capacidad nueva

`formato-de-ticket` ahora tiene destino. El ticket que pasa las cinco secciones se guarda como `tickets/NN-slug.md`, se publica como issue de GitHub, o las dos cosas. **El que no pasa no llega al tablero** — publicar un ticket incompleto es lo que la skill existe para frenar, y en el tablero ya no lo lee su autor sino quien va a implementarlo.

Las barandas, porque publicar es hacia afuera y no se deshace: confirma antes de crear, chequea duplicados, guarda el archivo primero, y no inventa handles, labels ni tableros.

Un efecto lateral que vale: los `- [ ]` llegan a GitHub como checklist tildable. Es otra razón por la que la sección tiene que ser verificable — *"funciona bien"* no se tilda.

## Probado

`tickets/01-bloques-de-foco-del-dia.md` es el primer ticket escrito con la skill, publicado en #5 y agregado al project del repo. Escribirlo destapó dos cosas del código: `expand()` en `src/lib/google-calendar.ts` recibe el `end` de Google y lo descarta, así que no hay hora de fin con la que medir huecos; y `/api/events` no pide `attendees` ni `eventType`, así que tres de las siete reglas del spec no se pueden aplicar todavía. Las dos quedaron declaradas en el ticket en vez de descubrirse a mitad de la implementación.

author: qazuor
body:
## Contexto

Seis complementos declaran `billingType: 'recurring'` y su descripción dice literalmente *«Renews monthly»*, pero **se cobran una sola vez y nunca vuelven a cobrarse**: `addon.checkout.ts:469` emite siempre `mode: 'payment'`, y `expiresAt` sólo se setea para los `one_time`. El comprador paga una vez y conserva el beneficio para siempre.

Decisión del dueño: construir el cobro recurrente de verdad, **en 8 PRs encadenados**. Éste es el primero: sólo infraestructura, detrás de un flag apagado. **No cambia ningún comportamiento.**

El plan completo está en `.specs/HOS-847-addons-recurrentes/plan.md` (incluido en este PR).

## Antes que nada: el «arreglo de una línea» no existe, y es una trampa

Cambiar `mode: 'payment'` → `'subscription'` **no crea un preapproval**. En `@qazuor/qzpay-mercadopago` los tres modos de `checkout.create()` terminan en la API de **Preference**; el modo `subscription` sólo consulta el plan para *mostrar* el precio. El preapproval sale únicamente de `billing.subscriptions.create({ mode: 'paid' })`.

Un cambio así **pasa el typecheck, se ve correcto, y sigue cobrando una sola vez**.

Y confirmado contra los tipos, no contra la documentación: `PreApprovalCreateBody`/`PreApprovalUpdateBody` llevan **un** `auto_recurring.transaction_amount` y ningún array de ítems. No se le pueden adjuntar ítems a un preapproval existente. La única vía es **un preapproval por complemento**.

## Qué trae este PR

**El flag** `HOSPEDA_BILLING_RECURRING_ADDONS_ENABLED`, apagado por default, con sus 5 pasos: schema Zod, entrada en el registry de `@repo/config`, `.env.example` y `env-registry.json` regenerados con sus generadores (`gen:env-examples` / `gen:env-registry-json`), y JSDoc explicando que queda apagado hasta que la cadena entera esté mergeada. `pnpm env:check:registry` verde.

**La migración** `0118_mean_bill_hollister.sql`, generada con `db:generate`:
- `billing_addon_purchases` gana `mp_subscription_id`, `current_period_start/end`, `cancel_at_period_end` y `billing_interval`.
- Tabla nueva `billing_mp_addon_plans`, espejo de `billing_mp_plans` pero indexada por `(addon, billing_interval)` — **sin la dimensión `trial_days`**, porque un complemento no lleva prueba.

## El flag protege de verdad, no sólo en el papel

Verificado en la revisión: **`HOSPEDA_BILLING_RECURRING_ADDONS_ENABLED` no tiene ningún consumidor en código**. Un grep sobre `apps` y `packages` sólo lo encuentra en el schema, el registry, el `.env.example` y el JSON generado.

Con cero lecturas, no hay forma de que rompa nada apagado. Esto importa porque hay un patrón conocido en el que un flag gatea el comportamiento pero **no una lectura previa**, y entonces rompe igual con la feature apagada. Acá no hay ninguna lectura que gatear.

## Riesgos que este PR NO corre, y que sí corren los siguientes

El plan los documenta ordenados por qué tan caro sale equivocarse. Los tres primeros:

1. **Seguir cobrando después de cancelar.** Hoy `cancelUserAddon` hace cero llamadas a MercadoPago — correcto ahora, agujero el día que exista un preapproval. Ya pasó acá: HOS-751, un preapproval quedó `authorized` tras un reembolso y volvió a cobrar.
2. **Contaminar el motor de entitlements.** `subscriptionMatchesDomain` **falla abierto** para `accommodation`, así que una fila de complemento se contaría como la suscripción de alojamiento del dueño. Por eso el PR 2 de la cadena es el aislamiento de dominio, **antes** de que exista una sola fila que pueda romperse.
3. **Doble cobro**, por un pago de complemento contabilizado además como renovación de plan.

## Una fuga del guard G-1, encontrada de paso

`scripts/check-no-trial-to-mercadopago.sh` prohíbe `freeTrialDays`, `freeTrial`, `free_trial` y `start_date` — pero **no `trialDays`**, que es la grafía del input de precio de qzpay y la que efectivamente hornea el `free_trial` en un `preapproval_plan`. Se puede mandar un trial a MercadoPago sin que el CI se entere. El PR 3 de la cadena lo cierra con una constante y un test.

Es la misma familia de incidentes que ya costó ARS 18.000 en producción (HOS-522).

## Si la cadena se corta acá

El sistema queda **idéntico a hoy**. Ninguna columna nueva se escribe, la tabla nueva queda vacía, y el flag no lo lee nadie.

Parte 1 de 8 de HOS-847. No cierra el issue.

body:
## Summary
- R4 (naming consistency) encoded the **personal skills tree** convention — a colon-namespaced `name:` mapping to a hyphen directory. Every repo these skills audit is a **marketplace** repo, where that is inverted and a colon in `name:` is a hard CI failure.
- `structure-check` therefore had no defined verdict for the only CI-passing form, and `structure-refactor --op --apply` would have rewritten a green repo into a shape CI rejects.
- R4 is rewritten to the marketplace bare-name rule in all six sites, in both `structure-spec.md` copies.

## Changes
- `structure-check/references/structure-spec.md`, `structure-refactor/references/structure-spec.md`: R4 table row and rule body replaced with the bare-name rule. `name:` must be the bare skill-directory basename; a colon, or any divergence from the basename, is WARN. Cites the SSOT (`authoring-skills/skills/skill-check/references/naming-convention.md` → "Exception: marketplace repos use the bare form") and notes that its marketplace test — a root holding `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — is the plugin-root discovery M3/M4 already performs, so no new detection was needed. The `devx:ai-context → devx-ai-context` example (a dotfiles-era name illustrating the wrong rule) is dropped. The two copies stay byte-identical.
- `structure-check/references/help.md`: the one-line R4 summary now reads `name: bare, == directory basename`.
- `structure-check/references/report-template.md`: the sample R4 PASS line no longer shows a colon-namespaced `name:`.
- `structure-refactor/references/op-rules.md` and `plan-and-report-templates.md` (plan line, verb glossary, apply rule 7): the `--op` action now rewrites `name:` in `SKILL.md` to the bare basename and **never** `git mv`s the directory. The directory name is what the user types after `/packaging:`, so renaming it is a public API change; `name:` is internal. This also resolves the contradiction where the plan template rewrote `name:` into the colon form while apply rule 7 and `op-rules.md` renamed the directory instead — both branches failed CI.

As restated, R4 is exactly the CI gate in `harness-skills/.github/workflows/skill-check.yml` ("Skill frontmatter name matches its directory"), so the audit rule is now a local preview of a gate that already exists.

## Test plan
- [x] All four skills in this repo score R4 PASS under the new text, with the reason "bare `name:` equals the directory basename" — verified mechanically (`create`, `rename-repo`, `structure-check`, `structure-refactor`).
- [x] A skill with `name: packaging:structure-check` in a directory named `structure-check` scores WARN under the new text (a colon is unconditionally WARN) — it scored "correct" under the old text.
- [x] The R4 table row and rule body are byte-identical between the two `structure-spec.md` copies (`diff` of both sections is empty).
- [x] No `devx:ai-context` / colon-namespaced-`name:`-is-correct text remains anywhere under `skills/`.
- [ ] CI (`skill-check.yml`) green — no `SKILL.md` was touched, so the frontmatter and line-cap gates are unaffected.

## Notes
- Deliberately **not** done, per the issue: collapsing the duplicated `structure-spec.md` into one file plus a pointer. The issue defers that to a follow-up; its "so each skill installs independently" justification no longer holds now that all four skills ship as the single `packaging` plugin.
- `docs/skill-output/structure-check-usage.md:29` still shows `R4 PASS` for this repo. That verdict is still correct under the new rule, so the recorded run needed no edit.
- This lands before #9, which defers the same `structure-spec.md:175-176` / `:189-190` lines to this issue.

## Summary

Implements CB-024 as a receipt-driven, non-executing supervisor policy layer.

- immutable supervision policy, observation, circuit-breaker, and receipt contracts
- deterministic classifications for success/failure/crash/timeout/stall/cancel/termination uncertainty/cleanup uncertainty/security failures
- bounded retry eligibility with explicit retry cap
- fail-closed circuit breaker and kill switch
- exact binding to CB-022 execution receipts and optional CB-023 artifact-intake receipts
- worker text is excluded from supervision decisions
- no process launch, retry execution, network, DB, GitHub, publication, queue transition, or trust promotion authority

## Important limitation

CB-024 does not add a new runtime heartbeat transport. The current CB-022 runtime returns terminal execution receipts, so stall/liveness differentiation is represented as a trusted supervisor-observation contract for future runtime integration rather than fabricated from worker output.

## Validation

GitHub CI is the broad regression gate. This PR adds focused CB-024 tests and intentionally leaves CB-025/verifier/provider-router/GPU work out of scope.

author: justus-ship-it
body:
Reshapes the inherited e-commerce ad generator toward its actual use: producing Meta static ads for Singapore gym clients.

Three commits, oldest first.

## Phase 0 — competitor swipe intelligence (`2be621d`)
Pulls gym ads from the Meta Ad Library via Apify, ranks them by a longevity + volume survivorship proxy, distils recurring patterns into reusable templates, and promotes approved ones into the library. Competitor creatives are used for structure only — never republished, never used as generation references, and `swipe/` is gitignored.

Note the ranking is a **survivorship proxy** (how long an ad ran x variant count), not measured spend or CTR. No real performance data is available for commercial ads.

## Security fixes in the original generators (`e20fbda`)
xlsx CVE, exec injection, gallery XSS.

## Client config layer, control panel UI, drift fix (`09bef27`)

**Why:** the pipeline carried client knowledge in prose (`brand-dna.md`) and in conversation, so every campaign re-asked the same questions and nothing was enforceable. Nothing anywhere captured targeting or budget — `grep -rni budget` across the repo returned zero matches.

**Client configuration as data.** `client-config.mjs` loads `gym-profile.json` (stable identity, brand lock, targeting defaults) plus `offers/{slug}.json` (one per campaign), deep-merges them into `.resolved/{offer}.json`, and validates before writing anything. Split by change frequency: gym identity changes yearly, offers monthly.

Validation is a hard gate. It blocks outcome guarantees, fabricated scarcity, capacity claims with no real spot count, scarcity types missing their dates, CTAs outside the Ads Uploader enum, price/locale currency mismatches, and em dashes in name fields (they break the importer). The resolved brief carries budget in SGD and a geo radius pin — neither had any representation before. `--init` scaffolds the files and the `brand-assets/` tree.

**Local control panel (`ui/`).** Zero-dependency Node server plus a single-page UI: setup status, brand lock with colour pickers, offer authoring, targeting/budget, run triggering with streamed logs, and links into generated galleries. Start with `node ui/server.mjs` → http://localhost:4310.

**Skill/command drift fix.** `.claude/commands/static-ads.md` had silently lost template 51 because `promote-swipe-templates.mjs` wrote `SKILL.md` but never the command twin, so every promotion widened the gap. The script now writes both, and `check-sync.mjs` diffs all three pairs and exits non-zero on drift (`--fix` repairs).

## For a reviewer

- **The UI re-implements no validation.** It imports `loadClientConfig`, so the form and the CLI cannot disagree.
- **Server security posture:** bound to `127.0.0.1` only, since it serves repo files and spawns processes. Runs use `spawn(process.execPath, argvArray)` with no shell; allowed commands and their argument shapes are fixed server-side in `RUNNABLE`; slugs are constrained to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` rather than sanitised.
- **Branch name is stale.** It says `phase0-swipe-intel`, but the branch now carries the config layer and UI too.
- **Known follow-ups, not in this PR:** `static-ads/SKILL.md` still runs the old e-commerce flow and does not yet read these config files; the ~51 templates are still product-shaped and need curating to a gym-native set; `rebuild-upload-csv.mjs` is a live footgun that silently collapses three funnel rows into one and should be deleted; `CLAUDE.md` environment notes and `SETUP-GUIDE.md:35` ("targeting") are stale.

author: satyam7jha
body:
`assessRisk` and `tracePrd` are real agents now, so nothing on the `Agents` interface is a stand-in any more. That closes the brief's last Must Have — the final test quality report, including the risk of the flows nobody tested — and its first Bonus, the PRD-to-test-plan gap analysis.

Both are gated rather than trusted. The risk score is computed from signals we can see; the model may adjust it, but an adjustment with no justification is discarded and the computed score stands, with `priorScore` shown beside anything that moved. A PRD citation whose quote is not verbatim in the PRD is struck out as invented. A surface the model adds without citing an observation is dropped.

Also here: `report.md` beside `report.json`, so the report is a document you can open a PR with, and `GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/*`, so the report shows the screenshot of the page at the moment a test died instead of naming a path on a disk the reader does not have.

Writing the tests found two defects in our own code, both of which failed by rendering a plausible-looking table rather than by erroring:

- The report's "Scenarios covered" table looked results up by `t-${id}`, a shape only `fixtures.ts` produces. Against a real Generator every row read `pending`, on a fully executed suite, in the one table the Must Have names first. The join now lives in `lib/report-join.ts` and is pinned.
- The coverage map rebuilt spec filenames from scenario ids instead of reading `GeneratedTest.file` — correct for flat paths, silently wrong for nested ones, and every surface then reported as untested.

101 unit assertions, up from 40. Full account in §14 of the implementation plan.

author: shevvik88-dot
body:
## Summary

Fixes an income-side blind spot in the transfer-detection rules: the expense side already excluded Transfer/Transfers rows from spending totals, but nothing mirrored that on the income side — so a self-transfer or an incoming P2P payment inflated Net, savings rate, health score, and every other income-derived figure.

**B — income-side asymmetry fix.** New `isRealIncome` (mirror of `isRealExpense`) in both `financialConstants` modules, wired into `financial-diagnosis`, `generate-monthly-report`, and `get-insights` on the backend, and into `App.jsx`/`Transactions.jsx` on the frontend. Once income excludes transfer/P2P legs, "Net" was no longer an accurate label (money left over after spending, not a strict accounting net) — relabeled across all 4 locales to match.

**A — Zelle/Venmo guard removal.** `plaid-sync-transactions`'s P2P override was outgoing-only (`!isIncome`), so an *incoming* Zelle/Venmo credit was left categorized as `'Income'` — exactly the gap B needed a source-side fix for. Now tags both directions; `type` still follows the sign, only `category_name` is forced to `'Transfers'`.

**New `linkIntraUserTransfers` matcher + backfill.** Catches transfers Zelle/Venmo description-matching can't: a credit-card payment or a checking→savings move, where both legs share a bank confirmation number. Runs once per user after every sync path (`resync_all`, `sync_item`, normal per-user sync) — token-only match by design, since a dry run against production data showed a purely structural match (amount + date + opposite account) produced only false positives (a same-day Zelle to a person; real outflows to unconnected external cards). Tags depository→credit pairs on the income leg only (paying down a card is real spending); tags both legs for depository↔depository pairs. The rejected structural fallback is logged in `BACKLOG.md` for revisiting once there's more multi-account traffic to validate it against.

## Commits

1. `fix(income): exclude transfers from income totals (isRealIncome)` — shared constants + the three backend edge functions
2. `fix(ui): mirror isRealIncome in Dashboard/Transactions; relabel Net` — frontend consumers + the Net→"Left over" locale rename
3. `feat(plaid-sync): tag incoming P2P transfers, link intra-user pairs` — the P2P guard fix + the new matcher/backfill

## Testing

Not run live in this PR — logic-level fix mirroring the existing `isRealExpense` pattern already proven across these same surfaces. The token-based matcher was validated with a dry run against production data before being wired in (see code comments / `BACKLOG.md` entry: 11/11 real pairs matched, zero false positives).

author: zarame-sato
body:
## 原因

**ファイル一覧キャッシュのバージョン管理漏れ**です。

#24 で `thumbnailLink` を Drive API の `fields` に追加しましたが、`FILE_CACHE_KEY` を据え置いたままでした。このキャッシュは 24 時間有効かつ「マッピングとルートフォルダが変わっていなければ有効」と判定するため、**`thumbnailLink` を追加する前に保存された一覧をそのまま掴み続けます**。

結果、どのファイルにも `thumbnailLink` が無く、`thumbAttr()` がサムネ対象の印を一切付けない状態になっていました。実機で PDF が線画アイコンのままだったのはこれです。

## 修正

- `FILE_CACHE_KEY` を `mdviewer_file_cache_v2` に。旧キーは起動時に削除して容量を空ける
- 「`fields` を変えたら版を上げる」旨を `HANDOVER.md` に明記

## あわせて、サムネ取得を 3 段構えに

`thumbnailLink` は `lh3.googleusercontent.com` から配信され、Authorization ヘッダ付きの fetch に対して CORS を返さないことがあります。1 段目だけに頼ると環境次第で出ないため、フォールバックを用意しました。

| 段 | 手段 | 備考 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `thumbnailLink` を認証付き fetch | 最も軽い。失敗は想定内 |
| 2 | 画像は実体を取って blob 化 | 画像ビューアと同じ経路なので確実に通る |
| 3 | PDF は pdf.js で 1 ページ目を描画 | canvas → JPEG blob |

- 実体から作る場合は `THUMB_MAX_BYTES`（12MB）を超えたら諦める。サムネのために大きなファイルを落とさない
- `thumbCache` は **Promise** を保持し、同じファイルの二重取得を防ぐ
- サムネ対象の判定から `thumbnailLink` 依存を外した（実体からも作れるため）

pdf.js の呼び方は既存の `renderPdf()` と同一です（`getDocument({data}).promise` → `getPage(1)` → `getViewport({scale})` → `render({canvasContext, viewport}).promise`）。ArrayBuffer の detach を避けるためコピーを渡しています。

## 検証

Chromium 実機で、`thumbnailLink` が CORS で失敗する状況を再現したうえで確認しました。

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| サムネ対象 3 件（PDF×2・画像×1） | 3 件すべてサムネ生成 ✅ |
| 取得経路 | `link`（2回失敗）→ `media`（3回成功）とフォールバックが働く ✅ |
| md ファイル | 線画アイコンのまま ✅ |
| リスト表示 | サムネを出さない ✅ |
| 表示形式の保存 | リロード後も維持 ✅ |

回帰テストも通しています。

- 認証の自動復元 11 項目 → 全通過
- HTML プレビューのリンク遷移・相対参照・サンドボックス隔離 → 全通過

**未検証**: この実行環境では CDN が遮断されており **本物の pdf.js を読み込めません**。3 段目は pdf.js を差し替えて制御フローのみ検証しています。API の使い方は既に動作している `renderPdf()` と同一なので risk は低いと判断していますが、実機で PDF のサムネが出るかは確認してください。

## その他

Service Worker のキャッシュを `folio-v32` → `folio-v33` に更新しました。

## Summary
- return controlled 400 responses for invalid registration e-mail/password input instead of accidental internal-server errors
- bound credential input lengths before expensive password work
- keep unknown-account and wrong-password login failures externally identical and perform a dummy scrypt verification for unknown accounts
- require current-password re-authentication and a dedicated rate limit before irreversible account deletion
- add a dedicated client controller and labeled password field for the destructive action
- add API security regressions for registration validation, login failure contracts, failed deletion re-authentication, successful deletion and session invalidation
- align disposable Render staging smoke with the stronger deletion contract by logging out its synthetic session rather than bypassing re-authentication
- refresh readiness/status documentation

## Security scope
The dummy scrypt path reduces the obvious account-existence timing distinction; this PR does not claim to eliminate every possible timing side channel. Render remains disposable test-only staging and no production hosting claim is added.

author: mathruangguru
body:
## Apa

Lesson type baru **feedback**: admin assign satu "orang X" (target) per ronde, mirip presensi (ganti target = bikin lesson baru, bukan edit yang lama). Murid lain di course itu ngisi feedback lewat form in-app — reuse penuh sistem Form yang udah ada (sama kayak refleksi). Target bisa lihat feedback yang masuk **anonim**; admin lihat semuanya **nggak anonim**.

## Keputusan desain penting

**Anonimitas ditegakkan di database, bukan cuma disembunyiin di tampilan.** Target baca feedback-nya lewat RPC baru `get_my_feedback` (security definer) yang query-nya SENGAJA nggak nyertain kolom `user_id` sama sekali — nggak ada policy SELECT baru di `coaching_form_responses` buat target, RPC ini satu-satunya jalan masuk. Jadi nggak ada baris mentah (dengan `user_id`) yang pernah nyampe ke browser target lewat jalur apa pun.

Ini keputusan yang sempat di-breakdown bareng: awalnya "realtime" (biar target liat masuk langsung) kelihatannya butuh Supabase Realtime — tapi `postgres_changes` ngirim baris MENTAH lewat websocket (termasuk `user_id`), jadi kalau target di-subscribe-in ke situ, anonimnya bocor lewat network tab walau UI-nya nggak nampilin nama. Setelah diklarifikasi "realtime" di sini maksudnya cuma "feedback-nya nggak hilang" (bukan live-push pas lagi diketik), solusinya jadi simpel: fetch biasa lewat RPC yang aman, nggak perlu Realtime sama sekali.

## Model & alur

- **Admin** (`CurriculumEditor.jsx`): bikin lesson tipe `feedback`, pilih form pertanyaan + target (dibatasi ke murid yang enrolled course itu, `getCourseEnrollments` + `getUsers`).
- **Giver** (murid lain): buka lesson → `FormPage.jsx` (reuse 100%, sama komponen yang dipake `form`/`refleksi` — cuma beda `noun` buat teks "sudah mengisi") → submit sekali per ronde (RLS `once per form+lesson` yang udah ada).
- **Target**: kalau dia buka link submit lesson-nya sendiri, di-redirect ke `/course/:courseId/feedback` (nggak masuk akal ngasih feedback ke diri sendiri — RLS insert juga nolak ini). Halaman itu (`MyFeedbackPage.jsx`) nampilin semua feedback masuk, dikelompokkan per ronde (satu ronde bisa banyak pengirim, beda dari refleksi yang cuma 1 punya sendiri), anonim.
- **Admin liat rekap**: tab baru "Feedback" di editor course (`CourseFormPage.jsx`) → `CourseSessionRecap.jsx`'s `FormLessonRow` (generalized dari `RefleksiRow` lama, karena struktur data refleksi & feedback identik) — Ringkasan/Jawaban seperti refleksi, tapi "Jawaban" nampilin nama asli.
- **Kartu materi**: giver lihat "Sudah/Belum kasih feedback", target lihat "Lihat feedback buat kamu" (`CourseSection.jsx`, pakai `useAuth()` buat tau siapa yang lagi login).

## File

**Baru**: `supabase/feedback.sql`, `src/pages/MyFeedbackPage.jsx`
**Diubah**: `src/lib/lessonTypes.js`, `src/components/ui/LessonIcon.jsx`, `src/lib/courses.js`, `src/lib/forms.js` (+`getMyFeedback`), `src/pages/FormPage.jsx`, `src/components/course/CourseSection.jsx`, `src/pages/CourseMateriPage.jsx`, `src/components/admin/CurriculumEditor.jsx`, `src/components/admin/CourseSessionRecap.jsx`, `src/pages/admin/CourseFormPage.jsx`, `src/App.jsx` (2 route baru)

## Sengaja belum ada

Kartu "Feedback" di lobby course (StatCard agregat, kayak Skor/Presensi/Refleksi) — bukan bagian inti fitur, gampang ditambah belakangan kalau diminta.

## Catatan

- **Perlu jalanin `supabase/feedback.sql`** di SQL Editor (SETELAH `schema.sql` + `admin.sql` + `forms.sql`, idempoten) — fitur nggak jalan tanpa kolom/RPC baru ini.
- Nggak bisa di-test end-to-end tanpa migrasi jalan; `lint` + `build` hijau, UI (picker admin, 3 state badge kartu, halaman penerima) di-QC lewat harness statis.

author: notoluwayimika
body:
**The pay screen shipped unreachable. This makes it reachable, and sends the payer somewhere to come back to.**

## 1 · Two gaps, and the second one was invisible

**No nav entry.** `parent/finance` shipped registered, gated on `parent_portal.access`, backed by a controller that withholds unreleased bills on both keys, with a pay screen, a fee preview, a return route and a return page — and **no entry in `guardianNavGroups`**. A guardian's whole menu was one item, `My Wards`. The page was reachable only by typing the URL.

Every arm green, feature unreachable, and nothing failed **because nothing links a route to a menu**.

**`callback_url` was never wired.** It was deferred to *"the rebase commit where both halves exist"* — and #399, #405 and #406 merged twelve seconds apart, so that commit never happened. The deferral was a remembered rule wearing a mechanism's clothes: worse than the literal-with-a-comment it was chosen over, because that at least left an artefact someone could trip over.

## 2 · Why these three changes are ONE commit

**The nav gap is the only thing currently protecting against the missing callback.** Nothing reaches the pay screen, so nothing reaches a payment that would return a payer to Paystack's dashboard default instead of the page built to tell them what happened.

**Landing the nav entry without `callback_url` opens exactly that path.** They go together or not at all — stated in the commit message so nobody splits them later.

## 3 · The arm, and how it avoids passing vacuously

Restoring the entry alone leaves the gap able to reopen on the next edit of that array, **looking exactly as green as it did**. So:

- It **extracts the guardian block by name and asserts the extraction succeeded.** If `guardianNavGroups` is renamed, `indexOf` returns −1, `slice` returns the whole file, and every assertion would pass against the **admin** nav — which also links to a finance surface. Broken-open, silently.
- It **asserts `My Wards` survives**, or swapping one entry for the other satisfies the fees check while moving the gap rather than closing it.
- **Bite-proof:** removing the entry reds it.

**Read as text rather than rendered**, because `vitest.config.ts` runs in `node` and argues against installing a DOM for anything that does not genuinely need to render. The limit is stated in the file: it proves the entry is **declared**, not that the sidebar renders it for a given user — the route's middleware is what decides that.

**The stronger gate is named and not built:** every parent-facing route either linked from the nav or on a stated allowlist. It needs a route-to-nav map this codebase does not have, and inventing one the evening before resumption is the wrong trade. Named so it is a deferral, not an omission.

## 4 · One thing this PR's own gate caught

The `resources/` arm that forbids naming the release-stamp column in the frontend **refused this commit** — my new test file's docblock referred to *"the `reviewed_at` … arm"* in prose. That is the rule working exactly as designed: its docblock says a comment tripping it is the intent, not collateral, because naming the physical column in that layer is the first step toward someone filtering on it. Reworded to *"the release-stamp arm"*.

I wrote that rule yesterday and violated it today, in a sentence describing the rule.

---

⚠️ **GitHub Actions has never executed a job here** (billing-locked, permanent — ADR 0053). `bin/quality` passed locally on `e3c0c8a3`.

author: yohimik
body:
ListenConfig.Listen and ListenPacket currently return a not-implemented error. This stops callers that use a zero ListenConfig even though the netdev can listen.

Use the existing TCP and UDP listen paths. Check context before and after address lookup, before a socket is created. Reject Control and explicit TCP keep-alive settings with an error that wraps errors.ErrUnsupported. UDP ignores TCP keep-alive settings. The netdev has no raw socket control hook. It also has no lookup cancellation hook, so a lookup in progress must return before cancellation is reported. Default socket options and MPTCP fallback stay as provided by the existing netdev.

This replaces the local fork patch 895d524. That patch ignored context and Control. The new tests fail on that patch for both cases.

Validation uses released TinyGo 0.43.0-net.1, Go 1.26.7, and an isolated TINYGOROOT with this net tree. No LLVM build is required. Five tests pass on Linux arm64 and Linux amd64. The amd64 tests ran under emulation on an arm64 host. Tests cover a real TCP exchange, UDP receive, listening after context cancellation following creation, netdev delegation, cancellation before and during lookup, expired context, and rejected options. The native tests use getsockname directly to stay independent of #80. Test processes had an external 20-second timeout. Run tools/test-listenconfig.sh with a released compiler to build the tests in an isolated root.

The [Crier record](https://github.com/yohimik/crier/blob/7edaff9/docs/operations/tinygo.md) describes the original listener failure and a historical Linux arm64 run with 142 passing tests. That run used local listener, shutdown, and cookiejar patches. It predates later Crier changes. It is not validation of this branch or of a new Crier release.

Related work and scope

- #77 owns Linux close cancellation and deadline interruption. This PR does not change socket close or the poller.
- #80 owns the bound TCP port. This PR does not change address reporting.
- #78 owns Dialer.Control API fields and other API additions. ListenConfig is a separate API and this PR does not implement raw socket control.
- #79 owns server TLS methods. #67 owns Client.Timeout and transport selection.
- #72–75 cover client redirects, DNS errors, darwin sockets, and darwin client trust roots.
- tinygo-org/tinygo#5631 is closed in favor of tinygo-org/tinygo#5530 for signal delivery.

This PR is based on net main. It needs no change from those PRs to build or to run these Linux tests.

### Current integration status

Darwin fcntl work is in tinygo-org/tinygo#5612. tinygo-org/tinygo#5632 is closed and remains a history reference only. The integer and pointer tests were offered on #5612. Builder socket and spawn symbols in tinygo-org/tinygo#5636 are an independent prerequisite at e8394f67. The direct syscall test needs no net update, so that PR does not wait for this net series. tinygo-org/tinygo#5634 is limited to process support.


### Current Crier evidence

[The Crier report](https://github.com/yohimik/crier/blob/7c4ea43/docs/operations/tinygo-comparison-2026-09-05.md) separates the original size comparison from a new CI-built candidate test. The original stripped Linux ARM64 result is 13,829,248 bytes versus Go's 30,277,794 bytes. Two render fixtures exceed pixel tolerance.

Candidate `e7d34c8c126e0eecd2ce711915f2f88d112d833a`, with net `0f460803`, passed all 24 fork CI checks. Its downloaded compiler artifacts, with no source overlays, build unchanged Crier `7edaff9`. Linux ARM64 E2E passed 143 cases with no failures or skips. Darwin ARM64 passed 142 with no failures and one platform trust-store skip. Darwin startup now works. A separate Darwin local-TLS matrix passes certificate rejection, plaintext refusal, update to a Go 1.1.0 target, and offline rollback. Both platforms pass spawn, signal, cookiejar, os/fcntl, and network probes.

These are combined-candidate results, not proof that this PR alone supplies all features. No new pixel or stripped-size comparison, amd64 execution, or current Dispat acceptance is claimed. WaitDelay and the recorded net limits remain open. No fork release was published.

author: vlumi
body:
## Summary

Stops the Info.plist from silently drifting on every \`make build\`. xcodegen was merging the properties block from project.yml into the tracked plist every run — I clobbered it twice in the last two PRs and had to revert. Move the merge target to \`.build-xcode/generated/Info-iOS.plist\` (already gitignored), delete the tracked file. project.yml stays the source of truth for the values.

Also drops two long-standing build warnings by removing keys that are no longer needed:

- \`UIDeviceFamily\` — superseded by the build setting \`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY=1\` (which is already set on the target).
- \`UIRequiresFullScreen\` — deprecated in iOS 26 with no replacement. The app is iPhone-only anyway, so multitasking modes never applied.

## Verification

- \`make ci\` green from a clean tree (\`.build-xcode/\` + \`PhotoDiary.xcodeproj\` both deleted first).
- Info-iOS.plist materialises under \`.build-xcode/generated/\` on first run.
- \`git status\` clean after \`make build\` — no more stray plist modifications on unrelated branches.
- Xcode build output no longer prints the UIDeviceFamily / UIRequiresFullScreen warnings.

## What this doesn't change

Runtime behavior is identical: the app is still iPhone-only, portrait-only, iOS-latest-only. Only the on-disk location of the plist and two deprecated keys changed.

author: yasu-isct
body:
Closes #83

## Root cause

APP-03 had no trusted single-document rulebook joining the accepted document identity, reviewed applicability rules, precedence policy, interaction policy, and honest coverage declaration. The precedence contract also required at least one override edge, so the only accepted real one-rule scenario could not pass through the real resolution API.

## Scope

- add strict immutable `ReviewedReportPlan v1` with canonical bytes and regular non-symlink path loaders
- validate rule/category ordering, exact document/PDF binding, one common reviewed KB binding, exact precedence subject coverage, policy endpoints/subjects, and existing narrower-scope proof
- allow an empty precedence edge tuple while preserving non-empty exact subjects and all existing edge validation
- commit the reviewed `fact:00063`, page 7 single-rule plan with explicit partial `eligibility` coverage
- document server ownership, later allowlisted identity mapping, partial-coverage wording, and the retrieval/job-status boundaries
- add focused, M4, privacy, inert-import, and private real-PDF regressions

APP-03B/03C, profile execution, evidence materialization, HTTP routes, report prose, automatic rules, overall eligibility, and new hashes remain out of scope.

## Acceptance evidence

- Focused plan/resolution/interaction: `98 passed, 3 skipped` (Windows symlink creation unavailable)
- Existing M4 plus plan: `263 passed, 7 skipped`
- Private real-PDF plan/applicability: `2 passed, 26 deselected`; the local licensed artifact was available, the rebuilt KB contained 298 Facts, and the plan resolved `fact:00063` to page 7 and the accepted authoritative text hash
- Full non-model suite: `1024 passed, 15 skipped, 1 deselected` in 118.77s; all 15 skips are Windows symlink-permission cases, and the one deselection is the explicitly excluded model integration test
- Ruff: `ruff check . --no-cache` passed
- Format: `ruff format --check . --no-cache` passed (`115 files already formatted`)
- Compile: `python -m compileall -q src tests` passed
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` passed
- RET-09: passed with unchanged signed implementation SHA-256 `58e70acc444f5b096a35c9d98890854f64f20e0a577063d89f663ed0e0ab2a79`; no policy, benchmark, metric, rank, page, provider, model, runtime, or threshold changed

## Review notes

`coverage_status` can only be `partial_reviewed_rules`; the committed limitation explicitly forbids treating this atomic rule as route approval, overall eligibility, admission, or recommendation. Retrieval rank remains evidence-discovery metadata and durable job status remains processing state.

author: ianlkl11234s
body:
## 為什麼

使用者回報「一些國家的標記做得還不夠好」：INTEL 面板 526 件裡 117 件「待定位」，
且「干邑熱潮：馬戲舞蹈與驚險體驗」「高等教育界作弊風氣猖獗」這類條目跟重大事件並列。

唯讀調查（去重後 `DISTINCT ON (candidate_id)`）＋ 下載 16 個 GKG 原始檔反查 `V1LOCATIONS` 的結論：

1. **截圖裡 117 筆待定位有約 105 筆是舊帳**。metadata fallback（`50cc8df`）在 2026-09-03
   09:00–10:00 UTC 之間才上線；上線前那批 150 列有 105 筆待定位，上線後 507 筆只剩 75 筆（14.8%）。
   這批會自然滾出 7 天視窗。
2. **殘留待定位不是「GKG 有卻沒用」**：26 筆抽樣中,「有 type 1/3/4 + 座標卻沒被用」**0 筆**。
   殘留全部落在兩桶——只有 type 2/5（US 州 / 世界一級行政區）被 `kind` map 丟掉（8/26），
   以及 GDELT 自己完全沒 geocode（18/26）。**國家標錯 0 筆，只有沒標。**
3. `coup` / `epidemic` / `invasion` 誤命中把慣用語與比喻送進 LLM，佔用配額也污染面板。

完整基線、分桶、逐筆抽樣與 A/B/C 建議收在 `docs/GLOBAL_EVENTS_GEO_QUALITY.md`。

## 這支 PR 做了什麼

三項都是確定性修正，**不動 LLM 契約、不改 prompt、不需要 migration**。

### 1. C-1｜per-signal veto（`IMPACT_VETOES` / `title_impact_signals`）

只讓誤命中的那個 signal 失效，標題若還留著其他 signal 就照樣進 LLM。候選層級的規則會把
`What to know about a reported US airstrike that hit a wedding in Iran` 這種真 keep_core 一起殺掉。

實測 507 筆 production 候選：**32 筆（6.3%）失去所有 signal，其中 28 筆原判 drop_noise（精確度 88%）**，
誤砍 2 筆 keep_core。刻意不加 cyclone 規則（forward-only lookahead 分不出
`after Cyclone Narelle` 與 `Cyclone Opener`，加了精確度反而從 88% 掉到 84%）。

### 2. A-1a｜ADM1 提及降級為 **batch 級**國家代表點

ADM1-only 提及是「國家」的真實證據，但座標是州質心。掃**整個 batch** 所有候選的 type 1 evidence 建
`country_code -> 國家代表點` anchor（同 cc 依 `evidence_id` 排序取最小，同批次結果才穩定），
ADM1 evidence 改用該 anchor 的名稱與座標發佈 `country_center`。

> anchor 必須是 batch 級：候選在 fallback 之後還待定位，就代表它自己的 evidence 裡沒有可用的
> type 1，只掃單一候選永遠不會 fire。

`evidence_basis` 明寫「座標為 GDELT 在本輪其他文章中使用的該國固定質心，非本文報導之位置」，
維持 ADR-0002 的「不編造座標」。不走 `admin1_center` 新 kind（要動 migration 399 CHECK + RPC 398 +
前端 + workbench 四個 repo）。

### 3. A-2｜Headline gazetteer（**migration 399 早就鋪好路，collector 從沒走**）

`399_global_event_headline_geography.sql` 的 `source_kind` allowlist 已含 `headline_gazetteer`，
lineage regex 已允許 `<kind>:<url>#<片段>` 形式，只禁止它搭 `event_point`——但 collector 全檔沒有這個字串。

做法不引入任何外部資料集：在 `parse_gkg_artifact` 把 GDELT 自己的 `V1LOCATIONS` 地名累進索引，
對 `places` 仍為空的候選用代表標題做最長地名比對。**名稱與座標都來自 GDELT 自己的 geocoding**，
只有「這個標題提到這個地名」是我們的判斷，`evidence_basis` 逐字引用標題讓人可覆核。

索引持久化到 `<LOCAL_DATA_DIR>/global_events/gazetteer.json`（滾動 7 天）。這不是加分項：
`collect()` 在有 `routing_work` 時直接沿用上一輪 batch、**不再跑 `parse_gkg_artifact`**，
那條 resume path 上 run-local 索引會是空的。

## 預估效果

| | 待定位（上線後 507 筆母體） |
|---|---|
| 現況 | 75（14.8%） |
| ＋A-1a | 約 53 |
| ＋A-2（實測下限 5/26） | **約 39** |

A-2 的桶上限是 10/26 ≈ 38%；加上跨輪字典成長會往上限靠。
另外 C-1 讓每輪少 6.3% 的 LLM 呼叫。

## 風險與緩解

| # | 風險 | 緩解 |
|---|---|---|
| **R3** | migration 399 的 lineage regex `^<kind>:(gdelt:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\|https?://[^\s#]+#.+)$` | gazetteer 用 `<kind>:<url>#<片段>`；**URL 本身含 `#` 時退回 `gdelt:headline_<sha>`**，有測試 |
| **R4** | `evidence_url` 必須在 `source_urls` 內 | 只用已在 `source_urls` 的代表文件 URL；測試涵蓋「文件在 documents 但不在 source_urls 要跳過」 |
| **R5** | `evidence_basis` 不得為空、≤500 字 | 三條路徑都填固定句型，契約測試逐欄驗 |
| **R6** | `place_key` 重複 → **整批** ingest 失敗（不是掉一個點） | 沿用既有 `place_identity` / `seen_places` 去重路徑，不另外 append；契約測試驗 place_key 不重複 |
| **R10** | gazetteer 假陽性 | 只比對第一個 `\|` / ` - ` / ` – ` / ` · ` 之前片段（實測 `\| My Grande Prairie Now` 就是這條造成的）＋ masthead stop-list ＋ `evidence_basis` 明示「未確認為精確發生地」；ADM1 型別條目不發佈 |
| R2 | 399 的 `location_kind` enum 違反會 `RAISE EXCEPTION` | 全程沿用 `country_center` / `city_center`，未新增 kind |
| R8 | `pulse-intel-workbench` 若窮舉解析 `source_kind` | 399 已 allowlist `headline_gazetteer`，代表設計時就預期它出現；上線前仍建議 workbench 側確認一次 |

新增一支測試逐欄對照 migration 399 的 CHECK 與 lineage regex（`_assert_migration_399_place_contract`），
因為任何違反都會退掉整批而不是只掉一個點。

`gazetteer.json` 放在 collector 根目錄：既不在 `_cleanup_local_artifacts` 掃的
`raw/` `handoff/` `stage1_cache/` 三個子目錄裡，也不是 `tasks/archive.py` 的 `YYYY/MM/DD`
數字目錄，另有測試釘住「ancient mtime 也不被清掉」。

## 測試

`pytest tests/ -q` → **462 passed, 2 skipped**（`test_global_events.py` 從 68 增至 91）。
不打 OpenRouter、不寫 production。

新增 23 支測試，覆蓋：veto（干邑 `coup de`、作弊 `epidemic` 隱喻、`home invasion`、政治地震、
RAF Typhoon 皆 veto；airstrike/coup attempt/Cyclone landfall/Ebola outbreak 仍可路由）、

body:
## Summary

Follow-up fixes from the post-ConPTY / split-pane review.

### 1. Child terminal close is now non-destructive on backend failure
- Removed the optimistic `REMOVE_CHILD` before `close_channel`.
- A child is removed only after the backend call succeeds (the normal `channel-closed` event may arrive first; the post-success reducer action is intentionally idempotent).
- Removed the frontend `getTabs()` recovery path that replaced the rich frontend `TabInfo` state with the backend's intentionally smaller runtime tab snapshot.
- Result: a failed child close keeps its Terminal and Pane assignment intact so the user can retry.

### 2. Split lifecycle fallback is now a tested core invariant
- Moved `remapRemovedChildrenToDisconnectedRoots` into `src/core/split-layout.ts`.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - child -> disconnected root Pane fallback;
  - multiple children of one root preserving only the selected Pane;
  - closing one child while the parent remains connected (must not remap to root).

### 3. ConPTY startup partial-probe tail cannot be stranded
- If the startup interception window expires while only a partial `ESC[6n` prefix is buffered, the bytes are released to xterm instead of remaining in the backend forever.
- Added Windows fragment-boundary coverage for `ESC`, `ESC[`, `ESC[6`, and full query removal.

### 4. Network Debug listener registry cleanup
- Added a generic plugin-store `onRelease` hook for permanent session deletion.
- Network Debug now releases its module-level listener dependency entry and framer/decoder state when the session is permanently deleted.
- Registry refresh moved from render-time mutation to `useLayoutEffect`.

## Regression focus

- Close a Local Shell / SSH child normally.
- Force/induce a close failure: child + selected Pane must remain intact.
- Disconnect a parent container: selected child Pane falls back to the disconnected parent root.
- Close one child while siblings remain connected: no parent fallback.
- Repeatedly create/delete Network Debug sessions and reconnect them.
- Windows Local Shell CPR startup + CMD / PowerShell / Git Bash / WSL smoke tests.

body: Closes #109 ## 해결할 문제 Scalar 문서의 ERD 가 읽히지 않았다. 원인은 둘이고, 층이 다르다. **1. 래스터로 굽고 있었다.** 서빙 PNG 는 1904x1058 인데 Mermaid 원본 레이아웃은 4600x2557 이다 — 41% 로 축소해 구운 셈이다. PNG 는 1904px 가 정보의 상한이라 확대해도 보간일 뿐 없는 픽셀이 생기지 않는다. **2. 소개 칼럼이 애초에 좁다.** Scalar Introduction 칼럼 폭은 실측 **470px** 다. 16개 엔티티 ERD 를 여기 넣으면 벡터로 바꿔도 글자를 읽을 수 없다. 즉 인라인 이미지만 고쳐서는 풀리지 않는 문제였다. 작업 중 **세 번째 문제**가 드러났다. ERD 가 실제 스키마와 **컬럼 9개** 어긋나 있었다: `users.ranking` `point` `highest_grade` `vote_count` `active_nickname`, `post.popularity_score`, `comment.container_type`, `post_product.container_type`, `item_container.access_urls`. ERD 첫 줄은 "정본은 JPA 엔티티다(`ddl-auto: validate` 로 보증)" 라고 적어 두었지만 **보증의 방향이 한쪽뿐이다.** validate 는 *엔티티가 선언한* 컬럼이 DB 에 있는지만 보고, DB 에만 있고 매핑이 없는 컬럼은 보지 않는다. V7 과 V8 이 `ALTER` 로 넣고 네이티브 쿼리로만 읽어 `@Column` 이 없던 탓에 조용히 쌓였다. ## 왜 지금 M2 기능 개발이 끝나 스키마가 안정된 시점이다. 지금 ERD 를 맞춰 두지 않으면 드리프트가 계속 쌓이고, 나중에는 "어디부터 틀렸는지" 를 되짚는 비용이 커진다. 실제로 이번에 9개가 쌓여 있었고, 다음 마이그레이션이 들어오면 더 늘어난다. 문서 표면을 손대는 김에 검사까지 같이 넣는 편이 싸다. 렌더 파이프라인을 이미 건드리고 있어서, 정합 검사를 붙이는 한계비용이 낮다. ## 어떻게 **표면을 둘로 나눴다.** 하나로는 470px 와 "확대해서 읽기" 를 동시에 만족시킬 수 없다. | 소스 | 산출물 | 역할 | |---|---|---| | `docs/erd/erd.mmd` | `docs/erd/erd.svg` | 물리 ERD, 자료형까지. 리뷰용 | | `docs/erd/erd-logical.mmd` | `/docs/erd.svg` | 논리 ERD, 본문 미리보기(클릭하면 상세로) | | `docs/erd/erd-logical.architecture.json` | `/docs/erd.html` | 상세 페이지, 확대·팬·검색·테마 전환 | **물리 ERD 를 지우지 않았다.** `BadgeEntity` `UserDailyActivityEntity` 등 코드 주석 다수가 물리 자료형을 근거로 인용하고 있어(`TINYINT` 매핑 함정 등), 지우면 근거가 끊긴다. **테마는 따라가지 않고 고정했다.** `` 로 들어간 SVG 는 Scalar 의 다크/라이트 토글 상태를 알 수 없다(`prefers-color-scheme` 은 OS 설정을 따라 Scalar 토글과 어긋난다). 그래서 자기 배경을 가진 밝은 카드로 굳혀 어느 배경에서도 대비를 보장한다. **정합 검사는 엔티티가 아니라 실제 스키마를 정본으로 삼는다.** 위 "해결할 문제" 의 사각지대가 정확히 그 이유다. CI 에 `erd-drift` 잡을 추가했다. ## 변경 유형 - [ ] 기능 추가 - [x] 버그 수정 - [ ] 리팩터링 (동작 변경 없음) - [ ] 스키마·마이그레이션 - [x] 문서 - [x] 빌드·설정 ## 한계와 트레이드오프 **1. `erd.html` 은 archify(개인 스킬 설치본)가 있어야 다시 만든다.** 이 검사가 통과 조건이므로, archify 없는 사람이 spec 을 고치면 **CI 가 막힌다.** 한 번 검사에서 빼봤다가 되돌렸다. 빼면 테이블 집합만 보게 되어 관계선·라벨·설명· 그룹핑이 바뀌어도 통과하는데, `DocsConfig` 가 이 페이지를 "실제로 읽을 때 여는 정본" 으로 안내하므로 독자가 옛 그림을 보게 된다. 그 구멍이 막다른 검사보다 나쁘다고 봤다. 대가를 줄이려고 둘을 뒀다 — `render-erd.sh --check` 로 archify 없이도 무엇이 낡았는지 알 수 있고, 실패 메시지가 README 의 ERD 절로 안내한다(spec 만 커밋하고 렌더 요청). **이건 완전한 해결이 아니라 완화다.** 근본 해결은 렌더를 CI 잡으로 옮기는 것이고, 이번 범위를 넘어 따로 다룰 일이다. **2. `erd.html` 이 655KB 다.** jar 에 들어가고 git 에도 커밋된다. `docs/diagrams/develop-infra.html`(648KB) 선례를 따랐지만, 저장소에 대형 HTML 이 둘이 된다. 협업 효율을 우선해 그대로 두기로 했다. **3. 검사가 보지 않는 것.** 자료형·길이·nullable 은 `ddl-auto: validate` 가 이미 잡으므로 뺐다. **관계선도 대조하지 않는다** — 애그리거트 경계를 넘는 참조는 FK 를 걸지 않으므로(ADR-0008) FK 와 대조하면 정상 설계가 실패로 뜬다. **4. 논리 ERD 는 개수만 본다.** 한글 엔티티명이라 테이블명과 직접 매칭되지 않는다. 이름까지 보는 건 archify spec(`sublabel` 에 실제 테이블명이 있다)에서만 한다. **5. CI 마이그레이션은 Flyway 런타임이 아니다.** 순서는 맞췄지만 트랜잭션 경계· checksum·baseline 은 다루지 않는다. "최종 스키마 모양" 만 필요한 용도라 그렇게 뒀고, `R__`·`U__` 가 나타나면 실패시켜 이 전제가 깨지는 걸 알린다. ## 검토한 대안 | 대안 | 기각 사유 | |---|---| | PNG 를 4000px 로 크게 굽기 | 확대 한도만 미룰 뿐 원인(래스터)이 그대로다. 파일만 커진다 | | mermaid.ink SVG 를 그대로 임베드 | **글자가 통째로 사라진다.** 기본 SVG 는 텍스트를 `` 로 내는데(실측 483개, `` 0개) `` 는 이미지 모드라 렌더하지 않는다. 최상위 `htmlLabels:false` 로 해결 | | `er.htmlLabels: false` | 먹지 않는다. foreignObject 483개 그대로 — 최상위 키만 유효 | | SVG 안에 `prefers-color-scheme` 미디어쿼리 | `` 안에서는 OS 설정을 따라 Scalar 토글과 어긋난다. OS 라이트 + Scalar 다크면 깨진다 | | 다크/라이트 2장 + `` | 위와 같은 토글 불일치가 남고, Scalar 가 raw HTML 을 통과시킬지 불확실 | | Mermaid 로만 상세 페이지까지 | ER 레이아웃이 가로 폭을 못 줄인다. 논리 ERD 도 4364px 라 470px 칼럼에서는 여전히 못 읽는다 | | archify HTML 단독(인라인 제거) | 본문에서 그림이 사라져 "문서 열자마자 구조 파악" 이 안 된다 | | 물리 ERD 를 논리로 완전 교체 | 코드 주석 다수가 물리 자료형을 근거로 인용 중이라 근거가 끊긴다 | | Flyway Gradle 플러그인으로 CI 마이그레이션 | 스키마만 세우면 되는데 빌드 의존성이 늘고 버전 정합을 따로 관리해야 한다 | | 신선도를 mtime(`src -nt out`)으로 판정 | **CI 에서 항상 통과한다.** git 체크아웃이 모든 파일 mtime 을 같게 만든다(fresh clone 으로 확인). 소스 해시를 산출물에 새기는 방식으로 교체 | | 마이그레이션 정렬에 `sort -V` | `V1.2` 를 `V1` 앞에 놓는다. Flyway 는 `V1 < V1.2` — 직접 구현 | ## Edge Case - **소수점 버전.** `sort -t V -k2 -n` 은 `1.10` 을 소수로 읽어 `V1.10` 을 `V1.2` 앞에 놓는다. Flyway 는 조각마다 정수 비교라 `V1 < V1.2 < V1_5 < V1.10 < V2 < V10` 이다. 현재 마이그레이션은 전부 정수라 당장 깨지지 않지만, 소수점을 처음 넣는 날 터진다. - **`R__`·`U__` 마이그레이션.** 버전이 없거나 짝 V 와 같은 버전이라 순서대로 먹이는 방식과 의미가 다르다. 발견 시 실패시킨다. - **버전 중복.** 같은 버전 두 파일이면 실패시킨다. - **파일명 공백.** `for f in $(ls ...)` 대신 `while read` 로 견딘다. - **생성 컬럼.** `container_type` 은 `GENERATED ... STORED` 인데 `information_schema.columns` 에 나온다. ERD 에도 넣어 일치시켰다. - **`.mmd` 들여쓰기.** 파서는 4칸 들여쓰기를 전제한다. 어긋나면 블록 판정이 풀리는데, 집합 비교에서 양방향으로 튀어 **조용히 통과하지는 않는다**(3칸으로 어긋뜨려 확인). - **컨테이너·클라이언트 부재.** 원본 에러 대신 안내를 낸다. ## 아키텍처 규칙 - [x] 규칙을 추가·수정하지 않았다 - [ ] 규칙을 추가·수정했고, 일부러 위반하는 코드를 넣어 해당 규칙만 실패하는 것을 확인했다 ArchitectureTest 는 건드리지 않았다. 다만 같은 규율("통과만으로는 증거가 안 된다")을 새 검사에 적용해, 위반을 **양방향으로 주입**해 잡히는지 확인했다(아래 테스트 표). ## 마이그레이션 **해당 없음** — 스키마 변경이 없다. 기존 마이그레이션을 읽기만 한다. ERD 문서를 실제 스키마에 맞춘 것이지 스키마를 바꾼 게 아니다. 어긋나 있던 컬럼 9개는 이미 DB 에 있던 것이고, ERD 쪽을 고쳤다. ## 리뷰 포인트 **자신 없는 곳부터 적는다.** 1. **`erd.html` 검사를 켠 판단** (`scripts/check-erd-drift.sh`) — 팀원 PR 을 막는 대가를 치른다. "한계와 트레이드오프" 1번의 판단이 맞는지 봐 달라. 반대 의견이면 끄는 쪽도 받아들일 수 있다(그 경우 관계선 변경은 검사에서 빠진다). 2. **`scripts/list-migrations.sh` 의 버전 비교** — Flyway `MigrationVersion.compareTo` 를 셸/파이썬으로 옮긴 것이라 원본과 어긋날 여지가 있다. 특히 `_` 구분자 처리. 3. **CI `erd-drift` 잡이 Flyway 없이 SQL 을 직접 먹이는 것** — "최종 스키마 모양만 필요하다" 는 전제가 맞는지. 4. `DocsConfig` 마크다운이 산출물 경로에 강결합돼 있다. 경로를 바꾸면 같이 고쳐야 한다. **리뷰 이력:** 동종 reviewer 1회 + Codex 이종 적대적 리뷰 1회를 거쳤다. author: d8a[bot]
body:
Change evals/run_all.py to stream eval stdout/stderr to temporary files and cap how many bytes are read back (default 100 KiB); add a CLI flag to override the cap and booleans to indicate truncation.

This proposal implements the change approved in decision #74 by modifying evals/run_all.py so the runner no longer captures subprocess output into memory. Instead it directs stdout and stderr to temporary files on disk and reads back at most a configurable number of bytes from each. The default cap is 100*1024 bytes (100 KiB) and an argparse flag --max-output-bytes allows per-run override.

Why it matters:
- Prevents a misbehaving or malicious eval that prints many megabytes from exhausting the runner's process memory and destabilising automated runs or a contributor's local environment.
- Keeps the JSON summary format compatible while making truncation explicit to consumers.

Concrete changes made (files touched):
- evals/run_all.py: added MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES constant; added --max-output-bytes CLI option; changed run_file() to invoke subprocess.Popen with stdout/stderr redirected to tempfile.TemporaryFile(); read back up to the cap and decode with errors='replace'; added stdout_truncated and stderr_truncated booleans to each result; preserved returncode, passed, timed_out, duration_seconds and JSON atomic write behaviour.

Reviewer checklist and how to verify:
- Run evals/runner_eval.py (self-test) and ensure the runner still passes its checks.
- Create a test eval that prints >MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES, run python evals/run_all.py --json-output evals/last_run.json and confirm memory usage does not grow unbounded and last_run.json includes stdout_truncated/stderr_truncated = true and a truncated stdout/stderr string.
- Run a normal short eval and confirm stdout_truncated/stderr_truncated are false and other fields are unchanged.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Uses temporary files (disk I/O) rather than pipes; small performance cost but avoids unbounded RAM use. Logs larger than the cap are truncated; the new flags make truncation discoverable and the cap is adjustable (0 for no limit).

If this passes, the group commits to changing evals/run_all.py so the runner writes eval output to temporary files, enforces a per-eval capture cap (default 100KB) with a --max-output-bytes option, and adds stdout_truncated/stderr_truncated to each result.

author: joshua-jingu-lee
body:
## Summary

`#2461`이 큐 선별의 「타입·area 라벨 판정 → 통과 시에만 `이슈 검증` 게이트」 선후를 확정했으나, `.agent/skills/github-ops.md`의 `/autopilot` 스텝 목록에는 그 한정이 없었다. 문자대로 따르는 오케스트레이터가 라벨 없는 후보에도 `이슈 검증`을 요구해 `autopilot.md` 정본과 갈라진다.

**1파일 1줄**(`+1/-1`)이다.

- 한정 `**타입·area 라벨 판정을 통과한 뒤**`를 주절 앞에 부착
- bare `큐 편입 전` → 정본 어휘 **`구현 큐 편입 전`** — 바로 위 불릿이 2단계 `큐 snapshot`을 가리키는데 라벨 판정은 3단계 집행이라, 무표시로 두면 두 뜻이 인접해 읽힌다
- 선후 정본 포인터 부착

## 범위가 게이트마다 단조 축소됐다

**Gate 0 3사이트 → Gate A a1 2사이트 → a2 1사이트.**

같은 무조건 서술을 담은 다른 표면은 **고치지 않는다.**

| 사이트 | 판정 | 근거 |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/runbooks/01-development-process.md:45` | 명시 제외 | **이미 위임 꼬리가 있고 위임 대상 둘이 모두 한정을 담는다**(`00-issue-management.md:252`·`autopilot.md:141`). 재진술은 동기화 표면만 늘린다 |
| `.agent/agents/issue-reviewer.md:3`·`:13` | 명시 제외 (유계) | 에이전트 레지스트리는 **frontmatter만 노출**하고 본문은 **호출 결정 이후** 로드된다 — 본문 한정이 결정 지점에 닿지 않는다. 호출 조건은 `autopilot.md:141`이 소유 |
| `01-development-process.md:30` · `02-agent-structure.md:76` · `D-019:14` | 명시 제외 | 「구현 착수 전」 상대 서술이라 무조건이어도 참 |

**위임 절이 없는 것은 이 한 줄뿐이다.**

## Test Plan

docs-only. 회귀 락 L1~L6 `RC=0` (`docs/temp/`, gitignore).

- **L1** 변경 파일 1건 + **변경량 floor+cap**(추가 1 / 삭제 1)
- **L2** 대상 줄이 **기대 문면과 바이트 등가** — 극성·술어·어휘·포인터·배치가 한 판정에
- **L3** 지목 절이 **실재·유일**하고 **선후 규범을 실제로 포함**
- **L4** 규범 본문 복제 0 + #2514 축 불가침(추가·삭제 양쪽 전체 diff)
- **L5·L6** 대조군 — 선후 정본 3줄 불변 + 명시 제외 파일 무변경 / 생성 산출물 3종

**반례 실측**: 반대 극성 3종 · 술어 무력화 · 깨진 포인터 · 대상 줄 삭제 · **같은 파일 다른 줄에 무조건 서술 추가** → 전부 FAIL.

생성 산출물 3종 `--check` PASS. `.github/`에 `.agent/`를 읽는 스텝이 없어 CI 무영향(실측).

## Gate A 이력 — 4라운드

| attempt | findings | 축 |
|---|---|---|
| a1 | 11 | Gate 0의 3사이트 판정 둘을 뒤집음 |
| a2 | 13 | `01-dev:45` 편집이 애초에 불필요 → 1사이트 |
| a3 | 9 | 실질 판정 통과. **내 락 수정 3건이 전부 새 구멍** |
| **a4** | 13 | **머지되는 바이트에 대한 blocking 결함 0건 — 「브랜치는 그대로 머지 가능하다」** |

a4의 13건은 폐기되는 락의 한계 3 · 이슈 본문 거짓 서술 4(정정함) · 산출물 **관행** 축 4(→ **#2516**) · 논증/증거 2다.

**관행 축 4건을 지금 고치지 않은 이유**: 넷 다 「그 줄을 따르는 행위자의 판정을 바꾸지 않는」 표기 문제이고, 이 이슈에서 **「고치면 옆에 구멍」이 4연속 재현**됐다(줄 안 → 같은 파일 다른 줄 → 줄의 위치). 소유를 #2516으로 옮긴다.

Closes #2490
