## Resumen de cambios generados por la auditoría de seguridad de GPT-6-Astra

Este pull request aplica las correcciones identificadas en la auditoría de seguridad para los endpoints proxy y utilidades de URL en el visor minero:

### 1. \pp/utils/planchaUrl.js\
- **Control estricto de dominios**: Restringe los dominios permitidos a \sgc.gov.co\ y \gov.co\ comparando etiquetas de host completas.
- **Saneamiento de URL**: Límite de longitud máxima de 8192 caracteres, eliminación automática de credenciales de usuario (\user:pass@\) y fragmentos (\#hash\).
- **Validación de esquema y extensión**: Permite únicamente \http:\ y \https:\ que terminen en \.pdf\.

### 2. \pp/api/sgc/route.js\
- **Protección contra DoS por parámetros**:
  - \ box\: Valida coordenadas finitas y verifica que \minX < maxX\ y \minY < maxY\.
  - \	am\: Valida enteros seguros, rango por eje (máximo 4096 px) y límite acumulado de píxeles (\ncho * alto <= MAX_PIXELES\).
  - \sub\: Límite de longitud, enteros seguros y máximo 256 subcapas.
- **Prevención XSS/MIME-sniffing**:
  - Excluye activamente tipos como SVG o respuestas HTML/JSON enmascaradas como imágenes, permitiendo únicamente formatos ráster seguros (\png\, \jpeg\, \webp\, \gif\).
  - Añade cabecera de seguridad \X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff\.
- **Propagación de cancelación**:
  - Si el cliente interrumpe o cancela la conexión, la señal de aborto se propaga inmediatamente a la petición aguas arriba hacia el SGC.

### 3. \pp/api/plancha/route.js\
- **Control de tamaño y límites de transferencia**:
  - Límite máximo estricto de descarga de 120 MB (\MAXIMO_BYTES\).
- **Verificación de tipo de contenido**:
  - Detección y rechazo de respuestas de error disfrazadas de documentos válidos (\html|json|xml\).
- **Cabeceras de protección**:
  - Añade cabecera de seguridad \X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff\.
- **Propagación de señal y timeout**:
  - Control de tiempo de espera (50 s) y propagación de desconexión del cliente.

---
### Verificación
- **Pruebas unitarias**: \
pm test\ pasó al 100% (52 suites de prueba, 725 pruebas pasadas).
- **Compilación de producción**: \
pm run build\ compiló exitosamente sin errores.

body:
## Related issue

Part of #6496

## Summary

- Native Codex terminal creation and background-title preparation called a synchronous launch builder on the runner event loop. SDK initialization can block on DNS/auth before the later model-listing timeout applies. Run both builder calls with `asyncio.to_thread()` so the runner remains responsive during that wait; short comments explain the boundary.
- Preserve model resolution, legacy/bare ID translation, default selection, profile validation, and authentication unchanged. The earlier model-discovery bypasses have been removed: the resolver and its original tests are identical to the PR base.

ELI5: a slow launch can wait without stopping the runner's other work. This changes where preparation runs, not which model or credentials it selects.

~~~text
async terminal/title preparation
  -> await worker: unchanged launch builder
       -> existing profile/auth/model resolution
  -> native process startup

runner event loop keeps handling traffic during the builder wait
~~~

## Test Plan

- Real-caller/real-builder regressions prove another coroutine can release a blocked builder dependency. These failed before the offloads. Background-title coverage also checks cancellation during preparation and temporary-directory cleanup.
- Restored model/provider suites, including legacy-ID resolution: **132 passed**.

~~~bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_codex_native_app_server.py tests/test_databricks_model_discovery.py tests/test_native_codex_provider.py
~~~

- Codex terminal/title suites: **27 passed**.

~~~bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/runner/test_app_sessions_native_terminals_runtime.py tests/runner/test_background_session_title.py -k codex
~~~

- Staged pre-commit checks: **passed**, including Pyrefly, Ruff, and test-quality checks. Worktree-local SDK import paths were supplied through `PYTHONPATH`; no checks were disabled.
- Verified an empty diff against the PR base for `omnigent/codex_native_app_server.py` and `tests/test_codex_native_app_server.py`.

Suggested manual verification (not executed): run `omnidev` from this branch and open its displayed UI. Start a native Codex session and resume an existing session with a previously working saved model ID. Confirm model selection is unchanged and that the Files panel and an existing conversation remain responsive while startup/title preparation runs. The deterministic blocked-dependency tests cover the slow-lookup case without changing real DNS or credentials.

## Demo

- [ ] Visual demo attached below
- [x] Non-visual evidence provided below or in Test Plan
- [ ] Not applicable — no behavioral change

N/A — non-visual backend change; reproducible regression evidence is in Test Plan.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] UI / frontend change
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

## Test coverage

- [x] Unit tests added / updated
- [ ] Integration tests added / updated
- [ ] E2E tests added / updated
- [ ] Manual verification completed
- [x] Existing tests cover this change
- [ ] Not applicable

## Coverage notes

This is an event-loop responsiveness fix, not a complete startup-latency fix. It does not shorten the lookup, impose a preparation deadline, terminate a worker when its awaiter is cancelled, or change server/tunnel cancellation behavior. Those remain follow-up work, so the linked issue stays open.

The builder only prepares configuration; native process startup remains after the await. Existing model compatibility and authentication behavior are unchanged. No live provider requests or credential changes were needed for validation.

During the broader investigation, three unrelated Pi SDK session tests returned HTTP 400; those failures also reproduced with unchanged production modules. The 159 targeted checks above pass.

## Changelog

Slow native Codex launch preparation no longer blocks the runner's event loop; existing model selection and authentication are unchanged.

## Why

#27 made the vault end‑to‑end encrypted for listing, adding and deleting; tapping an item still did nothing. This completes the read path.

## What

- **Repository** — `download(item)`: key from `AccessKeyStore` (no key → the item is sealed on this device; nothing is fetched), `GetDownloadUrl(media_id)`, GET the ciphertext, open the AES‑GCM blob. Tampered bytes surface as `VaultException`. `BlobStore` gains `get`.
- **UI** — `VaultViewModel.openItem` emits the decrypted bytes; the screen writes them under the app's private cache and starts `ACTION_VIEW` through a new read‑only `FileProvider` (`${applicationId}.fileprovider`, cache path `vault/`) with a per‑URI grant. Missing viewer, failed open, and add/delete outcomes show in a snackbar. Cards are now tappable.

The plaintext exists only in the app sandbox cache while being viewed; nothing leaves the device unencrypted.

## Verification

- Whole project: `testDebugUnitTest ktlintCheck detekt lintDebug` clean.
- New tests: download decrypts under the stored key and fetches by media id; a sealed item fetches nothing and a tampered blob fails; view model emits bytes and reports failures.
- Not exercised against object storage from here.

body: ## Summary - Hot reload now applies an added method even when the call reaches it through a compiled type that was not passed to this reload. - When a declared return or parameter type cannot be resolved, the skip reason says so instead of calling the type invisible. ## User Impact - Before: a call such as `holder.Host.Added()` failed with a missing-member compile error if `holder`'s type was not in the reload, even though `Added` was declared in another file of the same reload. Skip reasons for a missing type also said the type was not visible from an external assembly. - After: that call binds and the patched method runs. An unresolved type is reported as unresolved (missing using, typo, or not compiled yet) and still needs `uloop compile`. ## Changes - When `GetSymbolInfo` cannot bind an added-method call, look it up by receiver type name, method name, and argument count. - Qualify a compiled outer call that stayed unbound for the same reason (error-typed argument). - Treat `TypeKind.Error` on a method signature as unresolved, not as a visibility failure. ## Verification - `dist/darwin-arm64/uloop run-tests --filter-type regex --filter-value 'TransformWorkerCrossFileTests|HotReloadCrossFileE2ETests' --project-path "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` → `"FailedCount": 0`, `"PassedCount": 16` - `dist/darwin-arm64/uloop run-tests --filter-type regex --filter-value 'TransformWorker' --project-path "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` → `"FailedCount": 0`, `"PassedCount": 194` - `dist/darwin-arm64/uloop run-tests --filter-type class --filter-value TransformWorkerAddedMemberTests --project-path "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` → `"FailedCount": 0`, `"PassedCount": 48` - `dist/darwin-arm64/uloop run-tests --filter-type regex --filter-value 'HotReload|TransformWorker' --timeout-seconds 1200 --project-path "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` → `"FailedCount": 0`, `"PassedCount": 721` - `scripts/check-file-length.sh` → no files exceeded the limit - `scripts/check-code-complexity.sh` → 0 issues - `cd cli/release-automation && go run ./cmd/check-skill-size --root "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` → exit 0 - Rebased onto `origin/main` (`66ab19c3a`, #2611) with no conflicts

## 1. 相場との比較で「割安さ」を点数化する（課題#49・取得まで）

### ⚠⚠ 自DBから相場は作れないと実測で分かった

当初の計画は「`t_listings` を市区×間取りで集計して中央値を相場とする」でしたが、**実測で否定されました**。

| 帯 | セル | **中央値 ÷ MUST上限** の中央 | 0.90以上（上限に張り付き） |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 東京23区賃貸 | 66 | **0.93** | **68.2%** |
| 近郊60分圏賃貸 | 183 | **0.93** | **66.1%** |

⚠ MUST 1段目を通った掲載しか残らないため賃料上限で右側が切断されており、**自DB中央値は「実勢相場」ではなく「MUST上限の93%」をなぞっているだけ**でした。しかも切断の度合いは**セルごとにバラつきます**（足立区で実勢比 1LDK 75% / 2DK 60%）。一様なら順位への影響は小さいのですが、バラつくと**市区・間取りごとにものさしの目盛りが変わります**。

### 実装

| 区分 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| パーサ | `market/soba.py`。⚠ 同じ間取りが2回出たら例外（マンション用とアパート用の表が同居したとき、どちらを採ったか分からないまま値が入るのを防ぐ） |
| スキーマ | `m_market_rates`（手書きマイグレーション）。⚠ **縦持ち**なので売買の㎡単価は行の追加で足せる |
| 生成 | `scripts/tools/build_market_rates.py`。⚠ 原典HTMLは **Git 外**、生成物のCSVは **Git 管理下**（ハザードと同じ形） |
| 同期 | CLI `sync-market-rates`。値域（1万〜200万円）と間取りの正規化を読み込みの段で検証 |

### 実測

- robots.txt で `/chintai/soba/` は**許可**・`Crawl-delay` なし
- 都県索引の JSON から**市区スラグと JIS の対応が4リクエストで採れた**（HOMES・ATHOME で苦労した工程）
- **82市区すべて取得成功（失敗0）・991行を投入**
- `rent_total ÷ 相場`: 中央 **0.54** / 幅 0.12〜1.81（判別力あり）。⚠ **1.0 を中心に best/worst を置いてはいけない**

### ⚠ 残る論点（課題#49 に記録済み）

- **2DK の相場が 82市区中56市区にしかない**。相場ページが「賃貸マンション」限定で、2DK はアパートに多い間取りのため。⚠ **DB 最多の間取り（9,387件）**なので影響が大きい
- 相場の定義（管理費込みか・平均か中央値か）が**ページに書かれていない**
- 建物種別が DB の **22%** しか分からず、マンション相場をアパートにも当てるしかない

## 2. 一覧0件バックストップの偽陽性（課題#45 の続き）

⚠ HOMES は市区ローテーション（1回5リクエスト上限）で、**予算切れになると全市区が0件になるのが正常**です。それを「異常の疑い」として2時間ごとに通知していました（実測 2026-09-05 14:13）。ローテーションサイトを対象から外しました。

## 検証

- **988テスト緑**／`ruff check src/ tests/` 通過
- マイグレーションは本番・テスト両DBへ適用済み

author: prasadthx
body:
## What

`twiggy` attributed **152,571 B — 21.8% of the eager artifact** — to `regex_automata` / `regex_syntax`. The two largest single symbols in the whole wasm were the regex `Builder` (40,465 B) and `DynamicCatalog::resolve` (40,306 B).

Nobody had looked at it. This workstream had been sizing the four signer exports at 92,434 B while a dependency worth **twice that** sat in the eager path.

## Why it was removable

All 37 catalogue patterns share **one shape** — `{{$name}}` or `{{$name:arg}}` — and `catalog.rs` already spelled that shape out, as the catch-all it used for the unresolved-variable warning:

```
\{\{\$([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?::[^}]*)?\}\}
```

The grammar was not a new invention; it was already written down. A ~70-line scanner recognises it and a `match` on the name replaces all 37 patterns. `resolver.rs`'s `{{var}}` pattern went the same way, so the crate no longer depends on `regex` at all.

## Measured

| | raw | brotli | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| before this workstream | 606,318 | ~193 KB | 93,682 |
| after TR-433 (`unicode-perl`) | 573,412 | 178 KB | 126,588 |
| **after this PR** | **301,732** | **100 KB** | **398,268** |

**A 50.2% reduction from where this started.** CONVENTIONS.md records KP-209's ≥150 KB headroom target as unmet and *"blocked on tropel splitting the OAuth builders out of the eager crate"* — it is now met by a factor of 2.6 **with no split**.

## Incidental win

`resolve` walked the whole input **once per variable kind** — 44 sequential passes, each with a `contains` pre-check, whether or not that kind was present. One scan replaces all of it. The crate's test suite went from **13.3 s → 3.3 s**.

## Risk — this is a rewrite, not a refactor

Stating that plainly: 37 behaviour-bearing patterns were replaced. Four new tests cover the grammar edges a hand-written scanner is most likely to get wrong:

| Edge | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `{{$randomInt:abc}}` | a known name with a non-numeric arg must still be **recognised as a token** so it warns once and stays literal — what the old `(?::[^}]*)?` catch-all did |
| `{{$guid:5}}` | an argument on a no-argument variable matches nothing |
| `{{$guid`, `{{$}}`, `{{$9bad}}` | malformed tokens are left alone, not allowed to consume the rest of the input |
| `🎉{{$randomInt}}日本語{{$guid}}—مرحبا` | byte offsets must never split a codepoint — that is a **panic in production on any non-English payload** |
| two `{{$guid}}` in one input | each occurrence gets a **fresh** value; a scanner that computed once and reused would silently break load fixtures |
| `{{$randomString:99999…}}` | the `MAX_DYNAMIC_LENGTH` clamp that backlog line 162 added after an unbounded parse attempted a ~10 GB allocation and aborted the process |
| every `PREDEFINED_VARIABLE_META` entry + all ten W2 #199 aliases | a dropped `match` arm would otherwise surface as a literal `{{$…}}` on the wire, not a test failure |

Existing coverage held unchanged: **46 tests**, plus the core-wasm smoke test (38 catalogue variables, resolution corpus **16/16**, all three escape modes).

## What this retires

The plan's F9 conclusion — ship the signers in a separate lazily-loaded wasm artifact — is **no longer forced**. With 398,268 B of headroom the four signer exports (92,434 B) fit with ~306 KB to spare. The lazy seam in knockport's `packages/core/src/oauth-wasm.ts` is still the right *shape* for a future split, but it is no longer a prerequisite.

## Docs

`packages/core-wasm/README.md`'s generated Size line is rewritten by `build.sh`, as designed.

Processed `recentSaleExport_20260905153209.csv` into **Eastern Suburbs - Sold Properties 2026.xlsx**.

## Export summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows in export (cumulative since 1 Jan 2026) | 201 |
| Already present in the workbook — skipped | 188 |
| Genuinely new — added | **13** |

## New rows by sheet

| Sheet | Rows | Month block |
|---|---|---|
| Bellevue Hill UNIT | 2 | September — new header |
| Darling Point UNIT | 2 | September — new header |
| Potts Point UNIT | 3 | September — new header |
| Bondi UNIT | 1 | September — new header |
| Maroubra - HOUSE | 1 | September — new header |
| Maroubra UNIT | 1 | September — new header |
| Rose Bay UNIT | 1 | September — new header |
| Zetland UNIT | 1 | September — existing header, count 2 → 3 |
| Waterloo UNIT | 1 | August — existing header, count 22 → 23 |

Seven September headers were created, each bold Arial 19pt, fill `#93C47D`, and **merged across A:G**. The merges were re-read from the saved file (and spot-checked in the raw sheet XML) after saving.

Every new row is Arial 19pt, address in `#4285F4`, Sale Price and Rate PM2 carrying the `"$"#,##0` format, size taken from land size for Houses and internal size for Units, and Rate PM2 written as a `=Bn/Fn` formula. No export column contained a URL, so no hyperlinks were added.

## Repairs to the previous run's output

The previous run merged A:G onto the data row *above* each new month header instead of onto the header itself. That left headers unmerged and, because merging clears the covered cells, wiped columns B:G of the rows it merged. This PR fixes both:

- **10 month headers merged** that had been left unmerged — Randwick UNIT 212, Darling Point UNIT 56, Potts Point UNIT 118, Maroubra UNIT 130, Bellevue Hill HOUSE 40, Rose Bay UNIT 63, Point Piper HOUSE 4, Waterloo UNIT 179, Zetland UNIT 177, Waterloo HOUSE 2.
- **7 data rows restored** from the export data — 122A Avoca Street, 70/13 Thornton Street, 103/24-30 Springfield Avenue, 2/43 Bond Street, 11 Trahlee Road, 10/39 Dover Road, 328/349 George Street.

## Judgement calls worth a look

- **Rate PM2 left blank when size is missing.** Three added rows have a sale price but no internal size in the export (12/9 Goomerah Crescent, 5/36B Fairfax Road, C309/5 Hunter Street). A `=Bn/Fn` formula there would render `#DIV/0!`, so the cell is blank with the `"$"#,##0` format applied.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem

On the **Patch Selection Menu**, the highlighted patch's description went **beyond the display** — it was painted over the box's bottom border and chopped off mid-word at the screen edge.

### Root cause

`dialog` always draws the highlighted item's description (via `--item-help`) on the **very last line of the terminal** (`dlg_item_help()` does `wmove(stdscr, LINES - 1, 0)`). The patches list was opened with auto full-screen sizing (`-1 -1 0`), so the box grew down to exactly that line — its bottom border landed on the same row where descriptions are drawn. Descriptions longer than the screen width were also cut off at the edge with no truncation marker.

## Fix

In `modules/json/patches.sh`:

1. **Reserve the last screen line for the description.** Size the checklist explicitly from `tput lines`/`tput cols` so the box ends one line above the bottom and the description gets its own clean line below the box. This matches how every other `--item-help` menu in the app (`Custom_keystore.sh`, `Bundle_Parser.sh`, `import.sh`) is already sized — the patches list was the only one using full-screen `-1 -1 0`.
2. **Trim descriptions to the screen width** in the jq query (with a `...` suffix) so the help line always fits; dialog's own edge-truncation remains as a backstop.
3. Safe fallbacks: `tput` failure → 24×80, and minimums for box height / list height / description length on tiny screens.

## Verification

Reproduced and verified with a locally built `dialog` (1.3) driving the **real** `managePatches` function end-to-end on rendered terminal captures:

- ✅ 24×60 (phone portrait): description on its own line, borders intact — before/after captures confirmed the fix
- ✅ Bottom of a 30-patch list (the reported case): clean description line with scrollbar
- ✅ Narrow 24×40, wide 30×100
- ✅ Done / Recommended / Enable All / Disable All button flows — valid JSON written, options merged with defaults
- ✅ Empty-selection guard still fires and recovers; Back button still returns `TASK=CHOOSE_APP`
- ✅ Tiny screens (10–13 rows): no crash, list auto-shrinks with scrollbar
- ✅ Mid-dialog terminal shrink (rotation) exits cleanly — no `Window too big` error
- ✅ `tput` failure falls back to safe defaults; `bash -n` clean on all repo scripts

author: martialcayre-sketch
body:
Arbitrage rendu en session le 2026-09-05. C'est la **première case du Done du
LOT-02** — la décision précède le code, et elle ouvre le lot.

## Le fait qui a structuré la décision

Le cadrage du lot disait : « selon la forme retenue, une migration additive
**peut** être nécessaire ». C'est faux, et c'est ce qui a déplacé la question.

`cb_resultat_bio_patient_analyte_idx` est un index **UNIQUE** sur
`(id_patient, analyte_code, preleve_le)`. Or corriger une valeur, c'est écrire
une seconde ligne sur **exactement cette clé**. Le patron maison — nouvelle
ligne chaînée, au moins **dix chaînes `supersedes_*`** au schéma — est donc
*structurellement interdit* sur cette table. La migration n'est pas
« peut-être », elle est certaine ; et elle n'est pas additive : elle
**remplace un index unique existant**.

Second fait, qui a éliminé la forme évidente : le 409 `doublon_mesure` est un
rattrapage de **`P2002`** ([route.ts:221](web/src/app/api/praticien/biologie/resultats/route.ts#L221)).
Rendre l'index simplement non unique — le patron d'`AgendaSommeilNuit` —
**supprimerait en silence la garde anti-doublon**. `AgendaSommeilNuit` n'avait
aucune garantie base à perdre ; cette table-ci en a une.

## Ce qui est tranché

**1. Régime : nouvelle ligne chaînée, jamais de correction en place.** La
correction en place est écartée comme **dominée** — elle exige de toute façon
des colonnes pour dire qu'une correction a eu lieu (donc la migration est
payée), tout en détruisant la valeur erronée et en rendant une correction
indiscernable d'une saisie neuve. Même coût, moins de garanties.

**2. Forme C — une colonne, un index rendu partiel :**

```sql
ALTER TABLE resultats_biologiques ADD COLUMN supersedes_resultat_id TEXT;

DROP INDEX cb_resultat_bio_patient_analyte_idx;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX cb_resultat_bio_patient_analyte_idx
  ON resultats_biologiques (id_patient, analyte_code, preleve_le)
  WHERE supersedes_resultat_id IS NULL;
```

Une saisie **neuve** porte `NULL` : elle reste soumise à l'unicité, et le 409
`doublon_mesure` est **inchangé**. Une **correction** porte un `supersedes`
non nul et sort de l'index. Une colonne, **aucun `UPDATE`**, append-only
strict intact ; la lecture réutilise l'idiome déjà en place,
`resolveActiveVersion`, qui tranche aussi une fourche de deux corrections
concurrentes par « la plus récente ».

L'autre forme viable — marqueur `remplace_le` + unique partiel dessus — coûte
deux colonnes, un `UPDATE` de la ligne corrigée et la fin de l'append-only
strict, pour rien de plus en échange.

**3. Périmètre V1 : valeur et unité seulement.** Corriger le `analyte_code` ou
le `preleve_le` serait **annuler** une mesure et en saisir une autre — la
suppression reste hors périmètre et n'existera pas sans décision propre.

## Ce qui est nommé d'avance plutôt que découvert plus tard

Une correction qui atterrirait sur une clé `(patient, analyte, date)` déjà
occupée **n'est pas rattrapée par `P2002`** — elle est hors index par
construction. Une vérification applicative est **due au geste de correction**,
et le Done du lot la porte désormais comme un banc à part entière.

## Pourquoi maintenant

`WN_CB_RESULTS_ENABLED` **n'est pas posé** en production et
`resultats_biologiques` compte **0 ligne** (`one-off-7473`, agrégat seul). Un
échange d'index unique sur une table vide est gratuit ; sur une table peuplée
il peut échouer sur les données existantes et exige un plan de reprise. Et une
fois des mesures saisies, le régime de correction devient très coûteux à
changer.

## Le diff

- `docs/DECISIONS.md` — `D-124`, en tête des décisions actives.
- `CAMPAGNE.md` — la question sort des « questions ouvertes », `D-124` entre
  aux décisions qui bornent la campagne, `lot_courant` passe à **LOT-02**.
- Fiche LOT-02 — l'arbitrage d'ouverture devient l'arbitrage **rendu**, avec
  le SQL retenu, les deux formes écartées et leurs motifs ; première case du
  Done cochée, quatre cases neuves ajoutées (migration seule dans sa PR,
  contrat SQL amendé, banc du `P2002` inchangé, banc de la clé occupée).
- `resultats/route.ts` — **commentaire seul** : l'arbitrage est rendu, et
  l'avertissement utile à qui touchera cette route — le 409 `doublon_mesure`
  ne bouge pas.

**Aucune migration dans cette PR**, aucun `schema.prisma` touché, aucune borne
clinique : la correction revalidera la FORME exactement comme la saisie
(`DC-19`/`DC-20` inchangés). Pas de fragment `changelog.d/` — rien de visible
pour l'utilisateur ne change encore.

## Validation

- T1 vert (381 tests).
- `wn-campaign-audit` avec les codes bloquants du CI : exit 0.
- T2 `--fast` lancé sur la branche.

author: tttmmmyyyy
body:
Closes #558

language server は、1 回の診断の中で panic が起きるとその診断スレッドごと終わり、二度と起動しなかった。エディタからは、書きかけのコードを 1 度踏んだあと、どう直して保存しても波線が更新されない状態として見える。復帰の手段はサーバの再起動だけである。

この変更は、panic を 1 回の診断の失敗にとどめる。スレッドは生き続けるので、次の編集は普通に解析される。

## 壊れていた側の運び

エディタが、コンパイラが panic するプログラムを保存する。診断スレッドは `DiagnosticsMessage::Run` を受け取り、打鍵が止まるのを待ってから `run_diagnostics_and_publish` を呼び、その中の `run_diagnostics` が elaboration に入る。

elaboration が panic すると、巻き戻しは `run_diagnostics_and_publish` を抜け、`diagnostics_thread` のループを畳み、スレッドの本体そのものを抜ける。そこを受けるのが `handle_initialized` の `catch_unwind` で、これは **`diagnostics_thread` 全体**を包んでいた。したがって受け取った時点でスレッドは終わっている。

このとき残る状態は次のとおりである。

- スレッド関数が返り、そこが所有していた `Receiver<DiagnosticsMessage>` が drop される。
- 主ループは打鍵のたびに `Run` を送り続ける。送信は receiver が落ちているので毎回失敗し、ログに 1 行ずつ残る。
- 誰も `run_diagnostics` を呼ばないので、`publishDiagnostics` は 1 通も出ない。エディタの波線は、panic の直前に成功したパスのものが残り続ける。

## 直した側の運び

同じ panic は、`run_diagnostics_pass` が `run_diagnostics_and_publish` の呼び出しを包む `catch_unwind` で止まる。分かれるのはこの 1 点で、そこから先の状態はこうなる。

- panic の内容が `.fixlang/fix.log` に書かれる。エディタには何も出ない。解析が失敗したことはそのプログラムについて何も述べないので、利用者に見せる報告としては扱わない。
- `prev_err_paths` は、最後に publish したパスが残したままである。前の波線は画面に残る。
- `$/progress` の end が送られるので、エディタの "Analyzing" の表示は閉じる。
- `run_diagnostics_pass` が返り、ループは `recv` に戻る。

次の打鍵が `Run` を送り、打鍵が止まったところでパスが走る。直したプログラムは elaboration を通り、`send_diagnostics_notification` が新しい誤りを publish して、前のパスが報告したファイルのうち誤りの無くなったものを取り下げる。

## 併せて直したもの

`send_diagnostics_error_message` は削除した。これはコンパイラ自身の失敗を 1 件の診断として組み立て、プロジェクトの**ディレクトリ**の URI へ publish していた関数である。同じファイルの `send_diagnostics_notification` は、span を持たない誤りをディレクトリの URI に出すとエディタが付けられずに落とすので `fixproj.toml` に寄せる、と述べている。つまりこの関数の通知は届いていなかった。この変更で失敗の報告そのものを出さないことにしたので、呼び手がいなくなった。

`MemoryCache` のロックは、ポイズンを中身で開ける形にした。この変更で「panic したパスの次のパスが、同じキャッシュの上で走る」ことが前提になったためである。ロックを持つ区間は `BTreeMap` の操作だけなので、中断された更新が残す不整合はない。

## テスト

3 本。いずれも `cargo test --release` で緑である。

- **`test_the_next_program_is_analyzed_after_a_pass_panics`** (`src/tests/test_lsp/test_diagnostics.rs`) — panic するプログラムを開き、普通の誤りを 1 つ持つプログラムに置き換えて、その誤りの報告が届くことを見る。この変更が無いと、最初のパスの `$/progress` の end が来ないので `Timeout (180s) waiting for progress end count to reach 1` で赤になる。
- **`test_the_reports_of_the_pass_before_a_failing_one_are_taken_back_by_the_next_one`** (同) — 誤りを 1 つ持つプログラム、panic するプログラム、誤りの無いプログラムの順に書き、真ん中で前の波線が残り、最後に取り下げられることを見る。失敗したパスが前の報告を取り下げる形に変えると、真ん中の検査が赤になる。
- **`entries_answer_after_a_thread_panicked_holding_them`** (`src/elaboration/typecheckcache.rs`) — ロックを持ったままスレッドが panic したあとも、キャッシュが panic 前に格納した項目を答えることを見る。`lock_data` を `lock().unwrap()` に戻すと `PoisonError` で赤になる。

パスが失敗したことは、テストからは「そのパスが何も publish しない」ことで見える。case project のプログラムは型変数を 1 つ 2 度宣言しており、panic しなければコンパイラはそれを報告するので、報告が届いたらこのテストはそう言って落ちる。

## 利用者に見えるテキスト

`CHANGELOG.md` に足したエントリ。

> - #558, #567: LSP: A program the compiler answers with a panic — a shape a program passes through while it is being repaired — no longer stops the diagnostics of the session. The language server published nothing on any file for the rest of the session, however the program was repaired afterwards, and restarting it was the only way back. It now analyzes the next program the editor writes, and keeps the diagnostics of the last program it analyzed on screen until then.

## 測ったこと

- `cargo test --release` は、lib の 179 本と bin の 1657 本がすべて通過する。
- 出荷済みの `fix 1.5.0 (f6614b8)` で、BOM で始まるソースを 1 つ開くだけで診断スレッドが死ぬことを確認した (#564)。この変更が入ると、同じソースは 1 回のパスの失敗にとどまり、次の編集から診断が戻る。

項目ごとの役割・変更・目的と、項目に区切った diff は、この pull request のコメントに置いた。

Add a dedicated HMAC-only `GET /api/integrations/commitments-worker/open` that reuses the existing queue reader, returns bounded obligation evidence and record references, and never refreshes fulfillment or changes customer records.

The new `hermes_commitments` identity grants only `commitments_read`. An additive migration expands the audit endpoint CHECK; rollback preserves evidence by refusing while new-lane audit rows exist. Existing worker identities and endpoints retain their behavior.

Also document the installed specialist team and fixed-GET code watcher. The existing watchdog client now identifies its User-Agent: live signed verification showed Cloudflare rejecting Python's default request with 403 and accepting the identified request with 200. ## Summary

Remove the unused `@fastify/jwt` dependency from `apps/api` and let its unused `fast-jwt` subtree disappear from the lockfile.

This PR was rebuilt from the current master rather than carrying the original stale branch history.

- BASE: `f596a2473c204b4972d571f8fce2420d2eb64ed9`
- HEAD: `728286fd6892b47b7832a78be59074271fd016d4`
- Commits ahead of master: 1
- Files changed: 2 (`apps/api/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`)

## Why it is safe

`@fastify/jwt` has no live import/register path in the application. JWT signing/verification is owned by `@exam/auth`, whose implementation uses `jsonwebtoken`.

So this is dependency cleanup, not an authentication implementation change.

## Change

Equivalent package-manager operation:

```bash
pnpm --filter @exam/api remove @fastify/jwt
```

Result:

- remove `@fastify/jwt` from `apps/api/package.json`;
- remove `@fastify/jwt`, `fast-jwt`, and no-longer-referenced transitive nodes from `pnpm-lock.yaml`;
- no source/runtime/auth changes.

## Audit result

The pre-removal production audit showed 3 critical advisories on the dead `apps__api > @fastify/jwt > fast-jwt` path. With that subtree removed, those critical findings disappear. Remaining audit findings are unrelated and outside this PR.

The advisories were not runtime-reachable because the package was never loaded; this PR removes dead vulnerable dependency-tree surface and scanner noise rather than fixing an exploitable auth path.

## Scope

- no dependency upgrades;
- no JWT/auth refactor;
- no work on unrelated audit findings;
- no source-code changes.

Final integration evidence is the CI run attached to the rewritten HEAD.

author: xzawed
body:
Two defects in the same promise, both found by **cross-checking the packaging invariants** during
the code audit — neither shows up as a failing test.

**The count.** `emit_robustness.rs`'s own header said *"the **three** deliverables are staged"*.
The `.lib` arrived in #124 and that sentence did not move.

**The scope.** *"All-or-nothing"* was unqualified in both places it is stated. The rollback is
in-memory state, so it holds against **I/O errors** — a destination that cannot be written, a
rename that fails — and **not against process death**: a kill during the four renames leaves
whatever the OS already committed, a mixed old/new set that nothing here can repair, *because the
code that would repair it is the code that died*.

Closing that needs an on-disk journal, which is out of proportion to a four-file publish. So the
honest move is to **scope the claim, not build the journal** — and not to let a reader take
"all-or-nothing" as crash-safe. Grok named it as the failure mode this design cannot protect
against; #146 had already told users a killed build leaves a staging directory, so the two
statements now agree instead of implying different things.

Comments only — no behaviour change.

| what | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p mlc --test emit_robustness` | 12 passed |
| `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |

author: tak-bro
body:
## Summary

Commands outside the bundled 715-spec set complete empty, and upstream `withfig/autocomplete` has had no commit since 2025-05, so the bundle never grows. This branch closes that gap from both ends: the daemon now counts which commands come back empty, and it fills most of them in by asking the command for its own `--help`.

Measured on this machine before the change: `zeph`, `aic2` and `aicommit2` are among the most-typed commands in shell history and none had a spec. After it, `aicommit2` completes 8 subcommands and 24 options, and `zeph` completes 20 rows, with no user-authored spec file.

## Changes

**Miss tally** (`nerv-engine::misses`) — when completion returns "no spec for X", the daemon records X in `~/Library/Caches/nerv/misses.tsv`, and `nerv doctor` shows the top five as an advisory row. Strictly local: the file lives in the cache dir, has no transmission path, and `nerv uninstall` removes it with the rest of the cache. Writes are throttled to one per five seconds and go through temp+rename, because `record` runs inside the completion the widget is waiting on and `nerv doctor` reads the same file from another process.

**Derived specs** (`nerv-engine::derived`) — a stem no layer has is asked for its own help, and the parsed result is cached in `~/Library/Caches/nerv/derived/`. Layer order is overlay, primary, derived, so a hand-authored spec and the bundled set both win. `[derived] enabled = false` in `nerv.toml` removes the layer and nothing is ever spawned.

The parser is a pure function over text, driven by four real help layouts captured from this machine (`uv`, `aicommit2`, `gh`, `zeph`). Two things it has to get right that are not obvious:

- Telling an entry from a wrapped description line. Some help texts wrap at the same indent as their entries, so indentation cannot separate them; the parser requires a column break after the name, which is what the text conveys visually. Without it `zeph` produced 31 entries, 11 of them sentence fragments.
- Choosing the help source by whether it *parses*, not by whether it looks help-shaped. `ls -h` prints a directory listing, which is long and multi-line and would otherwise be accepted, shadowing the `man ls` fallback that actually works.

**Adaptive generator TTL** — cache entries carry the lifetime their own compute time earned. A generator that outran the keystroke window keeps its result 60 seconds instead of 5. `brew formulae` takes ~600ms to return a list that changes weekly and was being re-run in the background twelve times a minute.

**Visibility** — `nerv doctor` gains `spec misses` and `derived specs` rows; `nerv spec list` marks derived rows `+` beside the overlay `*`. A broken derived file says "delete that file" rather than "reinstall nerv", and the primary row stays green.

**One atomic writer** — rc files, `frecency.tsv`, `misses.tsv` and derived specs all go through `paths::write_atomic`. Consolidating it surfaced two pre-existing defects in `nerv uninstall`: its own temp+rename dropped the rc file's permissions (a `0600 .zshrc` came back `0644`) and could leave a `.nerv-tmp` behind on failure, in the one command specced for zero trace. Both are fixed and tested.

## How to Test

```bash
cargo test --workspace          # 821 passed, 42 ignored
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

End to end against an isolated home directory:

```bash
H=/tmp/nerv-check; rm -rf $H; mkdir -p $H/Library/Caches/nerv/specs
cp crates/nerv-engine/tests/fixtures/specs/git.json $H/Library/Caches/nerv/specs/
HOME=$H ./target/release/nervd &
HOME=$H ./target/release/nerv _complete "aicommit2 " 10   # empty: derivation is deferred
sleep 3
HOME=$H ./target/release/nerv _complete "aicommit2 " 10   # 8 subcommands
HOME=$H ./target/release/nerv _complete "aicommit2 --" 12 # 24 options
HOME=$H ./target/release/nerv doctor                      # derived specs / spec misses rows
```

Verified this way: `zeph` 20 rows, `git` unchanged and never derived, re-entering a command does not re-spawn it (the cached file's mtime is unchanged), `[derived] enabled = false` yields 0 rows and creates no directory, and `nerv uninstall` removes `derived/` with the cache.

## Risks

- **Running the user's commands.** Derivation executes each spec-less command once per daemon lifetime. It goes through no shell, so aliases and rc files cannot change what runs and there is no string to inject into; the binary is resolved to an absolute path by `which`; the environment is cleared apart from `PATH`; stdin is `/dev/null`, the working directory is a temp dir, and each attempt is capped at one second and 256KB. `PATH` is the one inherited variable, because `#!/usr/bin/env <interp>` scripts cannot start without it — the binary is already resolved, so this costs no safety. A command with a side effect on `--help` would still run it; `[derived] enabled = false` is the off switch.
- **Parser accuracy.** The four fixtures are real output from four different help conventions, but a layout none of them covers may parse partially. The structure bar (one subcommand, or three options) is what keeps a bad parse from becoming a spec at all; a partial parse yields fewer completions, never wrong ones for a command that had a spec already.
- **Diff size.** +3100 / −150 across 25 files, of which roughly 1400 lines are tests and captured fixtures. Two new modules and their tests account for most of the rest. The work landed as five independently reviewed feature commits plus a cleanup pass, each with its own regression tests, so the history reads slice by slice.
- **`CLAUDE.md` is gitignored in this repo.** Its §3/§4 records for this feature were updated locally but cannot ride along in the PR. The contract docs under `docs/` carry the same content and did change here.

## Alternatives considered

- **A name list deciding which generators are slow**, rather than measuring compute time. Rejected: the list rots, and it cannot notice a normally fast generator that turns slow on a large repository.
- **`man` first, `--help` second.** Rejected: the commands that actually motivated this are Node CLIs with no man page at all.
- **Derived layer ahead of the bundled set.** Rejected: scraped structure should never outrank a hand-authored overlay or a curated bundled spec.
- **Recording a derivation failure to disk so it is not retried.** Rejected: the in-memory negative entry already stops the retry for the daemon's lifetime, and a file would mean a newly installed tool stays broken until it expired.
- **Generalizing `frecency` and the miss tally into one store.** Deferred: their key shapes differ and the tally adds throttling and a cap, so the shared piece was the atomic writer, which is now one function all four writers use.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo check` / `clippy -D warnings` / `fmt --check` / `test --workspace` green
- [x] Regression test for each fix, each verified to fail when the fix is reverted
- [x] Contract docs updated in the same commits (`spec-conversion-policy` §6.2, `error-states` §3.6.3–3.6.4, `uninstall-spec` §2)
- [x] `nerv uninstall` leaves no trace of the new cache entries
- [x] Workspace version bumped to 0.1.6 — merging to `main` triggers the auto-release

author: hsgwyuki0429-design
body:
## The run

`phase7-real-device-TESTING-2026-09-05T05-40-52-031Z.json` is the first device run on the corrected Phase 5 instruments, and it carries **Phase 5 and Phase 6 both PASSING on the device** in its own transition log.

Phase 7 held at TESTING with IMU-001, 003, 004, 005 and 007 `PENDING`. One number is upstream of all five:

```
handEye: calibrated false, pairs 5 of the 12 needed
mode:    VISION_ONLY on all 3825 frames, fusedFrames 0
imu:     imuAvailable true, imuSamples 9619, measuredImuHz 50.71
```

The chain runs one way: no extrinsic → `noteImuInner` returns before the filter → the EKF is never initialised → `hasImu` is false → no record that needs a fused frame can be evaluated. Nothing downstream is wrong; nothing downstream ran.

## Two things made that undiagnosable from the evidence

**The record blamed the sensor.** `confidenceWithheld` read *IMUConsistency — no IMU is reporting on this run*, in a bundle whose own `sensors` block, `imuAvailable`, `imuSamples` and `measuredImuHz` all say the opposite — and in which IMU-002 is declined *because* the gyroscope is live. The cause was one flag: `hasImu = imuSamples > 0 && main.isInitialised()` meant both "the sensor is delivering" and "the filter is running", and those differ for exactly one reason. `imuReporting` is a separate field now and the withheld term names the extrinsic. Rule 002: the bundle may not contradict itself.

**The bundle could not say which filter took the pairs.** `handEye.ts`'s own doc says `axisPairFrom` is exported *"because the caller counts the rejections by reason: a run that produced hundreds of pairs and used none of them should say which filter took them, not simply report that no estimate exists."* The caller did not. `estimateHandEye` returns a `HandEyeRejections` tally on both branches now — `offered`, plus `tooSmall` / `tooLarge` / `angleDisagrees` / `noAxis` partitioning the rest — and the refusal reason names the dominant filter, so the phone screen carries it rather than only the JSON.

## No threshold moves

`MIN_PAIR_ROTATION_DEG`, `MAX_PAIR_ROTATION_DEG`, `PAIR_ANGLE_TOLERANCE`, `MIN_HAND_EYE_PAIRS` and `AXIS_SPREAD_FLOOR` are untouched, and no pass criterion is touched. This makes a stalled run legible; it does not make it pass.

## The lead the retained samples point at

`pose.gyroscope.recent` keeps 12 comparisons, all from one stretch at anchor ages of 871–1538 ms — the interval length hand-eye uses. Every one fails `PAIR_ANGLE_TOLERANCE`:

| anchor age | visual | gyro net | gyro path |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 871 ms | 10.40° | 2.56° | 3.47° |
| 1004 ms | 10.41° | 2.12° | 6.76° |
| 1201 ms | 12.25° | 5.22° | 10.03° |
| 1538 ms | 15.04° | 6.51° | 12.40° |

The visual rotation is two to three times the gyroscope's net over the same interval, and at 1538 ms it exceeds even the gyroscope's total **path** length — which one motion cannot do. Run-wide the two agree (`agreementRate 0.9025`, median disagreement `0.65°`), so the disagreement is a function of interval length and hand-eye forms its pairs at exactly the length where it is worst.

That is a lead, not a finding — 12 samples from one stretch. The new tally settles it run-wide on the next device run. If `angleDisagrees` is what eats the pairs, the question is Phase 6's anchor-relative rotation over a long anchor age, not how the phone was moved.

## Also on the record

**IMU-002 cannot pass in the same run as IMU-001** — one needs motion permission granted, the other denied. Phase 7 needs two device bundles, the way Phase 1 passed *across two runs covering both permission scenarios*.

## Verification

`npm test` — 893 passed, 4 skipped (28 files). Five new tests cover the tally (each filter counted separately, the four partitioning `offered − pairs`, the tally present on the succeeding branch too, the dominant filter ranked first), plus a regression on the single-axis fixture asserting the withheld term no longer claims the sensor is absent while `imuSamples > 0`.

author: vsbuffalo
body:
A refused PGAS chain names the observation that killed it by its position on the union axis. That position is not a stable identifier — it renumbers whenever the bound stream set changes, so it cannot even be used to compare one ablation against another. The observation-time work makes it worse: an interval stream will contribute two boundaries per row, severing `obs_idx`'s one-to-one correspondence with observations. A diagnostic keyed on `(stream, time)` survives that.

Docs only.

## An adversarial review changed the design in four load-bearing ways

**Dead particles.** `pgas_init.rs:348` scores `*lw = if dead { NEG_INFINITY } else { … }` — a particle killed by a chain-binomial overshoot carries `-inf` without the observation model being consulted, and `fold_into_acc` runs for it anyway. A mixture would have been reported as a unanimous observation refusal, which is the exact confusion the instrument exists to remove. Every field now reduces over live particles only, with `n_dead` beside them.

**The motivating mechanism was wrong.** The first draft repeated gh#752's hypothesis that a modelled flow exceeding an observed specimen count makes a `beta_binomial` impossible. `obs_loglik.rs:541`: `k > n` involves only data, so it is constant across particles and θ cannot cause it. The model-dependent routes are NaN or non-positive shapes. The proposal now carries the guard table and says so.

**Three states, one number.** A hole, a stream on another cadence, and a genuine zero-density row all return `0.0`. The code separates the first two deliberately; a bare `Option<f64>` would have collapsed all three.

**Step 3 already exists.** `WeightCollapse` (`pgas.rs:402`, recorded at `:2683`) already tracks per-sweep collapse in the running filter, including `min_alive` for the near miss. Step 3 extends it rather than adding a third parallel diagnostic.

Also corrected: the claim that this does the observation-time proposal's `reset_due_acc` split (it does not — same index, reordered passes, ten call sites untouched); the anti-enum argument, whose stated premise was false; and the cost framing, since `unconditional_smc_pass` runs once per chain, so the gate is correctness rather than speed.

## Verified before writing

`pgas_init.rs:342-358` (dead branch, fold, reset-inside-closure, collapse check), `obs_loglik.rs:525-548` (the four guards), `pgas.rs:402`/`:2683` (WeightCollapse), `pgas_init.rs:120` (once per chain), `multi_stream_obs.rs:1300-1376` (score_streams, the per-stream sibling, privacy).

author: hyperb1iss
body:
## What this changes

The UI can now mount below an application path while serving bundled assets from a separate prefix. Package assembly creates and verifies every declared asset root. The distro-installed user unit has the correct service identity, and five installer corrections make fresh installation agree with real filesystem, systemd, and daemon behavior.

## Why

Embedded applications need route matching, links, and images to agree on their host paths. The UI previously assumed the origin root in several rendered links and bundled image URLs. A new startup mount carries separate application and asset prefixes; the standalone UI keeps its root defaults. Imperative navigation stays application-relative because Leptos already applies the router base.

Package assembly also had two mismatched contracts. The manifest declared an optional site directory that the producer omitted when empty, and the shell verifier accepted the missing root. The distro-installed user unit identified itself as a system service despite running in the user manager. The producer now creates all declared roots, verification checks their exact file counts, and both shipped user units advertise user-service ownership.

Actual fresh installation exposed one more mismatch: systemd does not return a service-specific `ExecStart` property for a nonexistent unit. The parser now supplies an empty command only for an explicitly not-found unit. Every other required field, loaded-unit identity check, and transactional ownership check remains intact.

The installer also inspected public entries before creating their missing parent directories. Reads now accept absence only through checked ancestor observations. Each present observation retains its directory authority, so a replaced directory cannot silently become the new trusted parent. One observation map owns both state and authority; mutations keep their strict preconditions.

Three later installation checkpoints needed the same producer/consumer alignment:

- Managed icon links now have one validator. Fixed-layout inspection owns their exact targets; the legacy extras walk no longer rejects links created by the current transaction. Unsupported legacy symlinks still fail.
- Systemd may discover a published unit before an explicit reload. The launcher checkpoint accepts that exact inactive candidate, but still rejects foreign paths, commands, enablement, and active processes. Reload and running-process ownership proof remain mandatory.
- Runtime proof now reads the current `/api/v1/system` resource and its nested identity instead of the retired server endpoint. Health, exact version, bounded responses, and process ownership remain required; flat or incomplete identities still fail.

## Verification

- [x] Added or updated tests
- [ ] Added or updated docs (README, AGENTS.md, relevant spec, or guide)
- [ ] `just verify` passes locally (Rust fmt + lint + test)
- [ ] `just deny` passes (required for dependency or license changes)
- [x] `just ui-test` and `just ui-build` pass (required for `crates/hypercolor-ui/`)
- [ ] `just sdk-lint`, `just sdk-check`, and `just sdk-build` pass (required for `sdk/`)
- [ ] `just python-verify` passes (required for `python/`)
- [ ] `just compat-check` passes (required for `data/drivers/vendors/*.toml`)
- [ ] `just docs-build` passes (required for docs or README changes)
- [ ] `cd docs && zola check` passes (required for docs link/content changes)
- [x] Packaging scripts were syntax-checked (required for `scripts/` or `packaging/`)
- [ ] `just e2e-build` passes with the normal Servo stack (required for daemon/UI/effect integration changes)
- [ ] `just e2e-build-cpu` passes when validating the CPU smoke fallback
- [ ] `just e2e` passes against the Servo stack (required for end-to-end behavior changes; starts daemon/browser)
- [x] Tested on real hardware, simulator, or e2e harness (describe below)

The dependency/license, SDK, Python client, compatibility database, and documentation gates do not apply to this diff. The workspace check and standalone UI build pass. The complete local `just verify` and Servo E2E gates have not run for this head.

- The package producer/verifier fixture suite passes five tests, including missing-root, incorrect-count, and wrong-root-type rejection. The unchanged defective archive now fails with the same missing-site-root error as the runtime installer.
- The UI route suite passes eight tests, including mounted preview links with display selection. The display suite passes 21 tests.
- The full standalone UI suite passes 429 tests. The complete native-app suite passes 179 tests, including 53 packaging cases. Two older archive fixtures now include their declared empty roots without weakening their rejection assertions.
- The new shell suite runs in the existing shared CI job. Packaging-only changes now select that job. Actionlint, shell syntax, and scoped diff checks pass.
- The complete CLI suite passes 252 tests. Regressions cover captured absent-unit output, virgin-home creation, replaced parents, managed icon ownership, exact inactive launcher discovery, and the current nested runtime identity. Negative cases retain rejection of missing fields, foreign ownership, unsupported symlinks, and malformed responses. Each installer correction passed independent review and focused execution.
- Actual Ubuntu 24.04 packages pass artifact verification and require at most glibc 2.39. The four-case Debian package proof passes installation and serving-byte checks, restart, crash recovery, and purge. The final tarball installs successfully into two disposable user-service guests with matching archive and executable hashes.
- The final packaged CLI passes seven real-binary updater scenarios: TLS refusal, manifest tampering, artifact tampering, signed installation, installed health, signed rollback, and rollback health. The proof uses disposable signing material and distinct current/previous daemon binaries.
- Independent browser QA passes mounted navigation, deep reload, preview query selection, keyboard navigation, and separate asset loading. A second browser run passes both successful loading and corrupted-manifest refusal.
- Independent review found the remaining Studio preview link and stale service-identity assertion; both corrections passed closure review. The configured cross-family source review found no further production-code defect in the declared scope.

## Notes for reviewers

The small fixture binaries exercise package assembly only; the installation and updater results above use rebuilt native executables. Successful installation does not claim complete downstream journey coverage. The shared Rust check previously reported test-only `unwrap_used` diagnostics. Descriptive test expectations now pass the exact shared Clippy command locally and in hosted CI on `a42dc5151`. Hosted run `33954174819` completed successfully on that exact head, including shared Rust checks/tests, UI, native-app and daemon tests, macOS on both architectures, Windows, and Servo and CPU E2E. Release-only jobs were not selected. The PR is ready for review; no merge, release or production deployment is claimed.

body:
## Problem and verified baseline

Rechecked every requested finding against fresh origin/main `5381be4287a0f60a3a19a77449b6e5b64049756e` (PR #59). All nine findings were still present; none were silently treated as already fixed.

The normal live path returned a readonly connection to the shared write pool. Other failures could mix host/image releases, cross the time window, misreport a committed result as failed, permanently block a match in JSON, or silently miss a window.

## Changes and root causes

1. **Pooled connection state:** rollback and restore readonly=False/autocommit=False before returning a shared app connection; discard it if cleanup fails. The separate GPT read-only mechanism is untouched.
2. **Release consistency:** package the three auto-result scripts in the immutable image (they were excluded by .dockerignore), remove the host scripts bind mount, and verify immutable digest, actual image ID, health and managed release under the existing shared deploy lock. Deployment holds that same lock exclusively through image/control-plane sync and rollback. The nested deployment script reuses its inherited descriptor, avoiding self-deadlock. On the first rollout it also drains the existing managed auto-result cron lock, covering legacy wrappers that do not yet take the deploy lock. Legacy standalone auto-result cron entries are removed by the existing managed-cron installer.
3. **Strict window:** recheck actual time after source lookup, and PostgreSQL clock_timestamp() under the row lock and before commit, including after scoring/notification insertion. Expired work rolls back and uses the final-notice path. The +120…+180 interval is unchanged.
4. **Commit vs notification:** an additive migration stores the operational success notification in the same transaction as the result, points and existing user-push rows. File publication happens separately using atomic rename, with pending DB rows retained on failure. No notification error can set save_failed or ask for re-entry of a committed result.
5. **Category selection:** SQL treats NULL/empty/rpl consistently while retaining national_team routing and excluding other categories.
6. **Parser recovery:** HTTP success alone is not healthy. Recovery requires validated parsing, and parser errors remain fail-closed.
7. **Retries:** remove permanent JSON blocks. Each scheduled retry obtains fresh source consensus and row-locked DB eligibility; attempts stop at the same +180 boundary. A lost commit acknowledgement is reported as unknown, never as proof of failed storage. The next selection excludes any result already committed. PostgreSQL transaction advisory locking also covers duplicate invocations outside shell flock.
8. **Liveness:** the existing independent production monitor runs a diagnostic-only mode. It detects a missing recorded check after 12 minutes when a match needs work, and catches missed expired notifications for seven days. It does not alert merely because there are no eligible matches, and ignores pre-enable backlog.
9. **Q42:** store observed reasons in PostgreSQL bound to teams/kickoff/scope identity. Final notices explain source not-found, not-finished, conflicting scores or technical failure. Missing evidence is explicitly unknown, not inferred.

## Safety

- No game/scoring formula or source URL changes.
- Existing PR #59 row identity guards and admin auto-result marker retained.
- Existing scores, including partial scores, or an ineligible status prevent automatic updates.
- FOR UPDATE serializes manual and automatic result writes; a manual result committed during the wait takes priority.
- Result, FINISHED status, points, user-push outbox and operational success notice commit atomically.
- Final notices recheck pending status and identity before requesting manual intervention.
- JSON has no authority over result correctness or retry permission.
- Migration 0005 is additive; existing user push tables are unchanged.

## Validation

Added real PostgreSQL/psycopg2 integration tests using an isolated schema per test and an explicit disposable DSN in the existing CI PostgreSQL service:
- same-backend readonly selection → pool return → FOR UPDATE/UPDATE;
- manual-result lock contention;
- strict DB-time boundary and rollback after scoring crosses the boundary;
- result, score calculation, existing user push and durable notice consistency;
- outbox failure and actual child-process exit immediately after commit;
- next run must not re-finalize a committed match;
- real SQL transaction failure → safe next-run retry;
- lost commit acknowledgement;
- duplicate worker advisory lock;
- empty/NULL/category routing;
- missed-window/liveness detection, honest durable final reasons and identity mutations.

Added shell tests exercising real flock with Docker substituted at the process boundary, plus parser recovery, delayed lookup, final-reason and atomic-publication unit regressions.

Final head: `4c50e3efd155d1aaced2bdb8f0cb63712082d733`.

[Final CI run](https://github.com/mmaximm2017-netizen/football-totalizator/actions/runs/33948473088) completed successfully:
- **954 tests passed, 124 subtests passed, 1 existing optional OCR smoke test skipped.** All newly added PostgreSQL regressions executed; none were skipped in CI.
- Both existing blocking Ruff gates passed. The unchanged advisory full-Ruff step reports 283 findings versus 288 on the baseline; unrelated legacy lint debt was not refactored or hidden.
- Dependency audit: **no known vulnerabilities found** (also checked locally).
- Docker image build passed, including the check that all three auto-result scripts are inside the image.
- Image publication was intentionally skipped for this PR, as configured. No merge or deployment occurred.

The first CI attempt exposed incomplete integration-test setup (the legacy push DDL was missing from the isolated schema) and a percent-sign handling bug in the test SQL helper. The fixture now runs the canonical existing push DDL, and SQL parameter handling is correct. No tests or gates were disabled.

A final chain review covered cron/wrapper, DB selection, fetch/parsing/health, consensus, hard window, row locking/manual priority, atomic scoring/push/commit, durable Telegram publication, JSON loss, safe next-run retry, monitoring and deploy interaction. The independent monitor now reports its own timeout rather than failing silently.

## Remaining operational limits

- Two finished sources must agree within the fixed window. A delayed, unavailable or conflicting source can still require a manual result.
- Telegram publication is at-least-once: a crash after file publication but before its DB acknowledgement can duplicate a notice, never a result.
- The independent monitor shares VPS/cron. A complete VPS/cron outage cannot self-report in real time; catch-up covers seven days after recovery. External monitoring would be needed for that failure mode.
- Losing diagnostic JSON can duplicate health notices, not authorize writes.
- The time predicate is checked immediately before commit; network/commit acknowledgement latency cannot be given a physical wall-clock delivery guarantee.
- After merge/deploy, verify actual live flags, cron/monitor execution and a controlled successful finalization. Web health alone is insufficient evidence.

Operational details: `docs/AUTO_RESULTS_RELIABILITY.md`.

**Do not merge or deploy. This PR is for review after full CI, pending the owner's separate confirmation.**

body:
## Summary

Make the existing BigBlade Verilator platform build and link on macOS without changing Linux behavior.

This adds small ELF32 and endian compatibility headers, Mach-O shared-library and runtime-path flags, Homebrew `argp-standalone` discovery, portable Python and line-reversal commands, and Darwin guards for glibc and `RTLD_DEEPBIND` interfaces. It also restores the Verilator profiling target and splits generated C++ to reduce Clang memory pressure.

The change fixes an existing undefined-behavior bug in `hb_mc_platform_drain`, where an uninitialized packet pointer was dereferenced. The replacement is a stack packet value using the portable DPI type merged in bespoke-silicon-group/bsg_manycore#768.

The HammerBench submodule is pinned to the small-machine support merged in bespoke-silicon-group/hb_hammerbench#101.

## Notable implementation choices

- Existing `.so` filenames remain unchanged on Darwin; the files contain Mach-O dynamic libraries with `@rpath` install names.
- Darwin uses `-dynamiclib -Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup`; Linux retains `-shared`, ELF sonames, and `-ldl`.
- Apple ld is forced to extract one generated DPI export from the static Verilator model archive; that object supplies the complete DPI API.
- `ARGP_CPPFLAGS` and `ARGP_LDFLAGS` remain overridable for non-Homebrew installations.
- Generated C++ output splitting defaults to 10,000 statements and remains configurable.
- Pipeline failure propagation makes simulator crashes fail execution and profiling log targets even when output is piped through `tee`.

## Validation

- Verilator v5.050 elaborated a 492-module 4-by-2 HammerBlade model

## Fix

`d_inverter_1_p`/`d_inverter_2_p`/`d_inverter_3_p` (Balco260/EP2000, registers 50256/50260/50264) were decoded as `UINT16`, despite the official Cassandra register list also documenting them as "uint" - but a live Balco260 with a single active inverter proved otherwise: `d_inverter_total` (already fixed as signed in 0.13.0/release 0.0.36) read exactly -1211W while `d_inverter_1_p` read 64325 at the same instant, which reinterpreted as a signed int16 is *also* exactly -1211 - an exact mathematical match a genuinely unsigned reading could never produce (single active inverter => total must equal that inverter's own reading).

author: pinhead001
body:
The runbooks claimed ~110 commits total and 21 touching `app/`. Both numbers came from a **shallow working clone** — two grafts, and `git log` looks perfectly plausible against one, which is what makes the error easy to miss.

Real history: **174 commits**, **35** touching `app/`.

## Why it matters beyond accuracy

The same shallowness broke the first two Phase 1 pushes with `remote unpack failed: index-pack failed` and `did not receive expected object` — the pack referenced objects past the graft boundary that the remote couldn't resolve. The Phase 1 runbook now tells you to check for `.git/shallow` when the count looks low, and to fix it with a bounded `git fetch --depth=1000` rather than `--unshallow`, which some repo policy hooks reject.

## Also recorded

**Tag pushes need a developer machine.** `git push origin v0.3.0` from a Claude Code web session returns HTTP 403 from GitHub — annotated and lightweight alike — while branch pushes to the same repo succeed and the egress proxy records no denial. That's a credential boundary, not a transient failure, so retrying doesn't help. It's the one step of Phase 1 that can't run from a session, and the runbook now says so.

## Status

Phase 1 is marked **complete** in the runbook header: `main` at `c76a3e6` with all 174 commits, `v0.3.0` tagged and pointing at it.

Docs only — no code, config, or test changes.

body:
Split the two W3 oversized modules (task #2498) and ship the split-audit gate.

## File tree

- ★ `shared/events/contract.py` (1763 → 222) — stable re-export facade: merges `EVENTS` from the two registry shards (`{**_EVENTS_RUNTIME, **_EVENTS_OPS}`, declaration order preserved), keeps every derived view (`TIER_BY_EVENT`, `tier_for`, `category_for_kind`, `telemetry_events`, `lineage_event_names`, `family_events`, `payload_keys`, `_sql_keys`, `*_KEYS`, `registered_payload_keys`, `sql_join`) and re-exports all 67 payload classes + builders + vocabulary.

- `shared/events/system.py` (new, 442) — system/ops payload TypedDicts + `EventSpec`.
- `shared/events/registry.py` (new, 499) — spec builders `_audit`/`_telemetry_audit`/`_telemetry` + the first registry family (`_EVENTS_RUNTIME`).
- `shared/events/registry_ops.py` (new, 372) — the second registry family (`_EVENTS_OPS`).
- ★ `shared/migrations.py` (957 → 665) — keeps `MIGRATIONS_DIR`, baseline constants, schema checks, the mutation lock, cutover, authority assertion, `apply_pending_migrations`, `apply_down`, `rollback_to`.
- `shared/migration_errors.py` (new, 82) — the 9 migration exception classes.
- ★ `shared/migration_layout.py` (new, 260) — layout enumeration/validation (`_git_probe`, `_migration_stem`, `_down_path`, `_tracked_migration_paths`, `_list_migration_files`, `untracked_migration_files`, `validate_migration_layout`, `validate_migrations_at_ref`, `required_migration_set`). Reads `MIGRATIONS_DIR` through a function-level lazy import so existing `monkeypatch.setattr("shared.migrations.MIGRATIONS_DIR", ...)` call sites keep call-time semantics.
- `scripts/audit_split_reexports.py` (new) — three-form reference audit gate (from-import / attribute access / monkeypatch string targets, `hasattr`-verified), the W1 QA BLOCK lesson (missed `UNANCHORED_DB_SENTINEL` re-export in PR #1729).
- `scripts/lint_code_structure.py` — drop the two stale `_OVERSIZE_ALLOWED` entries.

## Data flow

Event contract: payload TypedDicts define each event's attribute shape; `EventSpec` binds name × category × tier × payload × destination × family × retention; the two registry shards declare one `EventSpec` per event name; `contract.EVENTS` merges them in declaration order and the derived views (`tier_for`, `family_events`, `payload_keys`, SQL-key constants) fold from it. `shared/events/registry.md` regenerates byte-identical; producers (`shared.telemetry.emit`) and readers (Loki/OTLP/ops panels) keep importing the unchanged `shared.events.contract` surface.

Migrations: `migration_errors` is the leaf exception vocabulary; `migration_layout` owns file enumeration and pre-flight validation and reads the migrations directory lazily (patch-transparent); `shared.migrations` orchestrates schema mutation on top, so every monkeypatch target that existed before (`MIGRATIONS_DIR`, `_schema_mutation_lock`, `apply_down`, `assert_schema_current`, `machine_name`, `checkout_anchored_home`) still resolves on the facade at call time.

## Summary

Durable evidence state, per-shot media categorization, content-fingerprint
duplicate protection, and original/derivative integrity for listing media,
plus two fixes Codex required before this package could be called ready.

- **Durable evidence ledger** (outcome A): a lister marking a guided-evidence
  item "does not exist" (with a required reason) or clearing that mark is
  now saved permanently instead of living only in Studio component state.
  The draft preview route now reads it too, closing a gap
  PKG-LISTING-CREATION-1A's own deferred-contracts doc disclosed.
- **Per-shot photo categorization** (outcome B): a lister can tag each photo
  with which named shot it answers (asset-type specific, all 15 real asset
  types), whether it shows the building or a unit, and current vs.
  illustrative condition.
- **Cross-session duplicate protection** (outcome C): the same file uploaded
  twice, in different sessions, is now recognized and refused rather than
  silently attached twice.
- **Original preservation** (outcome D): the untouched original upload is
  now kept alongside the re-encoded derivative, and the upload route
  actually calls this codebase's existing, previously-uncalled
  `mediaPublishable()` integrity check against it.
- **Evidence-mark invalidation on asset-type change** (Codex finding 1): a
  mark keyed on a shot name shared across asset types with different
  meanings (e.g. "frontage": retail's shopfront vs. showroom's display
  glazing) is now invalidated, not silently carried over, when the asset
  type changes, mirroring the protection outcome B's migration already
  gives `shot_key`, shaped to fit an append-only audit ledger.
- **Public media visibility enforcement** (Codex finding 2): a shared,
  tested rule (`visibility = 'public' AND moderation_state <> 'removed'`)
  is now the one thing every public consumer of listing media applies, with
  a structural test that fails if a future route queries listing media
  without either applying it or being on an explicit, reasoned
  owner-scoped allowlist.

**This is a draft.** Nothing here has been applied to production. The full
production migration plan, exact checksums, schema diff, RLS/security
evidence, rollback procedure, and both Codex findings' full resolution
detail are in
[`docs/pkg-listing-creation-1b-migration-runbook.md`](https://github.com/saleemzeidan123/satmarkets/blob/pkg/listing-creation-1b/docs/pkg-listing-creation-1b-migration-runbook.md).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm test`: 2060/2060 passing.
- `npm run ar-lint`: clean.
- `npm run lint-gate`: ESLint ratchet held at 49 pinned errors, no new rule.
- `npm run build`: clean, exit 0.
- **Isolated-environment testing**: native Supabase branching against the
  real production schema is confirmed broken (recorded in `CLAUDE.md`'s
  blocked-evidence queue) and this environment has no Docker to stand up a
  local Supabase stack (Postgres + PostgREST + GoTrue) either, so no
  schema-dependent journey has been run through this app's own Supabase
  client against a live, migrated backend. As a real substitute, not a
  stand-in claimed to be equivalent: a genuine local Postgres 16 engine
  (`embedded-postgres`, userspace, no Docker/sudo), running a reconstructed
  stand-in schema (the real base schema and RLS helper functions exist only
  in production and are in no local migration file, confirmed by grep),
  applying all five migration files verbatim, passes **53/53** checks:
  idempotent reapplication, RLS policy logic under every access branch
  (owner, a different account, SAT, forged-actor rejection), concurrency on
  both unique indexes, the derivation-shape constraint, the new
  asset-type-change invalidation trigger, and rollback-then-forward-reapply.
  Harness and full raw output are committed
  (`docs/pkg-listing-creation-1b-isolated-test.mjs` /
  `...-output.txt`). This proves the migration SQL itself; it does not
  prove behavior against production's real schema, grants, or RLS function
  bodies, which remains the one gap before the production-migration gate
  can open.
- A Fable-model review of every new Arabic string, the 15 asset types'
  shot lists, and the schema's vocabulary under a Saudi-Arabic-first lens
  is acted on throughout (see the runbook's own section 12/13 for exactly
  what changed and what was deliberately deferred with reasoning).

## What is not yet done, honestly

- **Live, schema-dependent QA** (outcome E) is blocked by the same
  environment limitation named above: no reachable isolated Supabase-API
  backend to point a preview or Playwright at. Once this PR's own Vercel
  preview exists, build and schema-independent checks (visual layout,

- Full moderation enforcement (acting on `flagged`, a real review workflow)

author: jichu4n
body:
`CPUFetchNextInstruction()` opened every decode by zeroing the whole 12-byte `Instruction`. Most of that is written again immediately, so the decode now settles each field where it becomes known instead:

- `opcode`, `size` and `immediate_size` are assigned on every path that returns success
- `has_mod_rm` and `displacement_size` in **both arms** of the ModR/M branch
- `mod_rm` is read only where `has_mod_rm` is set
- `displacement[]` and `immediate[]` are read no further than their size fields say

Only the two prefix fields are cleared before the decode starts, since `ApplyPrefixByte()` writes them only where a prefix is actually present.

## Measured

400MHz, `dos-boot`, against master `cba32ee`. Noise floor is 0.0065%.

| level | master | this | gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-O3` | 7.1220 | **6.7926** | **4.63%** |
| `-O2` | 7.8267 | **7.5169** | **3.96%** |
| `-Os` | 9.4612 | **9.2380** | **2.36%** |

**The invariant is unchanged at every level and every clock: 27,701,507 emulated cycles and 2,328,015 retired instructions.**

## The one fact that decides this

`has_mod_rm`, `displacement_size` and `immediate_size` share a byte with two bits of padding the compiler must preserve, so **every write to any of them is a read-modify-write of the whole byte, never a store.** What matters is how many of those a decode performs — not how many fields it writes. Naming more or fewer bitfields in a single write is free: it changes the mask immediate and nothing else, `movs r2, #63` against `movs r2, #7`.

Clearing the pair up front is a read-modify-write every instruction pays, and the ModR/M arm then pays a second to set them. Writing them in both arms costs one either way, because GCC coalesces the pair:

```
else arm:  ldrb / bics / strb          ; has_mod_rm = 0, displacement_size = 0
if arm:    ldrb / bics / orrs / strb   ; has_mod_rm = 1, displacement_size = N
```

## Rearrangements that lose

All built and measured on hardware, all recorded in AGENTS.md so they are not rediscovered:

- **`has_mod_rm = metadata->has_modrm`**, which always carries the same value, dropping both the clear and the `= true`: **0.99% slower**. It adds a read-modify-write on every instruction, where the branch only pays on the roughly half that carry a ModR/M byte.
- **Writing all three bitfields once at the end of the decode**: **0.81% slower**, for 32 bytes *less* code.
- **Clearing `immediate_size` with the other two**: neutral, and dead — it is assigned unconditionally further down.

## The ModR/M REG field

`GetImmediateSize()` consults it whether or not the instruction carries a ModR/M byte. Only `0xF6` and `0xF7` actually look at it and both do carry one, so the value was never *used* — but it still has to be *defined*. It is kept in a local initialized to 0, which is cheaper than either alternative: a ternary on `has_mod_rm` puts a branch on the hot path, clearing `mod_rm` puts back a store, and the local costs neither while also removing a load.

## Testing

938 tests pass, including the full 8088 hardware suite.

The change rests on a reused destination keeping nothing of the instruction before it — the ordinary case, since `CPUTick()` holds one `Instruction` for the life of the CPU. `ADecodeKeepsNothingOfThePreviousInstruction` pins that directly, walking a reused destination through an instruction rich in fields and a bare one, alternating.

The hardware suite catches a dropped clear too, and emphatically — thousands of encodings across most opcodes — but as a diffuse result rather than a named one, which is why the targeted test is worth having.

author: delightech28
body:
## Description
Closes #798.

Implements the **Shielded Private Transaction Note Indexer Service** to support zero-knowledge deposit commitment notes and spent nullifier sets emitted as Soroban contract events on Stellar.

This PR adds:
- Event parsing for `NoteDeposited` and `NullifierSpent` contract events.
- Poseidon-BN254 incremental Merkle tree root history maintenance in PostgreSQL (depth 20).
- Celery range backfill task with exponential retry backoff.
- Low-latency verification REST query endpoints for frontend ZK proof generation.

---

## Key Changes

### 1. Data Models & Alembic Migration
- **ORM Models (`app/models/shielded.py`)**:
  - `ShieldedCommitment`: Stores commitment note hashes, deterministic ascending `leaf_index`, ledger sequence, and `event_hash` dedup key.
  - `SpentNullifier`: Stores nullifier hashes with database-level unique constraint to enforce double-spend prevention.
  - `MerkleRoot`: Stores incremental Poseidon-BN254 roots and 20-level tree frontier state.
- **Migration (`alembic/versions/0006_add_shielded_note_indexer.py`)**: Creates `shielded_commitments`, `spent_nullifiers`, and `merkle_roots` tables with indexes and unique constraints.

### 2. Core Indexing & Merkle Services
- **`app/services/note_parser.py`**:
  - Validates 64-character lowercase hex commitment and nullifier strings (`_validate_hex64`).
  - Deterministically assigns ascending `leaf_index` positions ordered by `(ledger_sequence, index)`.
  - Skips duplicate event hashes and double-spent nullifiers while emitting warnings and incrementing Prometheus metrics.
- **`app/services/merkle_service.py`**:
  - Incremental Poseidon-BN254 Merkle tree construction.
  - Generates 20-element sibling hash inclusion proofs (`compute_merkle_path`) for frontend proof generation.
  - Ensures batch-boundary confluence and idempotence.

### 3. Celery Task & Routing
- **`app/tasks.py`**: Added `index_shielded_notes_range` task with automatic retries on DB errors (up to 3 retries, exponential backoff).
- **`app/celery_app.py`**: Configured `index-shielded-notes` queue and routing key `shielded.index`.

### 4. REST API Endpoints
- **`app/routers/shielded.py`**:
  - `GET /api/v1/shielded/note/{commitment}`: Returns `leaf_index`, `merkle_root`, `merkle_path` (20 sibling hashes), `leaf_count`, and `is_spent` status. Returns `422` on invalid hex format and `404` when not found.
  - `GET /api/v1/shielded/root/latest`: Returns latest Merkle root checkpoint, with optional `at_ledger_sequence` query parameter for point-in-time proof generation. Returns `503` if roots are not yet available.
- **`app/main.py`**: Mounted router under `/api/v1`.

### 5. Testing
- **`tests/test_shielded_indexer.py`**: Unit and property test coverage for ORM models, hex validation, event decoding, deduplication, Merkle hashing, confluence, and FastAPI route registration.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Ran unit tests covering parser validation, deduplication, Poseidon Merkle paths, and router endpoints:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest tests/test_shielded_indexer.py
