author: huyplb
body:
Typing `demo_a.` in the SQL editor opened an **empty popup**. The tables were already loaded — there was just no way to ask for them by schema.

## Why it was empty

The dot handler treated everything before a dot as a table or an alias and offered its **columns**. A schema has none, so it fell through to nothing.

`/schema/load` fetches one schema per connection and names come back bare, so the completion bundle had no schema→tables index. The connection knows its schema name; it just was not carried into the completion context. It is now, and `buildSchemaTries` indexes tables under it — both from that name and from any `schema.table` in the name itself, since both shapes occur depending on dialect.

Schema names are also offered **before** the dot, so this is findable rather than something you must already know. Accepting one inserts the dot and re-triggers the suggest widget, so the table list opens immediately.

## Two things the tests caught that reading would not have

- **The new branch was unreachable.** `extractTableAliases` self-maps a bare table name in FROM, so `aliases[ref]` is truthy for `nowhere.` as well as for a real alias — the existing `(no columns for X)` branch shadowed it entirely. Only a name resolving to a *different* table is an alias, and only that case can honestly say a table is missing its columns.
- **An empty schema looked unloaded**, so the editor told the reader to go load a schema they were already looking at. The schema name is registered before its tables now, so "no tables in demo_b" and "schema not loaded" are different answers.

## Ordering is deliberate

A name that is both a table and a schema keeps its **columns** — that is what `orders.` means in a query, and the schema is still one keystroke away. The schema branch runs only when columns come back empty, so nothing that worked before changes. There is a test for exactly this.

## Verified against the live demo database, not fixtures

```
demo_a.      → categories, coupons, customers, fox_created_table, fox_employees,
               order_coupons, order_items, orders, products,
               v_active_products, v_customer_orders, v_low_stock
demo_a.or    → order_coupons, order_items, orders
demo_a.v_    → v_active_products, v_customer_orders, v_low_stock
```

Covered by a new fake-Monaco harness that drives the real provider — the risk here is ordering, which a trie-only test cannot see, and the provider had no test at all before. Both new suites A/B'd against the previous behaviour.

Gates: 3378 tests, typecheck clean, 0 ESLint errors.

## Known limit

Only schemas that have been **loaded** can be completed, which is the connection's own schema. Completing a schema nobody has opened would need an on-demand fetch (session passwords, async completion, error states) — a bigger change, and the editor now says "schema not loaded" instead of showing an empty list.

author: santaval
body:
## Description

Implements **LASCE-INF-001-017**. `apps/web` had no way to put a file into MinIO: the Python worker owns `readings/*` through `apps/worker/app/clients/storage.py`, but the web side had no counterpart, so no feature needing an upload could be built.

This adds a storage service layer behind an `IAssetStorage` interface, its MinIO implementation, typed errors, unit tests, and the documentation for putting a caller in front of it.

Scope is the **service layer only** — no route handler, Server Action or UI calls it yet, which is deliberate: MinIO is not provisioned in any deployed environment (`docs/deployment.md`, section 10), so a caller could not ship regardless.

## Related Issue

- Issue ID: LASCE-INF-001-017 (#39)
- Group ID: g01

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Tests
- [x] Configuration

## What Was Done?

- **`IAssetStorage` contract** (`app/services/storage/interfaces/`) with six members: `createUpload`, `delete`, `createDownloadUrl`, `bucketExists`, `ensureBucket`, `verifyAsset`. The I-prefix is a deliberate exception to the repo's unprefixed type names, marking the seam a second backend implements.
- **`MinioAssetStorage`** (`app/services/storage/implementations/`) — a server-side `putObject` upload, presigned GET downloads, and bucket creation on first use, mirroring the worker's `ensure_bucket()`.
- **Validation before the backend is touched.** `verifyAsset` enforces a 25 MiB cap and a content-type allowlist, and `createUpload` calls it first, so an invalid file never reaches MinIO.
- **Typed errors** extending a new `BaseError` (`app/errors/`), each carrying an HTTP status and an error code so a future route handler can map them onto a response: `InvalidFileSizeError` (413), `InvalidFileTypeError` (415), `InvalidServiceConfigurationError` (500).
- **A barrel at `app/services/storage/index.ts`.** `container.ts` and both error classes already imported from it, but it did not exist — the module failed `tsc` with three `TS2307`s until this was added.
- **15 unit tests** at `apps/web/tests/unit/services/storage/MinioAssetStorage.test.ts`, mocking the `minio` SDK at the module boundary. `vitest.config.ts` gained `tests/unit/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` in its `include`; Playwright's specs are `*.spec.ts`, so the two suites still cannot pick up each other's files.
- **Configuration:** `MINIO_*` added to the `web` service in `infra/docker/docker-compose.yml` and as `preserve()` entries in `.railway/railway.ts`; `MINIO_DEFAULT_BUCKET` added to `.env.example` and the `packages/config` schema; `minio` added to `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.ts`.
- **Documentation:** `docs/manage-assets.md` written for the service as built; `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/deployment.md` and `docs/tests/component_testing.md` corrected where they described this service, plus a new "Service tests" section in the testing guide.

## Testing

`pnpm --filter @lasce/web typecheck`, `test:unit` (24 tests, 3 files) and `pnpm run format:check` pass locally. `MinioAsssetStorage.ts` is at 100% statements, lines and functions; 91.3% branches.

The service is verified by unit tests rather than against a live server, because MinIO is not provisioned anywhere yet. The MinIO SDK is mocked at the module boundary — the class builds its own `Minio.Client` in a no-argument constructor, so there is no injection seam.

**The `test` check on this PR will fail, and it is not a test failure.** See below.

## Additional Notes

**1. `test` fails on a coverage threshold this branch raises.** `vitest.config.ts` moves the `apps/web` floors from 15%/15%/25% to 50%/50%/45%, but the workspace measures **38.5% lines / 39.0% statements**, so `pnpm turbo run test` exits non-zero. The storage tests took the workspace from 11.0% to 38.5%; the remainder is untested pre-existing files — `JobLauncher.tsx` (0%, the largest), `PublicHeader.tsx`, `CreateWidget.tsx`, `Brand.tsx`, `PublicFooter.tsx`, `site.ts` and `container.ts`. Two ways to green it, and this needs a reviewer's call: test `JobLauncher.tsx` in this PR, or set the floor just below the measured figure per the convention in `docs/tests/component_testing.md` and ratchet later. The docs currently record the real number rather than a target.

**2. Known gaps, deliberately not fixed here.** They are recorded in `docs/manage-assets.md#known-gaps` and in #39, and the tests pin *current* behaviour so none of them is hidden. The two that matter before a caller is built:

- **The documented endpoint value does not construct.** `MINIO_ENDPOINT` is passed to MinIO's `endPoint`, which rejects a `host:port` string — `InvalidEndpointError: Invalid endPoint : localhost:9000`, which is what `.env.example` ships, what `packages/config` defaults to, and (as `minio:9000`) what this PR adds to Docker Compose. It is latent only because nothing imports `container.ts`, which instantiates eagerly at module scope.
- **Upload and delete use different buckets.** `createUpload` reads `MINIO_DEFAULT_BUCKET`; `delete` and `createDownloadUrl` read `MINIO_BUCKET`. `.env.example` sets both to `lasce-files`, which masks it.

Also: `delete` implements neither the idempotency nor the prefix guard its own JSDoc promises; `createUpload`'s doc comment describes a presigned POST policy that is not what the code does; object keys are `<timestamp>_<filename>`, unsanitised and with no prefix separating them from the worker's `readings/*`.

**3. Not in this branch.** An unrelated WebDots annotation widget and a Prisma schema reformat are in the working tree but deliberately uncommitted — section 1 asks for one objective per branch.

## Checklist

- [x] The change meets the acceptance criteria.
- [x] The project builds and all tests pass. — `typecheck`, `test:unit` and `format:check` pass; the `test` job fails on the coverage floor described above, not on a failing test.
- [x] I reviewed my own changes.
- [x] I did not include credentials or sensitive information.

body:
## M45 -- `i32`, signedness by kind, narrow returns, `p_cp()`

Spec: `docs/specs/M45.md` (Amendment + Implementation notes). `stage0/` untouched (2848/3000; `git diff origin/main -- stage0/` empty).

**What lands**

- **`i32` registered by the core** through the M24 mechanism -- `type_new("i32", 4, 4, TK_SINT)` in `core_types_init()`, before `user_init()`, at the three process entry points (`src/cli.mc`, `src/driver.mc`, `src/limits.mc`); `type_disable(ty_i32)` removes the word (`examples/avr` does). `TY_MAX` stays 7, `K_U8..K_EXTERN` do not shift, `check-lex` keeps comparing the two lexers.
- **Signedness by kind**: `type_signed(t)` (`TK_SINT`, plus `TY_I64`); `fold_taught`/`fold_cast`/`bin_op`/`const_bin` keyed on kind, so `#define M (i32) 0x80000000` folds to -2147483648 and `INT_MIN / -1` is 2147483648 with no trap.
- **A call returns what it declares** (D5): the walker narrows a call's result AND a function's return value through `MTASK_CAST` when the declared type is narrower than the word -- so `extern i32 f()` reads the low 32 bits sign-extended, whatever the callee left above bit 31. The defect class is real and measured: `atoi`/`strcmp` under musl (both arches) and `strcmp` under glibc x86_64 return `0x00000000ffffffff`, and `clang -O2` on macOS compiles `int f(){return -1;}` to `mov w0, #-1`. `callp` stays `i64`, documented.
- **Machines**: `LDRSB/LDRSH/LDRSW`, `SXTB/SXTH/SXTW` on arm64; `movsx`/`movsxd` on x86-64 (register and memory forms); `examples/kernel`'s riscv64 machine gains the `srai` pair (funct6 column). Contract **version 4**: a machine keyed on the core ids is silently wrong; key on `type_kind`.
- **`c_int()`** (`src/arena.mc`): the seed set's own reading of a C `int` return (the frozen seed cannot spell `i32`, and a `u32` declaration makes `mc1` emit an extension `check-asm` compares against `mc0`) -- used where the compiler tests the sign of `open`/`creat`/`waitpid`. Documented in `docs/reference/language.md` § 6 and `hooks.md`; `scripts/check-docs.sh` now extracts the `c_` prefix.
- **`p_cp()`**: the lexer cursor, public, for a module that records source under substitution (teko/ngen).
- **`p_skip_balanced` false positive fixed**: a region ending exactly at the end of an included file was refused with `region crosses a file boundary` because the frame depth was read AFTER the lookahead `next()` popped the include. The depth is now sampled at the closer; a region that really crosses is still refused, same message, same position. The message had no test before; two `check-surface` cases now.

**Inertness, exactly.** Nothing a program that declares no narrow-returning function emits moves: `check-obj` 32/32 identical to the frozen seed, and `scripts/check-inert.sh` between a `mc1` from `origin/main` and this one is identical on the 33 objects and on `lang`, `conc`, `desktop`, `kernel`, `avr`. The ONE difference is `examples/api`: the `class` sugar in `oop.mc` synthesizes `u8 todo_done(uptr)` for `bool done;`, and D5's narrowing adds `and x9, x9, #255` after the `ldrb` (a no-op on the value; `build/api` still 55632 bytes). That is the design, and the record says so.

**Review**: two findings from the reviewer pass, both fixed in `ff5aecf` (the false `examples/api` inertness claim corrected in the spec and CLAUDE.md; `c_int` documented + gate widened), plus the riscv64 funct7->funct6 rename (kernel image byte-identical) and the `p_skip_balanced` fix.

**Gates** (rebased on e4a4c40): `make bundle` first (78 files, raw 871568 -> LZ 407042, blob 407995 B). `make check` **RC 0, zero FAIL**: `budget` 2848/3000, `test` 32/32, `check-lex`/`check-ast`/`check-asm` 126/126 (2 skipped), `check-obj` **32/32 identical to the frozen seed**, `bootstrap` at a fixed point (`mc2.o == mc3.o`, 941576 B; `--dump-asm` diff mc1/mc2 **empty**), `check-surface` 32/32 + 116 ok lines, `test-exe` 32/32, `check-mc` 11/11, `check-standalone`, `check-parts`, `check-toml` 10/10, `check-build` 53/53, `check-stubs` 9/9, `check-sysroots`, `check-limits` 17/17 under 90%, `check-minimal`, `test-linux` 39/39, `test-linux-x86_64` 36/36, `test-linux-exe` 42/42 musl + 42/42 gnu, `test-linux-x86_64-exe` 39/39 + 39/39 (the M45 corpus and `072-int-return` on both `--exe` legs, both libcs), `test-windows` 40/40, `test-windows-x86_64` 38/38, `check-examples`, `check-lang`, `check-conc`, `check-desktop`, `check-float` (13/13 on the three run legs, 11/11 + 11/11 Windows objects), `check-wide`, `check-kernel` (QEMU 11.0.1, exit 0), `check-avr` (simavr + QEMU), `check-docs` (188 symbols, 22 flags, 20 TOML keys, 10 directives, 48 samples, 287 links), `site` 85 pages + `check-site` 0 link problems. `make check-linux-host` RC 0 on all four cells (musl/gnu x aarch64/x86_64), each with its own `mc2l.o == mc3l.o` and the cross proof (`mc2l --backend=macho src/mc.mc` byte for byte the macOS `build/mc2.o`).

**Goldens** (five, rewritten once, each after its own criterion): `mc2.sha256` `90ce56dcfc6f3c7a785013871b5df9f8ad6ed36ad24acb28256e60385435ee38` (empty `--dump-asm` diff + `cmp mc2.o mc3.o`); `mc2-linux-arm64` `8cb319f2648b2a1eb37dcdc19b46290ca111ad7543482fbd349c6c2bcb415856` and `mc2-linux-x86_64` `c0882f93933469e066ba73f461fe2be4caa13de558d09ba534955b0a80e19b93` (deleted and re-recorded by `make check-linux-host`, matched again by the gnu cells); `mc2-windows-arm64` `2c55021d3a87ebb087165f77d03fbf8d96f58bb6e4cfb428328f05c909382eab` (959407 B) and `mc2-windows-x86_64` `af21fe6f17f6d0ca13554b122536178688284f759b990cc8ebb1ccb336ed947f` (978891 B), cross-computed per `tests/golden/README.md` and written byte for byte by `build/mc2` too.

Consumer: teko/ngen (`extern i32`, `TK_SINT`, `p_cp()`, the boundary fix). Release: minor (0.13.0).

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

`.github/scripts/wsl-bringup-watchdog.ps1` bounds a WSL2 bring-up that wedges a Windows runner past the caps the runner enforces itself. It arms a detached sentry that kills the WSL services, then the step's node trees, then the runner worker. `Test-SentryStale` decides when that sentry stands down, and it read an absent or unreadable `arm-token` file as "a later arm superseded me". `RUNNER_TEMP` sits on the volume a wedged bring-up holds, so a failed read there is the sentry's own fault condition: the watchdog could disarm itself on exactly its input. It now stands down only on a token that reads back different.

```
pwsh -File wsl-bringup-watchdog.ps1 -Mode arm -DeadlineSeconds 8
rm "$RUNNER_TEMP/wsl-bringup-watchdog/arm-token"

before  sentry: stood down, a later arm superseded this token   # no `fired` file, ever
after   sentry: FIRED after 8s with no disarm; stage one starting
```

That flips the posture on an unreadable `RUNNER_TEMP` from stand-down to fire, since `Test-Path $disarmFile` fails silently the same way. It is the error a watchdog should prefer: a wrong kill costs one job, and a wrong stand-down cost 45 minutes of a runner and a frozen merge queue. The diff also drops the disarm's `Remove-Item` on the token, which under the new rule stands nothing down, and a comment whose remove/write hazard the same rule removes.

I have not proved this caused job 101251991654, which held `Set up WSL2 (Ubuntu)` for 44 minutes against a 5-minute step cap while it was the merge queue's frontmost entry. That job never finalized, so its log 404s and `sentry.log` died with `RUNNER_TEMP`. This is the branch that can silently no-op the watchdog, not a confirmed cause.

Closes #5879.

## Review focus

`Test-SentryStale` is the whole change. The second added test drives the supersession direction the fix could have broken: a token that reads back different must still release the sentry.

author: chethanuk
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`ExtProcServerRunner` is built by hand at three places: `(*Runner).setup`
(`cmd/epp/runner/runner.go:479`), `(*Runner).runWithFileDiscovery` (`:1140`, ~660 lines away),
and `NewDefaultExtProcServerRunner` (`pkg/epp/server/runserver.go:86`). The struct has 22 fields,
and a composite literal zero-fills whatever it omits, so adding an `Options` field and wiring it
at one site still compiles — the other ext_proc servers just run with the zero value and nothing
points that out. That's how #1362's two gRPC message size fields reached one server and not the
other. The three literals agree today, so this is preventive rather than a live bug.

`runserver.NewExtProcServerRunner` becomes the one place `*Options` is mapped onto the runner. It
takes the options plus the seven dependencies the caller already built, and all three sites now
call it.

- `GrpcListener` and `EvictChannelLookup` stay caller-assigned — both are optional and only some
  call sites have one.
- `PriorityBandControlPlane` is a constructor parameter rather than a post-construction
  assignment, so a silent omission fails to compile instead of staying invisible to every
  cluster-free test.
- `NewDefaultExtProcServerRunner` collapses onto the factory and passes five `nil` dependencies —
  what its doc comment already promised ("set separately"). Behaviour-preserving: every field the
  factory sets beyond the nine it used to set is zero under `NewOptions()`.

`TestNewExtProcServerRunnerPopulatesEveryField` walks `reflect.VisibleFields` over the returned
runner and fails on any field left zero except the two the caller owns; same-typed fields wired
to each other's source (the two durations, the five bools) are pinned directly since `IsZero`
alone can't tell a swap from a correct assignment.

Before:
```
$ go test ./pkg/epp/server/... -run 'TestNewExtProcServerRunnerPopulatesEveryField'
pkg/epp/server/runserver_test.go:77:14: undefined: server.NewExtProcServerRunner
FAIL	github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pkg/epp/server [build failed]
```

After:
```
$ go test ./pkg/epp/server/... ./cmd/epp/runner/...
ok  	github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pkg/epp/server	22.811s
ok  	github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/cmd/epp/runner	2.609s
```

`bands` (`PriorityBandControlPlane`) stays `nil` in file-discovery mode, same as before this
change — there's no reconciler driving it on that path.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #1370

author: resonaura
body:
Hey @caplaz!

I've been using this plugin with my Eufy camera (Indoor Cam 2K / Solo) and ran into a few common P2P headaches:
- 3 to 5 second stream startup delay and lag
- Aggressive video compression / bitrate drops (often dropping to 720p)
- Scrypted detecting audio as `unknown` in P2P mode (no sound without extra transcoding args)
- HomeBase / camera locking its single P2P connection slot while streaming

Since Eufy cameras support local RTSP (via the NAS/RTSP toggle in the mobile app), I added direct RTSP streaming support:

1. **Auto-detection**: If RTSP is enabled on the camera, the plugin picks up the stream URL automatically from `rtspStreamUrl` / the `got rtsp url` event.
2. **Custom RTSP URL setting**: Added a `customRtspUrl` field under camera Streaming settings. Eufy's cloud API often omits the credentials from the RTSP URL, so this lets you set `rtsp://user:pass@192.168.x.x/live0` directly if needed.
3. **Audio & Video**: Uses `-rtsp_transport tcp` and advertises native `h264` + `aac` (16kHz mono). Scrypted detects the audio immediately without guessing or transcoding, and local stream startup is basically instant.
4. **Talkback preserved**: Two-way audio / intercom still works as before. When you talk through Scrypted / HomeKit, `startIntercom()` opens the P2P session strictly for the reverse audio channel and tears it down on release, without interrupting the active RTSP video feed.
5. **Fallback**: If RTSP is disabled or if a client explicitly asks for the `p2p` stream ID, it falls back to the existing P2P logic unchanged.

Tested on my own setup and it works smoothly. Added unit tests for the RTSP handling (`tests/unit/eufy-device-rtsp.test.ts`), and all 282 monorepo tests + lint pass.

Happy to make any adjustments or tweak anything if needed!

body: ## Problem The user guide was reported shipped on 2026-09-04, but `main` only ever received the **scaffold**. The actual content and the two JSON endpoints the in-app tooltips depend on never made it. Cause: the stacked PRs were merged **bottom-up, out of dependency order**, all within about four minutes. Each parent PR was merged *before* its children landed on the branch it was merging, so GitHub merged the parent's then-current state: | PR | merged | | |---|---|---| | #26 `docs-scaffold` → `integration` | `18:30:41` | ← merged **first** | | #27 `docs-content-v1` → `docs-scaffold` | `18:31:01` | too late | | #28 `tooltips-manifest` → `docs-scaffold` | `18:31:58` | too late | | #31 `docs-content-v2` → `docs-content-v1` | `18:32:17` | too late | | #32 `docs-content-v3` → `docs-content-v2` | `18:32:30` | too late | Every PR reads `MERGED`, which is why this wasn't caught. The net result on `main` was 4 early placeholder pages, no content, and no `tooltips.json` / `source-map.json`. ## What this PR does Recovers the lost work by merging the two branches that actually hold it, in the correct order: 1. **`user-guides/docs-scaffold`** — brings `src/pages/docs/tooltips.json.ts`, `src/pages/docs/source-map.json.ts`, the `DocsLayout.astro` screenshot resolution, 2 screenshots, and replaces the 3 stale placeholder `.mdoc` files with properly-slugged ones. 2. **`user-guides/docs-content-v3`** — brings the collection up to the full 25 pages. Both merged **cleanly** — no conflicts. `tooltips-manifest` is *not* an ancestor of `docs-content-v3`, so the scaffold merge is genuinely required first; merging the content alone would have left the JSON endpoints missing. It also adds the missing entry point: a **"User Guide" link in the site header** for all three locales. Previously nothing anywhere linked to `/docs`. The docs are English-only, but the nav renders per-locale, so omitting es/ms would have hidden the guide from those visitors. ## Verification `yarn build` locally: - **25 doc pages** built under `dist/docs/` - `dist/docs/tooltips.json` → **25 entries**, correctly shaped (`slug`, `title`, `description`, `product`) - `dist/docs/source-map.json` → **25 entries** with populated `sourcePaths` - Pagefind indexes 3 languages / 5897 words - `href="/docs"` present in the rendered header I also cross-checked the **15 `HelpTooltip` slugs used across the Flutter apps against the generated manifest — all 15 resolve.** (A 16th grep hit was an unrelated `HandbookSection(slug: '')`, not a tooltip.) ## Merge order Please merge **#33 first** (the `yarn.lock` fix). Without it the Pages deploy still fails on `--frozen-lockfile` and none of this reaches the live site. The two PRs are independent branches off `main`, so they can merge in either order without conflicts — but the site stays 404 until #33 lands. ## Still outstanding after this - `attendance-web-app` lost its entire `HelpTooltip` implementation to the same merge race — separate recovery PR. - The Phase 5 CI staleness gate is currently red on every PR in `attendance-web-app` and `educonnect-public` because it fetches `/docs/source-map.json`, which 404s. This PR plus #33 is what fixes that. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added comprehensive user guides for admissions, parent portals, staff workflows, accounting, analytics, attendance, timetables, and KinderCare. - Added note and warning callouts for clearer documentation guidance. - Added screenshot support within documentation pages. - Added searchable documentation data for source references and in-app tooltips. - Added User Guide links to English, Spanish, and Malay navigation. - **Documentation** - Replaced several placeholder pages with complete, task-focused guidance. - Removed outdated placeholder documentation pages.

author: markpippins
body:
## What changed

Completes the night-shift timer setup — the final piece of the sonar-completion loop + night-shift doctrine (PR #154, receipt-isolation Option A). This makes the *scheduled* cycle real while keeping launches strictly gated on an explicit isolation flip.

### 1. `bin/nightshift-flip.sh` — scripted Option-A flip drill (full agent-facing surface)
The doctrine's drill (DEPLOY_DB_CONFIG.md) covers only the bridge daemon and is manual. Launched agents actually connect to four services that resolve their own DB: **conduit-mcp :3100** (`CONDUIT_PG_DSN`), **nebula-mcp :3102** / **nebula-srv :3101** (`PG_DB_NAME`), **wrp-bridge-daemon** (`CONDUIT_PG_DSN`). This script flips all four via reversible systemd drop-ins (`~/.config/systemd/user/<svc>.service.d/nightshift.conf`):
- `on` — creates launch-gate marker `~/.cache/nightshift-flip.active`, writes drop-ins → `nexus_nightshift`, daemon-reloads, restarts services
- `off` — removes marker + drop-ins, restarts → live `nexus`
- `status` — reports effective DB target per service
- Idempotent; canonical unit files never modified.

### 2. `systemd-user/nexus-nightshift-scheduler.{service,timer}` — dedicated evaluator
Same canonical tackle runner as the day evaluator, but with `CONDUIT_PG_DSN` **permanently pinned** to `nexus_nightshift` and its own log. The service carries `ConditionPathExists=%h/.cache/nightshift-flip.active` — so an enabled timer ticking every minute is a **no-op until the operator deliberately runs `flip on`** (which restarts the shared MCP services; that decision is not delegated to a timer).

### 3. `sql/nightshift/seed-nightshift.sql` — hermetic bootstrap
Seeds a fresh `nexus_nightshift` with: 4 cycle roles (planner/builder/critic/reviewer), a provider + **verified** model (satisfies the `config_bundle_verified_gate` trigger), 4 CLI `config_bundle` rows (satisfies the runner's fail-closed `_is_interactive_hosted` path), 4 scheduler entries (`task_slug=nightshift`, interval 1800). **No live credentials** — the provider `api_key` is a placeholder (field is nullable; the launcher delegates to the harness's own model/provider config).

### 4. `tests/nightshift/checks.py` — 27 hermetic checks (registered in `tests/run_all.py`)
- Flip script driven end-to-end against a fake `systemctl` shim + temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (no real units touched): on/off/status, drop-in creation/removal, marker lifecycle, idempotence
- Unit contents, including the ConditionPathExists gate
- Seed idempotence **verified against the live `nexus_nightshift` DB** when reachable (skips otherwise) + a guard that the artifact contains no real API key.

## Why

Night-shift receipts must land only in the dedicated test DB (Option A). The scheduler runner's own DSN was already isolatable, but the agents it launches communicate via MCP servers that resolve their DB from their own environment — the leak Option A exists to prevent. This closes that gap and wires the cycle to a scheduled cadence.

## Migration / operations

1. `systemctl --user daemon-reload` (units are in `systemd-user/` — the canonical source; installed copies mirror them)
2. `systemctl --user enable --now nexus-nightshift-scheduler.timer`
3. To start a night shift deliberately: `bin/nightshift-flip.sh on` → cycle runs → `bin/nightshift-flip.sh off`
4. Verification: `bin/nightshift-flip.sh status`; receipt counts land only in `nexus_nightshift`

Already applied on the host: DB created + bootstrapped + repo-seeded; shadow acceptance re-verified against the repo seed (planner/critic would-launch, builder/reviewer gated by `eligible=0`); timer enabled and ticking with each tick logging `skipped, unmet condition check` until `flip on`.

Agent record: `321f9125` (architect, tags `to:engineer type:status-update project:nightshift`).

Four roadmap rows from the authentication and configuration backlog, three commits.

**spamd `User:` header, and TLS to the database from hMailServer.ini** (commit 1)
- `SpamAssassinUser` names a fixed spamd profile; `SpamAssassinUserFromRecipient=1` scans a single-recipient message as that recipient. Both off by default. Tested against a simulated spamd that records the request (`Infrastructure/SpamdSimulator.cs`), because the real one cannot say what it was sent.
- `[Database] PostgreSQLSslMode` / `PostgreSQLSslRootCert` go into libpq's conninfo (an unknown mode refuses the connection, HM5563); `ConnectionStringOptions` is appended verbatim to the MS SQL connection string. Not exercised against a live PostgreSQL or MS SQL here.
- Control Panel rows on the SpamAssassin card; README, `MigratingDatabaseBackend.md`, roadmap.

**SASL EXTERNAL on SMTP, IMAP and POP3** (commit 2)
- A client certificate that verified against the port's CA logs on as the mailbox it names (rfc822Name, subject emailAddress, or an address-shaped CN); an authzid has to be among those addresses. Offered only when such a certificate is on the connection. Identities are read once in `TCPConnection`, under the same verdict as the subject.
- Found on the way: POP3 (500) and SMTP (510) refused any AUTH line longer than a command line, so a real RS256 XOAUTH2 token had never worked on those two protocols. AUTH and the SASL continuation states now get 12288 octets (RFC 5034/4954).
- Tests: `SSL/ExternalSasl.cs` (in-process CA and client certificates via `Shared/ClientCertificateFactory.cs`), all three protocols, both SASL forms, the negative cases.

**JWKS key source and RFC 7662 token introspection** (commit 3)
- `OAuth2JwksUrl`: the provider's JWK Set as the RS256/ES256 key source, selected by `kid`, with the PEM file as fallback; refreshed on expiry and on an unknown kid (rate-limited); RSA 2048+ and P-256, `use:sig` only.
- `OAuth2IntrospectionUrl` + client credentials: every token that verifies is put to the provider; the verdict is cached by token digest; an unanswerable check refuses the token unless `OAuth2IntrospectionFailOpen=1`.
- Both through the new shared `HttpsClient` (verified https; plain http to loopback only). Tests: `Security/OAuth2Jwks.cs`, `Security/OAuth2Introspection.cs` against an in-process provider (`Shared/FakeHttpEndpoint.cs`).

author: scouzi1966
body:
The full-tier TTFT check previously timed parsing after the complete SSE response had already been buffered, allowing a slow first token to pass. Measure monotonic time from request start to the first nonempty content or reasoning delta as the stream arrives, and include the measured milliseconds in the assertion record.

Role-only and empty events do not count. The reader drains the stream after the first token so the existing transport failure handling still catches a disconnect or timeout. The existing request timeout remains in force, and the change sends no additional inference requests.

Validation: seven CPU clock/delayed-HTTP fixture tests passed, including a real 5.1-second first-token delay, a delayed stream tail, reasoning tokens, role-only output, disconnect after the first token, and a live-server timeout. All twelve transport fixtures, shell syntax, and `git diff --check` also passed. No GPU workloads.

Closes #257.

## Summary by Sourcery

Correct live SSE TTFT assertions to measure the actual time to the first visible or reasoning token while preserving stream failure detection.

Bug Fixes:
- Measure full-tier TTFT from request start to the first nonempty content or reasoning token received from the live SSE stream, preventing delayed first tokens from passing the threshold.

Enhancements:
- Continue draining the SSE stream after the first token so transport disconnects and timeouts remain detectable, while reporting the measured TTFT in assertion records.

Tests:
- Add deterministic clock and delayed SSE fixture coverage for token timing, reasoning output, ignored role-only or empty events, delayed stream tails, disconnects, and timeouts.

author: umeranjum17
body:
mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.97.0
Phone interactions should preserve the user's place: an agent ending should leave a usable shell, clicking an editor control should not summon the keyboard, and asking voice to stop should actually end its stream.

This follow-up combines the polite voice hangup fix with terminal interaction fixes. It also makes Tools an application launcher: enabled plugins' declared global actions appear there, while ordinary shells remain in Panes. There are no hardcoded Browser/Code provider IDs in the mobile kernel.

### End voice when asked

“Cool, go to sleep” now matches the shared backend hangup policy and closes the provider stream. The whole utterance must be a supported stop request; negated requests and instructions addressed to someone else do not close it. Native speech-to-speech transport stays intact.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Request[Polite stop request] --> Policy[Shared backend policy]
  Policy --> Close[Provider stream ends]
  Close --> Native[Native WebRTC stops]
```

### Keep the open terminal on its live pane

An agent route stops being valid when that agent exits, even though its shell survives. The mobile screen now follows the same observed live pane to its new shell or agent route and opens a fresh terminal surface/channel. It does not redirect historical routes or steal navigation from a file viewer above the terminal.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Agent[Open agent] --> Exit[Agent exits]
  Exit --> Pane[Same live pane]
  Pane --> Shell[Usable shell]
  Shell --> Next[Next agent in that pane]
```

### Deliberate Android keyboard

Automatic keyboard opening defaults off on Android. Clicking a terminal or graphical tool still sends its normal pointer event. A 44 dp keyboard button explicitly opens the terminal IME. Settings → Preferences → Terminal keyboard offers **Open keyboard on tap**, saved on that device. iOS and web keyboard behavior is unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Tap[Tap Browser, Code or shell] --> Preference{Open keyboard on tap?}
  Preference -->|Off by default| Click[Normal click; layout stays full height]
  Preference -->|On| IME[Open terminal keyboard]
  Button[Keyboard button] --> IME
```

### A smaller Tools list

Tools discovers explicitly global actions from enabled backend plugins. On the current installation these are Terminal Browser and Terminal Code. Setup panes, arbitrary executables found on PATH, and dozens of already-running shells are no longer mixed into that launcher.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Registry[Enabled plugin registry] --> Actions[Declared global actions]
  Actions --> Tools[Tools launcher]
  Shells[Running shells] --> Panes[Panes list]
```

### Validation and remaining evidence

- Existing terminal and catalog flows: 14/14 passed, including agent → shell → agent, background navigation protection, and persisted keyboard preference.
- Bundled plugin validation: 9 plugins, 7 primitive guards, Files flow, and actual Panes plugin discovery flow passed. The latter keeps 80 shells out of Tools while retaining them in Panes.
- Mobile TypeScript, tooling architecture, and native patch guards passed. Native Android release build passed.
- Prior voice validation: provider 11/11, mobile streaming lifecycle 7/7, voice RPC and packaged CLI checks passed; the shared hangup fix is installed in the local host.
- Matching-source local emulator full gate **PASS**, failures `[]`: all four 32.8-second feature/performance windows, viewer cold/warm/offline/recovery, Usage switching/recency, native graphics cell metrics, framebuffer colors and delivered frames.
- Android IME checks **PASS** in text and graphics modes: three terminal taps keep it hidden, explicit button opens it, Back dismisses it. Graphics after keyboard resize retains both expected framebuffer colors (25,560 / 25,576 sampled pixels).
- Signed ARM64 phone artifact: `muxr-0.1.26-terminal-polish-vc356-arm64-v8a.apk`, versionCode **356**, SHA256 `f972b9be43d1eb463514042cc43d1ea8bd5802290559fabd3a0876bdc3e1a69c`. Built from the same application/native bytes as the passing x86_64 gate. Existing production signer verified; delivered through the pane's watched attachments. This is a local preview, not an npm/store publication.
- Bounded ordinary live Code check: real native taps expanded both owned test folders, browser DOM confirmed their expanded state, IME stayed hidden, and the app PID stayed unchanged. Explicit keyboard opening exposed a transient dark frame; the editor subsequently repainted. Runner cleanup and final source/native freeze passed. No app-process crash was observed in this attempt.
- The shared local host now runs the packaged snapshot from this head; its actual Tools catalog returns Terminal Browser and Terminal Code.
- A half-circle Tools interaction is available as a separate interactive design preview. It is **not implemented in this PR or APK yet**.
- Reported physical-phone gray screen while opening Code folders and black flicker during scrolling are **not yet proven resolved**. No live audio or physical-phone acceptance is inferred from module tests or the emulator.



## Development and beta release workflow

Merging this PR advances `main`, our development stream. It does **not** publish production. The first rollout will be a beta for phone testing; stable promotion waits for the user's explicit acceptance.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PR[This PR and normal CI] --> Main[Development main]
    Main --> Nightly[Dev nightly: separate Android app]
    Main --> Beta[Beta: existing app identity]
    Beta --> Test[Install APK and test locally]
    Test --> Candidate[Final-version candidate]
    Candidate --> Approval[Manual production approval]
    Approval --> Stable[npm latest and explicit Play rollout]
```

The candidate workflow builds npm + signed ARM64 APK/AAB from one exact green commit, reserves an Android build number through a fast-forward-only Git ledger, verifies installed package metadata, and attaches immutable SHA256 manifests. Dev/beta npm publishing consumes the retained tarball without rebuilding. Stable npm publication requires an explicit final candidate, exact confirmation and the protected production environment. Android Internal intake can upload the retained candidate AAB; Closed/Production promotion verifies that artifact even after main advances.

`muxr update` stays on its installed channel. Switching uses `--channel dev|beta|stable`; downgrades remain explicit. The dev Android identity and URI schemes are compiled into the native manifest. Beta intentionally updates the current app and shares its data. iOS/OTA and parallel isolated CLI host installations are not claimed as delivered.

[Executable release runbook](docs/RELEASING.md). Local emulator testing remains local; no emulator GitHub workflow was added.

### APK and acceptance

[Download the signed terminal-polish phone preview, build 356](https://github.com/umeranjum17/muxr/releases/download/preview-840708b0/muxr-0.1.26-terminal-polish-vc356-arm64-v8a.apk). This source-pinned preview is being published with the merge; the automated beta will be linked here separately with its newer source/build identity. SHA256: `f972b9be43d1eb463514042cc43d1ea8bd5802290559fabd3a0876bdc3e1a69c`.

The preview's application/native code passed the retained local emulator gate and real Terminal Code folder taps. Release-channel changes have separate package/workflow/native identity checks. Build success does not erase the remaining beta limitation: a transient dark frame can still occur during explicit keyboard resize, and the physical-phone crash reproduction is not proven fixed. The half-circle Tools UI remains a prototype, not shipped code.

body: ## Summary Rigorous live testing of the `pi-agent` backend (Cesium's integration of the OSS `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` SDK) against a real OpenAI-compatible proxy, through the raw provider, the real Bun server (REST) and the browser UI, exposed a long list of correctness gaps, especially for the native `~/.pi/agent` (app-installation) mode and for custom extensions. This PR fixes them and adds unit, integration and live coverage. ### Defects found live and fixed | Defect | Fix | | --- | --- | | **Pi conversations could not be created from the app at all**: `computeBackendInfo("pi-agent")` hardcoded `available: false`, so `assertRunnableBackend` rejected every create (`"Pi Agent is not available yet."`) | Statically runnable like `cesium-agent`/`cursor-sdk`; credential gating stays in `createAgentProvider` and the cached listing | | Provider failures (`stopReason: "error"`, e.g. HTTP 400/401) reported as a clean `idle` turn with `lastError: null` and no visible text | Stateful normalizer surfaces them as a `system` error + `failed` status + `lastError`; retries keep the run open, exhausted retries report the final error | | `session.bindExtensions()` never called: extension `session_start` hooks, `resources_discover`, `ctx.ui.*` dialogs never worked (`confirm` auto-`false`, `select` auto-cancel, `notify` dropped) | `PiAgentUiBridge`: `confirm` -> permission card, `select`/`input`/`editor` -> ask-question card, `notify` -> system row; command context actions, abort/shutdown handlers and extension error listener bound | | Extension slash commands (`/hello`) left the conversation stuck on `running` forever | Status reset to idle when a prompt is handled without an agent loop | | A user **Stop** dropped the whole conversation memory (fresh Pi session, no recovery seed) | New opt-in `supportsCancelResume` capability keeps `providerSessionId` for harnesses whose native session survives an abort (Pi records the aborted turn); other backends unchanged | | Composer choices (thinking level, tool approval) reverted to cache defaults on the next prompt because idle runtimes are disposed after 5s and only model/mode were carried over | `withCurrentConfig` carries every persisted option into a fresh handle | | `tool_execution_end` lost tool titles/locations; custom tools showed raw names | Tool args remembered per `toolCallId`; extension `label` used; `edit`/`write` results carry an `editPreview` | | Every assistant message of a run merged into one bubble; cancel emitted duplicate end markers + conflicting statuses | Per-Pi-message ids; cancel closes the streaming bubble once and yields exactly one `cancelled` status | | `models.json`-only credential setups rejected as "not configured"; `GOOGLE_API_KEY` advertised for `google` while Pi expects `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Shared `createPiModelRegistry` drives the configured check; Pi-aligned env table + Cesium aliases applied as runtime keys; settings panel reports models.json providers as configured | | Default model was the first built-in (`openai/gpt-4`) even with a custom provider wired up; API-created conversations started as `auto` | Follows Pi `settings.json` default, then models.json providers, then first available; runtime manager resolves the same default | | Broken extensions failed silently (console only) | Startup diagnostics, extension load errors and model fallbacks surface once as system rows | | Disconnect in the settings panel threw for any non-OAuth provider | Removes any Cesium-controlled credential; hidden for env/models.json providers | | Missing Pi session on resume silently started a fresh session | Throws so the runtime manager's transcript-recovery fallback runs | | Context usage ring unsupported for Pi | Computed from Pi's native session JSONL (last assistant usage + trailing estimate, model `contextWindow`, compaction split) | | Bare `Awaiting_question` activity row rendered under question cards (shared projection) | `awaiting_question` treated like `awaiting_permission` | ### Additions - Live model/thinking sync (`model_select`, `thinking_level_changed`), session rename -> conversation title, compaction -> `compression_summary`, auto-retry notices, extension-injected user turns (`pi.sendUserMessage`, steering) surfaced as user messages with deterministic prompt ownership, `session_shutdown` + settings flush on dispose. - Optional **Tool approval** composer option (`pi` default = Pi CLI behaviour, `mutations`, `all`) implemented as an inline Pi extension on `tool_call`, wired into Cesium remembered permissions (`allow_always` persists a category rule). Older caches gain the option via an in-place migration. - `npm run sdk:pi-probe` drives the real provider end-to-end (approval, dialogs, cancel, resume). ### Tests - `server/test/pi-agent.test.ts` (29 tests): normalizer state machine (errors, retries, aborts, tool memory, previews, message segmentation, injected turns, compaction), UI bridge (permission/question mapping, timeouts, cancel), credentials (env aliases, models.json), catalog, config carry-over, context usage from a real session file. - `server/test/agents.test.ts`: cancel keeps the provider session for `supportsCancelResume` harnesses. `test/agent-completion-projection.test.ts`: no bare `Awaiting_question` row. - Server suite: 914 tests, 908 pass, 0 fail, 6 pre-existing skips. Root suite: 1176 tests, 1175 pass; the only failure (`mobile-workbench-voice-orb`) inspects a committed Android bundle artifact and fails on `main` too. ### Live verification (proxy `infer.techlitnow.com`, `kimi-k3` over `openai-completions` and `openai-responses`, Node + Bun runtimes) Raw provider: built-in tools, custom extension tools with streaming updates, extension `confirm`/`select`, extension commands, prompt templates, skills (global + project `.pi/`), project extensions + a deliberately broken extension, local Pi package (extension/skill/prompt), isolated agent home, `AGENTS.md` context, bad API key, cancel before/after tool start, model switch (completions -> responses) and to a missing model, thinking level, image attachment, resume, manual compaction, extension-injected/steered turns, both approval-gate modes. Real Bun server over REST: create + prompt, approval gate through `PATCH config` + `/permission` with `allow_always` persisting a remembered rule that bypasses later prompts, native-session resume across a server restart, cancel keeping conversation memory, queued prompt draining, context-usage endpoint. Browser (recorded): Pi Agent selected in the composer, tool cards, extension `select()` as a question card answered "green", extension `confirm()` as a permission card allowed, command output shown.

author: joelteply
body:
`airc msg --stdin` (#1382) exists so prose never passes through shell quoting. `airc publish` — the verb for posting to a room **other** than the current one — had no equivalent, so every cross-room message went back to inline `--body-text "..."` and back into the hazard.

## Measured, hours after #1382 merged

A backtick inside a `--body-text` argument was command-substituted by the shell and ate part of the message — **in the room where the fix for exactly that had already landed**.

A flag that stops at one verb stops at the verb people happen to use least. The workaround (switch the current room with `airc room`, then `msg --stdin`) mutates a scope pointer as a side effect of wanting to say something.

`--body-json -` already reads stdin, but that path parses JSON. There was no way to hand `publish` a body of prose without the shell in between.

## Both guards duplicated on purpose

Not the reasoning — the behaviour:

- **stdin is a TERMINAL** → refuse with the redirect and heredoc forms, rather than block forever waiting for an EOF the operator has to know to send.
- **body is EMPTY or whitespace** → refuse, rather than publish a blank frame.

Both were found on #1382 by review rather than by design (ce8b9074's catch). A flag whose guards differ between two verbs is worse than no flag: the operator learns one contract and gets another.

## The test pins the wiring

The specific way this would silently do nothing is a `--stdin` added to the CLI but never consulted by `load_body` — it would fall through to the "requires a body source" error. The test asserts a `true` reaches the stdin path instead.

`cargo test -p airc-cli --bins publish` → **12 passed, 0 failed**.

body:
Implements the memory-subsystem findings from the core review.

- `atomicWriteFile` uses unique tmp names + fsync; dead write-lock machinery removed.
- `graph.load()` never writes (repairs stay in memory); save order archive → ghosts → edges → nodes; a generation counter refuses to overwrite a newer on-disk graph (single-writer guard).
- Non-brain writers (dashboard goal edits, chat digest, workers, backup restore) append to a graph-ops inbox that the brain drains at boot and each tick; restore stages files atomically and requests a reload.
- LLM operations validated at the boundary; `remove_node` archives instead of deleting; pinned nodes protected; max 5 destructive ops per batch; merges keep metadata; id collisions re-minted.
- Sleep consolidation needs real evidence (token overlap or a contradicts edge; duplicates need cosine > 0.85 and Jaccard ≥ 0.5) and archives the loser.
- Restore floor 0.3; recall of decay-archived nodes possible; tag enrichment never adds tier tags and caps at 12; pinned nodes ≤ 30 % of context budget, ≤ 60 total, pinning needs importance ≥ 0.7.
- Corrupt archive/ghost files are never overwritten; embeddings merge-on-save and flush on shutdown; emergency prune to 90 %; gist originals archived; edge pruning by type; follow-ups merged by id; consciousness bounded.
- graph.ts split into persistence/validation/operations/correlate; shared text-utils; WAL (write-only, never read) removed.

author: khanzadimahdi
body:
Somebody may be trusted with their own articles without being trusted with everybody's. The dashboard already made that distinction for comments and files; this makes it for articles, and makes it the way files do.

## The shape

`deleteUserFile` and `getUserFiles` sit beside `deleteFile` and `getFiles`, each on its own `/dashboard/my/...` route with a single `self.*` permission, and each reaching the repository through owner-scoped queries. Articles now do the same:

| everybody's | one's own |
|---|---|
| `getArticles` · `GET /dashboard/articles` | `getUserArticles` · `GET /dashboard/my/articles` |
| `getArticle` · `GET /dashboard/articles/{correlationUUID}/{language_code}` | `getUserArticle` · `GET /dashboard/my/articles/{correlationUUID}/{language_code}` |
| `updateArticle` · `PUT /dashboard/articles` | `updateUserArticle` · `PUT /dashboard/my/articles` |
| `deleteArticle` · `DELETE /dashboard/articles/{correlationUUID}/{language_code}` | `deleteUserArticle` · `DELETE /dashboard/my/articles/{correlationUUID}/{language_code}` |

Each route asks for one permission — `articles.*` on the left, `self.articles.*` on the right — so what a request may reach is decided by which use case answers it rather than by a check inside a shared one. Nothing on the left changes: the diff is additive apart from the four routes, the permission constants and their seed rows.

## Not theirs is not found

The author-scoped half of the repository — `GetCorrelationUUIDsByAuthor`, `CountByCorrelationAndAuthor`, `GetByCorrelationUUIDAndLanguageAndAuthor`, `DeleteByCorrelationUUIDAndLanguageAndAuthor` — asks for an article *as its author's*. So to somebody who may only reach their own, an article that is not theirs and one that does not exist are the same thing: 404, not 403, and it cannot be written over by naming its correlation uuid. That is how `GetOneByOwnerUUID` and `DeleteByOwnerUUID` already work for files.

## Merging

Independent of #77 — both branch from `main` and either may go first. The hand-written files merge cleanly between them; the generated OpenAPI documents will conflict, since both add paths in the same region, and are resolved by re-running `make generate` after the merge.

Pairs with the frontend PR for the same change.

## Verified

`go test ./... -race` clean, including a use case test and a handler test per action: an article the person wrote goes through, and one somebody else wrote is not found and nothing is saved or deleted.

This PR changes release tooling, documentation and version metadata, not application behavior. Local validation ran on Windows. The native six-target release workflow runs after merge against the exact annotated tag. author: zahara-nour
body:
Cinq pages sont **cassées en production depuis huit jours**, dont l'export RGPD.

## La cause

La migration `20260829100000_refonte_referentiel_fusion.sql` (29 août) a renommé `skill_id` → `observable_id` sur `skill_attempts` et `evaluation_task_perimeter`, et remplacé la table `skills` par `observables`. La base a suivi ; cinq fichiers situés hors du périmètre du chantier, non.

| Page | Ce qui est cassé |
| --- | --- |
| `api/account/export` | **L'export RGPD**, sur ses **deux** sources d'évaluation |
| `student/competences/[code]` | La page compétences de l'élève |
| `teacher/evaluation-tasks/[id]/saisie` | La saisie d'évaluation |
| `teacher/evaluation-tasks/[id]` | Le périmètre de tâche |
| `teacher/evaluation-tasks` | La liste des tâches |

**Onze références corrigées** : sept colonnes et **quatre embeds PostgREST** vers la table supprimée. Chacune vérifiée contre le schéma de production — clés étrangères comprises — plutôt que déduite de la migration.

## Pourquoi rien ne l'a vu

`src/app.d.ts` déclare `supabase: SupabaseClient` **sans le générique `Database`**. Aucune requête de `+page.server.ts` ou `+server.ts` n'est donc typée : ni table, ni colonne, ni résultat. C'est le même trou qui avait laissé `/automaths` filtrer sur une colonne inexistante pendant dix mois (#127, #129).

⚠️ **Cette PR ne branche pas ce typage.** Le faire révèle **407 erreurs sur 145 fichiers** — dont douze autres colonnes inexistantes, sur `profiles`, `worksheet_exercises`, le marketplace et le cahier de texte. C'est un chantier à part, à traiter par lots ; le brancher maintenant passerait la CI au rouge.

Une limite à connaître, découverte en chemin : **le typage n'a signalé aucun des quatre embeds `skills(…)`** vers la table supprimée. Il attrape les colonnes, pas les relations imbriquées. Sans la vérification des clés étrangères en base, ce correctif aurait été à moitié faux.

## Validation

**7 tests d'intégration** exécutent les requêtes réellement émises par ces pages et vérifient qu'elles résolvent.

Et surtout : **contrôlé qu'ils échouent avec les anciens noms** — `42703` (colonne inconnue) pour les trois colonnes, `PGRST200` (relation absente) pour l'embed. Un huitième test garde que `skills` a bien disparu, pour éviter que les autres passent un jour pour la mauvaise raison.

- Suite d'intégration complète : **490 tests, 48 fichiers, zéro échec**.
- Prettier vert.

## Reste en suspens

Le **module anti-fraude** (`src/lib/server/anti-fraud/runner.ts`) est cassé par le même renommage, mais sa réparation n'est pas mécanique : il filtre sur `skills.family === 'knowledge'`, or la colonne `family` n'existe plus **nulle part** depuis la fusion des deux arbres. Le successeur le plus proche, `regime_acquisition`, ne recouvre pas la même frontière — et les 453 points sont tous en `diversite`, donc un filtre dessus ne trierait rien.

C'est une décision de sens pédagogique, laissée au PO : retirer le filtre, le remplacer, ou désactiver le détecteur.

author: nohwnd
body:
Fix #3007

> Based on #3023, not on `main`. It needs the discovery-only path to receive the map, otherwise `Run.SkipRun` would report an empty list. Retarget to `main` once #3023 merges.

A container's setup comes from every `Pester.BeforeContainer.ps1` between `Run.RepoRoot` and the test file's own folder, and nothing in the result said which ones were used. Opening `tests/unit/Foo.Tests.ps1` shows no `BeforeAll` and gives no sign that two folder setups ran before it. Reading the directory tree does not answer it either, because `#pester:no-inherit` can cut the chain short.

The applied files are on the container now, outermost first, in the order they ran:

```
U.Tests.ps1:
    <root>/Pester.BeforeContainer.ps1
    <root>/tests/Pester.BeforeContainer.ps1
    <root>/tests/unit/Pester.BeforeContainer.ps1
D.Tests.ps1:
    <root>/tests/docs/Pester.BeforeContainer.ps1
```

`D.Tests.ps1` sits under a folder marked `#pester:no-inherit`, so it reports only its own file. That is the case the folder tree cannot tell you.

On the container rather than the block, as the issue suggested. It is a property of the file being run, post-processors already walk containers, and it leaves the block model unchanged.

## Verification

`tst/Pester.RSpec.Parallel.ts.ps1` 47/47, `tst/Pester.RSpec.ts.ps1` 128/128.

Two tests added next to the other cascade tests, one for the full chain and one for the `#pester:no-inherit` truncation.

I checked that `Remove-RSpecNonPublicProperties` does not drop the new property. Its property lists are commented out, it only nulls the plugin fields, so the property survives to `PassThru`.

author: biomatix
body:
## What changed

- Gate the name-mangling warnings and the two preprocessing progress lines at `verbose >= 2`; pass `verbose = 0` to `gl.allele.freq` and `gl.drop.loc` so `verbose = 0` is silent (F1)
- Correct the documented `rm.autapomorphies` default to `[default FALSE]`, matching the signature (F2)
- Classify a population as polymorphic at a locus from allele counts (`0 < sum < 2 * nobs` in the popxloc table) instead of thresholds on rounded frequencies (F3)
- Guard the nexus `sink()` with a depth-recorded `on.exit` unwind so an error or interrupt during the write cannot leave the console diverted (F4)
- Return `invisible(NULL)` instead of `return(NULL)` (F5)
- Roxygen conformance pass: house tag order, DOC2 verbose clause, DOC7 author labels, typo fixes; `devtools::document()` run (F6)

## Why

The old classifier counted a population as polymorphic only when its rounded allele frequency fell strictly inside (0.0001, 0.99), so a locus at 199/200 in one population and 0.5 in another was scored as an autapomorphy and silently dropped under `rm.autapomorphies = TRUE`. The ungated preprocessing chatter printed 13 lines at `verbose = 0`.

## Evidence

- Characterization test (`tests/testthat/test-gl2snapper.R`): 21 assertions pass; every flipped expectation maps to an approved finding (F1 silence at `verbose = 0`, F2 documented default, F5 invisibility). The nexus structure assertions (ntax/nchar, `symbols="012"`, `missing=?`, pop_ind labels, genotype rows mirroring `as.matrix`) are unchanged and pass.
- End-to-end on `testset.gl` (`rm.autapomorphies = TRUE`, `nloc = 50`, `verbose = 3`): 54 autapomorphic loci removed, 50 retained, valid nexus written.
- `on.exit(sink())` alone warns "no sink to remove" on the success path (verified); the depth-recorded unwind is a no-op on success and pops only this function's diversion on failure.

## API impact

Signature unchanged. The set of loci retained under `rm.autapomorphies = TRUE` can change for datasets with near-fixed polymorphic populations (F3, approved with the output-change consequence acknowledged); `verbose = 0` runs are now silent; unassigned calls no longer print `NULL`. NEWS.md entry added. Sibling grep across the 8 dartRverse clones: no callers of `gl2snapper` outside dartR.base.

author: freekh
body:
Makes `s.record().external()` real. The contract from [#610](https://github.com/valbuild/val/pull/610) now executes: the Studio, the CLI and an app all read records whose entries live in a database, an HTTP API or a bucket.

**Based on #610** — review that first; this targets its branch so the diff here is phase 1 alone.

**Read-only, deliberately.** Reading works end to end. Writing from the Studio — publish, the two clocks, what happens when a commit lands before its build — is its own piece of work, and the add/change/delete affordances are hidden rather than left to fail.

## What an app writes

```ts
// content/products.val.ts — an ordinary .val.ts, with no driver in sight
export default c.define(
  "/content/products.val.ts",
  s.record(s.object({ title: s.string(), price: s.number() })).external("products"),
  c.external(),
);
```

```ts
// val/external.ts — server-only, where the driver belongs
const { entry, modules } = defineExternal<Tx>({ around: (run) => sql.begin(run) });

export default modules({
  products: entry(productsVal, { keys, get, put, delete: del }),
});
```

Then `initValServer(valModules, { ...config, external }, { draftMode })`.

## The registry and its executor

Where the retry loop sits is the decision worth stating, because it is not the same in both configurations. **With `around`** the loop wraps the whole scope: a database aborts its transaction on the first error and answers everything after it with "current transaction is aborted", so retrying the failed statement inside a dead transaction fails every time. **Without it** the loop wraps each call, which is both correct and far cheaper. `invoke` hides the difference from every caller.

A thrown error is never retried, wherever the policy would allow it: Val cannot tell a rate limit from a `TypeError`, and retrying a bug three times only fails slower.

Chunking is a hint, not a ceiling. A 50-key read against a store that serves ten at a time is five calls **in one transaction** — the Studio's page size must not depend on how a record is stored.

## Reading

Three things sit between an adapter's answer and what an editor sees, and none belongs in the adapter:

- **Inline entries shadow the store.** Content pasted into the `.val.ts` reads as written and wins for its own keys — otherwise moving content into a store would make the not-yet-moved half disappear the moment the store answered for its key.
- **Unpublished edits are applied on top.** The store holds published content only. Draft-added keys are spliced onto the first page and draft-removed ones taken out: the store's cursors are the store's, and a key it has never heard of cannot be positioned within them.
- **Content is validated as it is read, and degrades.** The store is not the repository — its rows can change under a schema that no longer describes them. A failing row is reported per key **and still returned**: an editor has to see it to fix it, and one bad row must not leave a hole in the page.

## Endpoints

`GET /external/keys`, `/external/entries` and `/external/search`, shaped like `/json` entry for entry. Paging is by **cursor**, not offset: an offset into a live store means counting rows it has already forgotten.

Search has three modes, and the caller is told which — an editor shown "no matches" by a search that never ran has been misled:

- **`delegated`** — the store searched, then Val corrects the answer for unpublished edits it could not see. A hit whose draft no longer contains the text is dropped; an entry whose draft now contains it is added. Both are wrong in a way an editor notices immediately, because they search for the words they just typed.
- **`partial`** — no `search` on the adapter, so Val answers from entries it has already fetched. The index is opportunistic and fetches nothing of its own: searching a 100,000-entry store must not quietly become downloading it.
- **`unavailable`** — `search: false`. A disabled box with a reason.

`count` likewise has three answers a caller must tell apart: a real total, a bounded one (`exact: false` → "200,000+"), and declined — which is **not** zero.

## Media: one `files` field, a tagged union

An adapter says where its bytes live in a single field, of which two arms ship:

```ts
files: { type: "bytes",     put, get }         // through this server
files: { type: "presigned", signUpload, url }  // straight to your store
```

The choice is driven by one question — **does the host cap request bodies?** Vercel, Netlify, Lambda and Cloudflare Pages do; a VPS, Docker, Fly and a self-hosted Node server do not. Between them every deployment is correct, so nothing is unreachable.

A union rather than four optional sibling methods, for two reasons:

- **A write path with no read path is unrepresentable.** As optional siblings this was a runtime check that could only fire once someone had already uploaded something. `externalNavigation.test.ts` pins both halves against a real `ts.LanguageService`, asserting the exact diagnostics (`Property 'get' is missing in type`, `'signUpload' does not exist in type`) so neither can pass for an unrelated reason — plus a positive control, so that tightening the union past what a real adapter can satisfy fails first.
- **The discriminant is data.** `checkExternalSetup` reads `files.type` at startup without calling anything, rather than inferring intent from which functions happen to exist.

That startup check **warns** — naming the platform, the limit and the fix — when a `bytes` adapter is deployed somewhere that caps request bodies. A warning rather than an error: a record that only ever holds small files is not misconfigured, and Val cannot know that it does not. So `checkExternalSetup` returns `{ errors, warnings }` and `ValOps` logs the warnings, because routing them through the error channel would surface "Val is not correctly setup" and block the module. It sits inside `initSources`' memo guard, so it is said once per instance rather than per request.

The schema-side check is now presence-only, since the union carries both halves.

## Reading from an app

`fetchVal` and `fetchValKey` work on an external record and are the **same functions** — an app must not have to change which reader it calls when its content moves into a store. `fetchValKeys` is the one addition, because no other storage mode has anything to page. `fetchVal` pages every entry out and fails on a **timeout**, not a size: "too big" is not something Val can judge.

Two decisions here, both about the read endpoint needing a session:

- **Server components read through an in-process handle** (`VAL_OPS`, a symbol the router cannot dispatch to), not the HTTP routes. Every other kind of Val content is bundled with the app; an external record's is only ever in the store, so the render path must read it with Val disabled and no session in sight. Routing that through the handlers would have meant either failing in production or opening published reads to anonymous callers, and enumerating someone's product table is not a capability to hand out by accident.
- **`useVal` and `useValKey` refuse an external module**, with an error naming the fix (read it in a server component, pass it down). This is the one place phase 1 stops short rather than half-working.

## The Studio

The same record UI as every other record. `SourceStore` builds the record's source from the keys it has loaded, putting the **marker** where content has not arrived — which is what makes `peek`, the field hooks, the skeletons and the retry path all work unchanged. A window of rows is one request. The footer says how much of the record is present and distinguishes the three count answers.

The read-only gate also fixes an existing gap: the add/change/delete popovers never consulted `schema.readonly` at all, so a readonly record's buttons were live and only the leaf inputs inside an entry were guarded.

## Two checks a whole-source check cannot make

- **Router keys are validated per key.**

author: hawkynt
body:
The largest thing left, and it was not an algorithm — it was numbers.

Every transform shape's weights come from a handful of values describing how the quantisation step grows with distance from the corner of the block. Those values are the format's, not a decoder's to choose. Most of the ones here were plausible round figures: a 32x32 starting at 22,000 where the format states 15,718.40830982518931456, with seven of them where the format states eight. A curve of the wrong length is also interpolated over the wrong range.

The 8x8 curve *was* right — which is exactly why a picture made of plain 8x8 blocks came out nearly exact while the same picture coded in 32x32s came out twelve levels wrong everywhere inside each transform, and why every earlier per-shape measurement pointed at "the shapes that are not 8x8" without saying why.

**How it was found.** Encoding one picture at six qualities and measuring each: the error was small at the finest setting and small at the coarsest, and large in between. That is not what a quantisation fault looks like — it is what it looks like when the encoder changes *which shapes it uses*. At `-d 8` the whole picture is one 64x64 (error 2.2); at `-d 2` it is four 32x32s (error 12.1); at `-d 0.3` it is all 8x8 (error 2.1).

Seven curves replaced with the stated ones: 16x16, 32x32, 8x16, 8x32, 16x32, 4x8, 4x4.

Differing pixels against `djxl`, and the worst single pixel:

| picture | before | after | worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16x16 | 2.17 | 0.27 of 256 | 26 → 2 |
| 128x96 | 113 | 21 of 12,288 | 31 → 7 |
| 128x128 | 146 | 26 of 16,384 | 39 → 7 |
| 160x160 | 203 | 40 of 25,600 | 41 → 11 |
| 200x150 plasma | 117 | 49 of 30,000 | 25 → 6 |
| 224x224 | 356 | 72 of 50,176 | 27 → 6 |
| 256x256 | 413 | 88 of 65,536 | 30 → 7 |
| 400x300, four groups | 798 | 304 of 120,000 | 28 → 17 |

Across the corpus: **4,317 differing pixels to 1,306**, a 70% reduction, with worst-pixel errors falling from 20–40 down to 1–11. Nothing moves the other way.

Tests pin the first value of each curve and its length, per channel — the first value sets the overall scale and a wrong length interpolates over the wrong range, so those two catch the failure mode that was here. They also assert that a shape and its transpose share one curve, as the format gives them one table.

author: vladislav15937
body:
## Что не так было

Агент, который пишет код, не имел правил: `docs/agent-workflow.md` описывает
**порядок** работы, `docs/defect-classes.md` — что искать, а как писать на Java
в этом проекте, не было записано нигде.

Пересказывать SOLID и каталог GoF я не стал — это есть где прочитать, и хуже
того, абстрактный список «лучших практик» разошёлся бы с собственными решениями
проекта (логика в Java, а не в базе; record'ы в ответах; Mockito здесь
не работает). Правила написаны по тому, что в коде **уже есть**, и по цене,
которая за это заплачена.

## Главное правило — и живой пример против него

**Паттерн вводится под давлением, а не заранее.** 179 файлов, ноль
`ServiceImpl`, ноль абстрактных классов, ноль своих фабрик. Восемнадцать
интерфейсов, пятнадцать — репозитории Spring Data. Оставшиеся три показывают
правило целиком:

| Интерфейс | Реализаций | Вердикт |
|---|---|---|
| `EventTransport` | 2 (Kafka, память) | оправдан: вторая работает в каждом запуске без Kafka |
| `EventHandler` | 1 | точка расширения диспетчера, вторые появятся с потребителем |
| `MarketplaceAdapter` | **0**, и ноль вызовов | написан под воображаемую площадку |

`MarketplaceAdapter` описывает `publish` + `pullStatuses`, pull у Авито и push
у Дрома. Настоящая выгрузка устроена иначе — генератор фида, отдача по
постоянной ссылке, отправка дельт — и в эту форму не легла. Это ровно то,
о чём проект **уже записал** в корневом `CLAUDE.md` про фискализацию: «интерфейс
раньше первого договора повторит форму воображаемого оператора». Только здесь
он уже в репозитории.

## Разделы

Инвариант живёт в сущности (`Deal` сам отбивает выдачу отменённой — путей к ней
четыре); модули разговаривают событиями; record в ответе; внедрение
конструктором; транзакции; **одновременность**; нагрузка; SQL; ошибки; тесты;
чего здесь не делают.

Раздел про нагрузку — весь на замерах этого проекта:

| Замер | Было → стало |
|---|---|
| `OFFSET` на 700-й странице (35 841 позиция) | 748 мс → 82 мс с курсором |
| `OR` вместо `UNION` в поиске витрины | 744 мс, 4,3 с при 30 пользователях → **38 мс** |
| Перенос склада пачками | 35 841 позиция и 440 машин за 68 секунд |

Плюс: потоковая отдача и проверки до первого байта, отсутствие N+1, `batch_size`,
триграммные индексы, пул 20 и почему в тестах пять, `lock_timeout`.

Раздел про одновременность — самый дорогой: условие в `WHERE` вместо
read-modify-write с проверкой числа строк, `@Version`, единый порядок
блокировок, `SKIP LOCKED` для очередей, ответ на одновременный повтор там,
где стоит уникальный индекс.

## Агенты

`.claude/agents/coder.md` — пишет код по задаче (`sweep` остаётся для перебора
дефектов). Оба обязаны прочитать правила; `reviewer` проверяет по ним же,
и в его список добавлены пять чаще всего нарушаемых.

## Как проверено

Каждое число сверено с кодом **перед** публикацией, и три утверждения оказались
неверными:

| Утверждение черновика | Правда |
|---|---|
| «258 файлов» | 179 — считал вместе с тестами |
| «744 мс — это `OFFSET`» | 744 мс — это `OR` вместо `UNION`; у `OFFSET` 748 |
| «`PhotoStorage` — интерфейс» | это класс, интерфейса нет |

Сверено также: 209 record'ов, 260 `private final`, 0 `@Autowired`, 0 Lombok,
0 `System.out`, 0 `printStackTrace`, 85 из 162 транзакций `readOnly`,
0 `@Transactional` на контроллерах, 150 индексов, пул 20, `batch_size` 100,
`lock_timeout` 5s, `open-in-view: false`. Все ссылки на файлы из агентов
и правил проверены на существование.

## Чего не тронул и почему

**`MarketplaceAdapter` не удалён.** Он мёртв (ноль ссылок), и его удаление
безопасно — но в нём записано рассуждение о моделях площадок (pull у Авито,
push у Дрома, auto.ru закрыт с февраля 2022). Удалять или оставить как заметку
— ваше решение; я привёл его в правилах как живой пример ловушки.

## Summary
- Follow-up to #163. Auto-share (`startNewMatch`) and auto-publish (`maybeAutoPublishTournament`) only ever ran going forward from when each shipped — a tournament match or tournament created *before* either existed stays exactly as invisible to co-owners as they were built to prevent, since nothing about scoring or viewing them afterward ever revisited that decision. Reported live: an in-progress match created before #163 still couldn't be opened by a co-owner, and its tournament's name still wasn't resolving on Home.
- `openMatch` (`src/components/cricketScorer.js`) now mints a missing share code the moment the match's own real owner opens it. `loadMatch` succeeding via their own `/users/{uid}/matches` copy (not the "known match" fallback, which can be a stale snapshot) is what makes this safe — it means this really is that match's own scorer, on the one path that can legitimately decide to share it. Reuses the exact same club/federation qualification `startNewMatch` already applies (club with >1 member, or federation with ≥1 co-owner).
- Opening a tournament — both Home's own tournament cards and the Cups tab, now routed through one shared `openTournamentDetail` helper instead of two near-identical inline handlers — similarly fires `maybeAutoPublishTournament`, which already safely no-ops for anything private, already-published, or a series. Previously this only ran on creation and on every edit, so an old, never-edited tournament could never get its public `tournamentMatches/{tournamentId}` doc created, and its name could never resolve for an outside account (`foreignTournamentNames`).
- No Firestore rules changes — both self-heals write through the exact same `sharedMatches`/`tournamentMatches` paths the manual Share flow and #163's creation-time auto-share already use.

Note: this only fixes it forward from the next time the *real* owning account opens the match/tournament — an account with no legitimate access to either (never having created or been shared them) still correctly can't see them, by design.

author: andrianm28
body:
## Summary
Closes a Critical, empirically-verified vulnerability found by two independent audit agents (security + financial correctness): the mock payment provider's webhook-signing key fell back to the literal `"mock-server-key-for-dev"` when `MOCK_MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` was unset. That literal is committed in plaintext across this repo's own tests and plan docs, `.env.production` never overrides it, and `POST /donations` requires no authentication — so any anonymous internet user could forge a signed "paid" webhook for any donation amount on any campaign, with real financial consequences (the fabricated total becomes withdrawable through the normal disbursement flow).

Fixes at both call sites that constructed the mock provider (`donations.ts` and `disbursements.ts`), mirroring the exact fail-closed pattern already used correctly for the Sumopod provider in the same file.

## Test plan
- [x] New regression test forges a webhook signed with the exact leaked literal against a real pending donation, with `MOCK_MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` genuinely unset in a fresh subprocess (not just filtered locally)
- [x] Verified with a real revert-then-restore check: reintroduced the old fallback, confirmed the test fails (catches the forged webhook being accepted); restored the fix, confirmed it passes
- [x] Full backend suite: 365/365 pass
- [x] `bun run lint` / `bun run typecheck`: clean

## Deployment note
This requires setting a real `MOCK_MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` in `.env.production` and restarting `galangdana-api.service` — I'll do that immediately after this merges and deploys, since production currently has no value set for this variable at all (same underlying gap the vulnerability exploited).
