author: ianmayo
body:
Fixes #256 (R9-04, **Medium**).

Fifth of the Medium series. **Based on #292** (→ #291 → #289 → #288) — merge those first.

⚠️ **This PR changes numbers analysts see.** Displayed speeds rise by 1.3%.

## The decision

R9-04 is a domain question, not a bug, and the review's only position was that the three sources must agree. I put it to Ian, who chose **1500 m/s** — the nominal seawater figure sonar training works to, and the value the documentation already stated.

## The problem

Three sources disagreed:

| Source | Said |
|---|---|
| `utils/doppler.js` code | **1481** (fresh water at 20 °C) |
| the same function's JSDoc | 1500 |
| `docs/Doppler-Calc.md` | 1500 |

Nothing in `src/` passes `speedOfSound`, so 1481 was what every analyst saw — 1.3% below what the specification described, with no way to tell from the screen. The review's worked example moves from **576.1 → 583.2 kts**.

## The change

The constant is now named `DEFAULT_SPEED_OF_SOUND = 1500`, and the signature carries no literal of its own to drift from. It stays module-private: it has no caller outside this module, and exporting it purely for tests would add a sixth module to the `ts-unused-exports` ratchet.

**The second half of the finding is also fixed.** `Doppler-Calc.md` claimed the readout is in m/s, when the LED is labelled `Speed (kts)` and `DopplerMode.updateSpeedLED` multiplies by `MS_TO_KNOTS`. The speed really is computed and stored in m/s, so the doc now says both things and says which is which.

## Keeping them in step

The defect was never a wrong number — it was three different ones. Five unit tests read the code constant, the JSDoc default, the specification's value and the specification's units claim, then assert the behaviour those texts describe.

Each guard was verified to fail when its source is drifted back:

| Drift applied | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_SPEED_OF_SOUND` → 1481 | 5 (3 behavioural + the constant guard + the cross-check) |
| JSDoc default → 1481 | "the JSDoc default matches the code constant" |
| `Doppler-Calc.md` → 1481 m/s and "in m/s" | the value guard and the units guard |

The "custom speed of sound" test now passes **1481** rather than 1500, so it still proves the parameter is read instead of accidentally re-asserting the default.

## Files

- `src/utils/doppler.js` — the named constant, corrected JSDoc
- `docs/Doppler-Calc.md` — 1500 with its provenance; the knots/m-s distinction stated
- `tests/unit/doppler.test.js` — updated expectations, 5 new drift guards
- `tests/doppler-mode.spec.js` — the two end-to-end formula checks

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `yarn typecheck` | ✅ |
| `yarn lint` | ✅ |
| `yarn hygiene` | ✅ all five ratchets at baseline |
| `yarn test:unit` | ✅ 208/208 (was 203) |
| `yarn test` | ✅ 399/399 |

author: tgorka
body: Epic 67's spine and four stories, stacked on #331 (epic 66). Three reports from the iPhone — nothing on the island or lock screen when the phrase is heard, no spoken answer unless keeper is opened, no way to say "stop" — and one measured cause behind two of them. **The one sentence:** the turn was finished by a screen that is not there — so when keeper was not in front it heard you, and then waited for you to come and look. **What was measured.** After `Heard` the turn was the webview's: `Effect::SendText` was a no-op in core, the send was `BotVoiceMic`'s effect and the speak was the pane's reaction to the stream's close. WebKit runs the WebContent process only for a visible view or a page that itself plays or captures (`WebPageProxy.cpp:3823-3893`); native audio in the Rust host sets neither flag. With the screen locked the turn parked in `Heard` until the pane's JS ran again. The lock screen had one surface (the island) the free-team build cannot draw, and the port threw the words away on barge-in. - **67.1 The turn lives in Rust.** `SendText` performed by the shell to a chosen voice target (the bot under Bots, else the pinned bot most recently talked to, else a refusal with its remedy), one stream code path, the close drives Speak. The webview observes; `speakIfHeard`, the `onHeard` hand-off and `voice_speak` are gone. Proven through a fake port and a fake bot host with no webview listener anywhere. - **67.2 The lock screen says what keeper heard.** A local notification, fixed identifier replaced in place — Heard / Thinking / Answer (first sentence) / Listening stopped — posted only when `UIApplication` says the app is not active, read on the main thread; cleared on turn end or foreground. No extension, no App ID. - **67.3 "Stop", and an ear that does not hear itself.** `SpeechDetected` carries its words; a stop phrase (default "stop", three letters, normalised) mid-answer ends the turn and re-arms the phrase; other speech still asks (FR-403). Session mode `voiceChat` explicitly; an 800 ms tail gate after every utterance drops the app's own voice and records each drop in the ring. - **67.4 The record.** Disclosure and `docs/ios.md` byte-identical; D-17; DW-222 re-scoped, DW-243…246. **Proven:** 4264 Rust + 5760 frontend, clippy/tsc/lint/design clean; macOS gate on hesperia; iOS + desktop checks with all three stories' shell code; **installed and running on kalypso**. **Owed on hardware (AD-210):** the run with the screen locked — phrase, question, banner, spoken answer, "stop" — and the ring afterwards. `docs/ios.md` "What the run on kalypso must show" lists the events in order; DW-243 is open until that run says whether keeper hears its own tail. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the iPhone voice turn so it finishes with the screen locked. Previously the turn parked in `Heard` until the webview ran again — sending and speaking were the webview's job, and WebKit suspends the webview when the screen is locked — so keeper heard you and then waited for you to come and look. Now Rust drives the whole turn and the webview only observes. **Turn behavior** - A heard question is sent by Rust to the chosen voice target: the bot picked under Bots, else the pinned bot most recently talked to, else a refusal with its remedy. - When keeper isn't in front, the lock screen shows a local notification — Heard / Thinking / Answer / Listening stopped — replaced in place and cleared on turn end or foreground; no extension or App ID needed. - Saying the stop phrase (default "stop") during an answer ends the turn and re-arms the wake phrase; other speech mid-answer still asks a question (FR-403). - The session mode is explicitly `voiceChat`, and an 800 ms tail gate drops the app's own voice and records each drop in the event ring. **Settings and rollout** - New keys `bots.voice_target` and `bots.stop_phrase` default to the old behavior, so existing installs keep working. - The webview's `speakIfHeard`, the `onHeard` hand-off, and `voice_speak` are removed; so is the composer's `heard` prop. - A hardware run with the screen locked is still owed (AD-210); `docs/ios.md` lists the events the run must confirm. Written for commit 415e47255faa2a7f4a1fad1ac194255b7a700aed. Summary will update on new commits.

## What

Registers `tauri-plugin-single-instance` in the companion's Tauri builder (first in the plugin chain, as the plugin requires). A second launch now hands off to the already-running instance and exits instead of opening another window.

## Why

On Windows, launching the companion again while it was already running opened a second window — two capture loops, two trays, two updaters.

Since the app starts hidden in the tray, the handoff callback calls the existing `show(app)` helper, so relaunching shows and focuses the running window. That is what a double-click on the shortcut is actually asking for.

- Diff is three lines plus the lockfile: one dependency, one `.plugin(...)`, and the comment explaining the ordering constraint.
- `_args` / `_cwd` from the second launch are ignored — nothing consumes CLI args or deep links today.

author: yongchenglow
body:
## Summary

Three related changes, split into two reviewable commits:

1. **Node 26.3.0 → 26.8.1** — bumped in `package.json` `engines.node`. CI extracts this and passes it as `NODE_VERSION` to the Dockerfile and all `setup-node` steps, so no other file needed touching. Verified 26.8.1 is the latest v26 release.
2. **`bun update --latest`** — 397 packages. Notable majors: `vitest` 4→5, `typescript` 6→7, `@vitejs/plugin-react` 5→6, `undici` 6→8, `yargs` 16→18, `@types/node` 25→26.
3. **Gitleaks secret scanning** in CI.

## Fixes needed to keep the build green

- **`test/setup.ts`** — imported the default `@testing-library/jest-dom` entry, whose `index.d.ts` only references `jest.d.ts` and therefore augments *jest's* types, not vitest's. This silently worked on vitest 4, but vitest 5 changed `Assertion` to take two type parameters, so the augmentation stopped applying and ~60 `toBeInTheDocument` / `toBeDisabled` calls failed type-check. Switched to the dedicated `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` subpath.
- **`biome.json`** — Biome 2.5.12 deprecated `linter.recommended` in favour of `linter.preset`. Applied via `biome migrate --write`.

## Gitleaks placement

Added as a reusable workflow scanning **full git history** (`fetch-depth: 0`), wired in as a gate **before** the Docker build — an image should never be pushed from a commit containing a leaked secret. This is deliberately separate from the existing Trivy scan, which is image-based and runs post-build.

`.gitleaks.toml` allowlists build artifacts and lockfiles: minified vendor bundles under `.next/` (cytoscape/mermaid) trip the `generic-api-key` entropy heuristic and produced 37 false positives locally. Those paths are untracked, so they never reach the history CI actually scans. Scoping also cuts a local `gitleaks dir` run from 1.13 GB / 2m46s to 1.92 MB / 375ms.

## Verification

- `bun run build` — passes
- `bun run test` — 110/110 pass
- `bun run check` (biome) — clean
- `bun run knip` — clean
- `gitleaks git` — no leaks across all 327 commits
- Dev server smoke test — `/`, `/blog`, `/about` all return 200, no runtime errors (type-check alone wouldn't catch runtime breaks from the Next 16 / framer-motion 13 / lucide 1.x majors)

## Note

`CLAUDE.md` and `next-env.d.ts` were modified by `next dev`, not by hand — Next 16 regenerates an agent-rules block on every dev run. Included so the tree doesn't stay perpetually dirty.

author: oohasikazuyuki
body:
## 概要

Issue #667 / SHOKUSU-32 への**緊急対応**。2026-08-31 に `/MUserInfo/login` へ海外の単一IPから3分間421回のSQLインジェクション脆弱性スキャンを受けた件に対し、入口で国外からのアクセスを遮断する。

**このPRは nginx 設定 1ファイル（135行）のみです。** アプリのコードは一切含みません。

## なぜ新しいファイルなのか

本番のリクエスト経路は次のとおりです。

```
Internet:443
   → ホストnginx  /etc/nginx/conf.d/kamaho-shokusu.jp.conf
   → 127.0.0.1:8091
   → kamakura-shokusu_web コンテナ
```

最前段のホストnginx設定は**これまでリポジトリ管理外**で、サーバー上でのみ管理されていました。そのため `docker/nginx/nginx.conf` を変更しても本番の挙動は一切変わりません。本番でそのコンテナは `Exited (128)` のまま4週間停止しており、経路上に存在しないためです。

「レビューは通るが本番は守られない」状態を解消するため、**ホストnginx設定の正本をリポジトリへ移します**。以後、本番の設定変更はこのファイル経由で行えばレビュー可能になります。

## 変更内容

### 国内アクセス制限

nginx の `geoip2` モジュールで接続元IPから国コードを引き、日本以外を 403 で遮断します。

```nginx
geoip2 /usr/share/GeoIP/dbip-country-lite.mmdb {
    auto_reload 5m;
    $geoip2_country_code country iso_code;
}

map $geoip2_country_code $is_jp {
    default 0;   # 日本以外は遮断
    JP      1;
    ""      1;   # 判定不能時は通す（DB欠損での全断を防ぐ）
}
```

遮断は `location /`（サイト全体）と `location ~* ^/m-?user-?info/login/?$`（ログイン画面）の2箇所です。

データベースは **DB-IP の無料版**を使用します。MaxMind と異なり**アカウント登録もライセンスキーも不要**です。`auto_reload` により、データベースを差し替えても nginx の reload は要りません。

### ログインのレート制限

POSTのみ10リクエスト/分。GET/HEADはキーが空になり計上されないため、ログイン画面の表示は制限されません。

## 意図的に制限の対象外にしている経路

**ここを塞ぐと障害になります。**

| パス | 理由 |
|---|---|
| `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` | Let's Encrypt の認証局は海外から接続する。塞ぐと証明書の自動更新が失敗し、**期限切れでサイト全体が停止する** |
| `/healthz` | 死活監視は海外のGitHub Actionsランナーから実行される。塞ぐと**誤検知のアラートが鳴り続ける** |

## 検証

Ubuntu 24.04 に nginx と `libnginx-mod-http-geoip2` を導入し、実際の DB-IP データベース（8MB）を配置した環境で確認しました。`nginx -t` 成功。

本番の監査ログに実際に記録されているIPで判定を照合しています。

| IP | 監査ログでの実績 | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| `122.136.188.132` | 攻撃元・421件 | **403（遮断）** |
| `122.208.143.223` | 正規利用者・40件 | 通過 |
| `180.14.255.248` | 正規利用者・20件 | 通過 |
| `118.9.96.93` | 正規利用者・15件 | 通過 |
| `133.106.34.1` | 正規利用者・携帯回線 | 通過 |
| `103.26.27.191` | 正規利用者 | 通過 |
| `8.8.8.8` | 米国（参考） | **403（遮断）** |
| 判定不能なIP | — | 通過（フェイルオープン） |

## マージ後の作業

**このPRのマージだけでは nginx に反映されません。** `deployment.yml` は発火しますが、変更が `infra/nginx/` 配下の設定ファイルのみでアプリのコードを含まないため、コンテナの再作成は発生せず実質何も変わりません。

反映には本番サーバー上での作業が必要です。**ダウンタイムはありません。**

```bash
# 初回のみ
sudo apt install -y libnginx-mod-http-geoip2
sudo mkdir -p /usr/share/GeoIP
curl -fsSL "https://download.db-ip.com/free/dbip-country-lite-$(date +%Y-%m).mmdb.gz" \
  | sudo gunzip -c | sudo tee /usr/share/GeoIP/dbip-country-lite.mmdb >/dev/null

# 反映
sudo cp /home/ubuntu/shokusuu1/infra/nginx/kamaho-shokusu.jp.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/
sudo nginx -t                    # 通らなければ絶対に reload しない
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

切り戻しは2箇所の `if ($is_jp = 0) { return 403; }` をコメントアウトして reload するだけです。

## マージ前に確認・判断が必要なこと

- [ ] **海外からの正規アクセスの有無。** 有効化すると国外IPからは一切利用できなくなります。出張先や一部の格安SIM・VPN経由が国外判定になる可能性があります。復旧にはサーバー操作が必要です。
- [ ] **`uptime-check.yml` の監視先変更。** 現在 `https://kamaho-shokusu.jp/` を海外ランナーから監視しており、有効化すると403で誤検知が鳴り続けます。`/healthz` への変更が必要ですが、「nginx設定のみ」の方針により本PRの範囲外としています。

## マージ後に必要な追随作業

- **main → develop の同期。** 本PRは main へ直接入るため、develop にこの設定が入りません。マージ後に同期PRが必要です。
- **アプリ側の防御。** ログイン試行回数制限・クライアントIP判定の是正・セッションCookie保護・公開ポートの閉鎖は #669 で実装済みですが、「今回は nginx 設定のみ」の方針によりクローズしています。ブランチ `hotfix/shokusu-32-security` に保持しており、全615テスト通過・CodeRabbit 指摘対応済みの状態です。本PRは入口での遮断、#669 はアプリ側での防御で、両方そろって多層になります。

author: willem445
body:
Slice A of epic #1689: a repo may declare **several** workflows, and a group records **which one it runs**.

`.orrerix/workflow.yml` becomes the workflow named `default`; every `<name>.yml` under `.orrerix/workflows/` is a workflow named `<name>`, same schema, same parser. A repo that has only ever had the plain file is byte-for-byte what it was — the name resolves to the same path and `workflows/` is never opened. `Guardrails.workflow` pins the name in `group.json`, in the same atomic write as the roster it produced, and every group-scoped reader (roster, gate + 30 s reload, board, locks, merge queue, driver, status, the `{{WORKFLOW_PATH}}` template var) resolves through one pair of functions instead of `workflow::load_workflow`, which only ever answered for `default`.

**What to look at.** `workflow_path_named` is the single place a name becomes a file name, and it takes `&WorkflowName` — the signature is what holds the property, since a textual scan cannot see types. `load_active_workflow`/`active_workflow_path` take `(repo, &Guardrails)` rather than `&GroupInfo`, because `create_group_ex` and `promote_orchestrator_cli` choose a file before a `GroupInfo` exists and a second spelling for those two is the drift the pair prevents.

**Decisions worth a reviewer's eye:**

- **`Guardrails.workflow` is a `WorkflowName`, not the `String` the plan specified.** A strengthening, not a semantic change: the compiler, not a scan, is then what keeps a hand-edited `group.json` from naming `../../../etc/x`. `load_group_file` is the one place a persisted string becomes one, and an unusable value falls back to `default` rather than failing the load — a group must stay rejoinable.
- **The plan predicted two residual readers of the `default` file; there is one.** `orch_workflow_preview_sync` was the second and stopped being one in this same slice, because gaining the optional `name` routed its no-name arm through `load_workflow_named`. The residual scan is what noticed — its stale-row assertion refused to carry a row matching nothing. The design note says one, not two. **One earlier commit body on this branch still says "two argued residuals"**; it is superseded, and cannot be edited in place — flagged here for whoever squashes.
- **No launcher wiring, and `docs/orchestration.md` now says so in its own tense.** `create_orchestration`'s wire shape is unchanged and `PromoteConfig` gains no field; the picker is slice D1's. A launcher group runs `default`, a reattaching promote restores what is on disk. Review round 2 caught the manual describing the picker, the naming diagnostic and the shadow warning in the present tense — three capabilities this head does not ship — so it now names the slice and keeps only the layout, naming and resolution rules, which are true today.
- **`{{WORKFLOW_PATH}}` moves for a named workflow.** It renders into `workflow.md` and `block.md` only — neither is `pre222`-fixture-pinned. The four pinned role templates were not touched, and the fixtures did not move.

**The plan's open unknown, confirmed and recorded in the design note:** which path writes a new block's `<id>.md`. `set_advanced_orchestrator` writes **no** instruction files; `spawn_agent_bound` re-renders one block per spawn but never removes one; `write_instruction_files` (create/resume) is the only path that also sweeps a removed block's stale file against `.instruction-files-manifest` (#423). So slice B's `apply_workflow` must call it rather than relying on the per-spawn render.

Part of #1689

All figures below are measured at head `e402567f`, base (merge-base) `34f92793`, unless a line says otherwise.

author: divyamtalwar
body:
The last pull request before tagging **v0.7.0**. Three things: the README images, the release record, and the version cut.

---

## 1 · The three README images

`docs/images/README.md` has specified three images since the Astra release. They now exist.

| File | Where | What it argues |
|---|---|---|
| `constellation.png` | end of *The four bodies* | four bodies, four pins, and that **Astra and Terra are alternatives** — one chosen per delegation |
| `flow.png` | top of *The flow* | one delegation end to end, including the four points where it can stop |
| `refusal.png` | end of *What it will not do* | the same command accepted and refused, with the filesystem untouched |

**Each was checked against the shipped repository rather than accepted on sight.** An earlier pass carried a FABLEWRIGHT wordmark and, in the proof image, two role filenames and a command that do not exist here — `orrery-sol-researcher.toml`, `orrery-terra-ops.toml`, `fw install`. Publishing that would have put a claim on the front page that the shipped files contradict, under the words "LAUNCH PROOF".

What is committed uses the real command, the three real filenames, and output whose load-bearing lines are verbatim from an actual run — the `INSTALL PASSED` line, the `ERROR: Astra destination is conflict` line, and `exit 1`. The narrower progress lines between them are a readable dramatization of steps the installer genuinely performs (destination classification, the legacy-Luna check, the post-install exactness re-check) rather than literal stdout.

Alt text describes content rather than naming files, so all three claims survive for anyone reading without images.

---

## 2 · The changelog catches up

**Four pull requests merged into `main` without a changelog entry between them** — #9, #8, #7 and #15. The `Unreleased` section described only the Astra lane, so the three most user-visible additions since 0.6.0 existed in the code and the README but nowhere in the release record. A changelog that omits four merges is worse than none, because it is read as complete.

| Merged | Now recorded as |
|---|---|
| #7 capability planner | **Added** — refuses hosts that would silently weaken requested effort or advisor isolation |
| #8 tool-surface review | **Added** — turns "the digest moved" into whether the change is permission-bearing; its baseline is asserted by `validate` so it cannot drift from the digest it explains |
| #9 semantic doctor | **Changed** — `schema: 2`; a marker-only or weakened adapter is no longer reported as healthy |
| #15 toolchain | **Changed** — `typescript` 5.9.2 → 7.0.2 (major, no source changes), with *why it was applied by hand* recorded |

Each entry leads with what the thing **refuses** to do, because on this project that is the part with value.

---

## 3 · The version cut

`Unreleased` becomes **0.7.0**; the three declared versions agree.

Minor, not major: a second native implementation lane and three read-only diagnostics are added, nothing is removed, no interface breaks. Whether this should instead be **1.0.0** is a maintainer's call rather than a semver one — and it is arguably the release that earns it.

---

## Verification

```sh
bun run ci
bun run tag:check -- v0.7.0
```

`VERIFY PASSED` three-role · **82 tests across 6 files, 0 fail** · validate (which link-checks the image paths, so the embeds and the files agree) · sbom now emitting `orrery-0.7.0.cdx.json` (18 packaged files, **0 runtime dependencies**) · release-check · **tag-check passes for v0.7.0**.

## Risk

Documentation, images, and version metadata. No code, no behaviour change.

author: x0ba
body:
`skl capture ` promotes a project-local skill into the **personal library**. **Library path (product correction):** `{Paths.data_dir}/skills//` — default `~/.local/share/skl/skills/`, override via `SKL_DATA_DIR`. SQLite index stays in `state.db` under the data dir. **`.agents/skills` is not the library.** It remains the project link destination (default `use`) and a home discovery root for `init`. ## Behavior 1. Resolve the skill under project roots (`.agents/skills` + sticky extras) 2. Copy into `~/.local/share/skl/skills//` 3. Default: replace the project path with a **symlink** to that library path 4. `--keep-copy`: leave the project dir as a real copy 5. `--force` overwrite / `--as ` rename 6. Symlink already pointing at the library skill → no-op success (refresh `state.db`) 7. Name clash without `--force`/`--as` → error (never prompts, TTY or not) 8. Missing `SKILL.md` → clear error 9. After local success, fail-soft `auto_sync::maybe_run` (`capture`); API down does not fail the verb 10. Index the captured skill in `state.db` (source `agents`) ## Tests Unit tests for symlink no-op, clash error, `--force`, `--as`, `--keep-copy`, fail-soft dead API, extra dest resolution, and name safety. `cargo test -p skl` green (144 tests).
  
> [!NOTE] > ### Add `skl capture` command to promote project skills into personal library > - Adds the `capture` command, which copies a project skill directory into `{data_dir}/skills/`, optionally overwrites existing library skills (`--force`), optionally keeps the project copy (`--keep-copy`), and replaces the source with a symlink to the library entry by default > - Accepts inputs as existing paths, project-relative paths, or bare skill names resolved against project destinations and sticky extras > - Successful captures trigger piggyback auto-sync; auto-sync errors are discarded and do not fail the capture > - Updates `resolve_skill` in `use_cmd.rs` to check the data-dir library before the DB-index fallback, and adds `LocalDb.upsert_skill` for transactional replacement of one indexed skill and its file hashes > - Risk: `capture.replace_with_library_symlink` removes the original source path before creating the symlink; reviewers should confirm `remove_path` handles all filesystem types correctly, and that `upsert_skill` in `local/db.rs` only removes the targeted name/source pair > > > > Macroscope summarized a5b25ff. > >

author: mjjsf
body:
Two deletions: the `<span className="device-indicator">` in `PhoneFrame.tsx` and its rule in `globals.css`. Nothing else referenced it — the one test that did, *"the home indicator does not swallow bottom-nav clicks"*, was replaced when the nav became inert. The bezel and side buttons stay; they weren't part of the ask.

## Why it came and went

Worth recording, because "appears on the first frame and eventually disappears on the recommendations frame" reads like a render bug and isn't one.

The element was **identical on both screens** — present, `visibility: visible`, `opacity: 1`, same position. What differed was the painted pixel:

| screen | painted colour where the bar sits | `elementFromPoint` there |
|---|---|---|
| Start | `rgb(176,176,176)` — the bar | `<div class="screen-enter">`, z-index auto |
| Recommendations | `rgb(243,243,243)` — the dock | `<section … z-20>`, the RefineDock |

`.phone-frame` is `position: relative` with `z-index: auto` and `overflow: hidden` — **none of which creates a stacking context**. So the dock's `z-20` and the nav's `z-30` join `.device`'s context, created by its `transform`, and paint above the indicator's `z-index: auto`. On Start nothing overlapping it carries a z-index, so it showed.

## What I deliberately left alone

**The stacking leak.** With the indicator gone, `.device` has a single child, so nothing can be overlapped and adding `isolation: isolate` to `.phone-frame` would change no pixel. Real, but not worth a change here.

**A test asserting it stays absent.** Every other guard in this suite exists because a specific bug reached a release; a deletion nothing depends on isn't that.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `.device-indicator` in the DOM | 0 on both `/` and `/chat/` |
| `.device` children | exactly one (`phone-frame`) |
| Screenshot | bar gone from Start; recommendations screen unchanged, since the dock already covered it |
| Nav geometry | still 16px from the frame's left, right and bottom (`framing.spec.ts`) |
| `lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `test`, `check:static`, `build` | pass |
| e2e | **40 passed**, three consecutive runs |
| `smoke` against local preview | all checks pass |

body:
# Phase 19B — Teaching load matrix and bulk assignment

Branch: `feature/teaching-load-matrix-bulk-phase-19b`
Base: `d5b0c19cd38f5add08273e0c88efe7da0c54e9cd`
Review-fix baseline: `41bbdc63554eefc54757843351dc15db600c0b08`.
Delivery HEAD and Preview are recorded in [Draft PR #35](https://github.com/smartschoolduhok/smart-school/pull/35)'s delivery status (avoids a self-referential commit hash in this file).

## Delivered workflow

- Normal loads view starts with active class cards sorted by order_index then ID.
- Cards distinguish active subject/section counts from expected **applicable** cells. Disabled cells do not count as missing. Completion counts only active, same-school employees with canonical `role = 'teacher'`; a non-NULL ID alone is insufficient.
- Separate `TeachingLoadMatrixTab`: canonical subject rows and section columns; section-specific subjects are disabled elsewhere. No-section classes use “الصف بالكامل” / NULL.
- Explicit periods/teacher apply-all, individual overrides, teacher clearing, explicit deactivation, row/whole-draft reset, search and missing/no-teacher/changed filters.
- Empty periods retain existing values or do not create missing loads. NULL teacher does not deactivate.
- No autosave. Preview shows old/new values, exact counts and warnings/blockers, including locked lesson impact. Only a valid preview offers “حفظ جميع الأنصبة”.
- Success clears draft/preview, reloads loads and readiness, refreshes cards and keeps selected class.
- Existing individual editor remains behind “تعديل متقدم”.
- Scope-keyed mounts and monotonic generations guard school/year/class ABA and async loads/copy/preview/apply. Draft changes invalidate preview immediately. School/year/tab/back navigation and beforeunload protect unsaved work. Cards exclude previous-school/year props during transitions.

## API, RBAC and canonical behavior

All four routes retain `ACADEMIC_MANAGEMENT_ROLES`: system_admin, school_owner, principal, vice_principal, registrar. Teacher/accountant are forbidden. System admin writes require an explicit active school; tenant users remain fixed to their authenticated school.

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/api/timetable/teaching-load-matrix` | Scoped class, sections, subjects, active teachers, canonical class loads, summary and revision |
| POST `/api/timetable/teaching-load-matrix/preview` | Strict parse, fresh canonical read, deterministic plan, zero writes |
| POST `/api/timetable/teaching-load-matrix/apply` | Explicit confirmation, fresh parse/plan, atomic revision assertion and writes |
| POST `/api/timetable/teaching-load-matrix/copy-preview` | Distinct same-school source year, canonical ID matching, read-only proposed draft |

Reject unknown fields, malformed IDs, duplicates, unsupported actions, invalid periods and more than 500 changes. Teacher eligibility uses `employees.role = 'teacher'`, not a second classification.

All new reference reads/joins are scoped in SQL. Missing and foreign IDs return indistinguishable errors; foreign names are never loaded. The private planner needs the full selected school/year schedule to detect cross-class teacher conflicts; the public GET returns only selected-class loads.

Upserts preserve active IDs and updater audit. If only inactive history exists, create a NEW active row, consistent with the individual-create API; no implicit reactivation. Omissions do nothing. Deactivation is explicit and blocked when ANY scheduled entries remain.

Copy matches class/subject/section IDs, never names. Periods-only preserves target teachers/new NULL. Periods-and-teachers copies eligible teachers, otherwise substitutes NULL with an explicit warning. Unavailable subjects/sections are reported separately. Omissions do not deactivate target configuration. No entries, locks, availability, constraints, days, slots, revisions or versions are copied. Accepting copy fills a draft; normal preview/confirm remains mandatory.

## Authorized migration 0027

`migrations/0027_timetable_safe_teacher_reassignment.sql` replaces only the absolute employee-change prohibition from 0025's `trg_timetable_loads_preserve_entries`. That old trigger rejected both safe NULL → teacher and teacher A → B changes whenever entries existed.

The replacement retains school/year/class/section/subject identity protection. New `trg_timetable_loads_validate_teacher_reassignment` is an AFTER UPDATE guard evaluating the resulting destination teacher's complete school/year schedule:

- Valid, active same-school canonical teacher required.
- Collisions and unavailable-period checks include preserved historical entries, matching the canonical validator.
- Daily/working-day/consecutive limits aggregate ALL destination loads and ALL lessons on the reassigned load.
- Capacity uses active days and active lesson slots. Breaks/unoccupied active lessons reset consecutive runs; inactive slots are excluded.
- Preferred/avoid remain warnings.
- Teacher → NULL is allowed; same-teacher updates have no new reassignment-specific validation.
- SQL ABORT rolls back data, audit/timestamps and revision effects.
- Existing entry validation, weekly lower bound, unique indexes, foreign keys, locks and immutable versions are unchanged.

No old migration was edited. 0027 has zero CRLF bytes. It has NOT been applied remotely.

## Combined planning and atomic execution

Preview checks the COMBINED final state, not independent updates against old assignments. Apply independently recomputes that plan.

One D1 batch contains:

1. Existing revision assertion, before any load writes.
2. One conditional set-based UPDATE temporarily clears only changing, previously non-NULL teachers, using exact affected IDs from a bound JSON array.
3. Separate non-empty groups: one INSERT ... SELECT FROM json_each for creates; one UPDATE ... FROM json_each for final updates; one UPDATE with JSON ID membership for explicit deactivations. Unchanged cells are excluded. No existing load is recreated.
4. Advance revision (including all-unchanged confirmed requests), remove assertion, return revision from the same batch.

This supports coupled swaps without transient collisions. No trigger disabling, general bypass, entry deletion or unaffected-load mutation. Any failure rolls back temporary NULLs, final writes, audit and revision. Two clients cannot apply the same revision. Old solver proposals fail the existing assertion.

The entire write batch is **4–8 statements**, independent of changed-cell count, up to the unchanged supported maximum of 500. The expected-revision assertion is always first. All triggers remain enabled and run per affected row. Five bound parameters at most per statement (one JSON value plus school/year/class/user); SQL text is fixed and contains no interpolated cell values. Null JSON values remain SQL NULL.

The complete successful HTTP apply request executes **19–23 D1 statements**, including 2 authentication reads, 1 active-school validation read, 12 canonical reads and 4–8 batch members. This leaves at least **27 statements of headroom** below D1 Free's 50-query limit. No subscription assumption/change. Sources: [D1 limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/), [atomic batch behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/), [D1 JSON table expressions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/sql-api/query-json/), [SQLite UPDATE FROM](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_update.html).

The test adapter counts **executed statements**, not prepare() or batch() calls. It throws if a request exceeds 50; every real Worker API test resets/enforces this budget per request. A separate guard test reuses one prepared statement 51 times in a batch and proves the limit is enforced.

| Apply case | Changes | Write-batch statements | Complete HTTP statements | Max bound parameters |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Small creates, 3 × 2 | 6 | 5 | 20 | 5 |
| Medium creates, 12 × 4 | 48 | 5 | 20 | 5 |
| Large creates, 20 × 8 | 160 | 5 | 20

author: kevdbg
body:
Le collecteur X ne lisait que le fil d'un compte suivi. Le board veut les deux :
des comptes choisis, **et** une recherche pour trouver la matière qu'aucun d'eux
ne porte.

## `q:<termes>`, la convention qui existait déjà

`hackernews.py` accepte `q:kubernetes` depuis toujours. Rien n'est réinventé : le
même préfixe, le même `@` pour le plancher, et le `sources.yaml` du studio
déclare une recherche X exactement comme une recherche Hacker News.

```
simonw
karpathy@500
q:agent framework@50
```

Le nom de source garde son préfixe, donc l'archive range sous `x/q:agent
framework` et le studio déclare `x/q:agent framework:50`. Rien ne se traduit d'un
bout à l'autre de la chaîne.

## Le crawling reste doux, et par trois choix

**Une requête au lieu de deux.** Une recherche n'a pas d'identifiant de compte à
résoudre : pas d'appel à `UserByScreenName`. Elle coûte donc *moins* qu'un compte
suivi.

**Une page, jamais le curseur.** `SearchTimeline` en rend un ; le suivre
ramènerait des centaines de publications au prix d'une requête par page, et
dessinerait un motif de trafic que rien ne distingue d'un aspirateur. Le
collecteur passe une fois par jour et cherche de la matière, pas un corpus.

**Le rythme ne change pas.** Il appartient à l'ordonnanceur, qui tient déjà un
intervalle, sa gigue aléatoire, et un frein qui s'étire quand X annonce son
compteur — plus un repli exponentiel borné sur `429`. C'est ce que `xcrowler`
obtient par des pauses aléatoires dans un navigateur ; ici c'est du code partagé
par les six médias, et il s'applique aux recherches sans une ligne de plus.

**`Top` et non `Latest`.** Le chronologique rend tout ce qui a été publié, y
compris ce que personne n'a lu. La ligne éditoriale du studio trie sur
l'engagement en aval de toute façon.

## L'identifiant de requête n'a pas de défaut, et c'est délibéré

Les deux autres ont été relevés sur une vraie session le 31/08/2026. Celui de
`SearchTimeline` ne l'a pas été. **En écrire un qui ressemble à un identifiant le
ferait passer pour mesuré** : toutes les recherches rendraient `404`, ce qui se
lit « les identifiants ont tourné » et envoie chercher du mauvais côté.

Il se relève une fois, dans l'inspecteur d'un onglet connecté, onglet Réseau, sur
une recherche lancée à la main : la requête `SearchTimeline` le porte dans son
chemin. Il se colle dans les options, comme les deux autres. Vide, les recherches
se taisent **en disant où le trouver**, et les comptes suivis continuent : ce sont
deux réglages, pas un.

## Vérifié

Toute la suite du dépôt : 240 cas, 0 échec. Six cas neufs sur la recherche.
`ruff` passe sur `x.py` ; les 12 avertissements du dépôt préexistent sur `main`.

**Chaque cas a été vu rouge avant d'être vu vert**, en passant `Latest` au lieu
de `Top`, en préfixant une recherche par une arobase, en retirant la garde de
l'identifiant absent, et en retirant l'aiguillage qui distingue une recherche
d'un compte.

Un cas tient aussi la frontière que le message d'erreur doit respecter :
« x : @q:agent framework a rendu 403 » enverrait quelqu'un chercher un compte qui
n'existe pas.

## Ce qui n'a pas bougé

La clause 4 de l'ADR 0036 autorise le cookie de session pour lire X en
automatique. Lire une recherche est le même geste que lire un fil : même session,
même famille de points d'entrée. Le coût déjà écrit ne bouge pas non plus :
l'accès automatisé hors API reste contraire aux conditions de X, et le compte
encourt la suspension.

## Summary

Follow-up to #1614 covering the two halves of #1612 it named as remaining work.

**`independence_verified` propagation (#1612 part 2).** The findings-mechanics helper reads `independence_verified` only from the reviewer return entry (`independent_reviewer()` in `findings-mechanics.py`), so when the orchestrator synthesizes or reconciles a return from on-disk artifacts, carrying the field in the artifact alone silently drops an `adversarial-<provider>` peer from `independent_reviewers`. `finish-review.md` now instructs copying `independence_verified: true` from the peer artifact into the synthetic return entry. Docs-side of the issue's "either, not both" - the helper-only-reads-stdin interface makes the alternative (accept from either location) a payload-format change; happy to do that instead if you prefer enforcement over contract.

**Interpreter-aware dependency evidence (#1612 part 3).** `subagent-template.md` gains a false-positive suppression class: before filing a dependency/import mismatch, verify under the project's own interpreter (venv/toolchain/container) and check the declared package's metadata (`Requires-Dist`) for transitive provision. A bare host-interpreter import failure proves nothing about the project's environment - the real defect in the issue's example was a routine invoking `python` that was not on PATH.

author: puzzlex5
body:
Claude red-team audit identified a real blind spot: some Seoul support offices expose recruitment postings on CMS boards even when the standard FUS/JOL11 surface is empty. The current supplemental recovery only consumes shallow homepage discovery, so it cannot prove pagination completeness and can miss posts such as the verified 2026-08-11 Dongbu recruitment notice.

This PR adds a fail-closed deep traversal for independently verified CMS recruitment surfaces (Dongbu, Bukbu, Seongdong-Gwangjin), merges that exact-URL evidence into the existing conservative recovery path, preserves the current persistent-URL-only dedup policy, and makes publication refuse unhealthy/incomplete deep traversal evidence.

Safety properties:
- same-host exact CMS detail URLs only
- 90-day bounded discovery, up to 250 pages
- fail closed on access/pagination ambiguity
- status/result notices filtered before recovery and rechecked on detail pages
- no semantic title/date auto-dedup; distinct persistent URLs remain distinct postings
- recovery replays on latest main before publication
- PR regression check compiles both scripts, enforces URL-only dedup, and performs a live traversal of configured boards

Do not merge unless the Seoul CMS regression check passes. After merge, the recovery workflow should be allowed to run and the generated deep-discovery report should be inspected before calling the gap closed.

author: badmintoncryer
body:
Closes #57.

## What

35 new rules from the KMS + Secrets Manager + SSM survey (survey comment with the full inventory, rejections and evidence: https://github.com/badmintoncryer/cdk-preflight/issues/57#issuecomment-5548766893).

| service | rules |
|---|---|
| `rules/kms/` (10) | `pf-kms-key-spec-usage`, `pf-kms-key-rotation`, `pf-kms-key-spec-region`, `pf-kms-key-origin`, `pf-kms-key-policy-statement`, `pf-kms-key-policy-lockout`, `pf-kms-key-policy-charset`, `pf-kms-alias-name`, `pf-kms-alias-target`, `pf-kms-replica-primary-arn` |
| `rules/secretsmanager/` (10) | `pf-secretsmanager-secret-string-exclusive`, `pf-secretsmanager-generate-secret-string`, `pf-secretsmanager-replica-regions`, `pf-secretsmanager-kms-key`, `pf-secretsmanager-secret-name`, `pf-secretsmanager-rotation-rules`, `pf-secretsmanager-rotation-lambda`, `pf-secretsmanager-hosted-rotation`, `pf-secretsmanager-rotation-schedule-unique`, `pf-secretsmanager-target-attachment` |
| `rules/ssm/` (15) | `pf-ssm-parameter-name`, `pf-ssm-parameter-tier`, `pf-ssm-parameter-allowed-pattern`, `pf-ssm-parameter-value`, `pf-ssm-parameter-policies`, `pf-ssm-document-name`, `pf-ssm-document-schema`, `pf-ssm-document-content`, `pf-ssm-maintenance-window-cutoff`, `pf-ssm-maintenance-window-schedule`, `pf-ssm-maintenance-window-task`, `pf-ssm-maintenance-window-target`, `pf-ssm-association-schedule`, `pf-ssm-association-targets`, `pf-ssm-association-document` |

Highlights (constraints that live only in doc prose / handler code):

- **Combination tables**: KMS `KeySpec` × `KeyUsage`, SSM `DocumentType` × `schemaVersion`, Maintenance Window `TaskType` × `TaskInvocationParameters` block, `ResourceType` × target keys.
- **Region / account binding (`deploy_region`, new `deploy_account`)**: SM2 keys outside China, alias targets and replica primaries in other regions/accounts, a `ReplicaKey` pointing at a `Key` in the same stack (always fails), secret replicas into the deploy region, rotation Lambdas in other regions, SSM parameter names whose ARN would exceed 1011 characters (the limit depends on the region name length).
- **DSL semantics**: KMS key policy lockout check (who can still call `PutKeyPolicy`), Secrets Manager rotation `cron()`/`rate()` acceptance rules, SSM document content (steps, plugins/actions, parameter declarations and `{{ ref }}` resolution, Automation step links, Session properties), SSM parameter policies, Maintenance Window / Association cron acceptance sets (the association one is far narrower than the maintenance-window one).
- **Cross-resource**: `SecretTargetAttachment` needs a JSON-shaped secret; associations against in-template documents check declared/required parameters, `DocumentVersion`, Session type, `SyncCompliance: MANUAL`, Automation targets.

## Mechanism changes

- `deployEnvironmentModule(region, accountId)` now also injects `deploy_account` when the account id is concrete (`src/private/enforce.ts`, test harness injects `123456789012`). Rules read it as `data.cdk_preflight.deploy_account`; absent means "assume any account is ours".
- AGENTS.md / the survey skill record the new engine facts: 1024-column source line cap, `input.template.transforms`, probe-process hygiene, and "call the service API first" triage.

## Verification

- Duplication guard: every fail fixture is clean on the bare engine (rules.test.ts).
- 22 inline branch tests (`describe('kms / secretsmanager / ssm rules')`) cover the table/cron/policy branches a single fixture cannot.
- Real-deploy gate: `bench/verify-rule.sh` for all 35 rules in ap-northeast-1 — see each `meta.yaml#repro.evidence` (35/35 verified: every fail fixture ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, every pass fixture CREATE_COMPLETE).

author: wongpatrick
body:
## Summary
Resolves backlog task 54: Consolidates duplicated utility patterns across the backend and decomposes oversized "god files" (>400 lines) into focused, single-responsibility modules while maintaining full backwards compatibility via facade re-exports. Also adds cooperative asyncio event loop yielding during intensive image audit scans to prevent Electron frontend heartbeat timeouts.

## Details

### 1. Extracted Shared Core Utilities
- **`app/core/vault_utils.py`**: Consolidated `resolve_vault_root` and `resolve_all_vault_roots` into a single module, replacing 5 duplicated implementations across `crud/set.py`, `audit_service.py`, `import_service.py`, `set_service.py`, and `api/audit.py`.
- **`app/core/parsing.py`**: Consolidated `parse_set_folder_name` and `DASH_SPLIT_PATTERN`, replacing duplicated folder-parsing logic across `library_scan_service.py`, `import_service.py`, and `api/audit.py`.
- **`app/core/image_analysis.py`**: Extracted `calculate_phash` and `calculate_dominant_color` from `audit_service.py` and `import_service.py`.
- **`app/core/constants.py`**: Centralized `THUMBS_DIR = Path("data/thumbnails")`, replacing hardcoded string paths across 4 files.
- **`app/core/utils.py`**: Reused `sanitize_filename` across import and upload workflows.
- **`app/crud/set.py`**: Consolidated `recalculate_set_rollup_tags` with an `additive` parameter to unify tag rollup calculations.

### 2. Decomposed God Files (>400 lines)
- **`set_service.py`** (899 lines) -> Decomposed into:
  - `set_crud_service.py`: CRUD, status changes, cover assignment.
  - `set_filesystem_service.py`: Folder sync, rename, delete, physical reorganization.
  - `set_tagging_service.py`: AI auto-tagging, character/franchise extraction, and manual rollups.
  - `set_service.py`: Backwards-compatible facade re-exporting all functions.
- **`import_service.py`** (778 lines) -> Decomposed into:
  - `import_parser.py`: Metadata detection, path parsing, folder grouping.
  - `import_processor.py`: Ingestion pipeline, background task execution, DB persistence.
  - `import_service.py`: Backwards-compatible facade re-exporting all functions.
- **`audit_service.py`** (638 lines) -> Split into 7 discrete phase runners (`_audit_ghosts_and_corrupted`, `_audit_filesystem_orphans`, `_audit_set_integrity`, `_audit_orphan_db_records`, `_audit_duplicate_paths`, `_match_visual_hashes`, `_backfill_missing_metadata`) with cooperative event-loop yielding (`await asyncio.sleep(0)`) and live progress tracking.
- **`crud/set.py`** (612 lines) -> Extracted batch import logic to `import_processor.py`, re-exporting `batch_import_sets` and `run_batch_import_background` for backwards compatibility.
- **`api/playlists.py`** (602 lines) -> Extracted `cross_vault_playlists.py` for cross-vault rotation logic.
- **`api/images.py`** (564 lines) -> Extracted `api/image_import.py` (import endpoints) and `api/mappers.py` (model to schema mapping).

### 3. Reliability & Fixes
- Added cooperative event-loop yielding (`await asyncio.sleep(0)`) to the audit engine so long CPU-bound image scans (across 66,000+ images) do not starve the asyncio event loop or trigger Electron heartbeat watchdog timeouts.
- Dynamic `SessionLocal` resolution in background workers to respect runtime test monkeypatches.
- Added `backend/db/` to `.gitignore` to prevent generated test thumbnails from being tracked.

## Motivation
High-traffic and large backend files had accumulated duplicated logic and multiple orthogonal responsibilities, making them error-prone to maintain. Splitting them into cohesive modules with preserved facade interfaces improves code clarity and maintainability without breaking any existing consumer APIs or tests.

author: chchatzop
body:
Both found by the full-program audit.

## A host-shaped hard ban was confirmed, listed, and never enforced

`check_user_status()` decided a pattern was "hostmask-shaped" only if it contained `!` or `@`. Anything else was matched against the bare **nick** — and an IRC nick can never contain a dot, so

```
!ban *.dialup.example.com
```

could not match anything, ever. But `!ban` accepted it, reported success, and `db.load_hard_bans()` listed it among the active bans. The admin believed a host was banned; the host walked straight in.

The same shape as #225, where the confirmation and the enforcement disagreed silently — which is the reason `is_over_broad_hard_ban_pattern()` was lifted out to be shared in the first place.

**Three shapes now, matched against three different things:**

| pattern contains | it is | matched against |
|---|---|---|
| `!` or `@` | a full hostmask | the mask |
| `.` or `:` | a host or IP | **the host portion** |
| neither | a nick | the nick |

RFC 2812 allows a nick letters, digits and the specials `` []\`_^{|} `` and nothing else, so what a pattern contains says what it is about.

**Matching the host and not the whole mask is the difference between working and appearing to.** My first attempt matched the full mask, and passed the `*.dialup.example.com` case purely because that pattern's leading `*` swallowed the `nick!ident@` part. A full mask is `nick!ident@host`, so `192.168.1.*` anchored over the whole of it cannot match anything — the IP test is what caught it.

## A bot nick containing `|` broke every cross-bot fetch from that bot

`_sanitize_bot_dir_name()` claimed in its own docstring to apply *"the same discipline"* as `dcc_fetch._sanitize_offer_filename()`, which is a **whitelist**. It was a blacklist: NUL, the two separators, `..` and surrounding dots.

`|` is an ordinary IRC nick character — RFC 2812's specials are `` []\`_^{|} ``, and `Bot|Away` is one of the commonest nick shapes on the network — and is illegal in a Windows path. So `os.makedirs()` on the extraction directory failed with `WinError 123` **after the zip had already come over DCC**:

```
nick 'Bot|Away'   -> dir name 'Bot|Away'   FAILED 123
nick 'Bot*star'   -> dir name 'Bot*star'   FAILED 123
nick 'Bot"q'      -> dir name 'Bot"q'      FAILED 123
```

The transfer worked, the bytes were on disk, and the fetch failed at the last step, every time, for that bot.

A whitelist now, as the docstring always claimed. Legal nick specials that are also legal in a path are kept, so the directory is still recognisably that bot's. `list_fetch.py` did not import `re` at all — caught by importing the module, not by parsing it.

## Verification

16 new tests, five mutations, all caught. Full suite 2586, `PREFLIGHT PASSED`.

## Deliberately not in this change

`adminchat`'s passive DCC CHAT branch opens a listener before any rate-limit or blocklist check, so a handful of CTCPs can take every port in `DCC_PORT_START..DCC_PORT_END` for 60 seconds. Real, and confirmed — but the fix needs the pending-session machinery rather than a reordering of the existing checks, so it gets its own change rather than being rushed in beside two unrelated fixes.

author: lukstafi
body:
## What is now true

The dead implicit-export ratchet (`test/operations/dead_export_scan`, gh-ocannl-806 / gh-ocannl-890) no longer censuses `sexp_of` converters. The `sexp_of` half of a `[@@deriving sexp]`, a standalone `[@@deriving sexp_of]`, and a hand-written `let sexp_of_x` (recognized by the `sexp_of_` name prefix) are all excluded by policy, and `[%sexp_of: M.ty]` credits nothing. `of_sexp`, `compare` and `equal` stay censused.

## Why

A `sexp_of` converter is the entry point for debugging and observability, not a helper an author meant to be private. It is consumed as often through ppx_minidebug's typed log annotations (`[%log (x : M.ty)]`, the parameters of a `%debug_sexp` function) as through spelled references, and those expand to converter calls a source-level census cannot see, so a converter used only from a log read as dead. A `sexp_of` with no caller costs nothing and cannot drift from its type; the only fix the ratchet could suggest was dropping the deriving, which takes the converter away from the next debugging session.

`of_sexp` stays: it is the persistence and config entry point, an unused parser over opaque fields is a runtime trap, and narrowing `sexp` to `sexp_of` is a real cleanup. Derived `compare`/`equal` stay: structural comparison over records is exactly where the census has already earned its keep (the annotated `Backend_intf.equal_mma_input_format` exemption).

## What changes

- `test/support/dead_export_scan.ml`: the name generators, extension derivers and deriving-dependency walk drop `sexp_of`; top-level values named `sexp_of_*` are skipped.
- `test/operations/dead_export_scan.ml`: the 37 `sexp_of_*` exemptions leave the baseline (they would fail the stale check otherwise); header comment updated.
- `test/operations/dead_export_scan_cases.ml`: new controls pin the exclusion (derived, hand-written, and the extension crediting nothing); the ignored/opaque and functor-path controls move to `of_sexp`; the two GADT controls go, since no censused deriver accepts a GADT (both ppx_compare and ppx_sexp_conv's parser refuse them, verified).
- `docs/agent-notes/build-and-test.md`: the scan's bullet records the policy and its reasoning.

gh-ocannl-915's triage of derived exemptions shrinks accordingly (37 of the 71 were `sexp_of`).

## Verified

`dune build @check`, `dune build @test/operations/scans`, and both `runtest-dead_export_scan` / `runtest-dead_export_scan_cases` aliases pass; the cases golden was promoted for the renamed and added claims.

author: helmi75
body:
Quatre corrections issues de **l'écoute de dix appels réels**, dont six enregistrés sur deux pistes.

## 1. L'outil qui manquait — et la promesse rompue

Le prompt demandait « prends le message et annonce un rappel ». Elle le disait, dans **5 appels sur 10** :

```
Appel 43 : « Je transmets votre candidature à l'équipe. Ils vous rappelleront. »
Appel 44 : « Je peux prendre un message pour Bertrand et lui transmettre. »
Appel 47 : « Je transmets à l'équipe que Loulou souhaite... »
Appel 48 : « Je transmets votre message. Ils vous rappelleront. »
```

**Aucun outil ne l'enregistrait.** Le message n'existait que dans la transcription, et ces appels tombaient dans le filtre « info » de l'admin, au même titre qu'une question d'horaires. Le restaurateur n'avait aucun signal qu'on s'était engagé en son nom.

- Nouvel outil `take_message`, table `messages` (migration v10).
- Filtre **« Rappel promis »** dans le journal des appels, encart en tête du panneau, bouton « Marquer traité ».
- C'est le **seul outil qui n'exige pas de numéro** : un appel masqué ne peut ni réserver ni retrouver quoi que ce soit — c'est justement celui qui a le plus besoin de laisser un mot. Le restaurateur voit alors qu'il n'y a pas de quoi rappeler.

## 2. Elle ne répète plus mot pour mot

Appel 48 : l'appelant dit « comment », elle rejoue la phrase **identique**, il répond « vous venez de me dire la même chose là ». C'est cette formulation-là qui n'était pas passée : la redire ne sert à rien.

## 3. Les tirades sont plafonnées

Une réponse a duré **16,3 secondes** — trois réservations lues d'affilée. p90 à 9,8 s. Une liste s'annonce (« j'en ai trois ») puis se donne **un élément à la fois**.

## 4. Le SMS

Elle répondait « je ne sais pas si vous recevrez un SMS » — sur **son propre fonctionnement**. C'est un fait qu'on connaît, pas une politique du restaurant : exception explicite à la règle « n'invente pas ce que le restaurant ne fait pas », avec la note d'entretien pour le jour où #34 livrera les SMS.

## RGPD

Un nouveau stock de données personnelles qui échapperait à la purge rendrait le registre faux. Les messages suivent donc les mêmes durées que le reste :

| Donnée | Durée | Traitement |
|---|---|---|
| Objet, détail, nom | celle du transcript (30 j) | effacés |
| Numéro | celle du numéro (90 j) | effacé |
| Droit à l'effacement | immédiat | **supprimés**, non anonymisés — un message n'a aucune valeur comptable, contrairement à un appel |

Deux garde-fous de mutation ajoutés : « une promesse de rappel laisse toujours une trace » et « les messages tombent sous la purge comme le reste ».

## Vérifié

**488 tests · 27/27 garde-fous.** Prompt maintenu sous la limite : 5 980 caractères.

author: tadasant
body:
Closes #566.

A message queued for a session could sit `pending` indefinitely. The issue records two occurrences with different preconditions, and they turn out to be two distinct windows rather than one: a message that arrives while the session is already at rest, and a message that was already queued when something resumed the session with an injected nudge. Both are closed here.

## What I established first, because the issue made the diagnosis conditional on it

The issue body flags its own root cause as unverified and names the thing to check: *"I did not confirm which status the auth-outage park actually left the session in, and if it parks into `needs_input` then `deliver_if_session_already_idle` should have matched and the real fault is elsewhere."*

**It parks into `waiting`, not `needs_input`.** `AuthOutageParkService`'s own header says so — *"Puts the session to sleep. A `waiting` session is dormant"* — and `#sleep_session!` is what carries it there, via `pending_sleep` and `execute_pending_sleep` on the pause path for a session that was still running. So `deliver_if_session_already_idle` declined correctly by its own terms, and the two-triggers reading in the issue is right: nothing was scheduled and no drain failed. There is no exhausted attempt budget to find — `metadata["enqueued_drain_attempts"]` was never written, because no attempt was ever made.

That makes the accurate statement the broader one the 2026-08-23 comment argues for, and it splits cleanly in two.

## Window 1 — `waiting` had no drain trigger at all

`EnqueuedMessage#deliver_if_session_already_idle` (`after_create_commit`) and `SessionStateMachine#drain_enqueued_messages_after_pause` both read `needs_input?`. But the three create surfaces — the web queue form, `POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/enqueued_messages`, MCP `manage_enqueued_messages` — all promise the caller delivery *"when the session becomes idle"*, and a session resting in `waiting` already is: asleep on an `open-pr` self-wake, slept by `action_session sleep`, resting after a park. Nothing came back for those rows. This is also exactly #690's guard analysis, which the 2026-08-29 comment folded in.

Both now read one new predicate, `Session#idle_for_queued_delivery?` (`needs_input? || waiting?`), deliberately cheap and coarse: it decides only whether to *schedule* the job. `EnqueuedMessageDrainJob#skip_reason` does the careful work under its own re-read, and gains three `waiting`-only refusals:

| Refusal | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `running_job_id.present?` | `waiting` is not only a resting state — it is also where a session sits for the whole of its **first start**, from the moment `AgentSessionJob` claims `running_job_id` through the clone, the session-id write and the spawn. Delivering there does not deliver early, it **loses the message**: the processor takes its `resume!` branch (which does not clear `running_job_id`), destroys the row, and the replacement job is refused by the concurrency guard as a duplicate of the live first-start job — queue empty, no turn behind it, and the drain counts it a success so nothing retries or alerts. Found by the fresh-eyes review, not by me. Scoped to `waiting`, so a stale job id on a `needs_input` session still reaches the bounded-retry-and-alert path that exists to report exactly that. |
| `session_id.blank?` | A follow-up prompt into a session with no runtime session id is reclassified by `AgentSessionJob` as a **fresh start**, which runs the session's own prompt and *discards* the follow-up. "Delivering" here would destroy the message. It goes out on the first turn's end-of-turn drain instead. Asks about the session id **alone** rather than `never_ran?`: the two differ by `transcript.blank?`, and the population that matters is a session that *has* run and whose stale runtime id was later released. |
| `SpotSessionHold.held?` | `SpotSessionHold` refuses the turn at the door and re-queues it as a fresh row, so a drain would churn the message's position and origin on every pass while the gate's own re-check is already the thing that will run it. This is the churn loop #690 warned about, and it is why the drain does not simply "go through `SpotSessionHold` like any other turn". |
| `SpotSessionPause.paused?` | Same gate, resumed by `SpotCeilingSweepJob`. |

The existing `auth_outage_reason` refusal already covered both states and still does — a fresh turn would hit the same wall, burn the message and park again.

One candidate is deliberately **not** refused: a session dormant on its own armed wake-up (`paused_until_scheduled_time?`). That is the case the issue's title is about. The `open-pr` skill has a session sleep on a bounded self-wake so it does not occupy the human's action queue while its PR is rated, and the merged-PR notice is *queued* rather than sent precisely because that session is `waiting`. Delivering consumes the wake, and that is the point rather than a cost — the notice is what the session is asleep waiting for. `EnqueuedMessage#stale?` is what keeps it honest: a notice whose subject moved on while it sat in the queue is retired rather than delivered, so a wake is only ever spent on a message that still says something.

## Window 2 — a resume that injects a nudge preempted the queue

The 2026-08-23 comment's reading is the one that holds: any resume path that injects a follow-up prompt preempts the queue, regardless of what the session was resting in or whether it was resting at all. A mid-turn kill and resume never produces a transition into a resting state, so `drain_enqueued_messages_after_pause` cannot fire and the `after_create_commit` hook ran and correctly declined hours earlier.

Every automated resume in Zimmer ends the same way — `AuthOutageParkService.resume_parked!`, `AgentSessionJob#auto_continue_after_interrupt` (which is the exact path behind session 7681's nudge text), `SessionRecoveryService#auto_restart_session`, `HealthMonitorService#retry_failed_sessions`, `SessionContinuation`, the REST/MCP `restart` surfaces — all of them call `AgentSessionJob.enqueue_with_prompt(session.id, AutomatedPrompts::SYSTEM_RECOVERY)`. So the decision lives at that one choke point in `AgentSessionJob` rather than being repeated at each of them: if the prompt this turn carries is a system-recovery nudge and the session has a pending message, the message takes the turn and the nudge is dropped.

`EnqueuedMessageProcessorService` performs the handoff under the locking it already owns — the row is claimed `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, the session stays `running` (its pre-pause handoff path, so there is no `running → needs_input → running` flap for `session_needs_input` watchers to trip over), `running_job_id` is released and a fresh `AgentSessionJob` is enqueued carrying the message's content and attachments. The arriving job stands down. The check sits after the archived guard, the pause guard and the spot gate, and before the job records `job_started_at`, so a refused turn is still refused first.

**The session has to be `running`, and that guard is load-bearing rather than defensive** — it is the same hazard as the drain-job row above, arriving from the other direction. Releasing `running_job_id` is something only the handoff branch does, and that branch is selected by the session already being `running`. From `needs_input` or `waiting` the processor resumes instead, leaving `running_job_id` pointing at the job that is standing down, so the replacement job would be refused as a duplicate and the message would be gone with no turn behind it. It costs nothing on the paths this is for: every caller that injects a nudge resumes the session before enqueueing the job. It also settles what happens to the session's armed one-time wakes, which a `SYSTEM_RECOVERY` resume preserves deliberately — a `running` session's `may_resume?` is false, so the processor performs no resume at all and `cancel_pending_one_time_wake_triggers` never runs. The wakes survive the handoff exactly

author: robertblust
body:
The notification services were **one package inside 3AP's own platform**, and the entry described
them as though they were the whole of it. The platform's own `components.plantuml` shows the rest: a
single reverse proxy terminating TLS and enforcing HSTS at the edge, a gateway verifying JWTs against
a Keycloak identity provider, and behind it the administration services, the notification services
and a shared store of queues and databases on Kubernetes.

So the entry **becomes the platform**, and the notification services become a part of it — rather
than four more entries for one system with one diagram. It now runs to October 2021 instead of June
2020.

## Three additions come with the widening

- **Identity became the platform's concern**, not each service's — Keycloak issuing tokens, social
  sign-in trusted into it, the gateway verifying before routing. A decision, not a library choice.
- **The company's own administration ran on it first** — a directory read from Google Directory,
  time records read from the system 3AP billed through, a scheduler keeping both current. Internal
  work proved the platform before a client did.
- **The organization model got an interface a normal application can use.** `3ap-organization` is a
  GraphQL service whose dependencies include `flatland-tcp-cdo-client-infra` — it reads the CDO
  repository through its client. That is what turned circles and role assignments from something
  only a modeling tool could open into something a front end could ask questions of.

**The administration front end.** 20 commits of 242 is somebody else's work. Same rule that kept

author: arloliu
body:
Seven tooling behaviours that each cost real time to rediscover are now written
down where an agent reads them, in `.agents/rules/`.
Every one was reproduced against this tree before it was recorded, and three of
the seven were corrected in the process.

## What is recorded, and where

`300-testing.md`, *Mechanics* — proving an assertion load-bearing.
The test cache does not observe the chart files `helm` opens in a subprocess.
A run narrowed with `-run` therefore excludes the one test that copies the chart
tree in-process, leaving no chart file among the run's inputs, and a stale pass
is replayed. `go test -run TestChartPodMonitor ./deploy/` returns `ok (cached)`
on a tree with a deliberately broken `podmonitor.yaml`; the same tree under
`-count=1` fails.

`500-validation-and-workflow.md` — six traps, in the sections they qualify.

- A refused commit message stops the commit after `git commit` has already run,
  and nothing in the terminal says the work did not land.
- The pre-commit check reports only what a diff owns, while `semlf check <file>`
  reads the whole file; `semlf` does not read YAML.
- A `helm template --show-only` render fails on a broken template elsewhere in
  the chart, and names that template rather than the one asked for.
- An editor diagnostic the validation block does not reproduce is noise.
- A chart check skips when its pinned binary is off `PATH` and the package still
  prints `ok`, which is why a pinned version is confirmed before it is written
  down.
- The end-to-end harness pulls three third-party images into the cluster before
  any scenario runs, so a failure at that point is the registry.

## Corrections made while verifying

- The commit-msg hook does not exit 0. It exits 1, and the misleading part is
  that the refusal lands after `git commit` has run, so the rule anchors on
  verifying with `git log` rather than on an exit status.
- An unresolvable tool pin does not fail silently in CI — `jdx/mise-action`
  installs with no `with:` block and fails loudly. The silence is local, where a
  missing binary turns 232 checks into an `ok` in 0.018s.
- The end-to-end image pulls are not skipped in CI, and they happen after the
  cluster exists rather than before: `PROFGATE_E2E_REGISTRY` substitutes only
  the kind node image.

## Validation

`mise run check` reports repository invariants hold.
`semlf` is clean over the full diff; the pre-existing findings in `AGENTS.md`
sit on lines this change does not touch and are left alone, per the rule it adds.

No Go, YAML, chart, or script is touched.

author: bardbyte
body:
**E19 delta line:** not measurable by the suite: the EAG check runs only on the laptop; the scripted capability line stays 100.0 / 0.0 on the fixture build.

**Which principle justified this component**, and what would have to be true to delete it again: the rule every plane has obeyed, prove it on the laptop before it enters the program, and the reality law under it: a 200 from the gateway is a fact, and a check that could not read it must say so rather than blame the gateway. Delete the check when the EAG plane is in the harness with its own doctor line, or when the path is abandoned.

**A transcript read**, not just a score: the laptop's first run printed `✗ token OneIdentity refused every attempt: ms: HTTP 200: {"authorization_token":"…; s: HTTP 403: {"description":"Client credential cannot be validated : {Signature Expired}","error_code":"UEXP001"}`. The millisecond signature had been accepted; the token sat under `authorization_token`, a name the reader did not know; the seconds signature was then sent and refused, as the gateway wants milliseconds; and the summary called every attempt refused. Against the scripted gateway, now written to behave like the real one, the same run reads `✓ token minted in 0 s with a ms timestamp · field authorization_token · answer keys: authorization_token · says nothing about expiry · JWT exp−iat = 300 s`, one attempt. From the sandbox, with no route to the gateway, the run reads `✗ token OneIdentity could not be reached: ms: no route reaches the gateway — direct · TLS …: unreachable via [Errno -2] Name or service not known; via http://127.0.0.1:… · TLS …: unreachable via Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden`, one attempt, no secret; and with `GEMINI_MODEL` set it opens with `! warning GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-pro is set and VERTEX_MODEL is not: the Vertex plane (the chat) reads GEMINI_MODEL as a fallback and would run on it too — use EAG_MODEL for this check, or set VERTEX_MODEL explicitly`.

## Two commits

### 1 · Read OneIdentity's authorization_token, and never sign again after a 200
- `authorization_token` is the first token name tried; a lone long space-free string is the last resort, so an unfamiliar name never turns a 200 into a false refusal again. The seconds timestamp is sent only when the gateway refuses the millisecond one, never after a 200. A 200 whose token could not be read is reported as exactly that with the answer's keys named; a 200 body is the token, so no message ever carries a byte of it. The token record names the field it came from.

### 2 · The first real POST decides the route; EAG_MODEL keeps GEMINI_MODEL away from the Vertex plane
- No GET probe of a POST-only endpoint: the token POST itself tries direct, then the corporate proxy, and whichever answers with any HTTP status (a 405 or a 403 included) serves every later call. A transport failure ends the token step after one attempt, the detail says could-not-be-reached rather than refused, and the route failures are this request's.
- The model id comes from `EAG_MODEL` first. `GEMINI_MODEL` still works, as the guide names it, but the Vertex plane reads that name as a fallback, so the check warns when it is set without `VERTEX_MODEL`. The env example and the runbook say so.

## Tests
Silo suite green; ten EAG tests: the laptop's case, the seconds fallback on a refusal, the no-leak rule, the route chooser, the one-attempt transport failure, `EAG_MODEL` precedence and the warning.

## On the laptop
Pull main, then rerun:

```bash
python scripts/eag_check.py
python scripts/eag_check.py --probe-ttl 7 --json eag_report.json
```

body:
## Scope

P1G4 implements the browser-side EN/RU Scope Handoff transport as **source only** behind an exact default-off boundary. It preserves the local brief, copy/download and manual `mailto:` fallback. No production runtime, environment, Blob or UI activation is included.

## Exact source

- Base/main: `ae930fc999a62f6098190be4143f0eb54980dd91`
- Base tree: `ce6cb9e85d660c5a1ec9302383a8bc56f64cc8d2`
- Head: `0b2da2edf8c9d8f29395f681b9ff13ccb33d7b5b`
- Head tree: `58e86a8445239d50b12311f8e6bb8ed9d0991080`
- Branch: `agent/p1g4-disabled-en-ru-scope-handoff-ui-r1`
- Commits: 1
- Changed paths: exactly 3

A fresh Linux clone was revalidated immediately before the ready/merge gate. It matched the exact head, tree and parent above and began clean. No history rewrite, force update or source mutation was used.

## Changed paths

1. `public/scope-handoff-r1.js`
2. `scripts/verify-scope-handoff-r1-ui.mjs`
3. `package.json` — wires the focused UI verifier into `verify:core`

No page source, API handler, schema, storage adapter, rate limiter, lockfile, Astro/Vercel/Cloudflare configuration, Worker source or environment configuration changed.

## Default-off and explicit-action boundary

- `const UI_ENABLED = false`
- Automatic mount is short-circuited while disabled.
- Disabled source performs no DOM work and no network request.
- No request occurs on page load, field input/change, Entry/Primary selection, mapper handoff, local brief generation, copy, download, reset or manual `mailto:`.
- One POST construction exists only for the separate explicit final button after a current local brief, secret-boundary confirmation and explicit consent.
- Existing EN and RU pages already load the shared controller; no page source change is required.

## Bounded payload and privacy

The controller maps the existing EN/RU form fields into the merged `bitevo.scope-handoff.r1` schema:

- Entry excludes all Primary-only fields.
- Primary includes the full required set and identical EN/RU enum semantics.
- Constants remain `submission_intent=scope_review_only`, `testing_authorization=false`, `secret_confirmation=true`, `consent_scope_review=true`.
- The generated brief, mapper draft, browser storage, cookies, analytics/fingerprint data and files are never included.
- Client-side field limits mirror the canonical schema.
- Fetch uses same-origin credentials, JSON, no-store cache, redirect failure and same-origin referrer policy.

## Idempotency and reconciliation

- One secure `client_submission_id` is minted immediately before the first explicit request.
- The exact canonical request body is frozen for the cycle.
- Concurrent clicks share one in-flight promise and one fetch.
- Manual retry after unknown, rate-limited or unavailable state reuses the exact body and ID.
- Accepted, rejected and conflict states are not blindly retried.
- A changed scope cannot mint a replacement ID while UNKNOWN or conflict is unresolved.
- No automatic retry loop exists.

## False-Green and accessible states

A 2xx response is accepted only after exact validation of schema, status, delivery status, human-review status, `testing_authorization=false`, echoed client ID, opaque server ID, timestamp and replay/status consistency. Partial or malformed 2xx is UNKNOWN.

Localized states are semantically equivalent across EN/RU: local-only, consent-required, ready, stale, submitting, accepted, rate-limited, unavailable, rejected, unknown/reconcile, conflict and changed-scope lock.

The UI exposes `role=status`, `aria-live=polite`, `aria-atomic=true`, a visible reconciliation ID and manual-contact fallback. Accepted copy does not claim sent, delivered, read, booked, approved or engagement started.

## Fresh deterministic validation

Fresh Linux environment:

- Node `v22.19.0`
- npm `10.9.3`
- `npm ci`: PASS
- dependency audit: 0 vulnerabilities
- Astro static build: 97 pages
- complete `build:core`: PASS
- exact local build receipt: head/ref/provenance valid

Focused terminal:

`SCOPE_HANDOFF_R1_UI_GATE=PASS checks=96 locales=2 progressive_enhancement=PASS auto_post=0 explicit_post_only=1 idempotency=PASS false_green=PASS accessible_states=PASS manual_fallback=PRESERVED ui_default=DISABLED`

Additional focused gates:

- `SCOPE_HANDOFF_R1_RATE_LIMIT_GATE=PASS checks=91 provider_writes=0 production_thresholds=UNSET`
- `SCOPE_HANDOFF_R1_RUNTIME_GATE=PASS checks=34 fake_provider_io_only=1 real_provider_writes=0 runtime_default=DISABLED ui_default=DISABLED`

The verifier covers default-off zero work, exact Entry/Primary mapping, EN/RU parity, no forbidden payload fields, field bounds, double-click serialization, exact retry body/ID, rate limiting, service unavailability, network uncertainty, malformed 2xx, conflict, definitive rejection/new cycle, accessible markup, manual fallback and mounted EN/RU behavior with fake responses only.

## Preview checks before ready transition

All checks on exact head `0b2da2edf8c9d8f29395f681b9ff13ccb33d7b5b` completed successfully:

- GitHub `quality-gate`: SUCCESS
- GitHub `main-history-audit`: SUCCESS
- Vercel preview/comments: SUCCESS, 0 unresolved feedback
- Cloudflare Workers preview build: SUCCESS
- Inline review threads: 0

No browser/provider POST was performed during implementation or verification.

## Current authority boundary

Source review and exact-head validation are complete. The current owner gate authorizes marking PR53 ready and **one ordinary merge-commit attempt** only while the head remains `0b2da2edf8c9d8f29395f681b9ff13ccb33d7b5b` and main remains `ae930fc999a62f6098190be4143f0eb54980dd91`, followed by automatic GitHub/Vercel/Cloudflare production verification.
