author: mlervaag
body:
## Hva endres

CI-jobben hadde vokst til drøyt seks minutter på nye PR-er, og teststeget alene sto for fire av dem. Det var ikke oppsettet som var tregt.

En instrumentert kjøring viste at `loadArchive` ble kalt **41 ganger mot `data/`** i én testkjøring, at hvert kall kostet **10,5 sekunder**, og at de 484 sekundene det ble til var **83 % av all CPU-tid i testene**. Kostnaden vokser med arkivet: `data/` gikk fra 3780 til 4401 filer på tretten dager, og hver nye fil gjør alle 41 lastene tregere samtidig.

Målingen pekte videre. I/O var ikke problemet — å lese alle 4400 filene tok 0,9 sekunder. YAML-parsingen tok 13. Hele kostnaden lå i ett bibliotek, og den ble betalt om igjen for hver eneste last.

Tre grep, i den rekkefølgen de betyr noe:

**Arkivet leses med js-yaml i stedet for `yaml`.** `CORE_SCHEMA` er det samme YAML 1.2-kjerneskjemaet koden allerede ba om med `schema: "core"`, og det er ti ganger raskere. Byttet gjelder bare lesing; `yaml` skriver fortsatt. At de to leser likt er ikke sluttet fra dokumentasjonen: `parse-equivalence.test.ts` leser hver fil i `data/` og `fixtures/data` med begge bibliotekene og krever identisk resultat, så et framtidig avvik blir en rød test med filnavnet i — ikke en stille endring av hva arkivet inneholder. To små tester dekker randtilfellene som skiller YAML-versjoner: usiterte datoer, og «no» som ikke skal bli `false`.

**`loadArchive` mellomlagrer per datakatalog**, med et fingeravtrykk av størrelse og endringstidspunkt for hver fil som nøkkel. Å stat-e filene koster 0,2 sekunder mot de 2 det tar å lese dem, så et verktøy som skriver en fil og laster på nytt ser fortsatt det det nettopp skrev. Kallerne får hver sin kopi — arkivet blir sortert og endret på av dem som bruker det, og en delt referanse ville latt ett verktøy stokke om på lista til det neste.

**Filene leses med overlappende I/O**, 64 om gangen. Grensen er der fordi en `Promise.all` over 4400 filer ville gått tom for fildeskriptorer. Feilene samles per fil og skjøtes sammen i filrekkefølge, slik at `pnpm validate` gir samme utskrift hver gang.

Målt likt før og etter, på samme maskin:

| | før | etter |
|---|---|---|
| `loadArchive`, ett kall | 10,5 s | 2,2 s (0,5 s ved gjentatt last) |
| Testsuiten | 224 s | **67 s** |
| `pnpm validate` | 11,0 s | **3,4 s** |
| `pnpm data:duplicates` | 11,1 s | **3,7 s** |
| `pnpm data:uncertain` | 10,3 s | **3,4 s** |
| `pnpm data:historical-preservation` | 11,8 s | **3,5 s** |

Med i endringen: `baseRevision` i `sunnmorsposten-1963-1971-production.yaml` pekte på en commit som ikke finnes. Squash-fletting skrev om SHA-en da PR-en ble slått sammen, og siden steget kjører uten `--base` på main, har **hver eneste push til main vært rød siden #248**. Den peker nå på forelderen til commiten som la til manifestet, slik de andre manifestene gjør. Alle 25 harvest-batcher er kontrollert grønne.

## Kilde

Ingen dataendring. Den ene YAML-linjen som endres er en git-referanse i et innhøstingsmanifest, ikke en opplysning om klubben.

## Kontrollert

- [x] `pnpm validate` er grønn — samme tall som før: 1723 kamper, 105 sesonger, 488 personer, 2149 kildedokumenterte resultater
- [x] `AAFK_DATA_DIR=fixtures/data pnpm validate` er grønn
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` og `pnpm test` er grønne — 1518 tester i 121 filer, 0 lint-feil og nøyaktig samme 167 advarsler som på main
- [x] `pnpm build` og `pnpm smoke` er grønne — 20 sider ser riktige ut
- [x] Alle 25 innhøstingsbatcher kontrollert enkeltvis

## Merknader

Den nye ekvivalenstesten bruker knappe 20 sekunder, fordi den per definisjon leser hele arkivet med det trege biblioteket. Det er med vilje: den kostnaden betales én gang, mot de 41 gangene den ble betalt før. Den er nå det tregeste enkeltsteget i suiten, og det er en grei bytte for å ha bevis framfor antakelse om at parserbyttet ikke endrer dataene.

`parseArchiveYaml` returnerer `any`, akkurat som `yaml.parse` gjorde. Alternativet — `unknown` — ville ikke gjort noen av de rundt 100 kallstedene tryggere, bare tvunget inn en cast på hvert av dem og gjort et fartsgrep om til en typerefaktorering. Kontrollen av innholdet gjør arkivet med zod, der den hører hjemme.

Byggesteget (41 s i CI) er ikke rørt. Det er Next.js som rendrer sider, ikke arkivlasting, og det er en annen jobb.

author: charlesvestal
body:
Two reports from the device, one screen.

### 1. A two-value option showed a menu

The "menu" is the **enum peek**. It exists because a 30px *grid cell* cannot show a word — but a **list row prints the option in full**, right-aligned beside its label, so the panel covered a legible answer with the same answer and took the four rows around it down as well.

Global Settings is pinned to the list, and `skipback_shortcut` is two options:

**Before** — turning `Skipback`:

```
SKIPBACK                TURNING
  Cap
  Vol+Cap                     *


[TURN] SET
```

**After** — the row is focused and the jog changes it in place:

```
GLOBAL > SETTINGS    SHORTCUTS
 Open With               Both
 Recall Q                 Off
 Skipback          [Vol+Cap]
 Skipback Len              30s
```

It is **not a two-option problem** — a 47-model list is the same occlusion for the same reason — so the gate is the LAYOUT. On `s.layout` rather than `knobsAsList()`: by the time the turn is handled the page is known to be a knobs page with a key under the cursor, and what is left to ask is only what the layout can *show*. **The grid is unchanged**, switches and wide graphics included.

### 2. The peek disappeared too quickly

`ENUM_PEEK_MS` 700 → **1500**, which is the rule rather than the number: it has to **outlive `TURN_CLAIM_MS` (1200)**. The same detent raises both — the header claims the cell and names the parameter, the peek shows what is either side of the value — so a shorter peek took the list down mid-claim and left the screen answering half a question. 700 was matched to the chain editor card's `KNOB_CARD_DECAY_MS`, a constant that never shares a screen with this one, so the match bought nothing and cost the read.

### Tests

`tests/host/test_enum_peek.sh` gains both, and **both halves of each**:

- the list suppression **and** the grid still peeking, on the same two keys and the same fixture — asserting only the suppression would pass just as well if the peek were deleted
- the duration as an **ordering between the two constants**, so tuning either cannot silently re-cross them

Reverting either fix fails it (verified: 3 FAILs). Full `tests/host/` suite green, `make -C tests/host test` green.

Not yet verified on hardware.

- Add a battery percentage checking driver. It follows the sequence
  - (1) Enable the read pin
  - (2) Burst read 15 samples
  - (3) Olympic filter to reject top and bottom 3 samples

author: chongchonghe
body:
### Description

Quokka can read a stellar luminosity table for `StochasticStellarPop` particles (`particles.rad_table`), but there was no way to produce one from real stellar tracks. This PR adds `scripts/python/slug_luminosity_table_for_quokka.py`, which runs slug2's `write_isochrone` with one top-hat filter per radiation group and converts its output into the CSV format read by `quokka::DataTable<2, nGroups>::CSVReader`. Bands are given as photon-energy ranges (`--eV`) or wavelength ranges (`--lambda`), repeatable and order-preserving; the defaults are ages $10^5$–$2 \times 10^8$ yr and masses 2.1–120 $M_\odot$ on `mist_2016_vvcrit_40`. Stars that no longer exist at a given age, and bands whose numerical integration returns a small negative value, are floored to zero.

The bands must match Quokka's radiation-group energy edges: they are checked in photon energy (so `--lambda` is converted first), must run in increasing energy, and adjacent bands must share a boundary. A gap such as `--eV 6 11 --eV 11.2 13.6`, or a sequence that goes to lower energy, is rejected.

A new 3D test problem `ParticleRadiationSlug` validates the whole path. A single 120 $M_\odot$ star of age 1 Myr — both values are exact nodes of the table's log-spaced axes, so the interpolation is a lookup — radiates into an FUV band (6–13.6 eV) and a Lyman continuum band (13.6–54.4 eV). The test checks that the radiation energy deposited on the grid equals $\Delta t \, (L_{\rm FUV} + L_{\rm LyC})$.

Verified by running the test: the expected luminosities $L_{\rm FUV} = 2.44698 \times 10^{39}$ and $L_{\rm LyC} = 3.88642 \times 10^{39}$ erg/s hard-coded in the test come from a separate `write_isochrone` invocation on a different mass grid (`-m0 60 -m1 120 -nm 2`, explicit time `1e6`), independent of the grid used to build the committed table, and the deposited energy matches to a relative error of $9 \times 10^{-16}$. The other CLI forms (`--lambda`, single band, connected mixed `--eV`/`--lambda` pairs, `--floor`) and the new band-sequence checks (gaps, reverse energy order, overlapping bands) were exercised directly, and the existing `ParticleRadiation` test still passes.

body: ## Bug and impact Agentic optimization mode could silently mark valid generated molecules invalid or crash at the final summary. WorkerAgent and agentic property tools passed raw strings into the surrogate `predict()` API, which expects a list of SMILES; strict/list-based predictors either raised or treated strings as iterables, corrupting scores. The agentic engine also mixed aggregated critic/meta usage dictionaries into `aggregate_usage()`, which expects `LLMUsage` objects and could crash after an otherwise completed run. ## Root cause Recent agentic-mode code diverged from the established surrogate contract used by the classic inner loop and only partially handled critic/meta usage aggregation. It also logged the newly proposed prompt state rather than the state that generated the evaluated candidates. ## Fix - Use `predict_single()` for scalar agentic predictions and one batch `predict()` call for batch property tools. - Parse both supported worker JSON schemas, including fenced `generated_molecules` mappings. - Validate/canonicalize worker candidates with task marker and similarity settings before scoring. - Score and log the evaluated current prompt state in agentic mode. - Keep aggregate critic/meta usage dictionaries separate from raw `LLMUsage` objects and merge summaries safely. ## Validation - `python3 -m pytest tests/test_agentic_correctness.py -q` -> 4 passed - `python3 -m pytest tests -q` -> 36 passed, 1 torch deprecation warning

author: accelanalysis
body:
## Release 1 Track B — Experience Architecture

Implements **NUR-07, NUR-08, and NUR-09** using the existing Nurture chassis and is reconciled against the final Release 1 Track A/C/D/E/F contracts.

### Implemented
- canonical `Experience`, module manifest, capability, entitlement, host-context, media, and event contracts
- trusted primary/secondary Experience registry
- `/experience/*` defaults to **public** access; `/app/experience/*` and `/app/secondary/*` are authenticated participant hosts; `trial` remains a distinct mode that must be established explicitly rather than inferred from page entry
- module routing/navigation, loading/unavailable/error/restricted states, and route-resettable crash containment
- fail-closed presentation access resolver
- concrete Track A opaque-extension serializer + **published-only** Experience definition adapter + public organization adapter
- Track C-compatible stable Customer handoff and registration continuity via the actual `returnTo` / `entryPoint` / `organizationId` / `source` query contract
- Track C-owned onboarding adaptation/validation/persistence; Track B keeps only the minimal requirement and completion port
- Track D commercial→entitlement projection in `shared/experience/entitlements.ts`, including bounded-trial enforcement
- Track E-compatible protected-operation authorization helper; Track E remains authoritative for trusted organization–Customer binding and server security
- exact shared Momentum Check capability keys and Entry/Primary/Premium reference mapping
- Track F-compatible `nurture:experience-event` transport, `experience.started`, `experience.premium_feature_requested`, and namespaced module signals
- shared image/YouTube/Vimeo/direct-video presentation boundary; YouTube readiness/error is driven by the IFrame Player API, not iframe document `load`
- usable `Momentum Check` reference module plus different-domain `Next-Step Checklist` portability fixture
- convergence/acceptance record in `docs/product/release-1-track-b.md`

### Final cross-track alignment
- **Track A / #7:** Track B consumes `ConfigurationProvider.publicOrganizationId` and the final opaque `ConfigurationExtension` store through `src/features/experience/configuration.ts`. Stable key: `experience:<slot>:<moduleId>:<moduleVersion>`. Track B reads only `getPublishedExtension`; Track A's immutable configuration version ID becomes `Experience.configurationVersion`.
- **Track C / #11:** Track C's final `customerScopeSource` returns the stable Customer/Profile ID with optional organization context. Track B treats that as identity context, not tenant authority. Track C owns `experienceRequirementsToOnboardingExtension(...)` and `createExperienceOnboardingBridge(...)`; Track B removed its temporary duplicate adapter. Experience registration passes the validated return path through Track C's supported query handoff.
- **Track D / #10:** Track D remains authoritative for Offer/pricing/Stripe/subscription reconciliation. Track B projects only trusted published Offer + reconciled subscription state into Experience capabilities. A `trialing` subscription without a valid trusted `trialEnd` or `currentPeriodEnd` fails closed. The shared reference capability map is the source for final Entry/Primary/Premium reference Offer keys.
- **Track E / #8:** Track E's `OrganizationCustomerBindingPort` must bind verified identity + trusted organization to one active Customer before entitlement presentation/protected operations. Staff `experience.view/manage/publish` permissions stay separate from participant entitlements.
- **Track F / #9:** Track F already consumes Track B's browser transport and keeps browser organization/identity/Customer fields non-authoritative until trusted ingestion.

### Trust rule

`verified identity + trusted organization binding -> Customer relationship`

`published Offer + reconciled subscription -> entitlement`

`Customer + organization + Experience + entitlement -> protected capability`

Checkout return URLs, browser storage, Firebase authentication alone, staff roles, onboarding completion, browser events, or client controls cannot grant protected access. Visiting `/experience` cannot manufacture trial access.

### Review + verification
- all five automated review findings are addressed and their review threads are resolved
- latest CI on head `e773be0661516317bd514252e357346e3c244016`: **green**
- TypeScript check covers `src` and `shared`
- `npm run test:experience` covers active/cancelled commercial states, tenant mismatch, unknown capabilities, expiry, missing/bounded trial expiration, protected authorization, Track A published-extension reading, and public/authenticated organization selection

author: shohruh-yuldashov
body:
A64-027A.2 built the visual foundation. This applies it to the eight management routes, and fixes what the foundation made visible.

Baseline: `6734639` (main, with A64-027A.2 merged). **Backend diff is empty** — `git diff origin/main -- apps/api` returns nothing.

## Database values stopped reaching the screen

`queue`, `russian_8x8`, `swiss`, `blitz`, `account` — all rendered verbatim, in tables, in detail pages, and in the filter dropdowns an operator picks from. Twelve backend enums now resolve through one `vocab.*` namespace.

**The fallback is the identifier, never the key.** `t()` returns the key it was given when nothing resolves, so a built key would print `vocab.auditSubject.queue_ticket` for a member this build has not heard of — a raw translation key, strictly worse than the enum it replaced. `useVocab` compares and degrades to the value, which is what the append-only trail needs.

`analytics` held a private copy of the termination labels and now reads the shared ones.

## One toolbar, five pages

Each page had assembled its own, and the search field's helper sentence sat *beside* the box — which is what pushed the filters onto a second row everywhere. It moves under the field; the label becomes visible rather than a placeholder; an applied filter is counted beside a control that clears it, because an operator who cannot see a filter is on reads an empty table as "there is nothing here".

## The pages became about their subject

| Route | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `/matches` | A **matchup** cell — two seats with side pips — replacing `Alice — Bob`. Result reads "Light won", not "Light" |
| `/matches/{id}` | Titled by the matchup with a status badge instead of the word "Match"; four panels; time control as `3+2` rather than `180s + 2s` |
| `/tournaments` | Entrant progress from the two real numbers, green when full; Create is the row's trailing primary action |
| `/users`, `/users/{id}` | Identity cell; standing moved into the header as badges |
| `/moderation` | Status and indefinite expiry as badges; the reason carries its glyph |
| `/audit` | Action wears a glyph for its family, tinted when refused; outcome is a semantic badge; payload behind a disclosure |

## No summary cards, and the reason is recorded

§5 offers them *where the data is truthfully available*. It is not: every admin listing is keyset-paged with **no total**, by A64-024's deliberate choice — a count over a growing table is an expensive query whose answer is stale before it renders. The dashboard's read model does hold real figures; coupling four listings to it for a number meaning "as of when the dashboard composed" would be worse than the stronger composition they got instead.

## Two defects the redesign surfaced

`match-detail` keyed its participant list on `player.side` — a duplicate the moment a server sends two seats with one side. It keys on `player_id` now. And the user detail rendered "Restricted" twice on one screen once the header carried the standing.

## Verification

- **Browser:** 9 pages × 6 widths (360–1440) × light and dark = 108 renders, no horizontal overflow, no console errors.
- **Contrast:** 24 pairs across both themes, lowest 5.65:1 — unchanged from A64-027A.2.
- **Tests:** 91 (8 new), tsc / eslint / prettier clean.
- **Mutation checks:** four — a leaked enum, a failure rendering the empty state, a filter count that stops counting, invented entrant progress. Each turns the intended test red.
- **Bundle:** JS +9.5 kB (+2.5 gzip), CSS +4.2 kB (+0.7 gzip). No dependency added.

## Responsive table strategy, documented once

Deliberate horizontal scroll inside the framed container, with a card list below 48rem. **Not** priority-column hiding: a table whose columns disappear at some widths teaches an operator that a column is absent when it is merely off-screen.

## Deferred

Analytics and Notifications composition → **A64-027A.4**. Cross-product visual QA → **A64-027A.5**. Both recorded in `specs/admin.md` §12.6.

author: sgajbi
body:
The downstream leg of #283's revision wiring: the canonical revision identity rides the render package into Render and the custody block verbatim into Archive — built on the three owner-stated contract facts confirmed by the Render session, with the deployment-boundary defect from the #300-era P1 designed out rather than worked around.

## What flows where

- `render_context.report_revision_id` — the durable snapshot record's identity, stated only when the record has one; a pre-identity snapshot omits the key entirely (never a fabricated id).
- `render_context.archive.report_revision_id` — passes through Render's `build_archive_metadata` verbatim into Archive's document record (archive#124 / migration 011, already merged and gate-green consumer-side).
- All four report families get it through the ONE shared envelope; replay/regenerate flows inherit it through the same builder; rerender submits only newly created attempts, which are conflict-free by construction.

## The named requirement: resolve before resubmit

Render's submission is create-or-get on (render_job_id, package hash): identical resubmission converges, a changed package under the same id refuses. The old resume model rebuilt the package and resubmitted unconditionally — correct only while rebuilds stay byte-identical, which any builder evolution (this field, or any future one) breaks for jobs in flight across a deployment, stranding them as non-retryable `render_conflict`.

`render_for_job` now resolves a persisted render (status `rendering`/`completed`/`archiving`) via `GET /renders/{render_job_id}` BEFORE any resubmission:

- terminal outcome (`rendered`/`failed`) → **adopted verbatim** through the same handling as a submit response — the status projection carries every submit field except the artifact bytes, which Report never consumes;
- governed 404 → the original submission never landed, so submitting the current package is safe (nothing exists to conflict with);
- render still in progress, or an unanswerable lookup → **retryable** `render_execution_failed` with no blind resubmission — a blind resubmission under a shape-evolved builder is exactly the non-retryable conflict this resolution exists to prevent.

This makes package-shape evolution deployment-safe permanently, not just for this field. Fresh submissions (`data_ready`) are unchanged.

## Reader/operator outcome

An archived document answers "which report revision does this present?" from its own custody record; the render evidence chain carries the same id end-to-end. Resumed jobs can no longer strand on deployments.

## Failure posture

Adoption preserves the existing failure mapping (an adopted failed render fails exactly as a converged failed submit did). The two new refusal paths are retryable by construction and name why in the operator message.

## Historical compatibility

Pre-identity snapshots render and archive with the key absent — same package bytes as before this change for their resumes' 404 path; their adopted outcomes never depended on package shape at all. No historical evidence rewritten.

## Validation evidence

New service tests: resumed render adopts the persisted outcome with a client that fails on any submit; resume submits exactly once on a verified 404; in-progress and unanswerable lookups fail retryable without submitting; fresh package carries the revision in both render_context and custody; pre-identity snapshot omits the key in both. Resume-after-restart and pending-custody tests updated with status projections mirroring the real contract (every submit field minus `artifact_base64`). 378 render+identity+lineage tests green; whole-repo lint, mypy, coverage gate green.

## Simplification

One resolver method; no per-status special cases; the failure handling and archive-outcome recording paths are reused unchanged for adopted outcomes.

Remaining under #283 (unchanged order): evidence-pack label retirement (consumer declarations first), portfolio-memory events revision (blocked on event-identity stability), AcceptedDocumentContract, trust separation, lifecycle metadata, the 17-point integrated proof.

body:
> EP-Ⅱは、法人と所属営業のそれぞれ契約を巻く必要があると思いますがいかがでしょうか？
> EP-Ⅱでは間違ってスケール80％の報酬を支払わないように気を付ける必要があるので、
> EP-Ⅱであることがちゃんとわかる仕様であるようにしてほしい。
> EP-Ⅰは、顧客に対しては担当者ではなく法人からURLを発行送付をするようにしたい。
> 解約も同様に担当者ではなく法人パートナーに通知が行くような仕様にしたい。

## ⚠️ 調べていて見つかった、いちばん危ないところ

**計算そのものは EP-II を正しく除外していました。** 問題はその手前にありました。

```js
var r = await sb.rpc('ep_affiliation', { p_users: userIds });
if (r.error) return out;   // ← 引けなかったことを黙って飲み込んでいた
```

ここが失敗すると **全員が個人扱い**になり、EP-II の方に**スケール（上位料率）が効いた
金額**が並びます。そのまま払われます。**払い過ぎは取り戻せません。**

直したこと：

- 引けなかったことを外に出し、配分画面のいちばん上に**赤い警告**を出して
  **「この画面のまま支払わないでください」**と止める
- 各行に **「EP-II・スケール対象外」** の赤い印
- 契約の一覧でも EP-II は赤

**計算そのものには手を触れていません。** 見え方と、失敗の伝え方だけです。

## ① EP-II を二本立てに

本部だけ巻いても、実際に顧客と向き合う個人が何にも縛られません。個人だけ巻いても、
監督する本部の責任が定まりません。**両方要ります。**

| | |
|---|---|
| `partner_ep2` | EP-II 本部（法人） |
| `partner_ep2_member` | **EP-II 所属パートナー（個人）** |

所属パートナーの書面には**本部名を差し込みます。** 「本部から離れたら契約は終わる／
個人として続けるならあらためて契約が要る」という条文も入れました。

## ② EP-I の顧客契約は法人が出す

EP-I は顧客との関係を法人が持ちます。担当者が個人の名前で送ると、**契約の相手が
担当者個人**になってしまいます。

担当者（staff）からは送れないようにし、**権限側でも止めました。** 画面には押せない
ボタンを出さず、**誰に頼めばよいか**を書いています。

## ③ EP-I の解約は法人にも届く

契約は法人が持っています。担当者だけが気づいて法人が知らない、という形にはできません。
**法人の管理者にも見える**ようにしました。

**担当者からも見えるままにしてあります。** 知らされない担当者は動けないためです。
これは私の判断なので、担当者からは隠すべきであればお知らせください。

## そのほか

- 契約書の本文を**運営画面から編集**（版で管理。過去の同意は動かない）
- 記名を**法人名と個人名**に分離（顧客・EP-I・EP-II本部は法人名必須）
- 区分の判定（`ep_badge`）は**誰にでも答えません**。運営・本人・同じ法人の管理者だけ

## 検証

- `contract_test` 224件、`rate_test` に2件追加、全 **1,256件**成功
- SQL は PostgreSQL 16 で **56件**（法人名30・EP26）

```
EP-I の担当者は顧客契約を発行できない／管理者は発行できる
EP-I の解約は法人の管理者にも見える／よその法人には見えない
引けなかったことを外に伝える（黙って通さない）
EP-II 所属の書面に本部名が残る
```

- `APP_BUILD` / `version.json` = `20260906-02`

## マージ後にお願いしたいこと

Supabase → SQL Editor で **2本**を上から順に。

| 順 | ファイル | 期待値 |
|---|---|---|
| ① | `20260906000000_contract_org.sql` | 公開中の雛形=4、法人名の欄=1、**同意の関数=1**、法人名を差し込む雛形=4 |
| ② | `20260906010000_contract_ep.sql` | 公開中の雛形=5、法人の欄=1、区分の判定=1、発行の判定=1 |

author: cazares
body:
## Sunday 2026-09-07 hardening — seven fixes toward build 480

Base `fa5b8bd` (build 479). Every fix was seen RED under its defect before GREEN, each defect is re-injected by `scripts/verify-behavioural-guards.mjs`, and the two mesh/web ones were reproduced and re-verified on two isolated iOS simulators pairing over real Multipeer.

| Commit | What it fixes | Choir impact if unfixed |
|---|---|---|
| `7d2f37b` | A serving director holds its transports only on a **recent** follower sighting (`discoveredFollowerSeenAt`), not a memory; soft reset and a failed takeover both stop relay publishing and re-enter follower mode | A deaf advertiser pinned for the rest of Mass; a device that just reset draining a queued frame to every web follower |
| `5bd3afc` | The `.notConnected` follower branch **arms** the wedge clock instead of restarting it on every failed invite; a peer re-sighted as `role=follower` loses its director records and `peerIsKnownDirector` requires a fresh sighting | A follower sitting wedged "with the director in plain sight" until someone tapped ⟳; the winner of a director conflict refusing the demoted loser forever |
| `d8fefc3` | On a native boot with nobody directing, `state.currentPage` was set to the boot default (2) **without rendering** and the reader revealed on the static page-001; "Ser Director" sent state | **The director saw the cover while the whole choir was sent to song 2** — present in the choir's build 472 (introduced 2026-08-18, 485bfb4) |
| `d0b8e0d` | `scripts/sim-isolated/` — the isolated two-simulator mesh tooling (svsimtest service, session 7777, local relay) now lives in the repo | — (tooling; it found `d8fefc3` on its first run) |
| `c622f2b` | `renderPage`'s already-on-this-page return now cancels a render still in flight for a different page; a `version-mismatch` stage failure counts toward quarantine | A mis-tap correction (B→A→B) committed A over a correct B; every current device with internet looped on the stale 471 arm pointer every 4 minutes |
| `57473b9` | `release.sh` gains `SKIP_OTA_ARM=1` — step 5b had no off switch (Phase 1 release-tooling-1); the fail-soft test's 1200-char slice is now marker-bounded | A plain release would have armed OTA fleet-wide and redeployed the worker seconds after `pages deploy` — the exact thing the Sunday posture forbids |
| `9140eb4` | **Skeptic-driven:** the boot reconciliation is web-local (`renderPage(..., { notifyNative: false })`); the director's hold also honours a handshake in flight (`pendingAdmissions`) and invite-accept stamps the sighting; `configureTransport` clears all three director records; the already-directing failure exit stops the heartbeats and mirrors role off; literal pins on both freshness comparisons; no per-check-in breadcrumb once quarantined; reset-alert copy; contracts doc | Without it, a **director whose WebView remounted** with a late native re-assert would adopt page 1 and broadcast the cover; a re-inviting follower lost one handshake to the refresh tick |

### Adversarial review (4 skeptics, one per fix commit — `wf_0a0e1a3d-c2f`)

| Commit | Verdict | What it found |
|---|---|---|
| `7d2f37b` | sound | 1 bounded regression (handshake vs sighting age) → fixed in `9140eb4`; nits closed there too |
| `5bd3afc` | sound | token-presence pins survived `<`→`>` → literal pins in `9140eb4`; mixed 472/480 fleet caveat (the conflict-loser fix needs the **winner** on 480) |
| `d8fefc3` | **defect** | director remount + late re-assert → cover broadcast → **fixed in `9140eb4`** (web-local reconciliation) |
| `c622f2b` | sound | nits: quarantine has no TTL (design caveat); dashboard `bookStage` stays `error:` after settling; native fix reaches iPads only via this native build (it does) |

### Receipts

- Harness: **71 CAUGHT / 0 MISSED / 0 SKIPPED** (was 45 on `fa5b8bd`).
- Safe suite: **622 pass / 2 skipped / 0 fail** (`node scripts/run-safe-suite.mjs`).
- Isolated-simulator scenarios on the rebuilt app (fresh installs both): **S1** fresh director broadcasts the cover it shows (old build: song 2 — `ble:page-send page=1` vs `page=2` in the log); **S2** director swipe → follower follows; **S4** takeover by the second iPad demotes the first, which then follows the new director's turns; **S7** director killed and relaunched comes back on its last page. BLE cannot run in a simulator and was not exercised.
- Adversarial skeptic review: table below; the one defect it found is fixed in `9140eb4`.

### Not in this PR, on purpose

- OTA stays **unarmed** through Sunday; the live worker still names 471's book (redeploying it disarmed is the owner's call — it also ships HEAD's relay code).
- Confirmed-but-not-Sunday-reachable findings from Phase 1 (resolve races on the OTA apply path, page-past-book clamp, stale `pages.json` totalPages, web preload timeout committed as success, `sw.js` cross-cache shell match, release-tooling process risks, truncated-webp acceptance) are listed in the campaign handoff for the next cycle.
- BLE "is this my director?" corroboration — architecture change, parked for a decision.

Merging does **not** deploy: `scripts/release.sh` ships build 480 (it bumps first), skip step 5b, Transporter upload only, **never** attach an external TestFlight group.

author: ybrllk
body:
fixed:
1. **A patient could be admitted twice at the same time** — violated assumption 2
   ("a Patient can have at most one Admission at a time") and UC01 alt flow 3a.
   One patient could occupy two beds in two wards simultaneously.

2. **An occupied bed could be marked AVAILABLE while the patient was still admitted** —
   data-integrity bug. The freed bed could then be handed to a second patient.
   UC05 alt flow 3a says the system should reject invalid transitions; now it does.

3. **A nurse could never be reassigned** — UC04 alt flow 3a says the Admin
   "changes selection or relocates", but once a nurse had a ward the assignment
   always returned `false`. Now the system warns about the conflict and asks the
   Admin to confirm the relocation.

4. **A transferred admission could not be cancelled** — assumption 8 allows cancelling
   any time before discharge, but `Admission.cancel()` only accepted `ADMITTED`.
   
Added:
- Transfer / Ward Status / Notifications tabs now refresh when selected. Previously
  they showed whatever existed at startup, so the Transfer tab was always empty.
- Bed dropdown shows current status (e.g. `B3 - OCCUPIED`), covering UC10 tracking.
- `Report` now stores the `period` it was given (was accepted and discarded).
- Report with zero rows shows UC03 alt flow 1a's "no records found" message instead
  of reporting "0 records".

author: seeker19110
body:
`roadmap.md` mục **11.1** viết *"Phần đánh giá thuần ở `Shared.Logic/Ids` (`IdsSpec` + `IdsEvaluator`, 6 loại facet), có test"* — ở **thì hiện tại**. Thư mục đó **không tồn tại**; `grep IdsEvaluator` toàn repo ra **0 kết quả**. Đúng lớp lỗi *"tài liệu nói một đằng, mã làm một nẻo"* mà bốn bộ test đối chiếu mã nguồn sinh ra để bắt — nhưng chúng soi catalog/Ribbon/suite, không soi roadmap. PR này làm cho câu đó thành sự thật.

## Tầng thuần `Shared.Logic/Ids` — 34 ca test, phủ 100% dòng

- **`IdsSpec`** đọc XML **IDS 1.0**, bỏ qua namespace khi so tên thẻ (file ngoài đời khai nhiều kiểu). Đủ 6 facet: `entity` / `attribute` / `property` / `classification` / `material` / `partOf`; ràng buộc `simpleValue`, `xs:enumeration`, `xs:pattern`, bốn cận số, `cardinality="prohibited"|"optional"`.
- **`IdsValue.Accepts`**: pattern **neo hai đầu** — XSD khớp toàn bộ chuỗi, Regex .NET khớp một đoạn; không neo thì `AB-01-rác` đạt quy tắc `AB-\d\d` và quy tắc đặt tên mất hiệu lực trong im lặng.
- **Gặp thứ chưa hỗ trợ thì từ chối file**: facet lạ, ràng buộc `minLength`, file không có `<specification>`, specification không có `<requirements>`. Bỏ qua im lặng là in ra dấu ✓ cho một quy tắc chưa từng được kiểm.

## Đường Revit

Lệnh Core **`IdsValidate`** (chỉ đọc) + nút Ribbon *Kiểm tra & AI → Kiểm theo IDS* + 2 ca kiểm trong `revit-smoke`. `RevitIdsElement` là **toàn bộ** chỗ dịch Revit ↔ IFC: `IfcExportAs` (instance → type), bảng category → lớp IFC, tham số đóng vai property / phân loại / vật liệu.

## Chạy thật — Revit 2024, Snowdon Architectural: 38 đạt / 0 trượt / 1 bỏ qua

```
Kiểm 1270 phần tử theo 3 specification: 42 phần tử không đạt ở 1 specification,
1 specification không có phần tử nào để kiểm
```

42 cái không đạt đều là **tường kính không khai vật liệu** — đọc từ chính file CSV, không đọc từ summary. Specification thứ ba nhắm `IfcTank` (lớp không có trong model) và được **đánh dấu riêng** thay vì in "0 không đạt": bài học §16 — số 0 ở đó nói về bộ lọc, không nói về mô hình.

## Ranh giới — ghi trong tài liệu và trong chính báo cáo HTML

DHCB đọc mô hình theo **ánh xạ Revit → IFC**, cùng ánh xạ bộ xuất dùng, **không phải chính file IFC** → kết luận là *"mô hình sẽ đạt khi xuất"*. Và điều **chưa** chứng minh: chưa đối chiếu với IfcTester/Solibri trên cùng một file IDS — mà "ba phần mềm cùng kết luận" mới chính là mục đích của IDS.

Tài liệu mới: [`docs/kiem-ids.md`](docs/kiem-ids.md). `ParameterRuleCheck` + `configs/checksets/` giữ nguyên cho quy tắc nội bộ công ty mà IDS không mô tả.

author: digitalfils
body:
## Summary

The app was dark-mode-only — every screen hardcoded `S8llColors.grey`/`charcoal`/`white` directly instead of reading from the active theme, so there was no way to support light mode without a full sweep.

- **`theme.dart`**: introduced `S8llTint`, a `ThemeExtension` holding the roles that differ between light/dark (background, surface, surfaceHigh, textPrimary/Secondary/Tertiary, divider) plus a light-mode palette (soft off-white background, white cards, dark text) alongside the existing dark one. The brand constants (lime, error, warning) stay identical in both — same identity regardless of brightness. `buildS8llTheme()` now takes a `Brightness` and returns the matching `ThemeData` with the extension attached; `context.s8ll.xyz` replaces every hardcoded `S8llColors.grey/charcoal/white` call site across 11 screens/widgets. Colors that are intentionally theme-independent (black-on-lime badges, the SOLD photo-overlay stamp) were left as literal constants — those pairings are correct in both modes.
- **`ThemeController`** (`state/theme_controller.dart`): a `ChangeNotifier` wrapping `SharedPreferencesAsync`, exposing light/dark/system and persisting the choice locally — a per-device display setting, not account data, so it deliberately never touches Firestore. `main.dart` wires it into `MaterialApp` via `themeMode`/`theme`/`darkTheme`; a segmented control on the Profile screen lets the user switch it.

## Verification

Built a throwaway (deleted, not part of this diff) web preview rendering real widgets (`ListingCard`, `SellerRatingBadge`, `StarRatingInput`, chips, buttons, an input field) against both themes side by side, toggling between them in a headless browser — text hierarchy, card elevation, and the lime accent all read correctly in both, no console errors.

## Test plan
- [x] `theme_test.dart`: every built theme carries the `S8llTint` extension; light and dark differ; the lime accent stays constant across both; the `ThemeExtension` lerp/fallback contract
- [x] `theme_controller_test.dart`: defaults to system, `setMode` persists, a previously-stored choice loads on construction — using shared_preferences' own `InMemorySharedPreferencesAsync` test double
- [x] `auth_screen_test.dart`'s three tests needed a fix: `context.s8ll` null-checks `Theme.of(context).extension<S8llTint>()`, which a bare `MaterialApp()` without our theme doesn't provide — updated the test to use the real theme, matching what `main.dart` does
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean, all 32 Dart tests pass

author: ayushb3
body:
## Summary

Every modal in the app — `AddItemModal`, `PantryAddSheet`, `CookModal`, `RecipeEditModal`, `RecipeImportModal`, `RecipeRefinementModal`, `RecipeDeleteConfirm`, `ThemePicker` — was a plain `div`: no focus trap, no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, no Escape-to-close. A keyboard or screen-reader user could open one and lose their place in the page entirely. This gives all 8 one shared, tested mechanism instead of eight ad hoc ones.

This issue predates its own tracker home — the work was built once on a since-closed, since-stale PR (#150) against a duplicate issue (#10). This PR is written fresh against the current codebase (that old branch is ~100 commits stale on the files it touched) but the requirements are the same.

## What lands

- **`useModalFocusTrap`** (new hook, `nextjs/src/hooks/`) — one shared mechanism: focus moves into the panel on open (respecting a field's own `autoFocus`, e.g. `RecipeImportModal`'s URL input), Tab/Shift-Tab cycles within the panel (recomputed on every keypress since several modals swap content mid-flight), Escape closes, and focus restores to the trigger element on close — a documented no-op rather than a crash if the trigger has since unmounted.
- **All 8 modals wired to it**, each carrying its own `role="dialog"` (or a justified variant — see below), `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing at its own heading.
- **The one genuinely tricky case, handled explicitly**: `RecipeDeleteConfirm` swaps a "Delete" button for a confirm/cancel row in place, unmounting whatever had focus. The trap re-arms on that swap and deliberately moves focus onto the new view's first focusable element instead of letting it fall to `<body>`.
- **Two justified ARIA deviations**, not oversights: `ThemePicker` keeps `role="group"`/`aria-label` (no `aria-modal`) — it's a lightweight anchored popover with no backdrop, not a page-blocking dialog, and changing its role would have broken its own existing test assertions. `RecipeDeleteConfirm` uses `role="alertdialog"`, the correct standard variant for an inline confirm prompt.
- **Landmarks were already done** — `layout.tsx`'s `<main>` and `BottomNav.tsx`'s `<nav>` predate this PR (confirmed by a prior triage pass and independently re-confirmed by this PR's spec review). Audited, not touched — this PR's diff doesn't touch either file.

## Two latent risks found in review, hardened before merge

Neither was a live bug in the 8 modals shipped here — both are architectural assumptions a future caller of this shared hook could silently violate:

1. **`getFocusable` didn't filter by visibility.** Fine for today (every modal here hides sections via conditional JSX, never CSS), but a future modal with a CSS-collapsed accordion or `display:none`'d block would silently inherit a broken trap. Added a `getComputedStyle`-based visibility walk — deliberately not `offsetParent` (every panel here is `position: fixed`, and `offsetParent` is spec'd `null` for a fixed element regardless of visibility, which would have misreported everything as hidden). Proven with tests that fail without the filter and pass with it.
2. **A code comment overclaimed safety.** The render-phase trigger capture (needed to beat React's commit-phase `autoFocus`) was described as React's "sanctioned lazy-init-ref pattern" — it isn't, precisely: it's a prop-transition-gated write reading live `document.activeElement`, not a pure at-most-once computation. Corrected to state the real, narrower guarantee: it's safe because every modal here opens via a synchronous `useState` setter in a plain event handler, not because the pattern is inherently safe. No behavior change — comment-accuracy only.

## Tests

`cd nextjs && npx tsc --noEmit` → clean · `npx jest --silent` → 34 suites / 309 tests passing (baseline 296 before this PR; 13 new). New: `use-modal-focus-trap.test.tsx` (hook in isolation — trap-on-open, both-direction Tab cycling, Escape, restore-on-close, unmounted-trigger no-op, and the two new visibility-filter cases), `add-item-modal-focus.test.tsx`, `recipe-import-modal-focus.test.tsx`, `recipe-delete-confirm-focus.test.tsx` (end-to-end on 3 representative modals, including the nested-swap case). Every new test was verified to fail against the pre-fix code (via `git stash`) before landing, not just written to pass.

**Not fully verified**: actual screen-reader announcement behavior (role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby as spoken by VoiceOver/NVDA) can't be tested headlessly — closest proxy was asserting the DOM attributes and the `aria-labelledby` target's real text content directly.

## Reviewed

Two-axis review (`/code-review`) via fresh subagents against `main`, twice — once on the initial implementation, once specifically re-scrutinizing the shared hook's React correctness (render-phase ref mutation, concurrent-rendering assumptions) given how much depends on it.
- **Standards**: found and fixed both hardening items above. One duplication judgement call left as-is — the `panelRef`/`useModalFocusTrap(...)`/ARIA-attribute triplet repeats across all 8 files, but each modal's heading id and panel markup genuinely differ (bottom sheet vs. centered dialog vs. inline `alertdialog`), so factoring the hook out (not a wrapper component) was judged the right cut.
- **Spec**: every acceptance criterion satisfied and traced against real code, not just described. Confirmed exactly 8 hook call sites, confirmed landmarks genuinely untouched, confirmed no visual/business-logic drift in any of the 8 files beyond the a11y wiring, confirmed the `RecipeDeleteConfirm` nested-swap case against its real caller in `RecipeBook.tsx`.

## Linked issue

Fixes #291

## Out of scope

- Actual screen-reader manual testing (VoiceOver/NVDA) — not possible in this environment; worth a manual pass before relying on this in production.
- The review-surface extraction work referenced in #259 — this PR's own note says doing #291 first means that future extraction inherits correct dialog semantics rather than needing them retrofitted.
- Any visual, layout, or business-logic change to any of the 8 modals — purely additive a11y wiring.

author: mlngaxri
rizukirr
body:
`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` required the six user override files with a bare `require`:

```lua
require("hypr.monitors")
require("hypr.bindings.applications")
require("hypr.looknfeel")
require("hypr.input")
require("hypr.windows")
require("hypr.autostart")
```

A syntax error in any one of them, or a deleted one, aborts the file. Every later `require` stops, **and so does the theme overlay at the bottom** — the block that applies the theme's colours. Measured in plain lua against the real entrypoint, with a one-character typo in `windows.lua`:

```
lua: error loading module 'hypr.windows' ... unexpected symbol near <eof>
THEME_LOADED=nil
```

Same with the file simply deleted.

These are files the user is invited to edit — the comment above them says "Your overrides". A syntax error in one is an ordinary event, not an exotic one, and the result is a session with no theme, missing the bindings from the later files, and nothing saying why. That is the same shape as the failure in #62/#63.

`default/hypr/vars.lua` already loads the user's `vars.lua` with `pcall`, with the reason written above it: "so a syntax error in the user's file degrades to these defaults rather than killing the session". The entrypoint did not.

## What changes

Each override is loaded with `pcall`. Any that fail are named in a critical notification once the session is up, since nothing can be shown while the config is still parsing. Single quotes and whitespace are stripped from the error text, because the message goes into a single-quoted shell argument — there is a check for that.

## Migration

`hyprland.lua` is user-owned, so `migrations/1788627800.sh` replaces it only where it is still byte-identical to a version hyprsimple shipped, keeping a `.bak`. An edited one is left alone, told what it is still exposed to, and pointed at `hyprsimple-refresh-config.sh`.

## Tests

`test/broken-override-test.sh`, 19 checks, running the real entrypoint in plain lua with `hl` stubbed. Both failure modes, one and two broken files at once, an error containing a quote, and the intact case — which is what stops the fix from being a way to load nothing at all.

Sabotage: restoring the bare `require` turns 8 red; dropping a checksum from the migration turns 3 red.

## Two corrections to my own work here

Both caught by the repository's own guards, which is what they are for.

- My first migration check read the previous `hyprland.lua` with `git show HEAD:`. CI checks out shallow, where that returns the *current* file, so the check would have compared it against itself and passed. `suite-hygiene-test.sh` exists because two suites did this before. It is a committed fixture now, with a check that the fixture actually differs from the current file.
- `committed-symlinks-test.sh` then failed: my temp directory was `$TMP/home/...`, and the literal `/home/` trips the hardcoded-path guard. Renamed rather than loosening the guard.

Sweep: 41 suites, 0 failing, three consecutive runs. shellcheck clean at `style`.

author: jaspercurry
body:
## Summary

`jasper-round-views candidates <round-dir>` answers the owner's "compare configs A/B/C at a held position" row. It groups one round's lateral takes by `candidate_id` at each pose that played more than one, reduces each candidate's curve to its deviation from its own median level over the band, and differences every pair — mean/max deviation and the frequency the worst bin sits at. Writes `candidates.json`, registered in `ARTIFACT_BY_VIEW` so `inventory` names it and the generated menu gains the row; `summary` first, the per-pose `tables` after. stdout carries that summary verbatim as the answer (ADR-0237); no curve or grid reaches it.

A round no pose of which played two candidates is refused by name (`candidates_no_ladder`), with the counts that tell "walked no ladder" apart from "takes named no config". `repeat` is deliberately untouched: it is a noise instrument and a metric that means "spread" cannot also mean "difference".

Both readers already existed: `record_index.bundle_measurements(candidate_id=…, position_deg=…)` selects, `position_cycle.read_take_curves` decides. `record_index.py` needed no widening.

## Premise verified at

`553f55403` (base `82ede4a29`).

- `git grep -n candidate_id -- jasper/cli/round_views` → **0 hits** on the base: no view read the label back.
- `jasper/active_speaker/crossover_v2/record_index.py:41` (`Measurement.candidate_id`) and `:132` (`bundle_measurements(candidate_id=…)`) — the query primitive already filters on it.
- `jasper/active_speaker/crossover_v2/position_cycle.py:65` — `candidate_id` rides `_DEFAULTED_TAKE_FIELDS` (batch 1 lane G), so the join is exact rather than by `(position_deg, vertical_deg)`.

## Line delta

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `jasper/cli/round_views/candidates.py` | 0 | 313 |
| `jasper/cli/round_views/_common.py` | 300 | 301 |
| `jasper/cli/round_views/__init__.py` | 164 | 165 |
| `docs/tuning-operator-runbook.md` | (one generated row) | regenerated |
| `tests/crossover_v2_banked_round.py` | 383 | 419 |
| `tests/test_active_speaker_crossover_v2_round_views.py` | 2916 | 3026 |
| `tests/test_cli_exit_vocabulary.py` | 283 | 284 |

No deletions, so no deletion verdicts.

## Proof

Fixture ladder through the product's own writers — `bank_measure_round(root, candidates=("cand-a","cand-b","cand-c"))` banks one lateral pose per candidate at one bearing, each rung a further 1 dB/octave tilt:

```
$ jasper-round-views candidates <round>
{
  "banked": true,
  "bytes": 5407,
  "candidates": ["cand-a", "cand-b", "cand-c"],
  "max_abs_delta_between": ["cand-a", "cand-c"],
  "max_abs_delta_db": 9.861453919221674,
  "max_abs_delta_hz": 200.0,
  "max_abs_delta_position_deg": 7,
  "max_abs_delta_role": "tweeter",
  "max_abs_delta_vertical_deg": 0,
  "out": ".../candidates.json",
  "pairs": 6,
  "poses": 1,
  "round_dir": "...",
  "takes_naming_no_candidate": 0,
  "view": "candidates"
}
```
stderr: `candidates: 3 candidate(s) over 1 held pose(s), 6 pair(s); widest gap cand-a vs cand-c 9.86 dB @ 200 Hz (tweeter at 7deg) -> .../candidates.json`

Refusal on the stock (ladder-free) fixture round: exit 1, `{"status": "refused", "reason": "candidates_no_ladder", "detail": "{\"candidates_named\": [], \"poses_walked\": 1, \"round_dir\": \"...\", \"takes_naming_no_candidate\": 1}"}`.

Menu row regenerated; `scripts/generate-tuning-tool-menu.py --check` exits 0.

## Review record

`/simplify` unavailable in this agent — its pass was folded into `/code-review`; **single-pass** otherwise. `/code-review` (medium) ran on the working tree and reproduced each finding by invoking the tool:

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| **high** — `np.interp` clamps rather than drops, so comparing a config swept 200–1000 Hz against one swept 200–12000 Hz published an invented 12 dB gap at a bin where the two read identically; the mirror case reported two configs sharing no measured frequency as identical | **fixed.** The declared sweep is now clamped to the grid actually banked at read time, so the per-role intersection is covered by every curve's own bins and no resample reaches past a measured span. Pinned by `test_candidates_compares_only_the_span_both_configs_actually_measured`. |
| **medium** — `candidates_no_ladder` fired for a round that plainly walked a ladder (two candidates, no shared band) | **fixed.** A pose that played two candidates now always publishes a table; a role with nothing to difference is simply absent from it, and the refusal means only what its name says. |
| **low** — `poses_walked` read 0 for a round that walked a pose whose takes named no candidate | **fixed.** The pose is recorded before the candidate check. |
| **medium** — the numeric core (`_deviation`, `_pair_delta`, `_role_table`) lives in `jasper/cli/`, against the package docstring's "thin argparse wrapper over `crossover_v2.round_views`, which owns every number" | **wontfix here, disclosed.** `jasper/active_speaker/crossover_v2/round_views.py` is outside this lane's file ownership for wave 9 batch 2b. The natural follow-up is to lift the four helpers into that module as one `candidate_ladder()` entry point; flagging for the architect rather than reaching across the boundary. |
| **low** — the shared band could be narrowed by a candidate later dropped | **dissolved** by the clamp fix: the intersection is built from bins every candidate actually has, so a candidate is dropped only when the whole role has no comparable span. |
| **low** — the worst pair named the bearing but not the height | **fixed.** `max_abs_delta_vertical_deg` rides beside it. |
| **low** — the fixture's `_tilted` took its gain from the module grid rather than the curve's | **fixed.** |

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_active_speaker_crossover_v2_round_views.py tests/test_cli_exit_vocabulary.py tests/test_crossover_v2_forward_model.py tests/test_round_bank.py tests/test_tuning_tool_menu_generator.py` → **211 passed, 13 skipped**. The roster pin in `test_cli_exit_vocabulary.py` runs the new subcommand to a success and asserts the one bounded answer document; its only edit is the `_VIEW_RUN` row and the fixture round now walking a two-rung ladder.
- `ruff check jasper/cli/round_views/ tests/` → clean.
- `mypy jasper/cli/round_views/` → 15 files, no issues.
- `scripts/generate-tuning-tool-menu.py --check` → exit 0.

body:
## What this changes

Clicking a message notification now opens its DM or space channel and restores the desktop window if it was minimized. Previously Electron discarded the channel context and only focused the window; the browser handler only pushed a mobile screen.

The notification carries its channel, space, and signed-in home user through an optional, backwards-compatible IPC payload. One shared controller handles browser and Electron clicks, checks that the account and channel still match, and navigates through React Router. Remote spaces use the existing channel-to-space and channel-origin maps. Incoming DM-call notifications also open their conversation, without automatically answering the call.

Also fixes the capped realtime-event buffer check: notification delivery continues after its 50 entries stop increasing in length. Self-message suppression resolves the user's identity on the channel's instance.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm build` succeeds (shared, server, and web production builds passed)
- [x] `pnpm dev` starts the server and web client without errors
- [x] Tests pass where applicable (`pnpm test`): web and desktop suites passed
- [x] I ran the change myself, and attached evidence (screenshot, recording, or terminal output) if it affects packaging, installation, or the UI
- [x] I updated the relevant `docs/systems/` spec if this changed schema, API routes, WebSocket events, the federation protocol, permissions, or the design system (desktop IPC and notification behavior documented)
- [x] This change resolves the correct federated identity where it compares IDs, checks permissions, or talks to remote servers (per-origin self ID; existing remote channel routing)
- [x] I have read and agree to the [CLA](../CLA.md) — a separate signature comment follows

## Notes for reviewers

Validation on Windows 11:

- Web: 81 files, 691 tests passed, including 9 notification regressions.
- Desktop: 9 files, 149 tests passed; desktop TypeScript compilation passed.
- Workspace typechecks, i18n checks, and production builds passed.
- Server started on port 3005 and Vite on 5173.

Ran the compiled desktop main process and real preload in Electron 40.10.6 against a local fixture mounting the production `NotificationController`. Native notifications were shown; the harness emitted `click` on the actual Electron Notification object and verified the route and window restoration. This validates the production IPC path, but is not a manual click in Windows Action Center. The fixture used synthetic IDs and no real accounts or messages.

```text
PASS native notification -> main -> preload -> controller -> /channels/@me/dm; minimized window restored
PASS native notification -> main -> preload -> controller -> /channels/remote-space/remote-chat; minimized window restored
PASS Electron 40.10.6 on Windows; screenshot saved
```

Regression coverage also checks stale accounts/deleted channels, an older desktop bridge without the new subscription API, listener cleanup, mobile stack behavior, and delivery after the realtime buffer reaches capacity.

Desktop chat navigation requires both the updated shell and web client; an older shell remains usable and retains its existing focus-only behavior. This does not add service-worker push or cold-start notification activation.

author: minuszka
body:
Starts day 7 of the [audit fix roadmap](docs/AUDIT_FIX_ROADMAP_HU.md). Two data defects that corrupt every closed experiment's numbers.

## Two writers, half-colliding keys

The masternode poller and the listdiff walker both recorded the same chain transitions.

`banned`, `revived` and `registered` were keyed on an exact chain height by both, so they **collided**: the poller's row won and the walker's block-exact one was a silent no-op. `penalty_up`, `service_changed` and `removed` were not — the poller keys those on whatever height it happened to poll at — so every one of them was written **twice**, and every closed experiment counted them twice.

The chain transitions belong to the walker. It reads them from the chain at their own heights, and the reorg rollback drops them again when the blocks that carried them are abandoned; the poller can do neither.

What is left for the poller is the Sentinel ledger, which `MnStateDiff` does not carry at all, plus the `removed` **state mark** — without which a departed masternode stays in the current-state view for ever and keeps being counted as live.

## `quorumHeight` was the mined height

Consensus sets `qcTx.height` to `pindexPrev->nHeight + 1` (`commitment.cpp:201`), which is where the commitment is mined. So the field held the mined height under a name that says otherwise, and every row read `quorumHeight === minedHeight`. The key survived only because the quorum hash is in it.

It is derived from the cycle now. For a profile whose layout is not known here the node's own field is kept: naming it imprecisely is better than inventing a number for it.

## Tests

Negative control by restoring the old poller wholesale. The Day 1 positive control had to be rewritten — it asserted the poller writes a `removed` event, which is now the walker's — and it asserts the state mark instead.

```
typecheck  exit 0
tests      74 files, 697 passing (was 695)
build      exit 0
```

## Still owed for this day

Reconciling the round record from the commitment index, backfilling `minedHeight`, walker durability across a mid-batch failure, `effectiveSize` at the round's own base height, and ZMQ supervision.

## Description

Adds a `labels` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs before the
rest of CI and fails a pull request that is missing either a
`component: ...` label or a `type: ...` label. Every other job now
`needs` this job (directly, or transitively through `rust-build`/
`rust-test`), so an unlabeled pull request's CI stops at this cheap
check instead of running the full suite.

The job reads `context.payload.pull_request.labels` straight from the
event payload via `actions/github-script`, so it needs no extra
permissions. On an ordinary push to `the-one` (no pull request in the
event), the check step is skipped and the job succeeds, so push-triggered
CI runs are unaffected.

The repository already had two `type: ...` labels in occasional use
(`type: feature`, `type: documentation`), but that requirement wasn't
documented anywhere alongside the existing `component: ...` requirement.
This also documents it in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (kept byte-identical
per the repo's own synchronization convention) and `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
next to the existing component-label documentation.

author: apholmes7-bot
body:
**The owner, after rebuilding Nine Mile Creek:** *"the wharfs need layering work as you can disappear under them, also theres gaps between sections."*

Both are true, and measuring them found a third thing nobody asked about: **every boat moored at the wall was drawn inside it.** All three have one cause — the quay face is drawn as Y-sorted decor, and it is not decor.

---

## 1. The diagnosis, measured before anything was touched

### The vanishing band — 3.19 m deep, along the whole wall

`logCrib` is not a face. It is a face **plus its own 5 m deck top**, drawn foreshortened. Measured on the committed sheet, at the mooring face's facing (cell 4) the ink runs from **2.63 units below** the pivot to **5.56 above** it, while the lip — the line it was sorted on — sits only **2.38** above. So **3.19 units of drawn deck stand up-screen of the sort line**. The apron's facing (cell 6) measures **3.20**.

Anything Y-sorted standing in that band sorts *behind* the piece and is overdrawn by it:

* the player anywhere in the first 3.19 m in from the edge — the working strip, where the ladders and the crew coming off a boat are;
* the quay's own **bollards**, at lip + 0.5 m: order **852** against the face's **854**.

Plate 01 is the walker at berth 5, one metre in from the lip: she is not there. Plate 02 is the same frame with the face hidden: she is. (The painted ground already *is* the deck, so those pixels were a duplicate of terrain that cost the player her body.)

### The fleet — and why no sort line could ever have fixed it

Every `BoatVisualDef` ships `SortingOrder 1`, and `BoatHullSkinner` hands it straight to the hull's composite overlay — **below `SortingBands.DecorFloor` (2)**. A face anywhere in the decor band beat every boat at the wall at every position. At Nine Mile Creek that meant **the five moored boats were drawn inside the wall and invisible**; plate AB-2 is the before/after. This is `hull-sorts-below-the-decor-floor`, live.

That is why the handoff's option (b) — move the sort line to the piece's back edge — could not be the answer on its own, and why option (a) — re-bake the face without its deck top — would not have been either: a boat alongside overlaps the wall **below** the lip, where a deck-top re-bake changes nothing.

### The gaps are not at the junctions. They are three edges with no run on them at all.

The wharf is a fill: the deck stands at **+3.00 m** and the harbour shoal at **−1.60 m**, so **every** edge of it is a 4.60 m wall. Walking the perimeter on the built terrain and asking, every half metre, whether the ground 3 m outside is more than a metre below the deck:

| edge | stands over water | drawn before |
|---|---|---|
| quay SOUTH (the mooring face) | x 92.3 … 170.0 — 77.7 m | ✅ |
| **quay EAST (the wharf head)** | y 87.0 … 93.8 — 6.8 m | ❌ **6.5 m bare** |
| quay NORTH | — | n/a: the spit stands behind it |
| apron EAST (the working face) | y 44.0 … 86.0 — 42.0 m | ✅ |
| **apron WEST** | y 44.0 … 92.0 — 48.0 m | ❌ **47.5 m bare** |
| **apron SOUTH** | x 82.0 … 92.0 — 10.0 m | ❌ **9.5 m bare** |
| apron NORTH | — | n/a: the spit's bank runs onto it |

**63.5 m of 4.60 m wall with nothing drawn on it.** Those numbers are the new coverage test run against the face list `main` ships — the null case, run first.

**The junctions the charter named are fine, and the numbers say why.** Along a run nothing can gap (10.9 m drawn on a ≤ 9.6 m pitch), and the ends overhang: the mooring face covers x 91.40…170.60 for a wall of 92…170, the apron's east face 43.32…87.68 for 44…87, the arm 93.66…186.34 for 94…186. The two runs cross *past* the L in both directions. The gap the owner saw at "the wall's east end" is the head having no run at all, and "the apron's end" is the same.

## 2. What changed

**The face leaves the decor band.** A quay face is the edge of the land, and that has a property no other sprite in the region has: **nothing is ever behind it.** Everything that can overlap it is either standing on the deck it holds up or floating in the water in front of it — both draw over. The only things behind it are the sea and the seabed. So it draws on a **fixed rung of `SortingBands.WharfDeckMin…Max`**, the band #462 kept open for exactly this ("a pier stands over water, so the whole deck is above `Sea` and below `DecorFloor`"), under the rung a hull composites on and over the sea.

#462's objection to that band — *"six orders cannot resolve an 84 m wall"* — was about resolving the wall against **itself**, which it never has to do: every piece of a run shares one lip line, and overlapping pieces of a run are the same picture at the same height. What the six orders must resolve is the six **runs**, and only five pairs of them overlap. The ladder, nearest the camera first:

| rung | run | why |
|---:|---|---|
| **0** | apron SOUTH, breakwater | the seaward corner of the wharf; the arm overlaps nothing |

author: sebtardif
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where four docs workflows could occupy a GitHub-hosted runner until the six-hour default if a step hung. `update-skills`, `Translate Incremental`, `Stale`, and `CodeQL` had no `timeout-minutes`. Sibling workflows (`r2-pages`, `pages`, `docs-code-ci`, `llms-full`, `translate-locale`) already set one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each local job in those four files now sets `timeout-minutes`. Short jobs use 15. CodeQL uses 30, matching Docs Code CI. Incremental `prepare` uses 70 so the default 3600-second debounce can finish. GitHub does not allow `timeout-minutes` on a job that only `uses:` a reusable workflow, so incremental `validate-workflow-shell` and `finalize` are bounded in the callee files (`15` and `60`). The locale worker already had 360.

## User Impact

A hung skills update, incremental debounce, stale scan, or CodeQL run now fails on a job budget instead of holding a runner for up to six hours. Healthy runs are unchanged. Incremental translation still waits up to one hour for main to settle.

## Evidence

Live `node` reading the four workflow files (plus the two incremental callees). The reader walks `jobs:` and reports each job's `timeout-minutes`. It was first run against `origin/main` copies written to a temp dir (production files left in place), then against the patched files.

Before, every job in the four files reports `timeout: null`:

```console
$ node C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-live-read.mjs C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-main-wf\update-skills.yml C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-main-wf\translate-incremental.yml C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-main-wf\stale.yml C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-main-wf\codeql.yml
[
  { "workflow": "update-skills.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "update", "timeout": null } ], "hasTimeoutString": false },
  { "workflow": "translate-incremental.yml", "jobs": [
      { "name": "validate-workflow-shell", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "prepare", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "plan", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "translate", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "provider-preflight", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "finalize", "timeout": null }
    ], "hasTimeoutString": false },
  { "workflow": "stale.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "stale", "timeout": null } ], "hasTimeoutString": false },
  { "workflow": "codeql.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "analyze", "timeout": null } ], "hasTimeoutString": false }
]
```

After the patch, local jobs report a positive timeout. Reusable-call jobs stay unset on the caller (GitHub restriction). Their callees now report 15 and 60:

```console
$ node C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-live-read.mjs .github/workflows/update-skills.yml .github/workflows/translate-incremental.yml .github/workflows/stale.yml .github/workflows/codeql.yml .github/workflows/translate-shell-check-reusable.yml .github/workflows/translate-finalize-reusable.yml
[
  { "workflow": "update-skills.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "update", "timeout": 15 } ] },
  { "workflow": "translate-incremental.yml", "jobs": [
      { "name": "validate-workflow-shell", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "prepare", "timeout": 70 },
      { "name": "plan", "timeout": 15 },
      { "name": "translate", "timeout": null },
      { "name": "provider-preflight", "timeout": 15 },
      { "name": "finalize", "timeout": null }
    ] },
  { "workflow": "stale.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "stale", "timeout": 15 } ] },
  { "workflow": "codeql.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "analyze", "timeout": 30 } ] },
  { "workflow": "translate-shell-check-reusable.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "check", "timeout": 15 } ] },
  { "workflow": "translate-finalize-reusable.yml", "jobs": [ { "name": "finalize", "timeout": 60 } ] }
]
```

`rg -L timeout-minutes .github/workflows/` now lists only `docs-live-smoke.yml` (sibling #164). The four files from this finding are no longer in that list. `r2-upload.mjs` and `docs-live-smoke.yml` are not in this diff.

Related: [#164](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/pull/164), [#69](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/pull/69), [#70](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/pull/70), [#61](https://github.com/openclaw/docs/pull/61).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Four docs workflows had no job timeout, so a hang could occupy a runner until GitHub's six-hour default.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node v24.19.0, repo checkout at C:\Users\sebta\.grok\tmp\pr-gate-batch\docs-f004 on branch fix/workflow-timeouts. origin/main copies were written to a temp dir; production files were left in place.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** node C:\Users\sebta\AppData\Local\Temp\docs-f004-live-read.mjs on the origin/main copies, then the same reader on the patched workflow files.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above. update=15, prepare=70, plan=15, provider-preflight=15, stale=15, analyze=30. Incremental shell-check callee=15, finalize callee=60. Caller jobs that only `uses:` a reusable workflow stay unset.
- **Observed result after fix:** A hung update-skills, incremental prepare, stale, or CodeQL job is now killed by timeout-minutes instead of the six-hour default. Incremental debounce still has 70 minutes so the default 3600-second wait can finish.
- **What was not tested:** A live scheduled run of update-skills, Stale, CodeQL, or Translate Incremental. This change only adds job budgets; it does not change what those workflows do when they complete.

## Summary

Audit finding F004. Sibling hang bounds are #161, #163, #164, and #165.

## Summary

Next's default static file serving only issues a revalidatable cache (`ETag`/`Last-Modified`, no explicit `Cache-Control`), so every return visit re-requests every file and pays a conditional-GET round-trip before sound is ready.
- Added a `headers()` rule in `next.config.ts` for `/audio/:path*` setting `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, alongside the existing global security headers (unaffected — still apply everywhere via the separate `/(.*)` rule).
- Trade-off (documented in a code comment): these filenames aren't content-hashed, so if a sound file's content is ever replaced, it needs a new filename rather than overwriting the old one in place — otherwise clients could keep an old cached version for up to a year. This is the standard trade-off for long-lived static asset caching and matches how these files are actually maintained (stable per-profile assets, not frequently edited in place).
- No visual/UI changes.

author: ikasast
body:
The first slice of at-rest encryption: **the key material only — nothing is encrypted yet.** Identity came before ownership for the same reason; putting the columns on top of key handling that has already been running is safer than shipping both at once.

## The shape

One random master key per account, wrapped **twice** — by the password, and by a recovery code shown once and never stored. Both hold the same key, so either opens everything and neither exists in the clear. **There is no third copy**: an administrator can issue a reset link and cannot read what it unlocks.

**A symmetric key, not the keypair the plan sketched.** A keypair lets a server encrypt without being able to read, which matters when writes happen with nobody signed in — and here they don't. Recording happens with the person present, and a queued job runs as its owner and *waits* for their key. The keypair would have been a moving part that bought nothing. Flagging it in case you'd rather I kept it.

## The lifetime is the queue's, not the session's

A key is in memory only because minutes are written after the browser has gone. The moment its owner has nothing queued or running, the dispatcher drops it and zeroes the bytes. A session lasts thirty days; tying a key to that would mean holding one for a month after the last thing needing it finished — most of the way back to not encrypting.

**What this cannot do**, which belongs in the docs and not only in a comment: while a key is held, somebody who controls the running process can read that account's data. What is protected is the disk, a database dump, a backup file, and an administrator reading rows.

## A password has to exist first

An account that only ever arrives through the tailnet has no secret to derive a wrapping key from, so it has no key until it sets a password — which the account screen already offers for a different reason. Worth knowing before the columns land: those accounts simply won't be encrypted.

## Resetting refuses to quietly destroy anything

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Reset with the recovery code | Same key kept; nothing rewritten |
| Reset without it | **409** — "enter your recovery code, or confirm you are starting again" |
| Reset with `startOver: true` | New key, new code shown once; the old data stays on disk and unreadable |

Somebody who has mislaid the code for a minute meets a refusal, not a year of unopenable meetings.

## Verified end to end

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First account | key + code issued once; **the code appears nowhere in the row** |
| Change password | key kept, no new code, sign-in works |
| Reset, no code, no confirmation | 409 `needsRecoveryCode` |
| Reset with the code | 200, recovery wrapping unchanged — same key |
| Wrong code | refused |
| `startOver` | new code, different from the old |
| Old code afterwards | refused; new code accepted |

478 tests pass; typecheck, lint and build clean. The crypto tests cover the cases that fail silently — a wrapping that opens with the wrong secret, a tampered ciphertext, a code typed back in lower case without dashes — and four guards were validated by reintroducing the bug, including removing the GCM tag check and letting the reset ignore its own flag.

## Still to come

Columns encrypted, the bigram blind index, the decrypt-and-scan fallback, and migrating existing data. Plus one UI piece I have deliberately not built yet: **the screen that shows the recovery code**. It is returned by the API and currently only visible there — I would rather agree what it says before writing it, since it is the one screen where somebody skimming loses their data.

author: kodes-agency
body:
`ops:deploy-ci-images` defaulted to all six GitHub-backed services, so every
run re-attempted the four sidecars. That is not a harmless retry: the second
run crashed `google-egress-gateway` exactly as the first did, with
`required Google gateway setting is missing: RELEASE_SHA`, taking the Google
review path down until it was reconnected to `release` and redeployed. Left
as-is, the next person to run the command would do it again.

`RELEASE_SHA` is platform-supplied deployment metadata that only exists for a
repo-sourced deployment. It is absent from the Railway variables API, from
`railway variable list`, from `Dockerfile.google-egress-gateway` (which bakes
only `IMAGE_SOURCE_REVISION`) and from the tsup config, yet the gateway
requires it unconditionally at `services/google-egress-gateway/environment.ts:137`
and `ai-egress-gateway` requires it identically at `:106`.

So the default plan is now the two services that are actually proven on a
digest source: `web` and `worker`, both moved today and healthy across two
revisions. `--include-sidecars` opts the other four in once that coupling is
fixed, and `--include-provider-redis` stays a separate opt-in ordered LAST.
Three tests pin the three plans.

Documents two consequences of the cutover that are easy to get wrong:

- A digest-pinned service NO LONGER follows `release`. A fix now needs two
  deploys - push `release` for the sidecars, then run this command for web and
  worker. `railway deployment list` reports the branch commit for the
  environment, so it will show the release head for a service that is really
  running an older image; read the service config instead.
- `/api/health/metrics` now reports `release.sha` as `unknown`, because that is
  the same platform-supplied `RELEASE_SHA` an image source never receives.
  Release identity in the ops snapshot is degraded until the coupling is fixed.

Also records the two remaining quarantined reply observations and why they did
NOT clear after #441: their predecessor material revision is
`legacy-unverified-v0` with a NULL `normalized_digest`, so the equivalence
#441 requires cannot be proven, only assumed. That is a claim about legacy
data rather than a guard bug, so the three options are written down for an
owner decision instead of being decided here. The events are inert - both
Inbox items are closed - and must not be discarded, because they are the only
evidence of the case.

---
Local verification: typecheck, lint:ci, full unit suite (1,307 files / 12,790 tests), 12/12 in `deploy-ci-images.test.ts`.
