author: zaynsaul
body:
## Summary
Splitting a supplier order and choosing "Opret ny ordre" (create new order) as the split
target cloned the source order's number (`ordrenr`) onto the new order instead of assigning
it a fresh one — so two (or more) supplier orders ended up with the identical order number.
This broke anything that looks orders up by number: `kreditor/ordre.php`'s own
ordrenr-based lookup, supplier-invoice matching, and the purchasing overview.

**This is very likely the root cause of previously archived production issue SST-237**
(MEDSHOP: "kreditorordre oprettet 2 gange med samme kreditorordrenummer" — a 0,00 duplicate,
reported happening "from time to time" in production, archived without a confirmed root
cause). Worth reopening/cross-referencing SST-237 once this is verified.

Related: MB-1 / SST-652 (#525) fixed blank pages in this same file — this is the numbering
sibling of that issue.

## Root Cause
In `kreditor/orderIncludes/moveOrderLines.php`, the "create new order" path copies the
source order row into a temp table, rewrites only the `id` column, then inserts it back into
`ordrer`:

```sql
CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE temp_table AS SELECT * FROM ordrer WHERE id='$id'
UPDATE temp_table SET id='$newId' WHERE id='$id'
INSERT INTO ordrer SELECT * FROM temp_table
```

Every other field, including `ordrenr`, gets copied over unchanged — nothing later in the
file corrects it.

## What are the changes about?
Before building the copy, compute the next free kreditor order number and set it on the temp
row alongside the rewritten `id`. Used the same scoping the codebase already relies on
elsewhere for this (`kreditor/ublimport.php`):

```sql
select max(ordrenr) from ordrer where art = 'KO' OR art = 'KK'
```
+1, then set on the temp row before the insert.

Confirmed via the database that kreditor (`KO`) and debitor (`DO`) orders use separate,
overlapping numbering — a plain global `max(ordrenr)` across all order types would have
picked the wrong (potentially still-colliding) number.

## Files Changed
- kreditor/orderIncludes/moveOrderLines.php

## How to Test
1. Creditors → Order → open an order with 2+ lines.
2. Click "Split" → in the target dropdown choose "Opret ny ordre", set a quantity to move,
   click Flyt.
3. Verify the newly created order has a **different** ordrenr from the source order — not a
   clone.
4. Open the split dialog again on the same source order and repeat the split — verify the
   dropdown does not show a duplicate order number, and each new split-created order gets
   its own distinct, incrementing number.
5. Check Creditors → Order list — verify no two orders share the same ordrenr.
6. Verify number-based lookups still work correctly for both the original and the newly
   created order: `kreditor/ordre.php`'s ordrenr lookup, supplier-invoice matching, and the
   purchasing overview.
7. Confirm both `KO` (order) and `KK` (credit note) order types are correctly included in
   the next-number calculation, and that a `DO` (debitor) order number is never
   accidentally reused or collided with.
8. Reproduce the original bug against pre-fix code (e.g. via `git stash`) to confirm it
   still occurs there, then confirm it's resolved post-fix — proving this is a genuine
   fix, not a coincidental non-reproduction.

## Acceptance Criteria
| # | Scenario | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Split a supplier order using "Opret ny ordre" as target | New order gets the next free ordrenr, not the source's number |
| 2 | Repeat split multiple times on the same or different source orders | No two orders ever share the same ordrenr |
| 3 | Number-based lookups (kreditor/ordre.php, invoice matching, purchasing overview) | Work correctly for all resulting orders |
| 4 | KO/KK numbering scope | Correctly separated from DO (debitor) numbering — no cross-type collision |

## Verification
Verified live end-to-end: built a test order and performed the actual split through the
real running app.
- Pre-fix: the new order came out with the same order number as the source, reproducing the
  exact reported bug.
- Post-fix: the new order got the next free number instead, with no duplicates left
  anywhere.

## Have you checked the following? 
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation at https://github.com/DANOSOFT/saldi/wiki
- [x] I have checked that i am not linking to any external resources such as external style- or JavaScript-files, that could compromise stability
- [x] I have read and understood the developer guidelines  
      https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GOmomtvKf21OV2VWNOIPweDi4gJHpMCK5qXzrPrypUc/edit?usp=sharing

author: roryweston26-source
body:
## What this is

`MEASURE-CLAUDE-LIMITS.md` was written on 2026-09-01 around an instrument that cannot see the usage it was trying to measure. This rebuilds it, adds the real instrument, and records what that instrument found.

**The old protocol said to pair panel readings with an EcoMeter export.** EcoMeter watches the claude.ai DOM; Claude Code usage never touches a browser. On a Claude Code account that export measures nothing that is burning the limit.

**The right instrument was already on disk.** The `.jsonl` transcripts under `~/.claude/projects` record every API request with exact input, cache-write (5m/1h split), cache-read and output counts. Caching stops being the protocol's headline caveat and becomes a measured field.

## The five-hour cap is measured, not estimated

A 429 is a **100% observation** and needs no percentage reading at all. Six exist in the transcripts, all pure Opus 5; five survive the contamination test.

Six observations of one cap that disagree by 3.8× in raw tokens are six observations of the wrong unit. `scripts/measure-claude-limits.js` grid-searches for the unit in which they agree:

| unit | spread |
|---|---|
| raw tokens | 3.84× |
| API dollars | 2.12× |
| **`input + cache_write + 0·cache_read + 7.75·output`** | **1.25×** (CV 8.3%) |

- **Cache reads weigh zero.** Forcing them to their billing weight of 0.1 — with the output weight re-optimised in their favour, so the comparison is fair — degrades the fit to 27% CV. Re-sent context is close to free against the limit, the opposite of what a naive token model says.
- **Output weighs ~8×, against 5× on the price list.** The meter is not the invoice; the same five windows span **$35–$74**.

**FIVE-HOUR CAP = 3.09M units**, confirmed four times out of sample: levels of **18% vs 17%** and **45% vs 43%**, plus caps of 3.43M and 3.21M back-derived from 12- and 14-point moves.

## Two counting traps, both hit first

1. **The transcript writes one assistant message once per content block**, every copy carrying the identical complete usage object. Dedupe on `message.id`. The usage panel's own **Local activity** line then validates that exactly — **72 (24h) and 2138 (7d), both matching to the request** — so the app counts requests right and tokens wrong. **The over-count must never be corrected for**: it is the mean blocks-per-message and varies 1.2×–2.6× with how tool-heavy the stretch was.
2. **Anthropic rounds a window's reset up to the next 10-minute mark**, so `resetsAt − 5h` can precede the true first request. A larger gap means unseen usage; that sample is dropped, not averaged.

**Trap 2 doubles as a detector, and it fired immediately.** A five-hour window opens on its first request, so `resets − 5h` names a moment something was sent. A window opened `2026-09-02T21:50Z` with the transcripts silent for 104 minutes around it. **Until that is explained the one-machine scope is unproven and every cap here is a floor.**

## The weekly is not solved, and nothing is published

Best estimate **~10.2× the five-hour cap, band 8.1–13.6**, from a four-point move. Nothing in `plan-limits.json`, `pricing.html` or the Auditor changes in this PR.

**It is Pro only, and Anthropic's own wording is why the ratio cannot be carried across.** The Max article quantifies the multiplier on one meter — *"Max 5x provides five times more usage **per session**"*, *"Max 20x provides 20 times more usage **per session**"* — then introduces the weekly separately, with no multiple and no size. If the weekly does not scale with the session, Pro's ~10.2× becomes **2.0× on Max 5× and 0.5× on Max 20×**, and a ratio below 1 means the weekly is exhausted before a single five-hour window can be filled.

That asymmetry is publishable today without measuring a Max account: **Anthropic quantifies the multiplier on the window that clears itself in five hours and leaves the window that governs your month unquantified, in the same paragraph.**

## Also in here

- **Use the panel's copy button, not a screenshot** — exact percentages, exact reset instants, indexed meter names (`session-0`, `weekly_all-1`) implying a list, and the request count that validated the parser.
- **Check the client version.** `1.44121.1` rendered Output as 186 / 361 / 555, wrong by three orders of magnitude while neighbouring rows over-counted consistently; `1.44121.2` fixed it.
- **A mid-week weekly reset is recorded and parked** at Rory's direction — dated to within eleven minutes by two independent methods, cause unknown, nothing about it publishable until someone establishes whether it was a credit top-up, a plan change, or documented behaviour differing from actual. The Δ-based method routes around it.
- **FRESHNESS B10** carries all of it; B6's pointer to the superseded provisional 9× now says so.

## Verification

All seven guards pass: `check-prices`, `check-auditor`, `check-clock`, `check-transparency`, `test-auditor`, `test-cost-model`, `test-water-model`.

<!-- Length matches the change: a one-line fix gets one-line sections.
     `pnpm verify` passes; no real names, amounts, payees or institutions
     anywhere below — this is a public repo about a private ledger. -->

## Summary

`pnpm e2e` is one command with no keypress: Playwright's global setup clones and seeds the scratch Postgres database as before, then starts the API and the Expo web bundle itself on probed ports, runs the five API probes and five browser journeys, and tears everything down. Tier 2 stays on demand and outside `pnpm verify`; what is gone is the person in the middle.

## Why

The suite printed a scratch `APP_DATABASE_URL`, asked the operator to start the API against it and Metro in another terminal, and blocked on Enter. A check that needs three windows and a copied URL is a check that stops being run, and the URL it printed carried the app role's password onto the screen. The owner's ruling: this should be automatic.

## What

- `tools/e2e/setup/global.ts` (new) is the `globalSetup` entry. Order: validate `E2E_API_PORT`/`E2E_WEB_PORT` and the two URL overrides, create the scratch database (`database.ts`'s `createScratch()`, formerly the default export), start the API, start the web bundle, set `E2E_API_URL`/`E2E_WEB_URL`, return a teardown that stops web, stops the API, drops the scratch database, each step in `finally`. A setup that throws unwinds by hand, because Playwright runs no teardown for a failed `globalSetup`, and a SIGINT during setup unwinds whatever exists so far (best effort, documented: a fast Ctrl-C can still leave a uniquely named `waltning_test_e2e_*` clone and a process the next run's probe steps over).
- `tools/e2e/setup/servers.ts` (new). `findFreePort` probes upward from the default (API 3300, web 8082, or the `E2E_*_PORT` value) for the first port that passes two tests on both loopback addresses: this process can bind it on `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, and a connect to each is refused. The bind catches a listener on one address family; the connect catches a wildcard listener, which macOS lets a specific-address bind sit under. A host with no IPv6 loopback skips the `::1` half. `EACCES`/`EPERM` throw naming the privileged port rather than scanning on. The chosen ports are printed.
- Readiness is two facts in order: the child's own log says it bound the exact port (the API's `server started` diagnostic with `"port":n`; Metro's `Waiting on http://localhost:n`, whose port comes from the bound address), then HTTP answers on `127.0.0.1:n`, then the child is still alive. A 200 before the log line never counts. Every poll and every emitted URL uses `127.0.0.1`, never `localhost`.
- Both children are spawned `detached` into their own process group with output in `tools/e2e/.logs/` (gitignored, truncated per run, tailed into every error). `stop()` sends the group SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 s, even when the group leader has already exited, and resolves as soon as the group is gone. A child that dies after spawning fails the run at once with its exit code and log tail instead of waiting out the readiness deadline; a spawn error goes through the same path; a permanent no-op error listener keeps a late error from taking the runner down.
- The specs require `E2E_API_URL` and `E2E_WEB_URL` and throw naming the variable; the `127.0.0.1:3000` and `:8081` fallbacks are gone, so a run can never pass against a developer's own API or Metro. `rates.spec.ts` now imports `support.ts` like the other four.
- Appliance mode is unchanged: with both `E2E_API_URL` and `E2E_WEB_URL` set (`make appliance-e2e`), nothing local starts. Exactly one set throws; both empty, which is what a `.env` copied from `.env.example` yields, runs locally.
- `.env.example` documents `E2E_API_PORT` and `E2E_WEB_PORT`. `README.md`, `docs/wiki/Getting-Started.md`, `Makefile`, `playwright.config.ts`, `database.ts` and `smoke.ts` describe what `make e2e` / `pnpm e2e` now do; Postgres (`pnpm db:up`) is the one prerequisite, and `pnpm e2e:smoke --write` is the read-only probe of a running stack.

## How

**Not a `webServer` block.** Playwright starts `webServer` before `globalSetup`, and the API must be pointed at a database only `globalSetup` creates. The setup owns the whole lifecycle instead.

**Probing replaced refusal.** The first design gave each server a fixed port and refused to start if it was held; the owner ruled that tooling probes for a free port automatically. Reusing an already-running Metro on 8081 was also rejected: it can be another worktree's bundle, and the browser's OPFS ledger is per origin, so the suite and a developer session would share one ledger.

**Why bind and connect.** A bind-test alone reads a wildcard listener as free (`SO_REUSEADDR`); a connect-test alone misses a listener bound to the other address family. Together they close both, without binding wildcards, which can trip the macOS firewall prompt. The probe is still not a reservation: the window between the probe and the child's bind is stated in the code, and the log-line-then-HTTP readiness is what confirms the server on that port is ours.

**Ports and overrides use truthiness, not `!== undefined`.** `process.loadEnvFile` turns `E2E_API_PORT=` into `""`, which `??` treats as set and `Number` turns into 0. Every numeric env read validates `/^\d+$/` and range.

## Test plan

- `pnpm e2e` twice in a row from a clean state: no prompt, 10/10, ports and `waltning_test_e2e_*` clones empty afterwards.
- Busy default port: `API_PORT=3300 pnpm --filter @waltning/api start` in the background, then `pnpm e2e` chooses 3301 and passes.
- IPv6-only squatter: `python3 -m http.server 8099 --bind ::1` with `E2E_WEB_PORT=8099` → the run skips 8099 and passes on 8100.
- Wildcard squatter: `python3 -m http.server 8082 --bind ::` → the run skips 8082 and passes on 8083 (a bind-test alone reports 8082 free; confirmed before the fix).
- `findFreePort(80, 3)` throws naming the privileged port instead of scanning.
- Failed setup: with the API deliberately unable to start, the scratch database is dropped and no process is left (`lsof`, `pgrep` by pid).
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm biome check .`, `pnpm vitest run tests` green; the pre-commit gate ran on every commit.

Five Opus adversarial rounds; every finding above L was fixed and re-verified in the following round.

## Evidence

```
[e2e] API → port 3300
[e2e] Web → port 8083          # 8082 held by a wildcard listener
10 passed (12.2s)
```

## References

`tools/e2e/playwright.config.ts` header; `docs/wiki/Getting-Started.md` §Testing; `packages/db/src/test/scratch.ts` (per-checkout template, the same isolation applied here to the web port).

author: jjackson
body:
## Product Description

Deploying the targeting-UI work and then *looking at production* turned up two defects worse than the one being shipped. Both are the same shape: **a number that was fixed, sitting next to an identical-looking number that was not.**

### `fever_prevalence` had never been loaded

It was in the measure registry. It was in the `child_health` load stage. It had **zero rows**.

So `malaria_treatment`'s `conditional_on` could never resolve, the corrected derivation produced nothing for it — and **1,700 rows of the pre-fix shape simply stayed**. That shape is the whole under-five population times the untreated share: exactly the six-times-too-high error that had just been found and fixed for ORS, alive and undetected in a second measure, one snapshot away from production.

Loaded now: 466 rows, 38 countries. Nigeria's malaria gap derives for the first time — 2,840,277 untreated fever episodes in a fortnight, 57,594,507 over a year — where it previously carried the wrong arithmetic.

### A derivation never swept the arithmetic it replaced

The root cause is structural. `upsert` refreshes the rows a loader emits and leaves everything else alone. That is **right for a source** — DHS not returning a region this year does not void last year's survey. It is **wrong for a derivation**, where a row is nothing but a function of other rows: if the function no longer produces it, the old value is not stale data, it is *the previous version of the arithmetic*, and it looks exactly like a fresh one.

Derivations now sweep their own scope. The indicator list comes off the registry, so a coverage measure added later is covered without anyone remembering — which is the failure the mechanism exists to catch.

Re-deriving removed **13,054 stale rows across 16 measures**:

| measure | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `itn_use_gap` / `itn_access_gap` | 3,480 | 2,261 |
| `irs_coverage_gap` | 3,456 | 2,237 |
| `vitamin_a_coverage_gap` | 3,029 | 1,857 |
| `ors_coverage_gap` | 2,803 | 1,746 |
| `zinc_coverage_gap` | 2,698 | 1,743 |
| …and 11 others | | |

Every survivor sits at ADM0/1/2 on a boundary this app owns. **Liberia's figures are unchanged to the digit.**

### A snapshot restore could only ever add

Which would have undone all of the above. The 13,054 swept rows would have survived on production regardless, because `targeting_import` upserts and never deletes — the restore step meant to ship the fix would have silently reverted it.

`--prune` makes a snapshot authoritative for what it covers: the `(indicator, country)` pairs it actually contains. A Liberia-only export cannot empty the continent, and an indicator the snapshot never mentions is left alone — **omission is not deletion**. Off by default, because a restore that silently deletes is not something a caller should get without asking.

## Technical Summary

- `derive.sweep_derived(produced, indicators, iso_codes)` + `derive.gap_indicators()` (registry-driven), wired into the `coverage_gaps` stage.
- `snapshot.import_snapshot(..., prune=True)` and `targeting_import --prune`; deletion batched at 5,000 to avoid one enormous `IN` clause.
- `fixtures/snapshot.json` pinned to `targeting-snapshot-20260905-1322.zip` — 122,885 values against 105,069 on 1 September.
- Also: the projection caveat named a country by ISO code (`No growth series for LBR`) where every sibling list on that panel is names.

## Safety Assurance

**753 tests pass** across `indicators` + `mcp`. Nine new:

- Sweep: removes what is no longer produced, keeps what is, never touches a measured source, stays inside its ISO scope, covers the annual siblings.
- Prune: removes what the snapshot lacks, leaves it alone without the flag, never deletes an indicator the snapshot does not mention, never deletes a country it does not cover.

Verified against the real dataset, not fixtures: all 36,571 surviving gap rows at ADM0/1/2 on owned boundaries, 53 countries, zero orphans. Liberia's ORS chain reproduces 713,882 / 51,429 / 1,025,769 unprojected and 791,563 / 60,671 / 1,210,108 at 2027 — identical to before the sweep.

Deployment: no migrations. Prod needs `targeting_import --from-manifest --prune` after this ships, which is why `--prune` had to land first.

body:
## Summary
- The MyInstants-specific `Referer`/`Sec-Fetch-*` headers were applied by `if needs_cf_bypass and "myinstants.com" in uri:` buried in the generic streaming path. Every additional Cloudflare-protected host would have meant another `in uri` special case in shared transport code.
- Replaced it with a `DOMAIN_HEADER_PROFILES` registry keyed by domain plus a `get_domain_headers()` lookup, so adding a host is a data entry at the top of the file rather than a branch in the fetch path.

### Deliberate behavior change worth reviewing
The lookup now matches the URI's **hostname** (exact or subdomain) instead of substring-matching the whole URI. The old check also fired for URLs that merely *contained* the string:

| URL | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `https://www.myinstants.com/media/sounds/x.mp3` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `https://myinstants.com/media/sounds/y.mp3` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `https://cdn.myinstants.com/sounds/z.mp3` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `https://evil.com/redirect?to=myinstants.com/x.mp3` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `https://notmyinstants.com/x.mp3` | ✅ | ❌ |

The last two mean the old code would send `Referer: https://www.myinstants.com` to an unrelated (potentially attacker-chosen) host. I treated tightening that as part of the fix rather than faithfully preserving it — say the word if you'd rather keep substring semantics.

Closes #156

## Test plan
- [x] Compared old vs new predicate across 7 URL shapes (apex, `www`, `cdn` subdomain, unrelated hosts, and the two spoofing cases above) — real MyInstants URLs all still match.
- [x] Confirmed the resolved header set is byte-identical to the previous hardcoded block.

> Note: this and #150 both touch the same region of `FFmpegAudioPlayer`, and #167 changes the `get_cf_session` call just above it — whichever lands later will need a rebase.

author: winding-lines
body:
Every figure on the performance page was re-measured on the same M4 today. Nothing is transcribed.

## The row that was wrong, not merely stale

`Parquet read, 4 cores / threads.parallel_for over row groups / 660M rows/s` described a measurement that could not have been taken: parquet.mojo had no threading of any kind until yesterday, and row-group parallelism landed the same day. 660M rows/s implies 1.5 ms for the 1M-row fixture, and nothing in the repository does that.

Measured, on `parquet.mojo` at `origin/main` (0.5.0), one benchmark at a time, AOT-built:

| workers | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p50 | 4.7 ms | 3.3 ms | 2.35 ms | 2.17 ms | 2.14 ms |
| p90 | 4.8 | 3.4 | 2.4 | 2.9 | 2.9 |

So the four-core row is **2.35 ms — 426M rows/s**, 2.0× the single-core figure. The whole ladder is on the page now: it bends at four, which is how many performance cores this M4 has, and past four the p50 buys about 8% while the p90 gets a quarter worse.

## Both pyarrow legs, labelled

`tools/bench_pyarrow.py` reports one thread (`set_cpu_count(1)`, `set_io_thread_count(1)`, `use_threads=False`) and threaded (pyarrow's own CPU count). On the 1M-row file those are 7.9 ms and 2.7 ms — **2.9× apart**, which is why a bare "pyarrow 9.0 ms" was not a comparison. Every row now names the leg and matches it to a thread count.

## Where the stack loses, on the page

- **Nested and mixed Parquet** — pyarrow is 1.4× ahead on one core, 1.6× ahead threaded. This is lost single-core, before threading enters into it; the stage profiler puts Dremel assembly at 30% of that read and decompression at another 25%.
- **Iceberg scans** — about 1.3× behind pyarrow at one thread and at four: 36.3 / 11.3 ms against 27.3 / 8.8 ms on the same four data files.
- **Iceberg nested columns** — 10.1 ms against PyIceberg's 4.0 ms.

## Method

p50 and p90 over real iterations, never a bare minimum and never a mean alone. Benchmarks **compiled and then run** — never `mojo run`, which JIT-executes a suite and inflated one of these figures 1.9×. Numbers taken per benchmark rather than from one pass over a suite. Every quoted run carries bench.mojo 0.4.0's `machine: steady` verdict; nothing else was building on the machine. The two repos not on that harness — iceberg (best-of-three warm) and objectstore (a single timed pass, so these are the median of three script runs) — say so in their own rows.

## Other rows that moved

Parquet write is parity now (31.7 ms both sides), not a 46.6-vs-31.6 loss — the writer stopped building and discarding a dictionary, and the old figure came from a JIT-executed suite. Footer read 56.6 ms (was 78) and write 2.6 ms (was 8). Iceberg append 192 ms. Avro decode 18.1M records/s against fastavro 1.70M. Roaring serialize/deserialize 22.2 / 60.3 ms. lz4 13.5–20.2 GB/s. S3 multipart 396 MB/s. The homepage's headline 232M rows/s becomes the measured 211M.

Two references were **dropped rather than restated**, because nothing in the repositories reproduces them: the threads tin's spawn+join figure is replaced by a round trip I timed (~11 µs warm, 15–20 µs cold), and objectstore's "19× / 11× faster than a fresh connection per request" by the coalesced-range contrast its bench does measure.

## Also here

`postgres.mojo` gained connection pooling, so its tin entry is no longer only a client: a bounded `ConnectionPool` behind `with pool.lease()` — acquire timeouts, `is_alive`-checked checkout, lifetime and idle recycling, `ROLLBACK` on return — and the invariant that makes it safe, that a connection whose statement or transaction outlives its lease is closed rather than handed to a second thread.

`npm ci && npm run build` passes; the rendered page was read, not just the data file.

author: sidbai
body:
Takes the directory from 16 to **25 clubs**.

## WPL is not the RCL
The [WPL directory](https://system.gotsport.com/org_event/events/20169/clubs) is **89 clubs across Washington, Idaho and Oregon**, spanning elite N1 down to recreational — where RCL full membership is a bounded 16. So this is a **chosen subset**: the Puget Sound clubs families actually pick between, not the membership.

## Added
| Club | City |
|---|---|
| Eagleclaw FC | Tukwila |
| Emerald City FC | Seattle |
| Everett Youth Soccer Club | Everett |
| FC Edmonds | Edmonds |
| Lake Washington Premier FC | Kirkland |
| Mukilteo Youth Soccer Club | Mukilteo |
| Northlake Soccer Club | Kenmore |
| Pilchuck Soccer Alliance | Marysville |
| Seattle Celtic | Seattle |

All nine URLs verified 200.

## The two restored
**Emerald City FC** and **Seattle Celtic** were dropped when you narrowed to ECNL/RCL; both are WPL clubs, so under this criterion they belong. Critically they also had to come **out of `RETIRED_SLUGS`** — otherwise the next seed run would have deleted them again, silently undoing this.

## Three deliberate exclusions, with reasons recorded in the script
- **Sno-King Youth Club** — it runs the FC Edmonds programme, so listing both double-counts one organisation.
- **Terrace Brier SC** — describes itself as recreational; the directory's stated scope is clubs families choose between.
- **Normandy Park FC** — could not be verified at all.

The reasons live in the seed script so a later pass doesn't helpfully re-add them.

## Verification caught one more trap
The first "Everett Youth Soccer Club" search results were for a club in **Massachusetts**. Seattle Celtic's city came off its own contact block (2633 Eastlake Ave E, Seattle) rather than a directory.

## Verified
Seeded locally then to production: **9 added, 0 updated, 0 removed** both times. All nine render on `/clubs`; search finds them by city (`kenmore`) and name (`celtic`); tab count reads 25. Existing logos untouched — prod is **25 clubs, 6 with logos**.

`typecheck` / `lint` clean. No migration.

## Still outstanding
19 of 25 clubs have no logo. That needs a fetch-and-eyeball pass — the naive scrape once picked a car dealership's badge off a sponsor strip.

## Changes (issue #72 MVP)

### Configurable WAL busy timeout
- New `db.busyTimeout` config option (default 5000ms)
- Env: `SYNAPTOMIND_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT`
- Replaces hardcoded 15s timeout — prevents SQLITE_BUSY under concurrent writes

### Disable embedder
- New `embedder.enabled` config option (default true)
- CLI flag `--no-embedder`
- Env: `SYNAPTOMIND_EMBEDDER_ENABLED=false`
- When disabled: embedder process skipped, search falls back to BM25

### Rate limit via config
- New `rateLimit.max` and `rateLimit.windowMs` config options
- Env: `SYNAPTOMIND_RATE_LIMIT=0` to disable, or set custom limit
- Previously hardcoded at 200/60s with no override

### Bulk import endpoint
- `POST /api/thoughts/bulk` — create up to 10,000 thoughts in one request
- Single DB transaction for atomicity
- Body size limit raised to 5MB
- Returns `{ created, errors, thoughts, error_details }`

### Files changed

body:
## 何を足したか

**1. `tools/cheap-code.mjs`** — `--provider deepseek|glm` で Claude Code 本体(`claude -p`)を安い/定額レーンで起動する実行者。Z.ai GLM Coding Plan を契約できたので、監督コストを下げる経路を実装した。

- **env は spawn する子プロセスだけに注入**。グローバルに書くと監督セッションが気づかず安いモデルに切り替わるため（`glm-code.mjs` の作法を踏襲）
- キーは標準出力・台帳に一切出さない（末尾4桁すら出さない。`--dry-run` は `keyPresent: true/false` のみ）
- executor 台帳に記録するので委譲率の計測に載る
- `--prompt-file` 対応（argv 直渡しはシェルがバッククォートをコマンド置換として実行する事故があるため）

**2. `tools/pending-actions-notice.mjs`** — kim にしかできない作業（購入・OAuth初回同意）を `~/.claude/pending-user-actions.md` に積み、**期日が来たら SessionStart で再提示**する hook。「明日やってください」と書いて忘れられるのを構造的に塞ぐ。

## 実測（検証は Claude 側で実施）

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `cheap-code.test.mjs` | 6 pass / 0 fail |
| `pending-actions-notice.test.mjs` | 4 pass / 0 fail |
| DeepSeek で `claude -p` | 正答・exit 0・95秒・台帳記録あり |
| GLM で `claude -p` | 正答・exit 0・108秒・台帳記録あり |
| 親 `process.env` の汚染 | なし |

## 踏んだ罠と対策

- **カタログ外のモデル名だと窓を 200k と仮定され早期に auto-compact される** → 子 env に `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1000000` を明示（DeepSeek v4系: context 1M/出力384K、GLM-5.3: context 1M/出力128K）。警告が消えることで確認できる
- **別名モデルは世代が張り替わる** → DeepSeek の既定を `deepseek-chat` から実モデル名 `deepseek-v4-flash` へ
- **z.ai の実応答は `glm-5.3`**（`glm-5.2` 指定でも 5.3 が返る）→ `glm-code.mjs` / `llm-ask.mjs` / `llm-fallback.mjs` / `cheap-code.mjs` の既定を一括更新。`codex-do.test.mjs` の `z-ai/glm-5.2:free` は **OpenRouter の別名前空間なので据え置き**
- **hook で `process.exit()` を呼ぶと Windows で libuv assertion を踏み、exit≠0 でホストが出力を丸ごと捨てる** → 自然終了させ、全体を try/catch で囲む

## スコープ

実装は Codex へ委譲、検証は Claude（§1.18）。共有作業ツリーに他セッションの未コミット差分が多数あったため、**専用 worktree を `origin/main` から切って本セッションの7ファイルだけ**を載せている。

author: seunlanlege
body:
Follow-up to #1199. Removes the local relayer setters that let a single key re-route governance or cross-chain deliveries without a governance message, gives the gateway proxy a version that says which implementation it has migrated to, and collapses gateway governance into one action. The contracts are deployed to mainnet from this branch; addresses, the governance batch, and what is still pending are at the bottom.

## Contracts

- **HostManager**: the `admin` is the governance relayer. There is no separate relayer slot and no local setter. A new `SetAdmin` action (variant `2`, body `abi.encode(address)`) rotates it through governance, delivered by the outgoing admin like every other message; zero is refused in the constructor and in `SetAdmin`, since a manager with no admin could never be reached again. `setIsmpHost` is now `init`: admin-only, one-shot, and unnecessary when the host is passed to the constructor. `onAccept` checks caller and relayer through one `restrict(who, expected)` modifier and both failures revert with `UnauthorizedAction`; the separate `UnauthorizedRelayer` error is gone. `pallet-ismp-host-executive` gains `set_host_manager_admin`; `ismp-abi` gains `encode_set_admin`; `HostManager.json` is regenerated.
- **IntentGatewayV2, relayer and version**: `setRelayer` moved to `ExtrinsicIntents` and is host-only, so `_owner` can no longer rotate the relayer. `initialize` takes the relayer and lands at `VERSION = 2` under `reinitializer`, so a fresh proxy comes out armed and at the version of the code it runs; it is refused on any proxy already at a version, so an upgrade that installs this code on a version-1 proxy without migration calldata leaves nobody able to initialize it. `migrate(address)`, host-only under the same `reinitializer(VERSION)`, arms a proxy deployed before this implementation and takes it from 1 to 2. `version()` and `relayer()` are exposed. An unset relayer gates nothing, so a pre-gate proxy can accept the migration that arms it; a rotation never touches the version.
- **IntentGatewayV2, `Execute`**: `RequestKind.Execute` (discriminator 5, the old `UpgradeContract` slot) delegatecalls the proxy's current implementation with the rest of the body as calldata, the host still `msg.sender`, so every host-only function is reachable through one governance action. `upgradeToAndCall` is a host-only function wrapping `ERC1967Utils.upgradeToAndCall`; an upgrade is `Execute` carrying it, a relayer rotation is `Execute` carrying `setRelayer` with no implementation change. Reverts inside bubble out so the host records the message undelivered. The old `(address, bytes)` body selects no function on this implementation and reverts, and the live implementation still reads it as `UpgradeContract`, so the pallet keeps `upgrade_gateway` for the one upgrade that installs this code per chain and gains `execute_on_gateway(state_machine, data)` for everything after, weighed as `upgrade_gateway`.
- **Bytecode**: the reinitializer did not fit under EIP-170, and every gateway getter and event has an off-chain consumer, so the room came from deduplicating internal code with no behaviour change: one `_sendValue` for native payouts, `_splitSurplus` shared by both fills, `_withdrawalBody` and `_postToSource` for the escrow messages, and `placeOrder` reading the fee token once and hashing the order once. Runtime size is 24,367 bytes.
- **HyperFungibleToken**: the relayer gate is lifted out of the base token. `HyperFungibleToken` no longer has `_relayer`, `setRelayer`, `relayer()` or the `_checkRelayer` hook; `onAccept` and `onPostRequestTimeout` are `public virtual`. `BridgeToken` owns the gate and wraps both callbacks, failing closed as before. Third-party tokens get nothing to configure and no extra storage slot.
- **Deploy scripts**: `DeployIsmp.s.sol` constructs the host first and binds the manager at construction with `GOVERNANCE_RELAYER` as admin; `DeployHostManager.s.sol` does the same for a replacement manager; `DeployBridgeToken.s.sol` reads the same variable. `DeployIntentGateway.s.sol` always deploys the implementation and the solver account, deploys the proxy only where `INTENT_GATEWAY_V2` is absent from the chain's config, reads `GATEWAY_RELAYER` for the init data, and records `INTENT_GATEWAY_V2_IMPL`.
- **ABIs and docs**: the gateway ABI is regenerated in `sdk`, `simplex` and the indexer. The mainnet contract-addresses page carries the new addresses below, an `IntentGatewayV2 (Implementation)` row, and the BridgeToken on BSC and Polygon.

## Tests

Foundry suites for the manager, the gateway and the tokens (417 passing, mainnet-fork suites included). The live Ethereum proxy is migrated on a fork with state compared before and after, then rotated through `Execute`; `migrate` and the `initialize` guard are exercised on a proxy written back to version 1; the legacy upgrade body is shown to revert on the new implementation. A throwaway fork test also delivered the exact body the pallet builds for the batch below through the real host and handler to the live proxy: `Upgraded` to the deployed implementation, `migrate` armed the relayer, version 2, state intact, a stranger's follow-up refused and the relayer's accepted. Rust integration tests deliver the pallet's `SetAdmin` encoding to the compiled contract; pallet tests pin the recipient and body of `set_host_manager_admin`, the `Execute` encoding and the new extrinsic.

## Deployed 2026-09-05, salt `nexus-mainnet-1000000`

| Contract | Address | Chains |
|---|---|---|
| HostManager | `0xc09A8229e2C18dEad6A2795154d7D8C7F1AC5Dfa` | all nine |
| IntentGatewayV2 implementation | `0x9d82B05156d0da273D66C5cCbDccef2b00EE06A7` | all nine |
| SolverAccount | `0x7cb55539d1144F62422099c3FA3405092022c88C` | all nine |
| BridgeToken | `0x5b0c50fDd52ECC0d4c682c441eaBaD41FfDEABBB` | BSC, Polygon |

All nine: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, BSC, Gnosis, Soneium, Polygon, Polkadot Hub. The gateway proxy stays at `0xAe041F7B0CB581876832830baeB6a2Aa2a3C9716`. The governance relayer on the managers and the token is `0xD15007f5fF5c8c5cCc77339A03a3EA60d1Ece854`. Every contract is explorer-verified on every chain, the Polkadot Hub HostManager last once Blockscout had indexed the deployment's internal calls. `config.mainnet.toml` records all of the above.

## Governance batch

One `utility.batchAll` of 21 calls, encoded against nexus runtime 8500 (the version on-chain, which includes the host-executive addressing fix from #1199), call hash `0x3fdd8adc75fa7235a93c07126b9096aead4fcd41d0bbf3be83119e174e17b379`, 1067 bytes:

1. Per chain, `hostExecutive.updateHostParams(EVM-n, { hostManager: 0xc09A… })`: delivered through the current manager `0x5918…`, which installs the new one.
2. Per chain, `intentsCoprocessor.upgradeGateway(EVM-n, 0x9d82…, migrate(0xD150…))`, init data `0xce5494bb000000000000000000000000d15007f5ff5c8c5ccc77339a03a3ea60d1ece854`. The live proxies have no relayer gate yet, so any relayer can carry this first message; everything after must come from `0xD150…`.
3. `hyperFungibleToken.registerToken` for BRIDGE (`keccak256("BRIDGE")`, native, BSC and Polygon at `0x5b0c…` with 18 decimals). Nexus has no HFT registration today, so this is a register rather than an update; if one lands first, `batchAll` fails as a whole.
4. `bandwidth.setAllowlist` for the token on BSC and Polygon.

## Still pending

- The runtime side of `Execute` (`execute_on_gateway`) needs a runtime release before governance can use it; the batch above uses only extrinsics that exist on-chain.
- `execute_on_gateway` reuses the `upgrade_gateway` weight rather than its own benchmark.
- The indexer's mainnet config still lists the previous SolverAccount on four chains; it is deployed separately from the npm packages.

## Releases

- `@hyperbridge/core` 2.3.4.
- `@hyperbridge/sdk` 2.8.11: every mainnet chain config points `SolverAccount` at the new `0x7cb5…`. Soneium has no `SolverAccount` or gateway entry in `chain.ts` at all, be

author: roozbehshafiee
body:
## Why

Reader half of Ubiquex/ubx-provider-dynamic#66, which renames `MinBinaryVersion` to `GeneratedByBinaryVersion`. The old name promised a floor it never computed: the field records which binary cut the snapshot, not the lowest one that can serve it.

## What

Resolution logic is unchanged. This prefers the new key and falls back to the pre-rename one, so an already-published snapshot and a freshly cut one resolve identically.

The fallback is load-bearing rather than defensive. Confirmed directly against all eight published `ubx-schema-<provider>` manifests: every one carries `min_binary_version` and nothing else. Without the fallback each would resolve as absent and silently drop to the `schema_format` bootstrap table, turning cloudflare's real 1.0.10 into 1.0.0, while logging a "published before UBI-194" line that is untrue of them.

## Merge order

This should merge before any snapshot is re-cut with the renamed binary. Once #66 lands, newly-cut snapshots carry both keys, so this reader works either way. Merging this first is the safe order.

## Verification

- Two new tests: legacy-only resolves with no fallback log line, and the new name wins when both keys are present
- Whole repo `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` clean, since this is shared provider-resolution code

Not self-merged.

author: lambda2
body:
Found while reconciling the WCVP synonymy: a fact said `merged_from_synonym` without saying **which** synonym. The same gap applies to every source.

### The gap
```json
{ "attribute_name": "average_height_cm", "source": "powo", "source_record_id": null }
```

The trail stopped at the database name. Anyone investigating a disagreement had to go and find the taxon by name at the other end — exactly the manual step the facts endpoint exists to remove.

### The payload already carried it
`source_powo: 'urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:857916-1'` names both the source **and** its identifier there. The ingester parsed the key for the slug and discarded the value. It now keeps both.

```json
{ "attribute_name": "average_height_cm", "source": "powo",
  "source_record_id": "urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:857916-1" }
```

### Details worth knowing
- **Rejected claims get it too**, which is where it matters most: a value refused as implausible is precisely one you want to trace back to the record that published it.
- When a payload carries several `source_*` keys, the identifier recorded is the one belonging to the source that **won** the naming — not whichever came first.
- Left null when the source is passed explicitly: an accepted community correction is not a record at some external database, and pretending otherwise would be worse than a blank.

### Verification
- 4 new specs covering each case above
- 958 examples / 0 failures, RuboCop 0, Brakeman 0

author: mobile-kevin
body:
## Why

A new user cannot get from `npm init` to a green test. Two problems, both on the Installation page:

**1. There are no prerequisites anywhere in Getting Started.** Xcode, a booted simulator, `ANDROID_HOME`, `adb`, a running emulator — none of them are mentioned. On a clean machine `npx mobilewright test` fails with nothing to explain why. `mobilewright doctor` already checks exactly this list, but it lives at the bottom of `guides/troubleshooting.md`, which a new user only reaches *after* the first failed run.

The page is otherwise modelled on Playwright's `/docs/intro`, which ends with a **System requirements** section. That omission costs us more than it would cost Playwright: `npx playwright install` provisions the browsers, so their happy path really does work on a clean machine. We can't provision a simulator or the Android SDK, so the requirements we don't list are exactly the ones that break the first run.

**2. The scaffold walkthrough doesn't match what the scaffold produces.** Checked against `create-mobilewright@1.0.10`:

| Page says | `npm init mobilewright@latest` actually does |
|---|---|
| non-interactive; "if either file already exists, it will be skipped" | prompts for language, test directory, and bundle ID — and runs `npm install` for you |
| `tests/example.test.ts` | `tests/example.spec.ts` |
| config with `platform`, `deviceName`, `installApps`, `timeout` | config with `testDir`, `bundleId`, `reporter` — none of the other four |
| `npm install mobilewright @mobilewright/test` first | redundant; the scaffold writes `package.json` and installs |

The "skipped" behaviour described is `mobilewright init` (the in-repo templates), not `create-mobilewright`. So someone following along sees different files than the page shows, and the config example points at `./builds/myapp.ipa`, a build they don't have.

## What changed

- **New `Requirements` section** before install. Version floors match what `doctor` enforces (`commands/doctor.ts`): Node >= 18, macOS >= 13, JDK >= 11, Windows 11 (build >= 22000). Notes that Linux does Android via the existing Docker image, and that mobilecli ships bundled so nobody installs it separately.
- **`Check your setup`** — pulls the `npx mobilewright doctor` block up from Troubleshooting, with a link back for the `--json` half.
- **Corrected `Installing Mobilewright` and `Directory layout`** to match `create-mobilewright@1.0.10`, plus the direct-install path for an existing `package.json`.
- **New `Choosing a device and installing your app`** section so `platform` / `deviceName` / `installApps` / `timeout` stay documented, now labelled as options you add rather than as the scaffold's output.
- **New `What's next`** block.
- **`writing-tests.md`** — the page walks you through writing a test and never says how to run it. Added a short section that does.

## Notes

- Docs-only; no code touched.
- Every claim was verified against `packages/mobilewright/src/{config,cli}.ts`, `commands/doctor.ts`, and `mobile-next/create-mobilewright@1.0.10`. All relative links follow the file-relative convention used in `cloud-providers/` and resolve to existing files.

## Not fixed here, still open

- **No sample app.** The scaffold asserts on the text `Welcome` against `com.example.myapp`. Playwright scaffolds against a public demo site; our equivalent would be a downloadable demo `.app`/`.apk`, or defaulting to a preinstalled system app. That needs a product call and an artifact, not a docs edit — so this PR just warns the reader that the assertion won't match their app.
- **No expected console output** for the first run. `## Running tests` still shows only a screenshot, so a reader can't tell success from silence. I didn't want to invent terminal output.
- Separately: `create-mobilewright` pins `mobilewright@0.0.51` in `createPackageJson`, while latest is `0.0.55`. Different repo, not a docs issue, but worth a look.

Four desktop/mobile/theme checks pass without axe violations or overflow. Acquisition, extraction and replacement-firmware compatibility were not execution-tested.

author: jayhesselberth
body:
Two papers have been showing their **publisher where the journal should be**:

| Paper | Was showing | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| Nanopore sequencing of intact aminoacylated tRNAs | *Springer Science and Business Media LLC* | *Nat. Commun.* |
| Systematic identification … 2A peptide-bond-skipping sequences | *Elsevier BV* | *Cell Rep.* |

The cause is in `publications.bib`: both entries carry the journal under **`journaltitle`**, which is BibLaTeX. The `academic` importer only reads `journal`, and falls back to `publisher` when it is missing:

```python
elif "journal" in entry:
    publication = "*" + clean_bibtex_str(entry["journal"]) + "*"
elif "publisher" in entry:
    publication = "*" + clean_bibtex_str(entry["publisher"]) + "*"
```

So the fallback is what has been on the site. Renaming the field fixes both.

### Also, four entries used `issue`

The importer doesn't read that either, so the issue number never reached the page. They now use `number`, like the rest of the file — White2025-bm, Rao2025-mb, Kolakada2025-wv and Nicholas2025-hi.

Two of those had further problems, checked against Crossref:

- **Kolakada2025-wv** had the article number in `issue` (100882), duplicating `pages`, and no volume at all. It is Cell Genomics **5(7), 100882**.
- **White2025-bm** was missing its article number: Nat Commun **16(1), 7781**.

### On the page bundles

The four pages are edited rather than reimported. `academic import --overwrite` drops `featured: true` and moves the DOI back to the deprecated top level, both of which are maintained by hand — so only the affected lines are touched, plus the regenerated `cite.bib` files.

### Verified

`pixi run build` clean, `normalize_authors.py --check` clean, and the publications list now reads *Nat. Commun.* and *Cell Rep.*

Volume and issue still won't display until #21 lands, since the flat string carries only the journal name. Once it does, these read *Nat. Commun.*, 16(1), 7781 — the corrected `cite.bib` is where that script reads them from.

author: fonderiejs
body:
## Billing capability audit — Phase 3a: refund/chargeback clawback (financial integrity)

Closes the **§C value-leak**: today a buyer can purchase credit-pack credits, spend them, then refund the card (or file a chargeback) and keep the goods — billing never reverses the credits. This PR makes a refund/chargeback claw them back.

### What changed
- **Provider normalization** — `StripeProvider.constructEvent` now normalizes `charge.refunded` and `charge.dispute.created` / `.closed` into a new `IBillingEvent.reversal` (`INormalizedReversal`). Refunds are read **newest-first** (Stripe list order), so each partial refund is a distinct clawback keyed on its own id.
- **`reverseWallet`** — writes a negative `type:'refund'` ledger row and is **deliberately floor-free**: a clawback must be able to drive the balance negative when the credits were already spent (a negative balance is "credits owed back"; the next grant/purchase nets against it).
- **Refund → purchase join** by `provider_tx_id` (the PaymentIntent) — the refund event carries no wallet metadata. Migration `007` indexes it. New helpers: `findPurchaseByProviderTxId`, `sumReversedCreditsByProviderTxId`, `findLedgerAmountByKey`.
- **Cap** — cumulative reversal is capped at the credits granted, **enforced inside the transaction under a per-PaymentIntent advisory lock**, so no mix of partial refunds + a chargeback (even concurrent) can over-reverse. Credits are prorated to the refunded amount; a partial amount with no proration basis is refused rather than over-clawed.
- **Idempotent** on the refund/dispute id; a **won dispute** restores exactly what its chargeback clawed. Emits `payment.refunded` + `wallet.debited` + the (previously reserved) `billing.refund-processed` notice — only on a real, non-replayed reversal.
- **`SubscriptionStatus`** widened to the full provider vocabulary (`+incomplete_expired`, `+unpaid`) — the DB column is already free-form text, so this only makes the type honest; the new states are inactive by default.

### Verification
- **207 unit tests** (buy→spend→refund negative balance, partial-refund proration, duplicate no-op, two distinct partials via the real normalizer, chargeback, dispute-won restore, dispute-lost no-op, cap, zero/no-basis guards, no-matching-purchase/no-PI ack, events+notice + none-on-replay, `unpaid`-inactive).
- **Real-Postgres integration leg**: negative-balance clawback + idempotent replay + **concurrent dispute+refund cap** (proves the advisory-lock serialization).
- **Adversarially reviewed** (5-lens): the review caught a confirmed *newest-vs-oldest-refund* bug (would have silently dropped every partial refund after the first, reopening the leak) and a cap-race under concurrent refund+dispute — both fixed, then a second pass re-verified all three findings resolved with no new defects.

### Scope
Phase 3a = the money-movement clawback (split out of the notification-only normalization so the security-critical path got a focused review). **Deferred to Phase 3b**: `invoice.paid`/`invoice.payment_failed` and `checkout.session.async_payment_failed`/`payment_intent.payment_failed` (dunning/receipt notices, no money movement).

Changeset: `@fonderie/billing` minor. Additive/opt-in — the new event slot and helpers don't affect existing flows. Full local gate run green (`lint:ci`, full `typecheck`, `docs:signatures`/`docs:brain`, all check scripts, tests).

author: ulookup
body:
Closes #71.

## Scope

Adds the first Janus authoring mutation tools on top of the shared v0.7 Reflection + CommandBus capability.

### Tools

- `scene.create_entity`
- `scene.delete_entity`
- `scene.rename_entity`
- `scene.add_component`
- `scene.remove_component`
- `scene.set_component_property`
- `scene.save`

### Mutation path

```text
MCP tool
  -> validate stable UUID / reflected names / typed JSON
  -> existing Engine Scene Command
  -> shared CommandBus::Execute
  -> structured MCP tool result
```

No MCP handler writes ECS/component state directly and no EditorActions dependency is introduced.

### Reflection JSON decoder

Adds strict JSON -> PropertyValue conversion for:

- Bool
- bounded Int32
- finite Float32
- String
- strict Vector2 object
- strict Color object
- nullable AssetReference UUID

Asset type constraints remain enforced by SceneReflection + AssetRegistry.

### Tool result semantics

- invalid tool arguments -> JSON-RPC Invalid params routing error
- valid tool execution failure -> MCP tool result with `isError:true`
- output schemas describe both success and execution-error structuredContent
- successful mutations optionally invoke host dirty callback
- host read-only callback guards all writes/save
- save uses only injected host save callback

### Shared history proof

Tests verify Agent mutations enter the same CommandBus and Human/shared Undo restores:

- created entities
- rename/delete
- add/remove components
- Transform property edits
- Camera.primary cross-entity side effects

## Scope boundary

No Editor process hosting, stdio worker/main-thread dispatcher, permission policy, or UI integration is added here. Those remain #72.

SNS 返信レーンの初回 run で、Bluesky への返信案が **いろママの声** で 2 案生成された。

`@omochairo.bsky.social` の実態を `app.bsky.actor.getProfile` で見たところ:

author: pr0d1r2
body:
Loop-native disclaimer heal (V443/T581): this repository is tended by an autonomous loop, and its README.md did not say so. A machine-authored commit is indistinguishable from a human one, so the fact has to be declared rather than inferred — a contributor opening a PR expecting a human reviewer cannot discover it from the artefact.

Two files, two owners. The README.md block is marker-delimited and one line long: it points at the document and is refreshed from a single template across the fleet, so a wording change is one heal rather than one hand-edit per repo. `docs/LLM-DISCLAIMER.md` is planted once and is then YOURS — the loop never rewrites it — because the paragraph worth reading is the one about THIS repository, and no fleet template can write that.

Edit either freely. Keep the README.md markers if you want that line kept current; remove them and the loop leaves your own wording alone.

body:
Plans the move of the PROD frontend onto the association's WordPress site at
**weteraniszermierki.pl**. CERT and the admin UI stay on GitHub Pages.

Docs only — **no code written, nothing deployed.**

## What this plans

The subject is the **mechanism**, not the calendar: a repeatable way to publish a PROD
surface as a full-screen WordPress menu item. Three surfaces queue behind it.

| Surface | Menu placement | Waiting on |
|---|---|---|
| Calendar (step 1) | Bottom of **LINKI** — „Znajdź zawody / Competition finder" | Nothing. Additive, replaces no page. |
| Ranking (step 2) | Not decided | An **SPWS Board decision**, which may also settle the placement |
| Points calculator (step 2) | Its own item, not decided | The DirectAdmin/FTP login |

## Decisions recorded

- Custom element in a normal WordPress page, shadow DOM (as ADR-007 anticipated in M8).
- Bundle served from the **existing GitHub Pages address** at a stable name, so WordPress is
  touched once and every later release updates the live page with no upload.
- New `view` / `chrome` attributes on `App.svelte`; `<spws-calendar>` becomes a wrapper over the
  real loader instead of the mock stub it is today.
- `asset-base` attribute for the organizer logos, which are bare relative filenames and 404 off-root.
- Embed ignores `?admin=1`; administration stays on Pages.
- CT/PD switch left untouched in code — it is derived from having all four credentials, so it is
  simply absent under PROD-only ones.
- The calendar lands on a **new** page. `/kalendarz-2/` and `/klasyfikacja/` are not touched.

## Measured, not assumed

- **XML-RPC authenticates as admin; REST cannot** — LiteSpeed strips the `Authorization` header.
  Proven rather than inferred: a deliberately wrong password returns the byte-identical error as
  the correct one.
- **Single-site install**, so `unfiltered_html` is expected to hold — step 1 confirms it with a
  draft page rather than assuming.
- **The anon key adds no new exposure**: it already ships in the public GitHub Pages bundle, and
  its blast radius comes from database grants, not from where it is printed.
- The missing registration rate limit (**ADR-079 §4 defence (d)**) is accepted and deferred to
  separate work, not silently inherited.

## Files

- `doc/plans/prod-deployment-wordpress-2026-09-05.html` — the approved plan

nitjsefnie
body:
## Summary

Adds an Overflow-issued API token so a member can register a repository over the API instead of driving the nineteen-field web form. The token is generated from a panel on the register-a-repository page, shown once, stored only as a hash, and limited to one active token per account that regenerating replaces.

## Related Issues and Pull Requests

Fixes #72

## Changes

- `src/lib/security/api-token.ts` — mints a token as `ovf_` plus 32 CSPRNG bytes in base64url, hashes it with SHA-256 over the whole prefixed string, and reads a bearer credential off a request. `hashApiToken` returns null for anything malformed, so a garbage credential costs no database round trip.
- `db/migrations/011_api_tokens.sql` — `api_tokens`, holding only the hash. `user_id` is unique, which is what makes one-active-token-per-account a property of the schema rather than of the code that writes it; `token_hash` is unique and constrained to 32 bytes.
- `src/lib/tokens/postgres-store.ts` — issues a token as a single-statement upsert on that unique constraint, so regeneration and revocation are one atomic step rather than a delete-then-insert with a window where the account has two tokens or none. Resolves an account from a hash without returning any token material.
- `src/app/api/tokens/route.ts` — `POST /api/tokens`, cookie session only. Its response body is the one place in the product where a plaintext token appears.
- `src/app/api/repositories/route.ts` — accepts the token as a second credential beside the session cookie. A token failure is never rescued by the cookie session, authentication precedes payload validation on both paths, and registration uses the account's stored GitHub OAuth token exactly as the form does.
- `src/components/api-token-panel.tsx` and `src/app/repositories/new/page.tsx` — the panel that generates and regenerates the token and displays it once. It is placed on the register page rather than the header navigation because #40 reports the navigation already wrapping at tablet widths.
- `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the endpoint, the credential, the permissions, a runnable example, and the error responses.
- `tests/` — five suites plus a shared console guard, covering the primitives, the schema constraints, both routes and the panel.

## Testing

Full gate against `0fc34d7`, the final head, bare and in order — `pnpm db:migrate && pnpm test --run && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`:

- 47 test files, 576 tests, **zero skipped, zero failed**. The zero-skip count matters here: a container-runtime failure in this project surfaces as skips beside a nonzero exit, so a run reporting skips is a failed run rather than a partial pass.
- Lint and typecheck clean; build compiled.
- The build emits three `node:crypto` Edge Runtime warnings. These are pre-existing: `main` emits the same three with the identical message, verified by building `main` separately. This branch introduces none.

Every task was implemented test-first and then attacked with mutants planted in the real modules. Findings that came out of that rather than from reading: a `console.log` of a plaintext token passed both the suite and lint, since the project has no `no-console` rule; a hardcoded account id satisfied every identity assertion in two separate suites; and three failure branches in `register.ts` could have leaked a credential-bearing error with no test noticing. All are now covered.

## Bugs Discovered

- #77 The settlement override store suite intermittently fails its container setup with ECONNRESET

The branch was rebased onto `main` twice while finishing, the second time onto four commits that reclassify GitHub registration failures on the exact route this touches. Both rebases were re-verified from scratch rather than trusting the earlier green, which is what caught two things a clean textual merge did not: a privacy assertion left expecting a renamed error message, and five of `main`'s own new tests failing `typecheck` because they omit the route dependency this branch made required. Both are fixed; the required-member design is unchanged, since it is what surfaced them at compile time rather than in production.

## Follow-ups / Known Limitations

- A token authenticates repository registration and nothing else. The mechanism is general, so widening it to other routes later is a policy change rather than a redesign.
- `src/lib/github/graphql.ts` and `src/lib/github/client.ts` independently construct and re-match the same `GitHub API request failed with status N.` string, so neither file owns it and editing one silently breaks the other's catch. Untouched here; nothing misbehaves today.
- The store's `findUserByGitHubUserId` avoids reading the stored OAuth ciphertext, and a test proves it is never *decrypted*, but bare selection of the column is still unpinned — closing that needs a query-level assertion on the emitted SQL.
- `src/auth.ts` runs a near-duplicate of the account lookup the token store performs. Deliberately not extracted: hoisting it would couple the NextAuth layer to the repository store, and both rely on the schema's unique index rather than on each other.

## Footer

author: pntgoswami18
body:
Version bump for the 0.5.5 release. Merging this, then pushing tag `v0.5.5`, triggers `build.yml`, which builds every platform and creates the GitHub release from the artifacts.

## What 0.5.5 ships

**Manifest writes no longer clobber `chromium-args`** (user-facing). Toggling *Native window frame* or *Allow Audio Passthrough* rewrote `chromium-args` to a hardcoded literal, dropping the `--no-sandbox` the shipped manifest has carried since 2024. On a packaged Linux build, turning on audio passthrough removed it.

**Manifest path resolution.** The startup reconcile opened the relative path `'package.json'`, which resolves against `process.cwd()` — the app directory only by coincidence. It now walks up from `process.mainModule.filename` to the manifest whose name and version match the loaded one, and skips the write entirely in a source checkout, where the manifest is a tracked file.

**The build can now fail.** The `nwjs` gulp task caught its own errors and resolved, so a packaging failure left `gulp build` green and `gulp dist` went on to package whatever tree was there. It now rethrows, and a pre-package check asserts every `/node_modules/...` script tag in `index.html` resolves against the file list.

## Note on scope

This is not a re-publish of corrupt artifacts. I verified the published `v0.5.4` `osx-arm64` zip and its central directory lists 24,827 `node_modules/` entries including jQuery and Backbone — the released builds were fine. The missing-`node_modules` failure was confined to a stale local `build/` directory. The build-side changes remove the possibility of that shipping, rather than correcting something that shipped.

## Why the version bump is in the repo

`gulpfile.js` compares `pkJson.version` against the git-describe semver and names the NSIS installer differently when they disagree, so `package.json` has to move with the tag.

## What

`docs/reference/benchmarks/frame_budget_20260905.md` §5 F3 cited
`src/saccade/perception/eval/evaluator.py:425` as the ingest expression. That line
cannot execute under the profiled command. This PR repoints it at the live site and
records the correction inline.

## Why that line is dead for this preset

- `evaluator.py:425` is inside `if getattr(cfg, "workbench", False) and wb is not None:` (`evaluator.py:414`).
- `workbench` defaults to `False` (`config.py:1280`), and the preset does not set it.
- `scripts/eval/mot17.py:125` rejects `--workbench` together with `--private-continuation`, and
  `configs/presets/mamba_whole_graph_m.yaml` sets `private_continuation_enabled: true`.

The documented headline command is
`scripts/eval/mot17.py --preset mamba_whole_graph_m --detector SDP --double-buffer`,
so the workbench branch is unreachable in the profiled run.

## The live site

`src/saccade/perception/eval/stages.py:1843`, inside `_run_detect` (`stages.py:1809`),
reached via `_launch_double_buffer_detect`. The `nv12_direct_from_hwc` alternative is
also inactive here: `pool.use_nv12` is set only by `SACCADE_NV12_BUFFER=1`
(`evaluator.py:419`), which the run does not set.

## What does not change

The expression text is byte-identical at both sites, so no measurement, no bit-exactness
check and no §6 probe result is affected. Only the citation was wrong. Nothing is
promoted to `evidence_ledger` or `report_data`; the document's scope statement is
untouched.

author: wmetcalf
body:
Found by taking the defect codex found in the FC launcher (#154) and looking for the same shape in the sibling module. It was identical:

```python
still = []
for leftover in stranded:      # the LIVE ledger
    ...
stranded[:] = still            # erases anything appended while we swept
```

Three failure paths append to this ledger, and each records something that must not be forgotten:

| appender | what it records |
|---|---|
| `checkpoint()` | a partial checkpoint whose cleanup failed |
| `boot_base()` | a base whose teardown could **not be confirmed** |
| `restore_in()` | a restore workdir, likewise unconfirmed |

The last two are the dangerous ones — they name a directory a **live sandbox may still be holding open**. Losing the entry loses the only record anything has of it, and nothing sweeps it afterwards.

## The fix

Take the batch under a lock, **prepend** what is still stuck so entries added during the sweep survive, and take the lock in all three appenders.

## Deterministic, not raced

The erase happens at the *end* of the sweep, so an append injected from inside the sweep's own `rmtree` lands exactly in the window the slice assignment closes over. No threads, no timing, no flakiness — restoring `stranded[:] = still` fails it every time.

That is worth contrasting with the two ledger locks on #154, which I shipped explicitly labelled as reasoned-but-unverified because their windows are microseconds wide and no single-threaded test can force them. This one is genuinely testable, so it is genuinely tested.

## I swept for the shape elsewhere

The only other snapshot-then-clear on shared state is `_retry_undead_bases`, which already takes its batch atomically under `_build_lock` and re-appends under it — the correct pattern. Left alone.

body:
## Cognitus Professional + Frenzy V35

This is a consolidation and product-direction release rather than another decorative feature layer.

### Professional Cognitus contract
- Introduces one restrained operational design system across authenticated Cognitus and Promotional/Feature Access surfaces.
- Replaces oversized headings, excessive radii, heavy shadows, dramatic hover effects, and inconsistent surface styling with a calmer institutional UI.
- Standardizes buttons, forms, tables, cards, navigation, record surfaces, locked states, and mobile presentation.
- Applies a consistent evidence-oriented context strip on restricted analysis tools.
- Renames several consumer/game-like feature labels into clearer operational terminology, including Relationship Analysis, Historical Record Analysis, Advanced Record Search, Network Analysis, Change Analysis, Record Signal Analysis, and Cross-Organization Analysis.
- Reframes the user-facing Promotional Access hub as Feature Access.

### Navigation consolidation
- Removes the dedicated Promotional Access/Promotions primary navigation tile.
- Consolidates advanced tools under an Intelligence / Analysis & research directory on desktop and mobile.
- Keeps core daily navigation focused on Dashboard, Profile, Employer Hub, Run Check, Reports, and Action Center.
- Owner navigation exposes the new Executive Control workspace.

### Executive_Eagle control center
- Adds `#/executive`, restricted to the active Owner account.
- Provides a personal Executive_Eagle command center for live site events.
- Displays Frenzy status, level, countdown, Signal Zero state, event identity, and current announcement.

### Frenzy Mode
- Uses the existing `settings/portal` document so no new Firestore collection is required.
- Owner can initiate a timed site-wide Frenzy event, set a starting level, publish an opening message, open/close the Signal Zero window, and optionally release a promotional drop.
- During a live event, Owner can change Frenzy level, trigger Maximum Frenzy, extend the event, publish live announcements, update a drop, or end Frenzy immediately.
- Users receive a restrained site-wide Frenzy status bar with live level and countdown plus a one-time activation presentation per event session.
- Event actions write to the existing Cognitus audit log where available.
- Frenzy changes presentation/event access windows only; it does not expand role or protected-record permissions.

### Frenzy-exclusive promotional feature: Signal Zero
- Adds a new promotional entitlement `signal_zero` at `#/signal-zero`.
- Requires **both** the Signal Zero entitlement and an active Frenzy event with the Signal Zero window enabled.
- Entitled accounts see the feature as Dormant outside Frenzy rather than receiving permanent access.
- During Frenzy, Signal Zero performs temporary cross-record analysis over records already authorized to the account.
- Ordinary promo users use screening-visible report summaries; Reviewer/Admin/Owner visibility remains role-scoped.
- Highlights defined cross-record conditions such as severe reviewed records, organization-date overlaps, report activity clusters, identity footprint, and organization footprint.
- Explicitly states that Signal Convergence is not a risk score, credibility score, guilt finding, or employment recommendation.

### Stability and security
- Removes V33's broad promo-root MutationObserver and uses render events/rAF instead.
- Simplifies mobile promo navigation and removes redundant retry polling.
- Adds a high-specificity Signal Zero contrast authority so the global professional contract cannot create dark-on-dark form text.
- Restores the last validated Firestore rules baseline from the V33 release after the current `main` rules file became malformed during a later manual rules rewrite. Frenzy reuses the existing public-read/Owner-write `settings/portal` rule and does not introduce a new collection.
- Adds dedicated Professional + Frenzy V35 validation and updates legacy V27/V29/V33 regression expectations for the consolidated product architecture.

### Important
A single promotional code/direct grant still follows the existing Firestore feature-array maximum from the validated rules baseline. Signal Zero itself can be assigned normally, but this PR intentionally prioritizes restoring a valid ruleset rather than preserving the malformed later rules file.

Board notes and quick opening now have direct mouse/touch gestures across Classic, Twin and Expedition. Right-click or hold a covered cell to cycle **flag → suspected safe → clear**; use the same gesture on an open number to quick-open. A shared toolbar above the board provides all four click/tap modes and stays available while scrolling. Confirmed states remain protected.

Nearby player safe notes and confirmed-safe cells are quick-open targets even when adjacent flags do not match. Other unknown neighbors still require matching flags. Unreachable or unaffordable safe targets retain their marks, and incorrect player notes can still cause normal mine damage.

In Expedition, **C** returns keyboard focus to the character's final square, including after a no-op. Pointer actions keep their selected target. Quick opening can reveal or reach stairs without finishing the floor or starting its Boss: select the exit in Reveal mode when ready to leave. The shared action pipeline retains ordinary movement, damage, discovery reactions and Boss AP costs. Rules revision 4 retires incompatible journals at their extraction checkpoint while preserving camp progress.

Also fixes a fresh tap being suppressed immediately after a Classic long press and delayed context menus issuing a second command after slow right-click handling. Only deliberate keyboard menu requests reset menu suppression. English, Chinese and Japanese help and the English interaction/save documentation describe the resulting controls. Shield descriptions now distinguish red triggered-mine markers from gold discovery flags. Camp purchases are displayed in ascending price order, with stable ordering for equal prices.

Validation: clean install and zero-vulnerability audit; formatting, explicit-type contracts, legacy typecheck, 191 behavior tests under each compiler, TS7 production build and artifact checks, six A/B rounds, and 555 documented business functions. Edge browser acceptance covers direct right-button and emulated touch gestures, both Twin boards, all three Bosses, safe targets with insufficient flags, keyboard focus, scrolling, tool priority, three languages and 320–3840 px layouts. All 26 camp purchases are checked for ascending prices in each language. Touch emulation does not replace physical-device testing.

author: alasdairmcmillan
body:
## The bug

`features_for_future_show` advances the effective `show_index` by the target's rank among upcoming shows, but its state only ever reaches the last **played** show. Every scheduled-but-unplayed show in between read as a confirmed miss, and the gap-ratio model rewarded that as mounting bustout pressure.

Across the 10 upcoming shows the heuristic escalated Harry Hood **0.138 → 0.287**, reporting `gap 10` at the far end. But all nine intervening shows will be played first, and at Hood's ~25–33% per-show rate the chance it survives them unplayed is ~`0.75^9` ≈ **7%**. The baseline was boosting a song on a one-in-fourteen branch — and the rotation-correct expectation is the *reverse*: by the far end of a tour a hot song has most likely already been spent.

Every track consuming `candidate_features` / `heuristic_prediction` inherited this. In the 2026-09-05 batch one model read the escalation as genuine and priced Hood at **0.434** for 10-10, over the ~0.40 line `AGENTS.md` reserves for exceptional evidence.

## The fix

All corrections are scoped to the unobserved-future path via a new `unobserved_since` argument defaulting to 0:

| Feature | Correction |
|---|---|
| `gap` / `gap_ratio` | capped at the song's own median spacing, so `gap_ratio` saturates near 1.0 (neutral) instead of climbing per show |
| `played_prev_show` | forced to 0 when the preceding show is unobserved |
| `plays_last_10/50/150` | windows anchor on observed history rather than sliding past shows that haven't happened |

Eligibility deliberately keys off the **observed** elapsed count, not the capped gap — it asks whether a song was alive as of the last real show, a question fixed regardless of horizon. Using the cap there pulled long-dormant songs with tightly clustered plays into the pool (418 → 610). Left on the raw count it thinned the pool 418 → 414 over ten shows, and since the heuristic renormalises to the expected setlist size, those silent drops inflated every survivor's probability — the residual escalation after the gap fix alone.

## Blast radius

`build_features` and `simulate.py` are unaffected — both keep state current show by show, so `unobserved_since` stays 0 and their features are byte-identical. `decayed_rate` was already invariant to rank (the `r^(eff-max)` factor cancels between numerator and denominator).

## Result

Hood is flat at 0.2445 from 10-03 through 10-09; pool holds at 418. The remaining step at 10-10/10-11 is genuine venue signal — Orion has prior Phish history, so `chalk-dust-torture` carries `venue_gap 1` and is suppressed 0.148 → 0.054, its mass redistributing under normalisation.

## Tests

380 pass (376 baseline + 4 new). Each new test was confirmed to **fail** against the old code, including strengthening two that initially passed either way because the 10-show fixture couldn't reach the 300-show eligibility cutoff.

luzia-like8's ladder (W3g) lost every step image to the failed proxy and the media columns went blank, so half of each row was empty. Plan row PR-3k.

author: spacejens
body:
Closes #697

## Summary

The team deepdive's "Top players" section previously ranked a team's players by raw total match-event count — a stand-in metric used before Star Player Points (SPP) was modeled. This PR switches it to rank by each player's stored career SPP total (`players.sppTotal`, including manual adjustments), matching how the player deepdive and the insights top list already rank by SPP.

Two intentional user-visible behavior changes:
- **The metric changed entirely**, not just its magnitude — the numbers on the embed now mean SPP, not event count.
- **Star players are no longer listed** in this section, matching every other SPP ranking in the codebase (one star's repeated hires would otherwise occupy multiple leaderboard slots on a single team).

### Changes
- Added `PlayersService.topPlayersByTotalSppForTeam(teamId, limit)`, a team-scoped counterpart to the existing `topPlayersByTotalSpp`, reading the stored `players.sppTotal` column across every era the team has played, excluding star players and null totals, ordered by total descending with no secondary tiebreak.
- Wired it through `TeamsStatisticsService`/`TeamsService` (mirroring the existing match-event delegation chain), and pointed the team deepdive at it.
- Changed the section header from `Top players by match events:` to `Top players by SPP:`.
- Deleted the now-dead match-event-count ranking chain (`TeamsService`/`TeamsStatisticsService.getTopPlayersByMatchEventCount`, `MatchEventCountsService.countAllMatchEventsByPlayerForTeam`) and its tests.
- Updated `docs/discord-bot/slash-commands/deepdive.md` to describe the new section.

Full design spec and implementation plan are in `docs/plans/` (gitignored, not part of this PR) if useful for review context.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm verify` passes repo-wide (build, lint, typecheck, format, tests — 90% coverage threshold met)
- [x] Every task self-reviewed and approved during implementation
- [x] Whole-branch review completed — no Critical/Important findings; one Minor doc-wording finding fixed

* **New Features**
  * Team deep dives now show top players ranked by total SPP.
  * Rankings include player position and era, exclude star players, and retain existing tie handling.

body:
Closes the post-merge Codex P2 on #307: the retirement wording implied schedules state a report type, but scheduling is portfolio-review-only — no report-type field exists, the definition validator binds the family, dispatch always creates portfolio-review jobs, and unknown config fields are ignored, so an operator following the old wording could configure `report_type: proof_pack` and silently receive portfolio-review jobs. Both the source map and the context doc now state the bounded truth. Typed multi-family scheduled dispatch remains unbuilt by choice, not implied.
