author: seanmizen
body:
Closes #146.

There was no repo-wide testing standard. Only `caroline-be` (`bun test`) and `ffmpeg-converter/web` (Playwright) had suites, and CI (`ux-check.yml`) guarded only the latter — everything else merged untested.

`inside` is being built out over many tickets, so it gets a harness, a documented convention agents will pick up, and CI that actually enforces it.

## Backend — `bun test`, 24 tests

`src/tests/setup.ts` gives each suite its own temp dir for database and uploads. Tests never create `database.db` or `uploads/` in the repo — CI fails if they do. (`caroline-be`'s equivalent declares `:memory:` but then seeds `./database.db`; this doesn't repeat that.)

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| `api.test.ts` | liveness, health, config, **admin scope 401** — the canary for anyone adding an unguarded admin route — and 404s. Driven by `app.inject()`, no port, no race. |
| `migrations.test.ts` | fresh apply, idempotency on reboot, and that `CHECK` / FK / `UNIQUE` constraints actually bite |
| `storage.test.ts` | the `StorageProvider` **contract**, written against the interface not `LocalStorageProvider`, so the future S3 provider should pass it unchanged |
| `images.test.ts` | variant widths, aspect preservation, no-upscale, filename collision safety |

## Frontend — Playwright, 10 tests

Runs the real app against the real backend on **4160/4161**, offset from the dev ports so a running `yarn start` never collides.

Covers render, config-driven copy, backend-reachable *and* backend-unreachable states, no console errors, and the full theme matrix — cycle, persistence, explicit-choice-beats-OS, **live OS change while on auto**, and **no pre-hydration flash**. The last two are regression guards for the specific bugs fixed in #143.

## CI

`.github/workflows/inside-check.yml` runs types → lint → unit → E2E on any PR touching `apps/inside`, uploads the Playwright report on failure, and asserts the test run left no artefacts in the repo.

Lint is scoped to `apps/inside` **deliberately**: a repo-wide `yarn check` currently reports ~138 pre-existing findings elsewhere, which would make this job permanently red and therefore ignored.

## The standard itself

`apps/inside/CLAUDE.md` documents it so future agents pick it up automatically — commands, what to test where, the bar for new work (new route → inject test; new migration → constraint tests; new flow → E2E spec; new shared module → contract tests), plus the locked product decisions, the `projects`/`briefs`/`pitches` vocabulary, and the theming and storage rules.

One hard-won note is written down there: **use retrying assertions, not a synchronous `page.evaluate()` read.** The theme specs flaked exactly this way while being written — the body class lands on a React re-render, and a bare read races it.

## Also

- Server and migration logging silenced under `NODE_ENV=test`, so a failing assertion is readable
- Playwright output gitignored

## Verification

Full CI sequence run locally on this branch, rebased onto #147:

- `yarn workspace inside test:types` — clean
- `npx biome check apps/inside` — clean
- `yarn workspace inside test:unit` — 24 pass, 0 fail
- `yarn workspace inside test:e2e` — 10 pass
- `git status --porcelain` clean after a full run

## Follow-up

#147's domain tables were verified manually by that worker (the harness didn't exist yet). Backfilling automated constraint tests for those seven tables is worth a ticket.

author: deity719
body:
Two commits, two issues, one file pair — both edit `scripts/sync-shell-common-vendor.sh`
and `tests/sync-vendor.sh`, so they are bundled to avoid a rebase chain.

Closes #31
Closes #30

## 1 — `Closes #31`: a stale SSOT checkout was a false green

The script reads the `--ssot` checkout's **working tree** and said nothing about
whether that tree was current. A checkout that has been `fetch`ed but not `pull`ed
still answers every comparison — against commits the SSOT moved past. Both
directions went quietly wrong: `--check` reported the copies clean against stale
content, and write mode regenerated them *from* it, rolling a vendored copy
backwards.

Not hypothetical. Reproduced against the real incident, with the real SHAs:

```
$ git clone ~/dotfiles /tmp/dots-stale && git -C /tmp/dots-stale reset --hard HEAD~2
$ scripts/sync-shell-common-vendor.sh --check --ssot /tmp/dots-stale ../gh-verify-skills
FAIL  /tmp/dots-stale is 2 commit(s) behind origin/main -- HEAD 9a6c40ba…, origin/main 165077dc…
      run 'git -C /tmp/dots-stale pull --ff-only', or pass --allow-stale-ssot to vendor the older revision
      (origin/main is only as fresh as your last fetch; this check makes no network call)
rc=1
```

Write mode stops the same way, before writing anything. Under
`--allow-stale-ssot` the run announces itself and proceeds — and immediately
surfaces the `DRIFT gh_pr_review.sh` that the old false green had hidden.

Design points, all from the issue body:

- **No network call.** The comparison is against the remote-tracking ref already
  on disk. Refreshing `origin/main` is `git fetch`, the operator's job; the
  failure output says so in as many words. A sync tool doing silent network I/O
  is its own trap.
- **A dirty SSOT warns and names the files** — an uncommitted local edit would
  otherwise vendor out wearing an upstream banner. Untracked files count:
  `$ssot/$rel` may itself be one.
- **`--allow-stale-ssot`** is explicit and prints what it is doing.
- **Nothing determinable is passed over in silence.** A checkout with no
  upstream, one whose status cannot be read, and a path that is not a git
  checkout at all each print a `note` saying what could not be checked. The
  whole class of bug here is a gate reporting green because it could not see; a
  new "cannot see" arm that stayed quiet would just be the same bug again.

## 2 — `Closes #30`: bridge-stub assertion tightened, without breaking honest stubs

The `# Bridge only` check scraped backticked identifiers out of the stub's prose
and required **at least one** to still be a function of the SSOT. A stub naming
several required symbols passed after all but one had been deleted upstream.

Of the three options weighed in the issue, this takes the first — a dedicated
banner field — **made opt-in**:

    # Bridges: _dotfiles_setup_mode

All names listed must still be functions of the SSOT, reported together. A field
entry lands in a grep pattern, so a non-identifier there is a loud failure rather
than a quietly wider search that matches anything.

The backtick rule stays as the fallback, unchanged. It is not merely lax — it is
the only thing sayable about a stub that never stated a contract. A prose header
legitimately backticks non-functions (`_SC`, `[ -f ]` in `gh-verify-skills`' real
stub), so requiring "all" over scraped prose would fail honest stubs. Scraped
prose cannot carry a contract; the field is how a stub says what it actually
owes. Nothing existing regresses, and the rule stays strictly better than the
`skip` of #28 that asserted nothing.

**Follow-up filed, deliberately not done here:** `gh-verify-skills`' stub for
`shell-common/tools/integrations/claude.sh` needs the `# Bridges:` line to
tighten from liveness to completeness. That is another repo's file, and what a
repo vendors is that repo's decision — `dEitY719/gh-verify-skills#25`.

## Verification — demonstrated, not asserted

- `tests/sync-vendor.sh`: **90 assertions, all green** (was 61). The new #31
  cases build a throwaway git checkout whose `origin/main` is one commit ahead of
  its working tree — `update-ref` standing in for the fetch that already ran, no
  network anywhere. The new #30 case is the exact false green from the issue: a
  stub that promises `_one_fn` and `_multi_fn`, with `_one_fn` deleted upstream,
  passes under the backtick rule and fails under the field, naming only the name
  that went.
- Real corpus, `~/dotfiles` level and clean: `ok 33 vendored file(s) match their
  SSOT, 0 skipped`, with no `WARN`/`note` line of any kind. `render()` and
  `extract_fn()` are untouched, so whole-file copies stay byte-identical.
- `shellcheck --severity=warning` clean on both files.

author: 0pcom
body:
Adds three panels to the reward server's statistics renderer, through the existing ANSI path so the terminal output and the served HTML stay one rendering: a transports-per-visor histogram, an architecture pie, and the per-visor uptime timeline `skywire cli ut tpd graph` draws.

The histogram is gated rather than drawn unconditionally. TPD's transport index oscillates (#4513), and a distribution taken mid-refill draws a network whose visors each hold half the transports they hold — a line chart at least shows the fluctuation, a histogram renders one sample as a static shape. It refuses to draw on the store's partial-read flag (#4542), on the stats feed's completeness stamp, or when the per-key index fails to sum to twice the aggregate's transport count, and prints the reason instead. #4542's flag was being dropped at publish time, so `stats/network` now carries `partial`/`missing_batches` and a partial read counts against that body's `complete`.

Architecture comes from the operator surveys, not TPD — TPD's heartbeat carries a version string and no arch field, so there is nothing to source from the discovery. The panel prints that provenance, since the surveyed population is a subset of the visors TPD counts. The pie is rasterized in-tree (nothing vendored draws one) with a distinct glyph per slice so it reads without color.

The timeline panel reuses the CLI's data path instead of shelling out: `ShadeForCount`/`BitmapToBlocks`/`RollingBar` move to `pkg/uptimestats` — they had already been copy-pasted into `visor/info.go` — and the v3 dump is read from the tpd-uptime CXO feed with HTTP over dmsg behind it. The liveness chart, which ran `skywire cli ut tpd graph --json` as a subprocess, now shares that fetch, so the ~2 MB body is pulled once for both.

Tests per panel, following the existing convention. `golangci-lint run` and `GOOS=windows golangci-lint run` are clean for the changed files.

author: cao825
body:
W1-T2668. W1-T2559 split retro, triage and inbox_draft into their own `synthesis:` mounts and stepped triage down to `low` on a measured volume argument. **retro and inbox_draft stayed at `claude-opus-5`/`high` because nothing measured them** — and that is still true today.

W1-T2560 then built the instrument whose own header states its purpose in terms: so that *"sonnet would do here" becomes a measurement instead of an opinion*. But `computeClassSweep` groups by `task_class` over `gatherRuns`, which requires a `run.start` and sums turns from implement/recon done-steps. **A synthesis rung is not a task run** — no `task_class`, so it landed in `"unknown"` or nowhere at all. The one verb built to price these rows was structurally unable to see them, and `.remudero/mounts.yaml`'s own *"$827 across 219 invocations, 22% of the pipeline, none of it shipping code"* came from a hand query that nothing re-derives.

## Neither the population nor the step names is a new list

That is the whole reason this extends the existing script rather than adding a second one:

| what | comes from | why |
|---|---|---|
| which rungs exist | `SYNTHESIS_ROLES` (`src/lib/mounts.ts`) | the same constant `loadMounts` validates the `synthesis:` block against — a fourth row added tomorrow is priced tomorrow |
| which ledger step each writes | `ARCHITECT_LANE_STEPS` (`src/lib/retro.ts`) | the ONE map that already identifies these lanes by "the ONE ledger `step` name each writes" |

That map was module-private; **exporting it is this task's only edit outside its own two files, and it is one line.** A local copy was the alternative and I rejected it: `inbox_draft`'s step is `inbox.draft_synthesized`, which no naming rule derives, so a second list would drift silently — and a test asserting on `retro.ts`'s *source text* to prevent that is precisely the fragility class W1-T2905 exists for. A test asserts the rung→step mapping is read from that map, with a control that `inbox_draft`'s step is **not** the name a rule-based guess would produce.

## The divisor is named, not reused

`computeClassSweep` divides by distinct settled `task_id` — cost per **completed task**. A synthesis rung completes no task and carries no `task_id`, so dividing by anything and calling it the same thing would be a category error. These rows carry `costPerInvocationUsd`, and the rendered table says:

```
synthesis rung | invocations | turns p50/p90/max | cost p50/p90/max ($) | total $ | $/INVOCATION
  (never $/completed task — these rungs complete no task and carry no task_id)
```

They render in their **own** table, never as extra rows in the per-task_class one — a shared column would put two different units side by side, which is how a reader ends up comparing them.

## Disciplines kept — the reason to extend this file

Percentiles never means; dedup by `run_id`; all three rotation forms and the row:run ratio still printed beside the tables; outcome before cost. Two additions in the same spirit:

- an **unmeasured** rung reads `null`, never `0` — a rung nobody ran must not render as a free one
- a terminal row with **no `run_id`** is dropped *and counted* (`rowsWithoutRunId`), so a corpus full of them is visible rather than silently thinning the percentiles

**It reports; it rules on nothing.** The existing header's last line binds this change too, and the new table says so where it is read.

## Verification

| falsifier | result |
|---|---|
| report a mean instead of p50 | 7 / 8 |
| reuse the per-completed-task divisor name | 7 / 8 |
| drop the `run_id` dedup | 7 / 8 |
| an unmeasured rung reads `0` instead of `null` | 7 / 8 |
| *restored* | **8 / 8** |

The mean falsifier is driven by nine cheap invocations and one $40 outlier: a mean reads ~4.5, p50 must stay at 1, and the outlier must still be visible as `max`.

- the suite: **8 / 8**
- **1459 / 1467** across the union of a symbol sweep (15 files) and `diff-class --list-census-suites` (63 — the verb from [#4076](https://github.com/craigoley/remudero/pull/4076), used here because this diff touches `src/lib/retro.ts`). All 6 failures are pre-existing in `test/merge-lcov.test.ts` (repo pins Node 22.22.3; this box runs 22.22.2)
- `rmd preflight --fast`: **16 / 16**

## Scope

`src/lib/retro.ts` is outside this shard's `files:` — one line, an `export` on an existing constant, forced by the single-source-of-truth choice above. Ratified widening, recorded here and in the commit message rather than in the shard.

## Acceptance

- the sweep reports the three synthesis rungs as their own rows, not folded into unknown | unit test: test/the-headroom-sweep-cannot-see-the-synthesis-rungs.test.ts
- each rung's row carries turn and cost percentiles, never a mean | unit test: test/the-headroom-sweep-cannot-see-the-synthesis-rungs.test.ts
- a rung with no divisor for completed work names its per-invocation basis rather than reusing a task divisor silently | unit test: test/the-headroom-sweep-cannot-see-the-synthesis-rungs.test.ts
- the existing per-task_class rows and the corpus controls are unchanged | unit test: test/the-headroom-sweep-cannot-see-the-synthesis-rungs.test.ts

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

After the ARIA-detection and top-level frame-scoping fixes (PR #45) shipped, automated LinkedIn login still cannot complete because of a newly-isolated root cause: LinkedIn's client-side JS redirects the WHOLE page away from `/login` to `fr.linkedin.com/legal/cookie-policy` (a fresh `lipi` token every load) whenever the browser session carries no consent cookie. By the time `fill-credentials` runs, the main frame IS the cookie-policy page, the login form is gone, and the endpoint clean-fails (correct behavior, wrong page).

Verified reproduction (live, on the PR #45 image):
1. Navigate to `/login` with `wait_until: load` — the real email+password form renders in the main frame.
2. Within ~1-2s LinkedIn's JS redirects the page to `fr.linkedin.com/legal/cookie-policy`.
3. `fill-credentials` then finds no form and clean-fails.
4. Manually accepting the cookie wall and re-navigating to `/login` re-fires the consent redirect (new `lipi` token) — consent does not persist across the navigate.

Secondary finding: the existing `_dismiss_consent_walls` helper aggravates this — its accept-click lands on the consent redirect page itself.

## Goal

Make the browser service reliably land on (and stay on) the real login form so `fill-credentials` can bind and submit, despite LinkedIn's consent-redirect wall.

## Acceptance criteria

- Detect the consent/cookie-policy redirect (URL pattern `**/legal/cookie-policy**` or equivalent) after navigation and BEFORE attempting credential fill.
- Establish/persist consent so the subsequent `/login` navigation is NOT redirected: set the required consent cookie(s) in the browser context up front, or accept the wall and re-navigate WITHOUT the redirect re-firing. The consent state must survive the re-navigation within the same session.
- After consent is established, `fill-credentials` binds to the top-level login form (email + password textboxes) and does NOT descend into any iframe (preserve the PR #45 frame-scoping behavior).
- Fix or gate `_dismiss_consent_walls` so its accept-click does not itself trigger/land on the consent-redirect page.
- Preserve the clean 4xx-on-miss behavior for a genuine missing form (no regression to HTTP 500).
- Add regression tests: (a) login page that consent-redirects then must be recovered; (b) login page with consent already set (no redirect); (c) genuine missing-form miss still clean-fails 4xx.
- Vault decrypt path and `/share`/other endpoints untouched.

## Scope

Single repo: yes — all changes within robotsix-browser. External changes: none.

2. 新增 `deploy/README.md`：明确划分单机 Compose 与 K8s/测试集群的拓扑边界，详细文档化专用 Secrets 命名规范（`PROD_SERVER_HOST`、`PROD_SERVER_USER`、`PROD_SERVER_SSH_KEY` 等），与集群维护所用的不稳定 `SERVERS_LIST_JSON` 严格隔离。

author: zkysar1
body:
## Summary

The plan (`update_plan` / the hierarchical task network) is the one thing keeping small models on rails, and it was a checklist, not a record. This lands ADR-0110:

- **The plan knows what it is for.** `TaskNetwork.context.request` is anchored at turn start and survives every full-replace; the re-injected plan is headed `Goal: …`, the ADR-0108 completion line quotes it, the compaction note and `AgentTaskUpdate.request` carry it.
- **Every step keeps what it did and what it produced.** `Task.evidence` is attached by the harness at the tool-execution seam (`<tool> <what> ✓|✗`, bounded); `Task.outcome` is the model's one-line result (new optional `update_plan` field), filled from the last evidence line when blank. `replace_from_author` carries evidence/outcome/origin across the full-replace by step title.
- **The plan has a history that outlives its steps.** A bounded `PlanEvent` log (authored / step / seeded / cleared / reset) written by every writer of the network; the reminder appends `Step N so far: …` and `Previously closed: …`.
- **Deep work does not start without a plan.** The plan-first gate is on by default for deep turns (`require_plan` now means every turn). After two withheld batches the harness plants a **request anchor** instead of failing open into nothing, and closes it at the conclusion only when it is the lone open step.
- CLI: the finished-plan collapse now matches glyph rows only (a hook's `[plan-completion-verdict]` tag kept a complete plan on screen).

## Verification

`uv run poe check`: ruff clean, format clean, mypy clean, **3441 passed, 9 skipped**. New `tests/test_plan_ledger.py` covers carry-over, outcome fill, chronological closures, the log bound, harness seeding, the anchor lifecycle, evidence attachment, the reminder's memory lines, the compaction note and the turn-start reset; `tests/test_render.py` gains the collapse regression.

## Docs

`docs/DECISIONS.md` ADR-0110, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/CONFIG.md`.

author: heet2107
body:
## Summary

Two new sections on the ContextQA site, both ported from React components that were supplied as reference.

### Stack — "works where you work"

A checklist of what ContextQA touches (code and CI, issues and support, AI coding agents) beside an **orbit** of the tools it plugs into. Three dotted rings turn around the ContextQA core at 26, 34 and 44 seconds a revolution, carrying four integration marks each, and every mark counter spins at its own ring's rate so the logos stay upright as they travel.

The section **replaces the thin text strip** that used to sit under the hero and listed the same surfaces as plain words, so the page gains a section rather than duplicating one.

The icons are our own integration set rather than the source component's stock ones: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Jira, Linear, Confluence, Slack, Zendesk, Sentry, Figma, Claude and Codex. Their marks are vendored from [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) (CC0) into the existing inline SVG sprite, each carrying a light and a dark theme colour so marks that are nearly black in light mode stay legible on the dark ground. Nothing is fetched at runtime, so the page keeps its no CDN rule.

The orbit is pure CSS keyframes, so it needs no build step and no JavaScript. It sits inside the section wrap as the second grid column, beside the checklist, which keeps the page free of horizontal overflow down to 390px. The whole thing is one `role="img"` with a screen reader list of the tool names beside it.

### Voices — staggered testimonial deck

The other pasted component, ported into this site's stack. Cards fan out from the centre with alternating tilt, the middle card lifts and takes the accent colour, and previous or next rotates the deck endlessly. Its controller is now generic over any `[data-deck]` stage rather than hard wired to the quotes.

Improvements over the source component:

- Cards are real `<button>` elements rather than click handlers on `<div>`s, plus arrow key support and a position counter.
- Off centre cards are hidden from assistive technology so only the centre quote is announced.
- The markup ships as an ordinary readable grid and the controller upgrades it, so the quotes survive with JavaScript blocked and under reduced motion, where the deck is left static and the nav hidden.
- Remote avatar photos are replaced with monogram tiles, keeping the zero external request rule.

### On the React components

This repository has no `package.json`, no `tsconfig.json`, no Tailwind config and no shadcn registry, and it contains zero `.tsx` files, so neither component could be dropped into a `/components/ui` folder. Both were reproduced in vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript instead, which keeps the site buildless and deployable as static files.

## Verification

Driven in headless Chromium in both themes at 1440×900 and 390×844:

- twelve marks render inside the orbit box with twelve distinct brand colours in both themes, all three rings turning and all twelve marks counter spinning;
- the deck advances and reverses with the counter tracking the centre card;
- zero console errors and zero failed requests;
- no element overflow at nine widths from 390 to 1920 pixels;
- no section overlap at six window sizes;
- with JavaScript disabled all twelve marks are still visible and all eight quotes readable; under reduced motion the rings hold still and the deck stays static with the nav hidden.

## Before launch

- The twelve integration marks are the surfaces named in the playbook plus the ones raised on the demo call. **Confirm the list against the real integration catalogue** and drop any tool that is not actually supported. Each brand remains the trademark of its owner and is shown for identification only.
- The testimonials are **illustrative**, written in the voice of the target persona and labelled as such on the page. Replace them with real, attributable customer quotes.

author: ymohanty
body:
Round 1 of the review loop on #155 (`dev` → `main`). Three P2s, all valid, all fixed here rather than filed — each is contained and two of them move money.

## 1. `v_activity` fanned out past `planned_activity` — closes #133

`admin_approval` and `technical_approval` are keyed on `row_id`, not `activity_code`, so neither is 1:1 with an activity by construction and the join was free to multiply. #133 reported +44 rows in June and *guessed* this cause without confirming it. Measured now:

```
admin_approval       734,658 rows   734,614 distinct   44 codes duplicated
technical_approval   745,508 rows   745,508 distinct    0 codes duplicated
```

Exactly the +44. Both sources are collapsed on the rule the scheme columns already use — largest value wins — with `row_id` breaking a tie so the choice is deterministic rather than whatever order the scan returned.

Verified against the real 6.4 GB build, views rebuilt in an in-memory catalog the way the consumer does:

```
planned_activity 4,073,745
v_activity       4,073,745   distinct 4,073,745   delta +0     (was +44)
v_approval         734,614 rows, 734,614 distinct activity_code
```

## 2. Mixed `assetDetails` shapes destroyed each other

Codex reported that a mapping-shaped record puts the union-schema `assetDetails_*` columns on the whole `pl` frame, so an unfiltered `pl` contributes an empty parent row for the list-shaped activity too — and since `_pl_child` dedupes `keep="first"` with `pl` appended first, the empty row wins and the populated child row is quarantined as a conflict.

That is correct, and there was **a second defect standing in front of it**: `astTyp` and `assetDetails_astTyp` both rename to `asset_type`, so concatenating the two shapes raw and renaming afterwards yields a duplicate column label and the build dies in `load.insert`. Confirmed against unmodified `dev` — this case has never worked, it crashed.

Both fixed: spellings are aligned *before* the concat, then only parent rows carrying populated asset values are appended. Removing the crash makes Codex's defect visible, and that is what the test pins — without the filter the assets come back `{"1": "well", "2": None}`.

## 3. Expenditure could load twice under fresh surrogate ids

`build.populate` writes `activity_expenditure` from two paths: the `re` dataset inside the snapshot loop, and the EXPENDITURE snapshots after it. The comment above the second says the `expenditure_id` counter continues across both — the cross-snapshot key set did not. It started empty, so a business line present in both walked past the guard added for exactly this and loaded twice.

The table's only key is that surrogate, so nothing downstream objects and the money simply doubles. Seeded from the table instead, read back rather than accumulated — the same reason `voucher_keys` is read back three lines below.

## Verification

Mutation-proved, each against its own failure:

| fix | fails without it |
|---|---|
| approval collapse | `assert 2 == 1` on `v_approval` |
| asset parent filter | assets come back `{"1": "well", "2": None}` |
| spelling alignment | duplicate-label `ValueError` in `load.insert` |
| expenditure key seed | `assert 2 == 1`, money doubled |

`592 passed`, ruff clean.

author: fuma419
body:
## Summary
- CIP-129 DRep hex is `0x22` + a 28-byte key hash (58 hex chars). The parser treated any 56 hex chars as a raw hash, so pasted explorer hex kept the header byte and dropped the last byte. Conway then rejected the cert as `DelegateeDRepNotRegisteredDELEG` (the hash in the error starts with `22`).
- Decode 58-char CIP-129 hex (and `0x…` prefixes) to the real credential. Prefer bech32 when listing DReps. Check the target is registered before building a named vote-delegation. Humanize the ledger error if submit still fails.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit: CIP-129 58-char hex (including the truncated `22288b58…` pattern), script-hash header, greedy-match still works for labelled text
- [x] Unit: `ensureDrepRegisteredForDelegation` throws when unregistered and allows build on indexer outage
- [x] Unit: `wrapSubmitError` maps `DelegateeDRepNotRegisteredDELEG`
- [x] UI: paste `drep1…` still builds; unregistered target does not call `voteDelegationTx`
- [ ] Vote → paste a live gov.tools `drep1…` on the same network → confirm builds
- [ ] Vote → paste CIP-129 hex for a live DRep → same
- [ ] Always Abstain still builds without a registration lookup

author: takemi-ohama
body:
## 何を変えたか

分割の基準を機械で見るようにし、超えていた 4 本を分割しました。あわせて確定仕様の
食い違いを 2 件直しています。

| issue | 直したこと |
| --- | --- |
| #354 | 行数の検査を新設し、基準を超える 4 本を分割した |
| #399 | `CHANGELOG.md` を分割の基準の対象外にした |
| #353 | 確定仕様の `cross-refactoring` の母集合を実装へ合わせた |
| #288 | 確定仕様から配布 Skill の数を外した |

**4 件を 1 本にしたのは、順序に依存があるためです。** #399 が決まらないと検査を入れた時点で
配布のたびに継続的統合が落ち、#354 の分割が済まないと検査を入れられません。

## 決めたこと

**`CHANGELOG.md` は分割の基準の対象外にします**（#399）。Keep a Changelog は最新の版が先頭に
あり、版の見出しを上から辿れることを読み手の期待にしています。分割すると「最新の版で何が
変わったか」を探す入口が増えます。

**「長くなったら分けない」という意味ではありません。** 書式が許す範囲で古い部分を退避する
方針を `markdown-writing` へ書きました。**退避の時期はメジャーの区切りで決めます**（行数で
決めると、版を足した拍子に退避が要るかどうかが変わるためです）。

**除外は片方向ではありません。** 除外したのに基準を下回っていれば、検査が「除外を外せ」と
言って落ちます。使われない除外が残り続けないようにするためです。

**確定仕様からは数を外しました**（#288）。数はランタイムごとに違い、版を上げるたびに動きます。
基準を持つのは `manifests/*-skills.txt` の行数だけです。**`docs/specifications/` を検査の対象へ
広げる案は採りませんでした。** 版を上げるたびに書き換えが要る文書が増えます。数を書かない
形にすれば、広げずに古くなりようが無くなります。

## 分割の内訳

いずれも節の切れ目で分け、各ファイルの冒頭に 3 本（または 2 本）への案内を置きました。

| もとの文書 | 行数 | 分割後 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `docs/claude-code-skills-survey.md` | 765 | `01-findings` 416 / `02-analysis` 179 / `03-plan` 190 |
| `docs/claude-code-skills-official-reference.md` | 720 | `01-frontmatter-and-description` 212 / `02-disclosure-and-placement` 243 / `03-budget-and-invocation` 285 |
| `docs/specifications/ndf-skill-inventory.md` | 580 | `01-ledger-and-criteria` 170 / `02-frontmatter-and-triggers` 228 / `03-version-history` 202 |
| `cross-refactoring/docs/02-apply-and-review.md` | 682 | `02-apply-and-review`（Step 4〜5）466 / `04-fix-and-report`（Step 6〜8）222 |

**`cross-refactoring` の分割だけは配布物です。** 既存の `03-review-viewpoints.md` は参照で
あって工程ではないため、番号を振り直さず `04-` を足しました。`SKILL.md` の 2 か所の参照と、
`02` の末尾からの案内を同じコミットで追随させています。

参照していた 11 か所（`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `docs/specifications/README.md` /
`plugins/ndf/skills/README.md` の 4 か所ほか）を新しい場所へ向けました。分割で 1 階層深く
なったため、分割後のファイルの中の相対リンクも繰り上げています。

## 満たすこと

- [x] 分割の基準を超える文書が 0 本になっている
- [x] 検査が `validate-runtime-plugins.sh` と継続的統合の両方から実行される
- [x] 走査の対象が git の追跡ファイルに限られ、記録は外れている
- [x] 除外が理由を持ち、要らなくなった除外を検査が拾う
- [x] 走査対象が 0 件のときは通らず、終了コード 2 で止まる
- [x] 分割した文書へのリンクがすべて解決する
- [x] 確定仕様の母集合が実装（参加する 4 CLI）と一致している
- [x] 確定仕様に配布 Skill の数が書かれていない

## Test plan

```console
$ uv run --project plugins/playwright-kit/skills/playwright-kit-ops --with pytest pytest . -q
2484 passed in 106.46s   # exit=0（新規 11 件：行数の検査）
$ python3 scripts/check-doc-line-limit.py --report
Markdown line limits are satisfied (191 files, limit 500)   # exit=0
$ python3 scripts/check-skill-frontmatter.py        # exit=0
$ python3 scripts/check-doc-staleness.py            # exit=0
$ python3 scripts/check-markdown-links.py --root .  # exit=0
$ python3 scripts/check-skill-repo-assumptions.py   # exit=0
$ python3 scripts/check-cross-skill-refs.py         # exit=0
$ bash scripts/build-runtime-plugins.sh --check     # exit=0
$ bash scripts/validate-runtime-plugins.sh          # exit=0
```

検査を入れた時点の上位は次のとおりで、**基準の手前 10 行以内に 4 本が並んでいます**。
1 度の加筆で超えうる位置にあるため、今後は検査が拾います。

```text

  493  plugins/ndf/skills/README.md

```

## 未確認

- **分割した 3 本の調査レポートは、内容を書き換えていません。** 節の切れ目で分け、冒頭の
  案内だけを足しました。当時の記録として読めるかは、通しで読み直していません
- `docs/external-reviews/` を記録として走査から外しました（474 行で基準内ですが、外部の
  レビュー結果をそのまま残す性質のためです）。#354 の一覧には挙がっていません

author: adamplatin123
body:
## What does this PR do?

One-shot mode (`hermes -z`) silenced logging with a process-wide `logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)`. That is a root-level kill switch: it suppressed every logger at or below CRITICAL **including the forensic file handlers**, so a failed `-z` run left `agent.log` / `errors.log` empty — no trail to debug for the exact (cron / SSH / subprocess) users who depend on it (#103056). The adjacent comment claimed file logging survived; `logging.disable()` does not work that way.

The console-silencing **intent** is real and preserved: `-z` stdout must contain only the final response text (the mode's contract). The fix now raises the level of only the non-file `StreamHandler`s attached at that point, leaving file handlers (and the queue feeding them) fully operational. The stale comment is replaced with one describing the real mechanism.

## Related Issue

Fixes #103056

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` — replace `logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)` with a targeted pass that sets `CRITICAL + 1` only on non-file `StreamHandler`s of the root logger; comment updated to explain why a global disable would also block the file-log queue
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_file_logging.py` (new) — regression tests running one-shot invocations hermetically (isolated `HERMES_HOME`):
  - a failing run writes the diagnostic trail to `logs/agent.log` and the failure/critical detail to both `agent.log` and `logs/errors.log`
  - the stdout contract holds on success and failure (final response text only, nothing else; stderr clean on the covered paths)

## How to Test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/ -q -k oneshot` → 32 passed, 2 skipped
2. Before the fix, the new tests fail with exactly the reported symptom: log files exist but are empty
3. Manual smoke (no network needed):
   ```bash
   H=$(mktemp -d); HERMES_HOME=$H .venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main -z --model m --provider nonexistent 'hi'
   wc -c $H/logs/agent.log   # non-zero after the fix; 0 before
   ```

author: junepark678
body:
Dashboard listing previously loaded the whole store and silently skipped unreadable jobs. Reuse startup recovery's bounded read-only scanner: 4,096 entries, 64 MiB aggregate metadata and the existing per-record/schema checks. Return sorted jobs only after a complete scan; incomplete listings produce a fixed HTTP 503 page instead of a misleading successful partial dashboard.

Listing never rewrites or removes records. Recovery still completes inspection before status writes and preserves its cancellation outcomes. The shared scanner also distinguishes a missing root from inspection failure rather than treating every failed existence check as an empty store.

All 22 selected store, recovery and HTTP tests passed with zero failures/errors/skips using offline non-incremental compilation. Tests cover entry and byte exhaustion, exact-budget success, record preservation, unknown/invalid metadata, recovery cancellation/retry and an actual dashboard request returning 503 for an unreadable record, then 200 after repair. Evidence: `build/job-listing-checkpoint/88319`. Full CI omitted because its patch lane executes vulnerability reproduction.

Refs #242, #71 and #69. This adds bounded truthful listing, not pagination, aggregate storage quotas or atomic observation against noncooperating writers. Writer ownership, safe reclamation, #68/#237 accepted-state recovery and #67/#72 full qualification remain open.

Stack: based on #321 (`b-job-metadata-schema`); merge the parent chain first.

author: artrayme
body:
## What changed and why

`TABL/DI` was a registry entry that existed only to refuse. A live probe settled why: ADT has no index resource under a table at all. Every route answers 404, and the table XML's one index link is a SAP GUI handoff to the SE11 Indexes tab, not REST. `DD_INDEX_INTERFACE`, the function module that tab itself calls, does work.

- `src/adt/index-create.ts`: a classrun bridge in the shape of the existing `VIEW/DV` and `TRAN/T` bridges. It generates a closed `IF_OO_ADT_CLASSRUN` fragment, calls the FM with `ACTION='I'` or `'D'`, commits, and re-reads DD12V and DD17S to prove the outcome, since there is no ADT resource to read an index back from.
- An index has no package of its own, so the bridge reads the base table's ADT resource and gates on that package; a caller-supplied `package` is only checked for agreement. The delete accepts `corr_nr`, unlike the view and transaction deletes, because the FM takes a transport for `ACTION='D'` too.
- Unique index on a client-dependent table: DDIC requires the client field in `index_fields`. A generated DD03L guard refuses that case as `BAD_INPUT` with a hint before the FM is called (confirmed live, not suspected).
- Delete path: `DD_INDEX_INTERFACE` reports `ACTFAILED='X'` on delete even though the index rows are already gone. The delete fragment now commits unconditionally and lets a three-way read-back (DD12V unfiltered, DD12V active, DD17S) decide. Rows still present stay `CHECK_FAILED` with all three counts and the flag value; empty read-back with the flag set emits a `ZMCP-DDIC-NOTE>` line and the tag `INDEX-DELETED-ACTFAILED`, and `abap_write` passes a note to the caller saying the flag's cause is not established. Every success path still fires `INDEX-DELETED INDEX-GONE`.
- Generated bridge source is checked before it is written: the delete fragment builds its long messages in a variable across short lines, and every bridge body is refused with `CHECK_FAILED` (naming the line and its length) if any line exceeds ABAP's 255-character source-line limit. A live round found the earlier note line was 268 characters, so every delete failed at the class-source PUT before the function module ran; worst-case tests now measure the assembled source at the longest legal names.
- Deployed bridge classes are refreshed when the generated body changes (confirmed live: the old class body did not survive a redeploy).
- Neither operation is verified or journalled, and both responses say so. Reversal is a `mode: "delete"` call, not a journal undo.
- Registry, capability table, orient skill, write-path docs, tool schema descriptions and CHANGELOG updated. The `abap_write` v2 surface cannot reach this route because `base_table` is v1-only; noted in the report as a follow-up.

## Verification

- [x] `npm test` passes locally (full offline suite on the merged branch: 295 files / 7764 tests, merge commit 1b828aa)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass
- [x] `npm run check:leaks` passes
- [x] Live-tested on an A4H appliance (branch HEAD f1251df, later merged with main as 1b828aa with only description-wording, CHANGELOG and bundle deltas, `$TMP` only): base table `ZTMD_I28_T` created, non-unique index `Z01` on one field created (`INDEX-CREATED INDEX-ACTIVE INDEX-FIELDS`) and deleted (`INDEX-DELETED-ACTFAILED INDEX-DELETED INDEX-GONE`, no long-line or check failure); the deployed delete bridge class was read back and contains the new read-back variable with no source line over 255 characters; a unique index `Z02` on the client field plus two more was created and deleted the same way; a second delete of `Z02` returned `NOT_FOUND` from the bridge's own catalog pre-check; base table deleted and confirmed absent via `abap_read`. Every create response reports `verified: false`, as documented. Not exercised: the transportable-package path (`corr_nr`, package-agreement gating), the free-name fallback on `ALREADY_EXIST`; the two `$TMP` bridge classes are left in place by design.

author: wms2537
body:
Part of #121's *"high-impact configuration changes expose a deterministic dry-run/plan response"* and *"a stale plan hash is refused when relevant state changed between plan and commit."*

## The audit that found it

I declined to tick these two criteria last time because I had not established **which** configuration changes were meant to be covered. Enumerating every config-mutating endpoint in the served contract gave a clear answer: `PUT /api/v1/system/retention` was the only one with a plan, out of 21.

Most of the rest do not need one — creating a backup destination or a site is not destructive. One does, and the code says so itself:

> `put_db_limit`: *"Same deferred-execution shape as the recording cap: written now, enforced later by a sweep that has no principal."*

The recording cap got a dry run and a plan hash. The DB cap, which on **that same sweep** sheds embed-query results, then CLIP embeddings, then detections (`retention.rs` step 11), got neither.

A setting that deletes rows later ought to say so before it is set.

## What the plan says

```json
{
  "plan_hash": "…",
  "confirmation_required": true,
  "effect": { "db_bytes": …, "new_cap_bytes": …, "would_shed_bytes": … },
  "sheds_in_order": ["embed_queries", "embeddings", "detections"],
  "protected": ["events", "audit_log"]
}
```

**The order is the useful part.** Shedding embed-query results costs a cache; shedding detections costs the record of what was seen. "Some rows will be deleted" is not a plan.

**It deliberately does not predict row counts.** The sweep first reclaims pages freed by ordinary row retention, so how much it then has to delete depends on what that pass frees. A confident number here would be invented — and an invented number in a confirmation dialog is worse than an honest absence.

## A test that passed while proving the opposite

Worth recording, because it is the failure mode this whole session keeps turning up. My stale-hash test did:

```rust
// Something else changes the cap between the plan and the commit.
put_db(&st, r#"{"max_db_gb": 4.0}"#)
```

4.0 GB is what the box was **already using**. The hashed state never moved, the commit was correctly *not* refused, and the test failed — but had the default been anything else, it would have passed while exercising nothing.

It now uses a value the box was not using **and asserts the re-planned hash actually differs** before relying on the refusal:

```rust
assert_ne!(moved["plan_hash"], plan["plan_hash"],
    "the intermediate change did not move the state the plan depends on, so this test would
     not be exercising the refusal at all");
```

Mutation-verified: removing the check fails both hash tests.

## Compatibility

The commit response keeps the `DbStatus` shape it always had — an existing client reading `db_bytes`/`max_db_gb` is unaffected by the handler now being able to return a plan. `dry_run` and `plan_hash` are optional; omitting them commits exactly as before. Contract regenerated, classifier reports **compatible**.

37 test binaries green, fmt and clippy clean.

## Still open on #121

`POST /api/v1/system/db/convert` rewrites the whole database file and takes a write lock for its duration. It is not destructive in the same way, but "how long will this take and what happens if I do it now" is a fair question with no answer today. I have not judged whether it warrants a plan — that is a product call rather than an obvious gap.

author: juvojustin
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #53 that reduces the migrated implementation by ~680 library lines (14,436 → 13,757) with no change to public exports, wire formats, token claims, or security checks. Every duplicated helper the migration left behind now has one owner, and the control plane resolves its per-request dependencies through one request scope instead of four hand-rolled copies.

## What changed

**Shared foundations** (six small new modules, all internal)
- `guards.ts`: the union predicates (`isAbilityAccess`, `isAbilityExposure`, `isAbilityTransport`, `isServiceHttpMethod`) plus `isRecord`, `isAsyncIterable`, `isAsyncIterator`, previously copied 8× across the tree.
- `encoding.ts`: `bytesToBase64Url` and `sha256Base64Url`, previously copied 4× and 2×.
- `authorization.ts`: one `Authorization: <Scheme> <credential>` parser behind the capability, JWK, and HMAC extractors (same messages, same statuses).
- `hono-context.ts`: `requestIdFromContext`, `mergedRequestHeaders`, and `deriveRequestContext`, replacing three near-identical per-call context builders in the service shell and the control plane.
- `call-headers.ts`: `applyForwardedCallHeaders` writes conn info, idempotency key, proof, request id, timeout, and token in one place for the direct client, the brokered client, the native binding path, and the broker's downstream call.
- `errors.ts` gains `servicePlaneErrorResponse`, `requireNonEmpty`, and exports the private transport status table so the oRPC adapter derives both the error map and the reverse status→code lookup from it instead of a 22-case switch.
- `paths.ts` loses the unused Hono-style route matcher (`pathMatches`, `joinPaths`, `pathAndQuery`) and gains `templateVariableName` for the three places that parsed `{name}` segments.

**Service**
- `OrderedWebSocketTasks.deliver()` owns bounded frame normalization for the manual and Hono-upgrade socket paths on both shells (queue still covers only normalization and synchronous delivery).
- `createAbilityBuilder` has one implementation behind its three methods.
- `schema-validation.ts` holds the fail-closed validation helpers that `orpc.ts` and `hibernation.ts` each copied.
- Both HTTP token requesters share one poster; only the request signer differs.
- The client builds its links through `fetchAbilityLinks` / `webSocketAbilityLinks`, which removes two unreachable throws and the transport re-check inside the native link.

**Control plane**
- `requestScope(context, surface, facts)` resolves services → registry → issuer lazily and at most once, and produces the broker or the invocation options for that request. Broker (Fetch and WebSocket), MCP, REST, and the in-process `abilityClient` all use it; `resolveBrokeredRequest`, `brokerForRequest`, `discoverServiceCapabilities`, and the per-mount memo triplets are gone.
- `brokerResolver` is the one place both broker transports turn logical-call headers into a broker.
- Caller-auth refusals go through a per-authenticator `refuse()`; the two event builders and default sinks collapse to one (the default sink is the shared one and emits the same JSON).
- The issuer's twin `issue*` methods share one body; the active-key round-trip lives in `validateActiveSigningKey` for both entry points.

## Behavior notes for reviewers

- Client-side scope validation messages now read `Service-Plane capability scope cannot be empty: <where>` instead of `client scope`; no test or doc pinned the old wording.
- `containsPrivateJwkMaterial` now rejects any present private member, not only string ones (stricter, fail-closed direction).
- Claim, header, and token-request parsers use the array-excluding `isRecord`; arrays were already rejected one line later with the same message.
- The MCP handler no longer receives `allowedOrigins` / `maxBodyBytes` from the mount; they were only ever read by preflight, which the mount still runs first.
- REST's registry is now wrapped in the same request-scoped snapshot as MCP and the broker; REST already pinned its snapshot via the matched route, so this is a no-op for it.
- The in-process client's service resolution is now raced against its own deadline like every other surface (previously only the outer call was).
- `body-limits.test.ts` patched two removed private methods; it now observes `requestScope` instead. Two tests for the deleted route matcher are removed with it.

## Verification

- `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test` (563), `npm run test:workerd` (533), `npm run build`, `npm run smoke` all pass.
- The Citation Wiki engineering-standards pages returned 403 from this environment, so this follows the repo's own conventions (CLAUDE.md, Biome) only.

author: henrymodisett
body:
## Intent

Two bugs from a driver's report on 2026-09-05. One concern: **the interface tells you to do something that doesn't work.**

### 1. Help denied a command the CLI tells you to run (AUT-1286)

They reported `touchstone pr answer` "doesn't exist in the installed CLI". It does — `touchstone pr answer --help` prints full usage. But `touchstone pr --help` listed only `open|status|merge|policy`, because `answer` lives in `respond-review.sh` while that usage text belongs to `touchstone-pr.sh`. An implementation split leaking into the interface.

They probed the narrower help — the natural probe, and the one the cold-start audit trained drivers to make — concluded the command was absent, and hand-edited the PR body with a marker. That path lacks base coordinates, fails review-binding, and wedges `pr open`. **A missing signpost pushed a driver onto a known hazardous route.**

Worse: the form they were told to run, `--finding` from #1143, appeared in **no** discoverable help — not `touchstone --help`, not `touchstone pr --help`. #1143's whole purpose was making the remedy reachable, and it advertised a form the help denied.

### 2. The reviewed slice was measured from a stale ref (AUT-1287)

Guidance said `touchstone review run --base <default>`, read as `main`. `--base` decides the slice through merge-base, and in a worktree the local default is routinely behind because nothing pulls it.

Theirs was **35 commits stale** → **138-file slice** → size limit blown → provider rejected it saying the reviewed slice was wrong. Three of the six rows in their incident table trace to this one word. They took the blame for passing `--base main`; they passed what every Touchstone surface told them to pass.

A stale base doesn't merely widen the slice — it fills it with already-merged work, which is why the rejection was about correctness rather than size.

## Invariants

- Every `touchstone pr answer` flag the CLI prints appears in both help surfaces.
- The serious-tier base is `origin/<default>` everywhere, and the bare form cannot return.

## Risk areas

- **Unverified, recorded on AUT-1287:** `touchstone-review.sh:526` passes `--base` straight to the Codex CLI, whose help documents `--base <BRANCH>`. Codex does no ref resolution before the model call — an invalid ref and `origin/main` fail identically on quota — so the Codex half cannot be confirmed until quota returns Sep 6, 22:28. The OpenRouter half **is** verified: this PR's own range pass resolved `origin/main` and reviewed the correct slice.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` changed, so an in-flight PR templated from the old text still reads `--base <default>`. Harmless — it is guidance, not a gate input.

## Validation

- Build: n/a — shell and prose.
- Automated tests: `test-pr-cli.sh`, `test-agent-steering-contract.sh`, `test-steering-render.sh`, `test-steering-size-caps.sh` all PASS. `TOUCHSTONE.md` is 12257 bytes against the 12288 cap; `render-steering.sh` re-run.
- Manual validation: probed the real `codex-cli 0.153.2` — `codex review --help` documents `--base <BRANCH>`; an invalid ref and `origin/main` behave identically (both echo the ref as prompt text, then fail on quota), so the Codex half is unconfirmable today and is recorded as owed on AUT-1287. Ran this PR's own range pass against `origin/main`, which resolved and reviewed the correct slice. Confirmed no `--base <default>` occurrence survives outside the test's own `assert_not_contains`. **A seventh site the sweep missed:** a manual grep across `TOUCHSTONE.md docs/ principles/ skills/` found six; the pull-request template surfaced only when an existing steering assertion failed on it after the other six changed — a test bound to the fact catching what a careful sweep did not, which is AUT-1272's argument in one observation.
- Review budget: v2 capability=interface-matches-guidance local_rounds=1 fix_rounds=0 prior_fix_rounds=0 reviewed_head=none cascade=false exit=continue
- Local review: openrouter on 49c2d9059441fbf0e7cfb7e29ef96fbd042e1e50: 0 findings, no changes required

## Review tier

normal

## Why this tier

Help text, guidance prose, and two assertions. No policy, schema or gate change.

Fixes AUT-1286

author: huntharo
body:
## Summary

A queued cross-thread message was mirrored from its 200-character `displayText` preview with empty attachment lists. Edit then canceled the authoritative FIFO entry and restored that preview, losing the remainder. The full input was intact before Edit. Local/federated viewers and Codex/ACP queues share this projection.

- Read full queue content from its owner on demand. Reuse transcript Markdown, thread links, image tiles, and the full-size lightbox. Recover content before Edit cancellation and compare a content hash to reject concurrent changes. Failed reads/transfers leave the entry queued; recovered file bytes use the existing PwrAgent attachment store.
- Add durable sender correspondence in PwrAgent-owned append-only JSONL, published during the active turn and reconstructed as ordinary transcript messages after reload/rollup. Recipient provenance opens the sender message; sender content links to its destination. Replay interleaves correspondence chronologically while retaining provider entry order.
- Distinguish last-confirmed queue admission, accepted execution, holds, cancellation, failure, and unknown outcomes. Late receipts cannot overwrite newer lifecycle evidence, and status-persistence failures cannot disrupt the recipient FIFO. No transcript/prompt history is newly stored in SQLite, and no Codex-owned storage is inspected.

## Verification

- 1,045 tests passed across 10 focused suites: registry, tool contracts, IPC/federation, attachment transfers, FIFO/projection, correspondence persistence, composer, and navigation.
- Coverage includes long Unicode/Markdown, multiple paragraphs, image/file/empty-file bytes, Edit/resend, failed loading, stale hashes, source/destination anchors, keyboard focus and Escape, sender restart/rollup, Codex and ACP FIFO ownership, peer identity isolation, and real federation router/attachment-transfer seams.
- Typecheck, ESLint, dependency boundaries, Codex storage boundary, theme-color checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

- Review regressions reproduced before the fixes: direct data/HTTPS images must bypass peer routing; Edit/resend must deduplicate hydrated file references while retaining authoritative metadata; reloaded correspondence must retain chronological placement. All 976 tests across the composer, IPC, image-protocol, correspondence, and backend-registry suites passed after the fixes.

## Notes

The existing recipient FIFO remains in-memory and does not survive an owner-process restart. Remote sender status remains the last confirmed result when later lifecycle information is unavailable. Oversized/unavailable remote attachment transfers fail before cancellation. Local attachment references retain the existing attachment-store lifetime.

All fixtures are contrived. No live queue or running user thread was modified. No headed visual pass or live federated/provider end-to-end test was run; ACP coverage exercises the shared queue implementation.

author: dev-connor
body:
## 배경

PR #40 에서 `resourceBundle` 이 `Contents/Resources` 를 **먼저** 보고 안 되면 `Bundle.module`(= .app 루트 → CI 빌드경로) 로 폴백하도록 했다. 요청에 따라 그 **2·3순위 폴백을 제거**하고 `Contents/Resources` 한 곳만 보게 정리한다.

## 왜 폴백이 불필요한가

`Bundle.main.resourceURL` 은 번들이 실제로 있는 디렉터리를 **양쪽 경우 모두** 가리킨다:

| 실행 형태 | resourceURL | 번들 위치 |
|---|---|---|
| 배포 `.app` | `Contents/Resources/` | ✅ 여기 |
| `swift run` (bare 바이너리) | `.build/<config>/` | ✅ 여기 |

폴백이 가리키던 두 후보는 배포본에서 **애초에 쓸 수 없었다**:
- `.app` 루트 → 거기 번들을 두면 codesign 이 `unsealed contents present in the bundle root` 로 서명을 거부(→ quarantine 시 "손상됨")
- 빌드 시점 하드코딩 경로(`/Users/runner/...`) → 사용자 머신엔 존재하지 않음

즉 폴백은 버그를 **가려 주기만** 했으므로, 번들이 없으면 조용히 넘어가는 대신 `fatalError` 로 크게 터뜨리도록 바꿨다.

## 변경

`resourceBundle` 을 `Bundle.main.resourceURL` 기준 단일 조회로 축소, 실패 시 `fatalError`. (AppDelegate.swift, +19/-14 — 대부분 주석)

## 검증

- **`swift run` 조건**: `.build/release/ConnorPet` 직접 실행 → 스프라이트/브리핑 정상 로드 (폴백 없이 동작 확인)
- **DMG 조건**: `make_app.sh` 로 번들이 `Contents/Resources` 에만 있는 ad-hoc 서명 `.app` 조립 후 실행 → 정상 로드

## 참고

이 변경은 **다음 릴리스(0.0.5)** 부터 반영된다. 이미 발행된 `v0.0.4` DMG 는 PR #40 의 3순위 버전이며 그 자체로 정상 동작한다.

author: florisvoskamp
body:
Forge treated reasoning effort as a single Forge-side dial. It was not one: it changed nothing about what the model ran at on most routes, and mesh scored every model as though it ran at its best-rated effort regardless.

Four things were wrong, and they compounded.

### 1. The per-effort benchmark data was fetched and thrown away

Artificial Analysis rates a reasoning model once per rung and names the rows `GPT-6 Astra (medium)`, `… (high)`, `… (max)`. `BenchmarkScores::insert` canonicalised the parenthetical away and kept only the highest-intelligence row. **356 of the 630 rows in the live feed carry an effort parenthetical**, so this discarded the effort dimension for most rated models in the catalog.

The real ladder for GPT-6 Astra, from the cached feed:

| rung | intelligence | coding |
|---|---|---|
| Non-reasoning | 47.8 | 76.2 |
| low | 49.3 | 75.7 |
| medium | 52.2 | **76.7** |
| high | 53.4 | **77.1** |
| xhigh | 54.3 | 75.9 |
| max | 54.7 | 76.9 |

Coding **peaks at high and falls at xhigh**, and medium lands within 0.4 of the top rung — so the collapse cannot be repaired by assuming the top rung is best either.

### 2. The effort pin did not reach the model on most routes

`grep effort` across all three codex transports returned nothing, and the CLI bridges never passed one — despite every binary documenting a knob (`claude --effort`, `agy --effort`, `codex -c model_reasoning_effort`). A pinned session ran at whatever the surface defaulted to while every readout reported the pin.

Worst on codex, where the two routes silently disagreed: the harness path passes `--ignore-user-config` and ran at codex's built-in default, while the text path inherited the user's own `~/.codex/config.toml`. Same model, same pin, two different real efforts.

### 3. Mesh could not choose the rung

Effort biased the ordering of models but was never itself a routing decision, and the score it ordered by was the effort-blind collapsed number.

### 4. The statusline reported the pin as though it were the truth

And in the most common state of all — nothing pinned — `W::Effort` returned `None`, so a statusline configured to show effort showed nothing while mesh quietly chose.

## What this does

Each commit stands alone:

1. **Keep the measured ladder.** `efforts_for` / `score_for_effort`; collapsed row unchanged, so every existing caller keeps its score.
2. **Make the pin real on every surface.** One `effort` module resolves a pin against each surface's ladder and returns the rung that will be sent *and why* — as-requested, clamped, no control, or nothing pinned. Clamps rather than drops, since dropping hands the turn back to the provider default. Unpinned turns are byte-identical, asserted directly.
3. **Show all three facts.** `[standard] codex-oauth::gpt-6-astra⟨med⟩ │ ⚙ mesh medium │ ◈ $3.28 │ ◆ Full` — provider dimmed, the model's own rung glued to its id, mesh's routing effort labelled separately.
4. **Route on (model, effort) pairs.** Cheapest rung not measurably worse than the best available; `/effort` becomes a ceiling; auto-effort on by default.

A coding turn on Astra now routes to **medium** instead of xhigh; a reasoning turn on the same model still routes high, because the two ladders genuinely differ.

## Scope and honesty

- Rung choice is **factored** (pick model, then pick its rung), not a joint search over pairs. A cheaper model at high effort beating a dearer one at low effort is not modelled.
- The selector does **not** optimise cost. What a rung costs is reasoning tokens burned, which the ladder does not carry; rather than invent that number it takes the cheapest rung that is not measurably worse. Measuring the real multiplier is the natural follow-up.
- `max` is excluded from codex's ladder: only claude's help documents it, and codex ships its `supported_reasoning_efforts` field null, so there is no authoritative list to read.
- `LiveEvent` is deliberately not widened; a remote observer shows no rung rather than churning a versioned wire contract for a display detail.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p forge-agent-mesh` — 283 passed
- `cargo test -p forge-agent-provider -p forge-agent-types` — 381 passed
- `cargo test -p forge-agent-tui` — 266 passed
- clippy clean workspace-wide; architecture size guard passes (three ratchets raised deliberately)

Tests use the six verbatim Astra rows from the live feed rather than a synthetic ladder — a made-up ladder is monotonic, and would let an implementation that assumes more effort is more quality pass while getting the real feed backwards.

One width regression was caught by an unrelated repo-name test rather than by any assertion of mine: the new cells silently clipped configured widgets on an 80-column terminal. Gated at 100/90 columns, after which both other statusline tests passed untouched.

author: bitwisecook
body:
## Summary

All seven code defects in #1412, the three contradicting doc comments, and the missing `tests/external/backend_constraints.tcl` overlay already landed on `rust` (#1795 lane `r6a-rename-interp`, and `d993e19`). The issue stayed open, and the docs still described the runtime as it *was*.

So this PR does three things: corrects the docs (that half carries `Closes #1412`), fixes six residuals the oracle exposed on the `$child` shorthand path — the same defect classes as the issue, on the path #1795 did not cover — and corrects a contract page whose statements are false.

### Why the shorthand diverged

`interp hide kid …` and `kid hide …` had separate implementations. C routes both through `ChildHide` / `ChildInvokeHidden`, so the fix extracts `hidectl_in` / `invokehidden_in` as `pub(crate)` owners in `cmd_alias.rs`, called from `interp_hidectl`/`interp_invokehidden` **and** `dispatch_child`.

Measured on tclsh 8.6.16 and 9.0.4 (identical throughout), before → after:

| # | case | before | after (matches C) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | `kid hide lst mylst` | `bad option "hide"` | succeeds |
| R1 | `kid hide` | `bad option "hide"` | `wrong # args: should be "kid hide cmdName ?hiddenCmdName?"` |
| R2 | `kid hide ::foo::bar` | **silently hid it** | `cannot use namespace qualifiers in hidden command token (rename)` `[TCL VALUE HIDDENTOKEN]`, command intact |
| R2b | `interp expose kid ::tok plain` | `cannot use namespace qualifiers…` | `unknown hidden command "::tok"` `[TCL LOOKUP HIDDENTOKEN ::tok]` |
| R2c | `interp expose kid tok ::plain` | `unknown hidden command "tok"` | `cannot expose to a namespace…` `[TCL EXPOSE NON_GLOBAL]` |
| R2d | `interp hide kid ns::nosuch tok` | `can only hide global namespace commands…` | `unknown command "ns::nosuch"` |
| R2e | `interp hide kid nosuch existingtok` | `hidden command named "existingtok" already exists` | `unknown command "nosuch"` |
| R3 | `kid invokehidden -global set g 9` | `invalid hidden command name "-global"` | `9`, `::g` set |
| R4 | `kid` | `…"interp cmd ?arg ...?"` | `…"kid cmd ?arg ...?"` |
| R4 | `kid eval`, `kid hidden extra`, `kid aliases extra`, `kid issafe extra`, `interp hidden kid extra`, `interp issafe kid extra` | **silently accepted** | correct `wrong # args` |
| R6 | `rename nosuch x` | errorcode `NONE` | `TCL LOOKUP COMMAND nosuch` |

R2b–R2e are all one rule: C resolves before it checks for a collision. R2d/R2e needed Missing-before-Collision in `hide_command`, and — not in the plan — symmetrically in `expose_command` (`interp expose kid nosuchtok set` → `unknown hidden command "nosuchtok"`).

Also fixed on the way: `is_global_command`'s hand-rolled `::` strip mishandled colon runs, so `interp hide kid ::::list tok` was refused where tclsh accepts it. That check now goes through the shared owner `tcl_cmd_core::namespace::qualifiers`, matching the VM and the shared-owner invariant rather than re-deriving the rule.

### Two claims in the issue and the contract are false

**The issue's item 5** says C rejects `-global` with `-namespace` (`cannot use -global option and -namespace option together`). **No such error exists on either release.** `-global` is `-namespace ::` internally and the *last option wins*: `-global -namespace foo` → `::foo::r`, `-namespace foo -global` → `::s`. The docs now state the measured behaviour and retract the claim explicitly.

**`command-binding-and-aliasing.md`** claimed self-rename is a no-op and that built-ins are protected. Both false: `rename pp pp` → `can't rename to "pp": command already exists` `[TCL OPERATION RENAME TARGET_EXISTS]`, and `rename return myreturn` / `rename error myerror` both succeed. There is no protected list, and `command_binding.rs` encodes none, so nothing downstream depended on it. That correction is commit `85eeaf9`, kept separate so it can be dropped in review.

## Validation

- [x] I ran relevant tests/checks locally and listed the exact commands.

```
cargo test --manifest-path runtime/rust/Cargo.toml
cargo test -p tcl-vm
make rust-check
```

All green, from a **cold rebuild** — the box hit ENOSPC mid-session, so the worktree's `target/` was deleted and everything re-run from scratch (an earlier `check-source-data` failure was the disk, not the change). `make rust-check` exit 0.

The **no-tommath** build was run too (`touch build.rs`, 500 lib tests): all 9 new tests pass there, and no new test script uses `if`/`while`/`for`/`incr`/`expr`, which are `#[cfg(have_tommath)]`. Both plan mutations caught their intended tests.

The full error sheet now diffs clean against tclsh 9.0.4 except three errorcodes deliberately left alone: the two `bad option` sites (`TCL LOOKUP INDEX option X`), which #1607 supplies, and `invalid hidden command name` (`TCL LOOKUP HIDDENTOKEN`), pre-existing and out of scope.

**One existing test was corrected — please review.** `rename_and_hide_error_shapes_and_lifecycle` hid `visible`, then hid it again expecting `hidden command named "visible" already exists`. Both oracles answer `unknown command "visible"` there: the source has already moved into the hidden table, so the resolve fails first. It only passed because the runtime checked the hidden table first — the very ordering bug R2d/R2e fix. The test now pins the oracle answer **and** re-creates the command to reach the genuine collision, so it covers strictly more than before.

author: copilot
body:
Clicking a product cell felt laggy: the yellow selection highlight was baked into each planogram face's canvas texture, and the selection key was global — so every click rebuilt the full texture (redrawing every product image) for **every face overlay of every gondola** in the scene.

Changes in `frontend/src/three/SceneEditor.tsx` (`PlanogramFaceOverlay`):

### Per-planogram selection key
- `selectedCellIdsKey` now only includes cells belonging to the overlay's own planogram (via `Selection.cells[].planogramId`, with a legacy `cellIds` fallback), so selections no longer invalidate unaffected overlays.

### Highlight rendered on a separate lightweight layer
- The yellow tint/outline is drawn on its own transparent `CanvasTexture`, displayed on a raycast-disabled plane just in front of the product plane:

```tsx
<mesh position={[0, 0, OVERLAY_Z_OFFSET / 2]} raycast={() => null}>
  <planeGeometry args={[planoW, planoH]} />
  <meshBasicMaterial map={highlightTexture} transparent depthWrite={false} />
</mesh>
```

- The heavy product texture memo no longer depends on the selection at all — a selection change now only draws a few rectangles instead of re-rendering hundreds of product images.
- Cell pixel-rect computation extracted to a shared `cellRectPx` helper used by both textures; highlight texture is disposed on change.

author: adamplatin123
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes cron create <schedule> [prompt]` failed with `unrecognized arguments` whenever a prompt positional was supplied, even a single quoted word (#102983):

```
$ hermes cron create "0 3 * * *" --name test-prompt-job --deliver local "Test prompt to see if positionals work"
hermes: error: unrecognized arguments: Test prompt to see if positionals work
```

Root cause (reproduced against the real top-level parse path): the `prompt` positional is declared `nargs="?"`. Plain argparse consumption sees the first option after `schedule` (`--name …`) and resolves the optional prompt as **absent** at that point; the trailing prompt token then becomes unrecognized, propagates up through the subparser chain, and surfaces at the top level (which is why the error banner showed top-level usage). It is not the subcommand-routing workaround or session-name coalescing — both were verified blameless.

**Reproduction note (version-dependent, likely why triage could not reproduce):** this is stdlib argparse behavior that changed in CPython 3.13. A minimal stdlib-only probe (top-level `--continue` nargs=`?` + `cron` → `create(schedule, prompt nargs=?, --name, --deliver)` + the issue's argv) yields `prompt=None, extra=['Test prompt']` on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 and parses correctly (`prompt='Test prompt'`) only on 3.13. The fix makes behavior identical on every supported version (3.11–3.13) instead of depending on the interpreter.

Fix: only the `cron create`/`add` leaf gets `parse_known_intermixed_args()` (the stdlib's supported API for positionals interleaved with options) via a small `parser_class` used by the cron subparsers. The top-level argv pipeline is untouched.

**Relationship to the earlier open #103027** (same bug, different site): that PR repairs the leftover token at the `main.py` routing layer but only accepts exactly one unknown (`len(unknown) == 1`) — a **single-word** prompt. The issue's original command carries a multi-word prompt ("Test prompt to see if positionals work") and still fails under that repair. This PR's leaf-parser fix handles single- and multi-word prompts uniformly (argparse's own intermixed consumption, not a hand-rolled token patch), keeps misspelled flags failing normally, and leaves the top-level pipeline untouched. If the maintainer prefers the routing-layer approach, it needs the single-token restriction lifted to actually close #102983.

## Related Issue

Fixes #102983

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/subcommands/cron.py`
  - `_CronActionParser`: an `ArgumentParser` subclass whose `parse_known_args` dispatches to `parse_known_intermixed_args` when the leaf opted in (subparser dispatch and intermixed parsing's internal second pass both still take the ordinary implementation)
  - `create` (alias `add`) is constructed with `intermixed=True`; every other cron sub-action keeps default parsing
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron_parser_builder.py` — regression tests through the real `_build_cli_parser` + `_parse_cli_args` top-level routing:
  - both issue command shapes parse: `args.prompt` receives the full multi-word prompt (and the single-word variant), `--name`/`--deliver`/`schedule` intact
  - `--no-agent --script` variant (no prompt) still parses
  - non-regression guards: other subcommands (`model`), bare top-level flags (`--version`), and the existing `-c` multi-word session-name coalescing behavior

## How to Test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_cron_parser_builder.py -q` → 21 passed
2. Before the fix, 4 tests fail, including both original issue commands
3. Manual: `hermes cron create "0 3 * * *" --name test-prompt-job --deliver local "Test prompt to see if positionals work"` now creates the job with the full prompt

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run the relevant test files and all pass (21 passed in `test_cron_parser_builder.py`; wider `tests/hermes_cli/` targeted runs green apart from known local socket/toolchain environment failures reproducible on unmodified `main`)

author: schmexs
body:
Fixes #1 — all three parts, in one change as the issue asked.

1. **A verifier.** `velstra_cloud_model::images::judge_signature`: Ed25519 (ring, already in the tree) over the digest line `sha256:<hex>`, base64, under keys the cell names with `--image-signing-key` (repeatable; `VELSTRA_IMAGE_SIGNING_KEYS` comma-separated). Verdicts: unsigned / verified / refused-with-reason. A cell with no key refuses every signature, as it did before.
2. **The node agent refuses to fetch** an image whose signature fails under its own keys, and with `--require-signed-images` one that has none; the reason lands on the guest that needed it. Same variables in a node's seed on NixOS.
3. **Admission and console, same commit.** The API stores a signature only when it verified and refuses one that did not at `spec.signature`; the blanket refusal is gone. Because nothing that failed is ever stored, the console's *Signature* column reads `verified` or `unsigned` and nothing else, and the image form has the field behind *Advanced*.

Docs: `rest-contract.md` (Signed images), `operating.md` §6b (making a key with openssl, signing the digest line, the flags), NixOS `controlPlane.imageSigningKeys`, `docs/openapi.json` regenerated, recorded shapes unchanged.

Tests: four in the model (verifies, wrong key, wrong message, no key, garbage, key parsing), three against the API (no key refuses; the cell's key stores and a stranger's is refused; a patch is judged over the digest it restates), the old "nothing verifies" test updated to the new sentence. Workspace tests, clippy and the console browser suite (92/92) are green.

이름 해소 봉인이 컴프리헨션 안의 왈러스를 오탐했다. `scripts/platform_db_migrate.py`

1. **`passwordHash` 列の復旧** — PR #1 のマイグレーション `drop_password_hash` を、新コードが本番に乗る前に手動適用してしまい旧ログインが 500 に。`restore_password_hash` で列を戻し済み（本番 DB 適用済み）。schema にも `passwordHash String?`（未使用）を残す。最終削除は別 PR。

4. **移行スクリプトに `--set-password`** — 旧アカウントのパスワードを設定するモード。

- ⚠️ **本番 DB は既にマイグレーション適用済み**（`restore_password_hash` 含む）。この PR のマイグレーションファイルは履歴合わせ用で、マージ後の `db:migrate:deploy` は no-op。

author: simolus3
body:
Exports in this package assume that `dart:io` not being available implies `dart:js_interop` being available.

When compiling Dart to WebAssembly without a JavaScript runtime (https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/53884), neither `dart:js_interop` nor `dart:io` are available. To make this package support that target, this exports the stub libraries whenever `dart:js_interop` is not available (instead of when `dart:io` is available).

Since the stubs don't actually import `dart:io`, this makes the package support that target.
