author: sanjaybnarayan
body:
The sweep that had covered twenty-four modules at 390px had never looked at Timeline, Chat's empty state, Investments with a portfolio in it, the assistant's field, or a subtle button on a quiet card. Each held a defect, and none of them was a layout fault.

### A heading that had never once stuck

`js/modules/timeline.js` sets its day heading `position: sticky` deliberately, with the reason written beside it — *"'3 March' above a run of changes is how somebody reads a history"*.

`.card--flush` carried `overflow: hidden`, there so a list's square corners stay inside the card's 22px radius. `hidden` makes an element a **scroll container**, and sticky resolves against its nearest one — so the heading was pinned to a box that does not itself scroll and rode off the top of the page with everything else.

| after scrolling 4,000px | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| day heading top | **−3,673px** | **60px** |
| covered by the app header | fully hidden | **0px** |

`overflow: clip` clips identically and creates no scroll container; 38 cards carry the class and clipping is unchanged for all of them. The other half was `top: 0` under an app header that is itself sticky and 60px tall — a heading parked behind the header is the same as no heading.

### The same absence, stated twice

Chat with nothing in it drew **"No conversations yet"** in its own card, and again 250px below inside the "Manage conversations" disclosure — same icon, same heading, above two buttons wording one act differently: *Start a conversation* and *Add the first conversation*.

The disclosure opened itself when there was nothing yet, and the comment saying why was true when written: it once held the only way to make a conversation. That was fixed later by giving the empty state its own button, and `section.openForm()` raises a **modal**, so it works whether the disclosure is open or shut. The `open` outlived its reason. Two comments in one file, each correct on the day it was written.

228px shorter, and it says it once.

### Two million percent, as the headline

    XIRR
    2117610.57%
    annualised

| | gain | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nifty index fund | 576.67% | 116,801.24% XIRR | *under a year* |
| Portfolio | +90.75% | **2,117,610.57%** | *not yet a year of transactions* |

The arithmetic is right — 576% over a short run genuinely extrapolates to that. What makes it a defect is where it sat: two lines below, the same card says *"3 of 4 holdings have no transactions recorded"*, and the card beneath says *"no interest rate is recorded"* rather than guess one.

**A rate is annualised over a year, or it is not offered** — the rule this application already applies when it refuses to compare a part-month of staff pay against a monthly agreement, and when it measures mileage only between two full tanks. Not a plausibility band on the output: a hand-picked ceiling would still pass a 900% figure built from eleven months while refusing a real one from a bad year.

Nothing true was withdrawn. The gains still read +576.67% and +90.75%; only the extrapolation is gone, and the screen says which of its two reasons it has for showing nothing.

### A placeholder that did not fit its own field

The assistant's field read *"Ask about spending, net worth, renewals, bills…"* — four examples naming what it understands, which needs **320px**. The field offers **182px** at a 320px viewport and 252px at 390px, the icon inside taking the rest, so it clipped at every phone width:

    Ask about spending, net worth, rene

The half that survived promised two topics; the half that did not was the point of the sentence. The six example questions below it carry that better.

### A button that was its own background

`.btn--subtle` paints itself `--surface-sunken`. `.card--quiet` paints its background `--surface-sunken`. **The same token** — so a subtle button on a quiet card was invisible by construction, not by accident.

| Insurance's "Open the estate review" | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fill against its own ground | **1:1** | 1:1 |
| edge against its own ground | **none** (alpha 0) | **4.58:1** light, **6.03:1** dark |

A 44px tap target sitting in a paragraph with nothing to say it could be tapped. Ten rules in `components.css` paint that token and twenty-six subtle buttons ship, so this was not one screen's bad luck.

The fix is this repository's own argument for the navigation bar — *"colour alone is not a distinction; the filled ground and the bar above the icon are both shape, neither needs colour to be seen."*

**`--border` was tried first and does not work.** A non-text part of a control needs 3:1, measured against all three surfaces in both themes:

| token | range | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--border` | 1.14 – 1.36 | no |
| `--border-strong` | 1.54 – 1.94 | no |
| `--text-faint` | 4.58 – 6.46 | yes |

### What the checks measure

Every one guarded so it cannot pass while measuring nothing.

- **The heading** is read as geometry against the app header's own box, and the guard *derives* how far the page must scroll from the heading's own position. The first draft asked for 1,000px, measured against a seeded household, and failed on this suite's 452px fixture — the guard catching its own check before it could pass for the wrong reason. Verified at six records that the defect and the fix are indistinguishable when nothing scrolls, which is exactly what the guard refuses.
- **The empty state** is counted by walking up to the nearest `details`, not by asking whether the node is visible: a closed `details` still reports a height and an `offsetParent` in this engine, so both of those measure nothing.
- **The rate** is tested from both sides in the node suite, since a rule refusing short spans is worthless if nothing is left that earns one. Mutation-proven: restoring the old predicate fails the first test and passes the second.
- **The placeholder** is measured against the field's content box at 320px, where it fails first — a check written at 390px would have passed the string that shipped.
- **The button** takes the better of fill and edge against whatever is actually behind it, walked up the tree because the button's own parent is usually transparent. Mutation-proven: removing the border takes the reading from 4.58 to 1.

### Gates

3251/3251 · **940/940 browser** (from 928) · 155/155 types · 5 lint rules clean · 64 class names · 3031 unrouted strings · 6 files over 800, none grown · 55 live doc numbers matching

author: jerry0022
body:
Every SC Companion product shipped the *identical* SCC monogram, so a taskbar full of SCC windows gave no way to tell which one you were clicking — while the PWA install icon, the Safari pinned-tab icon and the whole browser extension were still on the long-retired Verse-Compass mark. Three marks live at once, and none of them told the products apart.

The desktop app's brain-nebula artwork is now the master, vendored byte-for-byte into `public/icons/brand/scc-mark.svg`. Starscape and the Data Uploader are the **same drawing** with two surgical swaps: Starscape gets a four-point nova core and a single wide planetary ring, the Uploader an ascending data stream and orbits that break open where the stream exits. Same palette, same nebula, same star field.

**Colour is deliberately not the differentiator.** The desktop app's tray already uses hue for *state* — active / notification / error — so a red icon there has to mean "something is wrong", never "this is the uploader". Identity is carried by shape alone. That constraint drove the glyph choice: measured at 16px against the master's soft core, a crescent-lit planet collapsed into the same blob and a framed "vista" turned to mush, so both lost to the nova, which survives a 16px tray slot.

**Three size tiers**, because one drawing cannot serve 16px and 512px: the full artwork above 128px; a blur-free compact tier for 16–64px; and a tray tier that keeps the dark disc but adds a bright rim, so the disc carries the silhouette on a light taskbar and the rim carries it on a dark one. The tray geometry is the desktop app's own (StarOrga/Star-Citizen-Companion-App#1408) — with the nova and the data stream drawn larger than the master's core, which at 16px would otherwise collapse all three into the same dot.

## Also fixed, all found while wiring this up

- **Starscape's tray icon pulled the 32px entry out of the *app* ico** — i.e. the dark disc, invisible on a dark taskbar. It now embeds its own `starscape-tray.ico`.
- **`og:image`, `twitter:image` and `apple-touch-icon` all pointed at an SVG.** X, Facebook and iOS Safari silently ignore SVG in those positions, so the site had no working link preview and no working home-screen icon. Now a generated 1200×630 PNG card and a 180×180 opaque raster, with `summary_large_image`.
- **`/icons/**` matched no ngsw asset group** — the glob `/*.(svg|png|…)` is root-level only — so brand assets were served unhashed and could stay stale indefinitely. Added to the assets group, and the replacements got new filenames rather than overwrites.
- **`manifest.webmanifest` declared ICO sizes the file did not have.** The generated ico really carries all seven Windows sizes now.

## One generator instead of nine orphans

`npm run gen:brand-icons` replaces the single uploader-only script and nine binaries that had no source at all: `favicon.ico`, both PWA PNGs, all four browser-extension PNGs and Starscape's `.ico`. Its `--check` mode runs in `prebuild`, so a stale or hand-edited artifact fails the build — including the two inlined copies of the mark (boot splash, uploader header) that used to be hand-maintained duplicates. `public/icons/brand/family-sheet.png` renders the whole family at true pixel size so it can be judged in review.

## Verification

2146/2146 unit tests after merging the newer `main` in · production build · `cargo check` on the Rust app · mobile gate **GREEN** over 40 audits against this branch's own dist · a browser probe confirming every brand URL 200s with 0 console errors.

## After merge

Already-installed PWAs keep their old home-screen icon — the OS caches it at install time; only a reinstall refreshes it. The link preview needs one manual re-scrape via the Facebook Sharing Debugger and X Card Validator, which cache per page URL. `data-uploader` moves to 0.25.3 because electron-vite bakes the version into `__SC_TOOL_VERSION__` and this ship changes the binary's icons; the binary release itself is a separate `data-uploader-v0.25.3` tag.

author: jrnb2024
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the pre-existing hazard noted in #269's completeness lens. In the reusable `policy-check.yml`, "Build policy-check summary", "Check out SCP repo at workflow ref for schema lookup" and "Validate policy-check summary schema" are `if: always()`, and "Upload policy-check summary artifact" plus "Post policy-check read-back commit status" were gated only on the validation outcome. After any infra failure past the runtime checkout ("Install pinned OPA and Conftest runtimes", "Run shared policy-check invocation", a materialisation step), `output/findings/policy-findings.json` does not exist, `load_json` falls back to `[]`, and the red run still uploaded a zero-findings `policy-check-summary` and posted `N/M rules enabled, 0 disabled` on `scp/policy-check-readback`.

## What changed

- **"Render deny annotations and enforce threshold"** gets `id: enforce-threshold`. It now fails closed with SCP-E001 if the findings file is missing (`scp_policy_check_init_outputs` seeds it before any evaluation, so absence means the shared invocation never completed), and writes the step output `evaluated=true` only after the file has been loaded. Deny still exits 1, after the witness is written.
- **Summary upload, scorecard emit, read-back status** gain `steps.enforce-threshold.outputs.evaluated == 'true'`. A step that was skipped, cancelled, crashed on malformed JSON or found no file never writes the output, so the gate is shut in every not-run case. actions/runner processes `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` in a `finally` after the step handler (`src/Runner.Worker/ActionRunner.cs`), so the witness survives the deny exit.
- **Summary build and schema validation stay `always()`**: their SCP-E001 diagnostics (and #269's truthful install message) still surface on the infra path; only publication is gated.
- **ADOPT-001** read-back paragraph states the publication condition.

Correction to the premise: "Build scorecard emit" has no `always()`, so GitHub's implicit `success()` already kept it off the infra-failure path. Scorecard-emit adopters were not exposed; the clause on that step only makes the dependency explicit. The real exposures were the summary artifact and the read-back.

## The kill, observed

The step's script, extracted from the edited YAML and run locally with `GITHUB_OUTPUT` pointed at a file (exit codes echoed directly, no pipes):

| scenario | exit | witness written | annotation |
|---|---|---|---|
| findings file absent | 1 | no | SCP-E001 |
| findings `[]` | 0 | yes | none |
| one SCP-R-001 deny | 1 | yes | SCP-E003 + rule error |
| one SCP-R-030 deny (warn-baseline) | 0 | yes | `::warning` |
| malformed JSON | 1 | no | traceback |

`actionlint`: only the pre-existing SC2129 style note at line 472 (untouched). Instrument check: a copy with the step id misspelled in the three gates yields three `property "enforce-thresholdx" is not defined` errors, so a wrong id cannot pass lint. actionlint does not type-check output *keys*, so the key is spelled once in the step and three times in the gates, byte-identical. PyYAML parses the file; the three `if:` values load as single lines.

Selftest impact: fixture-pass and every fixture-scp-r-* invocation reach `enforce-threshold` with outcome success, write the witness, upload the artifact; stash jobs unchanged. fixture-fail denies, writes the witness, exits 1, still uploads; the aggregator's "Download fixture-fail summary", oracle comparison and "result must be failure when the oracle has denies" assertion are unchanged. The three fixture-scp-sha-validation failure fixtures and fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure fail before the runtime checkout, never reach the step, and the aggregator only asserts their result is `failure|cancelled`. No oracle changes; `validate-selftest-config`'s invocation count is unchanged.

**Not observed in CI:** no fixture fails *after* the runtime checkout, so the window this PR closes has no direct exercise on this PR. On today's failure-path fixtures validation already failed (no `.scp-runtime`). Once #269 lands (validation reads the lockfile from `_scp-workflow`), fixture-simulate-token-exchange-failure becomes the direct observation: its "Validate policy-check summary schema" step will succeed while "Upload policy-check summary artifact" and "Post policy-check read-back commit status" show `skipped`. Chip filed for a dedicated post-checkout failure fixture.

## Deliberate trades (please confirm)

- **Break-glass**: with `scp_bypass: true`, a failing "Enforce break-glass pairing gates" step now also withholds the summary and read-back (findings are complete at that point; the job is red with SCP-E004).
- **Stale rather than lying**: commit statuses are per-context and sticky. A re-run on the same head SHA that dies on infra leaves the earlier run's read-back in place instead of overwriting it with a zero-findings one. Noted in ADOPT-001.
- **`scripts/replay-canary.sh`** sets `observed_findings=-1` and skips the drift checks when the artifact is missing, so an infra-failed `deliberate-violation-pre` canary (conclusion FAILURE = expected) now reads OK instead of raising a (misleadingly worded) findings-drift regression. Not changed here (`scripts/**` is dispatch-gated); chip filed to treat an expected-but-missing artifact as REGRESSION.

## Relationship to #269

Independent hunks (#269: credentials step + validate-summary lockfile source; this PR: threshold step + three `if:` lines). Either merge order works. #269 is what makes the closed window reachable on the selftest's failure fixtures, as above.

## Review

Fast tier: one independent review (three lenses, read-only) on 6c8b0f5. Its MIN "outcome is a no-prior-failure witness, not an evaluation witness" and INFO "scorecard comment inverted" are fixed in a925699; its MAJ (replay-canary) and two MINs (break-glass, stale read-back) are recorded above. Verdicts: APPROVE_WITH_FINDINGS on all three lenses.

## R1 evidence

- correctness: Reviewer enumerated every step between the shared invocation and the threshold step (no `continue-on-error` anywhere in the workflow; the only `if:`s are skip-only: cosign install `!selftest-mode`, bypass-gate `inputs.scp_bypass`), so the threshold step runs iff no prior step failed, and the witness is additionally tied to loading the findings file (five local scenarios above). Implicit `success()` on the scorecard step confirmed against GitHub's status-check-function rule. Runner `finally` semantics for `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` verified in actions/runner source and exercised in CI by fixture-fail (a deny exit after the witness must still upload, or the aggregator's download fails).
- safety_bypass: Nothing is weakened: the gate can only remove publication, never turn a red job green; `threshold`, `scp_bypass`, `selftest-mode` and `simulate-*` inputs reach the threshold step through unchanged code; the missing-findings branch moves from silent exit 0 to SCP-E001 exit 1 (fail-closed). `attest-scorecard` (`needs: policy-check`, implicit `success()`) is unchanged. A non-deny failure of the threshold step cannot publish a bad summary: malformed findings also fail the summary build or the strict schema, so the validation clause still closes the gate.
- completeness_governance: All 24 selftest invocations analysed above; no oracle, invocation-count or stash change. Other consumers grepped: `scorecard-aggregator.yml` reads only `scorecard-emit`; the readback is not a required check (`docs/security/branch-protection.md`, `scripts/configure-020d2-required-check.sh`, live protection on main = `policy-check / scp/policy-check` + `check-invocation-log-entry`); `replay-canary.sh` consequence recorded with a chip. ADOPT-001 updated; OVERVIEW/HOME pipeline outlines make no "every run" claim. No `version-manifest.json` bump, matching #265 (the release ceremony bumps). SCP `audit_changed` (governance): GOV-002 (no enhancement spec) and GOV-003 (no docs/reviews evidence) waived for this PATCH-class CI fix per precedent #265 and

author: akira-toriyama
body:
## What

A sixth full-screen view, `X`: furrow's three maintenance passes on one screen.

- **archive** — the done tasks past the age guard (`furrow archive -r '' --json`, dry run; `older_than_days` echoed in the header)
- **tidy** — `done-deps` (open tasks with satisfied dep edges) and `unknown-keys` (shards carrying keys this furrow does not know), from `furrow tidy --json`
- **archived** — the archive store (`furrow ls -r '' --archived --json`), for `unarchive`

Every candidate is furrow's; ridge derives none (the fixture's memstore mirrors the rules for `-dump` and tests only).

**Writes**: `⏎` names the write in the header line (the exact id list an archive sends, the count a tidy class prunes, the one task a restore brings back), a second `⏎` applies, any other key cancels. `x` skips / includes an archive row — the write sends the **explicit ids on screen**, never the id-less form (which is the aged sweep over the board scope); an empty list is refused before exec (`board.ValidateSweepIDs`). All three writes are store-first through the funnel the epic overlay already used (`epicWriteOp` → `storeFirstWrite`), and the previews re-read off the same landing the board does (`sweepAfterWrite`).

## Measured (furrow v5.1.0, scratch store)

- `archive -r '' --json` (no `--yes`) → `{dry_run:true, older_than_days, repos, tasks:[ls rows]}`; by id without `--yes` is also a dry run
- `archive <open-id> --yes` → validation exit 2 (`only done-lane tasks…`); missing id → not-found exit 1; the whole list refuses
- `unarchive <id> --json` → array of `{before:null, after, changed:[], unarchived:true}`; a hot id exit 2, a miss exit 1 with `details.missing`, nothing restored
- `tidy --json` → `{applied, changed, done_deps:[{id,deps}], unknown_keys:[{id,file,keys}]}` (a class is absent when empty)
- `tidy --unknown-keys --yes` on an empty class → `applied:false, changed:false`, exit 0 — not a refusal; the adapter treats only "changed and not applied" as one
- Real board, read-only previews: ridge scope 4 archivable / whole board 289; tidy done-deps 13; 404 archived

## Headless

`-demo sweep` (at rest), `sweepconfirm` (archive gate, one row skipped), `sweeprestore` (restore gate on an archived row). Frames eyeballed at 200 / 240 / 400 columns; the suffix column (closed age, repos) stays aligned under CJK titles.

## Tests

- `internal/ui/sweep_test.go`: rows/cursor walk, open via `X`, skip → gate → cancel → apply → re-read → restore, tidy prunes the class, empty archive set refuses to arm, store-first refusal wording
- `internal/store/memstore/sweep_test.go`: preview rules, archive/unarchive round trip across Reload, tidy across Reload, the schema gate
- `internal/store/furrowstore/sweep_test.go` `TestContractSweepRoundTrip`: every shape above against the real CLI (bite-exempt like the rest of the contract suite; the bite is the ui/memstore tests)

`scripts/check.sh` green locally (lint 0, `-race` suite).

## Docs

README (Views: Sweep, Keys table, Verification), glossary (Sweep term, mode token ⟨SWEEP⟩, six full-screen views, store-first list), `provider.go`'s store-first section names the three new writes.

body:
## Summary

Completes B387, picked up from an earlier agent run that was killed mid-work by a shared session rate limit (its partial work — `onnx_ner_engine.py`, `shallow_parse.py`, `tests/test_torch_free_import.py` — was already committed on this branch at `34de043`). That agent chose `onnx-community/distilbert-base-cased-finetuned-conll03-english-ONNX` for NER and a hand-written shallow-parse chunker to replace spaCy's `noun_chunks`/dependency parse, but never reported Gate 0 and never finished the rest of the card's scope. This PR closes those gaps and finishes the card.

### Gate 0 — the three previously-open questions

**1. License (highest priority).** Verified directly via the HF API (`GET /api/models/elastic/distilbert-base-cased-finetuned-conll03-english`) that the *base* model's `cardData.license` is genuinely `apache-2.0` — the `onnx-community` mirror repo itself carries no license tag at all, so the base model is the real authority, not the mirror (the previous agent's header comment conflated the two).

CoNLL-2003 training-data provenance investigated separately: CoNLL-2003 annotations derive from Reuters RCV1 news text, distributed under a signed NIST/Reuters agreement. That agreement (per NIST's public description and the dataset's own HF card) gates **redistribution of the raw article text**, not use of statistical models fine-tuned on it. I could not obtain the verbatim agreement text (it's request-gated, not published), so I can't quote its exact restriction language — but:
- `elastic` (the fine-tuner, a real company) made an explicit, unchanged-since-2022 Apache-2.0 grant on the weights.
- This is not a one-off: `dslim/bert-base-NER` (MIT, ~2.1M downloads/month) is the same CoNLL-2003-trained pattern, in heavy uncontested commercial use for years.
- This is the same general "is a trained model a derivative work of its training corpus" ambiguity that applies to essentially every pretrained NLP model (including fastembed's own MiniLM lineage, already in this codebase since B355) — not something specific to this model.

I judge this clears the bar for proceeding, but it is **not** a legally settled question, and given the active patent filing + enterprise customer, I recommend actual counsel review rather than treating my judgment as final. If that review disagrees, the clean-provenance fallback I identified is `urchade/gliner_small-v2.1` (Apache-2.0, trained on synthetic `pile-mistral-v0.1` data, no Reuters/CoNLL lineage) — but it has no pre-built ONNX export today, so switching would mean converting it ourselves and re-running the whole Gate 0 + Gap 2 process.

**2. Extraction agreement (measured, not assumed).** Compared the new ONNX+shallow-parse pipeline against a real spaCy `en_core_web_md` baseline (installed in a throwaway venv) over 46 sentences drawn from this repo's own backlog/docs text (its own ingestion history) plus a handful of representative dev-decision sentences.

- **Entity spans** (exact character offsets): precision 0.434, recall 0.695, F1 0.534 (95 spaCy entities, 152 ONNX entities, 66 exact matches). The new pipeline finds strictly more entities (CoNLL NER catches things spaCy's NER missed entirely, e.g. "Reuters", "NIST"; the chunk fallback fires more liberally since shallow_parse's function-word list is narrower than spaCy's real POS tags — e.g. gerunds like "keeping"/"becoming" leak through as junk chunks that spaCy correctly folded away). A specific fixable regression: the tokenizer treats `/` as a hard boundary, so `FROM/TO` splits into three tokens where spaCy kept it as one chunk.
- **Relations**: 20/46 sentences produce byte-identical relation triples; +8/46 are identical except spaCy retains a leading article ("a valid token") that shallow_parse strips by design (61% effectively equivalent); 6/46 spaCy found a relation the new pipeline missed; 5/46 the new pipeline found one spaCy missed (some genuine gains — spaCy's simple `dobj`-only dependency walk never handled "X depends on Y" prepositional-object patterns; some noise, e.g. one case where a stray adverb got treated as a chunk); 7/46 both found relations but head/tail differ.

Full sentence-by-sentence diff was generated and reviewed; not attaching the raw dump here but happy to share if useful.

**3. Offline container story.** `onnx_ner_engine.get_engine()` already resolves `local_files_only=True` unconditionally at runtime (stricter than fastembed's `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`-gated approach — there's no local-dev reason for NER to ever hit the network at inference time) and respects `HF_HOME` for the cache location exactly like fastembed's `_get_fe_model()` does — verified directly by pointing `HF_HOME` at a throwaway directory, downloading, and confirming offline resolution + a clear `RuntimeError` on a cache miss.

**However:** `deploy/Dockerfile`, which `backlog/B385.md` lists as already built and checked off (multi-stage, pre-baked FastEmbed ONNX weights, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`), **does not exist anywhere in this repository** — confirmed via `git ls-tree` on both `main` and this branch. I can't verify an actual container build because there's nothing to build. This module's contract (HF_HOME-driven cache, offline-only at runtime, clear failure on a miss) is ready for whatever Dockerfile eventually bakes it in; recreating B385's missing artifacts is out of scope here and flagged separately.

### Implementation

- `step1_ner.py`: NER via `onnx_ner_engine.get_engine()`, noun-chunk-equivalent fallback via `shallow_parse.shallow_chunks()`. `extract_entities()`'s `(doc, entities)` return contract is preserved — `doc` is now a `shallow_parse.ParsedText` instead of a spaCy `Doc`.
- `step1b_relations.py`: `extract_relations()` takes `ParsedText`, no longer a spaCy `Doc`. Nearest-shallow-chunk-before/after-verb heuristic replaces the `nsubj`/`dobj` dependency-tree walk, never crossing a sentence boundary (`.`/`!`/`?`/`;`).
- `pyproject.toml` / `requirements.txt`: `spacy` removed entirely; `onnxruntime`, `tokenizers`, `huggingface_hub` declared explicitly (the first two were already transitive via fastembed; `huggingface_hub` per the task's own instruction since this module imports it directly).
- `campy/cli/install.py`: `install_spacy_model()` → `install_ner_model()`, downloads the ONNX model instead of the spaCy model.
- CI / `campy.toml` / `sidequests.toml` / `smithery.yaml`: the spaCy download step is replaced with an ONNX model download step, not simply deleted — tests exercise the real model end-to-end (zero-mock, required by `tests/patent_claims/`), so CI still needs a one-time fetch, just ~66MB instead of ~40MB+torch. The vestigial `spacy_model` config key is documented as unused rather than removed, for config back-compat.
- `tests/conftest.py`: removed the Python-3.14/pydantic-v1 spaCy compatibility shim entirely (spaCy is gone, so there's nothing to shim). This also removed the `SPACY_AVAILABLE` skip gate — 5 tests in `test_loop.py` and all of `test_orchestrator.py` had **never actually run** in this environment (permanently skipped since spaCy never worked on Python 3.14); they now run for real and pass.

### RSS finding — reported honestly, not absorbed into "done"

- **Cold** (`import campy.brain_daemon`, nothing else touched): ~45 MB.
- **Warm** (after actually calling `extract_entities()` once — matching what a real daemon does on its first message): ~193-209 MB.
- **Fully warm** (NER + fastembed embeddings both actually invoked): **~382 MB, not the <80MB this card's acceptance criteria assumed.**

This is not a regression this card introduced. The card's own problem statement quotes "kuzu+fastembed: 76.1MB" as the baseline — that number turns out to be **import-time only**. fastembed's model is constructed lazily; nothing loads until the first real `.embed()` call. Measured directly: fastembed alone reaches **~266MB** warm RSS, not 75.1MB. For a fair, same-methodology comparison, I also measured spaCy the old way (loaded and run once, in a throwawa

## Summary

Three events were visible only as log lines; each now has a meter, a panel, and where it warrants one, an alert.

- **`chat_lease_conflicts_total`** — incremented in `ConversationLease.acquire` where the lease refuses, registered at zero in its constructor. The `Budget refusals (429) and overlaps (409)` panel on *Customer service* now carries it as a second query beside the 409 line, so the two can be seen to agree. The `ConversationConflicts` rule stays on the request timer (it also catches a refusal that never reached the handler); its comment now names the direct counter.
- **`chat_knowledge_unavailable_total`** — incremented in `HttpKnowledgeSearch`, which gets a `MeterRegistry` from `RemoteClientsConfiguration`. That client exists only in a `chat` process, so `ChatService` registers the same counter at zero (via a static factory on `HttpKnowledgeSearch`, the one definition of the name and description), which keeps `DashboardMetricsTest` honest in `all` mode. New stat `Knowledge unavailable, last 10 min` on *Customer service roles*, and a new **`KnowledgeUnavailable`** alert, `increase(...[5m]) > 0`, severity critical, with a paragraph on why.
- **`corpus_import_seconds{outcome="imported"|"already_present"}`** and **`corpus_documents`** — the timer wraps `CorpusImporter.importIfMissing` (lock wait included; both outcomes pre-registered); the gauge reads the recorded count for the bundled version from the database on each scrape, since with replicas the process that imported is usually not the one being scraped. The bundled version is memoised because reading it parses the corpus file. New stat `Corpus import` on *Customer service roles* showing documents and the import duration (sum/count, guarded so an absent series reads 0). The Pipeline row moved down one line to make room.

Docs: three rows added to the "This repository's" metrics table in `docs/observability.md`, the dashboard and alert descriptions updated, alert count eight to nine in both READMEs.

Tests: `ConversationLeaseTest` (counter at 0, then 1 after a refused acquire, own `SimpleMeterRegistry`), `CorpusImporterTest` (`@AutoConfigureObservability`; gauge 0 and both timers 0, then one `imported` and 36, then one `already_present`), `TopologyParityTest` (reads `chat_knowledge_unavailable_total` from the chat process's `/actuator/prometheus`: 0 before, >= 1 after the knowledge process is stopped). `DashboardMetricsTest`'s metric regex now also matches a `_documents` gauge so the new panel is held to the same rule.

`k8s/` and `scripts/` are untouched; the `k8s/observability/` overlay being added concurrently re-renders from these files after merge.

author: jaryl
body:
## What

Phase F **UI** on top of the M9 personal-state engine (#36) — **playlists, starred, and a recently-played row**, all decrypted on this device. The node never sees plaintext (Invariant 6).

Builds on the engine PR #36 (now merged).

## Pieces

- **`PersonalStateCoordinator`** — the app-facing façade over `SpaceSession` + `SpaceRegistry`. Folds every openable non-role space as a playlist (heyarr-core's device-gateway convention), creates the role spaces (starred / history / reading) **lazily on first write**, and exposes star / add / record / reading in one place. Reached via `AppViewModel.personalState(node, credential)` — **null, and every list empty, when the device is not enrolled** (playlists are device-side encrypted state, not a server list).
- **Playlists** — `Route.Playlists` / `Route.Playlist`, `PlaylistsScreen` (list + create) and `PlaylistScreen` (items resolved to works, **play through the audio queue**, remove, rename), reached from a "Your playlists →" link on Home. A playlist is **id-named** by default (`Playlist <space id>`, matching the gateway) with an optional local rename.
- **Star + add-to-playlist from any Home card** via a ⋯ / long-press menu (`PosterCard` gains optional actions — the shared music grids are unaffected), plus a **Starred row** and a **Recently-played row** on Home. `PersonalActionsViewModel` is **one shared instance per node+credential**, so a ★ anywhere and the Home rows read/write the same state; the `AddToPlaylistDialog` overlays whatever screen fired it.
- A play on Home / in a playlist **records to the history space** (feeds the recently-played row and the gateway's `recent` list).

## Tests

`PersonalStateCoordinatorTest` (playlists exclude the role spaces, a star creates the role space, history/reading round-trip) and `PlaylistFlowTest` (the ViewModels over the **real engine + in-memory node fake**, Unconfined). **364 unit tests green + `assembleDebug`.** Updates CLAUDE.md.

## Acceptance (phone-gated, owed)

Create a playlist on the phone, see it via `heyarr device gateway` Subsonic on the Mac, and vice versa — the engine's `SpaceRegistry` records the starred/history space ids the operator points `--starred-space` / `--history-space` at.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Per-track / per-episode ⋯ actions inside `AlbumScreen`/`WorkDetailScreen` (Home cards + the detail flow cover "any card" today); wiring the readingpos space into the reader's resume (the coordinator method exists; `ReaderActivity` still resumes from the local Locator + server `page`).

Closes #35.

author: clintongormley
body:
## SP-3a — Fiscal-record sync lane (fiscal module's sync enrolment)

First of four SP-3 slices (module system). Enrols the six fiscal tables onto the ordered sync lane so a subscriber becomes a **verbatim** copy of the immutable, hash-chained ledger — H2's fiscal-record lane, realised on the post-SP-2a/2b module-enrolment model.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-module-sp3a-fiscal-record-lane-design.md` · **Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-05-module-sp3a-fiscal-record-lane.md`

### What it does
- **`FISCAL_ENROLMENT`** (package-owned, `@waitron/fiscal-verifactu`): `registros_facturacion` **insert-only** (grant-enforced) + `registro_sif`/`cadenas`/`envios`/`envio_flujo`/`acks` watermark-upsert, all on the ordered lane. Verbatim — nothing recomputes a huella; `entorno` copies as opaque bytes.
- **Fiscal owns its capture DDL** (`0014_fiscal_sync_capture.sql`), calling sync's `sync_capture()` as an SPI (owner decision: fiscal independent, API-only). This adds a **`fiscal → sync`** module edge, so the manifest + `ALL_MODULES` were reordered so fiscal migrates **last**.
- **Graph-honesty guard extended** to detect the `sync_capture` SPI edge (the existing `CREATE TRIGGER … ON` matcher couldn't see it, since fiscal's triggers are on its own tables).
- **SP-2b module-version park** wired for fiscal.

### Gates (real-Postgres, proven-by-deletion, in `apps/server`)
Verbatim apply + immutability-on-mirror + idempotent · mutable-table upsert non-regression · FK-order 23503-defer + reserved-SIF (R2) coexistence · env handshake (both directions) + module-version park · a mirror issues no AEAT submission · capture on the six triggers · inmutabilidad re-run.

### Notable
- **Fiscal invariants preserved**: immutability honored on the subscriber (a stray mutation as the apply role → `42501` (grant); `WT001` only for a bypassing superuser — verified on `postgres:18-alpine`); `contadores_instalacion` not enrolled (installation numbers never reused); one-database-per-environment.
- Because `0014` calls the sync SPI, fiscal's migrations no longer run standalone, so the package's PGlite test harnesses migrate the full manifest (a **dev-only** `@waitron/migrations` dep — prod dependency graph stays acyclic).

### Out of scope (inherited, tracked elsewhere)
Secondary→survivor transport path, promoted-node-files-the-tail (R3), disposal-guard convergence gap, bulk backfill. Other SP-3 slices: vocabulary (3b), gated-provisioning seam (3c), backup/restore hook (3d).

## Qué arregla (cabo suelto 1 de ORCA-369)

El presupuesto de auto-recovery de 60s podía dejar el pane sin ninguna recuperación propia.
`RemoteRuntimePtyRecoveryState.schedule()` limpia `pendingRetry` **antes** de invocar el retry
(`remote-runtime-pty-recovery-state.ts:98-100`) y además saca la instancia del set
`scheduledRecoveries`. Si el deadline vencía con ese intento en vuelo, el pane latcheaba
`disconnected` sin nada parkeado:

- `retryNow()` → `false` (no hay `pendingRetry`)
- `online` / `onSystemResumed` → no lo alcanzan: `retryAllRemoteRuntimePtyRecoveriesNow()` itera el
  set del que la instancia ya salió
- Solo el botón Reconnect (`transport.retryRecovery()`, que solo mira la fase) lo revivía

Hay una segunda forma del mismo defecto: un intento que **nunca armó** backoff — el resubscribe que
arranca en `scheduleResubscribeAfterTransportClose` — tampoco dejaba nada para el cutoff.

## Cómo

- `inFlightRetry`: el retry que `schedule()` acaba de disparar (y el que revive `firePendingRetry`)
  queda guardado, invisible para todo lo demás — `hasParkedRetry` sigue en `false` mientras el
  intento está en vuelo, así que ni `retryForConfirmedReconnect()` ni el registro pueden
  dispararlo dos veces.
- `parkInFlightRetry()`: **solo** el cutoff lo promueve a `pendingRetry` y re-inscribe la instancia
  en `scheduledRecoveries`. A partir de ahí `retryNow()`, `online` y `onSystemResumed` funcionan
  igual que con un backoff parkeado (epoch fresco, ladder reiniciado).
- `setAttemptRetry(epoch, retry)`: cubre el intento que no arma timer.
  `scheduleResubscribeAfterTransportClose` registra el mismo thunk que ya usa en su rama `catch`.
- `discardPendingRetry()` ahora también descarta el `inFlightRetry`, para que el wait single-shot de
  `waitForHostSessionAttachRetry` no sobreviva al cutoff como trabajo revivible falso.

## Verificación

Test de repro primero, **rojo contra main**, en los dos niveles:

- `remote-runtime-pty-recovery-state.test.ts` — el cutoff con el intento en vuelo: `retryNow()` y
  `retryAllRemoteRuntimePtyRecoveriesNow()` devolvían `false` / `0`.
- `remote-runtime-pty-transport-stream-reconnect.test.ts` — extremo a extremo con el transporte:
  el `terminal.resolvePane` del resubscribe se cuelga, pasan los 60s, y `retryAll…` (el camino de
  `online`/`onSystemResumed`) tiene que producir un subscribe nuevo. Contra main: `expected 1, got 0`.

Guardas agregadas: el intento en vuelo **no** es revivible antes del cutoff (ni por `retryNow`, ni
por `retryForConfirmedReconnect`, ni por el registro), y un single-shot descartado no revive.

`npm test`: `Tests 1 failed | 59934 passed | 137 skipped`. El rojo **no es de este cambio** —
corrí la suite completa dos veces y falló un spec distinto cada vez
(`src/shared/remote-runtime-shared-control-connection.test.ts` con `Relay control queue exceeded its
bounded capacity` + error de WebSocket; después `src/main/native-chat/transcript-watch-liveness.test.ts`).
Ninguno de los dos importa nada de este diff, y los dos pasan aislados (28/28 y 7/7). Es contención
de la máquina bajo la corrida completa, no una regresión; queda anotado.

`pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --config config/oxlint-code-quality-type-aware.json src config tests --deny-warnings`: verde.
`npm run lint` y `npm run typecheck`: verdes.

## Cabo suelto 2 — anotado, no perseguido

`Client never mirrored host tab` falló **una vez**, antes del recovery, con 0/5 en las baseline
legibles. Una ocurrencia no es una tasa: queda registrado acá para que la próxima vez sea el segundo
dato y no el primero.

## Review (una ronda, lente `review-reliability`, riesgo medium)

Sin blockers. Confirmó lo que importa: el retry en vuelo no es disparable antes del cutoff
(`hasParkedRetry`, `retryNow`/`firePendingRetry` y el registro lo ignoran), no hay leaks
(`clearRetryTimer` lo limpia en todas las salidas), y la rama de `hasParkedRetry` en
`transport.ts:1521` no se puede activar de nuevo porque el mismo `onChange` del cutoff pone
`autoRecoveryWindowSpent = true`.

Tres warnings quedan abiertos, ninguno bloqueante:

1. `transport.ts:1696` — la rama no-web de `resubscribeAfterTransportClose` no revalida
   `recovery.isCurrent(recoveryEpoch)` después del await (la rama web sí, en `:1645`). Un intento
   de epoch gastado puede rebindear el handle y llamar `subscribeToHandle(E)` en paralelo con el
   revivido. Behavior-activated: la carrera ya existía por el botón Reconnect; ahora `online`/resume
   la alcanzan sin gesto del usuario.
2. `transport.ts:824` — el closure de `retryMirrorAttachLater` ahora queda en `inFlightRetry`
   durante los 15s del poll de inventario, así que el cutoff lo parkea y un `online` puede
   replayearlo mientras el primer attach sigue corriendo: `onPtySpawn` y `registerShutdownHandlers`
   dos veces para un pane. Ventana acotada a 15s.
3. `remote-runtime-pty-recovery-state.test.ts:361` — el test "ignores an attempt retry from a
   superseded epoch" no discrimina: sus asserts son ciertos por construcción aunque se borre la
   guarda `isCurrent` de `setAttemptRetry`.

## Residual conocido

`begin()` seguido de un intento en vuelo que no arma timer sigue sin cubrir en tres sitios:
`subscribeToHandle` tras un republish del host (`remote-runtime-pty-transport.ts:1536` y `:1548`) y
`transport.connect` dentro de `retryRecovery()` (`:2580`). Ahí el pane sigue dependiendo del botón
Reconnect si el intento se cuelga hasta el cutoff. Es la misma clase de defecto, con thunk distinto
por sitio; no lo metí en este PR para no ampliar el diff.

Refs ORCA-369.

author: antimprisacaru
body:
## Problem

Staging any file under `packages/dynamic-forms/src/` that imports from `@ng-forge/dynamic-forms/internal` fails the lefthook `pre-commit` `lint` step:

```
error  '@ng-forge/dynamic-forms/internal' import is restricted from being used by a pattern.
no-restricted-imports
```

218 files in the core package import from `/internal`, so this blocked commits across most of the package. It was worked around once with `LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=lint`.

`nx run dynamic-forms:lint` passed on the same files, and so did CI.

## Cause

The exemption already existed in the root config as `ignores: ['packages/dynamic-forms/**']`. ESLint 10 resolves the config file relative to the file being linted rather than the cwd, so the same config array gets loaded through two different base paths:

| Invocation | Config loaded | Base path | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nx run dynamic-forms:lint` (passes `--config <project config>`) | project | workspace root | glob matches, rule exempt |
| `pnpm eslint packages/dynamic-forms/src/x.ts` (the hook) | project | `packages/dynamic-forms/` | glob matches nothing, rule fires |

Confirmed with `--print-config` on a core file: `@angular-eslint` rules are present in both cases, so the project config is what loads either way. The only difference is the base path the relative `ignores` glob resolves against.

This also means the hook is no longer running at root scope; it already picks up per-project configs. Routing it through nx would have hidden a config bug and made every commit lint whole projects, so the config is fixed instead and `lefthook.yml` is untouched.

## Change

Path-based scoping inside a base config that nested configs import is fragile for this reason, so the exemption moves to where it is base-path independent:

- `eslint.config.mjs`: drop the `ignores` glob, and record in the comment why the path form does not hold.
- `packages/dynamic-forms/eslint.config.mjs`: turn `no-restricted-imports` off for its own sources with `files: ['**/*.ts', ...]`, which matches under any base path.

## Verification

- Hook end to end: staged 3 core files importing `/internal` plus both configs, `lefthook run pre-commit` exits 0 (2 pre-existing warnings in `dynamic-form.component.spec.ts`).
- Core file passes under both bare `eslint` and `eslint --config`.
- Guard still bites: a temporary `packages/dynamic-forms-material/src/__guard-probe.ts` importing `/internal` errors under both invocation styles. Probe deleted afterwards.
- `nx run-many -t lint --skip-nx-cache`: 23 of 23 projects successful.

author: jasonmcintosh
body:
## Summary

`rosco` and `clouddriver`'s `Dockerfile.ubuntu` (`ubuntu:resolute`) arm64 builds are broken: `ubuntu:resolute` ships a GNU tar patched for CVE-2025-45582, which now extracts via `openat2()`. The QEMU version pinned in `.github/actions/publish-docker/action.yml` (`qemu-v7.0.0-28`, pinned as a workaround for an unrelated segfault bug, `docker/setup-qemu-action#198`) predates QEMU's `openat2` support, so every emulated `linux/arm64` build fails during helm/kustomize/helmfile/gcloud-sdk extraction with:

```
tar: ...: Cannot open: Function not implemented
```

## Fix

Swap `bsdtar` (via `libarchive-tools`) in for GNU tar in the two affected Dockerfiles. `bsdtar` doesn't use `openat2`, so it sidesteps the incompatibility without touching CI topology or the QEMU pin.

Verified locally against the exact pinned `qemu-v7.0.0-28` image: reproduced the failure with GNU tar, then confirmed `bsdtar` succeeds for `get-helm-3`, the piped kustomize/helmfile extraction, and the gcloud-sdk tarball extraction.

## Status

This is a backup/fallback fix. The preferred fix (bumping the QEMU pin itself to `qemu-v10.2.3-68`, which appears to resolve both this bug and the original segfault bug it was pinned to avoid) is being pursued separately off `main`. Opening this as a draft in case that path doesn't pan out.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI run on this branch builds rosco and clouddriver's ubuntu-variant arm64 images successfully

author: qoega
body:
`getProfileEvents` builds a fresh `ThreadIdToCountersSnapshot` map for each response and stores one aggregate entry under key `0`. The previous code used `operator[]`, which default-constructed a full `Counters::Snapshot` before move-assigning the real snapshot into it.

This changes the insertion to `emplace`, so the map node constructs the moved snapshot directly. The key is inserted into a new local map, so the duplicate-key behavior is unchanged for this path. If allocation or construction fails, the exception still propagates before `last_sent_snapshots` is replaced.

Local public-build measurement from the object-cost audit showed that the old path created one redundant `Counters::Snapshot` temporary per call. With the measured public build, one snapshot backing allocation was `14,336` allocator-usable bytes.

- Performance Improvement

Reduced allocation work while reporting `ProfileEvents` snapshots by constructing the snapshot map entry directly.

`npm audit fix` without `--force`. package.json is untouched. Twenty-two lockfile entries moved within their declared ranges.

## Closed: seven of the nine

| Package | Was | Now | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tar (root copy) | 7.5.13 | 7.5.22 | critical |
| brace-expansion, four copies | 1.1.14, 2.1.0, 2.1.2, 5.0.5 | 1.1.18, 2.1.4, 2.1.4, 5.0.9 | |

| nanoid | 3.3.15 | 3.3.18 | |
| tmp | 0.2.5 | 0.2.7 | |

The other moved entries are transitive companions of those (nodemailer, libmime, mailsplit, caniuse-lite, postcss 8.5.16 to 8.5.28, and so on). Nothing was added or removed.

## Not closed: two of the nine, and why

npm reported a compatible fix for the `tar` and `@capacitor/cli` copies nested under `@capacitor/assets`. There is none. `@capacitor/assets` 3.0.5 is its latest release and pins `@capacitor/cli` ^5.3.0; that line's newest release, 5.7.8, still carries tar 6.2.1, and no 5.x cli or 6.x tar closes the advisory. Moving them needs either an override forcing `@capacitor/assets` onto cli 8 (untested against its code) or dropping `@capacitor/assets` from devDependencies and relying on `npx` at generation time, as `docs/IOS_APP_STORE.md` already suggests. Both are decisions rather than bumps, so they are left for you.

## Guard

`tests/audit-floors-are-held.test.ts` reads the lockfile, which is what `npm ci` installs, and holds every copy of the nine packages at or above the release that closed its advisory, per major line. The two unfixed copies are named in the test with their exact versions, so the moment either changes the file goes red and the exception gets looked at again. Mutated twice: mailparser set back to 3.9.14, and the excepted cli copy moved to 5.7.9. Red both times.

## Verification

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci --ignore-scripts` | exit 0 |
| `npm audit --audit-level=high` | 18 findings down to 10; remaining high or critical: next, postcss, sharp, @capacitor/assets, and the two copies above |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 |
| `npx vitest run` | 0 (335 files, 5529 passed, 1 skipped) |
| `npm run build` | 0 (the `unpdf` import.meta warning is pre-existing) |
| `npm run test:audit-guards` | 0 |

No test exercises mailparser directly, so 3.9.20 was smoke-tested on a synthetic multipart .eml: subject, sender, date, the plain-text and HTML bodies, and a PDF attachment all came back as expected. Dash and emoji sweep with a positive control, then clean on the new test.

Reproduction note, as on #31: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` leaves sharp 0.32 without its binary; `npm rebuild sharp` before running the suite locally.

body:
The README is the public front page of a repo whose pitch is community curation. It opened with
two sections addressed to us instead.

## What came out

**"Architecture and the asset inventory"**, which was the *first* section, above Contribute.
Governed assets, ADR-003, dependency contracts, and "Check it before assuming a table is
unused" — an instruction to a maintainer auditing tables. `docs/architecture/` covers
`assets.yaml` across four files, so nothing is lost.

**The "Maintainer & internal reference" `<details>` block**, a third of the file. Everything in
it is already in `AGENTS.md` (directory map, skills, maintainer operations) or
`docs/operations/`. It had also drifted: it said *"Eight skills in `skills/`"* against thirteen,
and listed them individually, so it needed re-editing every time a skill landed.

One pointer to `AGENTS.md` and `docs/architecture/` replaces both, and does not rot.

Contribute is now the first section. 191 lines to 140, no prose rewritten — the edit is
structural, applied by script so wording is byte-identical.

## plans/

Gitignored. It is session state: dated, superseded weekly, and addressed to us rather than to a
contributor. `REVIEWER-PROMPT-2026-09-05.md` was committed in #501 so a cloud run could read it,
which was a real need — a cloud routine clones the repo, so local-only does not reach it. That
run has finished, and the file supersedes its own predecessor by design, so it goes back to
local `plans/` (preserved there, not lost).

The rule going forward, recorded in `.gitignore`: durable decisions are promoted to
`docs/architecture/` as an ADR; reusable procedures become a skill in `skills/`; everything else
stays local.

## Two promotions considered and dropped

I had proposed promoting two local plans into the repo. Checking showed the repo already
absorbed both during the build:

## What

More things that move, and a few that actually respond to a click.

GitHub READMEs strip JS, CSS and `<video>`, so the realistic surface is: `<details>` drawers (genuinely interactive), animated SVG, mermaid, and links. This PR leans on all four.

### New animated SVGs (`assets/`)

Self-hosted rather than pulled from another badge service — the existing snake workflow already proves repo-served animated SVGs render fine through camo, and these can't rate-limit or 404 the way the vercel-hosted generators do.

| file | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `house.svg` | a dot walks home, street lamps light as it passes, the windows come on, mmWave rings pulse out of the house |

author: regenscheid
body:
Mathematical cryptanalysis work can be diverted into full scheme assessments, repeated background checks, and paper audits before the unresolved mathematics is developed. Fixed five/two limits and a cheap-falsifier admission gate also constrained research proposals. This PR revises the actual workflows and their shared references for mathematical research supporting cryptographic standards.

The updated discovery workflow distinguishes a requested research proposal from development of a selected question. It removes the fixed five/two limits, separates agenda breadth from active work, preserves unresolved prerequisites and conditional results, and recognizes supporting lemmas and precise obstructions as progress. A quick experiment is useful when informative; it is not required before mathematical development can begin. The router, completion contract, scheme-analysis entry, both domain orchestrators, and domain research handoffs now distinguish this work from a complete assessment.

Paper verification remains rigorous. `verify-claim` checks whether an assigned claim in a paper or argument is correct. Source interpretation and use of a published ingredient do not automatically trigger that audit. Finding a statement in a source establishes its attribution, not its correctness. The verifier's conflicting new-source requirement is removed: independence concerns the error challenged, and a separate derivation can use the same specification. Previously checked compatible inputs can be reused; fresh verification remains available when requested.

The literature extractors now distinguish attributed quantities from independently checked values. The repeated quantitative guardrails in 88 domain skills require appropriate accounting for new or independently verified quantitative conclusions while allowing reuse of compatible checked inputs. Cost and reproduction skills retain their rigor within the assigned task.

The mathematical-development skill supports alternative representations, actual derivations beyond an outline, conditional results, and continuation from supplied partial mathematics. Existing statistical guidance is directly available without formalization; its new reference distinguishes exploration, selection, confirmation, zero-event limits, low statistical resolution, and scoped negative results. Shared reporting guidance separates work status, evidence, review, coverage, and contribution without adding a project store or changing attack-record schemas.

Contribution guidance distinguishes routine parameter applications, elementary corollaries and direct derivations, new evaluations, substantive extensions, and potentially new methods. It asks for the chain from known ingredients to the conclusion and the additional substantive step, if any. A separately named statement, independent derivation, or absence of an exact catalog entry does not establish originality. Recognizing routine reasoning does not require an exhaustive priority search; mathematical novelty and practical significance remain separate. Important parameter-specific findings need not introduce a novel mechanism, and catalog absence does not establish priority. Catalog-reading guidance consumes the companion catalog's four editorial teaching notes through its existing MCP reads.

Earlier commits also correct finite-evidence interpretation, negative-control logic, discrepancy diagnosis, the subset-minimum bound direction, stale runtime assumptions, four repeated bibliographic records, and 63 unshipped reference footers. The offline scorer distinguishes format/loading evidence from research progress.

The orchestrator now supplies its own research judgment after delegated cryptanalysis, across proposals, source work, modeling, computations, mathematical development, and assessments. Its primary responsibility is to identify material omissions, premature stopping, connections across findings, and overlooked significance. The dedicated reviewer handles correctness checks; an accurate subagent report can still be narrow or undervalue an important finding. The orchestrator must explain what it sees beyond the submitted answers and incorporate justified implications into the synthesis, using established checks rather than repeating the reviewer's job. New inferences retain proportionate evidence requirements. Shared guidance is linked from the research entry points and both domain orchestrators, outside their mathematical-assignment sections.

The final consistency pass also permits compatible checked baselines in the scheme and domain callers, scopes the source-class inventory to assessments, removes automatic citation-audit routing from `crypto-review`, and corrects the inference that an unresolved citation must be fabricated. `verify-claim` no longer describes looking up an assertion as sufficient for checking its correctness. The two deliberate imported-tree changes were reviewed and accepted while preserving source hashes.

Validation on the final local changes: 162 skills audited with zero errors or warnings; all 151 imported trees verified; all eight edited skill entry points pass quick_validate; five evaluator regressions pass; git diff --check passes. Source provenance, skill identifiers, and domains are unchanged. The original fourteen-case fixture is unchanged, with six supplemental synthetic delegation cases in two separate fixtures. Three test mathematical review; three isolate research judgment after already reviewed findings: overlooked significance, a missed cross-report connection, and premature research closure. These bounded fixtures do not measure open-ended creativity.

Behavioral findings: no live comparison was executed. The CScience launcher fails with a missing runtime module. Claude Science 0.1.43 is running, but the browser tool denied localhost access because its admin-enforced policy could not be verified; no workaround or harness change was attempted. The reconstructed middle-condition prompt is explicitly labeled as reconstructed, as authorized by the user. Matched model/tool/resource settings, verified skill loads, and repeated runs remain required before claiming improvement. See `tests/local-host-evaluation-20260905.md` and `tests/evaluation-contract.md`. Canonical bibliography generation and a full passage-support audit remain unfinished.

Scope: no Claude Science changes, project-knowledge infrastructure, physical-security expansion, automatic catalog submission/publication, or attack-record schema changes. Registry identifiers and domains remain unchanged. The existing draft PR is updated for review; nothing is merged or deployed.

author: einlanzerous
body:
One bullet in `CLAUDE.md`'s Mechanics section, placed directly under the branch-naming rule it depends on.

## The rule

When a ticket turns out to need more than one PR, it is split into **sub-tasks before the work starts** — not delivered as a run of PRs all leading with the parent's key. Switchyard's hierarchy already carries it; nothing was using it.

## Why it belongs in this file rather than in a transcript

CLAUDE.md is the shared prefix every agent inherits, and it already argues this case about status: *"nobody should have to scroll a session transcript to learn where things stand"*. The same holds for a working agreement — a rule stated once in a session is a rule the next agent does not have.

Two reasons beyond hygiene, both of which the surrounding bullets already establish:

- **Attribution.** Branch names lead with the ticket key *so per-ticket spend attributes correctly*. Three branches named `CANT-18-*` bill three different pieces of work to one row, and the estimate that comes out is not about anything.
- **Boundaries.** The working agreement turns on decisions being written down at ticket boundaries *as they happen, never batched to the end of an epic*. A ticket that quietly grows into three PRs has moved its own boundary; the sub-task is what puts it back.

For a Mode B ticket the split is proposed in the plan and approved with it. **CANT-18's re-cut this session is the first ticket to carry that on its face.**

## Evidence

`./verify.sh` green on this branch — 22 steps, 41 vectors across all three runners, `CATENARY_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set so CANT-19's `log_seq` commit-ordering property ran rather than skipped. Docs-only diff, one insertion.

Closes CANT-81.

author: qoega
body:
`ActionLock` move construction currently delegates to move assignment. That works, but it makes construction take the assignment path, including an unnecessary lock attempt on an empty left-hand side.

This constructs the moved weak owner directly. `std::weak_ptr` move construction is specified to leave the source empty, so the moved-from `ActionLock` destructor will not release the counter after ownership has moved. The added tests cover moving a live lock and moving an already-expired lock. Standard reference: https://eel.is/c++draft/util.smartptr.weak.const#8

Local constructor-level measurement from the public object-cost audit showed the low-dependency move-construction case decreasing from about `3.0 ns` to `1.1 ns`. This is intentionally a small cleanup; no server-level latency claim is made.

author: hairyf
body:
Closes #187

## Implementation

React port of VueUse's `usePreferredContrast` (`source/vueuse/packages/core/usePreferredContrast/`):

- `packages/core/src/usePreferredContrast.ts` — `usePreferredContrast(options?: ConfigurableWindow)` returning a plain `ContrastType` string (`'more' | 'less' | 'custom' | 'no-preference'`) backed by three `useState` flags, resolving in upstream priority order (more > less > custom). A single self-contained `useEffect` creates all three `matchMedia` queries — `(prefers-contrast: more)`, `(prefers-contrast: less)`, `(prefers-contrast: custom)` — syncs each `matches` and subscribes to every `change` event with `{ passive: true }` (mirroring upstream's `useMediaQuery` + `useEventListener`); cleanup removes all three listeners. Non-function `matchMedia` is guarded; SSR never touches `window` during render (server default: `'no-preference'`).
- `packages/core/src/usePreferredContrast.test.tsx` — 9 deterministic vitest-browser-react cases with a per-query fake-MediaQueryList stub (matches flag + change-listener registry + dispatchable change): initial value per query state (`it.each` over more/less/custom/none), change events flipping the value (act + expect.poll), priority when several queries match, unmount removing all 3 listeners, non-function `matchMedia` fallback, custom `window` option, and exact query strings asserted.
- `packages/core/usePreferredContrast/index.md` + `demo.tsx` — docs page (category Browser, DemoContainer, Type Declarations, Source section) and React demo port of upstream `demo.vue`.
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` — barrel export inserted in ASCII sort order.

## Divergence notes

- The Vue `computed<ContrastType>` return becomes a plain string derived from three `useState` flags, so components re-render on media query changes (React-style plain value, per repo conventions).
- Upstream binds listeners via `useMediaQuery`/`useEventListener`; here the three `matchMedia` queries are inlined in one `useEffect` with cleanup for all of them.
- The initial `matchMedia().matches` sync happens in the mount effect instead of during setup, so SSR renders `'no-preference'` without touching `window` — matching upstream's pre-mount value (query refs start `false`).
- `ConfigurableWindow` is declared in-file but NOT exported: `useOnline.ts` already exports the identical interface and the barrel re-exports both modules, so a duplicate export would collide (TS2308).
- Upstream's `ContrastType` name is kept and exported (unique in the barrel); upstream's `useMediaQuery` `ssrWidth` branch is not applicable to the inlined `prefers-contrast` queries (no width media features).

- **client.go** (3 lines): `a auth` -> `an auth` x2; `a optional` -> `an optional`; `a empty` -> `an empty`
- **project.go** (2 lines): `fetchs` -> `fetches` x2; `a organization` -> `an organization`
- **events.go** (3 lines): `a event` -> `an event`; `a issue` -> `an issue` x2 (plus the `latest`/`oldest` fix above)
- **organization.go** (2 lines): `quote` -> `quota`; `There is not way` -> `There is no way`
- **stat.go** (1 line): `tetting` -> `getting`
- **datatype/stacktrace.go** (2 lines): `a exception` -> `an exception` x2; `olds` -> `holds`

### Notes for reviewers

- The `a empty` -> `an empty` change in `client.go` is inside the error text `fmt.Errorf("Endpoint can not be a empty string")`. It is the only change outside a comment. I grepped the repo -- no test asserts on that string.
- Deliberately **not** changed: the exported field `SymboleAddr` in `datatype/stacktrace.go` and its `json:"symboleAddr,omitempty"` tag. It is misspelled, but it is an exported identifier and the tag must keep matching Sentry's own wire field name, so renaming it would be a breaking API change rather than a typo fix.
- The same misspellings appear in files outside this change (`team.go`, `userfeedback.go`, `datatype/message.go`, and some `_test.go` files). I kept this PR to the files listed above to stay reviewable; happy to extend it if you would prefer a single sweep.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.3.0): pnpm 12.3

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.2.1...v12.3.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Every context-aware global command (`node`, `deno`, `bun`, and the shims created with `pnpm shim add`) is now a native executable on every platform, so environment variables whose names are not valid shell identifiers reach these commands. On Windows, `<name>.exe` replaces the `.cmd` and `.ps1` shims for them. Shims written by earlier pnpm 12 releases are migrated on the next global install or self-update.

- `pnpm remove` and `pnpm update` now accept `--trust-lockfile`, `--no-trust-lockfile`, `--trust-policy`, `--trust-policy-exclude` and `--trust-policy-ignore-after`, the same flags `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` take, so the supply-chain settings can be overridden for a single run. `pnpm remove` verifies the lockfile against the active policies the way `pnpm install` does, and `--trust-lockfile` skips that pass for every entry, not only the package being removed.

  `pnpm` now also honors `--config.trust-lockfile=<value>`, and accepts the bare `--trust-lockfile` / `--no-trust-lockfile` spelling on the commands that previously took the setting from the config file alone.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm add <local directory>`, `pnpm add <local tarball>`, `pnpm add file:<path>` and `pnpm add <tarball URL>` work again. A specifier given without a `<name>@` prefix is no longer read as a registry package name and rejected with `ERR_PNPM_PACKAGE_MANAGER_ADD_RESOLVE_LATEST` [#​14437](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14437).

- Fixed `pnpm deploy --legacy` ignoring `allowUnusedPatches` supplied through `--config.allow-unused-patches` or the `PNPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_UNUSED_PATCHES` environment variable [pnpm/pnpm#14450](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14450).

- Fixed `pnpm install --lockfile-only` writing a lockfile that referenced a missing peer-suffixed snapshot when an npm-aliased dependency took part in a cyclic peer dependency graph. The following `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` failed with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` [#​14449](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14449).

- `pnpm config` now accepts `-g`/`--global`, `--location`, and `--json` before its subcommand [pnpm/pnpm#14421](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14421).

- `pnpm dedupe` now converges in one pass when it re-resolves a lockfile created by pnpm 11, so a second run no longer changes the lockfile [#​14455](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14455).

- Fixed detached child processes being terminated on Windows when another program launches `pnpm` directly, without a shell, as `nr` from `@antfu/ni` does [#​14447](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14447).

- Fixed `pnpm docs <package>@<version>` ignoring the requested version. It now opens the selected version's homepage and reports a missing version instead of opening the package-level homepage [pnpm/pnpm#14428](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14428).

- Sped up installs in large workspaces. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is now read while the workspace projects are being discovered [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- Fixed filtered and recursive `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` hanging when a script reads from the terminal. Interactive prompts work again in a script that pnpm never runs alongside another one, such as a single `--filter`ed project, `--workspace-concurrency=1`, a dependency chain, or a task declaring `concurrency: 1` [#​14397](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14397).

- Fixed false unmet peer errors for auto-installed peers in linked workspace packages.

- Fixed npm global installs on Windows so the PowerShell shims invoke `pnpm.exe`.

- Fixed `pnpm with current <command>` when global options precede it, such as `pnpm --workspace-root with current --version` [pnpm/pnpm#14413](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14413).

  A short-option cluster that mixes a global flag with an option owned by the command, such as `pnpm -ro dist pack-app`, is now parsed like the same options written after the command.

  An option written before the command name is now reported as an unknown option unless that command accepts it, instead of being taken for the command to run. `pnpm -P exec echo` and `pnpm -z exec echo` fail the way `pnpm --tag next exec echo` does.

- Apply pure insertions in zero-context patches at the correct line instead of one line early.

- Improved peer dependency resolution performance when many packages reuse the same peer ranges.

- `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` now follow local actions and reusable workflows referenced with GitHub's self-repository syntax (`uses: $/.github/actions/setup`) when looking for outdated GitHub Actions, the same way they follow `./` references.

- The `pnpm install --help` descriptions of `--prod` and `--dev` no longer claim that the flags take precedence over `NODE_ENV`. pnpm does not read `NODE_ENV` when selecting which dependency groups to install [#​14445](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14445).

- Sped up installs in large workspaces. The check that decides whether the lockfile needs updating no longer compares every project against every lockfile entry [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- Sped up dependency resolution in large workspaces that use `link:` dependencies [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- On Linux, pnpm now resolves registry hostnames through the system resolver (`getaddrinfo`), as it already does on macOS and Windows and as pnpm 11 did. Previously, an `/etc/resolv.conf` containing an option the bundled pure-Rust resolver did not recognize, such as `options no_tld_query`, made pnpm ignore the configured nameservers and silently query Google's public DNS instead [#​14469](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14469).

- Sped up dependency resolution in large workspaces. The resolver builds fewer lookup keys for each dependency [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- `catalogMode` and `--save-catalog` no longer move a local path, tarball, or `workspace:<path>` specifier into a catalog. Such a specifier is resolved against the project that declares it, so one catalog entry cannot mean the same directory for every project that references it [#​14437](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14437).

- Sped up installs in large workspaces. The workspace dependency graph is now built once per run instead of twice [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- Sped up writing `pnpm-lock.yaml` in large workspaces [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14352).

- Fixed non-frozen installs through a pnpr server failing instead of regenerating a conflicted lockfile.

- `pnpm update --interactive` renders its checklist the way pnpm 11 does. Group headings and column headers are separators the cursor skips instead of checkboxes that select nothing. The columns of one group line up with the next. `a` toggles all and `i` inverts the selection. The confirmed sele
