author: fernandoalmeidapinto
body:
## Contexto

O deploy de homol do ms-omr **funcionou** no merge do #1 (run [33983635736](https://github.com/vcnafacul/ms-omr/actions/runs/33983635736) — `DEPLOY_HOMOL success`). O erro `can't connect without a private SSH key or password` veio do run do **#2**, que o GitHub auto-marcou como merged e disparou com a versão *antiga* do `ci-homol.yml` (ainda com `key: DEPLOY_KEY_HOMOL`). Nenhum secret está faltando ou errado para homol.

Este PR fecha as lacunas que sobraram.

## O que muda

**`ci-prod.yml` (novo)** — o ms-omr era o único repo sem workflow de produção. Espelha exatamente o de `api`/`ms-simulado`/`form`: push de tag `[0-9]*` → `BUILD_AND_PUSH` (`:<tag>` + `:stable`) → `DEPLOY_PROD` (SSH por senha) → `CREATE_RELEASE`. Sem etapa de build de app antes do Docker — a imagem Python se resolve sozinha no Dockerfile.

**`ci-homol.yml`** — nomes de step e aspas do `docker login` iguais aos do `ci-prod`.

**Scripts de deploy** — dois bugs reais:

- shebang era `#/!bin/bash` (typo). Vira comentário, e o script roda no shell default em vez do bash pedido.
- `docker rm -f` / `docker rmi -f` sem guarda. No primeiro deploy a imagem não existe e o `set -e` abortaria antes do `docker run` — o log do run #33983635736 tem o `Error response from daemon: No such image`. Só não quebrou porque o exit code veio 0; não dá pra contar com isso.

**`subir_ms_omr.prod.sh` (novo)** — versão de prod do script: puxa `:stable` (a tag que o `ci-prod` publica) e usa limites maiores.

## Servidor de homol mudou

Homol não é mais a Oracle VPS `168.138.157.99`. Agora é uma **VPS Hostinger `85.31.61.20`, 1 vCPU / 4GB**, separada da de produção. `api-vcnafacul` e `ms-simulado` já tinham sido atualizados (`Deploy em Homolog (Hostinger)`); o ms-omr tinha ficado pra trás — corrigido aqui, junto do `deploy/README.md`.

Com 4GB a RAM deixa de ser o aperto; o gargalo vira a CPU, já que **o vCPU é único** e dividido com api/ms-simulado/redis. Como o OMR é CPU-bound, sem limite uma leitura monopoliza o núcleo e a API engasga junto:

```
--memory 450m --memory-swap 900m  --cpus 1.0    (Oracle, ~954MB / 2 vCPU)
--memory 1g   --memory-swap 1500m --cpus 0.75   (Hostinger, 4GB / 1 vCPU)
```

`OMR_MAX_WORKERS=1` continua certo — com um núcleo não há o que paralelizar.

## Antes de taggear prod

`DEPLOY_HOST_PROD`, `DEPLOY_USER_PROD` e `DEPLOY_PASS_PROD` ainda não existem no repo. O `ci-prod.yml` só dispara em push de tag, então até lá fica inerte — mas a primeira tag falha sem eles.

## Fora do escopo

O `vcnafacul-form/.github/workflows/ci-homol.yml` também ainda diz `Deploy em Homolog (Oracle VPS)`. É só o nome do step (não afeta o deploy), mas vale um PR lá.

author: smartenok-ops
body:
Fixes #3599 (the protocol-rejection half).

## Problem

Clients that send their *preferred* MCP protocol version in the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header of post-initialize requests — instead of the negotiated one — get every `tools/list` / `tools/call` rejected with `400 "Unsupported protocol version"` and never see the injected Paseo tools.

- **Codex CLI >= 0.148** does this and does not retry, so a Paseo-managed Codex agent silently loses the whole injected tool surface (`create_agent`, `notifyOnFinish`, everything).
- **Claude Code >= 2.1.257** sends the same non-conforming header but recovers after one rejected request, which is why Claude agents look fine while Codex agents are broken.
- The bundled `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.29.0 (and the current latest 1.30.0) advertises versions only up to `2025-11-25`, while these clients speak `2026-07-28`. No SDK release accepts that header today, so the daemon cannot negotiate or tolerate it without help.

## Fix

The header is a post-handshake sanity echo, not a negotiation point: `initialize` already negotiates down to a version this server supports, and the stateless agent MCP transport serves every request independently. So in `runAgentMcpRequest`, when the header value is not one the SDK advertises, drop it (log a `warn`) and let the request proceed. Advertised values pass through untouched.

Two implementation details worth flagging:
- The check is against the SDK's own `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` import, so when the SDK is eventually bumped to know `2026-07-28`, this path simply stops firing for it.
- The header must be stripped from **both** `req.headers` and `req.rawHeaders` — the SDK's node-to-web-standard adapter (`@hono/node-server` `getRequestListener`) builds the fetch `Request` from `rawHeaders`, so deleting only the parsed headers has no effect.

## QA evidence

Against a production daemon (Linux x86_64, daemon 0.7.1, `daemon.mcp.injectIntoAgents: true`, Codex CLI 0.153.3), probing `/mcp/agents` directly with raw JSON-RPC:

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize` with `protocolVersion: 2026-07-28` | 200, negotiated `2025-11-25` | 200, negotiated `2025-11-25` (unchanged) |
| `tools/list` with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` | **400** `Unsupported protocol version` | **200**, full tool list |
| `tools/list` with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25` | 200 | 200 (unchanged) |
| `tools/list` with no header | 200 | 200 (unchanged) |

After applying the same change on the live daemon, a Paseo-managed Codex orchestrator session regained the injected `mcp__paseo__*` tools and subagent finish notifications started arriving; the daemon log shows no further `Unsupported protocol version` errors.

## Tests

- New e2e regression test in `agent-mcp.e2e.test.ts`: `initialize` with a never-advertised version (`2999-01-01`) must still negotiate down to an advertised version, and a following `tools/list` carrying that version in `MCP-Protocol-Version` must return the tool list instead of the 400. Reverting the fix makes this test fail with exactly `expected 400 to be 200`.
- `agent-mcp.e2e.test.ts`: the new test passes; the two pre-existing failures (`create_agent auto-injects paseo MCP by default and can be disabled`, `create_agent injects a loopback MCP URL...`) fail identically on unmodified `main` — not affected by this change.
- `bootstrap.smoke.test.ts`: 21/21 pass.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.server.typecheck.json --noEmit`: clean.

Tested on Linux x86_64 only (headless daemon); I did not test macOS or the desktop app.

author: convenientlymike
body:
The agent-facing capstone of the wake-reliability work.

Delivery of DMs is now a **mechanism** (v0.7.0) and visibility is **automatic** (v0.8.0). But two steps are irreducibly the agent's job — a hook physically cannot call the Monitor tool: **arming** the watcher, and **acting** on a DM once received. Compliance is the only lever left for those, so the managed `CLAUDE.md` stanza is where to amplify it.

## Changed
- **Rewrote the managed stanza into a compliance amplifier** for exactly those two steps:
  - **"ARM your inbox watcher first thing each session"** — explicit first action, with the precise Monitor-tool invocation (`persistent: true`, `timeout_ms: 3600000`), and a note that the `⚠ FLEET WAKE NOT ARMED` re-nudge (v0.8.0) fires every turn until done.
  - **"A FLEET DM is a TASK, not an FYI — ACT on it"** — delivery is guaranteed regardless of arming (arming only changes *latency*); so read it, do what it asks, reply with the result. Never merely acknowledge — an unactioned DM stalls a waiting agent.
  - Points to `fleet.sh monitors` for reachability before relying on a wake.

## Fixed
- **`init` no longer re-dirties `.claude/settings.json` every run.** The checked-in file was compact one-line arrays while `init` emits pretty-printed JSON, so each run produced a whitespace-only diff (drift that masks real changes). Committed the installer-canonical pretty form → **`init` is now byte-idempotent** on settings.json (verified: two consecutive runs = identical output).

author: psvampa
body:
Six ways this tool could answer "nothing changed" without having looked, plus
the coverage that keeps them closed. Every claim below is measured against the
real glibc clone; the CHANGELOG carries the detail.

## The six

| # | What it did | Could it move a verdict? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Printed `C.UTF-8` under "cannot affect an existing index", then said nothing about it at all on the other pair | **Yes** |
| 2 | Step 5's hand-written file list was the ceiling of what it read; `linereader.h` and `elem-hash.h` changed over 2.34..2.39 unseen | **Yes** |
| 3 | Discarded unreadable blobs, silently shrinking the `copy` graph | Latent |
| 4 | A failed `git` was indistinguishable from an empty diff | **Yes** |
| 5 | Files with no `LC_COLLATE` block counted, never named; a gained block invisible | Latent |
| 6 | A run of 5+ dots was not read as an ellipsis range | Latent |

The two that matter most are 1 and 4. `C.UTF-8` is the default in most
containers, which makes it the database collation, which puts every
`text` column without an explicit `COLLATE` behind it — and PostgreSQL cannot
warn either, since `collversion` is NULL for anything starting with `C.`. And #4
is not hypothetical: it happened on this clone mid-session
(`could not fetch <oid> from promisor remote`).

**No published verdict moved.** The affected-locale sets are unchanged. What
changed is their standing: the RHEL9→RHEL10 clearance of `ko_KR` used to rest on
not having looked at two files, and now rests on having read them.

## What backs it up

- **111 tests**, stdlib only, three layers. Without a glibc clone the git-backed
  layers skip with a reason and the rest still runs.
- **Validated by mutation.** Every fix was reverted on purpose to confirm some
  test fails. That found three tests that guarded nothing — including one where
  the verdict was computed correctly and then thrown away, with the whole suite
  green.
- **Provenance.** The audit reads a third-party mirror and a git tag is a mutable
  pointer. Step 1 now prints the commit id behind each tag and its signature
  state; an invalid signature aborts. The suite pins the three tags, so a moved
  tag reports itself as a moved tag rather than as a count mismatch.
- **CI** runs the full suite on a freshly cloned glibc and **fails if any test
  was skipped** — green-because-nothing-ran is the exact failure this repo exists
  to catch.

## What is still not covered

Said plainly, because "tests pass" must not be read as "the audit is correct":
the SQL template has no automated coverage and is half the method; the empirical
confirmation on real nodes is irreplaceable; distro backports are by definition
absent from upstream tags. See `tests/README.md`.

No badge, deliberately.

body: ## Why PR 3 of the web-console data-diet series (after #727 compression/cache headers and #730 client refetch discipline). Two payloads were still fat on the wire for a phone on cellular: - `GET /api/v1/bootstrap` returned every agent's thread lists (up to 200 active + 200 archived rows per agent). Live fleet: 187 KB of a 219 KB response; nothing in the agent rail needs other agents' threads, and the client re-fetched the selected bucket anyway. - `GET /api/v1/threads/:id` returned the newest 100 messages with every tool result, subagent transcript and provider telemetry event inline. A 4-message tool-heavy thread was 231 KB raw, 211 KB of it tool-call result bodies; ~10 KB per thread was telemetry the console never renders. ## What **Bootstrap** — `?sourceId&archived&limit` (default 50) returns exactly one thread bucket plus `threadsSourceId`/`threadsNextCursor`; fallback is the source of `currentThreadId`, then the first online agent, then the first agent at all. Agent summaries are unchanged. The thread-list route default drops to 50. The client passes its selection scope on every bootstrap and seeds only the returned bucket and its cursor. **Thread events** — every thread-scoped `thread.changed`/`threads.changed` now carries `{thread}` (removals keep `{threadId, removed: true}`), so the sidebar stays fresh with zero fetches; `agents.changed` from a pin/unpin carries `{sourceId, pinned}` and is applied locally (external-review follow-up from #730). **Transcript shaping at the service boundary** — telemetry parts outside the allowlist the console reads (`usage_update`, `cron_run`, context usage/compaction/boundary, anything usage/cost-labelled) keep their position but lose `data`; tool-call and subagent `args`/`result` over 4,096 chars ship as a preview with `resultTruncated`/`resultBytes` (`args…` likewise; `structuredResult` and AskUser untouched); `GET …/messages/:messageId/tool-calls/:toolCallId` returns the full part; `?full=1` disables shaping; thread detail and message pages default to 30 messages (max 100); the per-conversation cost figure in the console now sums that 30-message window. Adversarial task reviews with fix rounds on both tasks, then a whole-branch review; residual nits recorded for the client sync PR (repaired tool calls are re-truncated by the next refresh until the per-thread cache merges them; docs-sync for the new route/flags lands with the series). https://claude.ai/code/session_01HYkKrNWwZpX6pBxT1pw7sB --- ## Summary by cubic Shrinks the web console's two largest payloads by 78-96%: the bootstrap now carries one thread bucket instead of every agent's threads, conversation reads are shaped for the browser with large tool outputs truncated behind a load-full control, and thread events carry summaries so the sidebar updates without refetches. - `GET /api/v1/bootstrap` now accepts `sourceId&archived&limit` (default 50) and returns one bucket plus `threadsSourceId`/`threadsNextCursor`; it falls back to the current thread's agent, then the first online agent, then the first agent. - Thread-scoped `thread.changed`/`threads.changed` events now carry `{thread}` (removals keep `{threadId, removed: true}`), and pin/unpin emits `agents.changed` with `{sourceId, pinned}`. - Conversation reads drop `data` from telemetry parts outside the console's allowlist and truncate tool/subagent `args`/`result` over 4,096 chars with `resultTruncated`/`resultBytes`; author: bob-ionis[bot]
body:
`wspr-download.service` has been red since 2026-05 and nobody trusted it. **The cause is structural, not incidental.**

`generateFileList` enumerates through the **current month** (`-end` defaults to now), so the in-progress month is **guaranteed to 404** until wsprnet finalises it. This tool has gone red at the start of *every single month*, by design. When wsprnet stopped publishing entirely after 2026-05, the red became permanent — 2026-06 through 2026-09 all 404, exit 1 every run.

Three months of a unit reporting **upstream's** state correctly, in the exact register reserved for **our** breakage, is how an alarm gets tuned out. It cost real time today too: the failure reads as a download bug, and only pulling the archive directory index shows wsprnet simply has not published since May.

## The rule

A 404 is never something a retry can fix, so it must not gate the exit code.

- `errNotPublished` sentinel, returned from both the HEAD and GET paths
- `stats.Missing` counted separately from `stats.Failed`, so *"upstream has no data yet"* cannot masquerade as *"our download broke"*
- The summary **names** the unpublished months — "which months are missing" is the operator's actual question, not how many
- Exit non-zero **only** for failures a retry could plausibly fix

## The gap does not go unwatched

Bronze-table staleness in the health check is the correct signal for "we are missing WSPR data", and it fires today (`wspr.bronze` stale since 2026-05-22). That is a **data-freshness** alert — which this is — rather than a **process-failure** alert, which it is not.

## Verification

Live, the exact failing scenario:

```
[wsprspots-2026-06.csv.gz] not published upstream yet
...
  Failed:     0
  Missing:    4 (not published upstream)

  Not published upstream (4) — nothing to retry, wsprnet has not released these:
    wsprspots-2026-06.csv.gz  wsprspots-2026-07.csv.gz
    wsprspots-2026-08.csv.gz  wsprspots-2026-09.csv.gz
EXIT=0
```

Negative test, unreachable host — genuine errors must stay loud:

```
[wsprspots-2026-09.csv.gz] FAILED: HTTP GET: ... no such host
  Failed:     6
EXIT=1
```

No `Missing`, exit 1. The new classification does not swallow real errors.

No version bump here; rides the same 4.0.4 release as #3.

## Review
3-panel per doctrine: non-author human-agent (Watson) + Turing + Hopper.

author: wrg-11
body:
`CITATION.cff` said `version: 3.5.0`. `package.json` says **3.11.0**, and
`v3.11.0` is the published tag — six minor releases of drift in the one file
whose entire job is *"cite me as this version"*.

Anyone following the citation would attribute this work to a release that
predates the SARIF export, the authorization-chain evidence, the five-language
rule corpus and scenarios S12/S13.

### Why it drifted silently

The release check swept documentation with a `*.md` glob, and this file is not
Markdown. It is a version surface all the same: it carries `version:` and
`date-released:`.

The check now compares CITATION's version **directly against the manifest**
rather than scanning for a leftover old version string. That difference
matters: the scan only works in the window between a version bump and a
release, because once the tag catches up there is no "old" string left to
find — so a stale CITATION becomes invisible exactly when a release is cut.

This file was found by the new equality check on its first run across all five
public repositories. A sibling repo's `CITATION.cff` had the same defect and is
fixed in WRG-11/ai-security-toolkit#40.

author: joaodrp
body:
go.mod declares `module ghealth`, so the module cannot be resolved by the path it is fetched from:

```
$ go install github.com/Google-Health-API/google-health-cli@latest
module declares its path as: ghealth
        but was required as: github.com/Google-Health-API/google-health-cli
```

That blocks `go install` and the version managers built on it, which is why the README has to say clone and build. It also leaves everything under `pkg/` unimportable, despite the layout announcing those packages as public.

Set the module path to the repository URL and update the imports that follow from it. No behaviour change.

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` and `gofmt -l` all clean.

author: afonsojanu
body:
Fixes #948.

\`apply_baseline_shear()\` accumulates \`fay * cur->advance.x\` into an \`int32_t shear\` variable and adds it (plus another product) straight into \`cur->pos.y\`. With a large enough \`\fay\` override value the double product goes well past \`INT32_MAX\`/\`INT32_MIN\`, and the implicit conversion back to \`int32_t\` on the \`+=\` is undefined behavior.

Built with \`-fsanitize=undefined\` and ran the subtitle from the issue:

\`\`\`
{\fax(1000000000)}{\fay(1000000000)}
\`\`\`

Before the fix:

\`\`\`
ass_render.c:2292:19: runtime error: 8.62e+11 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'
```

Clamped both spots with \`FFMINMAX(..., INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX)\`, which is the same pattern already used in \`mystrtoi32()\` for parsed integers. After clamping the shear accumulator, the same extreme value still overflowed a few lines further down the pipeline in \`render_and_combine_glyphs()\` when it got folded into the device-space y position, so I clamped that addition too, otherwise the crash just moves rather than going away.

Checked normal (non-adversarial) rendering isn't affected: rendered both sample files under \`compare/test/\` before and after the change and the output PNGs are byte-identical.

author: sanitdhar
body:
Closes #97.

## What changed

Writes down the two process rules agreed after #95, so they survive longer than memory.

**The PR loop.** Open, CI, CodeRabbit, triage, merge — with the part that actually matters spelled out: **every finding gets one of three responses, and none of them is silence.**

| Response | When |
| --- | --- |
| Fix it | The finding is right — push the fix, reply saying what changed and how it was verified |
| Reply why not | Wrong, or right but out of scope — "tracked in #96" is a reason, ignoring it is not |
| Escalate | It exposes a decision rather than a defect — that belongs in an issue, not a PR thread |

A stale review thread is indistinguishable from one nobody read, and six months on nobody can tell which it was.

**Verify before accepting.** #95 is the worked example: the Metro finding was correct, and checking it showed the real problem was *worse* than described — the override made Metro watch the whole repo rather than the four packages Expo detects on its own. Reply with that evidence, not "done".

**Stacked PRs.** Dependent work branches off the PR below it and targets that branch as base, so each diff shows only its own change. When a lower PR changes, rebase the stack with `--force-with-lease` — never bare `--force`, which is the difference between rebasing your own stack and silently discarding someone else's push.

## Checks

- [x] `npm run verify` passes locally
- [x] Scoped to one issue — documentation only, no code touched
- [x] Title is in conventional-commit form
- [x] No new architectural rules, so no new enforcement probe needed

author: yihanzhu
body:
## Summary

- Roadmap item 5, unit 4. The "protected-path, credential, network, and publisher boundaries" family moves from declared to seeded. Its sixteen cases in `evals/v1/seed-set-boundaries.json` replay execution-environment claims through the real inactive sandbox-policy evaluator (`control/v1/evaluate-sandbox.sh`), staged with its policy-set validator and policy in the private evals runtime at pinned digests. The evaluator finds its jq on PATH and its policy beside itself; both come from the runtime, nothing from the repo.
- Cases: a cleared, allowlisted sandbox is satisfied; a publisher role, an allowed network or endpoint, a tool that asks for network, an inherited environment or a secret-looking variable, a credential reference, a write root outside the fixed sandbox, any target or external write, and a stale policy-set reference are violated with their exact reason sets; unknown network or sensitive-material state is inconclusive; a claim with an unknown field or a wildcard path is refused. Each expectation was checked against the real evaluator before being written.
- Contracts: seed source `control.sandbox-policy.v1`; sandbox cases carry policy-set, duty, and claim pairs; expectations are `evaluated{verdict,reason_ids}` or `rejected{error_token}`; the evaluator pins a six-file control closure; grading adds `evals.verdict-mismatch`, and an incomplete reason set fails.
- Stacked on #235 (base is that branch). When the base lands, this branch takes a merge of `main`; no rebase of published work.

## Honesty of the grade

The evaluator is the only judge. The framework records its verdict and exact reason set, or its one refusal token, and grades that against the case. A wrong verdict or an incomplete reason set is graded `failed`.

## Inactive boundary

Unchanged: no candidate, adapter, model, credential, network, write outside private scratch, qualification, authority, or profile activation. The replayed evaluator is itself declaration-only. An edited evaluator is refused as `E_STALE` before anything runs.

## Exact candidate

- Head: `44ff407`

author: nlohmann
body:
## Summary

The BJData ndarray writer (`write_bjdata_ndarray` in `include/nlohmann/detail/output/binary_writer.hpp`) validated the *kind* of each `_ArrayData_` element (integer vs. float) against the declared `_ArrayType_`, but not its *range*. Each element is written with a narrowing cast, e.g. `write_number(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(el.get<std::uint64_t>()), true)` for `_ArrayType_ = "uint8"`. An out-of-range element (e.g. `256`) was silently wrapped by that cast instead of being reported — no error, no fallback.

```cpp
json j;
j["_ArrayType_"] = "uint8";
j["_ArraySize_"] = json::array({2});
j["_ArrayData_"] = json::array({1, 256});   // 256 does not fit uint8
auto v = json::to_bjdata(j);
// json::from_bjdata(v).dump() used to give "[1,0]" instead of round-tripping
```

## Fix

Each `_ArrayData_` element is now range-checked against the C++ type named by `_ArrayType_` before being cast:
- integer types (`uint8`/`int8`/`uint16`/`int16`/`uint32`/`int32`/`uint64`/`int64`, plus `char`/`byte` which share the `uint8` range) are checked with the existing `value_in_range_of<TargetType>` helper, handling both signed and unsigned JSON number storage (so a negative value is correctly rejected for an unsigned target).
- `single` (32-bit float) is checked so that a finite `double` which would overflow to infinity when narrowed to `float` is rejected.
- `double` needs no additional check since it already spans the full range of the internal float representation.

When any element is out of range, the function falls back to the same plain-object encoding already used by this function for other invalid-annotation cases (mismatched kind, non-array `_ArraySize_`, overflowing dimensions, etc.), so the value round-trips through `from_bjdata(to_bjdata(j))` instead of being silently corrupted.

## Tests

Added a new section `"ndarray with out-of-range _ArrayData_ elements stays as object"` in `tests/src/unit-bjdata.cpp` covering:
- an out-of-range `uint8` element (256) falls back and round-trips
- an out-of-range `int8` element (200) falls back and round-trips
- a negative element under an unsigned type (`uint16`) falls back and round-trips
- a `single` (float) element that overflows to infinity (`1e40`) falls back and round-trips
- in-range boundary values (`uint8` 0/255, `int8` -128/127, `single` 1.5) still use the compact ndarray encoding

Ran the full `unit-bjdata` suite offline (compiled against `include/` with a stub `test_data.hpp`): 693935/693936 assertions pass; the one failure and the one skipped test case are pre-existing and unrelated (they require downloaded test data, unavailable in this offline setup).

## Breaking change?

No breaking changes. This only affects the BJData ndarray fast-path encoding for annotated objects whose `_ArrayData_` previously contained values outside the range implied by `_ArrayType_`; such objects are now encoded as plain objects (as they already are for the other invalid-annotation cases handled by this same function) instead of emitting silently corrupted data.

Fixes #5403.

— opened by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann

author: mjcmatrix
body:
## Description

**Summary of Changes:**

Changing Rendering > Quality in the 3D view only took effect once the view was left and entered again. Most visibly, raising the quality away from Low left the scene with no fixture light at all. `MainView3D::setRenderQuality()` now rebuilds the frame graph, the same way adding or removing a fixture item already does.

**Related Issues:**

None.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read and followed the [QLC+ Coding Guidelines](https://github.com/mcallegari/qlcplus/wiki/Coding-guidelines).
- [x] My code adheres to the project's coding style, including:
  - [x] Placing opening braces `{` on a new line for functions and class definitions.
  - [x] Consistent use of spaces and indentation.
- [x] I have tested my changes on the following platforms:
  - [x] Linux
  - [ ] Windows
  - [ ] macOS
- [x] I have added or [updated documentation](https://docs.qlcplus.org/) as necessary.

No documentation change necessary.

## Testing

**Test Cases:**

Open a project with a spotlight fixture aimed at the stage, run a scene that lights it, and open the 3D view. The render quality starts at High.

1. Set Rendering > Quality to Low, staying in the 3D view.
2. Leave the 3D view and return to it.
3. Set the quality back to High, staying in the 3D view.
4. Leave the 3D view and return to it.
5. Repeat step 3 for Medium and for Ultra.

**Test Results:**

| # | Expected | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixtures stop lighting the scene | **Fail** - the beams in the air go, but surfaces stay lit | Pass |
| 2 | Scene dark | Pass - this is where Low finally took effect | Pass |
| 3 | Fixtures light the scene again | **Fail** - stays dark | Pass |
| 4 | Fixtures lit | Pass - this was the workaround | Pass |
| 5 | Fixtures light the scene | **Fail** - stays dark | Pass |

Tested on Linux (Qt 6, Intel iGPU, hardware OpenGL). No crash, GPU error or rendering corruption across the quality transitions.

## Additional Notes

`3DView.qml`'s `updateFrameGraph()` builds the frame graph once, and for each fixture it reads that item's `useScattering` and `useShadows` flags to decide whether to create a shadow map pass, a spotlight shading pass and a scattering pass. Those flags are bound to `View3D.renderQuality`, and at Low quality they are all false, so no spotlight pass is created for any fixture.

`setRenderQuality()` previously only stored the value and emitted the notify signal. The flags flipped, but nothing rebuilt the frame graph, so the passes stayed absent. The frame graph was otherwise only rebuilt on entering the view and on adding or removing a fixture item, which is why leaving the view and coming back appeared to fix it.

`raymarchSteps` is a plain shader uniform and did track the quality live, which is why the dial looked half-applied rather than inert: dropping to Low removed the volumetric beams immediately, but the surface lighting stayed until the frame graph was next built.

The call is guarded on `m_scene3D` so that changing the quality while the 3D view has never been opened stays a no-op, and it uses the same `updateFrameGraph(true)` entry point as `removeFixtureItem()`, which destroys the existing nodes before recreating them.

---

Replaces #28, which had the upstream-based branch as its head and therefore conflicted with the unmerged rendering-settings work already on `master`. The branch behind #28, `3dview-quality-framegraph-rebuild`, is based on `upstream/master` and stays as the head for the upstream pull request.

author: sartaj1995
body:
The log was written at [#17](https://github.com/sartaj1995/workout-tracker/pull/17) and has sat still through eleven more PRs — several of which taught more than the first fifteen did. **Nineteen new entries**, and one revision.

### The ones that carry furthest

| Happened here | Generalises to |
| --- | --- |
| Halving every dumbbell number would have been survivable; the factor landing on *some* exercises moved a day's workload 2.4× with no change in effort | An inconsistent error beats a large consistent one only on size — an even bias cancels out of comparisons, an uneven one corrupts all of them |
| A Legs session moves 4,130kg against Push's 1,808kg, so a combined chart would be a sawtooth tracking which day it was | A combined series can track its **mix** instead of its trend |
| A deploy was quietly providing a diff and a moment to notice; in-app editing had to rebuild that as per-day counts and parse warnings | Removing friction removes the checks the friction was doing — name what a step was catching before you delete it |
| "Chest sup row" → "Chest supported row" strands every session, chart and best on an invisible id, and nothing errors | A rename is a delete plus a create unless someone says otherwise; no diff contains the difference |
| `80x9` charts as `104` with nothing saying why, or whether you can lift 104 | Publish a derived number with the three ways it misleads — that's what makes the rest credible |
| "Have they granted Drive access?" was answered by looking for a 1-hour token | Don't infer a durable fact from a transient artefact |

### One entry revised, not added to

**"Timers stop when you aren't looking"** prescribed moving the rest alert onto the audio clock. The audio clock turns out to suspend too — measured, four seconds of wall time advanced it by zero — so the entry now tells both rounds and ends somewhere better than it started: *verify the replacement in the failure condition, because a different subsystem is not an exempt one.*

That's flagged as **revised** in the text, and the intro explains the convention. A log that quietly overwrites its own wrong advice is worth less than one that shows the correction.

### Also

- Checklist grows from 10 items to 20, absorbing the new lessons.
- All 25 cited commit hashes re-verified to resolve.
- Docs only — no code, config or build changes.

body:
## Summary

Reset `_init_lin_stats` at the start of every `solve()` call. An accepted warm start can skip cold initialization and finish with zero IPM updates; previously that return could report the prior cold solve's factor applications when the same QTQP object was reused.

Rebind to a fresh dictionary rather than clearing the old one, preserving statistics already attached to earlier returned solutions. This changes diagnostics only; warm-start acceptance, numerical steps, and the paper are unchanged.

## Regression coverage

Both SCIPY and SCIPY_DENSE now cover:

- Cold → accepted zero-update warm → cold on the same object: no stale initialization work, no initialization during the warm call, and fresh stats on the next cold call.
- Repeated equality-only solves: current initialization stats remain populated and earlier returned statistics remain unchanged.

The stale-stat regression fails on unmodified main for both backends and passes with this fix.

## Validation

- 122 related warm-start/initialization/equality tests passed.
- All 64 tests in the other five test modules passed.
- `ruff check --select E9,F src/ tests/test_qtqp.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
- An additional broad `tests/test_qtqp.py` run reached 1,099 passed with no failures before being stopped after about five minutes. This is not a completed full-suite result; the full PR CI matrix is running separately.

Local tests use Python 3.12, NumPy 2.4.2, SciPy 1.16.3. An external import shim marks the optional PETSc/MUMPS backend unavailable because its installed import terminates this local test process. No solver implementation is stubbed or modified for testing.

author: james9120
body:
## User feedback addressed
The previous build felt like slow motion, and the character looked like disconnected toy parts. Passing physics tests did not establish good character art or enjoyable pacing.

## Character replacement
- Removed the sphere-per-body-part hero and built connected swept surfaces for the torso, mask, arms and legs.
- Athletic proportions: smaller head, tapered waist, longer limbs and integrated shoulders rather than exposed round joints.
- Continuous two-bone limb surfaces with fixed arm and leg lengths; hands and boots are closed solids, including their end caps.
- Locally generated suit atlas with side panels, web pattern, mask lenses and back emblem.
- Replaced the symmetrical elbows-out airborne pose with an asymmetric reaching/trailing pose, plus distinct swing, dive and trick poses.
- New character mesh: 3,280 triangles. This remains original procedural art, not a production/scanned character asset.

## Pace and camera
- Starting forward speed: 32 → 46 game metres/second (+43.75%).
- Constant gameplay-tuned gravity: 9.81 → 24. This intentionally prioritizes a faster, heavier superhero arc over literal Earth-gravity timing; gravity does not change at the apex.
- Faster progressive reeling and ZIP, with attachment/release still preserving position and velocity.
- Lower, closer chase camera: approximately 7.6 m back and 1.55 m above, rather than 9.3 m back and 3.1 m above. Bounded speed FOV and faster camera following.
- Corrected the simulation-time loss on frames longer than 100 ms. Catch-up now accommodates 250 ms with bounded fixed steps, and camera timing follows the same cap. A reproduced 5-fps interval previously advanced only 0.5 seconds per wall-clock second; it now advances one second.
- Faster automatic resolution reduction when frame rate is particularly low. No claim that a physical iPhone is now guaranteed 60 fps.

## Validation
44/44 checks passed: 22 each in Chromium and WebKit.
Run: https://github.com/james9120/arcade/actions/runs/33984823391
Artifact: velocity-preview-results (exact tested HTML, JSON results, and actual day/night, swing/freefall/trick, portrait/landscape screenshots).

Verified the committed game blob matches the tested artifact exactly: a37a2573d84a4e6e7d2082ebe301d35e734dbac4.

Tests include touch start/cancellation, attachment continuity, tuned ballistic gravity, slack/taut ropes and energy bounds, collisions, ground death, pause, streaming/rebase, day/night wrap, rotation, drawing errors, fixed limb lengths, character budget, and matching game time at simulated 5/8/15/60 fps.

The updated scripted 30-second route completed 21 catches and 19 releases, with 1,033.28 m of path distance and 781.37 m forward progress. The script's release/reel inputs were retuned for the new pacing; this is a regression scenario, not a human play-test or an unlimited-survival claim.

Manually reviewed the generated screenshots and made a second pose/surface pass to remove the stiff freefall elbows and hollow-looking boot ends.

## Scope
Final diff contains only games/web-swing/index.html and tests/web_swing_browser.py. Temporary preview builders and their workflow were removed. Existing read-only regression workflow, Pages deployment, homepage and other games are unchanged. Runtime is still a self-contained HTML file with no build step or asset downloads.

Not merged: the live Pages game remains unchanged until this PR is merged. Hands-on phone feedback is still needed for subjective feel and device-specific performance.

author: gooyyu1
body:
Closes #1505

木材加工（`skill_woodwork`）と保存（`skill_preserving`）は、伸ばす操作を持ちながら効き先が1つも無い
——段は動くのに、動いても何も起きないバーが画面に並んでいる。**この2本を放置してよいかとは別に、
放置していることに気づけない**ことが問題なので、数え上げる検査を足した。

## 入れた検査

`tests/world-codex/skillsYaml.test.ts` に「伸ばす操作を持つのに効き先が無い腕」の数え上げを足した。
既にある逆向きの数え上げ（「伸ばす操作をまだ持たない腕は、開ける物が世界に無い4本だけ」）と対になる。

```ts
const gains = declaredSkillGains();
const effective = new Set<string>([
  ...skillsReadFromAgent(),
  ...ACCESS_BONUSES.map((entry) => entry.skill),
]);

expect(SKILLS.filter((name) => gains.has(name) && !effective.has(name))).toEqual([
  'skill_woodwork',
  'skill_preserving',
]);
```

**効き先は系統で分かれる**（`docs/world/Skills.md` 2節）ので、数え方も2つある。

- **製作系** — 誰かがその腕を読んでいること。`skillsReadFromAgent` が世界の定義を歩いて
  `{subject: agent, prop: <腕>}` を拾う。**読む側の書き方は1つ**なので、レシピの解放条件も操作の
  `conditions` も `base` の土台も、この1本で拾える。
- **アクセス系** — レシピを開けないので、効き先は重みへの上乗せ（同5節）にしかない。この対応は
  同じファイルの `ACCESS_BONUSES` が既に持っていて、隣の検査が実際の値で確かめている。

**「どこで読まれているか」ではなく「読まれているか」だけを問う**形にしたので、解放条件を持つ
レシピの可否とは独立している。

### 効いていることの確認

緑であることだけでは見張りになっていないので、3方向へ壊して赤くなるのを見た。

- `bedding.yaml` の `bed.spread`（レシピの解放条件）へ `skill_woodwork` を足す
  → `expected [ 'skill_preserving' ] to deeply equal [ Array(2) ]`
- `timber.yaml` の `strip_bark.conditions`（操作の条件）へ `skill_woodwork` を足す
  → 同じく `skill_woodwork` が一覧から外れる
- `fire.yaml` の `torch.light` へ `add: {agent: {skill_cooking: 2}}` を足す
  → 一覧に `skill_cooking` が増える（効き先の無い腕へ伸ばす操作が足された側）

どれも確認後に戻してある。

## 仮決め

**この PR では効き先を入れず、2本とも名前で残した**（issue が挙げた「今は入れない」）。代わりの案は
「今ある物へ条件を置く」だったが、担当のファイルには置き先が無かった。

- `salt.yaml` で腕を要求できる場所（`salt_pan.laid` と `cure`）は、**どちらへ置いても循環する**
  ——保存を伸ばす唯一の操作が塩漬け（`cure`）で、その塩はこの塩田からしか採れない
  （`SkillSystem.md` 3.2節）。
- `timber.yaml` には `recipes` を持つ型が1つも無い。操作の側（`fell`・`buck`・`strip_bark`）は
  木材加工を配る側で、そこへ要求を足せば同じく循環する。

覆すと何が変わるか: 干し場（`drying.yaml` の `drying_rack`）だけは保存の腕を要求できる位置に在る
（塩田が開いているので循環しない）。そこへ置くなら、保存の系統ぜんぶが「海に面した土地＋塩田」の
後ろへ回り、`Skills.md` 2節の「保存の最初の一歩は天日に並べる（道具不要）」と 4節の「保存は前半」を
両方書き換えることになる。担当外のファイルでもあるので採らなかった。

## 同じ誤りの兄弟

- 他の未解放レシピ（`fire_drill`・`splint`・`field`・`pitfall`・`raft`・`pen`）は、**どれも解放条件を
  持たない理由を定義の本文に書いてある**ので、木材加工を後付けできる場所ではない。特に `splint` は
  「木材加工の腕を求めると、折れてから作れないことがある」と名指しで却下している。
- `docs/engine/SkillSystem.md` 概要は、伸ばす行動を持たない4本について「開ける物が世界にまだ1つも
  無いためで、解放条件にも書いていません」と書いている。**嘘ではない**（その4本についての記述で、
  逆は主張していない）が、木材加工と保存が同じ空白を別の形で抱えていることはどこにも無い。担当外で、
  かつ自分の差分が嘘にしたわけでもないので触らず、下の issue へ入れた。

## 自己点検

サブエージェントの一次レビューを1本通した。止める理由は0件、スメル4件。

1. **「効き先」をレシピの解放条件と `ACCESS_BONUSES` の2つだけで定義している**（操作の `conditions`
   にも `agent` の腕の段は書けるので、その形で効き先が入った腕は効いているのに一覧へ残り続ける）
   → **直した。** 読む側の字面（`{subject: agent, prop: <腕>}`）を歩く `skillsReadFromAgent` へ
   置き換え、レシピと操作を1本で拾う形にした。3つ目の壊し方（`strip_bark` の条件）で確認した。
2. **`requiredSkillsOf` が「熟達すれば開く」を前提にした割り出しで、新しい検査はその前提を自分では
   確かめていない** → **直した。** 1. の置き換えで割り出しがレシピの可否から離れたので、隣の検査から
   括り出した `requiredSkillsOf` ごと要らなくなり、隣は元の形へ戻した。
3. **PR本文の「解放条件を持てるのは `recipes` のエントリだけ」は言い過ぎ**（interaction も条件を
   持てるので、採らなかった理由として効いているのは循環のほうだけ） → **直した。** 上の `## 仮決め`
   を書き換え、同じ記述を持っていた #1572 の本文も直した。
4. **「伸ばす操作を持つ腕は、画面で段の動くバーになる」は、バーになること自体は伸ばす操作の有無に
   依らない** → **直した。** テストのコメントを「段が動く／動いても何も起きない」の側へ絞った。

## 見た目

不要。触ったのはテスト1本だけで、画面には出ない。

## ユーザーへ

- **#1572**（木材加工と保存に効き先を入れる）を立てた。この PR は「気づけない」ほうだけを直して
  いるので、効き先そのものは残っている。順序の指定は無い。

author: certik
body:
## Summary

`size(matmul(...))` and `size(transpose(...))` used at type level were answered
with the size of the first array argument, so a declaration shaped by one got
the wrong extents.

The shape of `matmul` and of `transpose` follows entirely from the shapes of
their operands, and neither carries dimensions of its own in its result type,
so the query has to be answered from the operands: matmul is
`(n,k)x(k,m) -> (n,m)`, `(n,k)x(k) -> (n)` and `(k)x(k,m) -> (m)`; transpose
swaps the two extents of its argument. A `dim` the compiler cannot evaluate
picks between the two extents with `merge`.

## Scope

Split out of the GPU offload work in
[#12705](https://github.com/lfortran/lfortran/pull/12705), which needs it. This
is the part of that branch that changes behaviour for every front end and
backend independently of GPU offload, so it is reviewable and bisectable on its
own. The GPU work follows in a stacked PR based on this one.

- `src/libasr/asr_utils.cpp` — `array_intrinsic_shape_size`, consulted from
  `make_ArraySize_t_util`.
- `integration_tests/array_size_matmul_01.f90` — new test, registered
  `gfortran llvm`.

## Verification

The test fails on `main` and passes here:

```
$ ./a.out            # main
ERROR STOP matvec extent
$ ./a.out            # this branch
(exit 0)
```

It covers both paths the query can take:

- the type-level path, where the result shapes a declared object
  (`real :: t(size(matmul(x, y), 1), size(matmul(x, y), 2))`) — this is what
  was wrong;
- the executable path, where the size is computed rather than used to shape
  something. That path was already correct; the test locks it in, since the fix
  only touches the `for_type` branch and nothing else guarded it.

Both are checked against GFortran, which agrees.

Suites, LLVM 18 / Ninja / Debug:

- `./run_tests.py` — clean apart from `llvm-asr_text_compile_01`, which differs
  only as `i8**` vs `ptr`: an opaque-pointer artifact of the local LLVM version,
  present on `main` in the same environment and untouched by this change.
- `cd integration_tests && ./run_tests.py -b llvm` — **3962/3962 passed**.

## Rationale

`make_ArraySize_t_util` already special-cases `FunctionCall` and
`ArrayReshape`, whose results carry their own dimensions. `matmul` and
`transpose` do not, so the general "size of the first array argument" rule --
which is right for the intrinsics whose result has the shape of their argument
-- is wrong for them, and the answer has to be rebuilt from the operands. This
belongs in AST-to-ASR, where the shape of an expression is decided, rather than
in any backend.

author: alcimerio
body:
Stored Profiles can now be edited, cloned, renamed and deleted with explicit confirmation and revision-conditional persistence. Editing and cloning seed the existing builder from strictly validated exact stored bytes, preserve unavailable selections by source/path identity, and require a canonical representation preview before committing.

## Behavior and boundaries

- Adds `acs profile edit NAME`, `acs profile clone NAME --name NEW`, `acs profile rename NAME --name NEW`, and `acs profile delete NAME [--confirm NAME]`, with contextual help and independent operand/flag parsing.
- Reuses the merged revisioned repository for every commit. Immutable preview closures bind desired canonical bytes to captured revisions; stale conflicts preserve the draft and newer data and require explicitly confirmed reload before a new preview.
- Shows missing, ambiguous and unavailable/unchecked saved Skills without rebinding matching display names. Repair discovery preserves choices from readable sources; unresolved saves require a separate warning acknowledgment. Full launch and passive inspection/validation semantics remain unchanged.
- Discloses v1-to-v2 conversion and category/default/sorting/formatting effects. Unsupported/future/ambiguous documents and filename identity mismatch refuse rewriting without byte, mode or tree changes. Exact-name deletion can remove unsupported regular documents without decoding/re-encoding them, while preserving identities, Sessions and other Profiles.
- Keeps help, grammar errors and noninteractive rejections before runtime/recovery dependencies. Terminal cancellation waits for an already executing repository call to settle and retains Committed/Unknown outcomes instead of reporting false cancellation or offering blind retry.

The [user guide](https://github.com/alcimerio/ai-config-selector/blob/cbd82ccacc1e31f484fa2b6e5ccb3f09932e1ae9/docs/profile-mutations.md) describes commands, previews, cancellation and recovery. The [repository contract](https://github.com/alcimerio/ai-config-selector/blob/cbd82ccacc1e31f484fa2b6e5ccb3f09932e1ae9/docs/profile-repository-transactions.md) remains the persistence authority. These changes introduce no release, tag, new Profile schema, provider workflow, Session operation, launch plan or second recovery engine.

## Validation

Behavioral regressions first reproduced rejected mutation grammar and invisible/unremovable saved selections against the merged base. Separate PTY regressions cover context cancellation, SIGINT, SIGTERM and Ctrl+C while a save settles to committed success, Committed-with-error or Unknown. Orderly shutdown avoids the native cancellable-reader race exposed by forced termination, and restoration assertions use the live PTY master.

Local checks pass for mutation CLI/builder/category/inspection behavior, independent-process source and destination races, immutable preview bytes, unsupported-content tree preservation, deletion sentinels, actual source permission denial at UID 1000, and selected candidate-binary PTY flows (commit, cancel, signal, resize, exact-name mismatch and Ctrl+D). Formatting, vet and build pass. The unfiltered suite reproduces the 15 existing host-inapplicable Linux failures; the suite passes with only those freshly reverified names excluded. Linux race compilation is unavailable because gcc is absent.

The existing independent-writer repository test joins both original contenders before retrying Busy, preserving its stale condition and exactly-one-commit/one-conflict assertions; native scheduling exposed the missing barrier. All seven checks pass on the current corrected head, including both complete [native macOS normal/race and installed-candidate gates](https://github.com/alcimerio/ai-config-selector/actions/runs/33999137789), [macOS Verify and both Seatbelt stress jobs](https://github.com/alcimerio/ai-config-selector/actions/runs/33999137760), and Linux observation. No failed-job retry was needed on this head. CI synthetic merge `86cdbbd8e5471106b079faf3d009f1b30ff3838f` has exactly the reviewed tree. Fresh independent review of this corrected head passed, including controlled terminal/error and refresh schedules, old-head failure comparisons, real repository and candidate checks, and exact native-log inspection.

Independent review corrections preserve discard confirmation across asynchronous refresh, retire only observed ordinary noncommitted attempts, and keep unrelated terminal failures alongside known successful commitment. Reporting-only committed errors return nonzero without prescribing repository recovery; true recovery-required and Unknown results retain actionable guidance. New failing-before regressions cover both create/edit runtime paths, terminal errors joined with cancellation, modal success/failure/retry interleavings, and an installed-candidate edit/clone conflict followed by explicit reload and SIGTERM. The latter now reports current cancellation with exit 130 and preserves independently written newer data. The inspection guide's operand rule is also corrected.

Ctrl+D tests exercise an explicit key event, not actual stream EOF. Independent injected EOF invoked no save during a bounded observation, but automatic EOF shutdown is not established. No broad input-runtime redesign is included.

Current head: `cbd82ccacc1e31f484fa2b6e5ccb3f09932e1ae9`; base: `b4d35b6fc6da24cbc851e1e0c6f9fecfd2433f24`; tree: `050669ca71d55e05e5271e2beccdf7d552b6618e`.

## Summary

Establishes a persistent Skyforge soundtrack-authorship lane and records the accepted musical/production work through the first three frozen cues plus the active Track 03 contemplative development boundary.

This change adds a discoverable `docs/music` record, persists important MIDI authoring sources, captures the BBCSO/Cakewalk workflow, cue semantics, mastering measurements, rejected approaches, and current musical-language lessons, and now includes the active Track 03 thematic-audition lab.

## Scope and invariants

In scope:

- MUS-0001 soundtrack index and milestone record;
- production workflow and canonical 19-track BBCSO schema;
- project-level musical-language / anti-pattern record;
- Track 00 acceptance record and frozen MIDI source;
- Track 01 acceptance record and frozen MIDI source;
- Track 02 first-draft freeze / range-experiment record and frozen MIDI source;
- Track 03 development history;
- active Track 03 Sketch 5 / Sketch 6 authoring sources;
- Track 03 Theme Lab 01 candidate MIDIs;
- root README discovery link.

Preserved invariants:

- no executable or terrain behavior changes;
- no Minecraft/NeoForge dependency changes;
- no canonical terrain identity changes;
- no generated worlds, build output, logs, or game assets;
- no third-party audio, MIDI, notation, samples, or transcriptions;
- large derived WAV masters remain outside ordinary Git history.

## Verification

- [ ] `./gradlew check` — documentation/source-only lane; repository CI may provide verification
- [x] Terrain deterministic evidence — not applicable; terrain identity unchanged
- [x] No generated worlds, build output, logs, credentials, or third-party game assets committed

- [x] Frozen Track 00–02 authoring MIDIs persisted
- [x] Active Track 03 MIDI milestones persisted
- [x] Theme Lab 01 candidates persisted losslessly as gzip-compressed MIDI

## Evidence

Track 03 has deliberately moved back from development to thematic audition after Sketch 6 demonstrated that improved form cannot rescue weak thematic material.

Theme Lab 01 candidates:

- A / Far Lantern: `0b8cc98da97c5bb91ab1d0c7f2be9459b3e131646eda3098c105237ba52de479`
- B / Turning Question: `4b2a19206aa61748cdbe035fa28993fc467044b657485eeef70642df15879a6f`
- C / Homeward Sky: `87ce9b86fa0fb9437e616d5a711c2d7915f41e80fdb7c63c5684235c99ccd1de`
- D / Old Thought: `66662ced65c62a98ff630a9c79788ba651d91c6bf5b6f2eecaac861f83ce4dee`

The Track 03 record preserves failed/weak approaches rather than rewriting them out of history because those failures materially define the current composition method.

## Compatibility and documentation

- [x] Backend-neutral modules remain independent of Minecraft and NeoForge
- [x] Soundtrack records live under `docs/music`
- [x] Source-storage policy documented under `assets/music/source`
- [x] Intentional terrain-output changes — none

## Deferred work

- Select or reject Theme Lab 01 by ear before further Track 03 development.
- Do not add large WAV masters to ordinary Git history until the project deliberately chooses Git LFS, release assets, or another artifact strategy.
- Runtime adaptive music implementation remains downstream of concrete gameplay-state and transition requirements.


### Current Track 03 thematic boundary

Theme Lab 02 is now persisted under `assets/music/source/experiments/track-03-theme-lab-02/`. It explores new themes derived from the *traits* that made Lab 01 C / D relatively stronger (neighbor motion, asymmetry, exposed leap) without accepting or literally combining those earlier candidates.


### Current Track 03 boundary

Theme Lab 02 was rejected rather than promoted. The active boundary is now **First-Principles Theme 01**, a full melodic reset in 3/4 with a fresh B-flat-major-centered harmonic bed.

Persisted authoring sources:

- `assets/music/source/track-03-first-principles-theme-01.mid.gz`
- `assets/music/source/track-03-first-principles-theme-01-melody-only.mid.gz`

The melody-only diagnostic is the acceptance gate. No full-cue development or orchestration should resume unless the theme itself proves memorable.

author: fpresta0607
body:
## The defect

Nothing owned the question "what is still running that nobody is supervising". `cfo fleet-view` reads task metadata, `herdr agent list` reads panes, the OS knows about processes, and no code joined the three. A pane could be destroyed while its harness kept running: invisible to every CFO surface, still holding memory, still able to spend tokens. That is what PID 31032 was on 2026-09-05, with 553s of CPU and 445 MB resident and no record anywhere.

## What this adds

**`cfo reap`**, `--dry-run` by default. One sweep cross-references four sources, because none sees everything: `state/*.meta` plus each status log, `herdr api snapshot` plus `herdr pane process-info`, the Windows process table (one `Win32_Process` CIM query, for the command lines Toolhelp32 does not carry), and the `.worktrees/` directories under the home, `projects/*/`, and every project a task record names.

Five classifications, each needing a different action: `orphan_process`, `stale_server`, `orphan_worktree`, `orphan_meta`, `orphan_status`.

**The gates**, which is where the correctness lives. Every refusal is recorded on the finding as a `HELD:` line rather than dropping it, so the report always says both what was found and why it was left alone.

- Processor time is sampled twice, 3s apart; anything above 100ms in that window is refused. Log age is never consulted: a goblin waiting on an API response writes nothing for minutes and is very much alive.
- A process that cannot be measured, a harness with no Herdr ancestry, and every process finding taken while some pane could not report its own process identity are all held. The sweep also excludes its own ancestry, or it would report the session it runs in.
- A worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work is refused. `--force` cannot clear this one.
- A task that never reported a terminal status is refused unless `--force` names its id.

`--force` always takes a value: one pid or one task id, repeatable. There is no blanket override.

Worktree removal goes through the existing `cfo cleanup` path (or the same `worktree.Service.Return` primitive it calls, for a directory with no record). Processes end with `taskkill /T /F`. An orphaned status log is archived, never deleted. Everything reaped writes one line naming what and why.

**Automatic, with no new daemon.** The watcher runs the audit on its existing timer (`CFO_REAP_EVERY`, default 600s), persists the result, and appends an `orphan` wake the first time a given finding set appears, keyed by a stable digest so a known leak does not re-wake every cycle. The session-start digest gained an `ORPHANS` section that reads that record rather than sweeping, since that package never shells out.

## Verified against the live machine

```
ORPHANS: 4 orphan_worktree, 140 orphan_status
  orphan_worktree pdocs-fly-rightsize   ... | would return the worktree through cfo cleanup
  orphan_worktree pdocs-help-docs       ... | would return the worktree through cfo cleanup
  orphan_worktree pdocs-utah-bootstrap-stall ... | would return the worktree through cfo cleanup
  orphan_worktree slc-ordinance-sourcing ... | HELD: worktree has 11 commit(s) on no remote
```

Three of the six worktrees named in the brief's audit are still there and were found. The fourth is the gate doing its job on real data. The reaper's own live worktree is correctly absent. The evidence's orphan process and stale servers no longer exist on the machine, so those two classes are covered by synthetic fixtures modeled on the audit rather than by a live confirmation.

## Test plan

- `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` green.
- Table-driven classification over synthetic inventories for all five classes, plus the negatives that matter more: a healthy fleet produces nothing, a server in a working task's worktree is left alone, the sweep never reports the session it runs inside.
- Gate refusals, each proving nothing was killed or removed: busy process, unmeasurable process, dirty worktree, unpushed branch, non-terminal task, unresolved pane.
- `--force` proven per-target (named pid killed, unnamed one beside it not) and proven not to clear the work gate.
- A drift test that builds each harness adapter's real launch arguments and asserts the sweep's signatures still appear in them.
- Watcher: new orphan wakes, same orphan does not re-wake, a further orphan wakes again, a failed sweep is recorded as a failure.
- Digest: never-swept, recorded, and failed sweeps render distinctly.

Full report: `data/cfo-reaper/report.md`.

author: wtthornton
body:
## Summary

Four test-leak / runtime-socket-discipline fixes from the backlog-drain wave 2, lane L7. One issue (TAP-5896) is left `blocked` with a diagnosis — see below.

### TAP-6639 — metrics-hub isolation fails loudly on any leak to the live hub
Round 1 pinned the hub with a class fixture scoped to `TestTappsSetEngagementLevel` only. Round 2 replaced that with a **package-global autouse fixture**, `_isolate_metrics_hub` in `packages/tapps-mcp/tests/conftest.py:844-882`, which patches `tapps_mcp.server._get_metrics_hub` (the seam `_record_execution` and the `server_metrics_tools.py`/`server_analysis_tools.py` handlers all resolve the hub through, even where it's re-imported locally) to a `MetricsHub(tmp_path / "metrics-hub")` for **every test in the package** — not just the one class. That already covered `test_engagement_level.py` and `test_tier3_content_return.py`, the two files round 1's audit had listed as "not fixed"; they are fixed as of round 2, they just weren't re-audited against the new global fixture until this round.

**Round 3 defect and fix**: the round-2 fixture redirected writes but never *proved* the redirect held — a leak via any other path to the live `.tapps-mcp/metrics/` dir (a module building its own `MetricsHub`, a future accessor, a subprocess) would pass unnoticed, making the external md5 proof tautological. `MetricsHub` (`tapps_core/metrics/collector.py`) takes its directory only via constructor arg with no env/config injection point, so there is no seam to inject other than the accessor already patched — the fix instead adds a **detector** to the same fixture: it snapshots the live metrics dir's file set + `(size, mtime_ns)` before yield and compares after, `pytest.fail`-ing with the test's node id and the changed filenames on any difference, so the isolation now proves itself instead of relying on the external md5 to catch drift.

**Negative control 1 (bypass)**: a scratch test constructed `MetricsHub(repo_root)` directly (bypassing the patched `_get_metrics_hub` seam) and recorded one row. Detector output: `Failed: ...test_bypasses_patched_seam_and_leaks leaked to live metrics dir /tmp/tmcp-drain-l7/.tapps-mcp/metrics: changed files ['tool_calls_2026-09-05.jsonl']`. Removed after confirming.

**Negative control 2 (unpatched seam)**: temporarily removed only the `with patch("tapps_mcp.server._get_metrics_hub", ...)` line from `_isolate_metrics_hub` (kept the detector) and ran `test_server_pipeline_tools.py -k TestTappsSetEngagementLevel` — all 5 tests in that class failed at teardown with the same leak message, naming `tool_calls_<date>.jsonl` as the changed file. This is the gate's own control (round 1/2's md5 check), now caught by the suite itself. Patch line restored.

**Proof**: `test_server_pipeline_tools.py`, `test_composite_tools.py`, `test_engagement_level.py`, `test_tier3_content_return.py`, `test_memory_execution_metrics.py` — 166 passed with the detector active; `md5sum .tapps-mcp/metrics/tool_calls_<date>.jsonl` unchanged before/after that run.

### TAP-6591 — `_load_from_disk`'s brain read fired an unbounded sync HTTP call
`brain_metrics_bridge_available()` → `HttpBrainBridge.health_check()` used a 5.0s HTTP timeout with no circuit-breaker pre-check, so a stalling brain blocked every metrics read for up to 5s.

**Fix**: `health_check()` now (1) returns immediately when `self.circuit_open` is true, and (2) bounds its own HTTP probe to a new `_HEALTH_CHECK_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.0` (separate from the 5.0s constant other bridge calls still use). `brain_metrics_bridge_available()` now logs `brain_metrics_bridge_health`/`brain_metrics_bridge_unavailable` so degraded reads are never silent.

**Proof**: `pytest packages/tapps-core/tests/unit/test_execution_metrics.py -k stalling_brain` — 3 new tests using a real local socket that accepts a TCP connection and never responds. All three assert the call returns within a 2s margin (well under the old 5s bound) and that `get_metrics()` degrades to disk-only. Exit 0 after the fix.

**Control**: reverting the `brain_bridge.py`/`brain_telemetry.py` hunks and re-running the same `-k stalling_brain` selection fails all three tests with ~5.0-5.07s elapsed (over budget) — pasted below.

### TAP-6962 — `shutil.which()` mock leak into `Popen`
`TestDiskCacheIntegration.test_disk_cache_populates_memory_cache` patches `shutil.which` with no `return_value`. `_read_disk_cache()` invalidates its cache when the real venv's `pyvenv.cfg`/`uv-receipt.toml` mtime is newer than the cache's `timestamp_epoch` (`now - 60s`) — i.e. whenever the venv was (re)created within the last 60 seconds of the test run. When that happens, the code falls through to the live probe path, calls `shutil.which()` (the unconfigured mock), gets back a `MagicMock` "path", and passes it straight into `subprocess.run`'s argv — reproduced live: `TypeError`-shaped crash with `cmd=[<MagicMock name='which()' ...>, '--version']`.

**Fix**: the test now also pins `_venv_receipt_mtime` to `None` (removing the dependency on real filesystem timing entirely) and gives `shutil.which` an explicit `return_value=None`, so even if the live path were ever reached, no `MagicMock` can reach `Popen`.

**Proof**: 20 consecutive full-file runs, `pytest -p no:randomly test_tool_detection_cache.py`, all green (pasted below).

**Audit**: the other five `shutil.which` patches in this file already carry `return_value=None`/a string — this integration test was the only unscoped one.

### TAP-6694 — brain-bridge health probe flakes under xdist load
`test_brain_bridge_health_enabled_in_http_mode` mocked `httpx.get` (used by `health_check`) but not `HttpBrainBridge.auth_probe`, which makes its own unmocked `httpx.post` to the fake `http://brain:8080/mcp/` host — the source of the three 403s / circuit-opened sequence from the issue's lane log (whichever real endpoint "brain" resolves to on that CI runner rejects the fake `test-token`). Separately, all three `real_brain_bridge`-marked tests in this class called `_reset_brain_bridge_cache()` **after** their `with patch(...)` block exited, so closing the singleton (and draining any queued write) made a *second*, still-unmocked, real network call during teardown — reproduced locally as an 8-9s teardown that vanishes once fixed.

**Fix**: mock `auth_probe` in `test_brain_bridge_health_enabled_in_http_mode` (matching the already-correct sibling `test_memory_status_enabled_in_http_mode`), and move `_reset_brain_bridge_cache()` inside the `with patch(...)` block in all three `real_brain_bridge` tests in this class so the singleton is always closed while the network is still mocked.

**Proof**: `pytest test_server_pipeline_tools.py -k 'brain_bridge_health'` — both tests pass with sub-10ms teardown, repeated 3x for stability (pasted below).

**Control**: reverting to the original (auth_probe unmocked, reset outside the `with` block) reproduces an 8.82s teardown on this same host.

### TAP-5896 — blocked (rescoped remainder)

**Scope**: box 2 only — a `call_args` regression test asserting the in-process `AgentBrain` constructor's `agent_id` kwarg is not the literal `"tapps-mcp"`.

**Diagnosis**: `test_brain_bridge.py` is a 655-line file already below tapps-mcp's absolute quality-score threshold at `origin/master` (base score 66.87). author: jadzoghaib
body: The review found the age gate reading `year − birth_year` and calling a fifteen-year-old sixteen for the whole calendar year. PR #34 took the lower bound instead — the safe side, which also refuses some real sixteen-year-olds until January. This is the second half: **collect the date, compute exactly where we have it.** - Forms ask for a **date of birth**. The API accepts `birth_date` (real ISO date, not future, ≥1930) and **derives `birth_year`** from it, so every existing reader keeps working. A year alone is still accepted (clubs can't know a date) and still reads as the lower bound. - `age_on` — exact, birthday-aware. `age_of` — what the gate calls: date if present, year bound if not, nothing if neither. - The application page **does not invent a day** from an old year: the first draft prefilled `YYYY-01-01`, which would hand the exact path the *oldest* possible age — the wrong direction for a gate. Caught before commit. - Seed applications carry dates; the review queue shows the date where there is one. ### Verification - **346 passed, 2 skipped** — 5 new tests. Two run on a throwaway registered athlete: the first draft submitted as Kaia, admission re-ran, and her listing flipped for every later test — a contamination the full run caught and isolation hid. - `tsc -b && vite build` clean · `links.py` clean - Demo DB reset and reseeded: 2 of 2 applications carry dates - journey / permissions / propagation green against the relaunched API 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01UkTWBRwJv9k9Gytr2qrghD --- ## Summary by cubic Makes the age gate exact where a date of birth is known, so a January-born sixteen-year-old is no longer refused until the following calendar year. - Application forms now ask for a date of birth; the API accepts `birth_date`, derives `birth_year` from it, and rejects malformed, future, or pre-1930 dates. - The gate uses the date when present and falls back to the year-only lower bound, so existing applications and year-only submissions keep working unchanged. - The application page never invents a day from an old year, so it cannot hand the exact path the oldest possible age. Written for commit e9a79a8b1e572bb3ca653977e1a1c50bfe0727bc. Summary will update on new commits.

author: nehcuh
body:
Closes #371

## 为什么

`spawn_worker` 不 `chat.create`，子线程空转；`max_active_l2_per_run=1` 下 N 个 worker = N 次串行 L2。「组队」在现核上是空壳。I5 把只读匹配 + **一张**组队卡 + 任务切片 kick 做成 v1 核心。

设计基准：`.omx/artifacts/expert-team-20260905/FINAL-SYNTHESIS.md` I5。依赖 #367–#369 已在 main。

## 做了什么

- `propose_expert_team`：任务简述 → ≤4 个已安装 `kind=expert` id + rationale。发明 id / 停用专家被滤。LLM 只排序/理由。
- `spawn_expert_team`：**一条** L2（`L2_GATE_TOOLS` + `capabilityForceConfirm` 与 `spawn_worker` 锁步，无新 cruise waiver）。
  - Confirm Center 卡：队员、HARD_DENY 后有效工具面、完整可见可编辑切片、将升 orchestrator / 开 Board。侧栏快速允许禁用，逼进确认台。
  - token 绑定 pack id 集合 + 切片指纹；确认台编辑的切片经 origin-bound 回写后再发 token。
  - 批准后循环 `spawnWorkerThread` + `applyPack(allowTrust:false)` + `tool_allow=pack.tools.allow`。
  - 每 worker 写入 user brief 并 fire-and-forget `chat.create`。无 brief / 无 kick = `EMPTY_WORKER` + #292 回滚。
  - parent `board_mode=true`；>4 截断；总 worker ≤5。
- Worker HARD_DENY 含 `spawn_expert_team` / `propose_expert_team`。不写 `base_url`。无 auto-spawn、无 worker 互聊。

## 验收证据 [executed]

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 无 `security_token` | parent 角色/worker 数不变 |
| 空 brief / 无 kick | `EMPTY_WORKER` + parent restore |
| 中途 kick 抛错 | 已建 worker 全删 + #292 |
| 发明 id | 滤掉；不入 spawn |
| >4 | 截断为 4；`truncated=true` |
| 已有 4 worker + 组 2 | 只再 spawn 1，总 5 |
| `L2_GATE_TOOLS` | 仅一张组队卡（内部 `userConfirmed:true`，不再发 L2） |
| companion `npm test` | **4575 pass / 0 fail / 23 skipped** + settings-web 20 pass |
| extension `npm test` | **1198 pass / 0 fail** |

## Eval gate card — grok-371

**Blast tier**: T2（Autonomy：HITL 组队流 + 首次自动 kick worker loop）
**Capability declaration** (ADR-020):
  Surface: Side Panel Confirm Center + companion tools `propose_expert_team` (L0) / `spawn_expert_team` (L2)
  L2-classes: spawn_expert_team 与 spawn_worker 同 forceConfirm / 三旗巡航
  Compose: Pack `kind=expert` + 既有 spawnWorkerThread/applyPack
  Autonomy: 一张 HITL 卡后 kick worker loop（非 auto-spawn）
  Trust: applyPack `allowTrust:false`；token 绑 pack ids + slice fp
  Channel: 无 outbound 变更；#228 / #230 未动

### Machine (must pass first)
- [x] `npm --prefix companion test` → 4575 pass, 0 fail (exit 0)
- [x] `npm --prefix chrome-extension test` → 1198 pass, 0 fail (exit 0)
- [x] Outcome DoD: 见上表
- [x] 无 forbidden tools/paths；AGENTS.md 未改；ADR-015/016 内核语义未改

### Trajectory
- [x] Diff 限于组队工具 / L2 / Confirm Center / 测试 / CHANGELOG
- [x] 无 drive-by

### Judges（确认序：对抗 → Pi）
- [ ] 独立对抗 agent — **本实现 lane 不自评 APPROVE**（T2 闸门）
- [ ] Pi 复审 — 待对抗报告

### Blast
- [x] T2：dual-review 后才能合；实现者不得 merge-ready 自批
- residual: kick 是 fire-and-forget（worker LLM 失败记 warn，不回滚已开工的 sibling——与「任一步失败回滚」在 kick **调用**失败时生效；调用成功后的 LLM 错误走既有 worker 错误面）

### Verdict
- MACHINE: PASS
- ADVERSARY: N/A — 实现会话不得自批
- PI_REREVIEW: N/A
- MERGE: **NO** — 等独立对抗 → Pi

## NEVER 自检

- [x] 无 auto-spawn
- [x] 不是 N 次串行 spawn_worker L2
- [x] 无新 cruise waiver
- [x] worker 互聊未开
- [x] 未突破 5
- [x] 未抢 Stage 3 intent claim
- [x] LLM 不写 base_url

author: kajode
body:
## Problem

A chart grouped by attributes names every series after the whole group, so each tooltip row repeated its keys before reaching the first character that told the rows apart:

```
resource.k8s.cluster.name=kugel-eu-prod, deployment=ingress-..., state=...
resource.k8s.cluster.name=kugel-eu-prod, deployment=web, sta...
```

The row is `whitespace-nowrap` inside a card with no width cap, so the card grew past the panel and the value, the reason to hover at all, ended up outside it.

## Change

The keys are identical for every series on such a chart, so print them once below the timestamp and leave the values on the rows:

```
19:49
resource.k8s.cluster.name · deployment · state
  kugel-eu-prod · web · available              2 replicas
  kugelaudio-prod-us-west-2 · web · desired    1 replicas
```

- New `ChartLibrary/Utils/SeriesLabelDisplay.ts`. It compresses nothing unless **every** series name on the chart parses into the same key sequence, so a chart of plain names ("Failed generations"), a single-attribute group-by, or series grouped by different attributes render exactly as before. A wrong header would mislabel every row, so the bar for applying it is all-or-nothing.
- The compare-to-previous-period suffix survives on the row; the full original name stays reachable through the row's `title`.
- Card is width-capped, the label wraps and the value column is `shrink-0`, so a long label can no longer push the reading out of view.
- `TooltipEntries` now exports its renderable-entry predicate, so the anomaly band's `[low, high]` range series cannot disable the compression for a whole chart.

Applies to the Line, Area and Bar tooltips, which each ship their own copy.

## Tests

```
jest Tests/UI/Components/Charts/    75 passed
tsc --noEmit -p Common/tsconfig.json    exit 0
eslint + prettier    clean on changed files
```

New `SeriesLabelDisplay.test.ts` pins the compression and its six opt-out cases; `ChartTooltipSorted.test.tsx` gains a rendered-DOM case per chart type.

Not verified in a running UI: recharts' own overflow positioning at the edge of the viewport is unchanged by this diff, but I could not exercise it locally.

Refs https://linear.app/kugelaudio/issue/ENG-408

author: jdilla1277
body:
Agents running `agentcad inspect` now get a verdict that means the part will be accepted by a grader, a slicer, or another CAD program, with the failing layer named and the offending edges located. Before this, the verdict was the kernel's consistency check alone, and on the retained CADGenBench corpus AgentCAD accepted 18 parts the grader rejected.

This is M71 Slice 1a: the validator module and its first consumer, `inspect`. `run`, `import`, `measure`, `check-spec`, `recover`, and the `--validation-profile` flag follow in 1b; gating is Slice 2. `compute_metrics` is unchanged in this PR.

## What changed

- **`src/agentcad/validation.py`**: a registry of seven layers (file_parse, kernel_load, brep_check, shell_closure, mesh_manifold, structure, advisory), one runner, one report shape. `is_valid` is true only when every gating layer passes, false with `first_failure` named, `null` when a gating layer could not finish. The kernel-only result lives in `layers.brep_check`.
- **Shell closure** uses the kernel's closed-shell predicate plus loose-face detection, and lists free edges by the same IDs `inspect --ids` uses, with endpoints.
- **Mesh manifold** tessellates, stitches triangles by shared topology (edge polygons and vertices, degenerate edges collapsed), and requires every edge in exactly two triangles, consistent winding, and no pinch vertices. Defects are reported with a location and adjacent face IDs. It walks the same deflection ladder the downstream gate uses (1, 4, 16, 32) with a one-million-triangle ceiling, and runs in a bounded subprocess (`AGENTCAD_MESH_VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_S`, default 60 s) so a pathological part yields `status: timeout` and `is_valid: null` instead of a hang.
- **`inspect`**: the structural-validation phase runs the layered validator; the payload gains `validation`; `is_valid` is the verdict; notes explain the failing layer instead of explaining away a contradiction.
- **Docs**: `docs inspect` describes the new `is_valid` meaning and the `validation` object.

## Evidence

- Internal oracle over 412 retained candidate STEPs against the official CADGenBench gate: **393 agree-pass, 19 agree-fail, 0 AgentCAD-only pass, 0 gate-only pass, 0 undetermined.** The Slice 0 baseline was 18 AgentCAD-only passes. Report: internal `benchmarks/comparisons/20260905_m71_slice1_inspect_parity.md`.
- The first cut rejected 15 valid parts. Three stitching and sizing fixes closed that: closed-edge orientation chosen by whole-polygon alignment, degenerate-edge nodes merged, and the gate's deflection ladder adopted. Those are documented in the report and pinned by tests.
- Cost over the corpus: median 2.5 s per `inspect --summary`, 90th percentile 3.7 s, max 72 s on the 17.9 MB kernel-invalid fixture 202 (the pre-existing kernel check dominates there).

## Tests

- `tests/test_validation.py`: 33 contract tests against the fixture catalog (every case's verdict and failing layer), both real-world parts staying deliverable, localized evidence, bounded worker, timeout yielding `null`, ladder and ceiling behavior.
- `tests/test_inspect_graceful.py`: the open-shell case moves from "valid with a note" to "not valid, shell_closure named".
- Full public suite minus the daemon tests: 1217 passed, 7 skipped (run with an absolute `PYTHONPATH`; the CLI tests change directory, so a relative one makes the worker import the wrong checkout).
- Fresh-agent friction check (sub-agent with only the CLI and docs, build123d project, bracket with holes and fillet, a deliberately open shell, and edge-touching cubes): the open-shell inspect answered all four questions (not deliverable, which layer, which edges with endpoints, what to do) and the valid parts raised nothing alarming. Fixes applied from its findings: the shell-closure suggestion no longer points at `--ids` for data already in the response; valid multi-solid parts get a note saying they are separate bodies; `kernel_load` duration now reflects the load phase; docs state what `--validate-only` skips, that `suggestion` appears only on failure, what `ladder_divisor` and `budget_s` mean, and that `free_edge_count` is zero on a closed solid with through-holes.

## Known and deferred to Slice 1b (expected from this PR's scope)

The friction run confirmed the contract split this PR leaves in place: `run` and `measure` still report the kernel-only `is_valid` and a 6400 mm3 "volume" for an open shell that `inspect` then rejects. Slice 1b moves `compute_metrics`, `run`, `import`, `measure`, `check-spec`, and `recover` onto the shared verdict and adds `--validation-profile`. Also noted for later: the edit-risk workflow text mentions "heal/sew" without a documented helper (pre-existing), and `docs validation` still describes only static checks (it now points to `docs inspect` for geometry).
