author: chelseakr
body:
Refs #78, #92, #93, #94, #96, #100, #109, #110, #111, #114. **Closes nothing, deliberately.**

Six groups. Every one was reviewed adversarially and needed a fix round. Every one advanced its issue and none closed it, because each remaining issue either waits on a run only CI can perform, or asks for a decision that is the maintainer's.

## Gates

**#114 — the SAST gate now reads the scan instead of trusting its exit code.** `tools/sast_gate.py` answers in the three states of ADR 0008: a file the parser could not finish, and a tracked source under `src` or `tools` the scan never opened, are exit 2 and fail the job. A partial parse used to be a warning that left the job green over the unread remainder of a safety module.

The reviewer caught a false claim in the first version, and the fix is the interesting part. The gate's documentation said CI and a maintainer judge the same scan; only the argument list was shared. CI pins Semgrep 1.168.0, while `make sast` ran whatever was on `PATH`. Measured on this machine, 1.175.0 parses the exact construct the pinned scanner cannot, so a maintainer would have seen "clean" over the thing that broke CI. The gate now reads the version from the report, refuses a report that does not name its scanner, and exits 2 on drift with `ALLOW_SEMGREP_VERSION_DRIFT=1` as the deliberate override, mirroring `make secret-scan`.

**#93 — measured, nothing split.** The issue warned that splitting the gate wrongly is worse than leaving it, so this measures and records rather than acting: per-stage timings, per-module CPU, and a `make claims` check holding the prices against the stages and modules that exist, failing in both directions. No option taken. The issue stays open with the measurement as its record.

**#78 — claims corrected, no fault newly exercised.** F-002's refusal is now known to fire on the declared name use alone, over a faithful name too, so it is a contract that cannot express the fault rather than a mechanism that detects it. Six rows remain not yet exercisable.

## Decision records

Four ADRs, all `Status: proposed`, each with a recommendation and no decision recorded: what the pattern gate closes (#110), what a derived status column may assert (#111), what narrowing a published contract costs before the first tag (#109), and the removed document the host still serves (#92).

Two are `accepted`, and they record engineering choices already implemented and merged rather than anything awaiting you: the dependency audit's third state (ADR 0011) and the SAST partial parse (ADR 0012).

`docs/OPEN-DECISIONS.md` assembles the evidence for #100, #96 and #94 the same way.

**One thing the review repriced.** The memo first recommended dispatching `package.yml` as costless. Its `provenance` job has no ref guard, so a dispatch would attest a wheel built from `version = "0.1.0"` — a durable version claim, which contradicts the memo's own cost line. The recommendation now says so and names the guard as an option rather than adding it, because that would pre-answer #100.

## The exposure

**#92 is still live.** Re-measured against the host today: the subject is still served, the repository has one fork. body:
Adds `mcpplibs.tinyhttps@0.3.0` for Linux, macOS and Windows.

Upstream: [mcpplibs/tinyhttps#17](https://github.com/mcpplibs/tinyhttps/pull/17) · [release 0.3.0](https://github.com/mcpplibs/tinyhttps/releases/tag/0.3.0). It closes [#15](https://github.com/mcpplibs/tinyhttps/issues/15) — a socket whose body was not read to the end went back into the connection pool, and the next request read the leftovers as its status line — and [#16](https://github.com/mcpplibs/tinyhttps/issues/16), a write to a departed peer killing the host process with `SIGPIPE`. Eleven pool-invariant defects in total; the issue named two of them.

## Release and source evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| Tag commit | `40c1a4f` |
| GLOBAL | `https://github.com/mcpplibs/tinyhttps/archive/refs/tags/0.3.0.tar.gz` |
| CN | `https://gitcode.com/mcpp-res/tinyhttps/releases/download/0.3.0/tinyhttps-0.3.0.tar.gz` |
| SHA256 | `acb4d494bae2030632f4d91e4e8420cee9aed4560e4d0a6876e85232d2ba67f9` |

The GitHub archive was downloaded twice independently and both copies carried that digest. The CN mirror was uploaded from the first of them, and a fresh CN download is byte-identical (89080 bytes, HTTP 200).

## Verification

- `mcpp xpkg parse pkgs/t/tinyhttps.lua` → `parse OK`, Form A, 0.3.0 present in all three platform tables.
- `luac -p` on the descriptor.
- `mcpp test` in `tests/examples/tinyhttps` against **both** mirrors from a cleared cache — including the project-local `.mcpp/` registry, which otherwise short-circuits the download. Each run reported `Downloading mcpplibs.tinyhttps v0.3.0` and left an archive with the digest above, so neither URL is recorded on the strength of the other.

## Package shape

Unchanged. The upstream archive still ships its own `mcpp.toml`, so the Form A descriptor needs no `mcpp` segment and no inline recipe. 0.3.0 adds no index-level optional component, so no feature gate.

Two additions inside the tarball are worth noting even though they change nothing here: `templates/` (so `mcpp new --template tinyhttps[:fetch|download|stream]` works once this lands) and `examples/openkal/`. Its `mcpp.lock` is gone — the file does not pin anything, and eight of the ten mcpplibs packages already ignore it.

## Smoke example

Moved to 0.3.0 and given three assertions, chosen because they are the ones a version bump could break rather than because they are new:

- `parse_status_line` accepts `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and **rejects** `BBBB 999 XHTTP/1.1 200 OK` — the exact input from the issue, where every reader used to take the first run of digits it found and report an ordinary `999`.
- `bodyComplete` / `bodyError`, the new fields, hold their documented defaults.
- `HttpResponse{204, "No Content", {}, {}}` still compiles. That line is **unchanged from the 0.2.9 example** and is the whole compatibility claim for 0.3.0's added fields: they are appended, so a four-initialiser aggregate initialisation keeps working and `ok()` keeps meaning what it meant.

author: neuralempowerment
body:
`just bump-version` updated 11 manifests and `just check-version` printed **"OK: All 11 files at vX"** — while `uv.lock` (8 workspace-package records) and three plugin schema `$id` values sat stale. A green `check-version` was not evidence the bump was complete. This PR makes the script cover all 15 and makes `just bump-version` regenerate `uv.lock` then re-run `--check`.

That premise was re-checked independently against real commands in this rework and holds.

**A cross-model review of the original hand-written version of this PR returned "request changes"** with one correctness blocker and one design weakness, both real. This PR has been reworked (commit `aa8321ef`, on top of a merge of `origin/main`) to fix both. Everything below concerns the reworked state.

## Blocker 1 — accepted version language was broader than the normalisation

`SEMVER_RE` accepted arbitrary SemVer prerelease identifiers. `to_pep440()` only rewrote the exact substrings `-alpha.`, `-beta.`, `-rc.` and preserved numeric spelling verbatim. uv canonicalises PEP 440 far more broadly. Because `just bump-version` now always runs `uv lock` and then re-runs `--check`, an accepted input could leave a repo uv considers consistent while `--check` reported it stale — a bump failing its own gate with nothing wrong to fix.

Reviewer's table, reproduced against the uv actually installed here (uv 0.11.8):

```
input             accepted  to_pep440       uv lock
0.29.0-beta.9     yes       0.29.0b9        0.29.0b9      ok
0.29.0-alpha.1    yes       0.29.0a1        0.29.0a1      ok
0.29.0-rc.2       yes       0.29.0rc2       0.29.0rc2     ok
0.29.0-beta.09    yes       0.29.0b09       0.29.0b9      MISMATCH
0.29.0-beta1      yes       0.29.0-beta1    0.29.0b1      MISMATCH
0.29.0-alpha      yes       0.29.0-alpha    0.29.0a0      MISMATCH
0.29.0-dev.1      yes       0.29.0-dev.1    0.29.0.dev1   MISMATCH
0.29.0-rc.1.2     yes       0.29.0rc1.2     ERROR: invalid version
```

**Fix — option (a), narrowed the grammar.** `VERSION_RE` now accepts exactly `X.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z-{alpha,beta,rc}.N`, all numerals canonical and non-zero-leading — the language `to_pep440` actually normalises correctly. Rejection happens in `parse_version()` before any manifest is written, preserving the existing pre-validate-then-write property. Every tag this project has ever cut fits the narrowed grammar (historical tags only use `beta.N`). The pre-existing test that treated `rc.1.2` as valid was updated deliberately with a comment explaining why the grammar narrowed — not silently deleted.

Tests parameterise over every accepted prerelease branch (stable, alpha, beta, rc) and drive the assertion from a real `uv lock` run against a fixture repo, not a hardcoded expectation. Rejected forms — all five mismatch/error rows from the table above, plus a non-version input — are asserted to fail before any file is touched.

## Blocker 2 — the eight-package check could silently become seven

Workspace membership was glob-derived (`apps/*`, `packages/*` with exclusions) but `LOCKFILE_PACKAGES` duplicated the owned package names by hand. The reviewer proved the list can shrink undetected: removing `syn-tokens` from the list left the full targeted suite green (30 passed, exit 0) — a ninth-package addition would land in `uv.lock` automatically while `--check` stayed unaware, reproducing exactly the hardcoded-list drift this PR exists to fix.

**Fix.** Owned Python package membership is now derived mechanically from the root `[tool.uv.workspace]` configuration rather than hand-listed, then cross-checked against `uv.lock`'s actual workspace source paths. The four independently-versioned submodule packages (`agentic-events`, `agentic-isolation`, `agentic-logging`, `event-sourcing-python`) are excluded via one explicit exclusion set. A real-tree invariant test asserts `owned_packages()` agrees with `uv.lock`'s actual workspace records, so a future disagreement between the derivation and the real lockfile fails a test rather than passing silently. The Node manifest list remains an explicit allowlist (pnpm's workspace has one independently-versioned package mixed in) but is now checked against actual pnpm workspace membership in a dedicated test.

**Proof it bites**, reproduced in this rework: adding a `syn-tokens`-style exclusion inside `owned_packages()` failed four tests (per-package stale-lock test, missing-lock-record test, the real-repository derivation-vs-`uv.lock` invariant, and a missing-version-field atomicity test) — confirmed present in `git diff`, confirmed the tests fail, then reverted with a clean `git diff`.

## Hazard already fixed — not regressed

An earlier revision used absolute paths computed at import, so `bump()` escaped its tmpdir during tests and wrote `0.29.0` into the real `schemas/plugin/`. Paths now resolve at call time via `schema_files()` / `lockfile()`. `git status --porcelain` was confirmed blank both before and after the full test suite in this rework (see verification below) — no accidental writes to the real checkout.

## Real command output (from independent verification at `aa8321ef`)

Environment for cache-writing commands: `TMPDIR=/workspace/.tmp XDG_CACHE_HOME=/workspace/.cache UV_CACHE_DIR=/workspace/.cache/uv`

```
$ just preflight-agent
✅ preflight-agent: every static gate that RUNS in a workspace passed
   Not run here (no toolchain in the image): vsa-validate, fitness,
   codegen-check, check-submodules, check-compose-overlays,
   check-default-workspace-image, check-pinned-image-channels.
   CI runs all of those. Run 'just preflight' on a dev machine.
```

```
$ uv run pytest -m unit -q
................                                                         [100%]
```
(3 skips, 2 expected failures — the pre-existing TODO(#444) manager-routing tests — no failures.)

```
$ uv run pytest scripts/workflows/test_bump_version.py -q
........................................................................ [ 86%]
...........                                                              [100%]
```
(83 tests collected)

```
$ uv run ruff check scripts/workflows/
All checks passed!
```

```
$ uv run python scripts/workflows/bump_version.py --check
OK: all 15 version-carrying files at v0.28.0
```

`git status --porcelain` was blank before the gates and blank after the full suite ran, and remained blank after all mutation attacks below were restored.

## Mutations run and what each killed

1. **Broaden prerelease numerals to accept leading zeroes** (`(0|[1-9]\d*)` → `\d+`, accepting `0.29.0-beta.09`). Killed by `TestParseVersion::test_rejected[0.29.0-beta.09]` and `TestBump::test_rejected_version_touches_nothing[0.29.0-beta.09]` — the latter showed the mutated code had actually written all 14 non-lock files, confirming the atomic-rejection assertion is not vacuous.
2. **Silently remove one owned Python package** (excluded `syn-tokens` inside `owned_packages()`). Killed 4 tests: per-package stale-lock test, missing-lock-record test, the real-repository derivation-vs-`uv.lock` invariant, and a missing-version-field atomicity test. This is the exact drift the reviewer proved was undetected in the original PR — now caught.
3. **Silently remove one Node manifest** (removed `apps/syn-docs/package.json` from `PACKAGE_JSON_RELPATHS`). Killed `TestNodeManifestList::test_matches_pnpm_workspace` and `TestBump::test_updates_every_owned_manifest_and_schema`.
4. **Silently remove one plugin schema** (filtered `triggers.schema.json` out of `schema_files()`). Killed `TestCheckConsistency::test_stale_schema_id_fails` and `TestBump::test_updates_every_owned_manifest_and_schema`.
5. **Inspect only the first lock record** (`owned_packages()[:1]`, then corrupted the second item, `apps/syn-api`). Killed the parameterized per-member invariant test, confirming the assertion reaches every record, not just the first.

Every mutation was confirmed present in `git diff`, confirmed to fail the suite, then restored to an empty diff.

author: tigerblue77
body:
secretsFromFiles resolves <NAME>_FILE for five prefixes -- POSTFIX_, POSTFIXMASTER_, POSTMAP_, OPENDKIM_ and POSTSRSD_ -- and tests/test_secrets.py names all five in its module docstring. Only three were ever set by a test: POSTMAP_sasl_passwd_FILE, OPENDKIM_DOMAINS_FILE and POSTSRSD_SRS_DOMAIN_FILE. POSTFIX_<name>_FILE and POSTFIXMASTER_<name>_FILE had none.

The case for leaving it there is that this is one loop with a prefix-agnostic body, so the POSTMAP_ tests already walk every line of it -- the *_FILE filter, the suffix strip, the "is also set" branch, the unreadable-path refusal, the printf -v -- and the only regression a new test can catch is somebody deleting one of two words from the "for file in" list. Measured, that regression is both silent and complete: with "${!POSTFIX_*} ${!POSTFIXMASTER_*}" removed from that line, the suite as it stood is 237 passed, 1 skipped, while myhostname quietly stays at the image default, submission/inet never exists at all, and the container comes up and reports healthy. Two words on one line, with nothing between them and a released image.

Three tests, sharing one relay through postfix_shared because all three only read it back:

  - a POSTFIX_ setting from a file is what the relay runs with. Not postconf alone: myhostname is what the greeting says, so the banner is postfix's own reading of the value rather than main.cf read back.
  - a master.cf service from a file is added -- deliberately the same service and the same assertion as tests/test_config.py, so that what differs is only the route the value took. The "__" to "/" rule and the _FILE suffix meet on one name here and nowhere else.
  - the _FILE variable itself configures nothing, which is the unset that ends secretsFromFiles.

That last one is the half of #270 that was not quite as reported, and it is worth writing down. The unset was already caught for OPENDKIM_: without it, OPENDKIM_DOMAINS_FILE reaches the opendkim.conf rebuild, which skips only the exact name OPENDKIM_DOMAINS, opendkim rejects the whole file, and startService exits 1 above the postfix start -- so the existing domain-list test fails, but on "the container exited with 1 instead of answering on port 25", which reads as an opendkim regression and never names the unset. Through the two prefixes added here it was not caught at all, and both traces are quiet: postconf -e takes a parameter it does not know, so main.cf simply grows "myhostname_FILE = /run/secrets/myhostname" behind an unused-parameter warning, and postconf -Me refuses "submission/inet_FILE=..." with a fatal that run, having no set -e, never sees. The two assertions are on exactly those two traces.

CLAUDE.md 15 gets the test citation its neighbours carry and it had none of, and 17's "names the same five" becomes "exercises the same five", which is now true. README.md is unchanged: no user-visible behaviour moved, and the per-file table already has its row.

Tested on the built image: tests/test_secrets.py is 10 passed and the suite is 240 passed, 1 skipped. Verified against the two mutations these tests exist for. Deleting "unset $file" fails test_the_file_variable_itself_configures_nothing on 'myhostname_FILE' is contained here in main.cf, and, with the assertions reversed to reach it, on

  postconf: fatal: bad field count: "submission/inet_FILE=/run/secrets/submission"

Deleting the two prefixes from the loop fails all three of the new tests -- myhostname reading back as "hostname", postconf answering 'unmatched request: "submission/inet"' -- and, across the whole suite, nothing else.

Closes #270


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019XkYQc1Eh7QpuXBmkPbWEU

author: issaus2020
body:
Zwei Themen in einem Zweig.

## 1. Startbildschirm

**Der Kopf zeigt wieder die Zielmenge:** „380 von 605 ml heute". Der Satz zur
Lage („Etwas weniger als üblich bisher …") ist dafür raus – er war entweder
überflüssig, weil die Zahl darüber dasselbe sagt, oder er hat beschönigt. Was
wirklich auffällt, steht in der Ampel weiter unten, und die soll niemand neben
einem freundlichen Satz überlesen. Damit fallen auch die Sprüche selbst und
ihre Auswahllogik weg.

**Die Figur steht jetzt oben.** Bisher schob sich die Schnelleingabe davor,
sodass das Baby erst beim Scrollen auftauchte. Gemessen im Gerät (390×844):
Figur bei 313–501, Regler bei 630–660, Leiste ab 777 – beides ohne Scrollen zu
sehen. Laufender Timer und Schlafschalter rücken dahinter.

**Jede neue Mahlzeit lässt das Baby einmal schaukeln.** Der Zählerstand der
heutigen Mahlzeiten ist zugleich der React-`key` der Figur: Er hängt sie neu
ein, damit die Animation auch beim zweiten und dritten Mal von vorn läuft.

**Erreichtes wird gefeiert**, beim Trinken wie beim Gewicht:

| | |
|---|---|
| Tagesziel erreicht | Konfetti an der Figur, dazu ein Siegel in der Überschrift und ein warmer Schein hinter dem Baby, die stehen bleiben |
| Zunahme im Erwartungsbereich | eigene Meilenstein-Zeile mit der Rechnung dahinter |
| Geburtsgewicht wieder erreicht | ebenso, mit dem Lebenstag |

Gefeiert wird der **Moment, nicht der Zustand**: `useJustHappened` hält beim
Öffnen fest, wie es stand, und lässt Konfetti nur fliegen, wenn die Schwelle
danach fällt. Wer abends öffnet und das Ziel längst erreicht hat, sieht das
Siegel – aber kein Konfetti bei jedem Blick. Bewegung respektiert
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

## 2. Einladungslink nur zum Ansehen

Unter *Konto & Teilen* gibt es den Link jetzt zweimal: **zum Mitschreiben** für
die Person, die das Kind mit betreut, und **nur zum Ansehen** für Großeltern,
Hebamme oder Kinderärztin.

### Der Schutz sitzt in der Datenbank

Die Mitgliedschaft trägt eine Rolle (`editor` oder `viewer`), der
Einladungscode ebenso. Die eine Richtlinie für `entries` ist in vier zerlegt:
`select` für jedes Mitglied, `insert`/`update`/`delete` nur für `editor`.
Dasselbe gilt für das Umbenennen des Bereichs. Auch mit selbstgebauten Anfragen
kommt ein Beobachter damit nicht ans Schreiben.

`create_invite` verlangt jetzt die Editor-Rolle – sonst könnte sich ein
Beobachter Mitschreibende dazuholen und die Beschränkung so umgehen.
`redeem_invite` übernimmt die Rolle aus dem Code, hebt aber niemanden herab: Ein
Beobachter-Link nimmt einer Editorin nicht das Schreibrecht, ein
Mitschreib-Link macht aus einem Beobachter dagegen eine Editorin.

Bestehende Datenbanken laufen unverändert weiter: Die Spalten kommen per
`add column if not exists` mit Vorgabe `editor` dazu.

### Die App bietet gar nicht erst an, was scheitern würde

- Der Abgleich **holt, lädt aber nichts hoch**. Ohne diese Bremse liefe jeder
  Durchgang in einen abgewiesenen Schreibversuch und die App meldete dauerhaft
  „Abgleich fehlgeschlagen", obwohl alles in Ordnung ist.
- Die Schreibaktionen im Store sind für Beobachter wirkungslos – sonst entstünde
  lokal ein Bestand, den der Server nie annimmt, und die Ansichten liefen still
  auseinander.
- Eingabe-Knöpfe, Bearbeiten- und Löschsymbole entfallen auf allen Tabs; die
  Profilfelder sind gesperrt und sehen auch so aus. Im Kopf steht auf jedem Tab
  „Nur Ansicht", damit niemand nach einem Knopf sucht, den es nicht gibt.
- Die Geräte-Einstellungen (Design, Anrede) bleiben bedienbar: Die gehören dem
  Gerät, nicht dem Bereich.

### Nebenbei behoben

Die App liegt in einem Raster ohne gesetzte Spalte. Dessen Mindestbreite ist der
Inhalt – eine einzige lange, nicht umbrechbare Zeile im Kopf machte damit die
ganze Seite breiter als den Bildschirm und alles seitlich verschiebbar.
`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` stellt das ab.

## Geprüft

- 122 Tests (5 neue), `tsc -b --noEmit`, `eslint .`, `vite build` sauber
- **Das Schema gegen ein echtes Postgres 16 gefahren**, mit nachgebautem
  `auth.uid()`. Zweiter Lauf fehlerfrei (wiederholbar). Durchgespielt: Vater
  legt Bereich an und trägt ein → Beobachter-Code → Großmutter tritt bei, sieht
  den Eintrag. Ihre fünf Schreibversuche (anlegen, ändern, löschen, einladen,
  Bereich umbenennen) scheitern alle, Lesen geht weiter. Mitschreib-Link macht
  sie zur Editorin, ein Beobachter-Link nimmt ihr das Recht nicht wieder weg,
  Codes gelten einmal, Unbeteiligte sehen null Einträge.
- Im laufenden Browser durchgespielt: eine Mahlzeit unter dem Ziel schaukelt
  ohne Konfetti, eine darüber schaukelt und feiert; eine neue Wägung ins Soll
  löst die Gewichts-Feier aus. Beide Rollen verglichen – Beobachter ohne Regler,
  ohne Kachelreihe, ohne Bearbeiten-Knöpfe, mit gesperrtem Profil; Editor
  unverändert. Hell und dunkel, keine Konsolenfehler.

## Danach im Supabase-Projekt

`supabase/schema.sql` muss einmal neu im SQL-Editor laufen, sonst gibt es die
Rollen dort noch nicht. Bis dahin verhält sich alles wie bisher – ohne das neue
Schema meldet `my_family_role` nichts, und die App bleibt beim Schreibrecht.

author: yneveu
body:
Frees the **Canon Zoemini 2** (PV-223) from the Canon Mini Print app.

Verified end to end on hardware: identity, status, settings read/write, and printing.

## Protocol

Canon's `printer2` family, over **Bluetooth Classic** — no BLE at all, so `bleak` never sees this printer.

- 34-byte big-endian packets on **RFCOMM SPP channel 1**
- Start code differs by direction: `43 0F` client→printer, `43 F0` printer→client
- The photo is streamed as a **raw JPEG** down the same socket in 650-byte chunks — no framing, no wrapper
- Image is **640×1608**, deliberately not the 2:3 aspect of the print: the pixels are non-square and the printer undoes the distortion itself

## Two traps, both of which fail as complete silence

Neither produces an error, which is what makes them expensive:

1. **Pairing is mandatory.** Unpaired, channel 1 accepts the connection and then ignores every packet.
2. **Canon ships one app for two incompatible protocol families.** PV = printer only (Zoemini, Zoemini 2), ZV = printer with camera (Zoemini S, S2). Only the PV-223 line speaks `printer2`; legacy frames get no reply at all.

The device README records both, along with the wrong turns taken before landing on the right family.

## Also included

`driver/probe.py`, a device-agnostic transport reconnaissance tool: scans both radios, decodes the Class of Device, sweeps RFCOMM channels with the errnos interpreted, and dumps GATT. It is what identified this printer, and should help with the next one.

## Notes

- The printer is discovered by name; `--address` skips the scan.
- Factory auto-power-off is 3 minutes, short enough to make hand-timed testing unwinnable. The driver polls for the printer, and `--set-auto-off 10` raises the delay.
- Bluetooth Classic needs `socket.AF_BLUETOOTH`, which the standalone CPython builds shipped by `uv` lack — use a distro Python. Only Pillow is required.
- Hardware identifiers in the docs are anonymised.

author: lance0
body:
Correct TABLE_DUMP_V2 Add-Path entries to encode and decode Peer Index, Originated Time, then Path Identifier, as specified by RFC 8050. Both the snapshot reader and CLI MRT adapter recognize IPv6 unicast subtype 10; subtype 9 follows the unsupported IPv4 multicast path. Non-Add-Path encoding is unchanged.

The CLI adapter also rejects bytes left after a RIB record's declared entries. A malformed later record now refuses the entire conversion without emitting partial routes or a misleading completion trailer.

Warm manifests now use format version 2 and reject all version-1 bundles before opening their snapshot. Old malformed entries can otherwise pass semantic validation with silently swapped metadata. Regenerate checkpoints with a new coordinated shutdown; directory names, Rust type names, and policy-digest framing remain unchanged. The daemon does not restore these artifacts at boot.

Independent byte-vector regressions cover both entry encoders and readers, IPv4 and IPv6, zero and nonzero path IDs, truncated entries, invalid peer indexes, and unchanged legacy bytes. CLI record-boundary tests cover zero and nonzero entry counts across ordinary and Add-Path IPv4/IPv6 records, including no partial output after a valid preceding record. Bundle tests cover historical malformed input, version rejection before artifact access, and fresh publication. The canonical fuzz seed and current upgrade documentation are updated.

Validation: full workspace tests, strict workspace Clippy, all rustdoc targets, formatting, offline links, repository contracts, fuzz inventory, the canonical manifest seed replay, and both CI MRT snapshot benchmark smoke modes pass.

body:
…e-fix

Undersøgte "vises ikke i Jagten" mod det live projekt igen, samme disciplin som sidst: dataen og RLS er stadig fejlfri (verificeret på ny med en rolled-back RLS-simulering som netop den bruger). Den mest sandsynlige forklaring er nu appens egen PWA-opdatering, ikke en resterende databasefejl — se nedenfor.

Ny funktionalitet:
- Redigér (✎) og slet (🗑) på egne steder, kun synligt hvor `isUserSpot` er sand. Redigering er en inline-formular i selve rangeringsrækken, samme mønster som "+ Tilføj mit eget sted". Sletning bekræftes (native confirm — irreversibel handling), og falder aktivSpotId tilbage til et systemsted, hvis det slettede var aktivt.
- Et nyt sted bliver nu automatisk det aktive sted fra selve `addUserSpot` i AppContext, ikke kun fra UI-komponenten der kalder den — samme garanti uanset hvor et sted oprettes fra i fremtiden.
- Migration 0012: `spots_update` manglede en WITH CHECK. Uden den kunne en håndlavet PATCH (uden om appens UI) ændre `source` fra 'user' til 'system' på ens eget sted, hvilket ville gøre det offentligt læsbart via `spots_read`s regel. Rettet, og `spots_delete` tilføjet i samme omgang. Anvendt direkte på det live projekt og verificeret.

Sandsynlig rodårsag til "virker stadig ikke, selvom du sagde du rettede det": `registerType: 'autoUpdate'` (vite.config.ts) installerer en ny service worker i baggrunden, men uden en `controllerchange`-lytter tager den først effekt på den ANDEN genindlæsning efter en udrulning — den første henter bare selve den nye service worker. Tilføjet i main.tsx, så en ny version nu slår igennem på næste genindlæsning, ikke den efter den.

Verificeret direkte i browseren (midlertidig SessionRepo-kørsel): nyt sted vises straks i Jagten uden ekstra klik, redigering omdøber korrekt i den rangerede liste, sletning fjerner stedet og falder aktivSpotId tilbage til Gribskov. Genbekræftede bagefter mod det live projekt at den resterende ægte "Rønneholmsvej 29"-række stadig læses korrekt under de strammede politikker. 64/64 tests, build grøn.

## Summary

Update the repository workflow so GitHub MCP remains the preferred GitHub integration while local Git can publish an exact signed commit when MCP cannot transfer local Git objects. Keep application and validation work in the devcontainer, and make planning inventory-first.

## Description

- `AGENTS.md`: defines the verified remote `main` baseline, the devcontainer boundary, the local Git fallback, the `gh` last-resort rule, and the inventory-first planner requirement.
- `.codex/skills/sk-home-orchestrator/SKILL.md`: aligns orchestration, publication, signature checks, and the gateway inventory requirement with that policy.
- `.codex/skills/sk-home-orchestrator/references/planner.md`: requires the authoritative interface and VLAN inventory pair, plus DHCP inventory for address-allocation work, before planning.
- `.codex/skills/sk-home-create-pr/SKILL.md`: documents MCP-first publication and PR creation with local Git fallback for exact signed commits.
- `README.md`: updates the user-facing workflow, keeps operational examples centered on GitHub MCP dispatch, documents the last-resort `gh` fallback, and uses `act --secret-file .env` for local trusted-workflow testing.

This change updates policy and documentation only. It does not change infrastructure, firewall rules, credentials, or deployment behavior.

## Validation

- Ran `mise exec -- pre-commit run --all-files` inside the repository devcontainer.
- Ran repository policy-reference checks inside the repository devcontainer.
- Ran `git diff --check`.
- Reviewed the final tree against remote `main` with GitHub MCP.
- GitHub MCP verified the published commit signature and exact tree.

## Risks

The local Git publication fallback depends on a configured signing identity and Git transport credential. GitHub MCP remains the preferred path for supported remote operations, and `gh` is documented only as a last resort when MCP and local Git cannot perform the required operation.

## Cause
Quick Setup creates 50+ starter foods and performs Pexels search, image download, GD analysis, WebP rendering, and database image attachment inside the same onboarding request and database transaction. nginx can time out before PHP finishes, and the admin client then renders the raw 504 HTML as its error message.

## Fix
- Commit restaurant structure and starter menu before any external photo request.
- Load starter photos afterward in resumable, one-item HTTP batches.
- Add a soft per-item image-processing budget and candidate cap.
- Preserve custom restaurant images and all existing additive/idempotent rules.
- Render a clean timeout/recovery message instead of raw gateway HTML.
- Reuse the same batched flow for `Complete starter menu` and manual photo refresh.

## Safety
- No database migration or schema change.
- No delete/reset behavior.
- No payment, checkout, tenant routing, or customer ordering changes.
- A photo failure cannot roll back an already completed restaurant setup.

## Validation
- `node --check` passed for both modified Quick Setup JavaScript files.
- Local batch harness passed cursor progression, aggregate progress, button recovery, and raw-504 sanitization.
- PHP CLI is not present in the analysis environment; run `php -l` on the three PHP files before deployment.

author: claude[bot]
body:
A commit carries **check runs** and **commit statuses** as two disjoint sets on
two endpoints, and neither endpoint mentions the other's rows. `merge-gate.mjs`
and `ci-watch.mjs` read only the first, so `GREEN — all 19 registered checks
settled and passing` was a claim about `/check-runs` alone — printed, twice
today, on a head whose `merge-gate` commit status read `failure` and whose
`mergeable_state` stayed `unstable`. The names differ by one word:
`merge-gate-job` is the check run, `merge-gate` is the status.

`pr-board.mjs` already read both and its comment at `pr-board.mjs:115` states
the principle (#4739). The lesson was encoded in the board and not in the gate.

Fixes #5022
Fixes #5317

## One reader, and who calls it

`merge-gate-core.mjs` gains the shared vocabulary; the three tools present it
three ways rather than each deriving it.

- `reachedAVerdict` — the **existing** cancelled-run predicate (#4800, #4802),
  now exported rather than restated. Its two duplicates are deleted;
  `git grep -an 'conclusion !== "cancelled"'` returns one line.
- `ciRows({checkRuns, statuses, ignoreCheck})` → rows of
  `{source, name, state, detail, url, id}`, `state ∈ pending|failed|success`,
  plus `noVerdict` for a name whose every run was cancelled. `neutral` sits
  with `success`/`skipped` as the gate already had it — `pr-board.mjs` omitted
  `neutral` and is now aligned.
- `rowName(row)` → `check-run e2e (6)` / `status merge-gate`. **The source is
  in the name everywhere a row is printed**, because the collision is the trap.
- `ciVerdict({checkRuns, statuses, ignoreCheck, head})` replaces
  `checkRunsVerdict`.

`merge-gate.mjs` → `ciVerdict`. `ci-watch.mjs` → `ciRows` + `reachedAVerdict` +
`rowName`. `pr-board.mjs` → `ciRows` + `rowName`, reusing its own existing
two-endpoint fetch rather than adding a third reader.

Unreadable is its own state per tool: the gate exits 2 through `gh` (refuse,
never ignore); `ci-watch` exits 2; `pr-board` turned a failed read into `?? []`
and printed GREEN off half the evidence — it now prints `status?` and
`<<< commit statuses UNREADABLE`.

## The gate must not block on its own status

`.github/workflows/merge-gate.yml` posts the `merge-gate` status **by running
this script**. A gate that counted its own context would read back its own last
answer: a stale `failure` closes the gate, the workflow re-runs the gate, the
gate reads the failure it just posted and posts it again — a self-block with no
way out, in the one tool whose refusal stops every merge. That context is
excluded and recomputed; **every other context counts**, which is the half the
issue exists for.

Both directions are one fixture pair, driven through the real CLI so the status
fetch is exercised (`the self-block, both directions`):

- `merge-gate` = failure → **exit 0, GATE OPEN**
- `deploy` = failure → **exit 1, GATE CLOSED**, `red on this head: status deploy`

`merge-gate-workflow.test.ts` now pins the workflow's published context to
`GATE_STATUS_CONTEXT`, so the exclusion cannot silently stop matching.

Live, on an open PR whose gate status is failing right now:

```
PASS: all 19 check run(s) and 0 independent commit status(es) green on this head.
This head's own `merge-gate` status (failed) is THIS script's last answer and is
recomputed here, not read.
```

## Settlement that cannot green one check early (#5317)

Two matching fingerprints both landed before `merge-gate-job` registered, so
the watcher greened at 19 a minute before the twentieth arrived — and the late
check is the merge gate itself. `mergeable_state` held the contradiction on
screen the whole time.

It cannot simply block settlement: a non-passing status makes a PR `unstable`
too, and this repo posts `merge-gate = failure` on every pre-review head, so
"never settle while unstable" hangs on every healthy PR. So it blocks only
while **unexplained** — every check run and every status we can read is green
and GitHub still says `unstable`, which means something we cannot see yet. In
#5317's own measurement that head had no statuses at all, so it is unexplained
and now blocks.

Exit 2 says which condition it waits on:

```
UNSETTLED — waiting on: mergeable_state=unstable while every check run and commit
status we can read is green — a check has not registered yet (#5317). This is NOT
a verdict; re-invoke.
```

The RAW/filtered split is untouched: fingerprints still take `runs` before
filtering, and **statuses are deliberately out of the fingerprint** — a status
is replaced in place under its context, so folding it in would move the
fingerprint every time the gate re-posts the same verdict. The shipped
"cancelled run arriving between polls" fixture still reds under a
filtered-fingerprint mutation.

## What `ci-watch` now prints

```
GREEN — all 19 check run(s) settled and passing; 1 commit status(es) read, 1 not green.
NOT MERGEABLE YET — status merge-gate failed: gate CLOSED — no exact-head receipt: no review states this head SHA
  That is a commit status, not a check run, and merge-gate.mjs recomputes it before every merge.
```

Verbatim from a live `--once` run. The word *passing* never covers a row that
is not — the count says **read**, and the closed context gets its own line.

## The one deviation, upheld

A failing `merge-gate` status does **not** make `ci-watch` exit non-zero, which
departs from #5022's second acceptance criterion for exactly that one context.
`dispatch.md` runs `ci-watch` at step 3 and the receipt is posted at step 4, so
`merge-gate = failure` ("no exact-head receipt") is the normal state of a
healthy PR at the moment anyone asks whether CI is green — measured: five open
PRs whose only red is that context. Exiting 1 on all of them is how a check
becomes noise. What the criterion protects is that a failing status not be
invisible, and it is not. Every **independent** failing context still exits 1.
Ruled on #5022 (comment 5552233654) along with five others: unattributable
statuses count rather than needing an allowlist; `blocked` is not treated like
`unstable`; `merge-gate-core.mjs` keeps its name in this change; and the +90
net production lines are claimed out loud against the 2026-08-27 convergence
ruling rather than hidden.

## This PR's own head is the third instance today

Read straight off both endpoints at `97fad03b`, after CI settled:

```
/commits/97fad03b/check-runs   total_count 19   19 × (completed, success)
                               merge-gate-job present: True
/commits/97fad03b/status       combined state: failure
                               merge-gate = failure | gate CLOSED — no exact-head receipt
/pulls/5367                    mergeable true, mergeable_state unstable
```

Nineteen of nineteen green, `merge-gate-job` among them, beside a `failure` on
the other endpoint — the shape from `pr-board.mjs:115` and #4739, on the change
that fixes it. The old watcher would have printed an unqualified GREEN here.
This one prints `1 commit status(es) read, 1 not green` and names the row, and
`merge-gate.mjs` still passes its checks step because the closed context is its
own last answer:

```
PASS: all 19 check run(s) and 0 independent commit status(es) green on this head.
This head's own `merge-gate` status (failed) is THIS script's last answer and is
recomputed here, not read.
```

## Proof

Eleven mutations, each red **exactly** its own fixtures, all re-run after
prettier reformatted the sources so no anchor drifted:

| mutation | reds |
| --- | --- |
| `merge-gate` stops reading `/status` | 1 |
| the gate counts its own status (self-block) | 4 |
| the gate excludes *every* status (too loose) | 6 |
| `ci-watch` stops reading `/status` | 6 |
| `ci-watch` reds on the gate's own status | 2 |
| `ci-watch` settles on the check set alone (#5317) | 1 |
| `ci-watch` never settles while `unstable` (too strict) | 1 |
| `ci-watch` fingerprints the FILTERED set | 1 |
| `pr-board` reads unreadable as empty | 2 |
| `pr-board` drops its statuses | 3 |
| the workflow

author: jusus1300
body:
## Podsumowanie

Dwie poprawki wynikające z recenzji stanowiska — punkt 2 (mechanizm awaryjny modelu) i punkt 6 (kalibracja okulografu). Obie dotyczą usterek, które psuły wynik po cichu, bez żadnego sygnału dla operatora.

## 1. Synchronizacja zestawu awaryjnego z `model_config.json` (`a9ebd1e`)

Zaszyte w `calculate_risk_score` wartości domyślne pochodziły z modelu liczonego w pikselach: normy `sac_prog_y_stab` (14,27) i `sac_prog_dist_avg` (65,22) były porównywane z cechami, które `calculate_features` zwraca w stopniach kąta widzenia (0,368 i 1,737).

Przy braku `model_config.json` dawało to z-score −2,71 i −4,00, a w konsekwencji cichy wynik fałszywie ujemny:

| | przed | po |
|---|---|---|
| „Wysokie ryzyko" na ETDD70 | 13 / 70 | 34 / 70 |
| czułość | 0,34 | 0,79 |

Tabela STATS i wagi to teraz kopia `model_config.json` z retreningu na ETDD70 (T4 Meaningful Text, 70 uczestników). Komentarz przy zestawie odnotowuje jednostki cech oraz wymóg przepisania wartości po każdym uruchomieniu `model_trainer.py`.

**Weryfikacja:** `calculate_risk_score` uruchomione na wszystkich 70 rekordach w dwóch wariantach — z plikiem konfiguracyjnym i bez niego. Identyczne `P` i identyczna grupa ryzyka w 70 z 70 przypadków.

## 2. Rzeczywista kalibracja 9-punktowa (`60b6620`)

Open Gaze API nie zna komendy `CALIBRATE_TYPE`. Wysyłane dotąd `<SET ID="CALIBRATE_TYPE" VALUE="9" />` było odrzucane przez serwer, a ponieważ `_send_command` nie czytał odpowiedzi, odrzucenie pozostawało niewidoczne — w praktyce działała kalibracja ustawiona w Gazepoint Control, domyślnie 5-punktowa.

- `calibrate()` buduje siatkę 3×3 i konfiguruje ją zgodnie z protokołem: `CALIBRATE_CLEAR` czyści listę punktów, po czym każdy punkt dodawany jest osobno przez `CALIBRATE_ADDPOINT`.
- Margines siatki (0,1 / 0,5 / 0,9) trafił do `experiment_config.py` jako `CALIBRATION_MARGIN`.
- `_send_command` przyjmuje opcjonalne `expect_id` i czyta potwierdzenie: `True` dla ACK, `False` dla NACK, `None` gdy serwer nie odpowiedział. Brak odpowiedzi na pierwszą komendę wyłącza dalsze oczekiwanie, żeby wersje Gazepoint Control nieodsyłające ACK nie zbierały timeoutu przy każdym poleceniu.
- Ta sama kontrola objęła komendy startowe w `connect()` — odrzucone `ENABLE_SEND_POG_BEST` oznaczałoby puste kolumny `BPOGX`/`BPOGY` w nagraniu, co bez tego wyszłoby dopiero na etapie analizy. Przełączniki `ENABLE_SEND_DATA` celowo zostają bez weryfikacji, żeby nie opóźniały startu rejestracji.

**Weryfikacja:** atrapa serwera Open Gaze w trzech trybach — ACK, NACK dla `ADDPOINT`, brak odpowiedzi. W każdym leci `CALIBRATE_CLEAR` i 9 punktów o współrzędnych siatki 3×3, `CALIBRATE_TYPE` nie jest już wysyłane, a tryb bez odpowiedzi nie mnoży timeoutów.

## Czego ta zmiana nie obejmuje

- `config_path` w `calculate_risk_score` pozostaje ścieżką względną wobec katalogu roboczego — po tej zmianie nieszkodliwe, bo oba źródła dają ten sam wynik, ale rozjedzie się przy kolejnym retreningu.
- Nic nie egzekwuje zgodności zestawu awaryjnego z `model_config.json` — to nadal wymóg opisany wyłącznie w komentarzu.

author: ste94pz
body:
Summary

This PR makes the HoYoLAB API language configurable instead of always using the hardcoded en-us locale.

The main motivation is the daily check-in behavior: the locale used for the check-in request can affect the language of the corresponding in-game reward mail. With the current hardcoded English locale, these messages are always received in English regardless of the user’s preferred language.

A new top-level language configuration option is introduced, while keeping en-us as the default/fallback for backward compatibility.

Changes

* Add a top-level language option to the default configuration
* Use the configured locale for existing x-rpc-language HoYoLAB headers
* Add the configured lang parameter to Genshin Impact daily check-in requests (info, home, and sign)
* Replace hardcoded en-us locale values in other locale-aware HoYoLAB requests
* Add language support to the web-based configuration generator, including config import/export
* Document the new option in the README
* Preserve en-us as the fallback when language is unset

Motivation

I originally added this because Genshin Impact daily check-in requests were always performed using the English locale. This caused the reward mail sent to the in-game mailbox after check-in to be localized in English.

Passing the user’s desired HoYoLAB locale with the check-in request allows the in-game message to use the corresponding language instead.

Testing

Tested with Genshin Impact using a non-English HoYoLAB locale:

* daily check-in completes successfully
* the check-in API uses the configured locale
* the resulting in-game reward mail is localized accordingly
* existing behavior is preserved when language is unset by falling back to en-us
* the setup generator can import and export the language option

I do not have accounts for the other supported games, so changes affecting their locale-dependent HoYoLAB requests have not been tested directly.

Testing/feedback for Honkai: Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero, Honkai Impact 3rd, and Tears of Themis would therefore be appreciated.

author: gabrick75
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses the security findings from the audit report (all 16 `F1.1–F6.4` items, with only deploy-side configuration left out). It fixes stored XSS, stream-key leakage, authenticated-only endpoints, upload validation, unhandled async errors (DoS) and missing rate limiting.

## Changes

**Stored XSS & sanitization**
- Escape comment/chat/avatar/banner/user content rendered via `innerHTML` (`escA`/`escJs` helpers).
- Server-side normalization in `sanitizeText`: strips control chars, HTML `<`/`>`, trims and caps length (no new dependencies).
- `avatar_url`/`banner_url` validated with a hardened `isSafeUrl`: blocks `javascript:`/`data:` schemes, breaker chars (`' " < > ; ( ) \``) and malformed `/static/` paths (path traversal), closing the CSS-injection vector in `channel.ejs`.
- Video/live titles and descriptions sanitized on write.

**Access control & data isolation**
- Removed `stream_key` from every public endpoint and page (channels, live status/details/list, home, channel/live/user pages).
- `/api/rtmp/sessions` now requires authentication and never exposes the stream key.
- `/api/users/:id` no longer returns `email`.

**Upload validation**
- Split upload strategies: videos (MIME whitelist, 2 GB) vs images (MIME whitelist, 5 MB).
- File extension is derived from the validated MIME type, never from the client-provided filename.

**DoS / error handling**
- Global error handler + `unhandledRejection` guard (no more process crashes).
- Foreign-key existence checks before INSERTs (comments, likes, chat) returning 404 instead of crashing.
- Socket `send-message` wrapped in try/catch with channel existence check.

**Hardening**
- JWT secret validation at startup (≥ 32 chars, rejects known weak defaults) and `.env.example` documenting `openssl rand -hex 32`.
- Zero-dependency rate limiting on `/api/login` and `/api/register` (per IP + per-account lockout).
- CORS whitelist (env `CORS_ORIGINS`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on `/static`, explicit `express.json` size limit.
- Removed `_token` query-string session acceptance and token/email logging.

## Notes for the maintainer

- Cookie `httpOnly`/`Secure`, helmet/CSP and NMS bind/`allow_origin` are **not** changed here (they require an auth-refactor or deployment-level configuration) — documented in the attached report.
- Requires a strong `JWT_SECRET` set in the environment at deploy time; the app refuses to start with a weak/missing one.
- The full security audit PDF is attached.

## Commits

- `7bb44e8` fix: stored XSS in comments, chat, avatars/banners
- `930a646` fix: media security, upload validation, error handling and CORS
- `25cbac2` fix: rate limiting, reinforced sanitization and additional hardening
- `2c04f42` fix: block breaker chars and malformed paths in avatar/banner URLs

author: apolloccrypt
body:
Het publieke transparantielog gaf de exacte seconde weg. Wie een kopie van een
document had, kon daarmee bewijzen dat het door Paramant ging en wanneer.
Gemeten, niet geschat, op een echt opgestarte relay.

## Wat er misging, met de meting erbij

Een blad is een ongezouten hash van drie raadbare dingen:

```
blad = SHA3-256(0x02 || sha256(bestand) || SHA3-256(sector) || utf8(ts))
```

De bestandshash kent de aanvaller, de sector is een van vijf, en de tijd is wat
het log publiceert. Afronden op het hele uur laat 3,6 miljoen maal vijf
kandidaten over: **57 seconden op een kern**, 323.000 bladhashes per seconde in
kaal Node. Twee routes lieten er nul over.

| Aanval | Voor | Na |
|---|---|---|
| A. `/ct/feed` `t` koppelen aan de `leaf_hash` van `/v2/ct/log` op index | **1 hash** | mislukt na 5 |
| C. de STH bij `tree_size = index + 1` uit `/v2/sth/history` | **1 hash** | mislukt na 20.010 |
| B. het uurvak brute-forcen uit `/v2/ct/log` alleen | 57 s | 56 s, ongewijzigd |

Aanval C stond niet in het ontwerp en is de scherpste van de drie. Er wordt een
boomkop gemaakt bij elke append, dus `tree_size` N is blad N-1, en de
`timestamp` was `Date.now()` van microseconden na de `ts` van dat blad. Duizend
diep in `/v2/sth/history` in plaats van vijftig, gespiegeld naar elke peer, en
binnen een handtekening, dus niet in de projectie te repareren. `/ct/feed`
dichten en dit laten staan was theater geweest.

Aanval B blijft. Dat is stap 3, en die is groter dan een pull request.

## Wat deze PR doet

**1. De tijd op het hele uur, overal waar het log iets publiceert.** `/ct/feed`
rondt af zoals `/v2/ct/log` al deed. De boomkop rondt af **voor** het
ondertekenen, want anders is het een leugen in plaats van een reparatie. Koppen
van eerder houden hun precieze timestamp en blijven kloppen: verificatie bouwt
de canonieke payload uit de velden die een kop draagt en pint geen resolutie,
niet in `receipt-verify.js` en niet in `/v2/sth/ingest`. De volle tijd blijft in
de opgeslagen regel en in het bonnetje dat de klant zelf houdt, en daar hoort
hij ook: precisie in het private bonnetje, grofheid in het publieke log.

`/ct/feed` is niet gesloten. De ingebouwde `/ct`-pagina leeft ervan, met een
tabel en een verifieerknop, en `deploy/nginx-selfhost.conf` en `docs/api.md`
noemen hem. Afronden is de kleinere ingreep met hetzelfde effect.

De kosten, hardop: een archivaris kan uit een kop alleen niet meer zien waar in
het uur hij getekend is. `tree_size` ordent de koppen nog steeds, een per
append, dus versheidsbewaking en de consistentiebewijzen zijn ongemoeid.

**2. De boom verdampt niet meer bij een herstart, en kan niet stiekem forken.**
`CT_FILE` stond standaard op niets. `docker-compose.yml` zette hem, dus
productie was in orde en niemand keek nog. Elke andere relay hield het hele log
in RAM.

Gemeten: vier regels, herstart, `/v2/ct/log` komt terug op size 0 terwijl
`RELAY_IDENTITY_FILE` dezelfde ML-DSA-65-sleutel terugbrengt en `STH_FILE` de
oude ondertekende koppen. De relay tekent `tree_size` 1 opnieuw over een andere
wortel, en `/v2/sth/history` houdt daarna twee tegenstrijdige koppen voor een
boomgrootte onder een sleutel. Dat is geen leeg log maar een **gesplitst** log,
gepubliceerd, ondertekend, en niet van knoeien te onderscheiden. Elk bonnetje
van voor de herstart lost ook niet meer op: `/v2/ct/proof` antwoordt 404.

Het log wordt nu standaard bewaard, naast de koppen die het bevestigen: de map
van `STH_FILE`, anders `/data/ct-log.json`. De kop en de boom die hij bevestigt
horen op hetzelfde volume. Een expliciet lege `CT_FILE` kiest nog steeds
RAM-only, voor wie dat meent.

Los van de default weigert `produceSth` een kop die er een tegenspreekt die al
getekend is, of die `tree_size` laat teruglopen. Hij logt
`sth_refused_would_fork` op error, zet `forked` op het publieke `/v2/sth` zodat
een monitor van buiten een bevroren log van een stille week kan onderscheiden,
en er zijn twee gauges bij: `ct_log_persisted` en `ct_log_forked`.

**3. Gezouten bladen in een tweede boom: niet gedaan, wel uitgeschreven.** Zie
`docs/adrs/R021`. De reden staat daar met de koppelpunten erbij, kort: `size`,
`root` en `index` zijn overal een naamruimte zonder discriminator (`/v2/ct/log`,
`/ct/feed`, `/v2/ct/proof`, `ct-log.page.js`, de heartbeat, de relayregistratie,
de metrics, en de ingebouwde `/ct`-pagina die feed en STH op gelijkheid toetst);
`produceSth` heeft een `sthLog` en een `STH_FILE`; het zout kan de server niet
bereiken terwijl de bonnetjesbouw en `/v2/verify-receipt` het blad allebei
herberekenen; `.psign` draagt een kale `notary.ct_log_index` binnen een
ondertekende canonieke JSON; `/v2/sth/consistency` is begrensd op het venster en
niet op het log, dus een bevroren boom die voorbij `CT_MAX` veroudert kan geen
consistentiebewijs naar zijn eigen slotkop maken; en de controlepagina moet twee
tijdperken tegelijk aankunnen, want een oud bonnetje heeft geen zout. Dat laatste
is de valkuil die deze week al een keer toesloeg toen de pagina een van de vijf
relaysleutels kende. Kleine echte winst gaat voor.

**4. Een veldpoort die de klasse vangt.** `relay/lib/ct-fields.js` noemt bij
naam elk veld dat op een logregel mag staan, elk gebeurtenistype dat een familie
mag gebruiken en elke sleutel die een payload mag dragen. Elke `ctAppend*` gaat
erdoorheen. Een niet-genoemd veld wordt gestript voordat er iets is opgeslagen,
weggeschreven of gepubliceerd, en gelogd op error; een niet-genoemd type gooit.
Strippen in plaats van gooien, want een niet-genoemd veld is per definitie een
veld dat geen enkele lezer kent, terwijl doorlaten het voor altijd publiceert.

`relay/test/ct-fields.test.js` maakt er een poort van in plaats van een lijst.
Het houdt de opgave tegen een met de hand geschreven tweede kopie, en het scant
`relay.js`, `envelope.js` en de heartbeat op de literals die er echt langskomen.
Dat tweede maakt gooien veilig, en het vond meteen twee waarborgen die niet
konden afgaan:

- `ctAppendSigningPkEvent` noemde twee van de vier types die zijn eigen
  aanroepers doorgeven. `signing_pk_enrolled_tofu` en
  `signing_pk_enrolled_attested` gooiden in de outer catch van de route, na het
  opslaan van de sleutel, dus beide paden antwoordden **500** en kwamen nooit in
  het log.
- `ctAppendEnvelope` plakte `envelope_` voor namen die dat al hadden. Gemeten op
  `origin/main`: het log droeg `envelope_envelope_create`, terwijl
  `scripts/heartbeat/parasign.mjs` filtert op `envelope_sign`. Dat filter is het
  sterkste bewijs dat de ParaSign-heartbeat verzamelt en het kon niet afgaan.
  Er verschuift niets dat al getekend is: het bladvoorbeeld neemt de kale
  gebeurtenisnaam, nooit deze string, dus geen inclusiebewijs en geen bonnetje
  verandert van waarde.

## Sabotagetoets, per stap

Elke reparatie is teruggedraaid en de toets moet dan rood worden. Alle acht
werden rood.

| Sabotage | Wat er rood werd |
|---|---|
| 1a. de rauwe `ts` terug in `/ct/feed` | `route-ct-public-time` 2 en 5 |
| 1b. `Date.now()` terug in de boomkop | `route-ct-public-time` 3 en 5 |

author: sambetts
body:
## Release status: HELD — draft, not stable-ready

This is the technical review of the licence-activity feature actually merged into `dev` by #456. **Do not merge this PR.** Both measured Azure SQL tiers failed exact 180-day execution and memory acceptance, and the known correctness follow-ups remain unmerged. Successful CI, an earlier clean code-review round, and the earlier permission to merge #456 into `dev` do not satisfy those gates or authorise another merge.

Readiness rechecked on **2026-09-06** against GitHub API state and the pinned Git graph. The resumed performance/acceptance work is separate and has not supplied a new accepted, merged release candidate. The measurements below remain evidence for the old baseline only.

## Exact release diff and inclusion

| Reference | Exact commit |
|---|---|
| Base `main` | `3f9098fdd60b10c02840d0ee3f93bee0756518d1` |
| Head `dev` | `b415bc088a4c7bc3017cc1dfd9c0507121d8e3cc` |
| Merge base | `da52edcd70e0137f799699ea9668e740b3bc2a2d` |
| Merged #456 feature head | `f94fb84fe7e45f4efec3b2062cb01ba13db83769` |

The release contains **4 commits, 65 changed files, 15,708 additions and 94 deletions**: three feature/fix commits and the #456 merge commit. Both `main..dev` and `main...dev` have this file/line delta. The feature head is an ancestor of `dev`, and its tree is identical to the current `dev` tree. These are graph/diff checks, not inclusion claims inferred from PR prose.

| Follow-up | Current head | Verified state | Included here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| #457 — query performance and correctness | `830ccc36ee17f2dd2d07dfbf83ced07d6f27e6b7` | Open, draft, unmerged | **No** |
| #459 — expected-sample context and unnamed-SKU UI | `3c535436c014edd7f09a77c89206cf1a91d6664c` | Open, unmerged | **No** |
| #455 — independent synthetic demo generator | `87b5b46c1cdcf268f9d6e677dcbc53db27c85ea4` | Open, unmerged | **No** |

None of those heads is an ancestor of this release head. Any subsequent local candidate or new follow-up also remains excluded until its actual merged commit is verified in `dev`.

## Feature and architecture

- Always-visible **Insights > Reports > Licence activity**, with a SKU overview and separate Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Copilot distributions.
- Existing `license_types` and `user_license_type_lookups` remain the assignment source. Users are distinct within each SKU; overlapping SKU memberships are not summed into a unique-user total.
- Administrative drill-down supplies bounded most/least-active lists, SQL UPN/mail search, sorting and paging, evidence for all five workloads, and department/country filtering and breakdowns.
- Reporting uses exact inclusive UTC ranges of **7–180 days**, ending before today. The default is 28 days ending on the latest Sunday at least three days old. Presets and custom ranges are not shortened or rounded.
- The intended classification distinguishes missing, disabled, delayed, concealed or unmatched evidence from measured zero. Least-active ranking requires complete per-user coverage; positive partial evidence may inform most-active exploration. The known query-path inconsistencies listed below are not yet repaired in this release.
- Historical usage is compared with **currently imported assignments**, not historical licence ownership or proof that a particular overlapping SKU enabled an activity. There are no purchased-capacity, productivity, ROI or automatic licence-removal claims.
- SQL performs aggregation, ranking and paging behind `ILicenceActivityStore`; the web process and browser do not receive the full user/licence matrix. Display-name search is not promised because the importer/schema does not persist Graph user display names. Unicode metadata remains supported.
- The existing dependency-free `XlsxWriter` exports the exact cached overview and, when authorised and selected, the currently displayed bounded user lists/page. Expired or mismatched snapshots fail explicitly rather than silently rerunning a different report.

## Lifetime, access and deployment

ASP.NET session state remains disabled. Shared work starts through `Task.Run`, owns its store connections and does not inherit one caller's cancelled wait. Cache size, expiry, response size and admission are bounded; late generations cannot replace newer results. Publication precedes optional diagnostics. Lifecycle telemetry uses a privacy allowlist and bounded shutdown.

Individual detail and exports containing individual users require the optional Entra app role **`LicenceActivity.ReadUsers`**. Already-authenticated portal users can see aggregates and export aggregate snapshots. This role protects only the new licence-activity endpoints; it does **not** establish an aggregate-only security boundary around the existing portal.

Four admitted report loads do **not** mean four SQL commands. An overview can use a holding connection plus five workload connections. The process-wide six-overview-worker limit and four-report admission limit give code-derived mixed-load ceilings of ten open connections and eight active commands. Other portal/importer SQL is outside these limits; these are not measured tenant-wide capacity guarantees.

### Schema/configuration classification — verified from code

| Artifact or contract | Classification and evidence |
|---|---|
| EF migrations, designers and snapshots | **None changed.** No additive, removal or performance-motivated migration in this release. `Common/Entities/Migrations/` is unchanged. |
| Fresh-install database schema | **Unchanged.** `Common/Entities/Resources/Create DB.sql` and `AnalyticsEntitiesContext`/persisted EF model are unchanged. New query temporary tables/indexes are not product schema migrations. |
| Permanent SQL indexes | **None added or changed.** No permanent index has been justified by the failed benchmark. |
| Manual SQL upgrade assets/run order | **None required for this diff.** No new migration-specific maintenance-window or index-build estimate applies. Older installations still require their pre-existing upgrade prerequisites. |
| Installer saved-config schema | **Unchanged.** Persisted installer models and import settings are unchanged; `BaseSolutionInstallConfig.CONFIG_VERSION` remains **`2.2.0`**. |
| Runtime app settings/connection strings | **No new setting or connection string.** The feature consumes existing user/usage/Copilot import flags and the existing database connection. |
| Optional operational action | Create/assign `LicenceActivity.ReadUsers` on the runtime app registration for administrators needing individual detail, then sign out/in. This is an Entra role action, not an installer JSON-schema change. |
| Packaging/dependencies | New C# sources are registered in the existing projects and the SPA follows the existing publish path. New portal test dependencies are development-only with a matching lockfile. |

These classifications are for the exact head above. They must be repeated if the performance candidate or another follow-up changes the release.

## Correctness evidence and remaining exclusions

The historical feature validation reported 18 SQL semantics tests, 28 API/cache/domain/lifecycle tests, 85 portal tests, and passing TypeScript/Vite builds. The owned-Azure benchmark harness separately reported 49 targeted licence regressions; its benchmark-only additions are not part of this diff.

Hosted evidence was rechecked at exact heads:

- #456 feature head: [Tests 33972653828](https://github.com/pnp/Microsoft365-Analytics-Insights/actions/runs/33972653828) and [PR build 33972653801](https://github.com/pnp/Microsoft365-Analytics-Insights/actions/runs/33972653801) succeeded. Its tree is identical to this `dev` head.
- **Draft #458 itself has skipped Tests and PR-build runs**, not a new passing execution. Secret-scan checks succeeded. The draft guard is intentional; do not describe those skipped workflows as fresh validation.
- Excl

author: devflowza
body:
## Summary

The Cloudflare deploy is green, but the page is blank:

```
env.ts:3 Uncaught Error: Missing VITE_SUPABASE_URL — copy .env.example to apps/web/.env.local
```

Vite inlines `VITE_*` at build time and the Pages project has no build variables set, so `apps/web/src/lib/env.ts` throws while the module graph is still loading and nothing renders.

Until now nothing in the repository could supply those values, so a working deploy depended on a manual dashboard change — the same class of drift that broke the output directory in the previous PR.

## What changed

`apps/web/.env.production` is committed with the defaults for the current project. Vite loads it for production builds, so a build with no host configuration now produces a working site.

**Only publishable values are in it.** The Supabase URL and the anon/publishable key ship inside every browser bundle regardless, and they grant nothing on their own: the `anon` role holds zero table privileges and row-level security denies it every row (verified directly against the provisioned project). The file header, plus narrowly scoped `.gitignore` and `.gitleaks.toml` exceptions, are there so a service-role key, database password or provider credential is not added by habit.

## Verification

- The real project URL and publishable key are inlined into the production bundle.
- The missing-value guard still ships, so a genuinely absent variable still fails loudly rather than silently rendering a broken app.
- An inline environment variable **overrides** the file (`VITE_SUPABASE_URL=… vite build` wins), so per-environment hosts keep working and staging can point at its own project.
- The E2E bundle still points at its own `localhost` backend double, not the live project, so the Playwright suite is unaffected.
- `pnpm lint` clean; 27 web test files / 64 tests pass.

## Tradeoff worth a reviewer's attention

Because the file provides a default, an environment that sets **no** variables now silently inherits this project instead of failing. That is the price of a deploy that works without dashboard configuration. Set the variables explicitly on any deployment that is not the default one; host variables remain the better end state, and this file can be deleted once they are in place.

`VITE_API_URL` is deliberately left unset: the Hono API has no public origin yet, so it still falls back to `http://localhost:4000` and data requests will fail while the interface itself loads and authenticates.

author: meisnermax
body:
## Was das ist

`VALUATION-REHOST-01`, Welle **P-4** erstes Child: der Property-Workspace bekommt seine `Investment`-Domain, und darin `Bewertung`.

Die Bewertungsdomäne läuft seit Längerem in der Cloud, war aber nur über die Szenario-Seite und eine eigenständige Route erreichbar. Der Workspace hatte **keinen** Investment-Eintrag — die neue Übersicht konnte also die Bewertungsfälle eines Objekts zählen und bot dann nirgends an, sie zu öffnen.

## Rehost, kein Neubau

- **Queue**: derselbe property-scoped `ValuationsScreen`, den auch die eigenständige Route nutzt, eingebettet (ohne zweiten Seitenkopf).
- **Detail**: dieselbe Case-Sektion, die der Szenario-Host mountet — dafür jetzt öffentlich.

Zwei Flächen für denselben Fall wären zwei Orte, an denen seine Lifecycle-Regeln auseinanderlaufen können, und die Spec sagt ausdrücklich, dass dieser Screen die Cloud-Domäne **rehostet** statt sie neu abzuleiten.

Die Auswahl lebt im Controller der Queue, also landet man beim Zurückkommen dort, wo man aufgehört hat — genau wie bei ihren Filtern.

## Gruppierung, kein Zusammenziehen

`Investment` liefert Navigation und Property-Kontext, sonst nichts. Der Host zieht **nicht** Valuation-Faktoren, Szenario-Inputs und Finance-Actuals in ein domänenübergreifendes Formular.

`Szenarien` (`SCENARIO-VALUATION-01`) und `Performance` (`FINANCE-01`/`P2-D08`) sind **abwesend statt leer** — dieselbe Regel, nach der `Übersicht` und `Betrieb` registriert wurden.

Die Domain erscheint nur, wenn sie sich auch öffnen lässt: `valuation.read` **und** ein Host, der sie bauen kann. Fehlt eines von beidem, ist sie nicht da, statt in einen leeren Rahmen zu führen.

## Nebenwirkung: die Übersicht drillt jetzt durch

Das Bewertungsmodul der Übersicht hatte bisher keinen Drilldown, weil `Investment` nicht registriert war. Der zugehörige Test hielt das fest — er prüft jetzt beide Richtungen: mit `valuation.read` öffnet die Kachel die Domain, ohne behält das Modul seine Zahlen und verliert nur die Schaltfläche.

## Verifiziert

Keine Migration — reiner Client-Rehost auf dem bestehenden Contract.

`flutter analyze` sauber, **1961** Tests grün, davon 6 neue für Registrierung, Sichtbarkeit nach Permission und nach Builder, Sub-Navigation, Responsive.

body:
## Why
Part of [Publish pages (#648)](https://github.com/wheresrhys/totf/issues/648), requirement 1. Lets a signed-in ringing group control whether its own summary pages are publicly viewable, by adding the site's first group settings page with a toggle.

## What
Adds `app/actions/settings.ts` (`fetchOwnGroupPublicAreas`, `updatePublicSummaryEnabled`) and a new top-level `/settings` route (`SettingsPage` / `SettingsPageContent`) rendering a single "Make my summary pages public" checkbox wired to the action, following this repo's page/PageContent/dataFetcher and form/action-wiring conventions.

### Details
- `updatePublicSummaryEnabled(enabled: boolean)` never takes an explicit group id param — it reads the caller's own group id from the session cookie (the same JWT `getAuthenticatedSupabaseClient()` signs into its request) and adds/removes `'summary'` from that group's own `RingingGroups.public_areas` row, defence-in-depth backed by the existing `ringing_groups_update` RLS policy.
- `public_areas` isn't in the generated Supabase types yet — it lands with #768's schema migration (a prerequisite for this to persist meaningfully in prod). This ticket's own tests mock the Supabase layer and don't require the migration applied locally, per #769's stated scope. `getAuthenticatedSupabaseClient()` already returns an untyped `SupabaseClient` (same pattern as e.g. `app/actions/bird-encounters.ts`), so no type workaround was needed.
- Out of scope (per ticket): anything that reads/enforces `public_areas` when serving a summary page to a visitor, and any settings besides this one toggle.

Closes #769

- [x] `npm run qa` (lint + type-check + app tests) — all green, 1326 tests passed

author: akash-suresh
body:
`ignoreCommand` only diffed the newest commit, so a docs-only merge landing on top of a same-minute batch skipped the whole production build — proven 2026-09-05 when the OpenRouter adapter work rode under docs-only #858 and was silently `CANCELED`. Production is now never skipped; the diff-based skip still applies to preview/development.

Fixes: #867

## Change

`ui/vercel.json`'s `ignoreCommand`:
```
if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" = "production" ]; then exit 1; else git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- .; fi
```
Production always `exit 1` (build proceeds, never skipped). Everything else falls through to the unchanged `git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- .` check.

## Exit-code direction — verified live against Vercel's own docs, not just the issue text

Fetched two Vercel doc pages directly during this session:
- `/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json` (`ignoreCommand` section): "When the command exits with code 1, the build will continue. When the command exits with 0, the build is ignored."
- `/docs/project-configuration/project-settings` (Ignored Build Step): "If the command exits with code `1`, the build continues as normal. If the command exits with code `0`, the build is immediately aborted... set to `CANCELED`." Same page also confirms the command "can access all System Environment Variables" and that Vercel's own built-in "Only build production" option keys off `VERCEL_ENV == production` — same signal this fix uses.

So `exit 1` under production is correct (forces the build); the pre-existing `git diff --quiet` call already returns 0/1 in the right direction for the preview branch, unchanged.

Locally verified all four branches of the new logic with `VERCEL_ENV` set to each value plus true/false diff outcomes — all four exited as expected (see PR discussion/session log for the exact commands).

author: chethan123
body:
Ticket [`price-worker/06-the-app-cutover.md`](https://github.com/chethan123/portfolio/blob/main/docs/specs/price-worker/06-the-app-cutover.md) of spec 0018 (§3.3). The app stops fetching prices in its own process and asks the worker over the unix socket, and this is where the slice pays off: **the application can no longer reach `yahoo-finance2` at all.**

```
yahoo-finance2        server bundle: 0    client bundle: 0
createYahooClient     server bundle: 0    client bundle: 0
yahooPriceProvider    server bundle: 0    client bundle: 0
probeSymbols          server bundle: 0    client bundle: 0
```

The server bundle carried the package before this commit. Smoke gains the assertion that keeps it that way — a grep over the built bundle inside the image, which a container check cannot make and which fails today on the tree this replaces.

## What and why

`app/lib/provider-socket.server.ts` is one primitive and two thin callers. `ask` is a single request with **no agent**, because Node's global agent keeps sockets alive and pools them by socket path: without that, every call would leave an idle socket in one of the worker's eight slots for six seconds, and a call landing as the keep-alive timer fires is a reset the ledger would file as a provider failure.

Its outcomes are told apart in one order, each for a stated reason:

- **A connect failure is keyed on the syscall, not a list of codes.** `ENOENT`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `EACCES` and `ENOTDIR` all carry `syscall: "connect"` — re-measured on 24.12.0 — and a permission fault is persistent and *is* "no worker reachable". Keyed as a plain failure it would ledger five candidates a day and charge the retry clock for a misconfiguration fixed in a minute.
- **An abort arrives as an `AbortError` wrapping the signal's `TimeoutError`**, because `http.request` wraps the reason where `fetch` throws it. The raw error is kept as the `cause` so a test pins the discrimination rather than the friendly message on top of it.
- **The budgets differ on purpose.** History's outlives the worker's own 30 s watchdog so the app reads the worker's `504` *and its reason* instead of its own abort; the probe's is long enough to survive a cold worker's crumb handshake, because the verdict a short budget loses is the non-USD one — the only verdict a person acts on.

A malformed symbol is dropped before the call on **both** paths, not only quotes. The worker validates a batch atomically, so one bad symbol would refuse the whole request and cost ninety-nine good ones their answer — and on the probe path that is a submission's entire currency check skipped. Which is the other half of it: the probe now logs when a chunk fails. The function it replaces swallowed everything in a bare `catch`, so an outage during an upload left no trace at all, where the refresh path has always logged.

## What the review found, and it is the reason to trust this

Two adversarial reviews, fourteen findings, every one fixed. Two are worth your attention.

**`ask` never settled when the worker died mid-answer, and that holds the refresh lock for the life of the process.** If the peer destroys the socket *after* the response headers and *before* the declared body completes, Node emits neither `error` nor `end`, and the abort cannot rescue a request already closed. Measured: a 500 ms budget still pending at three seconds, with only `res data`, `res aborted`, `req close` and an unlistened `res error` to show for it. Because `runRefresh` awaits inside `withRefreshLock`, a hung `ask` holds the Postgres advisory lock and its pooled connection indefinitely — every later refresh, poller tick and pressed control alike, answering `busy` until the app restarts. **The previous release's own `mem_limit: 256m` is what makes the death reachable**, on exactly the large chart answers that span writes. Fixed with a `close` backstop, safe because `end` precedes `close` on every successful answer — measured for one write and for two hundred. Spec §3.3 and the module header both claimed one signal bounded the whole exchange; both are corrected in place, because that was true of the design and not of the platform.

**The worker scrubs and caps its error text; this code un-scrubbed it.** Ticket 04 made the worker collapse control characters and cap length before logging, reasoning that the response *body* needed no equivalent because `JSON.stringify` escapes them. That holds on the wire and stops holding the moment something parses it back — and this is the first code that does. A 300,000-character message and a forged line opening with the worker's own `Price worker:` stem both arrive intact, reach the operator's log, and land in `price_backfill.error`, a `text` column nothing prunes, at up to 2 MiB an attempt. Reachable from a compromised worker *or* an honest one relaying a hostile upstream. The same two lines now guard the reading side.

Alongside those: a `200` whose body is not JSON was swallowed into `undefined` — quotes became an empty answer that marked everything stale and logged nothing, and a history became `no-history`, which this codebase already calls a lie the ledger repeats. And four guards survived mutation with the suite green: that an unreachable worker propagates rather than reading as absent history (which the batch abort rests on), that a failed chunk does not abandon the ones after it, that a request error which is *not* a connect failure stays a plain failure, and that the history budget outlives the worker's watchdog.

The case pinning chunk independence failed the *last* chunk, so abandoning every later one was invisible — and it slept ten seconds through a budget with no injection point. Failing the *first* chunk instead kills the mutation and drops that file from eleven seconds to under one. **The suite got faster despite seven new tests**, 56 s to 48 s.

## Corrections and residuals

- **The ticket is corrected in place by banner.** Of its eighteen `file:line` references, five pointed where they claimed; **seven pointed at unrelated content** — a different subsystem, the wrong section, and two lines past the end of a forty-five-line file. Each re-read rather than recomputed. The banner also records work the checklist never counted: removing the two functions breaks two test files, one of whose cases exists to pin an earlier ticket's pre-range floor and says so in a comment. Both are migrated to the socket provider against a real worker; **no case was deleted**.
- **Spec §3.3 gains a sixth outcome** and §8's data-model claim is struck — the slice does touch that document after all.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md`'s ingest diagram** still named the deleted function, in §6, which no ticket's checklist covers. Fixed here rather than left to fall through.
- **The upgrade note spoke in the future tense** about "a later release, the one that has `app` dial the worker". This is that release; an operator reading it as written would conclude they still had time.
- **Left alone deliberately:** `docs/operating.md` still describes four services in three places and one compose network — ticket 09 owns every one of those.

## Evidence

Node 24.12.0, real PostgreSQL 17.10, on the merged tree:

```
npm run typecheck   clean
npm test            90 files, 1745 tests passed
npm run build       client and server, no errors
bash -n scripts/smoke-test.sh   clean
```

**Not run here: anything needing a Docker daemon.** No image was built, no container started, and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` was never executed — that is CI's container smoke job and I am not claiming it as passed. Everything else was measured rather than reasoned about: the connect matrix re-run on this Node, the abort shape, the mid-stream death and the ordering property its fix rests on, the log injection, and the bundle greps above.

No screenshots: nothing user-visible changes.
