author: mpsalisbury
body: ## Why Favoriting a scoped piece stored a reference to the **space-scoped document**, and two scopes' favorites collided into one entry. Three places dropped the scope, not the two the issue names — the third, `FavoritesManager.#deriveTags`, reads the piece's result schema without one, so a scoped favorite could be tagged from a different document. Same shape as #6912, which landed earlier: an address split from the scope that completes it. ## The migration question, and why it needed no ruling `favoriteKey` shapes stored data, so widening it normally re-keys every existing favorite. That is why the issue held it back for the favorites owner. It turns out not to need them, and the reason is by construction rather than by inference: **every key in durable storage was produced by `#createPieceRef`, which hardcoded `scope: "space"`.** Those are the only two production call sites. So: a space-scoped address writes no scope, and only a narrower one is appended. **Every stored key is byte-identical under the new spelling.** No favorite is re-keyed, dedup and keyed removal keep holding for entries already written, and the two scopes that used to collide now key apart. Rejected, with reasons: *always naming the scope* re-keys every stored favorite and breaks the two properties the key exists for, for a cosmetic gain. *A re-keying migration pass* has no machinery here, and this codebase's demonstrated response to a changed stored shape is tolerance of the old one, not rewriting. ## Why not #6912's derived invariant I looked for the analogue and there isn't an honest one. That check works because `IPCClientRequest` is an enumerable population and membership is "declares a `pieceId`". This path is four functions, not a union. The one population worth deriving from lives in `runner`, which imports `home-schemas`, so importing it back is a cycle `check-package-cycles` would fail. A `keyof` assertion here would be a hand-list in the costume of a derivation — **and it would not have caught this bug**, because the parameter type was narrower than the address, so `keyof` never saw a scope to demand. What does enforce it is the type: `scope` is required on both address types, so a caller holding an id and no scope fails `deno task check` at its own call site. ## Behavior change worth review The favorite menu row is now gated on the resolved address rather than on `pieceId`, so it is absent during the window before the pattern loads, where the id has no scope. Favoriting under a guessed scope was the bug; refusing to guess is the fix, but it is visible. ## Test plan Every assertion has a named mutation that reds it, run in isolation, with the clause as the unit. **One instrument was inert and was fixed**: the "writes nothing when the scope is unknown" clause first passed against the mutation it was written for, because its fixture never straddled the boundary that mutation draws. The type-check instrument was verified too — a deliberate surplus property in the new test file makes `deno check packages/home-schemas` exit 1 naming it, confirming the new tree is inside the coverage the gate claims.

author: simonbrunou
body:
Closes #509

## Problem
The `update_password` controller action hard-matches success from `Accounts.update_user_password/2`, causing a `MatchError` and HTTP 500 when the changeset returns validation errors (e.g., password too short).

## Solution
Changed the hard match to a `case` statement that handles both success and error returns:
- On success: disconnect old sessions, clear rate limits, re-login via create/3
- On error: show an error flash and redirect back to settings

The password remains unchanged and the session stays valid on validation failure.

## Tests
Added `test "handles invalid password during update-password gracefully"` that:
1. Submits a password shorter than the 12-character minimum
2. Verifies no crash (previously MatchError on line 81)
3. Confirms error flash and redirect to /settings
4. Confirms session remains valid
5. Confirms password unchanged in database

## Files Changed
- `lib/cinder_web/controllers/user_session_controller.ex:81-101` – case expression wrapping update_user_password/2 call
- `test/cinder_web/controllers/user_session_controller_test.exs:335-361` – new test for invalid password input

author: vyos88
body:
Two halves of "update the software", neither of which existed anywhere in the repo.

## The laptops update themselves

`scripts/self-update.mjs` fetches, fast-forwards if it is safe to, and **exits 10** to say a restart is needed. It never restarts anything itself — which service to bounce, and whether now is a good moment, is the machine owner's call rather than a script's. The exit code is the whole interface, so a scheduled task can act on it:

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | already current |
| `10` | updated — restart the agent |
| `1` | refused or failed; a person is needed |

`docs/AUTO_UPDATE.md` carries the wiring for Windows Task Scheduler + NSSM, systemd timers, and launchd — including the randomised delay, which matters once there is more than one laptop: without it the whole fleet restarts in the same second and the host briefly has no workers.

This is worth automating because **the drift is already visible and nobody acts on it.** The host logs `agent is not on the host's version of Alpha`, and `alpha-admin agents` prints an asterisk next to the version. A warning nobody reads is not a mechanism.

It is safe to automate because updating here is only a `git pull` and a restart — no runtime dependencies means no install step to get half-done. Restarting mid-task is safe too: `stop()` drains before it deregisters, so results still land.

## The Alpha host gets the same thing as a task

`alpha.update` is the second handler that runs an external program, so it follows `alpha-coordination`'s rules — pinned executable, allowlisted action, argv array, no shell anywhere. It drives `git` directly rather than a script on the host, because a script would have to be shipped there *before* the update mechanism could ship it.

```bash
node src/admin/run.js task --type alpha.update --payload '{"action":"Status"}'
```

- **Status** — what commit Alpha is on, and whether anything there is uncommitted. Changes nothing.
- **Fetch** — updates remote-tracking refs and reports how many commits are waiting; the working copy is untouched, so it answers "is there an update?" without taking it.
- **Pull** — fast-forwards, and only fast-forwards.

## What it will not do

The absences are the design, so they are stated in the code:

- **No action rewrites history, discards local work, or changes branch.** The allowlist is three entries and `Reset`/`Checkout`/`Clean` are tested as rejected.
- **`Pull` is `--ff-only`, and refused outright on a dirty tree.** The Alpha host's working copy is where Alpha actually runs; a half-applied update to a machine somebody is using is worse than no update. Tracked and untracked counts are reported separately, because on that host the untracked ones are the likely problem.
- **The remote is a validated name, not a passthrough.** Git takes a URL in that argv slot, and an update that can be pointed at an arbitrary remote by whoever queues the task is a way to run someone else's code on the Alpha host.
- **There is no Build and no Restart action.** Those are host-specific commands, and a handler that ran one from its payload or its configuration would be a remote shell with extra steps — the one thing `handlers/index.js` says must never appear here.

## Tests

**181 passing** (was 166), 15 new. Real git repositories rather than a stubbed git: the behaviour that matters is what git actually does to a working copy, and a fake would only assert that the arguments were the ones I chose to write down. The self-update script is driven as a subprocess, the way the scheduled task runs it.

Covered: the allowlist and the rejected actions; a remote that is a URL, a flag injection (`--upload-pack=...`) or traversal; `-C <root>` naming the repository in the argv rather than inheriting it from cwd; `Status` against a real repo including the tracked/untracked split; `Fetch` moving the tracking ref and *not* the working copy; `Pull` fast-forwarding, no-opping when current, refusing on a dirty tree, and refusing on a diverged branch while keeping the host's own commit.

## One thing this cannot fix, which you need to know

`vyos88/Alpha` contains **one file** — `frontend/src/app/shell/AppShell.tsx`. The backend its shell calls (`/speech/*`, `/avatar/*`, `/robot/*`, `/communication/*`, `/triggers/*`) is not in version control at all.

```
$ git ls-files
frontend/src/app/shell/AppShell.tsx
```

So `alpha.update` works the moment it is pointed at a real checkout, but today a `Pull` against that repo fetches one file. **Updating Alpha over the tunnel needs Alpha's code in the repo first**, and that push can only come from the Alpha host, where the code actually lives. `Status` is useful before then — it reports what commit that checkout is on and how much is uncommitted.

author: slevin-7
body:
## Problem

On Jellyfin 12 the scrub-bar thumbnails never show up while playback itself works (#2247). The server log fills with `CustomAuthentication was challenged` every time the player asks for a trickplay sheet.

## Root cause

Plezy authenticates every self-built Jellyfin URL through the query string with `api_key=`. Jellyfin 12 ships with `EnableLegacyAuthorization = false` (jellyfin/jellyfin#15559, merged 2025-11-27; 10.11.x still defaults to `true`). With that flag off, `AuthorizationContext.GetAuthorizationInfoFromDictionary` no longer reads `api_key`, `X-Emby-Token` or `X-MediaBrowser-Token` — only the `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="…"` header and the `ApiKey=` query parameter remain. `ApiKey=` has been read unconditionally since at least 10.8, so it is safe across every supported Jellyfin version.

Trickplay is just the visible symptom. Everything Plezy self-authenticates via the query string fails the same way on a default Jellyfin 12:

| Endpoint | `?api_key=` | `?ApiKey=` |
|---|---|---|
| `/Videos/{id}/Trickplay/320/0.jpg` | 401 | 200 |
| `/Videos/{id}/master.m3u8` (transcoding) | 401 | 200 |
| `/socket` (library-event websocket) | 403 on upgrade | handshake OK, `ForceKeepAlive` received |
| `/Items/{id}/Images/Primary` | 200 | 200 (endpoint has no `[Authorize]`, hence posters kept working) |
| `/Videos/{id}/stream?Static=true` | 200 | 200 (no `[Authorize]` either, hence playback kept working) |

Measured against a Jellyfin 12.0.0 server. Emby (4.10.0.31) is the mirror image: `api_key=` → 200, `ApiKey=` → 401, so the spelling has to be dialect-specific.

## Fix

- `MediaBrowserDialect.tokenQueryParam` returns `ApiKey` for Jellyfin and `api_key` for Emby.
- `buildJellyfinDirectStreamUrl`, `buildJellyfinTrickplayTileUrl`, `_withApiKey` (transcoding URL, subtitle sidecars, Live TV, subtitle downloads) and the websocket URI use it.
- Emby output is byte-identical (covered by a new test in `jellyfin_client_emby_dialect_test.dart`).
- Image URLs intentionally keep `api_key`: Jellyfin serves item images without authentication, and `download_artwork_helpers` strips that exact parameter name for cache keys.
- Log redaction already matches `api[-_]?key` case-insensitively, so `ApiKey=` is masked as before; a test now pins that.

## Testing

- `flutter test` — 6693 passed, 5 skipped.
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` on the touched files, `git diff --check` — clean.
- Live check against Jellyfin 12.0.0: the URL shape produced by the new `buildJellyfinTrickplayTileUrl` (`?ApiKey=…&DeviceId=…`) returns `200 image/jpeg`; the previous `?api_key=…` shape returns 401.
- Websocket with `?ApiKey=` completes the handshake and receives `ForceKeepAlive`; `?api_key=` is rejected with 403.

## AI assistance

Implementation and tests were written with OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6); diagnosis, orchestration and acceptance review with Claude Fable 5.1, plus an independent verification pass by Claude Sonnet 5. All measurements above were reproduced by hand against real Jellyfin 12 and Emby servers.

Fixes #2247

author: bloombar
body:
A course's settings screen was one long form holding every surface a course owns. It is now five named tabs, and the tab is part of the course's canonical address (`/o/:org/projects/:projectId/courses/:courseId/:tab`), so a tab can be linked to, survives a reload, and back/forward move between tabs.

- **General** — title, enable/disable, join links
- **AI** — model, read-only prompt id and its MDL-8 banner, requests-per-day cap, instructions, knowledge files, websites
- **Discord** — admins/students roles, the server binding, categories and channels, and the control that creates them
- **Roster** — file prefix (SPEC calls it the prefix that locates a course's roster CSVs) and the roster import
- **People** — everyone the course has ever enrolled

A new course keeps its single-form layout: it can have none of the sections gated on an existing record, so there is nothing worth splitting (D-80).

What the two review rounds surfaced and this branch fixes: a visited tab's panel stays mounted (hidden) rather than unmounting, so unsaved instructions text, a join link's shown-once secret and a running roster import's progress all survive a tab switch; a back/forward move that only changes tab no longer fires the unsaved-changes guard with a modal that discards nothing; the save-refusal tab switch no longer reads a stale tab across the request; `/courses/new/<tab>` no longer parses as a course whose id is `new`; and the tab bar implements the WAI-ARIA roving-focus keyboard model it claims.

The save payload is unchanged — `form`/`baseline` remain one object regardless of which tab renders a control, so no field can go unsent because its tab is hidden.

Verified: `npm run lint`, `prettier --check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (90/90), `vitest` (2448), Playwright (37/37). New tests confirmed failing without the change.

author: athei
body:
## Symptoms

After a `Reset` at unchanged back-buffer dimensions, the first frame could rasterize inside the viewport the game had set before the `Reset` rather than the full-target default `Reset` applies. With a small pre-`Reset` viewport, the following `Clear` and every draw of that frame land inside that rectangle and the rest of the target keeps what was there before, until the game sets a viewport of its own. The same-size `Reset` was also able to drop every op queued since the last `Present`, which for a texture or a Staged buffer upload whose dirty bookkeeping had already advanced meant content that never reached the GPU and was never rewritten.

## Root cause

Both halves come from the order in which `device_reset` (windows/d3d9/src/device.rs) handled `current_frame`. The unchanged-dimensions fast path did not flush before `reseed_current_frame` replaced the frame, so the queued ops went with it, and `reset_to_defaults` ran before the reseed, so the ops it pushes (the default viewport, the extra render-target unbinds, the vertex-texture unbinds) were handed to the reseed to throw away. The unbinds recover on their own because `PassState::reset_frame` zeroes the extra targets per frame, but the encoder's viewport is deliberately sticky across frames, so nothing else restores it.

Both were fixed when the fast path took its flush and the reseed moved ahead of `reset_to_defaults`, and the queued-upload half is pinned by `reset_same_size_keeps_uploads_queued_before_it`. The viewport half had no test of its own: `reset_same_size_restores_state_defaults` reads back the API-side `GetViewport` mirror, which is correct whatever the encoder holds, and only catches the encoder side by accident through the pixel it reads at the end.

## Changes

`windows/tests/tests/e2e/device.rs` gains `reset_same_size_restores_the_rasterized_viewport`: it paints the whole target, sets a 64x64 corner viewport, Resets at the same size, and then clears and draws a full-target quad without a `SetViewport` of its own before reading the centre pixel. A corner viewport that survived the `Reset` bounds both the clear and the draw, so the centre keeps the earlier colour.

`windows/tests/COVERAGE.md` records what the new test pins in the `device.rs` row.

## Alternatives

Skip the reseed entirely on the unchanged-dimensions path, since the back-buffer and depth handles did not change: rejected, the reseed also drops `DEPTH_EXPLICITLY_UNBOUND`, which `Reset` has to clear, and the flush already makes the reseed harmless.

Pin the vertex-texture unbind instead of the viewport: rejected, the device advertises no vertex-texture fetch, so no end-to-end test can bind one, and both ops ride the same ordering.

Add a second upload test for the `Op::StageUpload` a vertex-buffer `Unlock` queues: rejected as redundant, since the one flush on that path is what carries the whole queue and the texture test already fails without it.

## Verification

`make check` clean. `make ISOLATED=1 test`: 455 e2e tests per architecture, 455 passed and 0 failed on both i686 and x86_64 (3 processes each), plus 1053 and 253 host unit tests passed. Conformance was not run: the change adds a test and a coverage line, and touches no render, state or shader-emission code.

The new test fails when `reset_to_defaults` is put back ahead of `reseed_current_frame` in `device_reset` (`FAIL e2e::device::reset_same_size_restores_the_rasterized_viewport`, with `reset_same_size_restores_state_defaults` failing on its own post-Reset pixel read at the same time) and passes with the order as it stands.

Closes #345

author: mbeisser1
body:
## Feature Description

A message is stored as one instant, in UTC, and says nothing about where the phone was when it arrived. Turning that instant into a clock reading, a day, or a year needs a zone. This PR gives the account one: an IANA time zone, chosen at profile setup (the browser's zone by default) and changeable under Settings → Profile. Every date label in the app, every `date:` boundary in search, the year chips, and the conversation route's `year=` filter are computed from the stored instant plus that zone, so they all agree on which year a New Year's Eve text belongs to.

This is the second half of #326. The first half (#424) made a year page like everything else; this half decides what a "year" is.

## User Story

As someone reading a vault of messages that were sent while the phone moved between zones, I want the times and days shown the way I remember them, so that a text sent at 11:59 pm on New Year's Eve is filed under the old year in the thread, in the year chips, and in `date:2024`, wherever the vault happens to run.

## Implementation Details

**Storage.** `messages.timestamp` (and `staging_messages.timestamp`) is now a UTC instant in RFC 3339 with a `Z` suffix; `timestamp_utc` is gone because there was only ever one instant to store. `accounts.time_zone TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC'` carries the zone. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is 10. Phones store instants too (Android `Telephony.Sms.DATE` is a Unix millisecond long, `chat.db` stores nanoseconds since 2001, WhatsApp and SMS Backup & Restore store epoch milliseconds), so nothing is lost on import; the exporters' IR still carries the local rendering, the vault just does not keep it.

**Boundaries.** The search compiler's `date:`, `first-message:`, and `last-message:` words take a zone (`CompileRequest.zone`) and turn a day's edges into UTC instants (`search::value::utc_instant`) before comparing, instead of comparing the text prefix of a local timestamp. The same rule serves SQLite and Postgres. The conversation messages route's `year=` filter uses the same function, so the vault has one definition of a year. Every route that compiles a query (contacts, conversations, messages, export) loads the account's clock first: `db::account_profile::account_clock` returns `(Tz, today-in-that-zone)`, so relative dates like `7d` also resolve in the account's zone rather than the server's.

**Profile.** `GET /v1/account/profile` returns `time_zone`; `POST` accepts an optional `time_zone` and answers 400 to a name chrono-tz does not know.

**Web.** One `TimeZoneProvider` on the signed-in tree reads the zone from the profile query (no new fetching, per ADR-0002) and `useTimeZone()` hands it to every formatter: bubble times, conversation date spans, the header's month range, and `conversationYears`. Outside a provider (tests) the browser's zone stands in. Profile setup gains a Time Zone picker preselected to the browser's zone; Settings → Profile can change it, and every label re-renders from the returned profile.

### Key Files Changed

- `crates/vault/server/schema/sql/messages.sql`, `staging.sql`, `accounts.sql` - one UTC instant per message; `time_zone` on the account
- `crates/vault/server/src/search/value.rs`, `emit.rs`, `mod.rs` - day edges become UTC instants in the account's zone
- `crates/vault/server/src/db/account_profile.rs` - `load_time_zone`, `set_time_zone`, `account_clock`
- `crates/vault/server/src/profile.rs` - `time_zone` on the profile, validated
- `crates/vault/server/src/conversations_api.rs` - `year=` filter uses the same boundary rule
- `crates/vault/server/src/dedupe.rs`, `import/staging.rs`, `import/promote.rs` - content key and binds over one timestamp
- `web/src/lib/timeZone.ts`, `TimeZoneProvider.tsx` - the zone, read once, handed everywhere
- `web/src/lib/formatDate.ts`, `components/messages/chatBubbleShared.tsx`, `screens/message/useConversationMessages.ts` - formatters take the zone
- `web/src/screens/OnboardingScreen.tsx`, `settings/ProfileSettingsPanel.tsx` - pick and change the zone

## HTTP API Changes

- `GET /v1/account/profile` - response gains `time_zone` (IANA name)
- `POST /v1/account/profile` - request accepts optional `time_zone`; unknown name is 400
- `Message.timestamp` everywhere it appears - now a UTC instant with `Z`; `timestamp_utc` removed
- `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages?year=` and every `date:` word - boundaries in the account's zone

## Database Changes

- [ ] No schema changes
- [x] `schema/sql/*.sql` changed and `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped (every vault rebuilds empty and re-imports)

## How to Test

1. `cargo test -p message-vault-server` (SQLite) and `MV_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://vault:vault@127.0.0.1:5432/vault cargo test -p message-vault-server` (Postgres): the New Year's Eve tests in `conversations_api/tests.rs` and `search/tests.rs` put a `2025-01-01T04:59:00Z` message in 2024 for an account in `America/New_York`.
2. `cd web && npm test`: `formatDate`, `chatBubbleShared`, and `conversationYears` tests show the same instant landing on different days and years by zone.
3. In the app: create an account, note the Time Zone picker on Profile Setup preselects the browser's zone; open Settings → Profile and change it; message times and the year chips change with it.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the code
- [x] Added unit tests for new functionality
- [x] Added integration tests where applicable
- [x] Existing tests pass locally
- [x] Updated documentation
- [x] `./scripts/check-pr.sh` passes and formatter rewrites are committed

## Related Issues

Closes #326.

## Screenshots / Demo

Checked in the browser against the demo vault (Vite on :5173, vault on :8080):

- Profile Setup shows a Time Zone picker preselected to the browser's zone (`America/New_York`); the account is created with it and Settings → Profile shows the same value after a reload.
- Changing the picker to `Asia/Tokyo` saves without a Save button and survives a reload.
- On the demo account, conversation 1's first three bubbles read `Oct 11, 8:31 PM`, `Oct 11, 10:01 PM`, `Oct 12, 3:49 AM` under `UTC` and `Oct 12, 5:31 AM`, `Oct 12, 7:01 AM`, `Oct 12, 12:49 PM` after switching to `Asia/Tokyo`: the same instants, nine hours later, with the header range and year chips unchanged.
- The picker takes one line of the fixed-height setup card, so the account-row cap drops from five to four; at four rows the "+ Add account" button was already under the footer.

## Deployment Notes

Schema version 10: every vault rebuilds empty and re-imports, as every schema change does before the first stable release. `chrono-tz` is a new server dependency.

author: wikibutler
body:
## Docs: MODULARITY Part 7 — timing, freshness & multi-input policy

The design answer to "how do union/multi-feed widgets handle timing (fast vs slow sources, timeouts, retries, waiting)?" — grounded in peer-tool practice (Grafana per-query independence, TanStack per-query timeouts/staleTime, RxJS combineLatest/forkJoin/merge, Prometheus staleness, CDN stale-while-revalidate).

**Part 7 covers:**
0. **The reframe** — the hub dissolves most waiting: cascades run on *value writes* (reloadKey bumps), not polls; downstream converges as each source lands, no union-level wait at the dataflow layer
1. **Per-input timeouts & retries, never a union timer** — current budget table (REST ≤15s · batched ≤30s · SPARQL ≤60s · MinT/LLM POST ≤60–90s, retries 1)
2. **Incremental render with per-input state** (combineLatest-with-progress) — `waitFor:'all'` is the opt-in forkJoin mode
3. **Never blank what you have; never let stale work win** — SWR caches + the **supersede rule** (ISSUE-54 / PR #24 request-serial guard)
4. **Etiquette under the no-backend ceiling** — caches as first line, pacing, stagger, fan-out caps
5. **Failure attribution** — per-source error badges, never a bare "failed"

Docs-only. Companion to the #18 timing discussion.

author: alexg-g
body:
## Summary

Adds a Dependabot `ignore` entry pinning `@sentry/react-native` at 8.22.0, mirroring the existing `react-native-screens` precedent in the same list.

`@sentry/react-native` >= 8.23.0 raises `sentry_cocoa_version` from 9.19.1 to 9.24.0, and `RNSentry.podspec` then **raises outright** when `SENTRY_USE_XCFRAMEWORK=0` — the opt-out `ios/Podfile` sets deliberately to keep the RNSentry SPEC CHECKSUM from being a function of `$HOME`:

```
[!] Invalid `RNSentry.podspec` file: [Sentry] SENTRY_USE_XCFRAMEWORK=0 is no longer supported.
```

sentry-cocoa stopped publishing to the CocoaPods trunk at 9.20.0, so 9.19.1 is the last version reachable that way.

## Verification

`npm pack` of each release, reading `package/RNSentry.podspec`:

| version | `sentry_cocoa_version` | raises on opt-out? |
|---|---|---|
| 8.22.0 (current) | `9.19.1` | no |
| **8.23.0** | **`9.24.0`** | **yes** |
| 8.24.0 | `9.24.0` | yes |
| 8.25.0 | `9.26.1` | yes |

There is **no safe intermediate** — 8.23.0 is already the cliff, not 8.24.0. Issue #743's table (`8.22.0 → 8.23.0+`) should be read accordingly.

## Why it matters

Without this, Dependabot regenerates a `native-dependencies` group PR every cycle that cannot even run `pod install` — see closed #773, where ESLint, TypeScript and Jest all passed and CI died at the `Podfile.lock consistency check` step. That strands the five other native bumps (rn-fs, RNGH, safe-area-context, nitro-modules, react-native-config) behind a package that is structurally unmergeable, which is precisely the failure mode the native-dependencies group was created to prevent (#753).

8.22.0 is currently the only 8.22.x published, so `> 8.22.0` still admits a future 8.22.1 patch.

## Lifting this

Either path unblocks it, and neither requires a version bump to test:

- **#768** — drop the `SENTRY_USE_XCFRAMEWORK=0` opt-out. The Podfile's stated rationale is now stale: upstream's `stage_sentry_xcframework_in_pods` symlinks the cached xcframework into `Pods/sentry-xcframeworks/<version>/` and returns a `$(PODS_ROOT)/...` **relative** path, so the `$HOME` leak it guards against is fixed. `diff -u` of that helper between 8.22.0 and 8.24.0 is a single hunk (the SHA256 pin table). Probeable at 8.22.0 today.
- **Milestone #16** — the SPM migration.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML parses; the npm `ignore` list has 14 entries with the new one present and correctly shaped
- [x] Entry placed alongside the `react-native-screens` version-range precedent in the same list
- [ ] CI green (config-only change; no source, lockfile, or podspec touched)

Follow-up: the five non-Sentry native bumps still want a deliberate re-cut with a paired `pod install` commit and a two-platform device smoke — tracked in #743.

### Kernel additions (all exercised by `tests/domain/spellAuthoredWave3.test.ts`)
- `revive` primary: a `healing` op with `revive: true`; the life transition clears dead/unconscious and resets death saves (Revivify 1 HP; Resurrection/True Resurrection/Reincarnate full).
- `maximum-hp` primary: existing maximum-hp op + matching healing (Aid, +5/slot).
- `dispel` primary: removes every `spell`-tagged effect on the target (Dispel Magic; the level check is left to the DM and stated in the scope).
- Tracked-effect `preventsDeath`: the damage finalizer keeps the creature at 1 HP once and ends the ward (Death Ward).
- `armorClass.addTargetSaveModifier`: AC floor 13 + DEX save modifier at cast (Mage Armor).
- `attackDamage.consumeOnUse` + `dice.dicePerSlotAboveBase`: the attack compiler removes the rider's effect on a hit (Divine Smite 2d8 +1d8/slot, Shining Smite 2d6 +1d6/slot; both modelled as "next hit" since the runtime asks before the attack — stated in the scope).
- Tracked-effect `retaliation`: the attack compiler deals the dice to the attacker on a hit; `effectRetaliations` feeds the production attack transaction (Fire Shield, melee only).
- Definition `summons {monsterId, count, countPerSlotAboveBase}`: `spellSummonRuntimeAdapter` instantiates the catalog creature on the caster's side after the cast commits (Animate Dead → Skeleton ×1 +2/slot, Create Undead → Ghoul ×3). Composition order: after `productionSpellRuntimeAdapter`.

### Also
Freedom of Movement (ends Grappled/Restrained), Aura of Life (necrotic resistance), Earthquake (DEX save → Prone) with existing vocabulary. Roadmap gains gates C1-06 and C1-07; C1-05 merge SHA recorded.

## Tests
- `npm run test:spellcasting` (89 pass) incl. new `spellAuthoredWave3` (revive, Aid, dispel, Mage Armor AC, Death Ward, Divine Smite consumed on hit and kept on a miss, Fire Shield burns a melee hit and not a ranged one) and `tests/ui/spellSummon.test.ts` (installed summoning cantrip → two goblin warriors on the caster's side).

## Summary

- Preserve the existing visual design. Replace enterprise targeting and duplicate search/notes fields with one multiline requirement area and optional files; budget, invoice and certification remain separate controls.

- Save actual attachment bytes in PostgreSQL, with authenticated metadata/download, SHA-256 validation, bounded sizes/quotas and idempotent upload references. Files are not parsed, read by a model or sent to Sellers/Bazaar.
- Creating a modern request atomically links files and queues a discovery-only job. Visible flow: 提交需求 → 選擇服務 → 付款與憑證. No second exploration click and no payment until selection. Generation guards and a cross-kind unique index protect late/replayed workers.
- First invoice attempt succeeds in the normal Demo configuration. Retain genuine failure recovery, immutable historical evidence and necessary test-invoice/payment-mode disclosures. Normal UI does not expose raw invoice provider mode names.
- Support old unqueued drafts, lost-response recovery with the original key, and explicit re-upload after confirmed attachment expiry.
- Preserve guarded catalog migration: new IDs start UNREVIEWED; archive legacy A–D without rewriting legal identities, wallets, historical payments/invoices/caches or certifications. Reject stale credit-only Bazaar metadata; never silently substitute another category/local service.

## Verification

- API unit: 53 files / 550 tests passed.
- Isolated loopback PostgreSQL: 20 files / 123 tests passed, including four modern procurement flows, durable discovery, real attachment persistence and catalog/history guards.
- Web unit: 27 tests passed. API/Web/Docs typecheck and lint passed (Docs retains its existing image warning); Web and Docs production builds passed.
- Python Playwright, local production Web at 375/768/1280: 13 complete fixture purchases, 41 intercepted writes, first-attempt invoices, exact attachment upload/download bytes, keyboard file picker, lost-response recovery, legacy queued-state compatibility and expired-file recovery. No public network request, wallet or actual settlement.
- Separate real Next BFF/loopback upstream test: anonymous/cross-origin/unsupported routes rejected; ordinary 64 KiB and upload 3 MiB body limits enforced; authenticated metadata plus byte-identical 168 KB download.
- Independent reviews covered concurrency/generation, upload auth/privacy, recovery and old-draft compatibility; findings fixed and browser-regressed.
- The separate local-stack integration harness requires its own Anvil + HTTP services and is excluded from the isolated fixture result; public RPC/wallet credentials were not substituted.

No Railway deployment, live DB update, certification grant, funding or indexing payment was performed. Merge/deployment remains paused for review.

When authorized: deploy Sellers, then API/migrations, then Web/Docs. Apply the attachment/generation migration, cross-kind dispatch index and extended workflow-kind CHECK before new workers. Do not mix old workers with DISCOVER_TASK jobs. Existing overlapping active jobs deliberately fail the new unique index: investigate, never delete jobs to force migration.

Explicitly change any deployed MOCK_INVOICE_FAIL_ONCE=true to false; source defaults do not override existing runtime variables. Historical attempt-2 invoices remain unchanged.

New service scopes still require review and refreshed Bazaar metadata/index. Indexing fees require separate target/amount confirmation. See docs/service-first-catalog.md for file limits, retention, test commands and rollout guards. Local fixture success is not proof of funded testnet or Bazaar indexing success.

body:
`weekly_backtest.sh` and `com.stockmodel.weekly.plist` have been running the Sunday backtest from `~/Library`, unversioned and outside the repo.

Two consequences:

1. **The runbook never mentioned the job it describes is already automated.** `scheduled-tasks/weekly-backtest/SKILL.md` says "run on Sunday, never concurrently with `daily-stock-analysis` — both read and refresh `output/prices`" — but a launchd agent already runs the unattended half every Sunday 20:00 ET. An agent following the runbook on a Sunday could collide with it, breaking the exact rule the runbook states.
2. **It broke silently.** The script failed on 2026-08-30 with `cd: .../worktrees/backtesting: No such file or directory` after that worktree was deleted, and again the following Sunday. Nothing surfaced it because nothing was watching an unversioned file.

## Changes

- Track `weekly_backtest.sh` and `com.stockmodel.weekly.plist` alongside the runbook.
- Add a runbook section: the launchd job exists, what it covers (price refresh, `annotate`, `measure`, per-horizon `calibrate`) versus what it leaves to the agent (readiness census, publishing the summary), and to check `~/Library/Logs/StockModel/weekly_<date>.log` before starting a manual run.

The tracked script points at the `~/Projects` checkout and the `phase-1-api` venv — the repo-root `.venv` lacks `scipy`, which `backtest.py` needs transitively via `models/montecarlo.py`, so the previous interpreter would have crashed this Sunday.

The copies under `~/Library` are what actually execute; these are **not** symlinked. Edit here and copy out. Making them symlinks would be a reasonable follow-up.

author: meltface-80
body:
Groundwork for playing to devices that are not Sonos. This release moves code and adds no behaviour: 544 tests pass, and every one that existed beforehand passed unchanged, which is the only claim it makes.

lib/upnp.js holds what was never Sonos-specific — SOAP, SSDP, the H:MM:SS time format, the play-mode enum. soap() is TOLD its control path rather than looking one up: Sonos publishes a table every player shares, a stock renderer names its own in its device description, and a table in the shared file would be one manufacturer's paths pretending to be the protocol.

lib/sonos.js keeps the dialect and re-exports none of the rest. A re-export was the smaller diff and is exactly how a partial migration hides: two import paths for one function, changed for whichever half of the tree somebody happened to grep.

lib/queue.js states what a room's queue is — list, length, add, clear, startAt, jumpTo — because Sonos owns its queue and standard AVTransport has none at all, so a second kind of player does not need a different enqueue, it needs the queue somewhere else entirely. queueFor() is the one place that decides which kind a room has. lib/playback.js now asks a queue rather than a speaker and names no SOAP action, no x-rincon and no DIDL: what a track IS comes from the library, what a player wants to be TOLD about it is protocol.

Doing this first, alone, is deliberate. playback.js also counts plays and drives Random Album Radio; moving it while nothing else changes is the difference between a refactor the suite can vouch for and a rewrite nobody can review.

Tests: test/upnp.test.js fails the build if a Sonos word reappears in the shared module, matching code with block comments stripped — a check its own rationale trips is a check somebody deletes. test/queue.test.js holds the seam. All four guards were mutation-tested; the first version of the startAt/jumpTo one was not, and passed happily when jumpTo was changed to call startAt, so it now asserts what the speaker is ASKED rather than what the source says.

author: anishanup
body:
## Why
The deploy workflow currently pushes to the Space `pelta-ai/pelta-ai-backend`, which Hugging Face has flagged "abusive" and paused. Restart and Factory Rebuild both return 503, and only HF's safety team can lift the flag (a support ticket is in progress). Meanwhile `anishanup/pelta` is a healthy, running Docker Space serving the same app.

This repoints the CI deploy target to `anishanup/pelta` so deploys are no longer blocked by the flag review.

## What changed
`.github/workflows/deploy-to-hf.yml` — the `hf` remote now points at `https://huggingface.co/spaces/anishanup/pelta` (2 lines). Nothing else.

## Required for this to work (please verify before merging)
1. **The GitHub Actions `HF_TOKEN` secret must have WRITE access to `anishanup/pelta`** (a personal-account Space). If the current secret is scoped only to the `pelta-ai` org, replace it with a token that also has write on the `anishanup` user (e.g. a fine-grained token with `repo.content.write` on that account).
2. **`anishanup/pelta` must have the runtime secrets/variables set:** `HF_TOKEN` (Secret), `STORAGE_PROVIDER=mock` (Variable), `ENVIRONMENT=production` (Variable). *(Already set.)*
3. `anishanup/pelta` is a Docker Space. *(It is.)*

## Effect after merge
The next push to `main` (or a manual `workflow_dispatch`) force-pushes the built app — including the current UI on `main` — to `anishanup/pelta`, replacing its existing build. First build takes ~10–15 min.

## Note
This does not attempt to un-flag `pelta-ai/pelta-ai-backend`; that stays with HF support. If/when it is restored, the target can be switched back with a one-line change.

author: clintongormley
body:
Owner decision 2026-09-05: a PR that goes `BEHIND` is not rebased for that alone. A rebase + force-push re-runs the pre-push hook and CI over an unchanged code diff.

**Rule (CLAUDE.md §6):** when GitHub still reports the PR `MERGEABLE` and what `main` gained since the merge-base is documentation, or code in no file the branch changed, it lands as it is with `gh pr merge --squash --admin`. The up-to-date rule guards against semantic conflicts, which documentation cannot cause; the post-merge unfiltered `main` run tests the merged tree. Rebase in the worktree only for `CONFLICTING`, or when `main` touched a code file the branch also changed, and then push through the hook.

**Receipts:** #119 (code on main, zero overlap, `--admin` verified) and #240 (`MERGEABLE BEHIND` by four docs-only commits overlapping only `docs/backlog.md`).

The classifier that applies the rule lives in the owner's `/land-branch` command (step 2: what `main` gained, and the overlap with the branch), and `/finish-branch` step 10 no longer re-rebases on a mere advance. Docs-only change: one CLAUDE.md bullet.

共存実績を調べに来た人（M3）がそのまま投稿（M2）へ回れず、成長ループが画面上で閉じていませんでした。

※ `/posts/new` は植物の事前選択に対応していないため、単純遷移です（事前選択は別途検討）

### 26 — 図鑑の既定フィルタ

author: sterlanyu
body:
Three log sinks put values into records that ship to the log store with 14-day retention. Each is fixed at the source, where the value is known.

## What leaked

**1. Every SSO sign-in wrote a live authorization code.** The access log stamped `str(request.query_params)` on every request at INFO (`api/middleware/logging.py`, two call sites). The SSO callback takes the identity provider's authorization code and the CSRF state as query parameters (`modules/auth/api/sso.py`), so both landed in a record.

**2. Every web search wrote a Google API key and a slice of case content.** `httpx` logs one INFO line per request carrying the full URL, and the web-search tool reaches Google CSE as `?key=<GOOGLE_API_KEY>&q=<the investigation's search text>` (`modules/agent/tools/web_search.py`). Web search is on by default (`enable_web_search` defaults True).

**3. Copilot-captured page content was previewed at INFO.** `context_builder.py` logged `first_120_chars` of the document on the no-heading-delimiter branch, which is a routine parse outcome, not an error.

Leak 2 was measured under the real logging configuration before and after:

```
before:  HTTP Request: GET https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1?key=AIzaSy-REAL-GOOGLE-KEY-0000&cx=cx123&q=prod+outage%3A+db+creds+rotated+for+acme-corp&num=3 "HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request"
after:   HTTP Request: GET https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1?<redacted> "HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request"
```

## What changed

The access log records query parameter **names** instead of the query string. Which parameters a failing request carried is what debugging needs; the values are what leaks.

A `logging.Filter` on the libraries that log URLs (`httpx`, `aiohttp.client`, `urllib3.connectionpool`) drops query strings. It collapses formatting rather than rewriting the template, because httpx passes the URL as a positional argument — redacting `record.msg` alone would miss it entirely. Method, host, path and status survive, which is the signal the existing comment in `config.py` kept `httpx` unpinned for.

The content preview is deleted; `content_length` stays.

## Why not a redaction processor

This is the class `exception_handlers.py:1028` already documents (fm#1156): "there is no redaction processor in the structlog chain to catch that downstream." A processor is the general fix and is filed separately as the follow-up. It is not in this PR because it is new capability with its own design constraints — it cannot call `DataSanitizer`, which makes a blocking HTTP call to Presidio and logs internally, so it needs a pure regex layer lifted out of `redaction.py` first. These three sinks are fixed here because the source is where the value is actually known, and a processor would not have made this PR unnecessary.

## Verification

Both gates were mutation-tested at the surface, each mutant restored by content afterwards:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Restore `str(request.query_params)` in the access log | 1 failed |
| Empty `URL_LOGGING_THIRD_PARTY_LOGGERS` | 2 failed |

The second mutation initially failed only 1 test and exposed a vacuity hole in my own gate: emptying the tuple made the duplicate-filter test iterate over nothing and pass. That test now asserts the tuple is non-empty first, which is the second commit.

`tests/unit/api/middleware/`, `tests/unit/infrastructure/logging/` and `tests/unit/core/investigation/`: 3777 passed, 4 skipped.

---

## Added after code review

Review found the same credentials still reaching the log store on the **failure** path, which is where this class survives longest. Both are fixed here.

**The 500 handler logged the full URL.** `main.py`'s handler wrote `f"Internal server error on {request.method} {request.url}: {exc}"`, and `request.url` renders the query string — so any unhandled exception on the SSO callback still wrote the authorization code, at ERROR. Now logs `request.url.path`.

**The web-search error path logged the raw exception.** httpx renders `HTTPStatusError` as `"... for url '<full url>'"`, and the Google CSE URL carries the API key and the search text. Measured directly:

```
str(e) -> Client error '400 Bad Request' for url
          'https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1?key=AIzaSy-REAL-KEY-0000&cx=cx1&q=db+creds+for+acme-corp&num=3'
```

A 400 is precisely the response this PR used as its before/after evidence, so the demonstrated failure was only half fixed: the INFO line was clean and the ERROR line still carried both. Now logs the exception type and status code.

**Why the filter could not have caught either.** Review also asked whether the redaction should be applied where every record passes, rather than to an allowlist of loggers. It cannot be, as a stdlib filter: a first-party record's `msg` is structlog's **event dict**, and a blanket filter that rewrites `msg` to a string would destroy the structured event. Verified — `faultmaven.*` records carry `msg` of type `dict`, `httpx` records carry `str`. Covering every record needs a structlog processor operating on the event dict, which is fm#1340. Until then first-party sinks are fixed at the source, and the test module now states that scope.

## A pre-existing bug this turned up

Acting on a review point about reading the value from the request context rather than recomputing it revealed that the context version is **empty**. `start_request` takes `**initial_context`, so the `attributes=` kwarg lands as an attribute literally named `attributes`:

```python
ctx.attributes == {"attributes": {"client_ip": "1.2.3.4", ...}}
```

Every `context.attributes.get("client_ip", "unknown")` on the request-start line has therefore fallen through to its default. That line has been naming `"unknown"` as the client on every request — the same forensics failure the client-IP work fixed in a different line. All three fields now read from the dict the middleware just built, which is also the single source review was asking for.

## Test fixes from review

- The parameter-names anchor asserted `"code" in emitted`, which the `status_code` field of the completion record satisfies on its own. It now asserts the field's **value**, read from wherever the stack put it — structlog fields land in `record.msg`, `extra=` fields land as record attributes, and checking only one silently finds nothing.
- The redaction fixture reconfigured process-wide structlog and installed a filter on the global `httpx` logger with no teardown. It now saves and restores structlog config, root level and handlers, and the filter lists, and pins the levels it depends on rather than inheriting an ambient `LOG_LEVEL`. (The specific ambient-level failure did not reproduce here — `LOG_LEVEL=WARNING` still passed — so this is hardening against a mechanism that is real rather than a bug I observed.)

Each new gate was mutation-tested, every mutant failing exactly one test:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Restore `request.url` in the 500 handler | 1 failed |
| Restore the raw exception in web_search | 1 failed |
| Drop `query_param_names` from the start line | 1 failed |

body: Starts from `main` tip **`e49bf34`** (D-127-A / #244). Current tip **`1e99b89`** (includes the Trinity merge-gate amend). **Draft — do not merge.** Kaylee undrafts on green; Trinity merges. ## What ships **1. Four-path UI (Spec §6).** `app/piecewise_kabsch_path_read.py` projects A's `piecewise_kabsch/{parent_job_id}/` tree onto `assembly_review.four_path`. The review card names four paths — assembler / `kabsch/` / `confidence_kabsch/` / `piecewise_kabsch/` — with four non-colliding persist stems, and only when A's tree is actually on disk. **2. The mandatory Method addendum (Spec §7).** `docs/method-hold48-tiles.md` and the `/method` MethodNote gain a D-127-B section. §7 makes this a deliverable rather than a follow-up: D-127 is **not "done"** without it, and A correctly deferred it under its own GO. **Default served PDB stays the assembler.** No swap, no auto-flip. ## The D-127-specific hazard, and how the card answers it A D-127 seam is not one measurement — it holds *k* domain pieces, each with its own interval, Cα count, weighted RMSD, and refuse reason. D-126's lesson was that one flattering number can hide a 28–68 Å jump. A card that printed a seam mean, a best piece, or a pass count would re-create that lie surface inside the fix for it. So the card renders **one row per piece**, with the parent `rmsd_full_overlap_angstrom` / `max_ca_jump_angstrom` / `linker_n` / `max_linker_ca_jump` beside them as the cross-check rather than instead of them. Neither the reader nor the card derives an average. A refuse before any transform stays **null, never `0.00 Å`**, and a seam with no `pieces` list carries a reason rather than reading as "0 pieces refused". ## The OPS results — disclosed as recorded Per Matt's GO via Emma, plus the Trinity merge-gate amend. **Provenance (D-016): these are ops numbers handed to this PR — from a D-127 OPS restitch of the Spec 27 at tip `e49bf34`, and the D-126 recovery figure. This PR did not run any restitch, did not query Fly, and did not re-measure anything.** They are stated with that attribution attached, on the Method surface and not only in the log. | Fact | Value | |---|---| | D-127 run over the Spec 27 | PASS **17** · REFUSE **10** · FAIL **0** | | `recovered_of_primary_three` | **0** — 2939 `linker_jump_gt_10`, 3272 `rmsd_gt_10`, 3432 `no_domain_pieces` | | Refuse histogram | `linker_jump_gt_10` ×7 (2938, 2939, 3179, 3190, 3321, 3368, 3566) · `rmsd_gt_10` ×2 (3272, 3394) · `no_domain_pieces` ×1 (3432) | | `n_d125_pass_d127_refuse` | **5** | | `n_d126_pass_d127_refuse` | **7** | | `n_d126_refuse_d127_pass` | **0** — piecewise rescued nothing D-126 had already refused | | **D-126 OPS recovered** | **2 of its primary 5** — parents **3368**, **3394** | Seventeen accepted is not the headline, and the surface never prints it without the regress beside it. **D-126 remains the best experimental path among the stitch algorithms tried so far** — said plainly, in those words, on both Method surfaces, and now **quantified** rather than asserted: D-126's 2-of-5 sits directly beside D-127's 0-of-3. The sharpest form of the finding is a read of two already-recorded lists rather than a new number: **both parents D-126 recovered are back in D-127's refuse histogram** — 3368 under `linker_jump_gt_10`, 3394 under `rmsd_gt_10`. Piecewise did not merely fail to add ground; it gave back the ground the previous path had won. Most of its refuses land at the **linkers**, which is exactly where cutting one rigid body into several creates new joins. 0-of-3 was **pre-registered as an allowed outcome** (Spec §3). **No threshold moved**: the 10.0 Å piece gate, the linker gate, the `< 3` Cα floor, and ε = 1e-3 are all unchanged, and a test asserts their live values. Seams recorded ≠ seams solved. ## Tests — T-1134–T-1143 `tests/test_d127_b_four_path.py` (37 tests) plus vitest cases in `AssemblyReview.test.jsx` and `MethodNote.test.jsx`. Hermetic: no Fly, no GPU, no restitch. They can go red, and that was checked rather than assumed. Mutations applied and reverted: - softening the D-126-best statement → `test_method_says_plainly_that_d126_remains_the_best_path_so_far` fails - dropping `n_d126_refuse_d127_pass` from the owner doc → `test_method_discloses_the_d127_ops_run_and_its_named_regress` fails - collapsing the pieces into a mean RMSD in the card → `test_review_card_renders_pieces_and_never_derives_a_seam_average` fails, in both pytest and vitest - dropping, softening, or relocating the 2-of-5 disclosure, or dropping either parent id from it → `test_method_quantifies_the_d126_comparison_with_recovered_2_of_5` fails - dropping either parent from the give-back passage → `test_method_names_that_d127_gave_back_both_parents_d126_recovered` fails Two of those assertions were **too weak on first write and were tightened after mutation testing exposed them**: a bare `3394 in text` was satisfied by the refuse histogram further down the same page, and a backward-looking window around the give-back passage was satisfied by the sentence above it. Both are now position-aware. A's module `core/hold48_piecewise_kabsch.py` is **sha256-pinned** so B cannot edit the algorithm it reads. Three shipped assertions were amended, each with precedent from how D-126-B amended D-125-B's: two named the older payload helper in `app/reads.py` (widened to accept `four_path_payload`), and the D-127 Spec pins that asserted Method *had not* shipped now assert that it *has*. **Local status:** `1341 passed, 23 skipped, 1 xfailed` (pytest) · `493 passed` (vitest). ## Living docs `### D-127-B` was written into `docs/README.md` **before** the code, per rule 1 — the check is the heading, and a test asserts it exists rather than citing it. `#### D-127-B amendment 1` records the OPS disclosure, including the D-126 2-of-5, each with its provenance. `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/Test_Plan.md`, and the PLAN pointers are current. ## Hard stops honoured No ops restitch in this PR · no revised algorithm Spec · no Fly POST · no F-004 ingest · no rent / GPU · no persist rewrite · no edit to `hold48_kabsch.py`, `hold48_confidence_kabsch.py`, or `hold48_piecewise_kabsch.py` · no gate loosened · no served-path flip · no invented numbers · never seams solved · draft PR, and I do not merge or undraft.

body: ## Bug and impact After PR #64, same-instance remount resets `__connectTornDown` / kickoff flags, but an **in-flight async `super.onMount`** from the previous mount can still resolve afterward. Because remount cleared `__connectTornDown`, that stale promise calls `completeConnectMount` / `finishDispatchOnlyMount` and delivers `onUpdate` **while the new mount is still pending** — store→props updates and post-mount kickoff fire before user `onMount` finishes. **Trigger:** Connected component with async `onMount`; `onUnmount()` then `onMount()` on the same instance; resolve the first mount promise only after the second `onMount` has started but before it finishes. ## Root cause Teardown cancellation used only `__connectTornDown`. Remount legitimately clears that flag for the new mount, which re-arms completions belonging to the superseded generation. ## Fix Bump `__connectMountGeneration` at the start of each `onMount` and capture it in async completion handlers. Ignore (or avoid mutating) stale generations for both mapState and mapDispatch-only paths. ## Validation - New regressions in `tests/connect.async-remount-race.test.ts`. - `npx jest tests/connect.async-remount-race.test.ts tests/connect.remount-flags.test.ts tests/connect.spec.ts tests/lifecycle.mount-kickoff.test.ts --no-coverage` — 56 passed. Also still awaiting review (not duplicated here): - https://github.com/iamnikas/effectable/pull/61 - https://github.com/iamnikas/effectable/pull/62 - https://github.com/iamnikas/effectable/pull/63

## Arm B · B2 — W7: Jutila's Lemma 6 (the detector, its Mellin form, the contour node, the floor at a zero, F5's corollary)

One new module, statement-first from the frozen block; no landed file is touched.

- **`Salt/SW/JutilaDetector.lean` (W7, 7 defs + 44 theorems):** the `r`-summed detector `g(s,χ) = Σ_{z₁<n≤x} a(n)χ(n)K(n/x)n^{−s}Σ'_r r⁻¹ψ_r(n)` with the two-level Barban–Vehov weight, Selberg's `ψ = μφ` and the Riesz kernel `K(u) = (1−u)²₊`: (i) the split of the full sum into the `n = 1` term and the detector (Lemma 6's first line, from W6a's two identities); (ii) the mollifier's size `‖M(s)‖ ≤ 2√z₂·R^{3/2}` on `Re s ≥ 1/2`; (iii) the Dirichlet series `L(s,χ)·M(s)` on `Re s > 1` (the `r`-summed (2.2)) and the Mellin representation of the full sum as ONE vertical integral of `2x^w L(ρ+w)M(ρ+w)/(w(w+1)(w+2))`; (iv) THE CONTOUR NODE — the shift from `Re w = 2−β` to `Re w = 1/2−β` across the removable singularity at `w = 0`, by `dslope` of `φ(w) = w·F(w)` with `φ(0) = 0` at a zero and the landed Goursat on the rectangle, the horizontal edges vanishing against the corpus's growth bound and the verticals taken to improper integrals; (v) the two kernel integrals (`π/m²`, `π/m`) and the bound `‖Σ_{n≤x}‖ ≤ 25(T+2)√q(1+log q)√z₂R^{3/2}x^{1/2−β}` at a zero with `119/120 ≤ β < 1`, `|γ| ≤ T`; (vi) the floor `(1−1/x)²(6/π²)(φ(q)/q)log R − E ≤ ‖g(ρ,χ)‖` against W2's uniform harmonic bound; (vii) `q/φ(q) ≤ ω(q)+1 ≤ log q/log 2 + 1` and F5's corollary with the explicit threshold `D = qT ≥ 10²⁰`: the floor `(3/π²)(φ(q)/q)·log R`. Exit rows: the split at the smallest live instance and the F5 numeral at the threshold, each invoking its row.
- **`Salt/SW/All.lean`:** the import and one `#audit_axioms` block (`⟦B2 W7 0905⟧`, 44 names).

Every theorem: `#print axioms` ⊆ `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; no `sorry`, no `native_decide`, no new warnings. The growth bound is the corpus's Pólya–Vinogradov grade (weaker than convexity; the exponent table absorbs it with slack `D^{−71/240}`), `ζ` never enters, no `vonMangoldt`. Executor: Opus, one pass in three build cycles — 27 rows at one attempt, 15 at two, 2 at three, per-row attempts in the commit bodies. Nothing here bears on twin primes: Lemma 6 is one input of the density theorem's assembly (the next wave); the crown's conditions are unchanged.

body:
## Summary

- A content audit across all 36 papers (1155 questions) found 55 items marked Challenge difficulty whose explanation was just the final calculation line (e.g. `"R2 400 + R2 701 = R5 101."`) with no restated method or reasoning — thin for the hardest tier, where learners most need to see the *why*, not just the arithmetic.
- Rewrote all 55 explanations to state the method first (what's being combined, substituted, or divided, and why), then show the same calculation. No answers, prompts, marks, or ids were touched — only explanation text.
- Covers 37 Mathematical Literacy items (percentages, area/scale conversions, running-cost totals, probability from survey/raffle data) and 18 Mathematics items (discriminant = 0 for equal roots, regression line substitution, probability without replacement).

## Verification

- Re-ran the mark-sum + duplicate-id script against the full file — still 36 papers / 1155 items, no mismatches (unchanged, as expected since only explanation strings were edited).
- Re-ran the thin-explanation audit — 0 remaining (was 55).
- `npm run build` passes with no TypeScript errors.
- A mocked-backend Playwright smoke test confirmed affected papers still render correctly and answering a question still records learner progress; visually confirmed one edited item's expanded explanation displays correctly in the Answer & explanation panel.

## Test plan

- [x] Mark-sum + duplicate-id verification script (unchanged, all checks passed)
- [x] Thin-explanation audit (0 remaining)

## Scope

Activates the Phase 6E trusted booking-compensation execution core behind a real Firebase Functions v2 + Firebase Admin SDK runtime.

### Included
- `initializeBookingCompensation` callable endpoint
- authenticated actor identity from `request.auth.uid` only
- request surface restricted to `bookingId`
- active Owner authorization
- delegated Studio Operator authorization requiring active permission set with `booking.create` plus active reciprocal operator linkage
- server-authoritative booking `compensationContext`
- Admin-only protected compensation-rule loading with a 200-rule fail-closed bound
- Admin transaction preserving Phase 6D2 deterministic SHA-256 IDs, all-reads-before-writes, historical snapshot equivalence, immutable entry evidence, and retry lifecycle preservation
- redacted callable receipt and sanitized public error mapping
- generated Functions runtime source mirror from the existing 6C/6D/6E source graph so calculation/orchestration logic is not manually forked
- isolated Functions package on Node.js 22
- Functions emulator configuration
- targeted runtime tests + deployable module import smoke + permanent CI gates
- architecture contract

## Security boundary

The caller cannot submit actor UID, assignments, duration, studio/session type, effective time, percentage bases, compensation rules, rule IDs, expected amounts, source keys, or snapshots.

Raw compensation rules and calculated amounts never leave the trusted runtime.

Studio Operators are authorized only when account, permission set, and reciprocal operational identity are all active and consistent.

## Runtime activation status

This PR adds a deployable/emulator-ready Functions runtime but intentionally does **not** deploy it to production. General booking creation is also still out of scope; the callable requires an existing booking with server-authoritative `compensationContext`.

Tracks #67.

author: cto-new[bot]
body:
## Summary
Adds Apple's **Motion & Fitness** permission to the native iOS app and wires it into motion-assisted location capture, per owner directive ("Location on the Apple app should use Apple's motion and fitness permission for accuracy").

## What changed
- **`ios/App/App/Info.plist`** — added `NSMotionUsageDescription` with an honest, user-facing string matching the existing permission-copy tone.
- **`package.json` + `bun.lock`** — added `@capacitor/motion@^8.0.1` (official Capacitor 8 plugin).
- **`src/lib/native-capabilities.ts`** — new web-safe, fail-closed exports:
  - `requestMotionPermission(): Promise<boolean>` — native path calls `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` when available (gated by the plist key above); absent feature → `true`; any throw → `false`. Web → `true` (no-op). Never prompts at boot.
  - `startMotionAssistedCapture(onPosition, opts)` — listens for `accel` events and, on a meaningful acceleration-vector change (exceeding a m/s² threshold), fires a fresh high-accuracy `getLocation()` and routes it through the same report path the tracker uses. Debounced to at most one capture/30s. Returns a `stop()` cleanup handle. No-op on web / when permission denied / when plugin absent.
- **`src/components/driver-gps-tracker.tsx`** — native `start()` path requests motion permission and starts motion-assisted capture after location tracking starts (user-initiated flow: authenticated driver enters the portal); cleanup stops it.

## Honesty note (important)
Motion & Fitness / accelerometer data does **not** change GPS math. `@capacitor/motion` exposes accelerometer + orientation (Web `DeviceMotionEvent`/`DeviceOrientationEvent`), not Core Motion's step/activity classifier. What this genuinely does:
1. Requests the Motion & Fitness permission the owner asked for, and
2. Uses motion events to trigger **fresher** high-accuracy GPS fixes — more frequent while the device is moving, less battery waste while it is still.

Motion is a strictly fail-closed **enhancement**: if permission is denied or the plugin is absent, the existing GPS/location pipeline continues exactly as it does today.

## Gates (all green, run sequentially)
1. `bun test native-capabilities.test.mjs` — 11 pass / 0 fail (39 expect calls)
2. `bun test native-push-registration.test.mjs` — 4 pass / 0 fail (17 expect calls)
3. `bun test driver-gps-tracker.test.mjs` — 11 assertions passed
4. `bunx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0, 0 lines (zero-new)
5. `bun run build` — exit 0

author: sam-apostel
body:
You asked whether the infill-pattern cards should have been a plugin's job rather than compiled in. They should have been, and now they are — along with everything else the form registry was doing.

## The problem with the built-ins

The registry from #7 was described as "where a plugin would eventually attach", but the only way in was C++. So I registered `fill_pattern` as an eighteen-option card grid as a built-in — settling in compiled code a question that isn't settled. Whether eighteen bare labels in three columns beat the dropdown they replaced is a judgement that will change, that different people make differently, and that nobody should rebuild the slicer to revisit.

## Declaring, not drawing

A `form.plugin` defines a `forms` table instead of an `execute()`, and gets no _Plugins_ menu entry — there is nothing to run.

It declares rather than draws. The settings form is an immediate-mode UI redrawn every frame alongside the 3D scene, so calling into Lua to paint it would put a script interpreter in the frame loop. The script runs once when plugins are scanned; the controls it asked for are built and driven in C++ from then on. Edit the file, _Plugins_ → _Rescan_.

Storage is untouched: the controls read and write the same settings through the same path an ordinary row uses, so profiles, the backend and 3MFs never learn a plugin was involved.

## Four kinds

```lua
forms = {
    { kind = "slider", key = "fill_density", step = 1 },
    { kind = "cards",  key = "fill_pattern", columns = 3 },
    { kind = "section_toggle", key = "ironing" },
    {
        kind = "choice",
        label = "Travel detour",
        options = {
            { label = "Straight",
              set = { avoid_crossing_perimeters = false,
                      avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs = false } },
            { label = "Around perimeters",
              set = { avoid_crossing_perimeters = true },
              reveals = { "avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour" } },
            { label = "Around curled overhangs (experimental)",
              set = { avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs = true } },
        },
    },
}
```

`choice` is `TravelAvoidanceElement` made general, which is why that file is deleted. An option declares the value each flag takes while it is chosen; a flag it does not name is **cleared on write and ignored on read**, so "Around perimeters" is still recognised in a profile carrying both exclusive flags — the case the hand-written version special-cased. `reveals` keeps the revealed setting's own standard control, so it keeps its units, bounds and formatting.

`section_toggle` is the mechanism from #13, now declared rather than hardcoded.

## Groups are derived, never declared

A control never names its category or option group — the group is looked up from the settings it renders. A plugin cannot restate it wrongly, and it cannot drift when settings move.

The consequence: every setting one control names must be in one group, because a control renders in one place and can only take rows away there. That, plus existence, type, and one-control-per-setting, is checked at scan time. A rejected control costs that control and nothing else: its settings keep their ordinary rows, and the rest of the file still loads.

## The built-ins are gone

`ConfigFormElementRegistry` now has one mutator, `set_form_controls`, called only by the installer. Every control in the app comes from `resources/lua/com.prusaslicer.forms/forms.lua` — a plain text file in the installation.

Including the infill pattern grid. Judging it is now deleting one line and rescanning, rather than editing a registry and recompiling.

## Verification

No build here (this environment has no dependency tree), so I checked what could be checked:

- **The plugin file is valid Lua** and has the shape the C++ parser reads: built Lua 5.4.8 (the version `deps/+Lua` pins), ran the file, and walked the table the way `sol`'s `for_each` does. 12 controls, 14 settings, no duplicate claims, `forms` is a proper array.
- **Every spec would install**, checked against the real definitions parsed out of `ConfigDefsFDM.cpp`: all 14 settings exist, each control's keys share one category and option group, and every type matches its control (`EnumWrapper` for cards, `Percentage` for the slider, `bool` for toggles and choice flags). The resulting groups are identical to the built-in registrations this replaces.
- **The `choice` matching and writing logic**, compiled standalone against a `std::map` config: each option round-trips through write-then-read; both flags set resolves to "Around perimeters" as 2.x did; choosing an option clears the flags it does not name; a trailing flagless option acts as a fallback without swallowing the states the other options match.

## Testing

- Print Settings → Infill: slider and card grid still there, now from the plugin.
- Motion & Dynamics → Travel avoidance: three radios, max detour appears only under "Around perimeters". Then load a profile with both `avoid_crossing_perimeters` and `avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs` set — should show "Around perimeters", and picking anything should clear the pair.
- The three section toggles from #13 (ironing, wipe tower, ooze prevention) should behave exactly as before — they now come from the plugin.
- Undo across a choice, and a preset switch that changes a revealed value — the revealed control should follow (it now re-reads, which `TravelAvoidanceElement` did not).
- Open `resources/lua/com.prusaslicer.forms/forms.lua`, delete the `fill_pattern` line, _Plugins_ → _Rescan_ — dropdown comes back, everything else unchanged. That's the comparison worth making.
- Introduce a typo (`fill_paterrn`), rescan: one line in the log, that setting gets a plain row, everything else still loads.
- _Plugins_ menu: the forms plugin must **not** appear as a runnable entry; the calibration plugins must still work.

author: nuskooler
body:
**Part 4/8 of #281.** Stacked on #766 (→ #765 → #764). This is where validation starts speaking on its own, so it is also where *"never blocks boot"* has to be true rather than merely intended.

```
System starting up...
Configuration: 4 issues (1 error, 3 warnings)
  warning  general.boardnam: unknown key "boardnam" -- did you mean "boardName"?
  warning  scannerTossers.ftn_bso.paths.outbund: unknown key "outbund" -- did you mean "outbound"?
  warning  my_fancy_mod: unknown key "my_fancy_mod"
  error    general.maxConnections: expected number, got string
  Run './oputil.js config validate' for details.
```

...and the board carries on booting.

## Two surfaces

The first load has no logger — `Log.init()` runs from [bbs.js:269](core/bbs.js#L269), well after the config loads at [:104](core/bbs.js#L104). So the initial load reports to the console, one line per issue plus a pointer at the full report; a hot reload reports to the log, where an operator editing a live board is actually looking. Neither stops anything.

## The knob, and how it fails

`general.configValidation` — `warn` (default) or `off`. It gates only the two runtime surfaces. **`oputil config validate` ignores it**: someone who has silenced boot output still needs the command to work when they go looking, and that is the whole point of having a command.

It fails safe in a way worth spelling out:

- The mode is read from the *merged* config, so anything not exactly `off` means `warn`.
- A misspelled **key** (`configValidaton`) leaves the default in force *and* is reported as an unknown key.

So validation cannot be switched off by accident, only on purpose. Both directions have tests.

Deliberately two-valued — nothing here ever refuses to boot, so there is no `strict`.

## Avoiding a double report

`Config.create()` gains `reportValidation`, which oputil sets `false`. Without it, `config validate` would get the boot-time report from the loader hook *and* print its own. Verified it now reports exactly once.

## Verification

Booted `main.js` against a config with a typo, a type error and a mod section — reported, and startup continued past it to fail later on an unrelated missing `menu.hjson`. Then again with `configValidation: off` — silent at boot, while `oputil config validate` still reported all four issues.

11 new tests. Full suite: 2199 passing.

author: wouthh
body:
Playlist observation scans could overwrite an existing tentative Spotify match with confidence `1.0` and status `added`. After normal removal confirmation, reconciliation could then apply the confirmed-match exclusion/local-file path. Separately, timestamp-less logger records used ingestion time as observation time, making repeated historical imports unstable. These are reproduced synthetic behaviors, not claims of an observed incident involving real data.

The shared Spotify snapshot importer now preserves existing confidence and review evidence while updating membership, metadata, last-seen time and missing suspicion. It covers ongoing scans, backfill, excluded parents and reappearance, including the existing tentative-removal receipt after a threshold change. Conflicting Spotify IDs cannot replace an existing track/playlist association: apply rejects the snapshot transactionally, and dry-run validates the same associations through a read-only connection without creating or migrating a database. An association conflict also stops `run-once` before reconciliation or external sync. Already added associations retain their membership classification across threshold changes. The pre-existing removal safety rule still uses the current confidence threshold: a below-current-threshold score remains tentative for removal, even with membership status added. No removal predicate or matching threshold was changed. Confirmed removal, explicit exclusions and safety guards retain their existing behavior; the general-purpose database upsert is unchanged.

Logger input now requires valid source timestamps. Both configured files are validated before import writes; malformed records reject the entire invocation with a bounded, redacted source/line/reason error and CLI exit status 1. Dry-run validates without creating imported state. Named TSV columns are resolved explicitly, and fields preserve the literal quotation marks written by the poller. Valid timestamp spelling and observation identity are preserved. Bare lines and timestamp-less records formerly accepted now produce errors. The README documents this compatibility change and the absence of automatic recovery of existing database or file state.

Validation at `d6a1e3565e1e38570042c5109d73f954fa9889d8`:

- Added regressions before changing production code. At baseline `082464f35414788fe28a3a32f80f7b6c7181a57a`, the full synthetic sequence observed `0.8625/review` become `1.0/added`, then completed two healthy disappearance passes and demonstrated the incorrect exclusion/trash effect. The confirmed-match control passed. Timestamp-less rejection regressions also failed on that baseline (81 failed, 76 passed across the focused files).
- Corrected focused suite: **167 passed**. Complete canonical `python -m pytest -q`: **188 passed** on Python 3.14. Includes real SQLite, fake clients, controlled clocks, disposable audio/file effects, dry-run, tombstones, reappearance, association-conflict rollback, timestamp replay/distinct events, cross-file rejection and CLI redaction/stage stopping.
- Tests ran in disposable containers with networking disabled and no personal configuration/data mounts. Source syntax, complete diff/Markdown inspection, `git diff --check`, all 13 runtime ignores, both fixture exceptions and the seven-file/targeted-privacy gate passed.
- Checksum-verified Gitleaks 8.30.1 and TruffleHog 3.97.2: current tree and exact new commit range all exited 0, with **0 raw detections and 0 classified findings**. Verification and scanner updates disabled; scanners also ran with networking disabled. Earlier TruffleHog range attempts failed to resolve the shallow clone's merge base; those failures were retained, and fetching missing ancestry into the isolated clone allowed the same bounded range scan to complete. No historical credential audit was performed.
- Further preview regressions failed in four cases before read-only conflict validation and now pass. The complete synthetic sequence also verifies the unchanged conservative behavior after raising the current threshold.
- Review follow-up regressions reproduced confirmed-classification drift (scan and backfill), literal poller TSV rejection, and a later Spotify sync bypassing a refused snapshot: 4 failed before the correction, now all pass. The initial head passed all four hosted Python jobs; the follow-up head requires fresh hosted checks and completed cloud review before guarded squash merge.

Only the approved seven files change, including the narrow CLI guard for association conflicts. No schema, dependency, workflow, runtime configuration, real database/library, service, provider, license, release or deployment changes are included.

author: shawndibble
body:
Closes #513.

## What was wrong

A reaction Build Plan's quoted duration applied the Industry (-4%/level) and
Advanced Industry (-3%/level) skill bonuses, and applied nothing for the
Reactions skill. Both are wrong, and in the common case — industry skills
trained, reaction skills not — both understate the duration, so a reaction
plan's quoted ISK/hour came out too good.

## The sourcing #513 asked for

The ticket offered two mutually exclusive outcomes. Both turned out true.

everef.net ref-data dogma attributes, read on the skills and on the attribute
definitions themselves:

| Skill | Attribute | Value | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Industry (3380) | `manufacturingTimeBonus` (440) | -4 | manufacturing only |
| Advanced Industry (3388) | `advancedIndustrySkillIndustryJobTimeBonus` (1961) | -3 | type description: "all manufacturing and research times" |
| Reactions (45746) | `reactionTimeBonus` (2660) | -4 | "reduces time for reactions jobs" |
| Mass / Advanced Mass Reactions | `reactionSlotBonus` (2661) | +1 | job slots, not time |

Reaction is `industryActivity` 11 — neither manufacturing (1) nor research. A
separate `reactionTimeBonus` attribute existing at all is only coherent if the
manufacturing attributes don't reach reactions. The EVE University wiki
"Reactions" §Skills list matches: Reactions, Mass Reactions, Advanced Mass
Reactions, Remote Reactions — no Industry skill.

The one loose thread, recorded in `types.ts` rather than omitted: attribute
1961's *own* description reads "all industry job times", wider than the
skill's type description. The type description is the narrower and
authoritative of the two.

## The change

`timeModifier` picks its `(skill typeID, percent per level)` terms by
`ctx.facility.activity`. Facility and reactor-rig terms were sourced in #460
and stay shared, unchanged.

Nothing else needed plumbing: character skills already reach the engine as a
