author: astubbs
body:
depends on astubbs/parallel-consumer#340
depends on astubbs/parallel-consumer#334

## Description

**The FFI fast-path spike.** astubbs/parallel-consumer#334 shipped a Kafka Streams topology
described from Python and run in a JVM engine, and the windowed-aggregation spike it triggered
came back **bet off at both specifications**: a user could reimplement the aggregation in a plain
dictionary and beat the wrapper 69x at tumbling and 122x at hopping. The losing term was named
precisely - the per-record cost of crossing the language boundary, fitted at `33us + m x 135us`.

That paragraph in `STRATEGY.md` also named its own condition for reopening: *"a transport that
cuts the per-crossing cost by roughly two orders of magnitude - the embedded/FFI direction"*. This
branch is that work. **The condition is met, and meeting it did not settle the question.**

### The crossing is solved

A six-arm ladder measured the same fold across every mechanism available, against a pre-registered
1.35us bar:

| Mechanism | Per crossing |
|---|---|
| Numba `@cfunc` | **19.9 ns** |
| GraalWasm | **747 ns** |
| gRPC (the shipping transport, for context) | ~135 us |

Both clear the bar. The unpredicted headline is that **data placement dominates mechanism**: the
same GraalPy call costs 1,024 ns or 121,775 ns depending only on which side of the boundary the
accumulator lives on. That is now the seam's load-bearing invariant.

The engine can also run where the fast path needs it: the Kafka Streams engine builds and runs as
a **78 MB GraalVM native-image binary with 14 ms startup**, which had never been demonstrated. The
wall was one traced capture of `StreamsConfig`'s class-by-string defaults.

### The floor it was all measured against turned out to be wrong

Two results in sequence, and the second matters more:

1. **Most of the measured engine floor was an instrument choice, not Kafka Streams.** The spike had
   set `statestore.cache.max.bytes=0`. With the cache on and nothing crossing, the wrapper reaches
   **69,265 rec/s** at hopping-12 and **169,748 rec/s** at tumbling.
2. **The reimplementation figure it was being compared against was a stalled consumer.** Retaken
   in-session - the project's own rule, control arms measured beside their treatment arms - the gap
   is 4.70x at tumbling and 6.64x at hopping-12, not the 1.32x a cross-session pairing suggested.
   The reimplementation arm's apparent bimodality was traced to librdkafka halting fetches once its
   local queue passes `queued.max.messages.kbytes` and then waiting out `fetch.queue.backoff.ms`;
   78-81% of the original timed window was fetch wait priced as throughput. **The harness now
   raises rather than averaging over it.**

**And the floor itself is mis-specified.** It is a stateless, non-durable dictionary - no store, no
changelog, no restore, no rebalance recovery, no exactly-once - so it is the floor for a product
Kafka Streams is not in the business of being. Beating it or not decides nothing at any transport
speed.

### What replaces it: the feature-crossover ladder

The question that decides the design is *how many of the features a user actually came for can be
added back to that dictionary before hand-rolling becomes the worse choice*. Durability is the
first rung, measured here, and the answer is a negative worth having:

- Against a **careful** reimplementer, durability moves hopping-12 from 5.84x to 3.85x and tumbling
  not at all. One feature does not close it.
- Against a **naive** one it inverts - the wrapper is ahead 1.75x at hopping-12.
- The two rungs at the *same* feature differ by 6.7x. **So the crossover is not "how many
  features" but "which reimplementer"**, and any verdict that does not say which is unfalsifiable.
- 91% of durability's cost is the `produce()` calls, not the awaited `acks=all` flush - the exact
  volume term the engine's state-store cache deletes. The first feature drags a second in with it.
- The naive changelog also restores 17x slower for identical recovered state, and the variant that
  skips awaiting its writes lost 9,514 records of state with **zero error delivery reports**.

`STRATEGY.md` is updated accordingly: the not-offered verdict is deliberately **not** withdrawn -
it stands on its own evidence - but the reason recorded for it, that a reimplementation is simply
faster, is corrected as too strong.

### Relationship to astubbs/parallel-consumer#334

This branch was cut from astubbs/parallel-consumer#334 and carries that PR's base merged forward,
so the diff here is the spike alone. It answers a question astubbs/parallel-consumer#334 raised and
could not settle inside itself; it does not change what that PR ships.

### Scope boundaries

- **No product capability is added.** The one product-code change is a measurement-only escape
  hatch behind a system property, deliberately off the protocol and documented as such at the call
  site.
- **The `ffi/crossing-ladder/` harness is spike scaffolding**, kept because it is the reproduction
  path for every figure above.
- Two related spike branches (`spike/242-fastpath-wasm`, `spike/242-fastpath-numba`) are concluded
  and deliberately **not** included here.

## Checklist

- [x] Docs updated - the results notes under `docs/inflight/`, the settled-knowledge write-up in `docs/solutions/architecture-patterns/`, and `STRATEGY.md`
- [x] N/A - no user-facing feature is added; the only product-code change is a measurement-only system property that is deliberately not a capability
- [x] N/A - this is a measurement branch; its instruments are its tests, and each arm carries an instrument check that must be able to fail (recorded per section)
- [x] Title & body reflect the final content of this PR
- [x] N/A - asking for `@claude review this` on the PR instead; the diff is overwhelmingly measurement notes and spike scaffolding, where a local `ce-simplify` has nothing to work on

## Reviewing this

The numbers are not the argument - **every figure here is superseded by a later section of the
same note**, which is the point. Read
[`docs/inflight/perf-streams-engine-floor.md`](docs/inflight/perf-streams-engine-floor.md) top to
bottom rather than sampling it: its four dated sections are a chain in which each one falsifies a
consequence the previous one drew, and reading any single section alone gives a conclusion the next
one withdraws.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Gateway restart during cloud worker provisioning could mark the session placement failed and request teardown, preventing startup from resuming its already recorded provider operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The fresh-dispatch catch in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch.ts:261` on the base revision always tore down pending provisioning. Recovery already retained an admitted pending operation, so graceful interruption could terminalize work that an abrupt process exit left replayable.

### Change

Fresh dispatch and recovery share one synchronous retention decision. It checks the exact provisioning placement tuple, the matching pending environment, null destroy intent, and a live injected shutdown predicate. It records the bounded interruption through the existing environment error path, reports the unchanged placement, and rethrows the interruption.

The Gateway wiring combines sidecar shutdown, the environment service's stopping state, and the current process drain signal. Shutdown is visible before enrollment cancellation, and runtime reset reads the replacement drain controller.

## Invariants Preserved

- Explicit Stop and recorded destroy intent still win and tear down the environment.
- Typed session-authority rejection still fails; shutdown is never inferred from provider error text or the reversible restart-signal fence.
- Existing `recoveryRunStarted && pending` retention remains unchanged, including the direct service-stop replay contract in `provider-provisioning.shutdown-replay.test.ts`.
- Provider operation/environment identities, operation draining, schemas, configuration, retries, timeouts, and provider plugin behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

An interrupted pending allocation remains in `provisioning` with no terminal timestamp. Startup can adopt the same provider operation and environment, synchronize the workspace, and activate the placement without starting a replacement operation.

## Evidence

The new fresh-dispatch regression failed against the original catch: expected `provisioning` with a null terminal timestamp, received `failed` with a terminal timestamp. It now passes through reopening the SQLite database and activating the same operation, with one attachment and workspace synchronization.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-provisioning
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  117 passed (117)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch*.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-provisioning*.test.ts src/gateway/server-worker-placement-startup.test.ts src/gateway/server-worker-placement-provision-cancellation.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts
 Test Files  18 passed (18)
      Tests  379 passed (379)

autoreview scoped-clean: no accepted/actionable findings in the selected Git scope and priority
overall: patch is correct (0.87)
```

The explicit file list covers the hyphenated suites omitted by the wrapper's stem selection. The final run includes corrected fixtures and the startup wiring. Validation caught fixture type mismatches and a line-budget violation; the fixtures were corrected and redundant option forwarding was removed without weakening checks.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed with exit code 0, including core/test types, lint, full export scans, storage guards, and runtime import cycles. Main then added retirement tests at the same insertion point. The conflict resolution preserved both groups, moved the shutdown cases to `placement-dispatch-shutdown.test.ts`, and shared the existing recovery harness. All four production files are byte-identical to the fully checked version; after rebasing, all 379 related tests, targeted Gateway test typechecking, and lint passed. The full changed gate was run before this test-only conflict resolution.

Fresh Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Provider behavior was exercised with a synthetic provider and real SQLite state; no live cloud allocation was needed.

## Docs

Updated the replay and restart paragraphs in `docs/gateway/cloud-workers.md` to explain same-operation resumption and explicit Stop destruction. The general restart-recovery overview remains accurate. No changelog edit.

author: powersemmi
body:
# Description

The scaffold job has been failing on `main` since the workspace moved to a pre-release version.

`[patch.crates-io]` redirects where a crate comes from, not what a manifest asks for, and Cargo
keeps pre-releases out of a version range that does not name one. The rendered scaffold asks for
`ruststream = "0.7"`, so it rejects the very checkout the job exists to test, and the failure says
nothing about template drift - the thing the job is meant to catch.

The rendered copy now takes the version actually being built, read from `cargo metadata`, before
the patch section is appended. The template itself keeps `"0.7"`: that is the requirement a user
writes for the release it targets, and it should not churn twice around a release candidate.

Verified by rendering the scaffold locally with `cargo-generate`, applying the same two steps, and
building it against this checkout at `0.7.0-rc.1`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (a non-breaking change that resolves an issue)

CI only; no library code and no template content changes.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

The job this changes is the check itself, so the proof is the job going green on this PR.

Existing purchase orders linked to supplier bills in QuickBooks have no durable portal evidence of the native relationship. This adds a one-record API verifier: the operator selects a saved PO and enters the existing bill ID reviewed in QBO, then the portal checks the exact PO number, memo reference, vendor, and reciprocal transaction links. Ambiguous matches, other PO/bill relationships, and failed receipt saves block success.

Successful read-back saves a realm-scoped `qbPOBillMap` receipt with the transaction IDs, dates, totals, line details, and native link structures. The latest result is visible in the portal and the durable log survives reload. Previously verified pairs can be checked again.

This change reads QBO records only. It does not create native links, change bills, or unlock PO bulk. Programmatic native-link update semantics and controlled PO/link batches remain separate Gate 5 work.

author: mangokingtw
body:
Since the [January 2026 Windows update](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/new-behavior-restricting-certain-applications-to-autofill-credentials-introduced-by-the-windows-january-2026-security-update-29c0bc94-2588-41f9-8534-f058aa5214d5) (CVE-2026-20824), Auto-Type no longer reaches the "Windows Security" credential prompt. The prompt belongs to `CredentialUIBroker.exe` at integrity `0x200a`; an ordinary process is `0x2000`, so UIPI drops the input silently (`SendInput` reports success, the fields stay empty).

This adds `keepassxc-uiaccess-helper`, a small `uiAccess` executable built and installed like `keepassxc-proxy`, and `AutoTypePlatform::beginSequence()`/`endSequence()` around the action loop. The helper is started only for a credential prompt (window class **and** owning image `credentialuibroker.exe`) and stopped afterwards. Off by default (`Security/AutoTypeCredentialPrompts`). Without the helper, or where uiAccess cannot be granted, `::SendInput` runs exactly as before and a warning says why. A separate binary is what keeps the portable ZIP working: `uiAccess` cannot be granted from a user-writable path, which is why #13070 was reverted in #13116.

Fixes #12956. This replaces the approach of #13070, reverted in #13116 because an unsigned `uiAccess` build does not start at all, and a signed one only gains the grant under Program Files. The three cases named in that revert behave as follows, each one measured below:

| install | behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| MSI / ZIP unpacked under `Program Files` (signed) | the helper is granted uiAccess; Auto-Type reaches the prompt — code: [the location rule](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/5840527aab17b14ee906b9d7bb445ddb992e1fea/src/autotype/windows/UiAccessInjector.cpp#L73-L103); recording: `credui-evidence-patched/session_recording.mp4` in [the run's artifact](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/actions/runs/33993674882/artifacts/9977595696) |
| portable ZIP or any user-writable path | no helper is started; Auto-Type behaves exactly as it does today and the warning says why — code: [the location rule](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/5840527aab17b14ee906b9d7bb445ddb992e1fea/src/autotype/windows/UiAccessInjector.cpp#L73-L103) refuses, measured by [refusal-writable-location](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/6e1467893c7ae6b046ab7c50a8a9177a6acd4ea5/tests/ui-credui/verify_refusals.py#L283-L292) ([copy_to_writable_location](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/6e1467893c7ae6b046ab7c50a8a9177a6acd4ea5/tests/ui-credui/verify_refusals.py#L75-L90) moves the install to `%TEMP%`); recording: `credui-evidence-patched/refusals/refusal-writable-location/session_recording.mp4` in [the run's artifact](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/actions/runs/33993674882/artifacts/9977595696) |
| unsigned build, or `Security/AutoTypeCredentialPrompts` off | no helper is started; Auto-Type behaves exactly as it does today — code: [the setting check](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/5840527aab17b14ee906b9d7bb445ddb992e1fea/src/autotype/windows/AutoTypeWindows.cpp#L118-L121) (unsigned: Windows refuses the uiAccess token and the launch fails, so it ends on the same path); measured by [refusal-opt-in-off](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/blob/6e1467893c7ae6b046ab7c50a8a9177a6acd4ea5/tests/ui-credui/verify_refusals.py#L278-L281); recording: `credui-evidence-patched/refusals/refusal-opt-in-off/session_recording.mp4` in [the run's artifact](https://github.com/mangokingTW/keepassxc/actions/runs/33993674882/artifacts/9977595696) |

## About this PR

I have run into this problem before. My [ImeModePersistence](https://github.com/mangokingTW/ImeModePersistence) tool needed to act on windows the main program was not allowed to touch, and the answer there was the same shape as here: a small separate helper that carries the privilege, so the main program does not have to be elevated and does not carry the risk. Building that tool also taught me how badly automated UI testing on Windows goes wrong in CI — which is why [wintegrate](https://github.com/mangokingTW/wintegrate) exists. I believe a PR written with generative AI is only worth a maintainer's time if it is cheap to verify and review, and for UI behaviour that means recordings and measurements a reviewer can open, not descriptions to take on trust. That is what the recordings and measurements below are for.

**Generative AI wrote the majority of the code, the test harness and this text** (Claude Code, model Claude Fable 5.1). I chose what to build, the trust model (peers verified by process identity and install location; the helper's signature is enforced by Windows, with no publisher pinning on top), what to measure and what counts as passing; the AI implemented it and worked through the review rounds. My English is limited, so every sentence here and in the comments is the AI relaying what I mean; if something reads wrong, the fault is mine and I will answer through the same channel. This PR is offered as a complete, end-to-end verified proposal: adopt it, ask for design changes, or decline it on the trade-offs. Nothing in it asks you to trust either of us: every claim about behaviour is backed by a recorded run.

author: mohamed00076
body:
The last open item from `docs/arabic-schema-audit.md` — §4.1.

Every English product page and its Arabic twin describe the same physical product, and nothing in the markup said so. No `@id`, no identifier, no `url`, no `image` on either side. **Zero of the eleven pairs shared anything**, so the site advertised twenty-two unrelated products rather than eleven in two languages.

## What changed

All 22 Product nodes now carry `productID`, `@id`, `url`, `image` and `inLanguage`:

```json
{
  "@type": "Product",
  "@id": "https://olivesegypt.com/products/aggizi-green-olives#product",
  "productID": "aggizi",
  "name": "Aggizi Green Olives",
  "inLanguage": "en",
  "url": "https://olivesegypt.com/products/aggizi-green-olives",
  "image": "https://olivesegypt.com/assets/olive-aggizi-BuhWRZTd.jpg",
  ...
}
```

**Not a word of new copy.** Everything comes from values already in the repository — the canonical key from `scripts/product-order.js`, each page's own canonical URL, and the photograph the page already displays.

## The part that was easy to get wrong

The two halves pull in opposite directions:

| | Across an EN/AR pair |
| --- | --- |
| `productID` | **the same** — this is what says "one product" |
| `@id` | **different** — one per locale |

A shared `@id` would have merged each pair into a single node holding an English *and* an Arabic name for the same thing — which is exactly the contradiction the Organization schema just spent three pull requests removing. It would have been a very easy mistake to make twice, and the check now fails if anyone makes it.

## No fabricated commercial codes

No `sku`, `gtin` or `mpn`. Those denote real commercial identifiers; none has been supplied, and inventing one would be inventing data. `productID` carrying the internal key is honest where a made-up SKU would not be. **The check fails if one appears later.**

## Verification

`npm test` — 8 suites, all green:

```
product-order OK -- 8 surfaces match the canonical 11-product order, both PDF
sources keep Kalamata first in the black-olive section, and all 11 product
pairs share a productID while keeping separate @ids.
```

Confirmed against three injections, each caught:

- a shared `@id` across a pair → *"that merges an English and an Arabic name into one node"*
- a diverging `productID` → *"the locales disagree on productID"*
- a fabricated `sku` → *"asserts a commercial code that has not been supplied"*

## Audit now closed

`docs/arabic-schema-audit.md` §4.1 and §4.2 are both resolved. Everything the audit found is either fixed or was already correct.

## PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT REQUEST

**Not issued here.** Merging is the deployment on this site.

author: stevenjmiklovic
body:
**Problem.** The port driver references `erts_fprintf`, an internal ERTS symbol
removed from the exported ABI in OTP 27. The compiled driver therefore fails to
load on OTP 27/28/29 (`symbol not found in flat namespace '_erts_fprintf'` on
macOS; `undefined symbol: erts_fprintf` on Linux). Fixes #14.

**Fix.** `erts_fprintf` is used only for trace output (`TRACE_F`, behind an
off-by-default `#ifdef TRACE`) and one `sodium_misuse()` fatal print. Alias it to
the standard-library `fprintf`, which is signature-compatible, and drop the now
redundant `extern` declaration. No behavioural change; removes the dependency on
a removed ERTS internal.

```diff
--- a/c_src/drv/libsodium_drv_common.h
+++ b/c_src/drv/libsodium_drv_common.h
@@
 #include <sodium.h>

-extern int erts_fprintf(FILE *, const char *, ...);
+/* OTP 27 removed the internal erts_fprintf ERTS symbol from the exported ABI,
+ * so the driver no longer loads (dlopen: symbol not found '_erts_fprintf').
+ * It is only used for trace output; libc fprintf is signature-compatible. */
+#define erts_fprintf fprintf
```

```diff
--- a/c_src/drv/libsodium_api.h
+++ b/c_src/drv/libsodium_api.h
@@
 } libsodium_namespace_t;

-extern int erts_fprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, ...);
-
 extern void init_libsodium_api(void);
```

(`libsodium_api.h` includes `libsodium_drv_common.h`, so the single `#define`
covers the call site in `libsodium_drv.c`.)

**Testing.** Driver builds and loads on OTP 29 (and OTP 28 CI); a
`libsodium:open()` + `randombytes` round-trip succeeds where it previously failed
at load.

author: uid0
body:
## Intent

GOAL: find the CLASS, not the instance, of "a state change that does not update everything derived from it" — specifically: where does a status transition leave a derived field, timestamp, or linked record un-updated? The set was to be DERIVED from that sentence; the reported instance was only where it was noticed.

THE NOTICED INSTANCE: backend/reorder_queue/admin.py mark_as_sent did queryset.filter(status=DRAFT).update(status=SENT, sent_by=request.user) — status and actor, but no sent_at. I was asked to VERIFY the consequences myself rather than take them on trust. Verified: services/receiving.py create_lead_time_log returns early on a falsy sent_at, so an admin-sent order that is later delivered writes ZERO LeadTimeLog rows — the supplier's performance on that order never enters the table inventory.services.supplier_selection scores suppliers from (PERFORMANCE_WEIGHT 0.1 of a 0.8 max). Pinned by a test that drives the real admin changelist POST and the real receive_delivery, and failed on base with LeadTimeLog.DoesNotExist. Two corrections to the brief, both checked: the model property is days_since_ordered (not days_since_sent), and update_reorder_requests_from_po was never called at all by the admin path, so its timezone.now() fallback was not even reached — the linked requests simply stayed open.

DELIBERATE-OR-INCIDENTAL CALL (the brief asked me to decide and say which, because it changes the right fix): the .update() was INCIDENTAL, not a deliberate signal bypass. Nothing listens for a PurchaseOrder save — settlement_signals fires on the LINE model, signals.py only on request CREATION — so there was nothing to suppress. Therefore the fix routes each action through the service that already owns the transition, rather than adding one more keyword to the .update() call; a second hand-written copy is precisely how the first one drifted. N queries for a checkbox selection is the accepted cost, stated in the docstrings.

THE DERIVED SET, and its DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS (reporting these was an acceptance criterion):
- DRAFT->SENT owes: status, sent_by, sent_at, updated_at (auto_now, which a queryset write never moves), the linked approved reorder-request sweep, and the po_send audit row the staff feed at /api/dashboard/audit-feed/ reads. Admin had two of six.
- SENT->CONFIRMED owes: status, updated_at. EXCLUDED deliberately: expected_delivery_date — a bulk action has no per-order field for it and confirm_order's UNCHANGED sentinel is exactly the leave-it-alone answer. No PO_CONFIRM audit action exists on ANY path, so none was invented.
- ReorderRequest ->APPROVED / ->CANCELLED owe: status, reviewed_by, reviewed_at, updated_at. Admin had two of four. EXCLUDED deliberately: admin_notes on the bulk actions, same no-field reason.

THE CLASS, found by derivation rather than by tripping over it: inventory/admin.py mark_closed did queryset.update(status=CLOSED) where all three other routes to resolved/closed (AssetViewSet.resolve_problem, AssetProblemViewSet.resolve, and services.problem_auto_resolve — whose docstring says every work-order completion path calls it for exactly this reason) stamp resolved_at AND resolved_by. Both fields are on AssetProblemSerializer and both are decoded by ScanTTY. Its sibling mark_resolved stamped the date and left the resolver blank. Swept the remaining status-writers (forgekey redispatch_selected, device_commands.apply_command_ack): both already complete, no third instance.

DESIGN DECISIONS a reviewer would not see from the diff:
- services.mark_sent now records its own po_send event. This is a deliberate, documented exception to the #883 layering note ("views keep their record_audit_event calls; the workflow body lives here") because that transition has THREE performers and a fact-set split across callers is one each new caller can join incompletely. views._mark_sent no longer records it. Pinned with a COUNT == 1, not .exists(), so the view's copy coming back is caught.
- New services/reorder_requests.py mirrors services/purchase_orders.py as the home for that entity's review transitions; the API approve/cancel/auto-approve paths now call it too.
- POPULATIONS WERE PRESERVED on every converted action. mark_closed stays deliberately unfiltered (filing away an already-resolved report is its main use) and mark_resolved keeps its REPORTED precondition. An earlier draft narrowed mark_closed and would have removed an operator ability; a test catches that.
- inventory _settle carries the same "if not problem.resolved_at" guard the API routes use: closing a report somebody else resolved is a filing change, not a new resolution, and must not overwrite who did the work.

EXISTING RECORDS — explicitly instructed NOT to rewrite stored data, and to state plainly what is and is not recoverable. Shipped reorder_queue/management/commands/report_unstamped_transitions.py, a READ-ONLY report following the existing report_duplicate_work_orders convention (positive finding / established absence / explicit unknown). It has NO --fix and a test pins that no such flag exists. NOTHING IS RECOVERABLE: order_date is a different, operator-editable, backdatable fact; updated_at is auto_now and has been overwritten; the pre-fix admin send wrote no audit row either. A lead time needs an order date that was never written, and back-filling from order_date would put invented numbers into the very column that chooses suppliers — worse than the gap, which is currently honest because DeliveryRecord.factor returns 1 for no-history on purpose. What survives is sent_by/reviewed_by and an exact count of affected supplier links.

CROSS-PROJECT: ScanTTY was checked against its REAL remote default branch, not a local checkout — github.com/uid0/scantty, default_branch main per gh api, HEAD 80abc3ba577d6bec6eaef75b796cdc7413303a79, freshly cloned. NO CONTRACT CHANGE: SentAt *time.Time and DaysSinceOrdered *int are already nullable/optional and po_detail.go already guards on nil. No JSON field added, removed, renamed or retyped; fields that returned null now carry values. ScanTTY sends/confirms through the API actions, which were always correct, and does not read the audit feed.

EVIDENCE STANDARD demanded by the task, because several tests in this fleet turned out structurally incapable of failing: every check drives the REAL ModelAdmin action dispatch via a changelist POST rather than calling the action function or hand-simulating it. 27 new tests. 12 were watched failing on base. The other 15 pin preconditions that were already correct, so they were mutation-proved instead — 24 mutations run, all CAUGHT. Two harness results were not free and are worth knowing: one mutation was a syntax error masquerading as CAUGHT and was re-run properly, and one came back NOT CAUGHT, revealing a genuine hole (no fixture had a reviewer-less request in a reviewed status) which was fixed and then caught.

SCOPE CAP the task imposed: a finding earns a fix only if it is (a) an action with no operator-visible effect, (b) a screen or API showing or acting on wrong data, (c) operator input silently discarded, or (d) a documented claim the code does not honour — "cheap and safe" was explicitly NOT a fifth category. Everything fixed here is (a) or (b).

AGENTS.md records the durable rule and why the report has no --fix.

VALIDATION STATUS, stated honestly: lint (black/isort/flake8) clean; frontend 1968 tests pass; 27/27 new tests pass; inventory+maintenance_orders+reorder_queue 3050 pass on the final tree. A full-suite run on the final tree is NOT yet independently confirmed — I accidentally started two pytest sessions against the same Postgres test database and the second collapsed with "database test_oms_marksent is being accessed by other users", so please treat the full backend suite as unverified and establish it in this run.

## What Changed

- Admin bulk actions now route each row through the service that owns the transition instead of a hand-written `queryset.update()`:

author: alcyedmundo281
body:
Amplía [`docs/CICLOS-WEED.md`](../blob/main/docs/CICLOS-WEED.md) con dos ciclos que salieron después de escribirlo. No toca código.

## Ciclo 15 — La interfaz

Los tipos existen desde el ciclo 8 y **no hay por dónde producirlos**: todo entra todavía como texto suelto por un chat. La serie completa de un episodio son cinco documentos:

```
historia clínica            la base. Fase 1 de Weed.
primera nota clínica        el holón, revelado por primera vez
notas de evolución          el grueso del tráfico
notas clínicas intermedias  el holón, revelado otra vez
epicrisis                   cierra el episodio, y sale de la institución
```

La primera y las intermedias son el **mismo tipo**: su diferencia es de posición, y la posición se lee del orden.

Queda escrito que **la historia clínica no la teclea el médico**. Es la solución de Weed para la fase 1 y la interfaz tiene que reflejarla. Un formulario libre para el médico sería automatizar el caos, que es contra lo que este plan entero está ordenado.

## Ciclo 16 — La partida doble

HolonMed lleva su propio libro por debajo del que lleva el clínico. La conciliación tiene la misma forma de tres resultados que `conciliacion.py` ya usa para órdenes y ejecuciones:

| Situación | Qué significa |
|---|---|
| HolonMed lo vio, el clínico no lo escribió | **problema pasado por alto** |
| El clínico lo escribió, HolonMed no lo vio | fallo de cobertura del índice |
| Los dos | concuerda |

Weed midió el primero: **5.2 problemas por paciente** en la sala de urgencias, con un cuestionario de 32 preguntas y personal paramédico. Esa cifra hoy no la produce nadie.

**Y la restricción que lo sostiene no es una concesión al contrato.** HolonMed no escribe en el expediente, propone. Si el sistema fundiera en silencio sus hallazgos con el registro del clínico habría otra vez un solo libro, y la discrepancia —que es el producto— desaparecería. Los dos libros tienen que quedarse separados para que haya algo que conciliar.

## El orden, corregido

De fila india a grafo de dependencias. Serializar de más cuesta tiempo sin comprar nada. Lo que sí es firme: ningún ciclo empieza con su dependencia fuera de `main` — el ciclo 8 ya dejó esa lección cuando la epicrisis entró antes de fusionar, para no migrar dos veces la misma columna.

## 概要
自律営業へ向け、レジ会計を「客選択→サービス開始→未確定の所要時間→明示完了/売上計上」に分離し、初代で確認されている非FIFO挙動を壊さない差し替え可能policy境界を追加する。

## 実装
- `CheckoutSelectionContext`
  - staff / checkout / waiting customers / active service count / capacity
- `CheckoutCustomerSelectionPolicy`
  - 現在待機中の客から任意1名または選択なし
- `CheckoutSelectionCoordinator`
  - staffがcheckout taskへ割当済みであることを要求
  - FIFOを強制しない
  - capacity満杯なら開始しない
  - 待機集合外の客選択を拒否
  - `begin_checkout_service(...)` だけを呼び、売上計上/完了はしない
- `StoreRuntimeHarness`
  - `begin_checkout_service(...)`
  - `finish_checkout_sale(...)`
  - 既存 `complete_checkout_sale(...)` は明示リプレイ向けの即時start+finish互換helperとして維持

## evidence-safe境界
- レジ能力→所要時間式
- 2人打ちレジの協業式
- 体力切れによる中断
- 待ち客離脱
- customer selection rule
- tick/時刻との関係
は未確定のまま。

## Decision
`docs/decisions/0026-explicit-checkout-customer-selection-and-duration-boundary.md`

## テスト
- 後から来た客を選べてFIFOを強制しない

- 待機外客を拒否
- checkout capacity満杯時に2人目を開始しない

author: ppuzio
body:
## Cursor chats stay "working" for ever

`composerHeaders` never clears `unfinishedRunAt` when a run doesn't end cleanly — editor killed mid-run, or the run abandoned with the editor still open. Reading the field's presence as "busy" leaves the row spinning indefinitely; mine showed three chats at 28+ hours.

It can't date the run either. Measured against a real store it equals `createdAt` on every row that carries it, and a row with two turns seven minutes apart still reports the first. It's a flag.

So busy now means `conversationCheckpointLastUpdatedAt` — which Cursor moves on every message and tool result — is after the editor's launch and within `staleAfter`. Falls back to `lastUpdatedAt`, which a quarter of rows carry instead. `staleAfter` is 15 min, injected like the Codex and Antigravity monitors: the longest gap between writes inside a run, over 33,484 of them, was 826s, so 10 min would have cut live runs.

`NSRunningApplication.launchDate` is optional and usually absent (105 of 123 running apps here, Finder and Chrome included), so "running, start unknown" answers `.distantPast` rather than collapsing into "not running". Bundle-id lookup falls back to the bundle name for the same reason — a miss would silently retire every Cursor row.

Also fixes `DateFormatter` ignoring an injected calendar's time zone, in `ResetCopy` and again in `UsageBlock.summary`.

14 tests.

body:
Asked for by **barthel** in #balloon-does-docs: https://discord.com/channels/1430279849171222682/1536088194557419660/1545916365070671944

He corrected two things about the servo bracket from a real machine, and asked for photos and for the black box taken off the two servo adapter renders.

## What his correction changes

The page had the MG995 screwed into its housing through its own mounting ears, and the cover clipping on with no screws. Both are wrong:

- **The servo is not fastened.** It slides into the housing, the cover goes on over it, and the cover's two screws clamp the servo's mounting tabs.
- **The lower arm takes 2 x M3 x 8.**

Confirmed against the STLs, which also fill in the rest of the joint: the housing's 6 heat inserts are two on each of three faces, one screw per insert. Lower arm 2 x M3 x 8 (4.25 mm of arm), side arm 2 x M3 x 12 (8.40 mm), cover 2 x M3 x 12 (6.65 mm). The bracket's own totals are unchanged.

## The screw that falls out of the same measurement

Step 4 said the bracket bolts to the chute core with 2 x M3 x 12, flagged in the page's own words as "inferred by elimination rather than measured, since no STL exists for that joint". There is one, and the two arms are not the same thickness at the ear: the lower arm's is 8.40 mm and does take a 12, the side arm's is 5.00 mm, the same as the bearing covers', and takes an 8. A 12 there bottoms out in the core's blind 5.70 mm insert.

So one screw moves from the 12 column to the 8. The door module is now 5 x M3 x 12 and 21 x M3 x 8, and `chute` is stamped v2 in the catalog for the same change, `breaking: false`.

## Photos

**There are none of this module, and I could not make any.** Nobody in the Discord has photographed the door module or the servo bracket (searched the whole mirrored archive), and the MG995 video the page already embeds cannot be downloaded from CI-style hosts, so its frames are not available to cut. What is available without auth is the video's own poster frame, which happens to show the assembled servo adapter with its four countersunk screws in front of the servo in its bracket, so that is now a figure in step 4.

The rest is renders:

- The cover pulled off the housing, in step 2.
- The bracket assembled, in step 3.

An overview render of the whole module was in the first version of this branch and **has been removed**: barthel says it is wrong (https://discord.com/channels/1430279849171222682/1545916365070671944/1546028686539493446). The parts I placed it from are not all in the assembly frame I assumed they were.

## The servo adapter renders

The two loose half-views are replaced by an exploded view and an assembled one, colour-coded, following the Interface idler gear entry on the top-interface page. It now reads as a build order rather than two parts sitting next to each other: horn, then exploded. The assembled render came out again at barthel's ask (the exploded one carries it), the horn photo is mirrored so its splined sleeve points at the half it goes into, and the text says the sleeve seats in that half, which is the only way it fits. The preparation step is also reordered: the three heat-insert entries first, then the two sub-assemblies that go together there.

## The black box

Both servo adapter renders had a stub of the caption bar left in the bottom-left corner. Painted out and re-published; nothing else in either image changed.

## Later asks on the same page

- The overview render is gone (barthel: it is wrong).
- The two bearing-holder heat-insert entries are one entry with one render: the holders are a mirror pair, so the job is identical on both. The page now also says they are **handed** -- only a reflection maps one onto the other, no rotation does, so you print one of each.
- New preparation entry for seating the two 6704-2RS bearings, with a render. The seat is measured, and it closes exactly: the holder's bore is a **27.3 mm pocket 9.00 mm deep** onto a 24.4 mm step, the bearing is **4 mm** wide, and the bearing cover carries a **5.00 mm** annular boss. 4 + 5 = 9.
- New **step 4, hanging the door on its bearings and the race**, with a render. The order is not invented: both holder bores are exactly concentric with the door's Ø19.8 mm shaft, none of the four parts overlaps another in its own coordinates, and the race touches the holders at a 0.000 mm gap, so they are in one assembly frame and only fit one way. The shaft is captured once it is together, so the holders must go on before anything is bolted down. The door is also handed -- one shaft end is a ~12 mm hex spigot, and that is the servo side. Old step 4 is now step 5.
- **Fitting to the core is now two steps**: step 5 bolts the flap assembly on (the two bearing covers are the only thing holding it to the core), step 6 bolts the bracket on and couples the adapter to the door, and carries the video. The hex joint is measured too: the door's shaft ends in a **12.0 mm across-flats hex spigot** and the flap-side adapter has a **12.4 mm hex socket**, same orientation, so that is a confirmed pair rather than an assumption.
- Step 5 carries a **real photograph** of the flap assembly on the core, from 0:01 of the MG995 video. barthel screenshotted the frame (YouTube will not serve this box the video, so only four fixed frames are reachable here and none of them is that one); cropped here to the core, with the player chrome and the play overlay out of frame. The finished servo bracket is lying beside the core in the same frame, so **step 3 gets a real photo too**. barthel also confirmed the video is Spencer's, so the four captions on this page that said the filmer was not recorded now credit him, stills included.

The `chute` v2 version entry carries `"commit": null` on purpose. This branch was rebased onto main after #558, so the hash `stamp_versions.py` had written no longer exists, and since the board squashes, any hash written here is wrong by the time it lands. `layer` v4 already sits on main the same way; run `catalog/stamp_versions.py` after the merge.

author: stefanmaron
body:
Closes #2931

`RunnerPageInstance.RaiseOnAction` refused an action with no `OnAction` trigger, using the anchor `testpage-action` and the message "An action whose effect is RunObject (opening another page or report) cannot be performed here. See docs/scope.md". This performs the `RunObject` instead, and keeps the two message fixes that came with the earlier classification-only version.

## The dispatch was removed on a wrong premise, and the premise has been re-measured

An earlier version of this branch implemented the dispatch. It was stripped because corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#172 failed on all 8 BC legs, which was read as "real BC does not open the target".

That reading was wrong, and the reason had nothing to do with BC. The corpus CI's Linux image installed Patch #21, a hook that replaced `NavOpenTaskPageAction.ShowForm` with a no-op. `ShowForm` is the single point where a task-page open becomes a displayed form, so the target page was built and never shown: nothing opened, no handler was looked up, and no error was raised. The tier could not answer the question it was asked. #2986 records that blind spot.

`StefanMaron/MsDyn365Bc.On.Linux` #63 made Patch #21 faithful, and #62 fixed a 2048-character `CodeunitIds` overflow that had been breaking the 27.x legs. I re-ran PR #172 against the rebuilt image — run [34013909696](https://github.com/StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests/actions/runs/34013909696), head `e78e982`, same tree as the previous head, pushed as an empty commit so no existing log was overwritten:

| test | old image | new image |
|---|---|---|
| `RunObjectActionOpensTheTargetOnTheHostsCurrentRow` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `RunObjectActionToAStandardDialogTargetIsAnsweredByTheModalHandler` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `ActionrefToARunObjectActionOpensTheSameTarget` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `RunObjectFromACardHostProcessingArea` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `RunObjectFromACardHostNavigationGroup` | FAIL | **PASS** |
| `RunObjectActionWithoutAHandlerIsRefused` | FAIL | FAIL |
| `AnActionWithATriggerStillRunsItsTriggerAndOpensNothing` | PASS | PASS |
| `ControlPageRunReachesTheSameHandler` | PASS | PASS |

Identical on 27.0, 27.3, 27.5, 28.0, 28.1, 28.2, 28.3 and 28.4. Per-leg counts, not just conclusions: 28.x `2642 total, 2641 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped, 0 codeunit error(s)`; 27.x `2610 total, 2609 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped, 0 codeunit error(s)`, the 32-test difference being the `BC28PLUS` guards. Exactly one failing test corpus-wide on every leg. Full write-up in #2975.

So real BC does open the target, positions it on the host's current row for `RunPageOnRec = true`, picks the handler kind from the target's `PageType`, and behaves the same through an `actionref`. The dispatch is restored.

## What changes

- **The `RunObject` is performed.** `RaiseOnAction` tries the action's own trigger, then an `actionref` target, then `TryRunActionRunObject`. An AL action carries either an `OnAction` trigger or a `RunObject`, never both, so the `RunObject` half belongs exactly where the trigger lookup comes up empty.
- **A precompiled page's target is resolved from `SymbolReference.json`**, which states `RunObject` as a bare object NAME with no type beside it — measured across Base Application 28.1's 5,455 action `RunObject` values, not one carries a type. The name is resolved against the run's own page inventory, the same by-name resolution `CardPageId` / `LookupPageId` / `DrillDownPageId` already use.
- **An ambiguous name is refused, not guessed.** 73 names in Base Application 28.1 are shared between a page and a report, codeunit, xmlport or query, across 326 actions — page 31 "Item List" declares `RunObject = Report "Item Substitutions"` (5701) while page 5720 carries the same name. Opening the page for an action whose AL named the report would be a silent wrong answer, so this refuses and cites #2943.
- **The anchor stays `not-yet-implemented`**, not the false `docs/scope.md` claim, for everything still refused. `docs/scope.md` has no entry placing `RunObject` out of scope, and an `expect-oos` entry written against the old anchor would have buried a real gap permanently.
- **`See docs/scope.md — see docs/scope.md` stays fixed.** `RunnerOutOfScopeException` appends its own pointer, and throw sites also wrote one at the end of their reason, so the file was named twice. Normalised in the exception, so a throw site added later cannot reintroduce it. An anchored pointer (`docs/scope.md#email`) and one mid-sentence are left alone — both carry information the appended link does not. 37 sites across 10 files on current `main` render through it.
- **`BcAppSymbolCache` version 30 → 31.** `PageSymbol` / `PageExtensionSymbol` gained `MemberIdToRunObject`. A v30 payload deserialises it as null, which reads as "this action declares no RunObject", replaying the pre-fix refusal from cache rather than missing — a wrong answer, so it needs the bump.

Deliberately still refused, loudly, and out of scope for this PR: `RunPageLink` (#2942) and non-page target kinds (#2943). Both have a test pinning the refusal.

## Rebased onto current `main`

`main` moved a long way under this branch. Two places the merge mattered, both resolved by reading the merged file rather than taking either side:

- `RunnerOutOfScopeException.BuildMessage` — `main` gained #2894's widening, which lets a `docAnchor` naming its own doc file be used verbatim. The pre-strip commit predates it and would have reverted it. `main`'s version is kept, with the pointer normalisation added on top.
- `BcAppSymbolCache` — `main` advanced to `CacheVersion = 30` with its own v27-v30 notes. Those are kept and the `RunObject` bump is appended as v31, rather than reusing the v28 number the pre-strip commit had.

The only change to `RunnerPageInstance.cs` is `RaiseOnAction` plus making the class `partial`; #3007's validation-error recording is untouched.

## Tests

`tests/runner-extras/testpage-promoted-actionref` 9 → 14, `testpage-precompiled-member-names` 7 → 8. The dispatch arms:

- `RunObjectPageActionIsPerformedAndNoLongerRefusedByTheRunner`
- `ActionrefToARunObjectPageActionIsPerformedToo`
- `RunObjectOnlyAction_OnPrecompiledBasePage_ResolvesItsTargetAndRefusesOnlyTheLink`
- `AmbiguousRunObjectName_OnPrecompiledBasePage_RefusesRatherThanGuessing` — drives a real Base Application page, so the 73-shared-names case is pinned against real symbol data and not a fixture

Negative arms, so a "dispatch everything" implementation cannot pass: `RunObjectWithRunPageLinkRefusesAsANotYetImplementedGap`, `RunObjectNamingAReportRefusesAsANotYetImplementedGap`, `ActionWithNoEffectAtAllStillRefusesLoudly`, `ActionrefToAnEffectlessActionRefusesNamingItsTarget`, `ARefusalNamesDocsScopeExactlyOnce`.

**RED → GREEN, measured on this rebased tree.** RED is `main` at `9ba81187` with only the new AL test files copied in and none of the C# change: **284 pass / 9 fail**, each failing arm reporting the old refusal, and the pointer bug visible in the message as `See docs/scope.md — see docs/scope.md`. GREEN is this branch: **293 pass / 0 fail**.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| al-language corpus, CI invocation with `--count-baseline` | 2599 / 2599, exit 0 |
| `tests/runner-extras` with `--count-baseline` (cold) | 293 / 293, exit 0 |
| `tests/runner-extras` again, warm symbol cache | 293 / 293, exit 0 |
| `AlRunner.Tests` filtered to pointer / symbol-cache surfaces | 40 passed, 0 failed |
| `AlRunner.Tests` filtered to out-of-scope / TestPage / expectations | 176 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped |

The warm second run is there because this change alters what `BcAppSymbolCache` persists: both symbol-cache-dependent tests pass on a cache hit as well as a cold parse, so the version bump does what it claims.

## The one open question

`RunObjectActionWithoutAHandlerIsRefused` still fails upstream and PR #172 stays a draft. With no `[HandlerFunctions]` declared at all, invoking the action raises nothing — not a wrong

author: jongaydos
body:
## Summary

The Maintenance Due tile listed maintenance **records** only. Schedules are the recurring plan; records are the log of work performed, each carrying its own next-due date. A schedule nobody has completed yet has no record behind it — and that is exactly the case most likely to be overdue.

On the staging instance this was found on:

| | shown on the dashboard |
|---|---|
| Monthly Inspection, **31 days overdue** | no |
| Brinc Lemur #1 Inspection, due in 20 | yes |
| Brinc Lemur #2 Inspection, due in 20 | yes |
| Eglin AFB Authorization, due in 86 | no |

The compliance header said "1 overdue maint" while the tile named after it showed only the two things that were fine.

`GET /api/dashboard/maintenance-due` now merges both sources, sorted by days remaining ascending so overdue sorts above anything in the future.

**Deduplication.** Completing a schedule auto-creates a record carrying the schedule's new due date, so every recurring task done once exists in both tables. There is no foreign key between them, so they are matched on `(entity_type, entity_id, due_date)` and the schedule wins — it is the thing that recurs and carries the name a person recognises. A record for the same airframe on a *different* date is genuinely different work and is kept.

**Left out:** inactive schedules, so a paused one does not nag; anything with no due date, since there is no countdown to show and nothing to sort it by.

**Presentation:** the badge reads `31d overdue` rather than `31d -`, and the tile shows five rather than three — four items already exceeded the old limit.

## Test Plan

`backend/tests/test_maintenance_due.py`, 17 tests: both sources appear, the schedule-with-no-record case that started this, ordering with overdue first and name as the tiebreak so the tile does not reshuffle between loads, the duplicate a completed schedule leaves behind, a same-equipment-different-date record kept, inactive and undated excluded, the limit and a negative limit, and the auth gate.

`DashboardPage.test.jsx`: the three tones with the new wording, that the tile does not re-sort what the endpoint ordered, and that five rows render. The maintenance timezone test moved to pilot currency, which is where that arithmetic still happens on the client — maintenance and certificates are now handed a day count by the API.

Falsified: removing the dedupe fails 1; dropping schedules (the old behaviour) fails 11; including inactive schedules fails 1; reversing the sort fails 4. On the frontend, the terse label fails 2, re-sorting fails 1, and slicing back to three fails 1.

Backend 498 passed. Frontend 572/573, the one failure being the known local Node 26 case that passes in CI.

body:
Cron Triggers references currently repeat configuration, handler signatures, limits, and implementation examples that Cloudflare already maintains. This change replaces those copies with task-specific developer documentation links while retaining short guidance on execution boundaries, completion, and recovery.

The five existing filenames and repository entry point remain. The references now route agents to current schedule setup/removal, expression syntax, Green Compute, scheduled handlers, local tests, Workflows, Queues, and coordination documentation. This removes the Green Compute/Smart Placement conflation, the claim that a development scheduled endpoint is public in production, obsolete limit tables, and unsupported queue polling and retry recipes.

Validation: read the actual relevant developer documentation content, reviewed the diff, checked all 16 relative links in the changed files and Markdown fences, and ran `git diff --check` successfully. Markdown-only change; no runtime tests needed. Reference content shrinks from 864 to 87 lines.

Documentation gap: the reviewed Cron Triggers and scheduled-handler pages do not establish the previous reference's general at-least-once delivery and automatic retry-timing guarantees. Those claims were removed; this PR does not replace them with a guessed contract.

## Summary
- Phase 9.2: server-only `BatchLifecycleCoordinator` with binding/scope resolution, deterministic per-item identities, sequential `EntryService.completeEntry` delegation
- Additive durable batch/item evidence migration `0006_batch_operations.sql`
- Wired behind existing Phase 9.1 route gate; public result serialization deferred to Phase 9.3 (`202 BATCH_RESULT_PENDING`)
- RED-first delegation, partial failure, reconciliation-evidence, secret-safety, and D1 evidence tests
- Docs: phase9-todo + migration notes

## Test plan
- [x] Worker `tsc --noEmit` via local bin
- [x] Vitest (156 tests) via local bin
- [ ] CI + Bugbot green
- [ ] CODEX_VERIFIED before merge

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches authenticated batch mutation paths, per-entry lifecycle delegation, and new D1 evidence; public API behavior is still deferred but server-side effects now run on accepted batch requests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Phase 9.2** adds server-side batch lifecycle execution behind the existing protected `POST /api/batch` gate: a new **`BatchLifecycleCoordinator`** resolves each ID’s binding and scope on the server, runs the three allowed actions sequentially via **`EntryService.completeEntry`** (no duplicated Paste/lifecycle logic), and records per-item outcomes with deterministic item request IDs.
> 
> **Durable evidence** lands in additive migration **`0006_batch_operations.sql`** and **`BindingStore`** helpers (`reserveBatch`, `recordBatchItem`, `reconcileBatch`). Partial runs fail closed per ID with sanitized **`ENTRY_UNAVAILABLE`**, keep earlier successes, and mark batches **`reconciliation_required`** when lifecycle is uncertain or item evidence cannot be persisted (**`BATCH_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`**).
> 
> The worker dispatch seam now runs the coordinator but still returns **`202`** with **`BATCH_RESULT_PENDING`**—public batch results and idempotent replay stay in Phase 9.3. Tests cover delegation, partial failure, reconciliation, and D1 evidence; planning and Phase 6 docs note migration **0006**.

author: mauriciobenjamin700
body:
Tem Script? | Novas Env Vars
-- | --
Não | Não

> :warning: **NOTA**
> - **Opt-in puro.** Sem `session.unitOfWork()`, nada muda: linha continua sendo objeto simples escrito quando você pede.
> - Última issue do ciclo #24–#51. Depois deste merge, o release sai numa versão só.

## Problema

Registrado no `ROADMAP.md` como fase 13. Sem identity map, carregar a mesma linha duas
vezes na mesma sessão devolve **dois objetos** que podem divergir em memória enquanto os
dois se acham "a linha". E `activeRecord.save()` escreve na hora: dez objetos, dez round
trips.

A issue também avisava do risco: entregar isso sem que "rastreado × solto" apareça no
tipo trocaria um problema por outro.

## Solução

```ts
const uow = session.unitOfWork();
const ana = await uow.get(User, 1);
const mesma = await uow.get(User, 1);   // mesma instância, sem segunda query
ana.visits += 1;
uow.add(Post, { id: 10, userId: 1, title: "novo" });
await uow.flush();                       // uma transação
```

### `Tracked<Row>` no tipo

`get()` devolve `Tracked<Row>`. Uma função que exige `Tracked<Row>` **não** aceita um
objeto vindo do repository — coberto no `.test-d.ts`. É a resposta ao risco que a própria
issue levantou.

### Diff por valor

Só as colunas que mudaram entram no `UPDATE`; nada mudou ⇒ nenhum statement. `Date` e
`Uint8Array` comparados por **conteúdo**: por referência, toda linha com data seria
reescrita a cada flush.

### Ordem e atomicidade

Inserts → updates → deletes, numa transação. É a ordem que mantém FK satisfeita quando um
pai novo e seus filhos vão juntos — **não** é ordenação topológica, e isso está num
`!!! warning`. Falha no meio derruba o conjunto e **preserva** o estado rastreado, para
corrigir e reflushar.

## Screenshots

**Descrição do Screenshot**:
Não se aplica — mudança de biblioteca/backend, sem UI.

## Outras mudanças

- `tests/unit-of-work.test.ts` (9) — identidade com **uma** query só, update só do que
  mudou (e nenhum quando nada mudou), lote com um `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` verificado pelo
  `onQuery`, insert antes do update, delete e o "adicionou e removeu vira nada", rollback
  do flush inteiro com o estado preservado, `Date` igual não sendo mudança, `track()`
  mantendo identidade, e `clear()`.
- `tests/unit-of-work.test-d.ts` (3) — forma do `Tracked<Row>`, aceitação onde é exigido e
  o retorno de `get()`.
- Receita nova `unit-of-work` nas duas línguas, nos dois blocos de nav e nos dois índices;
  linha nova na referência.

## Notas sobre deploy

Sem passo de deploy; sem publicação no npm neste PR — o release do ciclo sai depois, numa
versão só.

**Validação local executada**:
- `npm run lint` — limpo, 129 arquivos.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — sem erro.
- `npm test` — 596 passaram, 69 pulados, 67 arquivos.
- `mkdocs build --strict` — limpo, `pt` e `en`.

**Novas Variáveis de Ambiente**:
- Nenhuma

**Novos Scripts e/ou Tarefas de Background**:
- Nenhum

**Novas Dependências**:
- Nenhuma

Closes #51

author: lestherll
body:
Removes the two temporary steps added while chasing the registration failure:

- **`DEBUG tailnet path`** (added in #15, extended in #16) — served its purpose.
- **`Prefer IPv4 to the tailnet`** (#16) — based on a wrong reading. The first debug run happened to fail over IPv6, which looked like an address-family problem. A later run probing each family separately showed IPv4 failing identically:

  ```
  family=-4      http=000 ip=100.79.20.20  FAILED
  family=default http=000 ip=100.79.20.20  FAILED
  ```

  So forcing IPv4 fixed nothing and the step was noise.

Keeps one real correction: the apiserver is on the LAN, not on a libvirt network reachable only from the homelab host. That stopped being true at the fleet migration.

## Registration is still broken, and not from this repo

For the record, since this PR removes the evidence-gathering:

- The runner cannot reach the apiserver's tailnet service VIP (`100.79.20.20:443`) on either address family.
- That same VIP answers `401` on both families from an ordinary tailnet device.
- The proxy **device** (`100.111.226.67:443`) serves nothing — connection refused — so reaching the apiserver depends entirely on the *service* grant, not on any device grant.
- In the homelab repo's `policy.hujson`, the `autogroup:member` → `svc:kube-apiserver-metal` grant works, while the `tag:ci` → `svc:kube-apiserver-metal` grant, identical but for its `src`, does not.

Also ruled out: the `HOMELAB_APISERVER` secret (updated; a stale hostname fails in DNS, not TLS), a stale control-plane policy (re-applied via lestherll/homelab#100; `control`, `local` and `cache` hashes now agree and the behaviour is unchanged), the proxy's health, and a propagation race.

Next step is on the tailnet side — confirming what `tag:ci` actually resolves to and what the live grant permits it.

author: michalik-maciej
body:
## Co się zmieniło

`packages/apps/api/src/routes/offers.routes.ts` nie stosował `requireAuth` na żadnej ze swoich sześciu tras, a `app.ts` montował ten router bez middleware. Listowanie, odczyt, tworzenie, edycja i kasowanie ofert były publiczne dla każdego, kto zna adres API. Trasy inwentarza były chronione od początku, więc odstępstwo dotyczyło wyłącznie ofert.

CORS z `origin: WEBAPP_DOMAIN` tego nie zasłaniał: ogranicza przeglądarki, a nie zwykłe żądania HTTP.

## Zmiana

- `requireAuth` na wszystkich sześciu trasach ofert, łącznie z `POST /preview`
- nowy `packages/apps/api/src/tests/offerRoutesAuth.test.ts`: każda z sześciu tras odrzuca żądanie bez ciasteczka z kodem 401, a podrobiony token dostaje 401 z `Invalid token`
- `calculateOffer.test.ts`: trzy istniejące testy dostały podpisane ciasteczko, bo endpoint podglądu też jest teraz chroniony

## Weryfikacja

- `pnpm validate` i `pnpm vitest run` (35 testów w 17 plikach) przechodzą
- przeklikane lokalnie w przeglądarce na bazie dev, z zalogowanym użytkownikiem: lista ofert 200, odczyt oferty 200, utworzenie 201, autozapis 200, usunięcie 204, a zmiana rabatu przeliczyła kwotę poprawnie
- bez ciasteczka, z `curl`: `/api/offers` i `/api/offers/preview` odpowiadają 401, `/api/health` nadal 200

## Uwaga na przyszłość

`POST /api/offers/preview` nie ma dziś żadnego konsumenta na froncie: `offerQueries.preview` jest zdefiniowane w `offer.api.ts`, ale nic go nie wywołuje. Endpoint jest chroniony i przetestowany, ale przy nowym UI warto zdecydować, czy wraca do użycia, czy znika.

body:
A subagent tried to build a product page using only the READMEs, the way an
outside adopter would. It got there, but only by guessing at things the docs
never said, and this fixes what it hit. The root README now has a Getting
started section with the whole sequence — payload in, rendered block out — and
it uses no provider, so the first thing anyone runs costs nothing and needs no
key. That example is a real test: `tests/quickstart.test.tsx` runs it and
asserts what it renders, and `tests/readme-quickstart.test.ts` fails if the
README and the test ever drift apart. Writing it that way immediately caught a
bug in my own first draft, which ran under vitest but did not typecheck because
`RudraComponent` wants parsed products and I had passed raw objects. Four
smaller corrections come with it: the install line said `zod` where the peer
range is `^4.5.4`, so a shop on zod 3 got `ERESOLVE` from the documented
command; running with no provider — the free path — was described only in the
shipped `.d.ts` where nobody reading on npm would see it; nothing said the
deterministic component emits exactly one grid block, so bundles never appear

author: sqave
body:
Reconnecting an account that is already connected appended a second row instead of overwriting the one that was there. A workspace was left holding two rows for one mailbox, both granted to the same profile, one of them carrying a password nobody had re-entered.

## Why it happened

`settleIdentity` matches the account across a vendor's providers, and that part is deliberate — iCloud is three services on one Apple Account sharing one app-specific password, so matching across them is what gives all three one id and therefore one credential ref.

It asked as a single `.find()`, so it returned whichever row carried the account first in the file:

```
con3  icloud_calendar   ada@example.com
con5  icloud_mail       ada@example.com   ← the row being reconnected
```

Reconnecting the mailbox settled on `con3`, the calendar's id. `declareConnection` writes by `<provider>.<id>`, looked for `icloud_mail.con3`, found nothing under it, and took the append branch — leaving `icloud_mail.con5` stale beside a new `icloud_mail.con3`.

So the id chooser and the writer were keyed differently and nothing held them together.

## What changed

- **This provider's own row wins the match; a sibling's id is the fallback.** Both steps are needed and they answer different questions — the second is what makes a family share one credential, the first is what stops it answering for a provider that already has a row. The label lookup had the identical ordering flaw and could offer the calendar's name for the mailbox.
- **The same duplicate had a second route in.** A provider that authenticates to nothing takes its own name as its account, so every connect resolves the same string, and that branch allocated an id regardless: `connect example` twice gave `lan8` and `lan9` for one surface. It now lands on the row it has.
- **The rule is one exported function**, `connectionForAccount`, rather than a comparison at each call site — two comparisons that could disagree is what the bug was. It trims as well as lower-casing, because nothing normalises an account on the way in and a row with a stray space matched nothing.
- **`doctor` reports a pair that already exists**, with no `fix` command on purpose: which row to keep is not in the file — it is whichever still holds a working credential — so a suggested `disconnect` would name the wrong one about half the time, and `--fix` would run it.

Refusing a duplicate at load was the obvious alternative and is wrong: `assertConnectionsUnique` runs on every read and on every `ConfigDocument.open`, so making this an error would take a workspace that already holds a pair off the air, and refuse `disconnect` the very file that fixes it. Two rows at one `<provider>.<id>` are unresolvable and still throw; two rows for one account both work, and one is merely stale.

No migration: an existing pair is reported by `doctor` and removed with `disconnect`.

## Verification

`bun test` and `bun run typecheck` both pass locally. Two failures — `emitted.test.ts` and `operate.test.ts`, both the `token`/`outputs` tests timing out at 5s — are present on `develop` before this branch and are unrelated.

The four new `settle.test.ts` cases were checked against the unfixed file and all four fail there:

```
(fail) lands on its own row rather than a sibling that shares the account
(fail) recognises the account through case and surrounding space
(fail) offers its own label, not the one a sibling sharing the id carries
(fail) lands on the row it already has rather than a second one
```

The two that assert preserved behaviour — adopting a sibling id where this provider has no row, and taking a fresh owner id the first time — pass on both.

End to end against a scratch workspace: three `connect example` runs now leave one row and one grant, where the first two used to leave two of each; and `doctor` on a planted pair reports

```
warn  example.con1 and example.con2 are one account declared twice (ada@example.com) —
      remove whichever no longer holds a working credential with "lanes link disconnect <ref>"
```

matching through both the case difference and a trailing space.

author: james9120
body:
## Player requests
Replace the thumb-controlled aim cursor with natural automatic anchor selection, keep the left stick exclusively for character steering/power, add direct screen taps for specific attachment points, and add wall-running near facades.

## Movement and automatic web selection
- Left/right steers and banks the character; up still powers the swing and reel. Stick movement no longer instantly selects a building side or changes an anchor's height.
- Auto selection follows momentum and a smoothed intended curve. It ranks actual facade candidates for forward progress, reach, height, street clearance, and recent-anchor repetition.
- The best candidates receive a bounded 0.9-second ballistic/rope look-ahead, rejecting predicted ground/wall paths. Cached-target hysteresis reduces needless target switching. Actual catches revalidate reach and line of sight.
- Removed the persistent cyan aiming cursor/dotted preview. Only a brief tap confirmation and the active web marker remain.
- Corrected an automatic-swing stall/reversal found during the long neutral-hold route. Releasing at safe height can now allow the next catch to become available rather than hanging on until the body reverses.

## Tap to swing
- Canvas touch/click raycasts through the exact last-rendered camera using CSS pixels, independent of render scale and portrait/landscape orientation.
- A reachable visible facade/roof point fires one targeted swing at that exact surface point. It is not replaced by auto aim mid-arc. Holding WEB resumes automatic chaining after that arc; a tap by itself does not latch automatic mode.
- Validate before releasing the old rope: sky, obstructed, unloaded, and out-of-range taps leave the existing rope intact.
- Separate scene-pointer ownership supports aiming a tap while steering/holding WEB. Scene drags and canceled/long-held touches do not shoot. HUD/control touches do not count as scene taps.
- Long tapped lines preserve their actual length at attachment instead of snapping to the old 100m limit. When needed, finite stamina-powered take-up shortens the line progressively; attachment and release do not teleport the character or directly boost velocity.
- Pause/resume preserves whether WEB was actually held, rather than silently converting a tap-only swing into permanent auto-chain.

## Wall running
- A sufficiently fast, glancing/parallel near-facade pass transitions into a wall run. Stationary motion, sky/rooftop gaps, ground-level contact, and the tested direct head-on collision do not.
- Running preserves along-wall motion, uses bounded adhesion/support forces and stamina, and ends at the facade edge, low stamina, or the time limit. Up-stick adds climb/power.
- Steer away or press WEB/TRICK/ZIP to leave; tapping another valid building switches directly from wall run to the selected swing with position and velocity preserved.
- A re-entry cooldown prevents immediate sticky recapture. Wall state and camera/feedback coordinates remain correct through floating-origin rebasing.
- Blended wall-run torso, arm and leg targets retain fixed bone lengths and the five-digit hands. Camera clearance offsets outward near the facade.
- Ground contact still ends the run; no invisible anchors/walls or ground bounce.

## Validation — full browser pass complete
**148/148 checks passed: 74 Chromium, 74 WebKit.**
Validated run: https://github.com/james9120/arcade/actions/runs/33995469483
Artifact: `web-swing-natural-traversal-final`
Exact tested and committed runtime blob: `3862c98bcab5f1c868f87d3ace06a645893b18a5`.
The artifact contains the standalone HTML, exact test sources, JSON results, metadata, and 34 screenshots, including six wall-motion samples.

The existing physics, city, animation, layout and long-route regressions remain. Only two obsolete direct-stick targeting expectations were removed; the new suite replaces them with movement-only input expectations and covers auto predictions, exact tap ownership, invalid-tap preservation, pause/resume, long-line continuity, wall entry/exits, head-on collision, stamina, animation and rebasing. Actual browser-dispatched touch taps pass in both engines; simultaneous three-pointer behavior is covered by synthetic PointerEvents. WebKit's fractional touch-coordinate quantization is accounted for by asserting against the actual delivered PointerEvent ray, not the requested fractional location.

Each browser completed the 180-second WEB-only route with collisions active: **6,875.08 game metres, 148 catches, minimum centre height 17.36m**. Sustained-power, pulsed-power, alternating-steer and queued-trick routes also passed. A 127.18m tapped line completed a 2.25-second arc without an instantaneous snap, and a separate ten-second WEB-held route resumed automatic catches after that long tap. These are deterministic regressions, not a guarantee of unlimited survival or a human rating of game feel.

The rendered tap and wall-run scenes were inspected. Review led to correcting long-line clamping and replacing the excessively horizontal wall pose with a more upright, wall-directed foot placement. Local mocked-API checks were used for iteration, not as render evidence.

## Scope
Final diff is only:
- games/web-swing/index.html
- tests/web_swing_browser.py
- tests/web_swing_flow_checks.js
- tests/web_swing_natural_checks.js

All temporary builders/workflows were removed after testing. Existing Pages deployment, persistent workflow permissions, homepage, city assets and other arcade games are unchanged. Runtime remains a self-contained HTML file with no external assets or requests.

The live game is unchanged until merged. This is not physical-iPhone performance validation or a claim of AAA/defect-free production quality. Normal PR regression CI is being checked before marking ready.

author: daniziller
body:
## O que muda

Completa o quadro 22 com o 4º formato do mockup: **"Para o grupo"** (22d) —
o moderador monta um plano de leitura de livro e envia pro grupo; cada
membro recebe como convite e decide se aceita (nunca troca a leitura de
ninguém sem avisar, ver README "Duas regras de produto").

⚠️ **Requer rodar `supabase/migrations/0048_group_reading_plans.sql`** no
SQL Editor do Supabase antes do envio/aceite funcionarem de verdade (a UI
já está protegida contra a RPC não existir — ver seção de verificação).

## Como funciona

- **22a**: "Para o grupo" só aparece pra quem modera algum grupo; ao
  escolher, pula direto pro seletor de livro (não tem "assunto" livre pra
  pedir — só o exemplo do mockup, formato Livro, existe pra grupo).
- **22d — Plano do grupo**: revisar antes de enviar — semanas do livro,
  pergunta da 1ª semana já sugerida por IA (editável), "quem publica"/
  "substitui a leitura" informativos, "Enviar para o grupo".
- **Aceitar/recusar**: banner em Comunidade, mesmo padrão visual do
  convite de membro. Aceitar troca a leitura de hoje pro plano do grupo
  (mesmo mecanismo de plano por tema/cronológico ativo).
- **19c**: linha "Plano do grupo" nova (gap do README §15, "Adição
  necessária") — criar um, ou ver quantos já aceitaram.

## Decisão de design (Regra Zero)

**1 semana = 1 capítulo, sempre.** A sala de discussão do grupo (17a) é
por UM capítulo só (chave `group_id + book + chapter`) — uma semana
cobrindo mais de um capítulo não teria uma sala única e correta. O mockup
mostra 3 "leituras curtas" por semana (Seg/Qua/Sex, faixas de versículo)
— dividir um capítulo em faixas de versículo exigiria contagem de
palavras POR VERSÍCULO, que o cliente não tem (só por capítulo). Em vez
de fingir uma divisão por posição, cada semana é o capítulo inteiro.

A pergunta da semana só é sugerida por IA pra 1ª semana — gerar de
antemão pra um livro grande (Gênesis = 50 semanas) custaria uma chamada
de IA por capítulo à toa. As semanas seguintes usam o fluxo que já existe
(editar a pergunta em ChapterRoomScreen.jsx via GroupAdminScreen.jsx)
quando a vez delas chegar.

## Verificação

- ✅ `npm run build` limpo
- ✅ Paridade de chaves pt/en: 1727/1727, zero diferença
- ✅ Auditoria de chaves usadas: todas resolvem em pt e en
- ✅ Testado no navegador (simulando um grupo moderado, já que testar de
  verdade precisa da migração rodada): formato "Para o grupo" aparece
  corretamente só pra quem modera; livro de 1 capítulo (Judas) e de vários
  capítulos (Filipenses) geram as semanas certas; "Enviar para o grupo"
  contra o backend AINDA SEM a migração falha com mensagem amigável, sem
  quebrar a tela — confirma que o tratamento de erro está certo antes
  mesmo da migração existir
