author: effortlesssteven
body:
## What this changes

Promotes the accepted temporal-tolerance semantics from EffortlessMetrics/hl7v2-rs-swarm#146 into canonical source and reconciles them with the syntax already shipped in the repository.

- makes `TemporalRule.tolerance` operational instead of silently ignored;
- accepts a non-negative ASCII integer followed by `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, or `y`;
- treats seconds, minutes, hours, and days as exact elapsed durations;
- treats `y` as calendar years, preserving month/day/time and clamping February 29 to February 28 in a non-leap target year;
- treats reverse deltas through the configured boundary as compliant;
- gives malformed values no runtime widening and reports the configuration error through profile lint;
- uses checked calendar arithmetic and clamps unrepresentable upper bounds to the maximum supported instant.

## Proof

The source-only repair completed on Rust 1.95:

```text
cargo test -p hl7v2 --lib conformance::profile   # 80 passed
cargo check -p hl7v2 --all-targets --all-features
cargo clippy -p hl7v2 --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

Coverage includes fixed units, the shipped `1y` and `150y` forms, leap-day handling, inclusive boundaries, insufficient tolerance, overflow behavior, malformed and multibyte suffixes, and a lint pass over both repository profiles that contain temporal tolerances.

## Claim boundary

This does not change temporal-rule serialization or timestamp parsing. An absent or malformed tolerance is equivalent to zero widening during message validation; malformed configured values remain separately visible as `invalid_temporal_tolerance` lint errors.

Origin: semantic promotion of swarm PR #146 under source reconciliation #977.

Refs #977 and EffortlessMetrics/hl7v2-rs-swarm#146.

author: arul28
body:
## Problem The model handoff chip appeared on every model change, so a switch from Claude Opus 5 to Claude Fable 5.1 drew a "Claude → Claude" chip. On iOS the chip was a plain text row instead of the desktop logo → arrow → logo divider. The iOS chat-info and PR badges took a fixed 44pt of thread height. On the iOS new-chat screen the composer squeezed the header into a tiny scroll area, the lane picker popover clipped, and its text was 10 to 11pt. ## Cause The handoff condition compared model ids as well as providers. The badge row was a child of the composer stack. The new-chat header ScrollView had no layout priority and the lane menu was a UIKit popover anchored inside it. ## Change and boundary - Desktop emits `model_handoff` only when the top-level provider group changes. Aggregators such as OpenCode, Cursor, and Droid collapse to one group, so vendor swaps inside them do not emit. The broader `modelChanged` flag still drives runtime teardown and title re-adoption. - Desktop renderer and the TUI skip a same-provider handoff row from older transcripts. No history migration. - iOS renders the handoff as a logo → HANDOFF → arrow → logo divider via `AgentChatNoticeKind.modelHandoff`. - iOS chat-info and PR badges float over the transcript with a tail reserve and a small scrim. The jump-to-latest pill stacks above them. - iOS new-chat: the lane picker is pinned, the header collapses in tiers from measured height with hysteresis, the usage carousel stays mounted while collapsed, and the lane menu is a sheet with 16pt rows and 44pt tap targets. Composer focus is restored after the sheet dismisses. - No shared type, IPC, sync schema, or SDK surface changed. ## Verification - Desktop vitest: `agentChatService.test.ts` and `AgentChatMessageList.test.tsx`, 1237 passed. Desktop typecheck clean. - ADE CLI: `format.test.ts` 72 passed. CLI typecheck clean. - iOS: build-for-testing clean on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator. Handoff, header tier, and card expansion tests, 34 passed. - Quality: two review passes, 13 findings fixed, gate empty. Post-rebase merge-region review clean. Authored with Claude Fable 5.1 via ADE Work chat.

  Open in ADE  ·  ade/mobile-thread-and-composer-overlays branch  ·  PR #1228

## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Same-provider model changes no longer display unnecessary handoff notices across desktop, CLI, and iOS. - Cross-provider handoffs now display consistently with provider details and accessibility support. - **User Interface** - iOS chat badges now float over the transcript while preserving message visibility. - Lane selection opens in a resizable, keyboard-aware sheet with improved controls. - New-chat headers progressively collapse based on available space while keeping lane selection accessible. - **Tests** - Added coverage for handoff filtering, replayed events, responsive header behavior, and lane-picker presentation.

body:
:robot: I have created a release *beep* *boop*
---

## [25.11.0](https://github.com/sava-software/sava/compare/25.10.0...25.11.0) (2026-09-06)

### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* Remove deprecated APIs for string signatures, one-shot HMAC-SHA512, Token-2022 extension maps and type enums, Base58 RPC requests, and the fixed transaction-size constant. Affected applications require source changes and recompilation; see the [migration guide](https://github.com/sava-software/sava/blob/main/MIGRATION.md) for replacements.

### Features

* **Transactions:** Build, parse, and sign SIMD-0385 v1 transactions. `TxBuilder` supports instruction editing, strict validation, priority fees, compute limits, heap size, and loaded-account data limits, including conversion from legacy compute-unit pricing. Legacy and v0 transaction support remains available; sending v1 transactions requires activation on the target cluster.
* **Signing:** Use `signInOrder` for positional signing or `signByKey` to match signers by public key, with corresponding Base64 conveniences.
* **RPC:** `getTransaction` and `getBlock` requests with full transaction details now allow v1 transactions. Use `BlockTx.skeleton()` to parse transaction bytes returned by `getBlock` into a `TransactionSkeleton`.

### Deprecations

* The positional `SequencedCollection<Signer>` overloads of `sign` and `signAndBase64Encode` are deprecated for removal. Use `signInOrder` and its conveniences to preserve the existing behavior; use `signByKey` when key matching is intended.

### Bug Fixes

* **Key import:** Import keys from JSON with fields in any order and ignore extra fields, including nested objects and arrays. Nested fields cannot supply or override the imported key, and missing-field errors now name the required field.
* **Instructions:** Equal instructions with valid data spans now have equal hash codes, allowing interchangeable use as `HashMap` keys and `HashSet` entries even with different backing arrays or offsets. Keep retained data and account inputs unchanged while an instruction is stored in a hash-based collection.

body:
Second race in the checks watch, same family as build-kit#10. There the fresh pull request had no checks yet; here a follow-up push (the `--finish` path after a review round) is watched while the request's rollup still shows the previous commit's runs. Seen on open-science-pillars/archive-observatory#17: the first commit lacked the verdict file by design, the second carried it and was green, and `--finish` read the first commit's red and stopped. Nothing merged wrongly; a second `--finish` a minute later merged the green head.

Fix: before `gh pr checks --watch`, wait until `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<local HEAD>/check-runs` reports at least one run, every ten seconds up to the same three-minute limit the fresh-PR retry uses. A repository without workflows skips the wait as before.

`bash -n` clean; the API call was tried by hand on a real head (2 runs) and on a missing sha (falls to 0 and keeps waiting).

author: rigel-mintaka
body:
Re-point jj-gt's release pipeline from its in-repo `Formula/` to the consolidated tap `mattwilkinsonn/homebrew-tap`, make `publish-release` idempotent, and fail-close the bump script. Part of the distribution-continuity plan (mattwilkinsonn/zireael#313), task T3.

## Idempotent publish-release

The v0.3.11 run failed at `gh release create` because the Release already existed (from the manual asset mirror), and that hard failure cascaded skips into `bump-tap` and `publish-crates`. Split the create into check-then-create (`gh release view … || gh release create …`, assets dropped from the create) plus a separate always-run `gh release upload … --clobber` step, so a first run and a `workflow_dispatch` re-run converge on the same asset set instead of failing on a pre-existing Release.

## Tap re-point (three coordinated changes)

A naive single-checkout re-point ships a green run that pushes nothing, so all three land together:

- Token scope: the `create-github-app-token@v2` step gains `owner: mattwilkinsonn` and a `repositories:` block listing BOTH `jj-gt` and `homebrew-tap`. `repositories:` replaces the current-repo default rather than extending it, so self must be listed or the self checkout that reuses the token fails to auth.
- Dual checkout: keep the self checkout (it supplies `.github/scripts/bump-formulae.py`) and add a second `actions/checkout` for `mattwilkinsonn/homebrew-tap` at `path: tap` with `fetch-depth: 0` (the retained fetch+rebase guard rebases onto origin/main and fails across a depth-1 shallow boundary). The rewrite runs with `working-directory: tap` invoking the script by its workspace-root path so its CWD-relative `Path("Formula")` resolves to the tap's `Formula/`; Commit+push runs with `working-directory: tap` so `origin` is the tap remote. A required fail-closed pre-bump guard verifies `tap/Formula/jj-gt.rb` exists and is not disabled before the rewrite — otherwise a missing/disabled formula yields a green bump-tap that shipped nothing (the script skips a missing formula and returns 0, and Commit+push's own `git diff --quiet` then reports nothing to bump).
- validate-tap: taps and installs `mattwilkinsonn/tap/jj-gt` instead of the per-repo tap.

## Fail-close the bump script

jj-gt's `bump-formulae.py` warned and continued on a missing sha, which would rewrite a partial-sha formula into the shared tap — a checksum-mismatch install failure for every user of that tool. Aligned it to jj-hooks' fail-closed form: collect the missing slugs and `return 1` before any write. Verified: a partial-sha invocation aborts with the formula left untouched; a full-sha invocation bumps as before.

The existing fetch+rebase guard is left as-is (the bounded retry-loop is a marked follow-up; the T6 tag serialization handles the cross-repo shared-tap race). No crate version bump here (that is T5).

Refs mattwilkinsonn/zireael#316, mattwilkinsonn/zireael#312.

Co-authored-by: Matt Wilkinson <mattwilki17@gmail.com>

author: josh-temple
body:
## Summary

Adds a Japanese-language mirror of the current public Studio Lab site while keeping all existing English URLs unchanged.

### Adds
- `/ja/` Japanese home
- Japanese Research, Trading, Projects, Writing, Methods, and About pages
- Japanese versions of both currently published research pages
- page-level English / 日本語 switching in the shared header
- localized research metadata labels
- `canonical` and `hreflang` alternate links for English/Japanese page pairs

### URL policy
English remains at the current paths (`/research/`, `/trading/`, etc.). Japanese mirrors the same structure under `/ja/` (`/ja/research/`, `/ja/trading/`, etc.). No existing public URL is moved or replaced.

### Translation policy
The Japanese pages are intended to preserve the same claim strength and evidence boundary as the English originals. In particular:
- an unrun comparison is not translated as a null result;
- mixed/inconclusive trading evidence is not presented as a profitable edge;
- risk reduction and profit improvement remain separate claims;
- private operational state and live trading information remain outside the public site.

### Review focus
Please review naturalness of the Japanese, especially research-status wording, and confirm that the Japanese versions do not strengthen or weaken the public claims relative to English.

author: kaidosgh
body:
Release notes — v0.2.0

Security
- Request bodies are capped on streamed bytes — chunked transfer can no longer bypass the limit; oversized requests get 413 behind every bundled reverse-proxy setup, including the Cloudflare Tunnel example
- The documented 100 KB secret limit is now enforced server-side (API ciphertext capped at 136,556 base64url chars; the browser UI was always capped)
- Full-history secret scanning in CI as a backstop for the local pre-commit hook
- Language cookie is now Secure

Added
- Configurable abuse-reporting limits: RATE_LIMIT_ABUSE_REPORTS_PER_HOUR (default 10/h) and RATE_LIMIT_ABUSE_ADMIN_PER_MINUTE (default 30/min) — large bulk deletes no longer silently lose calls to the fixed operator limit

Changed
- Hosting hardening: Docker log rotation (3 × 10 MB) for app and db, 512 MB memory limit on the app container; the nginx example documents error_log IP retention; the privacy template names CDN/tunnel providers as recipients
- Imprint footer label is per-locale ("Imprint" in English, "Impressum" in German)
- Reduced motion keeps opacity-only fades (gentler, not zero); spinner 1s → 600ms
- Background effect: ~30 fps cap, opaque WebGL context, low-power GPU preference, context-loss recovery — roughly half the GPU/battery cost with no visible change

UI
- Loading skeletons for client navigation (card-shaped on /create, landing-shaped at the root); the abuse queue no longer flashes the unlock form when a saved key auto-loads; dark first paint on new tabs and hard refreshes

author: scottlz0310-user
body:
## 概要

Play Console を実際に確認した結果、`README.md` の「リリース署名」セクションに**事実と異なる記述**があることが判明したため訂正します。

## 判明した実態

Play Console（Scottlz0310 / 組織アカウント）を確認したところ、以下が確定しました。

| 項目 | 実態 |
|---|---|
| アプリ | **登録済み**（ひらがな並べ替えクイズ / `io.github.scottlz0310.anagramanalyzer` / 未公開 / インストール数 0） |
| Play アプリ署名 | **有効**（「リリースは Google Play で署名済み」） |
| アプリ署名鍵 | **Google が保有**。量子対応ハイブリッド署名（従来の鍵 + ポスト量子暗号鍵） |
| デベロッパー確認要件 | **充足済み**（「すべてのアプリの登録が完了し、Android デベロッパーの確認要件を満たしています」） |
| アップロード鍵 | **未確定**。初回 App Bundle アップロード時に、その署名鍵が登録される |

Android デベロッパーの確認ページに並んでいた3件のフィンガープリントは、この Google 保有のハイブリッド鍵群のものでした。アプリの署名ページの Digital Asset Links JSON に含まれる `F0:82:08:...` が1件目と一致することで裏付けられます。

**自前証明書を「鍵の追加」で登録する必要はありません。**

## 訂正内容

### 削除した誤った記述

> 署名鍵を失うと、Google Play の Developer Verification に登録済みのパッケージ名の更新権を失います（新しい鍵で同じパッケージ名を再登録することはできません）

**アップロード鍵は Play Console から再発行でき、アプリが利用できなくなることはありません。** アプリ署名鍵は Google が保護しているため、開発者側の鍵の紛失が Play 配信を止めることもありません。この記述は自己署名で配布し続ける場合を前提としたもので、実態に当てはまりませんでした。

### 改訂内容

- **2つの署名経路を区別する構成へ全面改訂** — GitHub Releases 用（自前 keystore）と Play 配信用（Google のアプリ署名鍵）
- 自前 keystore の位置づけを明記（GitHub Releases 用の署名 + 将来のアップロード鍵）
- アップロード鍵の証明書は初回 App Bundle アップロード時に確定する旨を追記
- 「鍵を失った場合」を実態に即した内容へ差し替え。GitHub Releases 経路では依然としてバックアップが必要（署名の異なる APK へは更新できないため）である点は残しています

## 変更ファイル

- `README.md` — 「リリース署名」セクション
- `CHANGELOG.md` / `tasks.md` — 追随。フェーズ18を完了扱いに更新

鍵本体・パスワードはリポジトリ外で管理するため、本 PR には含まれません。リポジトリ外の保管先 `README.md` にも同じ訂正を適用済みです（Play Console の確認経路、新規／既存パッケージ名の違い、Digital Asset Links JSON を追記）。

## 検証

- コード変更なし（ドキュメントのみ）
- 差分に秘密情報が混入していないことを確認

author: bobberb
body:
Groundwork for macOS support (`uhexen2-aoqd`), plus the two verification harnesses that make the rest of it safe to attempt.

**Nothing here changes what the renderer draws.** Every commit is gated on a screenshot or a numeric baseline, and both are unchanged throughout.

## Why the route changed

macOS cannot run this renderer natively. Apple's OpenGL stops at 4.1 Core and its compatibility profile at 2.1, while `gl_vidsdl.c` requests **4.3 compatibility** and the engine dispatches compute and binds SSBOs throughout. That is not a slow path on macOS — the context cannot be created at all.

The scoped plan was ANGLE (GLES 3.0 → Metal). That works, but it permanently caps macOS at the browser build's feature level: ES 3.0 has no compute and no SSBOs, so `gl_worldcull.c`, `gl_lightcluster.c` and `gl_rmain.c`'s `R_SkeletalProgram` all compile out — no GPU culling, no clustered lighting, no GPU skinning.

So the target is now the second backend on **SDL_GPU** (`uhexen2-p4ln`), which reaches native Metal on macOS with no MoltenVK layer, no 64-bit-atomic caveat, and no bundled runtime. ANGLE remains the interim path so macOS runs *something* meanwhile.

## The thing worth knowing before reviewing

**Most of `p4ln` was already built once and reverted, and the revert is invisible to `git log`.** `d49e348a5` (uniform blocks), `e2f3182ec` (texture slot ranges), `334838e3c` (shaders to files) and `7a29dd3b1` (SPIR-V) were all reverted in **`3b98a4d4f`**, whose subject is *"chase: add bindable +chase / -chase / togglechase and a Key Setup row"* — the squash kept the first commit's subject, so ~37 lines of `chase.c` sit in the same commit that deletes `gl_uniforms.c`, `gl_texbind.c`, `EmbedShaders.cmake` and `CompileSpirv.cmake`.

Root-caused by bisect to `d49e348a5` alone; the shader work was collateral. And from that commit's own message, the reason it got that far:

> Behaviour is unverified on screen — no visual regression sweep has been run.

This branch recovers those patterns rather than reinventing them, and builds the missing sweep first.

## What is proven

Two deliberately tiny vertical slices, because the blocker is not the string literals — Vulkan GLSL forbids loose (non-opaque) uniforms outright, so *every* shader needs its uniforms in a block before it can become SPIR-V at all.

- **`hiz_copy`** (12 lines, compute) — touches all three SDL_GPU compute descriptor sets at once.
- **`s2d` + `sflat`** (graphics) — the graphics sets are numbered differently (vertex 0/1, fragment 2/3), and this is the first thing to compile on the **ES tier**, which is what the browser and macOS/ANGLE builds actually run.

Then the real change: **two shared std140 blocks**, `VertParams` (352 B, set 1) and `FragParams` (128 B, set 3), filled from a CPU shadow and pushed once per dirty block per draw. Split by stage rather than by frequency because SDL_GPU's stage separation is a hard API constraint while `PerFrame`/`PerDraw` is only an optimization.

The defect that caused the revert is **designed out, not patched**: it was call sites setting an alpha threshold without the matching force-opaque flag — harmless for per-program loose uniforms, a cross-draw leak for global block members. `R_SetAlphaMask` now takes both, so half the pair cannot be spelled.

## Bugs found and fixed on the way

- `SDL_GL_LoadLibrary` returns `bool` in SDL3, but `GL_OpenLibrary` tested `ret == -1` — the fallback branch was unreachable and a **failed GL library load reported success**.
- Seven raw `gl*()` call sites bypassed the loader table and linked directly against system GL — fine where GL is directly linked, fatal everywhere it isn't, which is every macOS route.
- The ES tier `#define`d the *real function name* `glPointSize` to a no-op to absorb raw calls; any future caller would have silently compiled to nothing.
- `glGetActiveUniformBlockiv` is a `GL_FUNCTION_OPT` entry point loaded by hand in `gl_vidsdl.c`, so declaring it in `gl_func.h` alone left the block-size check silently skipped.
- Three call sites (`sky stencil`, both `r_showtris`) uploaded the view matrix only under `if (u_mvp >= 0)` and would have quietly stopped once it became a block member.
- `layout.inc` used `#if VULKAN >= 100`; an undefined macro in a preprocessor expression is a **hard error in the ES profile** while desktop GLSL treats it as 0 — so that file could never have compiled on the ES tier.

## The harnesses (`tools/`)

Both were validated by proving they *detect a deliberate change*, not merely that they run.

**`sweep-worldcull.steps`** — the gate is `gl_hiz_stats` numbers, **not** screenshots. Correct occlusion culling is pixel-invisible by design, and a Hi-Z broken into culling nothing is *also* pixel-invisible (mean frame brightness differs by 0.0005). Do not run it on the demo maps: they yield `hiz=0` at every viewpoint, so the sweep passes while observing nothing. Cameras are placed with `setpos`, because a timed turn produced `frust=372/hiz=39` and `frust=382/hiz=34` from the same binary.

**`sweep-2d.steps` + `shot-diff.sh`** — pixel-exact, because this path *is* visible. Two blinking cursors must be masked. The second was found the expensive way, as a 15.78-pixel "regression" in a change that had none: frame 04 is the console, and `console.c:595` blinks the input cursor on `(int)(realtime*con_cursorspeed)&1`. It is a two-state blink, so **agreeing runs prove nothing** — three runs agreed and the fourth did not.

## What is NOT done

- **macOS does not build or run yet.** The CMake arm is correct and the ES tier is proven, but ANGLE is not vendored (`uhexen2-6wj4`), there is no `.app` bundle or notarization (`uhexen2-q7df`), and no darwin entry in the flake.
- **2 of 35 shaders converted.** The remaining ones are declaration swaps now that the machinery exists, but `sworld` is the first that genuinely exercises both blocks.
- **The ES tier is compile-verified only.** Nothing here exercises WebGL2 or ANGLE at runtime, so the permanent-UBO flush is unproven on the tier macOS runs. `scripts/webgl-smoke-test.sh` should join the gate before converting shaders the browser build leans on.
- No macOS hardware exists to test on (`uhexen2-nqy1`). Everything here was verified under llvmpipe, which is deterministic — good for gating, useless for vendor-specific behaviour.

## Verification

Every commit: `nix build .#default` clean, a from-scratch `-DUSE_GLES=ON` build clean, both SPIR-V frontends (`-G` and `-V`) emitting modules with descriptor sets read back via `spirv-dis`, and both sweeps unchanged.

author: navjyotnishant
body:
## What

`orion new PRIOR-3` reads an idea already written down in the tracker and skips the interview, because the questions it would ask have already been answered. `orion new` with no argument now asks for the idea instead of printing a usage error.

## Why

The interview exists because the idea usually is not written down — five questions asked while a person is present, since every later stage runs non-interactively. But a Product Discovery idea with a filled-in PRD has already answered them, and asking again spends the one resource this command spends: the human's attention.

The no-argument change is the same reasoning from the other side. This command's job is to interview, so a missing idea is its first question, not a mistake.

## Three paths

| Invocation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `orion new` | asks for the idea, then the five questions |
| `orion new "some idea"` | echoes it, then the five questions — unchanged |
| `orion new PRIOR-3` | reads the idea, skips the interview |

## The load-bearing check

Every idea in a fresh discovery project carries Jira's unfilled template. Planning from it would produce a confident, empty plan — a stage reading `"Define customer problems, why they're urgent"` as the problem statement will design for it. So a template is refused, by name, and the interview runs instead.

**This broke once and the tests did not catch it.** Jira stores descriptions as ADF and returns them flattened, so headings arrive as bare lines with no `#` markers — indistinguishable from prose by shape. The first implementation counted `Objective / Problem / Solution / Risks / Supporting documents` as five lines of real prose and accepted an untouched template as a written-up idea. It passed its tests only because the fixture was written from memory in markdown. The headings are now named explicitly, and the fixture is the live PRIOR text byte-for-byte, curly apostrophe included.

Verified against the real project:

```
WARNING   PRIOR-3 is not written up yet: its description is still the unfilled template.
  Interviewing instead. Fill the idea in and re-run to skip this.
```

## Design decisions

- **The idea's text is carried verbatim**, not summarised. It is the PM's words about their own product; a later stage designing from a paraphrase would be designing from Orion's reading rather than from what was written.
- **The back-link is a comment, and the idea's status is left alone.** Orion says which project came from the idea; whether that means it should move to Delivery belongs to whoever owns that board.
- **A failed comment does not fail the run.** The project exists by then, and losing the link is untidy where losing the run would not be. It warns and names the idea.
- **No Polaris API.** A discovery project's ideas come back through the ordinary issue API, verified against PRIOR, so this reuses the existing tracker client.
- **`ideaReader` is a two-method interface** (`Search`, `Comment`) rather than the full `Tracker` — it names exactly the two permissions the feature needs.

## Also fixed

`TestNoHandWrittenJQLClauses` caught `fmt.Sprintf("key = %q", …)`: Go quoting is not JQL quoting. Now `tracker.JQLEq`.

## Test plan

- `./scripts/test.sh` — green, 79.5% coverage against a 65% floor
- 15 new tests in `newidea_test.go`, including the real-template refusal, the back-link, the best-effort comment failure, and prose-that-mentions-a-key
- `TestCLIDoesNotDemandATerminalForAnIdeaKey` — the terminal gate is for the interview, not the command
- Real binary against live PRIOR-3: refuses with the reason
- Real binary, no arg, no terminal: refuses rather than hanging

The accept path is covered by unit tests rather than a live run — all five PRIOR ideas are the identical unfilled template, and proving it end-to-end would create a real Jira project.

author: ubugeeei
body: A story runner that is an implementation rather than a contract, and four bugs that made uf answer wrongly — three of them found by writing the tests the roadmap asked for. ## `@uniflowed/story` Forty lines in which every function was `nativeRuntimeRequired(...)` → six Flow modules and no native binding. The thesis is in `index.js`, because a story runner in a toolchain that already has a test runner, a DOM and request mocking has to justify itself: what a story adds is that the state has a **name outside the file that produced it** — `button--pending`, printable by CI, filable as a VRT baseline, carryable in a URL — and that the setup that state needs is declared once beside that name as data. The set carries complete props and a story is a delta, so "every story in this set renders" is true by construction rather than at render time. `withBrowser` is **deleted rather than ported**: `@uniflowed/browser` is still a declaration whose every function throws, and a story claiming to drive a real browser would claim a capability that does not exist. Twenty mutations, twenty killed — and two of them survived the first pass and were findings rather than gaps: a symlink guard that turned out to be dead code, and a fixture that created a directory *through* a `node_modules` symlink and left files in this repository's real one. ## Four wrong answers **One directory nobody could open stopped the whole project.** `walkdir` hands an unopenable directory back as an error *item*; `scan_source_files` propagated it. A single `chmod 000` directory made `uf fmt`, `uf lint`, `uf check` and `uf test` do nothing for everything else — the same failure as #164, one level up, and the `unreadable` mechanism that answers it already existed. **An argument uf could not parse exited 1**, which the reference documents as 2 — so `uf lint --oops` and `uf lint` finding a lint error were the same answer to a script. **`uf test PATH` matching nothing was a green run.** `uf lint`, `uf fmt` and `uf check` all refuse it; `uf test` filtered to zero files and reported success, so `uf test pacakges/ui` was a green CI run over nothing. **`uf test` silently dropped a file whose test names are not literals.** `it(name, …)` in a loop cannot be read by discovery, so the file looked like it held no tests: filtered out before any worker saw it, "0 passed, files 0", exit 0. A file with two failing tests in it was a green run. The unreadable declaration is recorded the way `it.each` already is, and the file is handed to a worker — which imports it and finds whatever registers. ## Tests Twenty-three behind the first three: a five-thousand-file project walked past twenty thousand files it must not open, ignored directories at every depth, a BOM and a truncated code point and valid UTF-16, a symlink cycle that must end the walk rather than hang it, a newline in a filename and a path at `PATH_MAX`, and a file deleted *while* the scan reads it — asserted so it holds whether or not the race is won. `every_command.rs` carries a checklist compared against `uf --help`, so a command added to the parser and not to the table fails. Twenty-four mutations applied to source, all twenty-four caught. ## The reference, corrected where it was wrong `uf use` takes a `uf@` and never took `node`/`bun`/`deno`. Exit code 2 covers one of the three cases it claimed; the other two are 1 today and the table now says so, because every command returns the same error type and telling "could not run" from "ran and found a problem" needs a distinction the command layer does not make yet. ``` ✓ 1069 passed, 0 failed uf test 34 passed cargo test -p uf_project 187 passed cargo test -p uf_test all green cargo test -p uf_cli, but the sandbox's socket-binding test ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added a complete component story workflow: define, discover, render, play, and run stories as tests. - Added story-file recognition and reserved story naming support. - Added structured story playback errors with story and step details. - **Bug Fixes** - Improved handling of unreadable files so scans can continue. - Test discovery now reports dynamic or unsupported test names instead of silently skipping them. - CLI commands now provide clearer unmatched-path errors and distinguish argument parsing failures. - **Documentation** - Updated CLI usage, exit-code guidance, and story workflow documentation.

author: chaliy
body:
## What changed

Individually review all 22 core tool-module tests and their fixtures/production consumers. Replace tests of test doubles and count-only registry checks with real dispatch, complete definition/result contracts, and validation checks. Consolidate duplicate default-tool inventory assertions. The ledger records every decision and replacement; 17 current tests remain.

Fix raw-output attachment losing caller-owned object fields that collide with the internal carrier keys. Colliding objects are wrapped before sidecar extraction, preserving both the original payload and separately retained raw output.

## Why

The original tests could pass while a supposedly preserved result changed shape. Several other tests asserted only registry length or a test double's own implementation, missing dispatch and output contract failures.

## Before / After

New regression failed on the original implementation: attaching raw output to `{"_raw_output_scalar":"user-value"}` returned the scalar `"user-value"` instead of the object. An existing `_raw_output` field was also overwritten. Both objects now survive unchanged while actual raw output stays in the nonserialized sidecar.

Revised tests cover direct/boxed/Arc replacement and execution, complete tool metadata, both executor validation paths with zero calls on rejected input, invalid registered schemas, unregistered monitor tools, full image/connection/error variants, planted internal-error redaction, and all nonobject carrier shapes.

Validation: all 928 core tests passed, including 17 tool tests. The failing-before/passing-after regression and ledger verification are recorded. All 50 host runtime integration tests and required pre-push checks passed.

## Risk

The production change only wraps object payloads containing reserved carrier keys when raw output is attached. Ordinary object and scalar behavior stays covered; no new enum variant, API schema, dependencies, or serialization format. One additional object wrapper is allocated only for colliding payloads.

## Security

Reviewed tool-result data integrity and internal-error disclosure boundaries. Caller fields cannot be overwritten by raw-output bookkeeping; actual raw output remains excluded from serialization. Full result expectations and planted private errors protect LLM-visible output. Registry tests prove argument/schema rejection happens before tool execution. No new authority, filesystem, network, or credential access.

## Follow-ups

The repository-wide review continues; remaining candidates are explicitly pending in the versioned ledger. No deferred findings in this module.

## Checklist

- [x] Every original tool-module test, fixture, and production path reviewed
- [x] Data-loss regression reproduced before the fix
- [x] Core unit tests and ledger checks passed
- [x] Host runtime smoke passed
- [x] Required pre-push checks passed
- [x] Final CI and post-green review sweep complete

body:
Plan batch: [1.9](docs/plan/p1-09-coverage-schedule-calendar.md). `index.html` unchanged. **165 passed, 18 skipped** under `--repeat-each=3`.

| File | Technique | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `calendar-edit-transitions` | State transition | 4, one pinned |
| `calendar-navigation-boundaries` | Boundary value analysis | 4, one pinned |
| `calendar-weekday-partitions` | Equivalence partitioning + grid snapshot | 4 |

Every test here rests on the clock pin from 1.5 — the editor opens on whatever month the app thinks it is, so `monthSelect = 5` / `2026` and "Today returns there" are now assertable at all.

## DEF-002 is worse than the registry said

It read *"month keys like `5-08-10`"* — correct about the shape, but easy to read as a short year. Typing `5` into the year is accepted as-is, day cells then carry `5-06-01`, and saving writes **that whole ISO date in as the month key**. That is precisely why the app's own CSV export can't be re-imported afterwards. Entry corrected.

DEF-012 is as described: no confirmation, dialog closes, selection gone. Both pins verified by removing the flag (`Received: "5-06-01"` and `Expected: true / Received: false`) and restoring byte-identical.

## The weekday header is not a toggle

Documented, not filed as a defect: **none** selected → selects all; **all** selected → clears; **some** selected → completes the set. So deselecting one Monday and clicking "Mon" does the opposite of what it looks like. Worth a second look during the React port.
